Heading: Schizophrenic woman electrocuted, man who promised marriage held - Indian Express
Content:
The Goregaon east police arrested a 35-year-old farmer from Dhule on charges of murdering his cousin, Gulab Sawle (40), a police constable, his wife Chitra Sawle (30) and injuring his three-and-a-half year old daughter Roshni. According to the police, a heated argument between the accused and his cousin turned ugly in the latter's house which culminated in murder at the SRPF quarters in Goregaon east on Tuesday evening .

According to the police, Gulab, who was a constable attached to the Thane rural police as a driver, used to stay with his wife and three daughters Mayuri (9), Maheshwari (6) and Roshni alias Sona (3½) at the SRPF quarters in Goregaon east.

"From what we have gathered, Gulab had taken a sum of Rs 15,000 from his cousin, Devidas alias Aaba Sawle, a farmer from a village in Dhule district. However, even after a year Gulab was unable to repay the loan which caused frequent quarrels between the two as Aaba used to regularly visit Gulab in Mumbai and had arguments over the payment of the loan," said DCP Ajit Patil (Zone 12).

According to Patil, Aaba had visited the family again on Tuesday evening to discuss the matter of payment. Gulab had just returned from work and was having an evening meal with his wife and his two elder daughters were in the school. "Aaba again made a demand for the payment and also threatened Gulab of dire consequences if the payment was not made. Both Gulab and Aaba probably got into an argument over the issue and an enraged Aaba attacked both Gulab and his wife with a weapon, which we suspect was a sickle.

Gulab suffered six injuries on his skull, whereas Chitra had three injuries on her head. Roshni, the youngest daughter, probably started screaming and was hit on her head by Aaba. At that time, Maheshwari, the second eldest daughter came home from school and was locked up in the bathroom by Aaba before he fled from the place," said Patil.

When the police came to know about the incident they rushed to the spot in the evening. Maheshwari told the police about the incident and were also told that in the past too, there had been frequent quarrels between Aaba and Gulab because of the loan. "Based on the description given by the girl, we also managed to find out that he was a resident of a village in the Dhule district.

A team of officials was immediately dispatched to Dhule where he was arrested on Wednesday morning from a bus-stop in Lamkani village near Dhule, where he was waiting to board a bus," informed Patil. However, the weapon used for the murder, suspected to be a sickle, has not been recovered yet.

At the Lifeline Hospital, where Roshni has been admitted, doctor Trilok Gupta said, "Roshni is in a critical state and is under observation. She has suffered three fractures in her skull as a result of the attack and is still unconscious. We cannot say anything for sure about her condition for the next 72 hours."

Heading: Trap money to be refunded to complainant after one month: ACB - Indian Express
Content:
A man who had consented to marry his friend's schizophrenic sister two years back despite being fully aware of her medical condition was arrested on Tuesday by the Nehrunagar police after the friend accused him of harassing her and eventually causing death due to negligence. A couple of years back, a conversation between Gajanan Ghagrum and Kailas Avghade had veered towards Avantika, Avghade's elder sister who was severely schizophrenic. Ghagrum had married Avantika and the couple also had a daughter.

On the night of September 14, Avantika, who was eight-months pregnant, had died after touching an electrical board fitted with live wires at their home in Chunabhati. "Late that night, Avantika had tried to use the socket when she must have touched the board. Ghagrum found her completely charred the next morning. When Avghade learnt about her death, he had filed a complaint accusing Ghagrum of being responsible for her death. The past few days went in perusing Avantika's medical history, asking the neighbours about the couple and examining the cause of death," said Police Sub-Inspector Aparna Joshi of the Nehrunagar police station where the case was registered.

Officials from the Public Works Department (PWD) had also been called in to check the connections and ascertain whether they were liable for the severe electric shocks leading to the death. "While the PWD's report is yet to reach us, we have arrested Ghagrum under Indian Penal Code section 304 related to causing death due to negligence. He is an electrician by profession and we cannot ignore the fact that his wife died due to electrocution," explained Police Inspector R B Salunkhe who is investigating the case.The police officials however said that the residents of the neighbourhood where Ghagrum stayed, bore testimony to the severity of Avantika's illness.

"She was reportedly very violent and also used to hit her child often. Fearing for his child's safety Ghagrum had also sent his daughter to stay with his sister. The neighbours told us that Avantika's violent nature would prevent people from even going near her but they all commended Ghargum's 'courage' for leading a married life with her. "We are still investigating the harassment claim," said Salunkhe.

Heading: Mother, uncle fight, three-year-old dies - Indian Express
Content:
The Anti-Corruption Bureau of the Mumbai police has informed the Bombay High Court that the 'trap money' provided by the complainant will now be reimbursed after one month instead of six months, according to a recent government resolution.

Additional Superintendent of Police, ACB, Sanjay Parande, in his affidavit has stated that "with a view to alleviate the hardships, if any, faced by complainants, the Home Department recently modified the orders regarding refund of trap money from six months to one month only" by a government resolution dated March 26. The affidavit has been filed in response to a Public Interest Litigation filed by former journalist Ketan Tirodkar, seeking that ACB should use its own money for the purpose of laying traps. "No situation as contended by petitioner of inability of the bureau to lay traps for nabbing public servants while accepting bribes due to lack of funds has come to the notice of the bureau," the affidavit states.

It further states that it has been a time honoured practice where the complainant himself physically participates in the exercise of laying the trap and also provides the bribe.

"There appears to be no need for changing this practice," the affidavit says.

Besides, Andhra Pradesh, too, follows this practice.The affidavit further points out that the ACB of Central Bureau of Investigations requires complainant to file request for refund of trap money in the competent court. Tirodkar's contention is that whenever a person approaches ACB alleging that a government official is seeking bribe, ACB does not lay the trap to arrest the official until the complainant does not arrange for the money.

Heading: First International Tourism Expo to be organised - Indian Express
Content:
A three-year-old boy died after an altercation between his mother and uncle turned ugly. The incident took place on Sunday at around 9:30 pm. Deceased boy Chotu Jadhav's uncle Appa Pawar (27) has been arrested by the Oshiwara police on the charges of murder.

Chotu was at Pawar's house at Vikasnagar slum in Behrambaug, Oshiwara, as his mother Sangita Jadhav (25), a housemaid, couldn't carry him around while at work. On September 20, she had taken Rs 400 from Pawar and had also asked him to get her TV fixed. The next day she returned Rs 200 to him.

However, the two got into an argument over the remaining money. According to the complaint filed by Jadhav, in the heat of the moment Pawar threw her TV and Chotu.

Chotu was hurt on his head as he fell on the concrete outside the house. He was rushed to Cooper hospital in a critical condition. Police Inspector (prevention) Shivaji Jamdade said, "Pawar got into an argument with his sister at 9:30 pm on September 21 and threw Chotu outside his house. Chotu was severely injured on his head as he hit the concrete. We have filed a case of murder against him, as anyone who throws a three year old with such force is bound to know he will be injured fatally."

When approached, a teary Jadhav changed her version and said, "My brother hasn't killed Chotu. I dropped him when he gave him to me in my hands. I had a fight with him and just wanted the police to scare him." She added, "I was very angry at the time of filing the complaint. As I am illiterate I didn't know this would happen." Reacting to Jadhav's change of heart Jamdade said, "We wrote the complaint at her behest but now she probably feels that having lost her son she shouldn't lose her brother too. She is just out to save him since he is a relative."

Heading: Top spiritual hit: Lalbaug cha Raja reaps top economic dividends - Indian Express
Content:
As part of its continuing efforts to promote Mumbai in the international tourism circuit, the Maharashtra Tourism Development Corporation (MTDC) is set to organise the first Mumbai International Tourism Expo (MITE) in 2010.

Singapore based Conference and Exhibition Management Services Ltd (CEMS), that had recently organised the Beijing International Tourism International Expo (BITE), prior to Beijing Olympics, will partner MTDC. The two day exhibition will be spread over a gross area of 12,000 sq km.

"The highlights of MITE will include Meetings, Incentives and Conferences, Exhibition (MICE) 2010 and CRUISE 2010. With MICE growing at rate of 15 to 20 per cent annually, India has immense scope in the MICE segment," said Suresh Shetty, minister of state for tourism. With a view to capitalise India 's 7500 km coastline, Mumbai has been organising the Mumbai International Boat Show since 2007. Shettly added that similarly, CRUISE 2010 would be able to tap the expanding cruise market,. Edward Liu, Managing director, CEMS said, "I believe with MITE, the government of Maharashtra has taken a giant leap to take tourism to a higher level. This will be a great opportunity for local and international buyers and sellers from tourism related business and activities."

Shetty added, "If we want to boost tourism, we will need to hold such exhibits, conferences more often. Events like MITE when held in a city like Mumbai are likely to have a multiplier effect and thus help in boosting tourism business. Maharashtra still lacks convention centers. We need to take such initiatives in order to boost the economy and generate employment."Schim Hock Seng, Consul General , Singapore said,"Mumbai's indomitable spirit was no more evident than during theGanapati Festival (immersion day) when the all the festivities carried on smoothly despite the Delhi blasts. Undoubtedly, we see this as a strong market."

Heading: Lukewarm response to Rly SMS update service - Indian Express
Content:
Devotees donate Rs 4.25 cr, 8 kg of gold, 200 kg of silver; mandal members spend more than a week counting the riches

Lalbaug cha Raja, which has for years been the city's most popular lord, has added another jewel in its crown this year. The city's biggest crowd-puller during the Ganesh festival has emerged as its richest mandal, with devotees donating Rs 4.25 crore, around 8 kg of gold and 200 kg of silver — that too after standing in queue for as long as 14 hours.

With its increasing popularity, the donation account of the Lalbaugcha Raja Sarvajanik Mandal has doubled since last year and the auction of gold and silver items will be held from Thursday to Sunday.

"We have received Rs 4.25 crore in cash through the 20 donation boxes that were kept in our premises," said mandal President Sunil Joshi. This year the mandal also received dollars from visiting non-resident Indians (NRIs).

Members of the mandal have spent more than a week counting the cash and evaluating the gold and silver items. While most devotes offer gold and silver finger rings, earrings, chains, necklaces and other jewellery — including modak and coconut for the lord — the mandal has also received unusual items like sea-shells and houses made of gold.

"It is difficult to verify exactly who made these donations as they are just dropped into the donation boxes. But many people make wishes and when they come true, they make the donations. It is possible that someone wished for a house and has got one now," Joshi explained.

The elephant-headed lord also received a 7-kg gold rose-flowered garland from a Taiwan company. However, the mandal has decided not to put this piece of jewellery for auction.

"We don't think anyone will bid for such a huge garland. It has, therefore, been decided to use it for the lord during the Ganeshutsav," Joshi informed.

Last year around Rs 2.5 crore was received as cash, which has been used for charitable purpose by the mandal. Usually patients with serious ailments, who come for treatment to government and municipal hospitals of the city like KEM, Nair, Tata, JJ and Wadia hospital, are helped with this money.

Joshi added that with the increase in the amount received as donations this year, the Trust will take a decision on increasing the money to be given to patients. "Many poor patients come from rural areas to Mumbai for treatment but have very little funds available. We will increase the amount of funds given to each patient," he said.

Each year around 1,000 patients at government hospitals benefit from the mandal's donations. It also runs a computer center, which has received around 20 computers as donations.

Heading: Hospitality World attracts over 150 exhibitors - Indian Express
Content:
The Western Railway's (WR) railway update SMS project seems to be gaining immense popularity among people in Gujarat and MP . However, this ambitious project of the WR has got a lukewarm response from the city, something that the WR did not expect. On August 15, the WR started this update service under which the commuters can get railway updates ranging from introduction of new services to cancellation of trains on their mobile phones through SMSes. This service played an important role when the trains were cancelled due to flooding in Gujarat last week.

According to the figures available from the WR, till September 23 over 50,000 people had subscribed to this update service. Interestingly, out of the 50,000 subscribers more than 20,000 people are from Gujarat. Second in the list is Mumbai from where a little less than 16,000 people had subscribed to the service. Some 9000 people from the rest of the state subscribed to the service. Everyday, around 32 lakh people use the services of the WR however only 16,000 people from Mumbai have subscribed to the railway update service. Sources said, though the WR tried popularising the update service by reaching out to people through advertisements and reports in the press, the service has still not gained much popularity in the city. "In the past week when trains were cancelled due to heavy rains in Gujarat, some 7000-8000 people from the state subscribed to the service. The service is faster than any other means and enables us to directly contact the subscriber ," said Shyam Sundar Gupta, chief spokesperson of the Western Railway.

Heading: Right image - Indian Express
Content:
Institute ties up with Schulich School of Business, one of Canada's top business schools

Besides Dubai and Singapore, students of two international campuses of SP Jain Centres of Management will now get an opportunity to visit Toronto, Canada.

SP Jain has recently tied up with Schulich School of Business, one of the top business schools of Canada. Students will get to spend 10 weeks in the Toronto-based business school, which is a part of York University.

This will be part of SP Jain's one year residential Global MBA programme conducted jointly between Dubai and Singapore campuses of the institution.

In each of the three cities, students learn local business practices, regulations and culture. The programme also boasts of an international faculty team.

Last year SP Jain Dubai and Singapore had 381 faculty members from around 18 countries, informed Professor Christopher Abraham, senior vice president, business development, SP Jain.

For the Toronto visit, 60 students will be chosen out of 250 from the Global MBA programme. According to Professor Christopher Abraham, the tie up would enable students to do an industry project in Toronto.

Nitish Jain, president, SP Jain said, "What sets SP Jain apart from other reputed business schools in the country is that while the traditional universities operate multiple programmes from a single campus, SP Jain conducts the MBA programme from its different campuses. A lot of students opt for SP Jain over other elite business schools because we offer a unique kind of global orientation to them."

Commenting on the success of the Schulich Business School, DezsoHorvath, dean, Schulich School of Business said that business schools need to have a diverse student population and an ability to see where the world would head in the future.

The fees for the Toronto programme would be not more than US $3000, informed Jain.On the effect of the US financial crisis on B-school placements Jain opined that the recent US financial meltdown would not have much impact on B-school placements. Unlike other top B-schools, SP Jain did not have Lehman Brothers as one of the recruiters on its campus. However, Jain said that many of SP Jain alumni were working in Lehman Brothers. "It is too early to comment on what impact it would have on the upcoming placement sessions. There will be uncertainty but after the initial knee jerk reaction, life will go on."Horvath felt that even as the markets collapsed in the US, financial institutions in Canada did 'very well.' He said, "It would certainly have an adverse impact on the salaries. We have provided placements for around 1000 students every year. It will be tough in such a scenario.However, other options (apart from investment banking) exist. But we haven't seen the end (of this crisis) yet."

Heading: Career info - Indian Express
Content:
Picking up a few tips on personal grooming always helps while stepping into the corporate world

Ramya Vishwanathan thinks joining a public speaking course, as part of a corporate grooming session, has been one of her best moves. This 21-year-old IT professional at present working in a multimedia company-did the four-day course while in college. When she started working, a number of communication tips she had got during the course came handy.

Such skills are important not only in corporate life but also in developing the overall personality of a candidate. And in today's highly competitive world, where social etiquettes matter a lot, personality development is not restricted to just honing of communication skills. This has given rise to the number of corporate and personal grooming workshops being held in the city. They help students as well as executives in bettering their persona.

Navaz Hilloowala-owner of ACTiIndia, a centre which focuses on social skills-feels such training is a must for freshers as it helps them get a feel of the corporate culture. This corporate trainer, who has been in the industry for 26 years, says, "Students come from various cultural backgrounds. Hence, there will be differences in their social mannerisms. Be it IT, multi-national companies, banks, hospitality and tourism industry or retail industry, the employees are expected to adhere to formal behaviour. They have to be conscious of people around them. We also advise them to wear the attire that suits their working culture."

When it comes to make-up, "Keep it minimum" is what experts say. Gauri Niranjan Chitre, a former HR executive and a freelance corporate trainer, has also completed a beauty therapist course from Clara International, Malaysia.

She says, "Having a light make-up enhances the personality of women employees but it should not be overdone. We also give tips on appropriate accessories." When it comes to men, the colour of the belt and shoes should be neutral, matching the trousers. Grooming courses also focus on dining and telephone etiquettes.

Since parties and get-togethers are a common feature in the corporate culture, the Isra School of Grooming and Finesse, Nariman Point, has a special session on salsa as a part of their four-day workshop on personal and corporate grooming. Sneha Shah, HR trainer and founder director of Isra School, says, "Apart from knowing how to dance, one needs to know the dancing etiquettes. We train them how to ask someone for a dance, how to say no politely and the space to be maintained between the dance partners."

Heading: Moving pictures - Indian Express
Content:
With the compulsory anti-smoking ban to go into force from October 2, restaurateurs feel that business too will go up in smoke

As the city gears up to stub those cancer sticks before getting into public spaces, the custodians of those public spaces (read restaurateurs and five-star hotels) are already beginning to rue the fact that the balance sheets are not likely to tilt in their favour come October 2. And for smokers who like to dangle it like James Dean did, it means tons of exercise stepping out every time they want to light up.

Although the collective voice of hoteliers and restaurateurs agrees with the ban, there are whispers of anxiety. AD Singh, of the upscale restaurant Olive, says, "There are no two ways about implementing the ruling. We will abide by whatever the government says. At the same time, I feel that a total ban on smoking in public places is a bit too drastic. In dining areas cigarette smoke can be pretty irritating. In the bar, on the other hand, it's part of the experience. I have been a non-smoker throughout but in the last one year I have begun to smoke cigars. Along with some music they just help me unwind. But I won't be able to do that any more. And I wonder why." At Indigo in Colaba, the rule will be enforced strictly too. That means no more lighting up the Cuban Cohiba at their Cigar Lounge.

At Café Mondegar, where many a pub-purist wafts through smoke clouds to get anywhere, there are no signs of a no-smoke makeover yet. Owner Hoshang Yezgardi says, "Last year we converted the A/C section into a no-smoking zone. We haven't heard anything from the government yet but we will implement the ban across the property once we do."

An off-shoot of the ban is a steep dip in the business. "Needless to say, it will affect us quite significantly. For many, not smoking will translate to not go out," says Singh.

Business in bars will slow down to a trickle. "There's recession everywhere. It's about time we were hit too," says Yezgardi.

Although standalone restaurants and clubs have not heard from the government yet, five-star hotels have already begun de-smoking their premises to address the smoldering issue. At Trident, Nariman Point, special signage will be put up amongst other things. "Besides, the areas that were originally smoking need to be cleared of the smoke smell and the smoke particles using ionisers. A separate area is being created for staff members, which needs to have separate ventilation as per government guidelines," says Devendra Bharma, executive vice president, Oberoi Hotels & Resorts, Mumbai.

At JW Marriott (where the trendy nightspot Enigma will be a no-smoke zone too) the management feels that at some level, they will have to appease the smokers too. "We have a smoking area available for them to smoke in the open as well as smoking rooms for in-house guests," says Kanika Hasrat, director of rooms, at the Mumbai property.

At other smoke-scented haunts like Poly Esther, Poison, Rock Bottom, Play, Zenzi and Ghetto, the ban is likely to smoke out tobacco lovers. What if people refuse to stub their cigarettes? Matan Schabracq of Zenzi says, "What then —Maybe eat the cigarette."

Heading: Khan do - Indian Express
Content:
Artist Sunil Gupta documents the gay movement in his new book of photographs

WHAT'S it like being gay in India? To which artist-photographer Sunil Gupta generally has one answer: "I don't know." Now, with a book of 100 photographs, Gupta hazards a guess, not just about gay life in India but also in Canada, the US and the UK. Called Wish You Were Here: Memories of a Gay Life, the book, to be released in Delhi, where he lives, on Friday, documents the development of the queer movement in several countries through a personal narrative that starts 40 years ago and ends with Delhi's first Queer Pride a few months ago.

"My family migrated to Canada in the 1970s when I was 15. Later, as I moved from one country to another to pursue the arts, I got a ringside view of the gay movement finally coming into its own," says Gupta, who came out early. Published by Yoda Press and priced at Rs 895, the book follows Gupta's pictorial autobiography Wish You Were Here, published in 2003.

There is a black-and-white shot of a young man at Christopher Street, the scene of the Stonewall riots in 1969. "I didn't visit Christopher Street till a couple of years later, but the historic impact hit you instantly. There was a flourishing gay subculture. Of course, this was before AIDS broke out," says Gupta, who was diagnosed with HIV in 1995.

There are several colourful shots of gay beaches, pubs and discos. "The biggest gay disco in the world was Heaven, in London. There would be 2,000 guys any evening and the atmosphere was quite something," he says.

The mood changes from uninhibited bonhomie to a guarded celebration of LGBT rights during the gay parade, called Queer Pride, in Delhi and Mumbai. "When I left India, there was no talk of homosexuality. When I returned to live here in 2004, a movement had begun. However, at the Pride, I noticed that many people had covered their faces with masks," he says. Things aren't always fine for people who choose to come out, he insists. Midway through the book, there is a picture of the Memorial for Matthew Shepherd, the gay American student who was fatally attacked in Laramie, Wyoming, as a chilling reminder to the threats faced by Gupta's "kind of people".

The book unfolds through faces - there is Saleem Kidwai, a leading queer rights activist, Sylvie, a celebrity hairstylist who went for a sex change and became a woman, as well as Gupta's friends and family.

Through the three months that Gupta took to sift through photographs, there was one strong thread of caution-"I have left out all the pictures of people who haven't come put openly," he says. When they are ready to walk out of the closet without fear, India would have taken a huge leap. And then, maybe, Gupta will publish another book.

Heading: Bowlers’ day out at Matunga - Indian Express
Content:
From Shivaji Park to Autobahn: Herr Deshpande spreads the mantra of Mallakhamb

He's not used to children who are aged a third of his 55 years addressing him by his first-name Uday, neither accustomed to them sitting sprawled during instructional lectures, sipping irreverently from bottles. Quite a cultural deviance from his usually earnest wards at Mumbai's Shivaji Park for the soft-spoken Mallakhamb instructor Uday Deshpande. But the initial, disbelieving looks were mutual in Munich, as the group of young German yoga students watched in awe while Deshpande's troupe of young Indians did their tricks with a rope and on a pole - an artful sport they hadn't imagined to be possible.

On his fifth trip to Germany early this September, Deshpande, a Customs official by profession and a Mallakhamb practitioner by passion, carried some extra canvas-cotton ropes since his German charges now are in the habit of hanging them in their backyards and practicing the quaint Indian sporting art-form in their spare-time. Jutta Schneider, a German tourist was smitten by what she saw at a local-gymnasium in Pune half a decade ago, and sniffed her way through to Shivaji Park's Samarth Vyayam Mandir, where Deshpande encouraged her to get onto the ropes soon after. She was 49 then and undeterred.

A 350-page book on yoga, with plentiful of space devoted to Mallakhamb followed, and in tow was an invitation to the Munich-based Yoga Forum for Deshpande to come train the enthusiasts. "They were amazed initially, but took to the sport quickly calling it Yoga am Seil (rope) and Yoga am Phal (pole). Mallakhamb has come some distance from being stared at like a circus or road-show to being taken up as a pastime to now being seriously considered as a competitive sport," says Deshpande, who first spent a year and half learning German before traveling, so he could communicate better.

The savant's ultimate aim is to get the Germans to compete internationally, even as he furthers his art to different continents, having set up facilities in Singapore and New Mexico earlier. The basic curiosity over the human furling and unfurling around the rope, and forming the pyramids on the pole, apart, German students sprung a few googlies - like how were they expected to twirl their tiny toes around the entire thickness of the pole. Patiently, Deshpande and his Indian students - five boys and five girls - answered all the queries, peppering the demonstrations with other novelties - all Indian. All sessions started with the bhajan Vaishnav jan to tene kahiye, and there was also the Ganpati celebrations this year, as the group of 60 Germans and the dozen Indians made do with Italian chocolates as prasaad.

"The Germans are very keen on learning new things, and now Indian children going there as instructors are even invited to stay with German families. But more than the cultural exchange, I'm glad that Mallakhamb is finding quick converts in Germany," says Deshpande. A former German consular general in Mumbai even joked that his countrymen with their superior physical fitness would easily beat the Indians to their game, if pressed into competition. "I said - look at the bigger picture. Mallakhamb's a one-stop centre to cure lifestyle-induced physical pain and depression," gushes Deshpande, who also trains blind children in the rope and pole-art at schools for visually challenged in Mumbai. It would seem, there's no barrier - cultural or physical, that Mallakhamb cannot overcome.

Heading: Thipsay, Negi share honours - Indian Express
Content:
Ravi Shankar Singh's remarkable figures of 6 for 36 weren't good enough to stop Lalchand Rajput XI from taking a crucial first innings lead on the opening day of their three-day encounter against Chandrakant Pandit XI in the Shalini Bhalekar Memorial Cricket (Mumbai Cricket Association under-22 trial) Tournament on Wednesday. Meanwhile, in the other game played at the Ramesh Dadkar Maidan in Matunga, Dilip Vengsarkar XI reached 68 for the loss of four wickets at the end of day's play in reply to Hemant Waingankar XI's first innings score of 191.

Rajput XI finished the day on 157 for 9, with a 70 run lead, after Pandit XI were bundled out for 87 earlier in the day. Harshal Nandu snared 5 for 40 for Rajput XI, and was ably supported by Balkrishna Shirke who took 2 for 25.

Anand Singh scored a stubborn 43 to give his team the lead, while Akshay Jambhekar with 37 and Hrishikesh Patkar with 34 played their respective parts.

Pandit XI captain Prashant Naik will be hoping to wrap up the innings early tomorrow, and put up a better show with the bat second time around.

Sachin Wagh's 53 for Waingankar XI was the only half-century scored on a day which was completely dominated by the bowlers. Ganesh Narsimhan returned figures of 5 for 32 for Vengsarkar XI, while Dinar Gavkar finished with figures of 3 for 68. But his team stumbled to 68 for four after the Waingankar bowlers led by Vivek Arothe struck a few early blows. Karan More is still at the crease with 35 next to his name, and will be hoping to stretch his innings further and give his team a first innings lead.

Heading: Song and dance - Indian Express
Content:
International Master 'B' Adhiban put himself in the title contention outplaying two-time former national 'B' champion and International Master Sriram Jha of LIC in the 11th round of the Monginis National 'B' Chess Championship at Damodar Sausthan, Zambaulim.

Adhiban, who hails from Tamil Nadu, now has a clear one point lead in the tournament and in all probability will emerge as the champion.

The much awaited encounter between the oldest and youngest Indian Grandmaster turned out to be an uninteresting draw.

Grandmaster Parimarjan Negi of Air India was slightly worn out by his previous encounter and was pleased to sign the peace treaty with Grandmaster Pravin Thipsay of Union Bank of India after just 18 moves of a Slav Defence.

In girls section Bhakti Kulkarni and Ivana Furtado won their respective matches.

Double world U-8 girl champion Ivana Furtado seized the advantage arising out of a positional blunder by her opponent and played efficiently to win against an unrated Kumar Sudarshan of Himachal Pradesh.

Nine-year-old Ivana now has five points from the total of eleven rounds.

Goa's national junior girls champion Bhakti Kulkarni demolished the highly ranked national Under-25 champion M Vinaykumar of Andhra Pradesh.

Bhakti won an exchange right from the opening itself and played precisely to win the game after 61 moves off a colle system.

She now has seven and a half points with two more rounds remaining in the tournament and takes on India's new International Master M R Lalith Babu in the next round.

Heading: One man, two tags: mastermind and loner who never left home - Indian Express
Content:
While Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime Branch) Rakesh Maria on Wednesday said today that a supplementary chargesheet would now be filed in the 7/11 serial blasts case, a comparison of what the state Anti-Terrorism Squad has stated in its original chargesheet and what the Crime Branch said suggests that investigators have gathered new evidence to buttress the earlier charges.

According to the chargesheet filed in the 7/11 case, 13 alleged terrorists, masterminded by a top Pakistani commander of the Lashkar-e-Toiba Azam Cheema alias Babji (absconding), Mohammed Faisal Shaikh and Asif Khan (both arrested), first conspired in 1999, and thereafter both within and outside India, to execute the serial train blasts of 2006.

The chargesheet says the plot to cause blasts in suburban trains on a working day was hatched at a meeting at Faisal's house in Bandra. "Azam Cheema sent RDX. Pakistan-based terrorists infiltrated the country from the Indo-Nepal and Indo-Bangladesh border and some from Gujarat," adds the chargesheet.

The bombs were said to have been made between July 8-10, 2006, at the house of accused Shaikh Mohammed Ali Alam Shaikh in Govandi. A reconnaissance of the target was done by Faisal and four others. The training for handling arms and ammunition was given in Pakistan. Funding was said to have been done by Azam Cheema.

On Wednesday, the Mumbai Police claimed the five alleged Indian Mujahideen terrorists posed as Pakistanis, using bogus names while dealing with the locals who were arrested in the 7/11 case. According to Maria, these men are the "Pakistanis" identified as the accused wanted in the 7/11 chargesheet.

However, the police today claimed the group arrested was controlled by one Ameer Razaq in Pakistan, and not by LeT commander Azam Cheema.

According to the chargesheet, seven groups — each comprising an Indian and a Pakistani — planted the 7/11 bombs. The Mumbai Police on Wednesday claimed the five IM men arrested were responsible for planting the bombs.

Heading: On industrialisation, discuss in advance, not in crisis, says Governor - Indian Express
Content:
The police call him the mastermind of several terror attacks; family and friends describe him as a quiet man who rarely left his house.

The family of Sadiq Sheikh said he had never been out of their sight - except for the past four days. The third of four brothers, Sadiq is part of a joint family that includes his elderly parents, wife and three children, along with the brothers' families. The family lives at Cheetah Camp.

"Four days ago, Sadiq had told us he was going out for a job interview. The next day, he called a couple of times, but for three days, there have been no calls," said Mohammed Asad, Sadiq's elder brother. That was the only time he has ever been away from home, he said.

As he spoke, Sadiq's wife, Suraiya Bano looked dazed as she sat with her children, two-year-old Aasra and year-old twins Rehma and Sana. Sadiq's mother Aasia (58) is a heart patient; his father Israr Ahmed (62) is an asthmatic. "All the years we have been here, neither I nor any of my sons was ever involved with the police in any way," said Israr Ahmed, who runs a grocery store.

Neighbour Zubeida Bano said, "Our families have known each other for several years. Sadiq has always been a quiet, silent boy who used to go to work, come home, and keep to himself. Over he years, the family won a lot respect, which has wiped out in an instant."

The two-storey house, where the family has lived since 1976, was crowded with friends and neighbours, few of whom were convinced by the terror charge. "When he hasn't been away from us ever, how can the police accuse him of planning such an elaborate attack? Such crimes need planning, time and money. If he was that rich, then the family would not have been living in such squalour," said Sharifa Sahebjan, another neighbour.

The family said that they had just ended their fast when the media flooded their house. They had no idea about the arrests as they had no television.

Asad said that they had not received any notification about Sadiq's arrest; they received a call only after 9.30pm, vaguely informing them about the arrest and asking them to go by the N M Joshi Marg crime branch at 11 am the next day.

Heading: Bengal plans to relocate Dankuni project - Indian Express
Content:
West Bengal Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi made some observations on Wednesday, which, seen in the context of Singur, appeared an indictment of the Left Front Government for creating the impasse.

In his speech at the Second Green Revolution Summit & Expo — organised by the Indian Chamber of Commerce at the Science City and attended, among others, by a large number of farmers — Gandhi said: "The way in which agriculture and industry are seen juxtaposed is not right. There is scope for both. The first imperative is therefore that of a dialogue, not when a crisis hangs overhead, but well in advance".

"Land is limited. Land is precious. Land holds a special value to farmers and their families. It is not an impersonal, dematerialised share certificate that you can buy and sell with every swing of the sensex. The farming community has a mind of its own no less than its urban or industrial equivalent. And we will have to think carefully on the location of industrial ventures not turning to arable land before exhausting all options."

The comment came hours before a Trinamool Congress delegation led by Mamata Banerjee met him, in what was said to be a last ditch effort to save the Nano project. Even after the meeting, she remained steadfast on her plans to begin agitation from Thursday.

At noon, around 200 TMC supporters led by Tapan Dasgupta, Trinamool working president at Hooghly and Dilip Yadav, Hooghly INTTUC president, gheraoed special Land Acquistion Officer Sumon Kumar Ghosh for an hour. Some of the farmers who were there to submit applications and receive cheques, escaped. "The TMC leaders complained that cheques were being given to wrong persons," said Neelam Meena, District Magistrate, Hooghly. "I have told them that we are verifying documents before disbursing cheques."

The police, meanwhile, drew a blank in Singur, being unable to arrest the men who attacked the security guards at the Tata plant on Monday night.

Heading: Tribal rally throws traffic out of gear - Indian Express
Content:
Facing a problem in purchasing land at Dankuni in Hooghly district, the state government is now mulling the idea of relocating the DLF project. The government had planned to build the township on a public-private partnership basis with Delhi-based real estate giant DLF Ltd.

"We will go ahead with the project but this may not take place at Dankuni," said Ashok Bhattacharya, Minister for Urban Development.

A meeting was held on Tuesday between the officials of the urban development department and representatives of DLF at Writers' Buildings. "We have decided not to go ahead with the acquisition of the land, we will purchase it. As of now, we have not yet been able to buy even one acre of land," said Bhattacharya.

The project was to come up on 4800 acres with an investment of Rs 33,000 crore.

In February 2007, the Kolkata Metropolitan Development Authority (KMDA) signed an agreement with DLF for building the project — Dankuni World Project — comprising a township and an industrial hub.

Following the Nandigram episode, the state government had set up a land procurement committee to purchase the land in Dankuni. But till date, the committee could make little headway because of the opposition from a large number of land owners.

The real estate giant has already paid Rs 270 crore to the government for the project.

Heading: ‘Ban on smoking at public places from October 2 may curb the menace’ - Indian Express
Content:
A massive rally by tribals threw traffic out of gear in certain parts of Kolkata on Wednesday. The tribals were demanding the institution of Alchiki as a language in schools.

The rally, which paralysed the city streets, was organised by the Adibasi Socio Educational and Cultural Association (ASECA), a popular tribal body.

Nearly 10,000 tribal youths, wielding axes, sticks, bow and arrows and swords to keep the pedestrians at bay, reduced the Kolkata police to the level of mere spectators.

Demonstrators from far-flung areas of the state marched towards Esplanade from Sealdah and Howrah stations. By 9.45 am, the people had congregated at Esplanade, blocking the key thoroughfares. Traffic disruption prevailed at the peak hours of the afternoon at the Strand Road, parts of S N Banerjee Road and Lenin Sarani.

ASECA president Madan Mohan Baske, however, played down the fallout of the rally and maintained that it was nothing but an aberration. "We had asked our supporters not to disturb the people and traffic. What happened is just a minor incident," Baske said after the rally.

"We have done our best to maintain law and order," said a senior officer of the New Market police station.

Heading: Rats wreak havoc at the  Nilratan hospital morgue - Indian Express
Content:
Director of the state Health department, Dr Sanchita Bakshi, expressed hope that the Centre's initiative to ban smoking in public places from October 2 will be effective in doing away with the menace.

Bakshi said this at a seminar in the city on Wednesday. "In 2003 too, the Central government had tried to implement anti-smoking laws after the Geneva Convention. But it had failed to create much impact," she said.

Satyoban Ghosh, nodal officer (tobacco) with the state government, said: "There are also recommendations for the creation of smoking zones. Apart from putting up no-smoking signs in public places, there will also be pictorial warnings on cigarette packets from November 30." Offenders, however, will be fined only Rs 200.

Although there is just one oncology unit at Chittaranjan Hospital at present, the state government plans to set up similar units in all government hospitals. It has already allocated Rs 6 lakh to establish such units, with one recently opening its doors at the Bangur Hospital in South 24 Parganas.

Heading: Bank strike total, ATMs not spared - Indian Express
Content:
In a horrifying case of negligence, the body of a suicide victim, which had been sent for postmortem to the government-run Nilratan Sircar Hospital, was found to have been partially eaten up by rats when the victim's family went to collect it on Wednesday.

Having seen the damaged body, angry relatives attacked the morgue attendants, said hospital officials.

Police sources said Uma Swain (27), a resident of Raja Rajendralal Mitra Road in Maniktala, had committed suicide on Monday. Her husband, Prashant Swain (35), works in a scrap dealer's shop.

Uma's brother-in-law Shankar Swain said: "My sister-in-law's pregnancy was terminated two months ago, after which she was very depressed. This led her to take the extreme step. The police sent the body to NRS for postmortem at 7 pm. We wanted to perform the last rites on Tuesday but the police said the body cannot be released unless a blood relative of the victim was present."

To preserve the body the family approached the morgue. "We were told by the attendant that if we wanted the body to be in good shape, we had to pay Rs 1,500 for one night. After a bit of haggling, we agreed on Rs 800, paid Rs 200 as advance, and went home. We returned on Wednesday with other family members and approached the Entally police station for release of the body."

Then, a policeman allegedly approached them and asked for Rs 150 as a bribe to hasten the releasing process. "As we were very disturbed, we paid the bribe and got the release papers," said Swain.

At the morgue the relatives were asked to pay the remaining Rs 600 by the attendant. "But inside the morgue, we were shocked to see the state of the bodies. When the attendants brought Uma's body, we saw that parts of her hands and feet, nose, one ear and part of her throat had been eaten up by rats. It was too much to bear, and we attacked the attendant," Swain added.

After the body was released, the family unsuccessfully tried to contact Medical Superintendent L K Ghosh. "His deputy sent us to the next table, from where we were sent to another. Not wanting to delay the last rites, we proceeded to the crematorium. We are now planning to write to the police and the hospital authorities for justice," Swain said.

Ghosh said he was aware of the incident, but could not intervene "because the body was in the morgue, which is in the provenance of the forensic department and not the superintendent." He added that a new state-of-the-art morgue is in the pipeline.

Heading: Cash & Carry officials meet CM - Indian Express
Content:
The two-day bank strike called by the employees of nationalised and scheduled commercial banks brought banking operations to a total standstill in the city on Wednesday. The strike also saw a total shutdown of all ATMs in the city, even those operated by private companies.

People had made a beeline to the ATMs as the last option, only to find the shutters down. The banking unions, which had called the strike, however, refused to shoulder any responsibility for the closure of the ATMs of private banks.

The Indian Banks Association and the United Forum of Bank Unions, the latter an umbrella union of nine bank unions, went on a two-day nationwide strike to protest merger and consolidation in the sector and delay in settlement of issues like wage revision.

"We have nearly 20,000 employees of both officer and clerical grade in the Bengal circle of State Bank of India all of whom participated in the strike. It was a total shutdown," said Ashok Kumar Mukherjee of SBI Staff Association.

There are around 1,500 ATMs operational in West Bengal, with 500 ATMs located in Kolkata itself.

"Foreign banks like HSBC and American Express have unions which are affiliated with us. They have voluntary decided to keep ATMs closed and there was no use of force," said Malay Roy, Convenor of the West Bengal state unit of United Forum of Bank Unions.

"With people making a beeline to withdraw cash from ATMs, it made sense to close down the ATMs to prevent vandalism," he said.

A source at the regional office of ABN AMRO Bank in Topsia said at 12.30 pm members of nationalised banks forced them to down shutters.

Heading: Mumbai FC looking to set up stadium, commercial complex - Indian Express
Content: Facing opposition from ruling Left Front partner Forward Bloc, and with their licence not renewed, officials of German wholesale giant Metro Cash & Carry met West Bengal Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee on Wednesday. After the meeting, Martin Dlouhi, Managing Director of Metro Cash & Carry India Private Limited, told reporters, "the meeting was very encouraging. We will make our decision known tomorrow".

Heading: New indoor stadium on the anvil - Indian Express
Content:
This is one football club which is distinctly different from other Indian clubs in character — focusing on its pronounced commercial identity above any other aspect. In just a year after getting launched, Mumbai FC Private Ltd is fast in a process of making the commercial focus their identity in the coming years. The message is clear — this club is here to make business its focus.

When the Mumbai-based outfit was launched last year, it was compared to FC Kochi and Viva-Kerala. But Mumbai FC is taking an entirely new path, with a pronounced focus on the commercial aspect. Speaking to The Indian Express, the visiting club's general manager Henry Menezes explained the limitations of running a club on just legal identity. "A club with only legal identity has to make do as a non-profit ogranisation. Naturally, that kind of a club cannot run its affairs with a professional attitude. But when you run the club as a business, you can naturally think about making profits as well. It's not fair for an average club to just look up to tournament prize money as its only source of making money. In modern-day football, a club should have other avenues of making money, it should be run with a professional attitude and a commercial focus," Menezes said.

Mumbai FC is officially a private limited company, and is now on the look-out for land in Mumbai, roughly a 25-acre plot. The club management's long-term plan is to build a well-equipped stadium along with a commercial complex. The club has already received a couple of 'offers' from Pune for setting up its complex. At the same time, Mumbai FC's mother company Essel Group has assured that it has adequate land at its disposal for the project.

Menezes is quite with the unwelcome response from the state government so far in their hunt for a plot of land. And the club's bigwig is equally disappointed with the role of the All India Football Federation (AIFF) on the venture. Menezes said: "The AIFF chief (Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi) is an influential person in the Central government. Why isn't he pushing with Maharastra government to help us out in obtaining land in Mumbai? Unless the AIFF shows enthusiasm or unless he himself takes an effort to do something about our case, why should football clubs with a professional approach come to Indian football?"

However, David Booth, British coach of the Mumbai FC outfit, doesn't want to read too much into the national team's AFC Challenge Cup recently. Instead, he warns that Indian football, and all its premier clubs, could take a tumble if they continue to rely heavily on ageing stars and imported players.

No foreigner for Chirag
Chirag United will play their first match of the I-League sans foreigners. Rather, they have signed centreback Subhashis Roychowdhury on loan. East Bengal, on the other hand, have decided to keep faith in veteran Suley Musah and registered him as their third foreign recruit.

Heading: Ant-Reels - Indian Express
Content:
Sports in Budge Budge and South 24-Parganas as a whole will get a boost as Eden City Maheshtala, along with Maheshtala Municipality sets off for a journey that has a three-tier plan.

In the first phase, an indoor stadium would be built along side Eden City's housing complex at Maheshtala. State urban development minister Ashok Bhattacharya today laid the foundation stone of the project. The stadium will have a sitting capacity of 2,000 and will house badminton, volleyball and basketball courts. There would be provisions for other indoor games as well.

Apart from sports, the complex, aptly named as Eden City Centre for Sports, Science and Culture, will also have a science library and a meeting and convention centre with facilities for 300 people. The centre is first of its kind in South 24-Parganas and is likely to come up in one-and-a-half years' time. The cost of this project is about Rs 3.75 crore.

"Our government is committed to the development of sports like any other sector. It will be great to see the youth here getting world-class facilities," Bhattacharya said.

In the second phase, there would be an outdoor stadium with 20,000 sitting capacity and then, they have the plan to build a football academy a la European style. Talks are on with some European clubs in this regard.

The entire project is the brainchild of local MP, Samik Lahiri. "We have been planning this for the last five-six years. We have the potential to excel in sports. Problem is, only 11 paise are allotted per Rs 100 for our sports budget. It's very heartening to see that Eden City has come forward," Lahiri said.

Chairman of the Eden City Group, Indrajit Dey said that they wanted to strike a balance between profit and social commitment and don't want to act like a nouveau riche.

This area, which is 25 km off Kolkata, has produced footballers like Shankar Banerjee and Manash Bhattacharya. Banerjee was present on the occasion and thanked Lahiri and Maheshtala municipality chairman Kali Bhandari for taking the initiative.

The important thing is, the outsiders too will have an access to this stadium.

Heading: Ali all the way - Indian Express
Content:
It's morals-meet-spice in the first Bengali animated film

If Bollywood boasts of singing, prancing, even smouldering roadside Romeos, Tollywood probably prefers remaining closer to the earth. So, it's spunky ants closer home, who would grace Tollywood's first ever animated outing. Lal Kalo, based on Girindrashekhar Basu's only novel, is a tale of two warring factions of ants — red and black. R D Mallik, CEO of Elecom Animation Academy, which tied up with Mumbai-based Fiesta Entertainment for the film, came across Basu's novel as a kid. "I remembered it as a delightful novel with fantastic illustrations and even a song in the Bhojpuri script. So, when I started toying with the idea of an animation film, Lal Kalo was the first work which came to my mind," says Mallik.

However, it's not all pure parapsychology (Basu was India's first para-psychiatrist) in animation that you get to see in Lal Kalo. The film, which also has a Hindi version called Cheenti Cheenti Bang Bang, was scripted by actor Kharaj Mukherjee from the novel, with generous doses of humour, romance and melodrama typical of a potboiler. "We did not want yet another preachy animation," says N D Nagpal, partner in Fiesta Entertainment. Lal Kalo will therefore treat you to a host of songs composed by Jeet Ganguly sung by Shaan, Shreya Ghoshal, Kunal Ganjawala, and Pt Rashid Khan.

Despite the masala, Lal Kalo remains a sarcastic commentary on the futility of wars and prejudices. "The two colours can be interpreted in several ways. From communal hatred to petty caste prejudices, the colours and their antagonism aim at deriding the difficulties faced by the society," says Nagpal of the novel that was written at least a century ago.

With a voice cast boasting of names like Mahesh Manjrekar, Ashish Vidyarthi, Asrani, Anjan Srivastav in the Hindi version and Sabyasachi Chakraborty, Biswajeet Chakraborty, Kanchan Mallik in the Bengali, Lal Kalo has been made on a budget of Rs 6.5 crore. From Dolby surround sound to SFX and ambience effects, the film had a team of around 100 animators work on the story board.

A Bengali animation quite obviously means treading unfamiliar and difficult terrain. However, Mallik is not perturbed. "Everybody loves quality entertainment. And that's exactly what you have in Lal Kalo," says Mallik, about his film which releases across India on October 10.

Heading: Moving Pictures - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistani singer Shafqat Amanat Ali releases his first solo album in the city with a concert

His vocal feats in songs like Mitwa from Kabhi Alvida Na Kehna and Ye hausla from Dor may have left you breathless, but in Kolkata , Pakistani singer Shafqat Ali Khan was only too happy to hand over the mike to the audience at the Rabindaranath Tagore Centre auditorium this Monday. "It's wonderful to be among people who understand music so well," said Amanat as he handed over the mike to a youth who crooned the track Aankhon ke Saagar from his earlier album with the Pakistani band Fuzon. The packed-to-capacity auditorium was playing host to the launch of Amanat Ali's album, Tabeer, which means fulfillment of dreams. The nine-track contemporary Sufi album happens to be his first solo album too. "With this, I have realised my dream of composing the kind of songs that inspire me," smiled Ali. There's one more reason to cheer: even before its launch, the album has soared the charts.

Ali, who left the band Fuzon in 2004, to pursue a successful career in Bollywood, performed for a good two hours, regaling the appreciative audience with tracks such as Naina, Khairhenya de naal and Dum Ali that feature in the latest compilation. But that wasn't all, as the rain lashed outside, he belted out Bollywood hits Mitwa from Kabhi Alvida Na Kehna and Ye hausla from Dor, apart from Aankhon ke Saagar, Tere Bina and Mora Saiyan too, which added to the already romantic atmosphere. And as the concert drew to an end, the mood mellowed with Allah tero naam, Ishwar tero naam. "If it were up to me I would have had this song on the album too," said a wistful Ali. As part of an initiative by Music Today and The Indian Express Group, Ali had earlier toured Delhi and Mumbai.

Heading: Quiz Master - Indian Express
Content:
Artist Sunil Gupta documents the gay movement in his new book of photographs

What's it like being gay in India? To which artist-photographer Sunil Gupta generally has one answer: "I don't know." Now, with a book of 100 photographs, Gupta hazards a guess, not just about gay life in India but also in Canada, the US and the UK. Called Wish You Were Here: Memories of a Gay Life, the book, to be released on Friday, documents the development of the queer movement in several countries through a personal narrative that starts 40 years ago and ends with Delhi's first Queer Pride a few months ago.

"My family migrated to Canada in the 1970s when I was 15. Later, as I moved from one country to another to pursue the arts, I got a ringside view of the gay movement finally coming into its own," says Gupta, who came out early. Published by Yoda Press and priced at Rs 895, the book follows Gupta's pictorial autobiography Wish You Were Here, published in 2003.

There is a black-and-white shot of a young man at Christopher Street, the scene of the Stonewall riots in 1969. "I didn't visit Christopher Street till a couple of years later, but the historic impact hit you instantly. There was a flourishing gay subculture. Of course, this was before AIDS broke out," says Gupta, who was diagnosed with HIV in 1995. There are several colourful shots of gay beaches, pubs and discos. "The biggest gay disco in the world was Heaven, in London. There would be 2,000 guys any evening and the atmosphere was quite something," he says.

The mood changes from uninhibited bonhomie to a guarded celebration of LGBT rights during the gay parade, called Queer Pride, in Delhi. "When I left India, there was no talk of homosexuality. When I returned to live here in 2004, a movement had begun. However, at the Pride, I noticed that many people had covered their faces with masks," he says. Things aren't always fine for people who choose to come out, he insists. Midway through the book, there is a picture of the Memorial for Matthew Shephard, the gay American student who was fatally attacked in Laramie, Wyoming, as a chilling reminder to the threats faced by Gupta's "kind of people".

The book unfolds through faces — there is Saleem Kidwai, a leading queer rights activist, Sylvie, a celebrity hairstylist who went for a sex change and became a woman, as well as Gupta's friends and family.

Through the three months that Gupta took to sift through photographs, there was one strong thread of caution — "I have left out all the pictures of people who haven't come put openly," he says. When they are ready to walk out of the closet without fear, India would have taken a huge leap. And then, maybe, Gupta will publish another book.

Heading: Aussies getting too much 'help' in India: BCCI - Indian Express
Content:
Vikas Swarup on Slumdog Millionaire, the adaptation of his debut novel Q & A, winning the People's Choice Award at the Toronto International Film Festival

Slumdog Millionaire, British filmmaker Danny Boyle's movie based on Indian diplomat Vikas Swarup's debut novel Q & A, has won the People's Choice Award at the just concluded Toronto International Film Festival. And in Pretoria, Swarup has a million-dollar smile — his picaresque through urban India has not only wowed the audience in Canada but is also set to close the forthcoming London Film Festival. "I guess everybody loves a good fable. In fact, Simon Beaufoy (who adapted the novel) told me that it was the element of Dickensian drama that drew him to the book in the first place," says Swarup, now India's deputy high commissioner to South Africa, over the telephone.

The film, which revolves around the tale of a poor Dharavi waiter who wins the Indian version of Who Wants to be a Millionaire and who has to explain how he knew the answer to each question, is set to make its debut in India in November. It has a largely Indian cast — NRI Dev Patel playing the protagonist Jamal, Anil Kapoor as the quizmaster, and model Frieda Pinto and actor Irrfan Khan in other important roles. Even though Swarup has yet to see Boyle's adaptation of his novel, he is convinced that the director of Trainspotting and 28 Days Later would have done justice to it. "I have watched all his movies and I was certain that his own unique style will bring a completion to the craft. It was him and Simon's mastery over the script that made me sign the contract in the first place. I am sure it deserves every bit of the adulation it is getting," he says.

In fact, it was the involvement of Boyle and Beaufoy, who had earlier written The Full Monty, that made it easy for Swarup to accept the creative changes. "In any such adaptation, you can either accept the change or reject it. I knew they had retained the framework of the novel and I saw both the first and second drafts of the script since I had the creative rights. It would have been cinematically boring to have retained all the 12 questions and answers. I trusted their creative vision and now, I am waiting to see the DVD which Danny has promised he will send," he says.

Heading: Chappell given task to address Ponting's problem - Indian Express
Content:
The Cricket Board has objected to top-class facilities being provided to Australian team by the Rajasthan Cricket Academy in Jaipur, where Ricky Ponting and Co are camping for a week before the start of Test series.

BCCI Chief Administrative Officer Ratnakar Shetty told a private television channel that the RCA was obliging the Australians more than expected.

"We won't get this kind of facilities if India went abroad, we would have got the bare minimum. RCA is being a little too obliging to the Australian team, they have done more than what a host country will do," Shetty said in a TV channel.

Former India coach Greg Chappell, who is the chief coach at RCA Centre of Excellence and is presently touring with Australian team as the assistant coach, has arranged all facilities using his influential association with the RCA.

Chief Curator of RCA admitted that specialised practice pitches, each of a different character had been offered to the Australians.

"Looking into the conditions of India, we have given Australia everything they wanted for practice. We have prepared 10 wickets for Australia," said Chief Curator Taposh Chatterjee.

But the RCA officials refused to agree that there was anything suspicious about their hospitality.

"Well, this is the first time a team has come a week before. So, why not if we are fair players," said RCA President Bimal Soni.

Ponting's men, who arriver on Monday will practice in Jaipur till Sunday. They will fly to Hyderabad for a four-day practice match against the BCCI President's XI starting October 2. The series opener starts in Bangalore from October 9.

Heading: Super secure Dhoni seeks pistol licence - Indian Express
Content:
Greg Chappell's role in the Australian team's scheme of things seemed to be getting even bigger than expected as the former India coach has apparently been given the job to address captain Ricky Ponting's dismal record in India during the Test series starting October 9.

Ponting has scored just 172 runs from 14 innings in India at an average of 12.28 as compared to his overall Test average of 58.37 and 'Guru' Greg was today seen devoting much of his time on the visiting captain during the three-hour team practice session at RCA's Future Cricket Academy in Jaipur.

He arrived at the Academy with the first lot of players comprising batsmen only, wearing his trademark round hat and scarf around the neck. Head coach Tim Nielsen reached later with the second lot of players comprising bowlers and all-rounders.

Chappell watched Ponting play his natural shots off fast bowlers locals and Rajasthan Ranji players -- on a specially-designed 'conventional fifth-day India pitch' at the RCA facility for around 20 minutes without giving much attention to other batsmen.

He then had a lengthy animated discussion with Ponting after the captain switched to the spinning wicket, apparently telling him how to adjust his techniques while facing an Anil Kumble or Harbhajan Singh on slow Indian pitches.

What actually transpired was out of bounds for the scribes as they had to watch the players from a distance and had to get into the RCA facility only after showing media passes.

Tight security was thrown around the ground with at least 40 police personnel led by senior officers, and private security men, manning the entrance and even the RCA officials were issued special passes.

The former Australia captain, now the assistant coach of the team, in his capacity as head of Cricket Australia's Centre of Excellence in Brisbane has also decided to end his hide and seek with the media with a formal interaction on Saturday.

Chappell, who is also Technical adviser at the RCA, has been unreachable since the Australians landed at the Pink City on Monday and today also he did not go beyond 'Hi people' greetings and waving off hands to the media posse.

Outgoing BCCI Secretary Niranjan Shah had on Wednesday added much spice to Chappell's distance from the media, saying that the stone-faced Australian had courted trouble during his controversial two-year tenure as India coach as he "communicated to the players through the media rather than talking to the players directly".

Australian team media manager Matthew Slade confirmed Chappell would express his views on various issues on Saturday at a press conference.

"Chappell will have a press conference on Saturday. It is better that he put across his views himself through a formal event (instead of any misunderstanding)," Slade said.

"He can answer queries on a range of issues," he added.

Opener Matthew Hayden and vice-captain Michael Clarke, both among the quartet who have Test experience in India others being Ponting and Simon Katich also got attention from Chappell, who had discussions with the two batsmen while slogging at the spinning tracks.

The bowlers were, however, exempted from sending down deliveries and only had catching, throwing and hitting-the-stumps practice.

Later, all-rounder Shane Watson, who batted and bowled on Thursday, told reporters that the bowlers were given a bit of rest to 'recover' from Wednesday's practice session.

"They (bowlers) had strenuous practice yesterday so they were given recovery time. They will resume bowling tomorrow," he said.

Heading: Australian media terms Kumble as danger man - Indian Express
Content:
India's ODI Captain M S Dhoni has a non-prohibited gun license and 'z' category security, besides all-women police ring to keep his girl-fans at a distance whenever he lands in Maoist-infested Jharkhand.

Still India's gloves-man seeks another license for a 9mm 'prohibited-bore' -- he applied for it around the same time he got admitted to St Xaxier's College to sharpen his 'rusted' pen.

His application is pending with the sub-divisional officer (sadar) from September 16, but held up following a change of deputy commissioners ranchi district, a senior police officer said in Ranchi on Thursday.

The district administration's duty is just to forward it to the home department after verification of the applicant's antecedents and its approval only be given by the union government after recommendation from proper channels, he added.

The Twenty20 skipper, who took admittion to the college in Ranchi to complete graduation, is also the cynosure of the Steel Authority of India Limited, which is looking into the prospects of romping him as its brand ambassador.

"I don't know the process of how brand ambassador is made. But I will definitely ask the director (of the sail) to look into the details... I will be more than happy to have Dhoni as brand ambassador," Union Minister Ram Vilas Paswan said during his two-day visit to Jharkhand that ended on Wednesday.

Jharkand Chief Minister Shibu Soren said "Dhoni is our pride and would be glad to involve him in the state's sports promotional activities".

Heading: Asif to plead his dope case on Oct 11 - Indian Express
Content:
The Australian media on Thursday said Indian skipper Anil Kumble's performance would have a strong bearing on the outcome on the four-match Test series between the two countries, beginning with the first Test in Bangalore on October 9.

"The leg-spinning Kumble is an astute, humble and skillful cricketer who will have a major role to play in the battle for the Border-Gavaskar Trophy," 'Daily Telegraph' said in its report.

Kumble, who will turn 38 next month, is under increasing pressure from ODI and Twenty20 captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni's supporters to step down and hand over the reins to the dynamic wicket-keeper but the report highlighted Dhoni's batting failure in Australia last summer while crediting the leg-spinner's feat.

"Dhoni can also be a batting hurricane but he failed to flatten Australia last summer, scoring just 141 runs at 17.62 while Kumble, the third-highest wicket-taker in Test history, responded with 20 scalps in an epic series.

"Dhoni has impressed some officials with his deeds in the Twenty20 and the 50-over game, but others are wary of over-burdening a man who had to sit out the entire mid-year Test series against Sri Lanka because of fatigue," the report read.

Dhoni, though, has played down the suggestions, saying it makes no sense.

"I've never given too much thought to these things. There's no point. I'm just happy to be playing the game, playing for the country and enjoying every moment," he said on Thursday.

Heading: 'Region has nothing to do with winning medals' - Indian Express
Content:
Tainted Pakistani pacer Mohammad Asif's efforts to get a fresh date of hearing finally paid off with the drugs inquiry tribunal of the Indian Premier League asking him to plead his dope violation case on October 11.

Asif had complained that he was frustrated with the delay in the IPL tribunal giving him a hearing so that he could clear himself of the doping charges.

"We have got a mail from the IPL saying that the hearing would take place on October 11 and we have been directed to appear in person with full documentation," Shahid Karim, the lawyer for Asif said.

He said that sports medicine and doping specialist, Dr Graham would accompany them for the hearing as he had played an important role in preparing the defense for the pacer.

Asif is presently suspended from playing cricket by the Pakistan cricket Board after he tested positive for a banned substance during doping tests conducted during the IPL semi finals in late May.

His "B" sample test also showed the same banned substance but there was a difference in the quantity of the substance found in his sample.

The Board has said that it would not be interfering in the case as the dope test came positive in a foreign country and Asif would have to fight his case according to their laws.

The IPL has constituted a drugs inquiry tribunal headed by a sports medicine and doping specialist and also includes former Indian captain, Sunil Gavaskar.

Asif who is presently in Karachi said he was confident of winning his case as there were some technical issues with the way the tests were conducted that would be placed before the IPL tribunal.

"I have never used banned substances in my life so I am confident that I will be cleared of this slur that has badly damaged my career," Asif said.

The IPL tribunal had earlier given August 30 as a date for hearing but Asif and his lawyer had requested for a fresh date because of shortage of time.

Heading: Holders Dempo will be the team to beat in I-League - Indian Express
Content:
Olympic wrestling bronze medal winner Sushil Kumar says intense practice, a bit of luck and God's grace help athletes win laurels.

"Practice coupled with a bit of luck and God's grace help in winning medals irrespective of the region one hails from," he told reporters in Madurai on Wednesday evening at a felicitation organised by a private engineering college.

Replying to a question on why sportspersons from Punjab and Haryana region won more medals, he pointed out that former sprint queen P T Usha, Leander Paes and Mahesh Bhupathi had also won medals. "Region does not have anything to do in wining medals for any sports."

Sushil said Delhi and Haryana had a sports policy and sports had been made compulsory in schools and this could be followed in other states. Sushil said he was willing to start an academy to promote wrestling in rural areas.

Describing cricket as a game with mass support and following, he said media played an important role in promoting the game. But other sports like football, volleyball and wrestling did not get such support, he added.

He said he was now focussing on the 2010 Delhi Commonwealth Games and the 2012 London Olympics.

Heading: Raikkonen desperate for another win - Indian Express
Content:
Buoyed by their progress to the AFC Cup semi-finals, Dempo once again look the team to beat when the second edition of the I-League gets underway tomorrow.

The team, which had been playing and preying together for a number of seasons, have risen gradually ever since they went down in 2000. But now that they are at the top, they are not going to let go of that mantle easily.

Armando Colaco's boys have won the title twice in the last two seasons - in 2006 when it was the National Football League and last year after it was re-christened the I-League - and would be now looking for a hat-trick when they start their campaign against JCT in Goa on Sunday.

Earlier, Dempo won the then National Football League consecutively in 2003 and 2004. East Bengal coach Subhas Bhowmick had also dreamt of a similar feat they could never achieve it. They finished a disappointing sixth last season and at one point had fetched just eight points from the first 12 matches before Manoranjan Bhattacharya turned the tide.

Bhattacharya have been replaced by India assistant coach Stanley Rozario after a third-place finish in the IFA Premier Division League.

With India players like Sunil Chettri, Subrata Pal, Renedy Singh, Mehrajuddin Wadao and Syed Rahim Nabi in the squad, the fans would be hoping for the team to come good this time around.

It is the red-and-gold brigade who set the ball rolling when they take on debutantes Chirag United in the opener at the Barasat Stadium.

The same day, Sporting Clube de Goa take on Vasco at Goa's Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium. Vasco are back in the top flight after going down in the 2004-05 season.

Both teams have undergone a change of coach. Vasco replaced Roberto Fernandes, the man who guided them to the I-League, with Elvis J Goes, while Vishwas Gaonkar taking charge of Sporting Clube de Goa in place of Clifford Chukwama.

Chukwama and Fernandes though still figure in the teams' scheme of things but the baton seems to have changed. How that will reflect in the teams' performance will be clear when the league comes to an end in April next year.

Failure of the All India Football Federation to make the league a pan-India affair even after 12 years of its inception means that teams from Goa, Kolkata and Mumbai will once again dominate the title contention, with JCT being the sole representative from the North.

But things are not going well for the Phagwara side with the AIFF's commercial entity criteria putting the team in a spot of bother. The club has not been able to pay the players' wages and has only made part payments to tone down the growing concern. They face defending champions Dempo in their opening encounter in Goa on Sunday.

Churchill Brothers, under a certain Karim Bencherifa, has made life difficult for Dempo and others and the league went down to the wire.

But things are not going well following the Moroccan's departure to Mohun Bagan. Nigerian World Cupper Emeka Euzego's tough talks didn't go down well leading to friction in the side. His sacking perhaps may get things back on track but in Okolie Odafa, they have yet another problem.

The Nigerian's goalscoring prowess is well known but has been found out in recent matches. He looked a pale shadow of himself in the Durand Cup and ought to improve his work ethic if the team is to make a serious bid for the title.

Mohun Bagan, under Bencherifa, have retained the Kolkata league and are now awaiting the big test. Bhaichung Bhutia and Jose barreto, despite their age, packs quite a punch. But over-dependence on the two could prove to be their undoing.

Mohammedan Sporting, the other team to make a re-entry to the elite league, would be boosted by their strong second-place showing in the IFA league.

But Shabbir Ali's boys need to grow up fast to counter the big boys. Done in by the AIFF's transfer deadline which got over before the second division I-League finished, Mohammedan Sporting along with debutantes Mumbai FC, Vasco and Chirag United were left struggling to get the right kind of players.

At a stage where the fittest only survive, they would be hard put not to go down after having worked so hard to reach the top flight.

Durand Cup champions Mahindra United look the best bet to challenge Dempo's authority. Edeh Chidi's inclusion have done them a world of good and apart from retaining Steven Dias and NP Pradeep, coach Derrick Pereira further boosted his midfield with Paresh Shivalkar.

His former club, Air India, though have a tough job to stay afloat. Their biggest plus in recent years was the Cooperage. But with infrastructural problems plaguing the stadium, the ground could be de-listed from the I-League venue and could pose the biggest problem for Bimal Ghosh, who have lost several first team regulars in the transfer market.
