Passing verdict on a petition filed by Nalini's counsel, Justice S Nagamuthu accepted the petitioner's contention that the Advisory Board of Vellore Special Prison for Women did not go through all relevant matter while preparing its report.

Holding that members of the board including its chairman were not informed about the meeting; that the district collector presided over the meeting without the authority of the law; and that all parameters enumerated in Prison Rules were not taken note of by the board, Justice Nagamuthu pulled up the authorities stating, "from the records available, what I could gather is that the entire exercise has been treated only as an empty formality and no serious concern was ever shown by the authorities to validly conduct the meeting and to seriously consider the issues in accordance with law."

However, the court held that the petitioners did not have any "vested right" to demand premature release either under Article 161 or under the provisions of the Code, but added, "they have got a right to demand that their cases be considered for premature release if they satisfy the requirements of the Tamil Nadu Prison Rules."

Citing several cases in the past, Justice Nagamuthu said that there cannot be any restriction to the power vested in the Governor under Article 161 of the Constitution as well as the power of the state Government under sections 433 and 433 (A) of the CrPC from providing further remission to Nalini on the grounds that she already received one when her death sentence was commuted to life.

Impleading himself in the case, Subramanian Swamy of the Janata Party had opposed considering Nalini's case for reconsideration on the grounds that she had already received one remission.

The court directed that a validly constituted prison advisory board reconsider the matter in accordance with the law and the state Government take an appropriate decision on the report.

In all, Nalini has spent over 17 years in the Special Prison for Women, Vellore. Though awarded death, her sentence was commuted to life in prison after the intervention of Rajiv Gandhi's widow and Congress president Sonia Gandhi.

Heading: Portraits of Terror - Indian Express
Content:
The Pay Panel issue raised by the Armed Forces is heading for a deadlock with the three services making it clear that revised pay scales will not be implemented unless anomalies are addressed even as the Defence Ministry has issued memos to pay cells of the services directing them to draw up salaries as per the Government directives.

The issue was after the Finance Ministry rejected two key demands of the Armed Forces to bring Lt Col level officers in the highest pay band and to include Lt Gen level officers in the newly created Higher Administrative Grade (HAG) pay band. Last week, Defence Minister A K Antony had personally raised the issues with the Finance Ministry in the form of a detailed letter highlighting the demands of the Armed Forces to address "core issues" of the revised scales.

Trying to find a way out of the deadlock, Antony has once again written to the Prime Minister asking for his personal intervention. The letter, sources said, was sent to the PMO on Tuesday.

Sources said Antony has written that while some demands have been met by the Finance Ministry, the two issues of Lt Cols' and Lt Gens' pay scales have not been accepted. "The letter says the PM may like to intervene and direct the Finance Ministry to re-examine the matter," a senior official said.

This comes even as it has come to light that the accounting departments of the three Armed Forces have not drawn up pay rolls for October as per the new recommendations. This, after the Defence Ministry issued a memo last week saying the revised scales be implemented from next month as anomalies could be addressed at a later date.

The tussle over pay has already created a fissure in the Armed Forces, especially within the Personnel Below Officer Rank (PBOR) cadre, who were expecting their new salaries and arrears before Diwali. The main contention of PBORs is that the revised Pay Panel for them be implemented as all issues regarding their salary structures have been accepted.

Heading: Karnataka attacks Delhi team as ‘agents of UPA’ - Indian Express
Content:
•Mohd Sadiq Israr Sheikh, 32

Identified as the co-founder of the Indian Mujahideen, he is originally from Sanjarpur in Azamgarh, UP. Sadiq is reported to be the man who "controlled" New Delhi's serial blasts through key executor Atif who was killed in the Jamia Nagar encounter. Sadiq had settled in Mumbai's Cheetah Camp area, a predominantly Muslim slum. "He worked in Mumbai as a programme engineer in an electronics company," said Joint Commissioner of Police Rakesh Maria, describing him as the "brain behind footsoldiers like Atif". Sadiq received "training in terror activities from a hostile country" on two occasions.

•Mohammed Ansar Sheikh, 31

A native of Sanjarpur in Azamgarh, Ansar is a software engineer. He was living in Cheetah Camp near Trombay for several months. Initial investigations point to his involvement in the Indian Mujahideen as the man who provided software knowledge to the terror module. His arrest is crucial for the investigation into the terror e-mails sent by hacking unsecured WiFi networks in the city. He was arrested from Chembur.

•Afzal Mutalib Usmani, 32

Also hailed from Azamgarh. Was reportedly responsible for the theft of four cars from Navi Mumbai, which were used in the Ahmedabad and Surat attacks. Arrested from Mhow in UP, Afzal is also alleged to have placed the explosive-laden vehicles at Ahmedabad's Civil Hospital and Bazar Peth. He has a crime record — the first case against him was an attempt to murder in 1996, at Shivaji Nagar police station, Mumbai. He is also wanted in a MCOCA case where he is charged with being an associate of the Fazl-ul-Rehman gang.

•Mohammed Zakir Sheikh, 28

Originally from Azamgarh, Zakir, a scrap deal, had settled down in Bhiwandi. He is reported to have received training outside the country in 2004, before he returned to Azamgarh. He later moved to Bhiwandi, on the outskirts of Mumbai, in Thane district, where he set up a scrap dealing business that took him to Surat often. He is alleged to have been in the team which conducted a recce in Gujarat, and helped the module in planting bombs at various locations. He was picked up from Bhiwandi on Tuesday night.

•Mohammed Arif Shaikh, 28

A native of Sanjarpur in Azamgarh, Arif moved to Mumbra a few years ago and started working as an electrician. Crime Branch officials have found that his expertise was in fabrication. He is suspected to be the man who developed the electric circuits used in the blasts in Ahmedabad and Surat. He received training in the preparation of bombs and specialises in preparing electronic circuits. He is reported to have prepared the circuits used in various blasts in the country since 2005. He was arrested from Kurla on Tuesday night.

Others wanted

•Roshan Khan

Hailing from Karnataka, Roshan Khan is believed to be "one of the founding members" of the Indian Mujhaideen. While the Crime Branch does not absolve Abdus Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer, Maria said Roshan Khan is high up in the Indian Mujaideen hierarchy along with Sadiq. The explosives found in Sewree also point to Roshan Khan.

•Ameer Razaq

Additional Commissioner of Police (Crime Branch) Deven Bharti said Sadiq was in constant touch with a man in Pakistan named Ameer Razaq, who appears to be controlling the group. "We have sufficient proof including telephone details to prove that he is handling the operation from Pakistan," said Bharti.

Heading: SEZ deadlock: CPI demands new policy - Indian Express
Content:
While the attacks on churches may have subsided in Karnataka, the political fallout is still being played out with the BJP-led state Government trading charges with the central team of observers sent to assess the situation in the trouble-torn state. Even as the two member team from the Home Ministry led by M L Kumawat, Special Secretary (Internal Security) criticised the state Government over the inadequate measures taken to protect churches, the state Government in turn has accused them of being agents of the UPA.

The two-member team after its visit to Mangalore and Udupi on Tuesday said the state had failed to maintain peace and reiterated in Bangalore on Wednesday that strong government action could have prevented the unfortunate train of events. "There seems to be a similarity in modus operandi in attacks on churches in Mangalore and Udupi and also in Bangalore, the government should take stringent action," Kumawat said.

The BJP Government reacted sharply with Law Minister S Suresh Kumar saying that, "their role is to report facts and what they saw and submit a report to the Centre. They cannot sit in judgement and pass it too". Kumar accused the UPA of trying to use the incidents of church attacks as a "political dice" against the BJP Government. "It is an unprecedented and unheard of development in a federal structure. Instead of helping the state in controlling the situation, the team has been making political statements that will vitiate peace," he said.

The B S Yeddyurappa-led BJP Government in Karnataka had initially shown little urgency to deal with the situation head on and preferred to blame conversion activities of Christian sects for the attacks rather than bringing to book the attackers from the Hindu right wing or ensure protection to churches.

Heading: Vienna past, India and China talk cooperation - Indian Express
Content:
The CPI(M)-led Left Government in Kerala has failed to break the deadlock over permitting special economic zones (SEZs) in the private sector after the CPI, a key ally in the Government, demanded a new legislation to protect the larger interests of the state and workers.

The CPI's decision, silently supported by Chief Minister V S Achuthanandan, has jeopardised the official CPI(M) faction's plan to rush through 10 SEZ applications. Last week, the LDF committee had agreed to allow SEZs in Kerala with 10 conditions. To avoid delay, the front had decided not to go for new legislation, instead preferring an SEZ policy. Curiously, CPI representatives in the LDF did not raise any protest against the front's decision.

However, things went into a tailspin after a section of CPI leaders revolted against the Left move to allow SEZs without legislation and concrete framework. Embarrassing the LDF, leaders of CPI's trade union arm All India Trade Union Congress and youth outfit All India Youth Federation declared they would stage agitations against SEZs and demanded that the party oppose the move to allow SEZs without clear policies. They also pointed out that the party sub-committee on SEZs had recommended special legislation, among other things. The impasse in the party over SEZ policy created an impression that the CPI had given in to the plan of the Pinarayi faction in the CPI(M).

As cracks developed in the party, the CPI was forced to take a firm stand on the demand for a special SEZ legislation. At Wednesday's Cabinet meeting, CPI ministers demanded that the SEZ applications be send for the Centre's approval only after bringing in necessary legislation. If that was not possible, the party sought issuance of a special ordinance. Hence, a final decision on SEZs was shelved.

AITUC State Secretary Kanam Rajendran told The Indian Express that the Left Government should not go for SEZs in a hurry, when even the UPA Goverment was mulling amendments in the SEZ Act, 2005. "The prevailing SEZ policy of the state was formulated by the Congress in 2003. That policy had taken little precautions to ensure the rights of workers. It had suggested flexible labour laws, which were detrimental for the state," he said. He said his union was against SEZs, which, according to him, were designed to protect the interests of capitalists only. It may be noted that the CPI had come out openly against the SEZs after maintaining silence in the last LDF coordination committee meeting, which gave the nod for SEZs. The CPI stand gave a breather to Achuthanandan, whose major demands, including Government equity in private SEZs, were rejected by the party.

Meanwhile, the Congress-led Opposition also sought adequate legislation before permitting SEZs. "The CPI(M) has been showing undue haste to get the SEZs sanctioned," said P P Thankachan, convener of the United Democratic Front.

Heading: SC: right to property now a human right - Indian Express
Content:
After the annoying 24 hours before the NSG clearance that saw India issue demarches to China which was stalling a consensus in Vienna, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on Wednesday sought to put the bitterness behind and agreed to start discussions on civilian nuclear cooperation between the two countries during his 45-minute meeting with Chinese Premier Wen Jiabao.

China, it may be recalled, had supplied fuel for Tarapur in the 1980s. Thereafter there has been little cooperation between the two countries though Singh and Wen had agreed in January to have DAE head Anil Kakodkar visit China for preliminary talks with his counterpart. Though Beijing never gave dates for the visit, sources said, this seemed a possibility now, especially after Wednesday's conversation.

"Let us be clear, China was in the end a part of the consensus at the NSG. And if China had blocked it, there would have been no consensus. So that issue is now behind us. Both leaders today discussed future civilian nuclear cooperation for which further discussions will take place," said Foreign Secretary Shivshankar Menon after the meeting between the two leaders.

Both countries have big plans to expand their civil nuclear industry and in days to come are expected to emerge as key global players in this sector. Both leaders discussed the similarities in their approach to channelise development and agreed to build on that understanding. In fact, Wen handed over a book which had published his speech on inclusive development and Singh's speech at Cambridge on inclusive globalisation.

While India has already started conversation with countries like China on civil nuclear cooperation, the US Congress is yet to give its final approval. In fact, when World Bank president Robert Zoellick, who called on Singh on Wednesday, started his meeting by felicitating him on the passage of the agreement through the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, the PM replied that he would rather wait till the US Congress gives its approval.

The Prime Minister has good reason for his scepticism. While the US Senate appears set to clear the Indo-US nuclear cooperation agreement after the approval of its foreign relations committee on Tuesday, there are issues in the approval statement of the committee which would either have to be reconciled or addressed in Bush's signing statement where he can choose to differ with the Congress, just as he did when the Hyde Act was passed.

It's learnt that National Security Advisor M K Narayanan, PM's Special envoy Shyam Saran and Foreign Secretary Shivshankar Menon are leaving for US on Wednesday night for discussions in Washington ahead of PM's arrival on Thursday.

The key to any success on this front is to prompt some forward movement at the House of Representatives for which the Bush Administration is in hectic talks with House International Relations Committee head and a prominent naysayer of the agreement Howard Berman.

Confirming this, Lynne Weil, a Committee spokesperson told The Indian Express: "Congressman Berman is in consultations with the Administration and is considering the various options before him."

It's learnt that different proposals were being discussed with Berman to find a way out of the deadlock which has been further complicated by the discussions on the continuing resolution for a $700 billion bailout package. The hope is that the India agreement can be voted alongside this package, for which a decision is expected in the House by Wednesday night.

However, sources said, Berman continues to make proposals that are certain deal-breakers like including the letter from the State Department in the resolution. The State Department opposed this saying it was only an explanatory note that could not be added to the resolution.

Heading: Khairlanji Dalit killings: six get death, two sentenced to life - Indian Express
Content:
Taking a cue from courts in the US and UK, the Supreme Court has taken a view that the right to property is now a human right.

Referring to several landmark decisions passed on the law of adverse possession of property, the Bench comprising Justices Dalveer Bhandari and H S Bedi noted, "The right of property is now considered to be not only a constitutional or statutory right but also a human right." Quoting from a decision passed by an English court, the Bench said, "Human rights have been historically considered in the realm of individual rights such as right to health, right to livelihood, right to shelter and employment, etc. But now human rights are gaining a multifaceted dimension. Right to property is also considered very much a part of the new dimension."

"Therefore, even claim of adverse possession has to be read in that context," the apex court remarked taking an 'activist approach' similar to the English courts. "But what is commendable is that the dimensions of human rights have widened so much that now property dispute issues are also being raised within the contours of human rights," Justice Bhandari, writing the judgement, said.

The bench said the Central Government should "seriously consider" a change in law to prevent squatters from dishonestly enjoying property. "There is an urgent need of a fresh look regarding the law on adverse possession. We recommend the Centre seriously consider and make suitable changes in the law of adverse possession," it ruled while dealing with a provision of law which requires that the burden of proof lies on owners to show that they have the title to and have been in possession of the property and were dispossessed within a period of 12 years from the date of filing the suit.

Observing that the law of adverse possession "which ousts an owner on the basis of inaction within limitation is irrational, illogical and wholly disproportionate," the Bench dismissed an appeal filed by a person who had illegally taken possession of a land from its original owner. "The law as it exists is extremely harsh for the true owner and a windfall for a dishonest person who had illegally taken possession of the property of the true owner," the court said, trying to comprehend as to why such a law "should place a premium on dishonesty by legitimising possession of a rank trespasser and compelling the owner to lose his possession only because of his inaction in taking back the possession within limitation."

Heading: POTA failed, need strong terror law: Rahul - Indian Express
Content:
Two years after four members of a Dalit family were murdered at Khairlanji village in Maharashtra, a fast-track court here today sentenced six of the accused to death, and life imprisonment for two others.

In all, 11 people were named as accused in the case probed by the CBI. Three of them were acquitted earlier for lack of evidence.

While Gopal Binjewar and Shishupal Dhande were sentenced to life imprisonment today, Sakru Binjewar (Gopal's father), Vishwanath Dhande, Shatrughna and Ramu Dhande (first cousins), and Jagdish and Prabhakar Mandlekar (uncle-nephew) were sentenced to death.

On September 15, Judge S S Das had convicted the eight accused, but acquitted them of charges under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. The acquittal under the ST/SC Act drew strong reactions from Dalit organisations which demanded a re-trial.

But most of the Dalit organisations and leaders welcomed the sentence today, saying they were pleased with the CBI and Special Public Prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam.

The case dates back to September 29, 2006, when four Dalits — Surekha Bhaiyyalal Bhotmange, her daughter Priyanka and sons Sudhir and Roshan — were beaten to death over a land dispute in Khairlanji. The brutality of the act had sent shockwaves across Maharashtra, and led to violent protests.

Heading: Nafed in the red, seeks govt bailout - Indian Express
Content:
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday said that the country needed a tough anti-terror law, but not a "failed" statute like POTA. "There should be a strong law (to deal with terror). A powerful law, not a failed law. POTA is a failed law," the 38-year-old scion of the Nehru-Gandhi family told reporters after a three-day visit to Punjab.

"When POTA was in operation, Parliament was attacked. We almost lost our MPs, Home Minister and the Prime Minister. When it was in operation, Kandahar took place," the Congress general secretary said, adding "fighting terrorism requires political will".

Praising Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, he said he had "full faith" in him and his handling of nuclear and economic issues.

Heading: Yoga crosses new borders, over 100 prisoners in Yerawada jail turn trainers - Indian Express
Content:
In the backdrop of the global credit crunch sparking fears of a financial meltdown in the country, the public sector behemoth National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation (NAFED) has pressed the panic button and sought a government bailout package.

After registering a profit of Rs 1.77 crore in 2006-07, Nafed on Wednesday announced a net loss of Rs 56.69 crore in 2007-08. In fact, the turnover of the federation has fallen from over Rs 6,381 crore in 2006-07 to a little under Rs 4,707 crore in 2007-08. "Favourable consideration of our request by the Central Registrar for special credit limit to Nafed would go a long way in strengthening the present financial position of the federation," said Nafed chairman Bijender Singh while announcing the results at the annual general meeting in the capital. He said Nafed was exploring all possibilities to come out of the crisis including seeking soft loans from financial institutions.

Nafed has been reeling under a tremendous financial crisis after it failed to recover about Rs 1,000 crore from about 30 private companies to which it had extended advances during 2004-06 for import of material. Nafed, which focused on procurement and trade of agricultural commodities, had incurred the current loss due to the huge interest liability on account of outstanding loans. Sources said the federation's annual earnings were less than its interest liability on the defaulted loans. "The annual interest payments for those default loans are eating away our annual earnings. It is very difficult to pay over Rs 100 crore annually as interest on our outstanding loan amount," said a source present at the meeting. The situation is so serious that even if the Government extends an interest-free loan to it, Nafed may take at least 10 years to recover from the crisis in the absence of recovery of advances it had extended to the private companies. The federation has decided to abandon this scheme of extending loans to private companies.

Meanwhile, with about half a dozen defaulters who owe Nafed approximately Rs 100 crore each, the federation is trying to recover this amount.

Incidentally, the Delhi High Court had issued notices to the Union Government and Nafed in 2005 on a PIL accusing the cooperative body of giving bank guarantees or extending loans to "black listed" companies and individuals for conducting their export-import business.

Heading: Post-Govt waiver, loan recoveries in Punjab rural banks take a hit - Indian Express
Content:
This is as unlikely a bunch of aspiring yoga teachers as one can expect — even though Rolf Ziegler and Martin Leen, both from Ireland, Kisan Mazgaokar from Mumbai and Ram Sonawane from Pune have been trained under the Hardwar-based Patanjali Yog Samiti headed by 'celebrity guru' Baba Ramdev. What makes them stand apart from other serene and meditative health experts is that they are part of an exclusive club of 110 trainers who also happen to be inmates of Yerawada Central Prison.

On Wednesday, when these newly anointed yoga teachers chanted the oath to pass on their skills to fellow inmates and later to their brethren back home, it created history within the high walls of Yerawada, where Mahatma Gandhi signed the Poona pact with Dr B R Ambedkar this very day in 1932.

Called upshikshaks (assistant yoga teachers), these prisoners started training 45 days ago in seven forms of Pranayam — Bhastrika, Kapalbhati, Baahya, Anulom-Vilom, Bhramari, Udgeeth and Ujjayi — as well as other aasanas. While many began training as a good way to de-stress and improve their health, somewhere along the line they discovered a new confidence and passion. And now that they've pledged before their trainers from Patanjali that they will introduce the joys of yoga to all the remaining 3,363 inmates of Yerawada jail. In a few days they will be issued identity cards and certificates.

"I feel more energetic, more focused and determined to change my life and help other people," said Ziegler, who discovered yoga for the first time in prison. Leen, who has been jailed for the last four years and had been practicing aasanas, added that Pranayam has helped him "expel bad energies and feel recharged". Both Irishmen are serving life terms for drug trafficking.

Equally enthused is Satish Sarode. He suffered a heart attack some years ago and also suffers from severe backaches, but now feels that he has fresh lease of life. "I will be taking back these skills to my village when released. I will be respected as a yoga teacher," said Sarode, also serving a life sentence.

"This is just the beginning. It is our pilot project before rolling it out across all major prisons in the country, "said Sapna Pednekar, founder member of Patanjali. "Next, we want to pursue a similar programme at the Sabarmati jail in Gujarat," added Hari Shah, a leading member of the Hardwar-based group.

According to Suresh Jadhav, Namdeo Ingle and J Vasekar who spent many hours each day for the past 45 days in the jail, the prison experience has given them a new perspective on what yoga can achieve. "They were a disciplined lot, determined to learn yoga and trained for over three hours every day. In fact, some of them showed more dedication than many others we have trained from other walks of life," said Vasekar.

Rajendra Dhamne, superintendent, Yerawada Central Prison, has directed this band of new teachers to form small groups and teach yoga to as many inmates as possible. "They have the task of imparting these teachings to other inmates, and that will be the true success of this project," he said.

Dhamne now wants to take yoga to the female inmates of the jail. "We have 300 inmates there and we will soon start training them," he said.

Heading: ‘Indo-US war game to be strictly bilateral’ - Indian Express
Content:
While the Rs 71,000-crore debt waiver scheme announced by the Central Government has failed to bring any major relief for Punjab farmers, the pinch is now being felt by rural cooperative banks in the state. From a healthy 95 per cent crop loan recovery rate, recoveries have plunged to around 50-56 per cent since the beginning of this year, first in anticipation and later announcement of the waiver.

Worse, the default is expected to plunge further when the payment for the current kharif crops becomes due from January.

"From a good over 95 per cent, crop loan recoveries by cooperative banks this year have fallen by almost half to around 50-56 per cent as the farmers saw a waiver coming from the beginning of this year. However, the total impact of the debt waiver after its implementation in June this year will only be known when the payment period for the current kharif crop begins in January next year," says Punjab Financial Commissioner Cooperation Kusumjit Sidhu.

But the good track record has not gone unrewarded. The cooperative banks of both Punjab and Haryana (recovery rate of over 85 per cent) will be flushed with funds this year with the highest share of Rs 5,000 crore out of total target of Rs 22,000 crore to be pumped into short-term refinance by the National Bank of Agriculture and Rural Development (Nabard) making its way into the two states this year.

"While the debt relief comes as a one-time settlement, the good recovery states bag a major proportion of agricultural credit year after year. Also, this credit limit grows by 10-15 per cent per year. So, both the states stand to gain the highest quantum of funds out of the total target of Rs 22,000 crore," says V Ramakrishna Rao, Chief General Manager, Nabard, Punjab and Haryana Regional Office.

Post-loan waiver, the focus of banks now is on extending loans to newly eligible farmers. But the process is fraught with difficulties as some accounts are several years old and defaulters are untraceable. State-level committees are monitoring the process of listing farmers whose accounts have been cleaned by the debt waiver scheme but so far a very insignificant number of such cases have been listed.

Meanwhile, the rural cooperative banking system of the two states is being overhauled after signing of MoUs between Nabard and the state governments as per the recommendations of the Vaidyanathan Committee Report.

While an estimated Rs 500 crore has been assessed as losses for cleaning the balance-sheets of Haryana's rural cooperative banks, the process of estimating the losses sitting on balance-sheets of Punjab's rural cooperative banks has been initiated after signing of an MoU in January this year. "By next year cooperative banking system in these states will come at par with commercial banking system," adds Rao.

Heading: Attack on leader strains Hurriyat unity - Indian Express
Content: Defence Minister A K Antony has said that a policy decision has been taken to not invite more countries to the annual Indo-US Malabar series of naval exercises, adding that last year's multi-national war game was an "exception". Asserting that the Malabar war game will strictly be a bilateral event, the minister said: "Last year, instead of an Indo-US bilateral exercise, a multilateral exercise took place. We have taken a policy decision that it will be a bilateral exercise (from now on)... similar to what has been happening for the last 16 years."  Last year's Malabar exercise, in which five countries including the US, Japan, Singapore and Australia took part, had come under criticism from various quarters including the Left parties who alleged that it was aimed towards creating a regional military bloc.

Heading: Cong list of 34 UP seats stumps SP - Indian Express
Content:
While they may be trying to whip up a fresh azadi groundswell, separatists in Kashmir are struggling with unity in their ranks.

The grenade attack on the residence of the Hurriyat Coordination Committee member Maulana Showkat Ahmad has put the severest strain so far on the newly forged separatist coalition, with JKLF supremo Yasin Malik saying that his outfit would "independently" investigate it and then take action. "Whether it is a state or any group, we will publicly expose the culprits once we find them," Malik said at a hastily called press conference here on Wednesday.

He added that the Hizbul Muslimeen, the group which owned responsibility for the attack, lacked conscience and courage. "This group of impostors cannot browbeat us," Malik said. In a hint at political adversaries, he added that if the hand of some other outfit is revealed, the JKLF would not take it lying down. "Some people who indulge in these dirty actions have already been identified in past, but we tolerated it in the larger interest of the Kashmir cause. This time we have decided we will not take it any longer."

Maulana Showkat, a moderate head of the puritanical religious group Jamiat Ahle Hadees, is close to Malik and is a member of the separatist coordination committee given the charge of chalking out protest programmes after the Amarnath land row. One of the largest religious organisations in the Valley, the Ahle Hadees owns around 500 mosques and claims a membership of seven lakh people.

Maulana Showkat however had recently drawn severe censure for being the only religious leader in Valley to have exhibited a soft spot for former governor S K Sinha. Showkat had not only backed Sinha in the setting up of a Sharda Peeth University in Valley but also sought his help in the establishment of an Islamic university in the state. Malik has also been pilloried by hardline separatists before for his "Gandhian" mode of struggle.

The attack on Showkat is being seen as a fallout of the divide over the method of leading the secessionist surge in the Valley, and while Malik may have stayed well short of finger-pointing, his outburst brought into sharp relief this rift.

Hurriyat hawk Syed Ali Shah Geelani, however, played down the incident. "We have ideological differences but we have resolved them in the larger interest of the movement. Nothing can drive us apart," he told The Indian Express.

According to him, the attack on Showkat's residence was the handiwork of government agencies. "India has the resources, media to assault us from many sides. But we are conscious of this and will, God willing, successfully negotiate these challenges."

Heading: HC to hear ITC’s plea against ban on smoking on Sept 30 - Indian Express
Content:
With the Congress handing over a list of 34 seats it wants to contest in Uttar Pradesh, the SP is in a quandary over stitching an alliance with the national party to counter Mayawati's rise in the state.

What has added to the SP's worries is the adamant attitude of the Congress in claiming seats held by the SP while conceding none of its seats. Senior party leaders wonder whether the party can accommodate the Congress in its scheme of things when the party chief has instructed its negotiators to concede less than half the seats being demanded.

In the last two rounds of negotiations, the SP has agreed to leave all 12 seats demanded by the Congress — Rae Bareli, Amethi, Varanasi, Hapur, Mathura, Bansgaon, Aligarh, Dharaura and Kanpur, held by the Congress, along with Khurja, Domariaganj and Bareilly, where the Congress vote share was more than the SP. It is the remaining seats, many of which are held by the SP, that have become a bone of contention.

While the Congress wants Rampur, Farrukhabad and Pratapgarh seats for its state leaders Noor Bano, Salman Khursheed and Ratna Singh respectively, it has also set its eyes on Muradabad in western UP, Banda and Jhansi in Bundelkhand, and Salempur and Padrauna in East UP, most of which are held by the SP.

The Congress also wants to contest from Sultanpur near the Gandhi family bastions of Rae Bareli and Amethi, though showing willingness for a friendly fight in Pratapgarh.

Senior SP leaders said SP negotiators Amar Singh and Ram Gopal Yadav had been instructed by party chief Mulayam Singh Yadav to concede only about 15 seats to the Congress. At best, half a dozen more seats could be conceded, they added.

Both the parties would sit again to finalise their seat-sharing agreement later this week, said sources.

Heading: Kandhamal burns under nose of police - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court will hear Indian Tobacco Company (ITC) Ltd's petition challenging Government's notification of banning smoking in private offices and other establishments on September 30.

A bench headed by Justice Vikramjit Sen deferred the hearing after Centre conten-ded that a case related to the issue is coming before Supreme Court on September 29.

Besides ITC, two other petitioners, including Indian Hotels Association, have also moved separate pleas challenging the May 2008 notification issued by the Union Health Ministry to implement smoke-free rules from October 2 in all public places, including restaurants, hotels, pubs and discotheques.

Representatives of the hotel industry had approached the ministry last week asking for various exemptions in the implementation of the new rule, claiming that they would approach the court if their demands were not met.

The Federation of Hotel and Restaurant Association of India, representing its case to the ministry, spoke against having separate enclosures, saying that it would spoil their decor. The ministry, however, did not budge from its position.

"Though we support the no-smoking cause ourselves, it's a service-oriented industry and smokers cannot be segregated by way of chambers. At the most we will create a lounge for smokers. Most of the rules are already adhered to but having full-height walls for smokers is not acceptable," said Rajindera Kumar, president of the Hotel and Restaurant Association, Northern India.

Considering the ill effects of passive smoking for those serving in segregated areas, the ministry had stipulated spaces for smokers should either be made self-service zones or that no service should be allowed. The representatives of the hotel industry say that this is not possible, as it will hit their revenue.

Heading: Global architects will compete to design 309-ft Shivaji statue - Indian Express
Content:
"My husband Freedom Nayak had gone to a church 30 km away on August 23. He never returned. We found his charred remains in Kakamaha forest a few days ago. My son recognized his father's body from his spectacles black cap. How can I return home now?"

Nalini Nayak has lost her husband, and her home in Breka village in Tikabali block of Orissa's Kandhamal district was reduced to a heap of ashes by a mob that attacked and set ablaze all Christian dwellings in the area.

A whole month after the killing of VHP leader Laxmanananda Saraswati and four others, Kandhamal continues to burn, giving a lie to Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik's claims that the "situation is improving", with only "stray cases of sporadic violence".

Here's what is happening on ground zero of the clashes, according to statistics provided by Patnaik's own government.

At least 26 people have been killed, and 2,892 houses and 10 government buildings have been either burnt or severely damaged. One hundred and forty-five Christian buildings have been damaged — 139 of them are churches and prayer houses, the rest hostels and buildings housing NGOs and self-help groups.

Over the past 7-10 days, five people including a policeman have been murdered, and a police station attacked and razed.

September 20: Iswar Digal, a Dalit Christian of Gutingia village in Tikabali block, was reportedly hacked to death by tribals who abducted him after he came to visit his ailing father.

September 18: At least 40 Christian homes were burnt in Gunjibadi, Digi, Dharampur and Mandasaur villages in K Nuagaon and Raikia blocks.

September 17: Ten homes and a prayer hall were torched in Sunagaon, Jhiripani and Lankagad villages of Tumudibandha block.

September 16: Eight Hindu families were threatened by Christians in Makabali and Salapjodi villages of Raikia block.

September 15: The Gochhapada police station and Balandapada police outpost in Phiringia block were burnt down by an armed mob of over 500 people from Salaguda village. Special security battalion constable Bibhudhendra Biswal was shot dead by the mob protesting the arrest of 16 comrades for arson.

September 14: Eight Christian homes were torched in Digi village of Raikia block.

September 13: Three tribals were killed after a mob of 500 villagers clashed with a CRPF contingent trying to protect Christians in Kurtamgarh village of Tumudibandha block. A CRPF jawan received bullet injuries on his face.

This terrifying violence has been taking place despite an average 30-35 law-enforcement personnel watching over each of the 74 riot-affected gram panchayats in the district. Nearly 3,500 policemen and paramilitary forces personnel are currently in Kandhamal: 22 companies of CRPF, 3 companies of RAF, 24 platoons of Orissa State Armed Police, 10 sections of Armed Police Reserve, three Special Operations Group teams, and four Orissa Disaster Rapid Action Force teams.

Several senior IAS officers and eight senior IPS officers are camping in the district, apart from district collector Dr Krishan Kumar and Superintendent of Police Praveen Kumar. There are 22 Orissa Administrative Service officers as well.

"The situation is slowly coming under control," said Divisional Commissioner, Revenue, Satyabrata Sahu, posted to Kandhamal after the riots. Director General of Police Gopal Chandra Nanda said: "Don't exaggerate the cases so much. Peace is returning to Kandhamal."

But a top official of the district told The Indian Express: "We can't say the situation is normal."

Careful planning is visible behind the attacks and arson. The mob attacks on a signal—— a whistle blown by a leader. Before each strike, roads leading to the area are blocked by huge trees, preventing movement of the police. In the Gochhapada police station attack, the building had been completely destroyed by the time the police party found its way around the roadblocks.

"It's an inaccessible district and the terrain is inhospitable. It's difficult for the police to reach each of the 300 affected villages," said Satyabrata Sahu.

Oddly, no officer of the stature of Sahu is a member of the 'peace committees' formed by the government in the aftermath of the riot— ¿ the panels have only junior representatives of the state like anganwadi workers, who inspire limited confidence. More oddly, these committees are the most active in places like Khajuripada, Daringibadi and Kotgada, which have seen zero or minimal violence so far, and are either non-existent or defunct in the trouble-spots where they are needed the most.

Privately, officials say the violence shown by the Kondh tribals against Dalit Christia—s — and in some cases Hin—us — have stunned even the CRPF. In Suleswar village, Siddheswar Pradhan, a tribal Hindu, was killed only because he tried to protect a Christian family from the mob; Bikram Nayak, a former member of Tiangia Panchayat Samity, died in the same way.

Heading: U S taxpayers don’t want their money used in Wall St bailouts - Indian Express
Content:
Architects from all over the world will compete to be a part of the ambitious project to erect a statue of Shivaji in the Arabian Sea.

Conceptualised to stand four feet taller than the Statue of Liberty in New York, the blueprint for the statue has already been drawn up by the state Public Works Department (PWD). The state government has now decided to announce an international competition in which architects worldwide will be invited. The first three winners will be given prizes of Rs 2.5 lakh, Rs 2 lakh and Rs 1.5 lakh each.

The architect who wins will also get the contract and paid a percentage of the project cost as his fee.

"Any architect who has carried out work of a similar nature globally can participate. By next week we will be issuing the draft for the competition. Once that is done, the architects will be given about two months to submit their proposals, which detail the design and technology to be used," said PWD chief architect Bipin Sankhe.

As per the PWD plans, the Shivaji statue will come up a kilometre into the sea from the Marine Drive, nestled between Nariman Point and Malabar Hill on a six-acre patch of reclaimed land. The architects will have to submit detailed designs for the statue, which will stand on a pedestal and have a total height of 309 feet.

Located centrally at the base of the statue will be an amphitheatre for light and sound shows on whose periphery will be six-feet high walls with murals on Shivaji's life. Also at the base of the statue will be a cafeteria for visitors, a garden and a museum showcasing the history of the period through literature and relics.

The participating architects will have to base their designs on the recommendations of a technical committee headed by the Chief Secretary. Said Thanksy Thekkekara, Principal Secretary for the General Administration Department (GAD): "We have provided the PWD Rs 1 crore for the competitive international bidding, they will take it forward from here."

The GAD estimates a budget of Rs 100 crore for the project this year.

Heading: ...And in Congress, massive CEO salaries become target - Indian Express
Content:
Most Americans don't believe the government has responsibility for bailing out financial firms with taxpayer money, a core part of the rescue plan Congress is considering to halt the near-meltdown of American financial markets, a Los Angeles Times/Bloomberg poll has found. Reluctance to use public money to rescue private firms runs across the population, the poll found: Democrats and Republicans, high-income and low-income families alike.

Asked whether the government should use taxpayer dollars to rescue financial firms whose collapse could have adverse effects on the economy, 55% of the poll's respondents said they did not believe the government should be responsible for funding a bailout plan.

However, opinions about the bailout plan appear to be malleable, perhaps because voters are still learning about the proposal. When some of those who opposed a bailout were interviewed, several said they would reluctantly accept a bailout plan if Congress decided one was necessary.

"It sticks in my craw," said Camille Woyak, 82, a retired office worker in Appleton, Wisconsin, who said she opposed a bailout. "There should be some other solution. But I think the taxpayers are going to have to cover it. I don't know any other way out."

Other polls have found that voters want the government to do something to prevent a financial collapse, even though they don't like the idea of footing the bill.

A poll released Tuesday by the Pew Research Center for the People and the Press, for example, found that 57% of respondents think the government is doing the right thing by intervening to stabilize the economy.

What the poll says

• In the Times/Bloomberg poll, a solid majority, 62%, said they believed that insufficient government regulation was partly responsible for the financial crisis.

• As to where the blame should go, respondents were divided: 32% blamed Wall Street financial institutions, and 26% blamed the Bush administration. (Democrats tended to blame the White House; Republicans tended to blame Wall Street.)

• Asked whether the country was "generally going in the right direction" or "on the wrong track," 79% said "wrong track" and only 13% said "right direction." That exceeded the previous record of 78% who said "wrong track" in June.

• Asked which candidate could do a better job of handling the financial crisis as president next year, 48% of registered voters named Obama and 35% named McCain

Heading: FBI Looking into 4 firms at Centre of the Turmoil - Indian Express
Content:
The U S Congress wants Wall Street to feel it where it hurts: the wallet.

The stratospheric pay packages of Wall Street executives have become a lightning rod issue as Congress shapes a $700 billion bailout for financial firms. Proposals circulating on Capitol Hill vary, but they all would impose some limits or approval authority on salaries of executives whose firms seek help.

The moves in Washington mirror the popular outcry — in constituent e-mail messages and postings in the blogosphere — over the prospect of Wall Street's tarnished titans walking away with tens of millions of dollars a year while taxpayers pick up the bill.

But Wall Street, its lobbyists and trade groups are waging a feverish lobbying campaign to try to fight compensation curbs. "We support the bill, but we are opposed to provisions on executive pay," said Scott Talbott, senior vice president for government affairs at the Financial Services Roundtable, a trade group. "It is not appropriate for government to be setting the salaries of executives."

Yet some formal restraint on executive pay seems unavoidable, even sensible, some finance experts and economists said.

Angry sentiments on the issue in Congress were palpable on Tuesday, when Treasury Secretary Henry M Paulson Jr and Ben S Bernanke, the Federal Reserve chairman, testified before the Senate banking committee.

Senator Christopher J Dodd, chairman of the committee, said the "authors of this calamity" should not walk away enriched.

The presidential candidates, Senators Barack Obama and John McCain, have also called for pay limits.

The proposals in Washington are still tentative. A Senate draft document calls for a ban on incentive payments that the Treasury deems "inappropriate or excessive" and a "claw-back" provision, requiring executives to give up pay or severance benefits if the firm's financial results are later shown to be overstated.

"Clearly, the level of pay at some Wall Street firms was appalling, given the performance," said Charles M Elson, corporate governance expert at the University of Delaware. "But the bailout is about saving the economy, while executive pay is a separate, and complex, issue."

Heading: Wall Street Turmoil Sparks Anger at the UN - Indian Express
Content:
THE F B I HAS EXPANDED

Its corporate fraud inquiries in the wake of the tumult in the last 10 days, officials told The Associated Press on Tuesday.

A PRELIMINARY PROBE

Is now open into possible fraud involving the four giant corporations in the eye of the storm —Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, Lehman Brothers and American International Group

F B I OFFICIALS CONFIRMED

The number of corporate fraud investigations at the bureau was 26, an increase from the 24 cases cited just a week ago by Robert S Mueller III, F B I boss. That number stood at 21 in July, but the bureau has not named most of the targets.

MUELLER HAS SAID

The probe is aimed at firms that "may have engaged in misstatements in the course of what transpired during this financial crisis."

Heading: US empire near collapse: Ahmadinejad - Indian Express
Content:
Wall Street and the Bush administration's record of financial oversight came under attack at the 63rd session of the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, with one world leader after another saying that market turmoil in the United States threatened the global economy.

"We must not allow the burden of the boundless greed of a few to be shouldered by all," said President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of Brazil in an opening speech that reflected the tone of the gathering. Virtually every president or monarch from around the world made some reference to the financial upheaval, and the looming cloud was also the buzz of the back corridors.

With a pillar of American power — its financial leadership — so badly shaken, there was satisfaction among some attendees that the Bush administration, which had long lectured other nations about the benefits of unfettered markets, was now rejecting its own medicine by proposing a major bailout of financial firms.

But there was also serious concern that the U S had not policed its markets carefully enough to prevent the damage to its economy and others, making it much harder to raise money for the world's most vulnerable people.

"The global financial crisis endangers all our work," said the secretary general, Ban Ki-moon, who used his opening remarks to question the reliance on free markets. "We need a new understanding on business ethics and governance, with more compassion and less uncritical faith in the 'magic' of markets."

President Bush, making his eighth and last address to the U N, with which he has had a troubled relationship, sought to reassure the world that his administration was taking "bold steps" to stanch the crisis.

Amid a long ode to the importance of continuing the fight against terrorism, he devoted one paragraph to the rescue plan. "We've promoted stability in the markets by preventing the disorderly failure of major companies," he said. He noted that many were watching how the U S responded because economies were "more closely connected than ever before."

But for some leaders, the Bush bailout plan seemed hypocritical given the tough course Washington has often advised struggling nations to take.

"What you are seeing here is the letting off of some political steam," said British cabinet minister Mark Malloch Brown. "They are all remembering the very hard, unforgiving advice that they got from American financial institutions" to "deflate your economy, let your banks go to the wall... There is a resentment at what they would see as a further evidence of double standards."

President Nicolas Sarkozy of France described the crisis as the worst financial mess since the Depression of the 1930s and the financial system as "insane." He called for a summit meeting in November to determine how to address the problems and to develop greater international regulations of financial markets. Sarkozy said Wall Street bankers had told him they did not know who was responsible for the mess. When banks and hedge funds hand out fat bonuses, they are all willing to gloat about their success, Sarkozy said, "but when there are deficits we don't know who is responsible."

The U S ambassador to the U N, Zalmay Khalilzad suggested that world leaders should accept that the U S was facing the issue. "We are very agile and we are moving very quickly to deal with it," he said.

Yet, doubts were being raised not just at the U N but farther afield, with Germany's chancellor, Angela Merkel, among the most outspoken. She said that at last year's meeting of the G8, she had strongly urged both the U S and Britain to be more rigorous in supervising financial activities, and even offered specific proposals to be applied to banks and other institutions.

But the U S was not interested, she said. "We did what we were supposed to do," she told the German newspaper Münchner Merkur. "We adopted a decent E U regulation on the national statute books," but "when it came to it, the Americans said, 'That's not for us.' "

"We've promoted stability in the markets by preventing the disorderly failure of major companies..."

George W Bush, President of the United States

"Let us rebuild capitalism in which credit agencies are controlled and punished when necessary, where transparency... replaces opaqueness... We can do this on one condition, that we all work together in our globalised world."

Nicolas Sarkozy,President of france

"The global financial crisis endangers all our work... We need a new understanding on business ethics and governance, with more compassion and less uncritical faith in the 'magic' of markets."

Ban ki-Moon,UNITED NATIONS Secretary General

"We must not allow the burden of the boundless greed of a few to be shouldered by all."

Luiz Inacio Lula da SilvaPresident of Brazil

Heading: Dress code police’s strength doubled - Indian Express
Content:
Iran's president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad told the UN General Assembly on Tuesday that "the American empire" is nearing collapse and should end its military involvement in other countries. Ahmadinejad said terrorism is spreading quickly in Afghanistan while "the occupiers" are still in Iraq nearly six years after Saddam Hussein was ousted from power in Iraq.

"American empire in the world is reaching the end of its road, and its next rulers must limit their interference to their own borders," Ahmadinejad said. He accused the US of starting wars in Iraq and Afghanistan to win votes in elections and blamed a "few bullying powers" for trying to undermine Iran's nuclear programme.

Ahmadinejad's hardline rhetoric came as no surprise and offered little in the way of compromise at the UN, where he faces a new round of sanctions if no agreement is reached on limiting Iran's nuclear capabilities. While he reiterated that the country's nuclear programme is purely peaceful, the US and others fear it is aimed at producing enriched uranium to make nuclear weapons.

Iran already is under three sets of sanctions by the UN Security Council for refusing to suspend uranium enrichment. Washington and its Western allies are pushing for quick passage of a fourth set of sanctions to underline the international community's resolve, but are likely to face opposition from Russia.

"A few bullying powers have sought to put hurdles in the way of the peaceful nuclear activities of the Iranian nation by exerting political and economic pressures against Iran," he said.

Ahmadinejad also lashed out at Israel on Tuesday, saying "the Zionist regime is on a definite slope to collapse, and there is no way for it to get out of the cesspool created by itself and its supporters." The Iranian president is feared and reviled in Israel because of his repeated calls to wipe the Jewish state off the map, and his aggressive pursuit of nuclear technology has only fueled Israel's fears.

Israeli President Shimon Peres reacted angrily to Ahjmadinejad's criticism. "It is again a repetition of the darkest accusations in the name of Hitler and almost anti-Semitism," Peres later told journalists.

Regarding the US war in Iraq, Ahmadinejad said, "Millions have been killed or displaced, and the occupiers, without a sense of shame, are still seeking to solidify their position in the ... region and to dominate oil resources." He suggested that the presence of US and NATO forces in Afghanistan has contributed to a sharp rise in terrorism and a huge increase in the production of narcotics. He predicted that the alliance would not be successful.

His speech came just hours after President George W Bush made his eighth and final appearance before the UN General Assembly, urging the international community to stand firm against the nuclear ambitions of Iran and North Korea.

During interviews ahead of his speech on Tuesday, Ahmadinejad blamed US military interventions around the world in part for the collapse of global financial markets. "The US Government has made a series of mistakes in the past few decades," Ahmadinejad said an interview with the Los Angeles Times.

Heading: New airport screening ‘could read minds’ - Indian Express
Content: Iran has doubled the number of police assigned to its more than a year-long crackdown against women flouting Islamic dress codes, Kargozaran newspaper said on Wednesday. The dress code requires women to cover their hair and wear long, loose clothes to disguise the shape of their bodies. Violators can receive lashes, fines or imprisonment, although most usually receive a stern warning by street patrols. In addition to women flouting the dress codes, police have stopped men with spiky haircuts deemed Western. Barber shops have been temporarily shut for offering such haircuts.

Heading: McCain aide’s firm was paid by Freddie Mac - Indian Express
Content:
Technology that aims to detect devices like guns or explosives at airports could soon be a passe, for scientists are to unveil a new type of screening gadget that can read minds. A team is testing a type of body scanner that uses a technology capable of detecting "hostile intent" — in fact, it can seek out invisible clues that one might be harbouring such as raised body temperature, pulse and even breathing rate.

According to the scientists, the system 'MALINTENT' uses a raft of "non-invasive" sensors and imagers to detect and evaluate a person's facial expression to gauge whether he could be planning to commit an attack or crime. And, if the sensors pick up anything considered alarming, analysts can decide whether to subject a person to questioning.

The technology, developed by the Human Factors Division of US Homeland Security's Directorate for Science and

Technology, would be used at border checkpoints, airports and special events that require security screening, The Daily Telegraph reported. According to the Department of Homeland Security, the technology, dubbed Future Attribute Screening Technology, or FAST, deploys a range of "innovative physiological and behavioural technologies" to pick up "indications of malintent or the intent or desire to cause harm".

But, Spokesman John Verrico said: "We're still very early on in this research, but it is looks very promising.

We are running at about 78 per cent accuracy on malintent detection and 80 per cent on deception."

Heading: North Korea ousts IAEA monitors - Indian Express
Content:
One of the giant mortgage companies at the heart of the credit crisis paid $15,000 a month from the end of 2005 through last month to a firm owned by Senator John McCain's campaign manager, according to two people with direct knowledge of the arrangement.

The disclosure undercuts a remark by Mr. McCain on Sunday night that the campaign manager, Rick Davis, had had no involvement with the company for the last several years.

Mr. Davis's firm received the payments from the company, Freddie Mac, until it was taken over by the government this month along with Fannie Mae, the other big mortgage lender whose deteriorating finances helped precipitate the cascading problems on Wall Street, the two people said.

They said they did not recall Mr. Davis's doing much substantive work for the company in return for the money, other than to speak to a political action committee of high-ranking employees in October 2006 on the approaching midterm Congressional elections. They said Mr. Davis's firm, Davis Manafort, had been kept on the payroll because of his close ties to Mr. McCain, the Republican presidential nominee, who by 2006 was widely expected to run again for the White House.

Mr. Davis took a leave from Davis Manafort for the presidential campaign, but as equity holder continues to benefit from its income. No one at Davis Manafort other than Mr. Davis was involved in efforts on Freddie Mac's behalf, the people familiar with the arrangement said.

A Freddie Mac spokeswoman said the company would not comment.

Jill Hazelbaker, a spokeswoman for the McCain campaign, did not dispute the payments to Mr. Davis's firm. But she said that Mr. Davis had stopped taking a salary from the firm by the end of 2006 and that his work did not affect Mr. McCain.

"Senator McCain's positions on policy matters are based upon what he believes to be in the public interest," Ms. Hazelbaker said in a written statement.

The disclosure comes at a time when Mr. McCain and his Democratic rival, Senator Barack Obama, are sparring over ties to lobbyists and special interests, seeking political advantage in a campaign being reshaped by the financial crisis and the plan to bail out investment firms.

Now

Obama has opened a 9-point lead. He leads McCain by 52 per cent to 43 per cent

Two weeks ago the race was essentially even, with McCain at 49 per cent and Obama at 47 per cent

Heading: Pak may seek fuel tech from China - Indian Express
Content:
North Korea has expelled U.N. monitors from its plutonium-making nuclear plant and plans to start reactivating it next week, rowing back from a 2007 deal to scrap its atomic bomb programme, officials said on Wednesday.

North Korea on Friday said it was working to restart the Yongbyon atomic complex it had been dismantling since last November under a disarmament-for-aid agreement with the five powers involved. The disagreement, has however, derailed since then due to disputes over implementation.

Olli Heinonen, the International Atomic Energy Agency's head of non-proliferation safeguards, told an IAEA board of governors meeting that monitors verifying North Korea's denuclearisation were forced to quit the plutonium facility this week. "There are no more seals and surveillance equipment in place at the reprocessing facility," IAEA spokeswoman Melissa Fleming said. North Korea further stated that from here on, IAEA inspectors will have no further access to the reprocessing plant, she said, summarising Heinonen's remarks.

North Korea also informed IAEA inspectors that they plan to introduce nuclear material to the reprocessing plant in one week's time, Fleming told reporters.

Heading: White House says move disappointing - Indian Express
Content:
In an apparent bid to counter the Indo-US civil nuclear deal, Pakistan plans to seek fuel technology from China for 10 new atomic power plants it intends to set up over the next two decades. During a high-level meeting, PM Yousuf Raza Gilani approved the construction of two new nuclear plants at Chashma in Punjab province, sources told PTI, adding these plants are expected to be built with Chinese assistance.

The September 19 meeting attended by top officials of the military and Strategic Plans Divisionhad drawn up plans to acquire new nuclear plants and a satellite communications system.

Heading: Pak finds suspected US spy drone wreckage - Indian Express
Content: The White House on Wednesday called North Korea's move to expel U.N. monitors from its nuclear plant and plans to restart the facility very disappointing and urged Pyongyang to reconsider its actions. "The North Korean actions are very disappointing and run counter to the expectations of the members of the six-party talks and the international community," White House spokesman Gordon Johndroe said.

Heading: Indian juniors register convincing victory - Indian Express
Content:
The Pakistani Army said Wednesday it had found the wreckage of a suspected US spy plane near the Afghan border, but denied claims that it had been shot down. Three Pakistani intelligence officials earlier said troops and tribesmen had shot down the aircraft late on Tuesday near Jalal Khel, a village in Pakistan's South Waziristan region. However, a Pakistan Army statement on Wednesday said security forces had recovered the crashed surveillance aircraft. It said a technical problem appeared to have brought it down and that it was investigating further.

The three Pakistani intelligence officials said the drone was hit after circling the Angoor Ada area of South Waziristan for several hours. A senior US official challenged the account. "We're not aware of any drones being down," said the official, who also asked for anonymity because of the diplomatic sensitivity of the issue.

Heading: I-League long way from meeting AFC guidelines - Indian Express
Content:
Opening their junior Davis Cup campaign against hosts Mexico could have been a tough one for the Indian team. But despite the numerous cheers ringing out in support of the home players at the stadium in San Luis Potosil, Mexico, the second seeds recorded a 2-1 victory in this tie.

After Saurabh Singh lost the first match to Alexis Carlo 6-4, 6-2, Yuki Bhambri ensured parity with a 7-5, 6-1 win against Fernando Larrea. In the crucial doubles, the Indian duo defeated Carlos and Daniel Fernandez 6-1, 6-4. They managed to beat the rain too, and now await the loser of the tie between Brazil and Great Britain.

Bhambri, ranked 18th on the ITF junior circuit charts, would have wished for a better start against the 408-ranked Larrea. After losing his first game, the Indian did manage to break back, only to surrender his next game on serve. Already a match down after Singh's defeat, and with a 4-1 deficit to make up, Bhambri didn't let the pressure get to him and continued attempting to find his rhythm.

He eventually managed to win the set 7-5, and compared to this one, the second set was a breeze. Bhambri lost just one game on his way to wrapping up the match and ensuring the tie would be decided in the doubles match.

The first set of the doubles featured a dominant Indian performance — they won this easily with a 6-1 scoreline. The second set was a much closer affair, but victory belonged to India.

Heading: Delhi on top, Rest in pieces - Indian Express
Content:
It seemed that the launch of the I-League last year would finally bring professionalism to Indian domestic football, but even at the start of the event's second edition, the All-India Football Federation (AIFF) is struggling to meet several basic international standards.

While most of the clubs are still toiling hard to fulfill the minimum requirements set by the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) — age-group teams, club licensing and own stadiums — the AIFF is struggling hard just to appoint the three mandatory posts needed to be filled to run a professional league — CEO, manager and assistant manager. If the clubs and federation fail to meet the AFC requirements quickly, they could pay a heavy price and India could even be denied participation in the AFC Champions League.

"Till now we haven't got a good candidate for the post of CEO. We are still looking for it and our host broadcaster Zee Sports is helping us find a suitable person. So we have decided to appoint an acting CEO for the time being," AIFF president Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi told reporters on Wednesday.

"From next year, the I-League will be a registered body with AIFF's general secretary Alberto Colaco as the chairman and Srinivas Dempo as deputy chairman.

To clear some of the on-field mess, the AIFF has at least decided to improve the standard of refereeing. Last year it had roped in referees from Maldives and this year it will call officials from Singapore and Malaysia. "Earlier, referees used to double up as linesmen in some matches but that won't happen now. This is an experiment we're conducting this season in line with the FIFA and AFC guidelines," Colaco said.

Mumbai's Cooperage ground, slammed for being ill-equipped to host top-level domestic matches, has been given the green signal by the venue inspection committee led by Gautam Kar, but only on an experimental basis.

"Cooperage will host the first two matches and if the conditions are suitable then it will host the rest of the matches. If the conditions are not suitable, then the matches will be either held at Kohlapur or DY Patil Stadium. We've also kept Delhi's Ambedkar Stadium and Gurgaon's Tau Devi Lal Stadium as neutral options," Colaco said.

The first leg of the I-League will conclude on November 30 and will be followed by the final round of the Federation Cup in Delhi and Gurgaon from December 5 to 22.

Heading: Line and strength: Delhi bowlers bang on target - Indian Express
Content:
Anil Kumble must have had a sense of déjà vu as he sat glued to the computer watching the day's dismissals. Though he was leading the Rest of India side in the Irani Cup, he was once again in a dressing room cohabited by batsmen with long faces, like on the Sri Lanka tour.

There were batsmen who got out early and batsmen who didn't capitalise on good starts. The collapse of the top and middle-order was so dramatic that the team slipped from 112 for one to 186-7. It was only because of the tailenders that they managed to finish at 252.

For Kumble it was like being in Sri Lanka all over again, and the memories he wanted to wipe out before the start of the series against Australia must have cascaded back. If mending the middle-order was top-most on his mind going into this match, the trip to Baroda hasn't quite helped.

When the skipper elected to bat in bright sunshine on a pitch with no real pace, he would've thought that he was providing a perfect platform of his middle-order to get into form. With Sourav Ganguly not picked and Sachin Tendulkar ruled out because of injury, the focus was on Rahul Dravid and VVS Laxman. Both the senior batsmen in the side spent enough time in the middle but still their stays weren't convincing enough.

Dravid, who opened the innings with Wasim Jaffer (50), scored 47 runs but he looked uncomfortable against Ishant Sharma, who bowled an inspired spell. Dropped by Aakash Chopra in the slips early on, Dravid's 168-minute vigil was finally ended by a big in-cutter from Sharma that tapped him plumb in front.

VVS Laxman would have been even more disappointed since he negotiated the Delhi pace trio of Sharma, Ashish Nehra and Pradeep Sangwan easily, and looked in sublime touch while hitting two consecutive boundaries off Nehra through mid-wicket and cover. But faulty shot selection saw him getting out to part-time offie Virender Sehwag.

Asked about the two senior batsmen missing the opportunity before the Aussie series, former selector VB Chandrashekhar said there was no need to panic. "Dravid wanted to spend some time in the middle, which is not a surprise especially as things aren't going his way. If you look at the pitch one can't say that it is perfectly batsmen-friendly. It's a slow wicket," he said.

Mohammad Kaif and S Badrinath, handed golden opportunities, also failed to capitalise. Badri looked out of sorts, especially as he kept getting inside edges to Ishant Sharma, and was finally bowled for 16 when he dragged back a widish delivery. Kaif, who scored 29, was far more comfortable at the crease. But just when he looked well set, he failed to clear the in-field with an ill-advised, and badly executed, pull against leg-spinner Chetanya Nanda.

A lot was expected from wicket-keeper MS Dhoni. When he had led the ODI team to a series victory in Sri Lanka, there was talk that things would have been different for India if he had been a part of the Test squad. But, in flannels today, Dhoni failed to bail out the team as he fell to an innocuous angling delivery from Sangwan.

The only silver lining for Kumble today was the bowling performance of Ishant. Though he was in the other team on Wednesday, Kumble will be hoping for a similar show when the Delhi paceman is in his corner against the Aussies in Bangalore.

Heading: Australia have their plans in place - Indian Express
Content:
On the eve of the Irani Cup match, Delhi skipper Virender Sehwag had simple advice for his young bowlers as they prepared for the formidable Rest of India batting line-up: Stick to a line just outside the off-stump and never bowl near the pads.

Sehwag, who has had a long association with opposition batsmen, didn't want the 20-year-old Ishant Sharma and 17-year-old Pradeep Sangwan to get carried away by experimenting too much.

"We knew their side was full of batting greats. Viru bhai told us not to bowl to their strengths," says Sangwan, who finished with figures of three for 57.

Among the three wickets he took — all with away-going deliveries — Sangwan said the dismissal of the in-form MS Dhoni was the most satisfying. Early in his innings, Dhoni tentatively pushed a ball that pitched outside the off-stump and moved further away. The snick was caught by wicketkeeper Puneet Bisht one-handed, inches away from the ground.

Tag team

Sangwan's out-swingers perfectly complemented Sharma's in-cutters. Though the trajectories of their deliveries were different, their line was same — outside off.

"It was really good to take wickets here. There was nothing in this pitch and we had to push ourselves hard. We had to stick to one line," Ishant said. He was impressive all day but it was his spell after lunch that got him two wickets — Rahul Dravid and S Badrinath — to put Delhi in control.

Delhi coach Vijay Dahiya also heaped praise on Sehwag for the impressive performance of the team's young bowlers. "Sehwag was the man responsible for all changes," he said.

Sehwag practiced what he preached when he came on to bowl. His off-spinners moved away from the off-stump, and VVS Laxman fell to the bait as his swipe went straight to Mithun Manhas at mid-wicket.

Heading: Former India analyst Ramki under the scanner in Jaipur - Indian Express
Content:
The Australian team bus rolled into the Sawai Man Singh Stadium towards afternoon, but there were no recognisable faces among those who got off wheeling the huge kitbags. Was this a second XI? Actually, it was. Like all things Australian, even the net session involved meticulous planning and their 11-member support staff had arrived early to oversee arrangements.

"Where's the gym, mate," enquired physical trainer Stuart Kappinner as he walked in. Greg Chappell, the assistant coach, collected a bunch of local boys and briefed them about the requirements, and allotted them to different nets. Bowling coach Troy Cooley distributed an equal share of old and new balls at the seven different nets. And chief coach Tim Neilsen had a hard look at all the wickets provided for practice.

The team arrived half an hour later, smartly dressed in their new training colours, with a heavy dose of sun bloc on their faces.

Three tracks

There was another bit of innovation at the nets as well. Chappell had asked the groundsmen to prepare three different kinds of tracks at the venue — one a slow turner, the second a flat batting track and the third one with some rough on it. On Wednesday, they started off on the good pitch, an attempt, perhaps to get their confidence levels high ahead of what should be a gruelling tour.

All the big guns — Matthew Hayden, Ricky Ponting, Michael Hussey, Michael Clarke and Brad Haddin — batted on the centre-wicket, while all five quicks in the team — Brett Lee, Mitchell Johnson, Stuart Clark, Doug Boullinger and Shane Watson — had a go at them.

Not just spin

Had they forgotten about Harbhajan Singh and Anil Kumble? Not really. "It's dangerous to just focus on the spinners alone," Hussey said at the end of the session. "India have some very good pacers who have won them matches recently and we are looking at the entire package of the Indian bowling attack. We can't just focus on the spin side of it alone.

"Chappell has arranged for different pitches at the RCA so that the visitors can adjust to different surfaces. It will be very enjoyable next few days and I am sure we will be very well prepared going into the first Test."

As far as first impressions go, the Aussies made a mark with their intensity and focus. Everything else, after all, had been taken care of half an hour before they arrived.

The Australian support XI

Coach: Tim Neilsen, Assistant coach: Greg Chappell, Physiotherapist: Alex Kountoris, Masseur: Julia Russel, Physical trainer: Stuart Kappinen, Performance analyst: Michael Marshal, Bowling coach: Troy Cooley, Fielding coach: Mike Young, Security in-charge: Reg Dickson, Doctor: Damien McCainn, Media manager: Michael Slade

Heading: India A win dress rehearsal - Indian Express
Content:
The director of the firm Sports Mechanics and former Team India video analyst S Ramkrishnan was asked to 'show cause' by the BCCI on Wednesday after a media report suggested that he was in Jaipur to help the Australian team. "There were enquiries from board officials on this issue and they were satisfied with what I told them," Ramki said.

"My company and I have been with the Indian team for the last eight years and we have always maintained great secrecy about our work and information that we collect. To be associated with the Indian team is a great honour for me. Why is my presence taken in the wrong sense? I could've been here to tape the Australians as well," he said.

Ramki, who was here to train analysts associated with Rajasthan Cricket Association, however, left on Wednesday evening to quell further speculation. Team India however haves already prepared for the Australian tour. Video tapes of all team members have been procured, and much of that work on visiting Australians was done during the Indian Premier League in April-May.

Heading: Rain man Lewis on familiar turf - Indian Express
Content:
Rohit Sharma (51) and skipper Suresh Raina (46) added 85 runs for the fourth wicket as India A defeated Australia A by three wickets in their last league match of the triangular series at the MA Chidambaram Stadium on Wednesday.

India, needing 273 in 50 overs, romped home with four overs to spare.

Though none of the batsmen fully capitalised on the flat wicket, India benefited from useful knocks by Yusuf Pathan (36), debutant Ravi Teja (33), wicketkeeper Wriddhiman Saha (25 not out) and achieved a comfortable victory.
