4) If you get stuck, clear a path with a shovel in front and in back of your vehicle, put sand or gravel on the cleared path, and slowly accelerate (with a standard transmission-rock try rocking back and forth to get free) without spinning the tires.

Heading: Warmin' Up - Indian Express
Content:
Nature & music merge
You don't need to be told where to go; the rhythmic notes of the piano, lead up a flight of steps and you are drawn to the library which houses the Strawberry Fields Kindergarten's warm reading-cum-music room. Seated there is a gathering of parents and the occasion is the school's bi-yearly week-long musical mornings. Students of Nursery are holding court as they confidently sing one rhyme after another, taking you through vivid scenes of the animal kingdom and other day-to-day facets of their life. Simple songs that talk of days of the week in Sunday Monday; animal kingdom in My Pigeon House, Crocodile and Beehive; nature's bounty through Out in the Garden and the world around us via, Wheels of the Bus and I tap, I catch, you also discover that along with an awareness about the myriad qualities of life, the children are developing a command over the Queen's English. "We try to gently weave in musical concepts, the beauty of balancing lyrics and rhythm and set these to tune on carefully chosen songs. The selection is a serious process where the attempt is to make it all relevant and meaningful,'' explains Atul Khanna, Director of the school.

A page-turner!
WITH over 5000 copies sold in just two weeks since its Delhi launch, 18-year-old Tishaa Khosla from Chandigarh might just be the new kid on the writing block. Her book 'Pink or Black' was formally launched in Mumbai by actor Anupam Kher at the actor's Actor Prepares Institute. "It's always fascinating to see young talent come to the fore. I am doubly proud for the fact that some of her story telling skills were honed here at our institute. Tishaa is a bright and energetic girl and from my interaction, one who explores various medium to express herself. It didn't come as a surprise that she has written a best-seller at 18," remarked Kher at the launch. The young author's debut novel is based on her life and experiences at her boarding school in Sanawar and may soon be made into a major Bollywood film! "Story telling is a great art and it's really encouraging to see publishing houses push in new authors," said Kher, adding, "Bollywood forever is on the lookout for newer ideas and subjects and I am sure, Tishaa's book has a perfect backdrop for a young teenage film." Speaking about the sellout first print, an elated Tishaa remarked, "I am thrilled on seeing the reactions to the book and never imagined that it would be a best-seller so soon. The book is already on its second run, and I am delighted with the reactions I have been receiving everywhere." The book has been published by Rupa Publications.

Tune in!
WANT to know what the city is listening to? It's 94.3 MY FM states a survey conducted by the Hansa Research, the body that also spear heads the IRS survey in the country. The survey states that My FM is way ahead with 50 per cent more listeners in Chandigarh, as compared to Big FM. It also states that MY FM has the highest number of listeners — almost 60 per cent and is also rated much higher in the survey on the 'Top of the Mind' awareness level.
The survey, which was conducted in August and September this year, has also stated about the consumption pattern and media habits of the people. The media consumption in Chandigarh, especially of radio has been found to be more than TV and Print media. The weekly consumption of radio in Chandigarh is 6.83 days as against the TV's 6.6 days.

Heading: For a beautiful you - Indian Express
Content:
It's that time of the year again when the weather's taking a turn and you can smell autumn in the air. It's around this time that designers and boutique owners kind of hit overdrive putting their collections in order, preferably before Diwali. Among them is the mother-daughter duo of Archana and Karishma with their all-new label 'Elements'. Working out of their studio and workshop in Industrial Area's Phase 1 (Plot no 41), the two are warming up pretty well. "Our USP is customisation to the T," Karishma is the first to speak. While the daughter spearheads the Western ensemble department, mom Archana is a Pro with traditional weaves, crafts and sarees. "I am originally from Lucknow and sport a lot of sarees. The last many years have seen me put together sarees from my own set of crafts persons for my friends. It's only when Karishma joined me that we decided to open Elements," explains Archana.

Their Autumn-Winter collection is all about the use of warm, woollen fabrics. "We are also making woollen mix Pashmina sarees that drape really well," tells Archana as we eye a somber grey one highlighted with applique work. The woollen fabric also runs into kurtis, ponchos and suits. "We are looking to revive traditional weaves and work. In fact, we have our own karigars in the studio where clients can come and personally spell out the look they want," chorus the two. Also noticeable among the collection is Kolkata's Shibori work on sarees and stoles apart from suits that run into warm colours. Then there are Lucknowi chikan churidaars and salwars on the shelves too. The mother-daughter duo have also dipped their hands into home furnishings having designed bedspreads, quilts and even lamps.

Heading: One for the road! - Indian Express
Content: Fretting over how to get that special look on your D-day? Here's some advice from the expert. "Drink lot of water, take proper sleep and scrub fresh cream with a few drops of lemon on skin to get rid of the tan," says Asmi, adding that to start the make-up prepping and priming of the skin is of vital importance. "This should be followed with a good concealer, which should be pat and not rub," Asmi says that tones of browns define the brows best. She tips that a peach cream blush when applied on the apple of the cheeks gives a very natural and flushed look. "But if you want to touch up your make-up during the day, only powder make-up should be applied using a brush," reels Asmi. Talking about the present trends, Asmi says while young girls now-a-days like the dusky or nude look, the brides want to look glamours with sharp contours, shimmer and glittery eyes. One can avail Asmi's bridal make-up package for Rs 5500, engagement make-up package for Rs 3000 and party make-up for Rs 2000.

Heading: High Five - Indian Express
Content:
Constant travelling should not stop you from achieving your fitness goals. Get movin' with on-the-go gym gear

Gear up for fitness on the go. If you're among those who can't give up working out even while you're at work, there's gym gear that promises to keep your fitness schedule bang on schedule. While basics like choose healthy options while planning your meals, taking the stairs, walking as much as you can...remain unchanged, there's now an option to pack up handy equipment which will help you work out your entire body, especially when you have no time to hit the gym or there's an absence of one where you are travelling.

Nods Harshbir Singh of Platinum Fitness, who feels if you're working hard at the gym to achieve your goals, it makes sense to keep up with exercise even if you're travelling frequently. "The market now has a range of fitness products which are both compact and effective and all you need is a little will and some tips from your trainer to work out any time, anywhere,'' Singh highly recommends resistance bands which ensure complete upper and lower body work out and also simple floor exercises, lunges and free-hand exercises.

At Prime Sports in Sector 7, Rajender Bajaj has at hand a range of effective equipment that can be your fitness companion. Light, stylish, affordable, Bajaj lists the current favourites like the body trimmer stretch and resistance bands that work out your entire body, a digitalized body sculptor skipping rope which will confirm the number of calories you have burnt, colourful grip and squeeze balls, dainty wrist and ankle weights, deflatable swiss balls, foldable push-up bar and foam covered hand-grips. "These don't occupy space and are not bulky either,'' adds Bajaj.

With a little innovation and will-power you can make the most of any place fitness trainer Jolly talks about the importance of a good warm up and using water bottles as weights, doing side stretches and side kicks for the waist, sit-ups, squats with the help of a chair et al. You can also use a calorie-tracking pedometer which accurately measures distance and calculates the calories burned. There's then the rowing action exerciser which tightens abs, strengthens back and tones thighs. "Aerobic bands increase your strength and flexibility and of course, give a great work out,'' confirms the trainer.

Another interesting concept comes from Technogym, an Italian company, which has created a travel gym which is compact and lightweight. The Wellness Bag fits easily into a suitcase or holdall or can be carried with the wellness pad. The product is accompanied by a series of manuals, while the products are modular, simple to assemble and easy to use in a vast range of exercises. From strength and conditioning, muscle flexibility, it's great for both intensive training and use by beginners. "Just 45 minutes to an hour of work out is what you need to not only look good, but also feel good. In fact, as I am always on the move, I never take out my essential exercise equipment for my bag,'' shares Roshan Rai, a banker.

Heading: At wits’ end - Indian Express
Content:
Cool and classic, get ready for a rocking PecFest

It cannot get bigger and better than this. An expected footfall of 25,000 students, 75 universities and 200 colleges. Punjab Engineering Colleges Fest is on a roll. Already four months into the preparations, the fest will have everything from cultural calls, technical treats and literary bites.

Seeing a sizeable addition in the number of events this year, Apurv Devgan, event manager and a final year mechanical engineering students point to the paint ball challenge as the highlight. As he hands over this year's marketing brochure and formally launches the mascot - -a squirrel on a skateboard, he explains how the "squirrel stands their undying enthusiasm and determination to never give up." "We call it Sira. It is synonymous with energy, exactly the levels students have shown," quips Abhinav Kumar, member of the creative team adding how about 30 different mascots were made before finalizing on this one. And the skateboard? "It's 'Going High, Going Five," chips in pal, Aseem Grover, who's also part of the public relations team. The Open Hand too finds significane here for this is the fifth PecFest. "It's for the years of existence and for the five elements that enable basic survival."

Conceptualized to rejoice the exuberance of youth and savour the brilliance of creativity, at the PECFest due on November 7,8 and 9, has nine teams -- discipline, event coordination, infrastructure, fine arts, hospitality, publicity, creativity, public relations and marketing. "We've literally burnt the midnight oil. The event has been planned to perfection and now what is left is the implementation," says Vinayak Talwar, a final year mechanical student, who tells us that delegations are going to Rajasthan and Mumbai to invite students for the first time. Also on the list of new introductions are solo dance, night-time quiz, street dance, beat boxing, war of DJs, tarot card reading, and a show of modified bikes, adds convener of the fest Gurinder Pal Singh.

From a mere Rs 3 lakh, the budget too has ballooned to Rs 30 lakh. "This is going to be the perfect melting pot of interaction, competition and evolution," Dr Manoj Dutta, Director, PEC, sums it aptly.

Heading: Since Feb 13, Bathinda got a project every third day - Indian Express
Content:
...stands a very grim sort of person, and that's me, actor-comedian Vrajesh Hirjee flips the funny side

It's not necessary that what you see is what you'll get. For instance, it's not necessary that when you catch up with a comic in a queue, he'll crack up in a jiffy and juggle with jokes. "Exactly! I'm a serious guy, a very grim sort of person," Vrajesh Hirjee braces this hallelujah moment and says that 'he doesn't see himself as a comic'. "It's performance, it's a job, acting is my profession, and this is a part of it." Nevertheless, you still want to see the guy do that hissing cobra act in Golmaal, get away with straight face act of humour in Naya Office Office, leave you in splits with his 'stammering' success and roll on the screen as the oddball with that funny grin on his face and a condom song as his ringtone. That's Vrajesh Hirjee, taking a laughing stock. In town for the shooting of Yashraj's Hrippaa, Hirjee rewinds to formation days. "I was always into acting, mainly stage performances. But life took a turn. I ended up doing commerce and law, and my first job was in fact in The Indian Express in Space marketing," financial consultancy came next and Hirjee soon knew that money was not his calling. Advertising followed suit. "Ravi Vasvani used to tell me that you are wasting your talent here, and I would stand in front of the mirror and think, no height, no looks, what will I do?" After Sorry Meri Lorry, Hirjee knew exactly what he was made and meant to do.

"By no stretch of imagination is comedy easy, and acting is not simple, so I try to variate and not repeat myself," Vrajesh enjoys the art and craft of acting, the cinema for its impact, stage for that instant gratification and television for the incredible reach. "I've done serious roles, but I feel when you use humour to put across a point, it works," he talks of the latest condom campaign and how it has got record number of downloads. "Real life can be extremely funny."

Cinematic times have changed, scripts are being tailor made for comic characters and even mainstream actors are jumping into it. "Look at Akshay Kumar," Vrajesh is now eyeing for "a greater reach and greater connect". Looking forward to his next releases including Kabir Sadanand's Tum Milo To Sahi where people started calling him junior

Nana Patekar, the supremely hilarious Golmaal Returns, some real life comedy in Daddy Cool and Roadside Romeo, Vrajesh feels that the moment he'll stop working, it will be time to say bye. Right now, it's carry on folks.

Heading: Jalandhar MC’s men, machines being used for BJP’s rally on September 28 - Indian Express
Content:
When Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal and SAD (B) chief Sukhbir Badal would lay foundation stone of Yatri Niwas to be built at a cost of Rs 2.3 crore in Talwandi Sabo tomorrow, they would go on to create a record of sorts.

Since February 13 this year--after Parkash Singh Badal kick-started foundation stone-laying spree by setting in motion a road project linking Maluka and Dod villages-- the father-son duo has laid the stones for as many as 72 projects. In the next two days, they would be laying stones of 13 more projects, taking the tally to 85. This means, a foundation stone is laid in the district every third day.

With the total cost of the 85 projects exceeding Rs 300 crore in monetary terms, it turns out to be more than Rs 1 crore a day spared for Bathinda district since February 13. Notably, majority of the foundation stones have been laid by Sukhbir.

In political circles, the stone-laying spree is being associated with the upcoming parliamentary elections, as it was being said that Sukhbir might contest from Bathinda. The Badals are showing unprecedented generosity for Bathinda-- where the Congress made a clean sweep in the February 2007 polls-- which stands de-reserved after delimitation.

Bathinda district has been gifted various projects, including that of water supply and sewerage, roads widening and strengthening, irrigation, 66-KV grid sub-stations and works of Bathinda Municipal Corporation and Bathinda Development Authority.

The funding for the projects is coming from different sources. For instance, while departments, like PSEB and Irrigation, will bear the costs for their respective projects, the Punjab Infrastructure Development Board (PIDB) will pump in money for water supply and sewerage projects of the municipal bodies.

The water supply and sewerage projects in Bathinda and Mansa will cost more than Rs 200 crore, it is learnt. The Rs 72-crore projects, the foundation stones of which would be laid by the CM and Sukhbir in Talwandi Sabo on Friday, would be funded from the Rs 85-crore grant given by the Centre for Guruta Gaddi Diwas celebrations.

As per information, while some of the projects have been completed and some are in progress, work is yet to start on a number of others.

Tenders for water supply and sewerage projects, the foundation stones of which were laid in May, will be opened on September 26, say officials.

Sources say out of the five projects, only Maluka power grid sub-station has become functional. The sub-station is said to entail a cost of about Rs 4 crore. For the irrigation projects of upgrading Dhipali, Bathinda and Phul distributaries, each at a cost of more than Rs 4 crore, the department claims to have forwarded the cases for sanction to the Chief Engineer.

Sukhbir had laid the foundation stones of these projects in August and this month. "Paperwork has been done and projects' proposals have been sent to the Chief Engineer for sanction," says Executive Engineer (Canal) Harlabh Singh Chahal.

Sources say out of 16 works of the MC, for which foundation stones were laid in February, six have been completed and 10 are in progress. The work on Transport Nagar, Dairy Nagar and Goniana-Mansa stretch on GT Road being carried out by Improvement Trust is also under way.

Ironically, the much-hyped project of developing an international cricket stadium, foundation stone for which was laid in December 8, 2007, on the occasion of CM's birthday, is yet to see the light of day.

Heading: PSEB officials locked up in a house, beaten up - Indian Express
Content:
Senior leaders of the BJP are leaving no stone unturned to make Vijay Sankalap rally on September 28 successful. So enthusiastic are the workers of the saffron brigade that they did not think once before engaging official machinery of the Municipal Corporation for rally preparations.

MCJ vehicles are being used to ferry flags and hoardings to be installed on roadsides, and corporation employees have been allotted duties for the event. Today, vehicles of

MCJ's horticulture wing were seen carrying rally material towards Kapurthala Chowk, where MC employees were busy installing flags.

Interestingly, the road from Kapurthala Chowk towards the rally venue at Sain Das School in Patel Chowk that had been crying for attention since long is also being spruced up.

The rally is being organised by the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha and senior leaders from the Centre, including BJP president Rajnath Singh and BJUM president Amit Thakkar, and in charge of Punjab affairs Balbir Punj will participate.

The rally will kick off campaigning for the Lok Sabha polls in Doaba. An MC officer said they were directed by BJP leaders to use corporation vehicles and take services of the staff.

However, BJP Mayor Rakesh Rathore said this was not true, and someone was spreading wrong information.

Heading: Villagers pitch in for water supply, sewerage projects - Indian Express
Content:
Two officials of the Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB) found themselves in an unsavory situation after they were allegedly locked inside a house in Bhodipura village on Wednesday morning, when they were conducting raids to check power theft, and thrashed.

"Bhagta Bhai Ka Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO) Paramjit Singh and Junior Engineer (JE) Kikar Singh were rescued after more than four hours by a police party after we made a call to our senior officials," Gurnam Singh, another JE, who accompanied the raiding team, said. The police have registered a case under Sections 186 (obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions), 332 (voluntarily causing hurt to deter public servant from his duty), 342 (wrongful confinement) and 353 (assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty) of the IPC against as many as 11 persons.

However, Bhagta Bhai Ka PSEB officials have decided to stage a dharna tomorrow, demanding immediate arrest of those booked, said Kikar Singh. A police official, investigating the case, said no arrests have been made so far. Kikar alleged that when they raided the house of one Major Singh, they found that the meter wasn't working. "Major Singh started misbehaving with me, and said that farmers' union had assured him that no one would check his electric meter," he said.

"And when the SDO intervened, he was forcibly taken inside. By that time, a number of villagers gathered and started beating up the SDO. As I tried to save him, I too received many blows," said Kikar, adding that the SDO was in shock. The SDO did not take the call made to take his comments. "This is very unfortunate. After all, the officials had gone there to perform their duty," said JE Gurnam Singh.

Heading: CM: Rahul’s road show wastage of money - Indian Express
Content:
Each household in Rajianikalan village, near Jagraon, has contributed Rs 1,500 for a water supply project started under the World Bank-aided scheme.

The scheme will cover 3,200 villages at a cost of Rs 1,280 crore. Work has also started in nearby villages of Marsianbhaike, Chaka and Ramgarh.

NK Dhir, senior project specialist, Water and Sanitation Department, said, "It is a demand-driven project. We will work in only those villages that spell out their demands, which can range from improving water supply or sewerage system, renovation of village ponds or even augmentation of the existing system."

In Punjab, 392 villages have already deposited their share, out of which 74 were in Ludhiana, said Mohammad Ishfaq, Executive Engineer, Ludhiana. The villagers have also been conveyed that once the facility is provided, they will have to maintain their projects. "The government's role is only to facilitate and generate the bill, and the revenue will go to the gram panchayat's water sanitation committee, which is being formed in the villages that opt for the works," said AK Soni, Superintending Engineer, Water Supply and Sanitation Circle, Ludhiana.

At present, Rs 70 per month is being charged from every household for water supply and this will be used for paying the electricity bills of tubewells and salaries of employees. The gram panchayat can also charge some more funds in case a development plan comes its way, said officials.

A few days ago, Sita Ram Aggarwal, programme director, held a meeting with the bidders for the works at Bachat Bhawan, where they were told about the rules of World Bank. Online tenders will also be available from the first week of October.

Heading: 130 people look after Governor at Raj Bhavan - Indian Express
Content:
Terming the recently-concluded road show of AICC General Secretary Rahul Gandhi in Punjab as wastage of money and energy, Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal on Thursday said the Amethi MP should have offered some "genuine help" to the state.

"He is the son of the person who runs the government at the Centre. But he did not give a penny to Punjab, which needs monetary help and not road shows," Badal said in a press

conference today evening.

When asked for his take on Rahul's mild reaction to his statements, Badal said, "Oh Rahul taan chala gaya hai. Ethe jehre Rahul baithe ne oh roj mainu gaalan kadade ne (That Rahul has gone. But the Rahuls (Congressmen) sitting in Punjab curse me daily)."

Badal was in Bathinda to lay the foundation stone of Dr Ambedkar Senior Secondary School in Canal Colony. The school is being built at a cost of Rs 3.25 crore. He also laid the stones of a community centre in Model Town, which entails a cost of Rs 3 crore, and the new building of Khalsa Senior Secondary School.

Heading: Bank strike ends, citizens hit as ATMs also run out of money - Indian Express
Content:
The staff does not include his Z+ security and Admn officials

The days of royalty may have come to an end in an independent India, but the institution of state governors seems to carry on with the same regalia. One such glaring example is Punjab Governor S F Rodrigues (Retd), the Administrator of Union Territory of Chandigarh.

Documents procured under the Right to Information Act shows that Rodrigues enjoys the services of six masalchis (masseurs), two bhishtis (watermen), eight khidmatgars (servants) and dozens of peons and sweepers. His dhobi (washerman) even boasts of an associate. Then there are others responsible for sundry jobs. In all, 130 employees are responsible for the welfare of the Governor and his family at the Raj Bhavan. And how much does it cost the state exchequer — Rs 175 lakh per year.

This army of 130 personal staff, however, does not include the heavy security paraphernalia around him, including his Z+ security cover and the expenses involved. It also does not include scores of other officers assigned to him by the

Punjab government and the Chandigarh Administration and his own salary or other perks.

The highest paid official in Rodrigues's staff is his Secretary M P Singh, a Punjab cadre IAS officer. He draws a salary similar to a secretary-level IAS officer.

The lowest paid are sweepers, masalchis, bhishtis, peons and the dhobi's associate. They draw salaries between Rs 2,620 to Rs 4,140, in addition to Rs 120 as special allowance.

Moreover, the entire staff at the Raj Bhavan is also paid monthly remunerations as per the rules and regulations of the Punjab government.

The Governor's personal staff also includes comptroller (Governor's household), two private secretaries, a chief medical officer, two superintendents, two personal assistants, five senior assistants, six store keepers, 9 drivers, three garage clerks, four PBX operators, four heads of 18 peons, four house bearers, a head jamadar, a camp jamadar, four assistant camp jamadars, six sweepers, cook and carpenter.

When asked, Secretary M P Singh justified the huge staff. "It's a legacy, which is being continued. A similar practice is being followed in other Raj Bhavans as well, but with a few changes."

Heading: Couple accused of duping students of Rs 12 lakh - Indian Express
Content:
The two-day strike by bank employees and officers, which ended on Thursday, has left the common man in a lurch. The banks will resume operations from Friday.

The call for strike was given by the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU), comprising all nine unions in the banking sector. Over 10 lakh bank employees across the country were opposing the privatisation or merger of public sector banks. They were also demanding the immediate implementation of the memorandum of understandings regarding pension options, compassionate appointments and wage revision.

As banking transactions were stalled for two days, several business establishments suffered heavy losses. "My entire business depends on daily transactions. But from last two days, no cheque has been cashed, which has created problems for me," said Sunil Verma, a resident of Sector 22.

Neelam Gulati, a homemaker, said: "I had to make a payment for the purchase order I placed two days ago. Now I do not have enough cash in hand and the dealer is not ready to accept cheques. I had to arrange for money from my friends."

Adding to their woes, even the ATMs at busy areas — Sector 17 and 22 — ran out of cash in the morning.

"After purchasing a mobile, I went to withdraw money as I fell short. But the ATM nearby was not functioning," said Sunil Thakur, an executive in a private company.

Those in emergency were the worst hit. "I had to take my mother to the hospital due to a sudden health problem. Due to the strike I did not have enough cash at hand. Later I learnt that the ATM in Sector 22 was also not functioning," said Shekhar

Mahajan, a resident of Sector 22.

On Thursday, the employees in Bank Square, Sector 17, took out a rally.

"Our next course of action will be decided in the next few days. If the government dioes not put an end to the mergers, acquisitions and privatisations, we can also launch an indefinite strike," said Vijay Magon, State Secretary of All-India Bank Officers' Confederation.

Heading: Ravinder confesses: It’s my money - Indian Express
Content:
A Couple has been accused of duping students of Rs 12 lakh by promising them jobs in foreign countries.

No arrests have been made so far in the case, which was registered on the complaint of a student, Jaswinder Singh, along with 14 others.

For the last one year, Kapil and his wife Bakshi Chaudhery had been running Travel and Sky Hotel Management and Air Hostesses Institute in Sector 35(C). They used to charge Rs 85,000 as fees per student.

It was alleged that in the middle of the course, the Chaudherys had closed down the institute and asked the students to go on a four-day holiday in July. When the students returned, they found the institute closed. Almost half of the students are girls, who had taken admission with an aim of becoming airhostesses.

"The accused belong to Sirsa. We are looking for their addresses and will conduct raids accordingly," said DSP B S Negi of the Economic Offences Wing of the police. A case under Section 420/120-B of the IPC has been registered against the couple.

"I had taken admission six months ago. They told us they will get us placed in Singapore, Australia or any other country we wished to go and assured us 100 per cent placements. They had also told us that half of our money will be returned after the completion of the course," said Jaswinder Singh.

During an examination in July, the couple asked the students to bring their own answersheets. "I grew suspicious. Then, as many of the students were told that they have got jobs in Jalandhar, they left. Others were told to take a holiday. We came back to find to find the institute closed," Singh said.

The other complainants who have been taken for a ride include Manpreet Singh, Sukhdeep Kaur, Ramandeep, Rajwinder Kaur, Ranjot Singh, Kaushal, Raj Kumar, Sahil, agandeep, Navdeep Kaur and Preeti.

Heading: At PU, 11,000 graduates fail to vote ‘correctly’ - Indian Express
Content:
Adding another twist to the 'cash-at-judge's-door' scam, Delhi-based hotelier Ravinder Singh, the prime accused in the case, admitted that the Rs 15 lakh, "wrongly" delivered to Justice Nirmaljit Kaur on August 13, belong to him.

But Singh clearly denied that the money was meant as bribe for the High Court judge, adding that he had given the money to Sanjeev Bansal, former Haryana Additional Advocate General and a co-accused in the case.

During custodial interrogation by the Central Bureau of Investigation today, Ravinder Singh confessed that Bansal had demanded the money on August 12.

"Ravinder said there was frequent exchange and lending of cash between him and Bansal. That is why he did not find it necessary to ask Bansal why he wanted the amount," said a source.

Ravinder has also denied that he had called Bansal in New Delhi on August 13 and asked him to deliver the cash. "Rather, he said Bansal had called him on August 12 as well as the next day. On August 13, the two had lunch at one of Ravinder's hotels after which Bansal left for Chandigarh," added the source.

Earlier, Ravinder had repeatedly denied that the cash had belonged to him. The accused will be produced in a special CBI court on September 27 as his police remand lapses on Saturday.

Heading: MC passes proposal on Sec 17 fun park... - Indian Express
Content:
At this year's Senate election at Panjab University's (PU) graduate constituency, out of the 66,000 votes being cast, 11,000 have turned out to be invalid.

PU, granted a five star status by NAAC, has a dubious record with its own graduates failing to cast votes correctly.

Further, the voters' list for the graduate constituency has not been revised since 1953 — when the Senate was constituted.

The main ground on declaring the votes invalid — the voters have not marked the preferences correctly. A voter, while giving first preference to a candidate, has to write numeric one against his/her name.

Most of the voters, whose votes have turned out to be invalid, have either written '1st', 'FIR', or 'One' against the candidates.

Asked about the invalid votes Panjab University Registrar S S Bari said: "This clearly shows the level of graduates being produced from the university. There are clear instructions at the back of the ballot paper on how to cast votes. So many invalid votes show the carelessness of the voters."

He added, "In the principal constituency, however, no invalid vote has been cast." The invalid votes have added to the concern of the contestants for whom every vote is important.

"It is the responsibility of the contestants to educate their voters on the way to cast a vote. There are many voters for whom language is a major hindrance," said Bari.

Further, over the years, there has been an addition to the voters' list since most of the students who have graduated, have become a voter. A mere Rs 15 has to be paid by a PU graduate become a voter.

The voters list has several voters who are dead, but their names have not been deleted as there has been no revision of the list.

Talking to Newsline, Ashok Goyal, a fellow at Panjab University, said: "Though a number of measures have been introduced to revamp the Senate, we have a long way to go. There is need to initiate further reforms."

Heading: PGI faculty ‘not happy’ over advertisements for new posts... - Indian Express
Content:
The nominated and elected councillors of the Municipal Corporation (MC) seem to be at loggerheads once again over the issue of construction of an amusement park in Sector 17.

Though the proposal was passed in the Finance and Contract Committee meeting held today, the nominated councillors did not seem very keen to implement the proposal. The issue will come up for debate in the House meeting to be held on Monday.

The amusement park was to mainly cater to children. Parents and guardians, who wish to go shopping in the sector, can leave their children at the park.

The nominated councillors, however, have other views. "Sector 17 is already very crowded and there is hardly space to park vehicles. Setting up an amusement park will further add to the chaos. It means an additional 200 to 300 vehicles in the sector. Without better facilities, how can an amusement park come up in the area?" asked a councillor.

Another councillor said: "Whether it is the Administration or the MC, arbitrary decisions are being taken. The Centra Mall, which was set up without adequate parking space, has resulted in creating chaos in the area. The price of land in Sector 17 is quite high. Why utilise such prime land for making an amusement park which will only add to the chaos?"

The elected councillors, however, were of the view that the park will add to the attractions of Sector 17, a hub for shoppers.

This is not the first time that nominated and elected councillors hold different views regarding a project. For instance, on the issue of the implementation of fines on encroachers, the councillors had opposing views.

While the elected councillors emphasised that the fine should be reduced to Rs 100, the nominated councillors debated that the amount should be enhanced to around Rs 1,000.

A final decision in this connection has not been reached yet.

Heading: ...All is not well at PGI research  front too - Indian Express
Content:
Without a professor since the last one decade, the Cardiology department at the Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER) is in the middle of a controversy regarding the pending appointments of senior faculty.

With the institute having invited applications to fill two posts of professors vacant at the department, the existing faculty allege that their credentials and experiences have been overlooked.

Take the case of Dr Yash Paul Sharma, head, Cardiology department, who faced the selection committee last year for promotion. He was the only candidate out of the four, who appeared before the panel for the post of additional professor and professor.

A year since the interview, Sharma's written representation to the authorities is still pending.

In his representations to the director, Sharma has requested that he be made professor, since no other candidate appeared for the interview.

He has appealed that his higher qualification and two years of post MD residency make him eligible for the post.

While the PGI has now advertised filling up two posts of professors, the authorities have overlooked the name of Sharma for the post. In fact, the general body meeting of the institute has not taken place even once this year, further delaying the matter.

Incidentally, Dr K K Talwar, Director, PGI is the only professor at the department and was serving the dual role of institute and department heads till he resigned from the chairmanship recently.

The next senior person, Sharma was then given the charge of head of department.

The department has nine faculty members at the moment, including Dr Talwar, while six posts are lying vacant. These include, besides two posts of professors, two posts each of additional professors and assistant professors.

The faculty, meanwhile, are resentful of the paucity of promotional avenues. "While the existing faculty members are not promoted or their promotion is long overdue, the institute has placed an advertisement for the new posts. This will surely demotivate the existing faculty," said a senior faculty.

Resentment over promotion is not new to this department. Not long ago, two other senior faculty members, Dr Anil Grover and Dr H K Bali, had left the institute to join private hospitals after they too, were not considered for the post of professor, lying vacant for long.

Amid these sentiments, PGI's advertisement, inviting application for the vacant posts ends on October 4.

A K Gupta, deputy director administration (DDA), meanwhile, said the institute has advertised for filling up the vacant posts of faculty at the department. "Dr Sharma was promoted as the additional professor last year and we have already placed an advertisement for the professors' post. The decision will be taken after that."

Heading: Provide bullet-proof vehicle to ADJ on security grounds: High Court to Punjab govt - Indian Express
Content:
Notwithstanding the discontent among the faculty at the department of Cardiology, Post Graduate Institute and Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), all is not well on the research front too. Hit with a staff crunch, the Cardiology department at the PGI, has not had any research scholar enrolling in its PhD programme since the last two decades.

Things have, however, begun to change in the last couple of years, and the department now has two PhD scholars, carrying their research in Cardiology.

Of these, one is associated with the department through the Experimental Medicine department.

The department did not have a single Ph D student with a cardiologist as the main guide since the last 20 years. "We did have one PhD student last year and two have enrolled themselves in this session. Things have started to change now and we are inviting more and more students to conduct their research," said a senior faculty.

Dr Yash Paul Sharma, head of department, meanwhile, said that while the doctoral students undertaking research on the clinical side are more than 10 at present, the department is making efforts to augment the number of PhD students.

A faculty can enroll three PhD candidates under him for research after a requisite period.

However, there has been a staff crunch at the hospital, owing to an increasing load of patients and due to some faculty leaving the hospital.

"Guiding research requires time. With nearly 250 patients visiting the out patient department everyday and no professor having been appointed in the last 15 years, research wprk definitely suffers," said a senior faculty.

Heading: Valet parking to be introduced at Centra Mall to ease chaos - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court today came down heavily on the Union of India (UOI) and the Punjab government for being irresponsible in issuing a bullet-proof vehicle to Additional District and Sessions Judge (ADJ) R K Sondhi, who had recently pronounced orders in the Beant Singh assassination case.

In light of the 'highly-sensitive case' handled by him, where he had awarded death sentence to two accused — Hawara and Balwant Singh, a demand for a bullet-proof vehicle was made.

More than one month ago, the High Court had directed the Centre to provide the vehicle. He is, however, yet to get it.

Taking a strong note, the HC took the Centre and Punjab government to task. "The role of respective governments in shying away from their responsibilities to provide proper security aids to a judicial officer, who dealt with a 'highly-sensitive case', is clearly noticeable. The counsels for Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh have not disputed that Sondhi requires security.

It is totally disheartening to notice that despite categorical directions, rejecting the stand of the Centre and direction to provide a bullet-proof car to a judicial officer with further direction to do so within one month from the date of order, the needful has not been done."

The HC has sought name of the concerned officer, who is responsible for non-compliance of the order. The counsel for UOI has been directed to supply the name of the officer within 24 hours so that showcause notices can be issued as to why contempt of court proceedings be not initiated against them.

The HC also strongly deplored the conduct of the Punjab government, which was directed to provide a bullet-proof vehicle till the time UOI does not provide the same.

"The Punjab government also not acted in a fair and proper manner. We are not concerned as to who all have been given bullet-proof cars," held the court.

The High Court has also directed Punjab to provide for a bullet-proof car within 24 hours even if a vehicle already given to an officer has to be withdrawn. The demand for keeping a personal weapon by Sondhi has also been allowed to the effect that he can get a personal weapon from Phillaur by paying the charges.

Heading: Biscuit company to pay up Rs 25,000 after packet found grossly underweight - Indian Express
Content:
In an attempt to wriggle-out of the increasing parking chaos around Centra Mall, the mall authorities had devised a new way to tackle the problem. In a first of its kind, the management is likely to introduce valet parking from September 30.

Around 12 drivers have been employed, who will be responsible for handling cars of upper, middle and lower segments. A visitor can take his vehicle till the entrance of the parking lot, where the attendant shall either direct him to park it in the basement of the mall, or in case it is full, the attendant shall be taking away the vehicle to a nearby parking lot giving a token/ slip to the owner.

Manoj Garg, who heads the local operations of Centra Mall, said: "The valet parking concept is definitely going to ease the parking chaos. Moreover, a new parking — with a capacity of 700 cars — has also come up nearby. Many industrialists, who don't have a parking space in front of or near their premises are also using the same parking lot."

With the increasing popularity of the mall, the chaos around it is also increasing manifold, worsening during the evening hours. A multiplex with nearly 1,100 seats, around 60 shops, food courts but the parking space available at Centra Mall is merely for 200 cars, constructed in its basement.

Heading: 167 kg of heroin seized in Punjab in last 10 months: PIL - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed Bector Food Specialties to pay Rs 25,000 as compensation after a packet of biscuits was found to be grossly underweight. While Rs 5,000 shall be paid to the complainant, the rest will be deposited with the State Legal Services Authority. The company has also been directed to pay Rs 500 as costs of litigation.

The complainant, Harjinder Pal Singh, a resident of Sector 49, stated that he had purchased 10 packets of biscuits in March 2008.

On reaching home, he weighed the pack and found it to be 70 grams although the printed weight was 100 grams. Alleging unfair trade practices, Singh moved the consumer forum.

In its reply, Bector Food Specialties outrightly denied that the complainant had purchased the packs. "In the absence of a bill, it cannot be ascertained whether the goods were purchased or not. The possibility of the customer buying duplicate or sub-standard goods is always there," the company said.

The company's counsel also argued that as the company has its manufacturing unit at Badli, New Delhi, and branch offices at Ludhiana and Phillaur — therefore, the UT consumer forum has no jurisdiction to try the case.

But the forum saw no merit in this argument. The packet was also weighed and found out to be only 78.980 grams. The forum also found that there is no evidence to suggest the packet is spurious.

"Simply because they have been caught selling underweight biscuit packets, they appear to have concocted this false defence, which cannot succeed. The company may be manufacturing and selling thousands of such packets daily and earning lakhs of rupees every month. An individual's loss may not amount to much but the actual loss to the society and consumers is considerably large," the forum observed.

Heading: ... and allots a parking lot to Bar members - Indian Express
Content:
In the last 10 months, various wings of the Punjab Police, Border Security Force (BSF) and Narcotics Cell have seized a total of 167 kg heroin in the state.

Between May 11 and 16, 123 kg of heroin has been seized from various parts.

This was revealed in a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by one Baldev Singh Sirsa, a resident of Amritsar.

In the PIL, he had alleged that there is a strong nexus between the politicians of Punjab and the smugglers. The High Court has directed the petitioner to appear in person in the next hearing.

Sisra has sought an independent probe by an agency like the CBI into the smuggling of intoxicants.

Sisra has also provided a sequence of events of the several seizures (see box).

The petitioner has submitted that during the hearing of a bail application of one of the accused, names of two Akali Dal leaders — Charanjit Singh Atwal and Sukhbir Singh Badal had surfaced.

Heading: Special train for pilgrims leaves for Nanded - Indian Express
Content:
The Finance and Contract Committee of the Municipal Corporation today approved the allotment of the District Court Complex parking area in Sector 17 to the District Bar Association. The rent of the open ground in Manimajra was fixed at Rs 6,000. The meeting was held under the chairmanship of Mayor Pardeep Chhabra.

A development plan for Maloya village was also approved. The committee has allowed for inviting an expression of interest for organising events in the Sector 17 Plaza.

They also allowed for the use of community centres for the Residents Welfare Association. An estimate for the construction of a community centre in Sector 39 was also passed.

The committee also decided to purchase as many as 100 garbage containers. They also approved the rough estimate for the development of a green belt in Sector 56.

An estimate for the purchase of five thermal imaging cameras, recovery vans (one big and one small), a power operated chain saw and mobile unit with diesel engine was also passed.

The committee also decided that interlocking paver blocks would be put up in front of Government Senior Secondary School, Sector 45. A parking lot will be constructed with paver blocks in front of the government dispensary in Sector 45. The committee fixed an amount of Rs 30 lakh as the reserve price of paid parking areas at Fun Republic in Manimajra.

The members who attended the meeting included: Davinder Singh Babla, Pallav Mukharjee, Chander Mukhi Sharma, Vijay Singh Rana and Surinder Kumar Jagota. Municipal Commissioner Dr Roshan Sunkaria, Additional Commissioner PK Sharma, Joint Commissioner T P S Phoolka, Assistant Commissioner Parminderpal Singh, Secretary Samwartak Singh, Chief Engineer S K Bansal, Superintending Engineer Public Health RK Goyal, Yogesh Gupta among others.

Heading: Senior citizens lead the walk at Sukhna - Indian Express
Content:
The Sangat Yatra special train to Nanded, for the 300th year celebrations of the guruship of Sri Guru Granth Sahib, left Chandigarh at 9.05 pm on Thursday.

The train with 15 second-class sleeper coaches, with around 1,300 passengers, is scheduled to reach Nanded at 7.30 am on September 27.

Sarbjit Singh Young Khalsa Sewa Society distributed fruits and organised a special langar for the passengers and their relatives.

Also, Chandigarh-Nanded-Chandigarh AC super fast special trains will leave Chandigarh on Friday and daily from October 1 to November 10 at 9.25 am and reach Nanded at 5.40 pm the next day. For the return journey, the train will depart from Nanded on September 28. From October 3 to November 12, a train will run daily at 7.45 am and reach Chandigarh at 4 pm the next day.

Heading: Mothers not keen on mid-day meals - Indian Express
Content:
A senior citizens brisk-walk competition was organised by the Chandigarh Police in association with the Chandigarh Senior Citizen Association at 7 am on Thursday at the Sukhna Lake. S K Jain, IGP, Chandigarh flagged off the competition. Over 250 senior citizens participated in the event.

A total of five events were organised for both men and women. S S Srivastava, IPS, SSP, Chandigarh welcomed the senior citizens and listened to their suggestions to help the police serve them better.

An informal interaction session was also held with the senior citizens. Various problems regarding traffic, paying guests, landlord-tenant disputes and visits by beat officers were raised.

IGP Jain also requested the senior citizens of the city to make use of the 24-hour toll-free helpline 1090, installed in Police Control Room of Sector 9.

Heading: KB DAV all set to stage Ramayana - Indian Express
Content:
The initiative of the Education department to involve mothers to contribute in mid-day meals has failed to find any takers. While the department is hopeful of its success, school authorities feel otherwise.

According to the project, the department will invite mothers to cook mid-day meals to be supplied to several government schools across the city. The project, which was the brain child of former Director of Public Instructions (Schools), S K Setia, has not found any takers even months after it was announced.

"It is practically not possible to implement the idea. In this fast-paced life, it is difficult to take out time and be a part of such a project,"

said a teacher at the Government Model High School, Sector 28.

Despite of being a volunteer venture, not many women had come forward to participate in the scheme, which was launched following complaints of unhygienic meals being served to students.

"It was a good but impossible effort. Had somebody come forward, the quality of food would have certainly been better," said Amarjeet Kaur, another teacher.

Accordint to Principal Sukhneer Sekhon of Government Senior Secondary School in Sector 27, the project had failed to take off, as the message had not reached most women.

"More efforts should have been made to involve mothers in the venture. Teacher-parent interaction would have solved the purpose to a large extent."

Parents too feel that the project was not a viable one. "Paucity of time is the main reason why nobody volunteered," says Simran Dhillon, a mother.

Deputy District Education Officer Chanchal Singh said: "The project is not workable in a city like Chandigarh where usually both parents are working."

Heading: Student council takes oath at PU - Indian Express
Content:
The students of KB DAV School, Sector 7, will be staging the Ramayana on September 30. Guests from Pakistan will be witnessing the same. The Ram Leela is being directed by Sunil Sharma, a city-based photojournalist. A dress rehearsal was held on Thursday in the school premises. During the programme, students enacted various scenes from the epic including Sita Haran, Lanka Dehan and Shravan's Pitrabhakti.  

The Ram Leela team of the school has children of political bigwigs playing different roles. Arjun Surjewala, son of Minister of Power, Randeep Singh Surjewala, has been given the role of Vibhishan. "The best thing about the character is that it has shades of grey. Participating in the show has deepened my knowledge about the epic, especially about the character that I am playing," said the Class IX student. 

The role of Ravana is being played by Mohit Chaudhary, son of Dharamvir Singh, Chief Parliamentary Secretary of Haryana. Talking about his character, Mohit said, "There are different perceptions of Ravana. For us, he is a villain but for the people of Lanka, he was their hero. His intellect was commendable. I feel that his is a very powerful and challenging role to enact."

Heading: Court vacates stay on appointment of 14,000 teachers in rural Punjab - Indian Express
Content:
The swearing-in ceremony for the elected student council was held today at the Panjab University. The elected panel of SOPU-ABVP alliance was made to take oath by Dean Students Welfare (DSW) Professor Naval Kishore. Also present on the occasion were PU Vice-Chancellor Professor R C Sobti and Dean Students Welfare (Women) Professor Nishtha Jaswal. While Prof Sobti apprised the students of their responsibilities, Prof Jaswal made all the department representatives (DR's) take oath.

Reacting to the demands regarding an increase in the allotted budget to the student council, Prof Sobti announced an increase of 10 per cent in the budget. The budget allocated at present to the student council is Rs 1 lakh. Speaking on the occasion, Prof Sobti said, "I am very happy that the elections went off peacefully. I have very high expectations from the new student council and want them to work hard

towards the development of the university and their fellow students."

Addressing the problems being faced by the students on the campus in terms of parking, Prof Sobti said that the varsity is planning to have a centralised parking and is seeking funds for the same.

Heading: Food advisory committees in Punjab soon: Minister - Indian Express
Content:
IN a relief for rural students, the Punjab and Haryana High Court (HC) on Thursday vacated the stay over the issuance of appointment letters to nearly 14,000 teachers in Punjab.

The appointment letters were not issued in light of the stay ordered by the HC, following a petition which had termed the selection illegal. The court, however, clarified that the final selection of the teachers will be subject to the outcome of the decision to the petition. On Thursday, the stay was vacated after Advocate General of Punjab, H S Mattewal, highlighted the sorry state of affairs in rural schools, most of which were functioning without teachers. Several teachers had also filed petitions in the court, demanding the quashing of Clause V of an ad issued by the Punjab government on September 5, 2007.

Punjab had advertised for the recruitment of teachers in the rural areas. A clause gave five extra marks to candidates who had passed their middle and metric exams from rural schools. The petitioners had challenged that as per merit, they were way ahead of rural teachers for the posts.

Heading: Civic staff defers snapping of basic services again - Indian Express
Content:
Assures simplifying PFA licencing procedures to benefit traders

The Punjab government will soon constitute food advisory committees at all the district headquarters in the state under its ongoing initiative to check adulteration of food products.

State minister for Health and Family Welfare Laxmi Kanta Chawla announced this while chairing a special meeting of the members and representatives of various food products and dairy associations of the state in Mohali.

She said the traders and health authorities of the concerned districts will be involved in these panels, which will meet regularly to discuss and take up the cases of food adulteration in their respective areas.

She also assured that the Punjab Food Act (PFA) licensing procedure will be simplified for the convenience of the traders.

Around 250 members of the various sweet sellers, confectionary, milkmen and karyina associations in the state were present during the meeting that was organised by the Health department with the objective to check adulteration in food items and dairy products.

All the trader associations welcomed the initiatives of the Health department and assured the Minister for extending their full support to check food adulteration in the coming festive season.

During the meeting, the representatives of these associations discussed various key issues with the minister and also gave suggestions on how to curb food adulteration.

Chawla urged them to ensure that no kind of food adulteration takes place as it was the collective responsibility of the traders and Health department to provide clean and healthy eatables.

She said the department officers have already been told to nab the "big fish" who indulge in malpractices rather than catching the small time vendors.

She also asked the members of the traders associations not to encourage any kind of corruption and favouritism and in case such incident comes to their notice, they must inform her directly.

Heading: 10-yr-old son of landlord kidnapped - Indian Express
Content:
BULL'S DEATH: Mohali ADC buys week's time to get FIR cancelled

THE employees of the Mohali Municipal Council (MC), who are on an indefinite strike and dharna since September 18, deferred their action to snap the essential services in Mohali once again on Thursday.

In order to intensify their ongoing stir and pressurise the district Administration to budge under its pressure,

the MC Employees' Union on Wednesday had threatened to suspend indefinitely the power and water supply, besides cleanliness services and streetlights in the entire city from Thursday.

The union had also threatened to spread their strike across the state by taking along the employees of all other civic bodies in the state.

Sensing the trouble, Mohali Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC) Jaspal Mittal today held a meeting with the 21-member action committee of the striking civic staffers and assured them that their demands would be fulfilled within a week.

Municipal Councillor Harman Preet Singh Prince told Newsline that the ADC told the action committee leaders to recommend the cancellation of the FIR against MC employees to Mohali SSP.

The ADC asked the striking MC employees to allow the official work to restore. On this, the action committee told the ADC that it will decide the matter at its general body meeting tomorrow.

However, the Municipal Council employees accepted the ADC's request to suspend their plan to snap essential services till next Wednesday.

Heading: Counselling for vacant BDS seats cancelled amidst controversy - Indian Express
Content:
Ransom of Rs 30 lakh demanded from the family

The ten-year old son of a landlord in Partapra village near Jalandhar was kidnapped today morning from near his house. Sources say a ransom of Rs 30 lakh has been demanded from the family.

It is learnt that though the family wanted to keep the matter secret, the villagers informed the police, which launched a massive search operation. This has reportedly alerted the kidnapper too. The family and the police are hesitating to say anything on the issue.

Tejinder Singh, a Class IV student in Manav Sehyog School, had gone to his farm house on the outskirts of the village, at about 6.30 am today. Tejinder had taken the bicycle of his friend, living in the neighbourhood.

Tejinder's father Ranbir Singh owns about 25 acres land, valued in crores. Ranbir's brother Daljit Singh is an NRI. After about an hour, when the other boy came to take his bicycle, the family told him that Tejinder hadn't returned yet. The boy went to Tejinder's farm house. He found his cycle lying near a school in the village. Tejinder was not to be seen anywhere.

The boy informed the family. By that time, Tejinder's mother Amarjit Kaur had received a call from the kidnapper, who demanded Rs 30 lakhs as ransom for releasing the boy. Sources said the caller demanded that the money be paid by 11 am the same day. It is learnt that the caller also told Tejinder to speak to his mother on phone.

When contacted, SSP PK Rai said that he could not comment on the issue. It is learnt that the caller didn't call again and switched off his phone, as the police is monitoring every move.

Heading: Woman murdered for refusing sex-determination test - Indian Express
Content:
Parents, students raise slogans, object to 'faulty' norms

The second extended counselling for admission to vacant seats in various dental colleges in the state had to be cancelled by Baba Farid University of Medical Sciences amidst high drama, after parents and students raised slogans and objected to the controversial new norms laid for admission.

Sources say that the students and their parents had gone to Government Medical College, Patiala, in the morning. The students were seeking admission to the vacant government/management quota seats in various dental colleges, after the surrender of All-India quota seats for the prestigious BDS course.

The students and their parents gathered at the venue at about 8 am. However, the process did not start till 10 am, making them restless.

When it started, the authorities conducting the counselling under the charge of Principal, Government Dental College, Amritsar, informed the students that no fresh counselling would be done for students who have already obtained admission in BDS course in various colleges.

The authorities further stated that no student already admitted would be allowed to change the college. Also, those who had taken a seat under the management quota would not be allowed a government seat.

The authorities also informed that only fresh students with marks less than 400 would be allowed to participate in the counselling. Those already admitted were not allowed to participate in the counselling today.

On this, students and their parents raised slogans against the varsity and did not allow the counselling to take place. A number of these students, who ranked higher in merit, were seeking admission to vacant government seats, which have lower fee. They objected to the 'faulty' norms laid down by Baba Farid University. The varsity authorities were forced to cancel the process today.

Harvinder Singh, whose daughter was seeking admission to a government quota seat, said, "How can the authorities not allow students with higher merit and more marks to get a government seat, which has a lower fee structure." Added Jitender Kaur, another parent, "The authorities cannot deny a good government quota seat to a student higher in merit, and grant it to a student lower in merit."

Over 145 seats had been rendered vacant in various government and private dental Colleges in the state, after the surrender of All-India quota seats in the BDS course. While the annual fee for a management quota seat in a private dental college is Rs 2.3 lakh, the fee for a government quota seat in the same private college is Rs 63,000. However, most candidates wanted seats in government colleges, where the annual fee is only Rs 13,000.

Heading: Farmers’ organisations oppose nuclear deal - Indian Express
Content:
A woman who refused to undergo a sex determination test, as demanded by her husband and in-laws, was allegedly murdered at Raungli village about five months ago. Her corpse is untraceable till now. Police have registered a case after investigation over the last five months. The woman's husband and in-laws are absconding.

The police have registered a case under Section 302 and 201 of IPC, pertaining to murder. The complaint has been filed by the victim Charanjeet Kaur's father Balwinder Singh. The accused named in the FIR are her husband Mahinder Pal Singh, and her in-laws Kulwant Singh, Harjeet Kaur, Karamjeet Kaur and Amarjit Singh.

According to police, Charanjeet was married to Mahinder in April 2008. She was in her third month of pregnancy. According to the FIR, Mahinder's family wanted to determine the sex of the foetus, for which Charanjeet was not willing. The FIR says that Charanjeet overheard their discussion and informed her parents.

"She feared that if her in-laws found out that she (Charanjeet Kaur) was carrying a girl child, she would have to undergo an abortion. Thus, she took a stand against her in-laws", reads the FIR.

Her father Balwinder Singh said, "Almost a week after Charanjeet Kaur went missing, her in-laws informed me that she was untraceable. They claimed that she left the house without telling anyone. I suspect that they killed my daughter and threw her body in the water", he alleged in the FIR registered police station Tripuri.

Police have dispatched teams to arrest the accused persons. SP City RK Sharma confirmed that the case has been registered.

Heading: SAD (A) leader speaks out against Makkar - Indian Express
Content:
Adopting a strict stand against the Indo-US nuclear deal, various farmers' organizations under the banner of Jamhoori Kissan Sabha, Punjab, today held a demonstration against the policies of the government and gheraoed the office of the Deputy Commissioner.

The farmer leaders sought immediate arrangements for paddy procurement, Minimum Support Price (MSP) of Rs 1,200 per quintal for paddy and waiver of loans. They also voiced their discontent over the privatization of the power sector.

Addressing mediapersons, Rattan Singh Randhawa of Kissan Sabha of Jamhoori Kissan Sabha stated that the farmers were opposing the nuclear deal, as it was likely to make power costlier. "If the deal is implemented, power will cost as high as Rs 7.50 per unit. It will also jeopardise our foreign policy," he claimed. Randhawa stressed that hydel power was cheaper and more beneficial for the people.

Heading: Shiksha abhiyan directionless in state - Indian Express
Content:
SAD (A) Panch Pradhani General Secretary Baldev Singh Sirsa and Baljit Singh Gulshan have charged that SGPC president Avtar Singh Makkar with using the services of the SGPC employees to canvass for his kin Gulwinder Singh and other SAD (B) candidates contesting the Municipal Council elections from Moga.

The duo have also approached the Sikh Gurudwara Judicial Commission against them. Sirsa has sought the removal of Makkar and other SGPC office-bearers, charging them with misuse of gurudwara funds and violation of the religious code of conduct. Makkar has termed these allegations against him and the SGPC staff as baseless.

Heading: Dhumal, Virbhadra clash over Mandi medical college - Indian Express
Content:
With six directors in eight months, it's no wonder that only 16 pc of budget spent so far

During the past eight months of administrative transfers, it is the Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) that has suffered the most, with frequent transfers of its state project director (SPD).

A look at the roll call of SPDs shows that ever since the BJP government took over, the department has seen five directors, whereas the project has not seen much headway in terms of annual plan proposed for the year, where under the proposed 20 interventions, only 16 per cent of the budget could be utilised so far.

The sixth SPD, Rajesh Sharma, who has been posted in SSA in the latest reshuffle is yet to take over.

Facts available with The Indian Express show that with half of the financial year already gone, the SSA has only been able to use up Rs 2,344.606 lakh of the Rs 14,398.725 lakh that were projected as the budget estimate for the year.

The Government of India has released its first grant of Rs 909.57 lakh, but the state has not yet contributed its share. Sources in the department said slow execution of works in the first half of the year is likely to have an impact on the release of funds from the Centre for the next half, bringing down the year's overall performance altogether.

When contacted, Principal Secretary, Education, P.C. Dhiman said, "The department does not depend on a single person, so there is no need to worry if the post of SPD was not stable. We would make up for the time lost."

Interestingly, the department's report till September 15 shows a blank under the head of "teaching, learning equipment", though the state in the past couple of years had tried to improve the learning levels of children through such special aids. A budget of Rs 139 lakh was proposed to be spent under this head.

Various other schemes that have suffered due to frequent change of guard and had been on the priority in the past are education for out-of-school children and girls' education, under which only Rs 3.6 lakh of the proposed Rs 724 lakh have been spent.

For education of the disabled, a mere Rs 13.6 lakh out of the proposed Rs 305.7 lakh have been spent.

The only head where some work has been done is civil works and repairs.

Heading: Jakhu ropeway: Firm to face FIR in case of laxity - Indian Express
Content:
Former chief minister Virbhadra Singh has crossed swords with chief minister Prem Kumar Dhumal over opening of a new medical college at Mandi, a issue which has already started creating unrest in the district, ahead of the upcoming Lok Sabha elections.

While the state government has taken a decision for opening a new medical college in the private sector, the opposition parties, including the Congress, are insisting on opening the college in the government sector.

In Mandi yesterday, Dhumal defended the government move and declared that instead of one, the government will be opening two new medical colleges in the district, both in the private sector.

Mandi district already has one private dental college and an engineering college in Sundernagar. From the next academic session, a new IIT will also become functional at post-graduate college, Mandi.

The medical college project, initially conceived by the Congress government ahead of the state Assembly elections, was basically a private sector initiative. But two Cabinet ministers — Kaul Singh Thakur and Rangila Ram Rao — got the private proposal dropped and instead favoured a medical college in the government sector.

Now, not only political parties, social activists and citizens are also demanding that the BJP government reverts to the proposal for a government sector medical college.

Last week, Virbhadra Singh, during his visit to Mandi, had accused the BJP government of reversing the decision. Today, after Dhumal announced the second college, Virbhadra Singh said, "The second college is welcome. More Himachali youth will be able to get an opportunity to get into the medical profession. But, there can't be a substitute to a government college and hospital. The people in Himachal cannot afford health care at a heavy cost."

The Chief Minister's stand on the medical college issue, in fact, has its basis on the BJP's larger policy for opening the state's doors to leading private institutions. The government has also appointed consultants for making a survey on the feasibility of at least five medical colleges in the private sector.

He asserts that the medical college project in the private sector will come up in a time-bound manner. The state government will have its right to fix the fee and also charges for the services at the hospital. Keeping in view the state's fiscal health, a government sector medical college will remain a distant dream for Mandi, he says.

The Chief Minister says that a Rs 750-crore international airport has been proposed to be constructed in Balh valley, while Rs 760 crore were being spent on the creation of infrastructure and campus to start the functioning of the IIT on priority.

He alleged that the previous government had opened an engineering college in the government sector without creating any basic infrastructure and budgetary provisions at Sundernagar. He said the students there were facing difficulty in getting proper engineering educational facilities.

"The Congress has misled the people of Mandi in the name of a government medical college after declaration of the Vidhan Sabha elections on October 10, 2007. The notification was issued much later just to gain political mileage in the Vidhan Sabha elections," he alleged.

Heading: IPS officers allege anomalies in pay-scale, meet CM - Indian Express
Content:
The threat posed to hotels and houses on Jakhu Hill due to execution of the ropeway project has come to the notice of the government, which today directed officials of the forest department to register an FIR against the company in case of any laxity.

A complaint was also made to the police at Police Station Sadar by Sanjeev Kuthiala about the threat to his house near the ropeway site and adjoining hotels, said Station House Officer, Shakuntla Sharma.

"On a report of the forest department, we are taking action against the company under Section 133 of the CrPC. A report of the life-threatening structures in the area would be prepared and submitted to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) on Friday. The SDM would hear the case and give directions for further action," said the SHO.

Acting upon the reports and complaints of the threat posed by the ropeway project, the Forest Secretary directed the Divisional Forest Officer (DFO), Shimla, to personally visit the spot and assess the damage.

A spokesperson of the government said the DFO has been directed to ensure that heavy earth-moving machinery is not deployed at the place, as it is not allowed to be used in this fragile green belt and that work should not be allowed till protective structures are put in place.

As per the police survey of the spot, danger looms large over the adjoining houses and hotels in the Richmond area, where a crack in the retaining wall erected by the company has threatened the safety of a few government houses as well.

For the past over 18 years, the ropeway project has been hanging fire, after which the previous Congress government allotted this project to Jagson International. But, subsequently, a consortium formed by Jagson also ran into trouble. However, finally the government allowed the lead company to induct a new technical partner and execute the ropeway project in a time-bound manner.

Last year, the then chief minister, Virbhadra Singh, had laid the foundation stone for the project. There were also issues about the felling of green trees and clearances of the Environment Ministry were sought. The Ministry finally gave permission to axe 31 trees in the area where the project is coming up.

Heading: INLD kicks off its election campaign - Indian Express
Content:
Indian Police Services (IPS) officers in the Himachal cadre are upset with the "serious anomalies" that have allegedly cropped up in their new pay-scales on the basis of the Sixth Pay Commission report.

The IPS Officers' Association today met Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal and pointed out that the latest notification, issued by the government, has put the police officers at a loss.

However, as compared to them, they said the IAS officers are understood to have got two increments, resulting in anomalies in the scales.

Said S.R. Mardi, an office-bearer of the IPS Association, "We have explained the issue to the Chief Minister and asked him to take up the matter with the Central government. If the notification issued now is implemented, the IPS officers will suffer injustice."

Sources said the Chief Minister has assured the IPS officers to take up their cause with the Union Home Ministry and has reportedly assured them to raise the issue with Union Home Minister Shivraj Patil, who is visiting Shimla on September 29 for addressing a meeting of the northern states' council.

Chief ministers of Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Delhi, Uttaranchal and representatives of the Jammu and Kashmir government will be attending the meeting.

Said senior GAD officials, "The meeting will be held at HPTDC's Hotel Peterhoff. All arrangements have been made."

Heading: BJP dilly-dallies on alliance - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) kicked off its election campaign for the forthcoming Lok Sabha election by giving a clarion call to dethrone Congress-led government.

Announcing several sops for all sections of the society, INLD supremeo Om Prakash Chautala accused the Congress for its failure at all fronts and asked the party workers and participants to work whole-heartedly to wipe out the Congress governmen. This samman rally was organised to mark the 95th birth anniversary of late Devi Lal.

It assumed political significance as Ajay Chautala, son of former Haryana chief minister Om Prakash Chautala, is a strong contender for Bhiwani Lok Sabha seat.

In a bid to woo farmers, Om Prakash Chautala announced that woods from the plants planted by them would be treated as agriculture produce, once the INLD is voted to power.

In addition, the loansfrom the cooperative banks would be available at 4 per cent rate of interest and maximum support price of wheat would be Rs 1,400 per quintal. Seeking white paper on power bill scheme involving Rs 1,600 crore, he accused the Haryana Congress for befooling the farmers and said no farmer has benefited out of it.

He said no agricultural land will be allowed to be used for setting up Special Economic Zone (SEZ).

Our government will ensure Rs 1 crore per acre to the farmers whose land falls under National Capital Region (NCR) and Rs 50 lakh in other parts of Haryana, he added.

The old age pension would be increased to Rs 700. He assured wheat would be available at Rs 700 per quintal to the poor under INLD regime.

He favoured 30 per cent reservation for Backward Classes, right from Panchayat to Lok Sabha election.

He said it would not be mandatory to fill the ST-38 by the businessmen.

He lambasted the Congress-led government for the delay in the completion of Satluj-Yamuna Canal (SYL). The Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal recalled the sacrifices of Devi Lal during freedom struggle and said he fought for the cause of farmers and downtrodden people of the society. JD(U) president Sharad Yadav also held Congress responsible for price hike, lawlessness, increase in terrorist activities and unemployment.

Heading: Sonia Gandhi to distribute free plots among poor on Oct 2 - Indian Express
Content:
The final decision will be taken by the High Command

Ahead of the crucial state executive meet of the BJP at Sonepat tomorrow, where vice-president Venkaiyah Naidu will be present, the party remains divided on the issue of alliance with another party for the next Lok Sabha polls. While one section of the party leaders favour an alliance with the Indian National Lok Dal (INLD), another section is against it.
