The former JCT striker had to battle poor refereeing, horrible ground conditions and an unorganised set-up in the Calcutta Football League (CFL) where he returned with just two goals from five matches, not the kind of start he was looking for in Kolkata, where he had begun his club football career with Mohun Bagan in 2002.

Lamenting the poor infrastructure, Chhetri said little had changed ever since.

"I'm representing one of the best clubs in the country and I am feeling proud of that fact... However, the football scene in Kolkata has not change an iota. It's not that great... still not organised. The recently-concluded CFL saw some poor refereeing and the ground conditions were horrible," the 24-year-old said.

However, the Indian striker said it should not be an excuse as he braces up for their I-League encounter against Chirag United tomorrow.

"We are all professional players. I must not crib about this and give my best shot in the I-League. I've not set any specific goals, I'll go match by match and put my best foot forward. After all, it's a team game... when you score a goal there are others behind it," Chhetri, who had scored seven goals for his former team JCT in the last season's I-League said. JCT, for the record, had finished third in the last edition.

Asked if it would be easy for them this time since beside him, the side boast of five national players (goalkeeper Subrata Pal, Renedy Singh, Mehrajuddin Wadoo, Surkumar Singh, Syed Rahim Nabi), Chhetri said: "The game is not about individuals. You bring on Ronaldinho for that matter... but if you don't play as a unit, you cannot be successful."

The AIFF Player of the Year 2007, Chhetri, said their team was undergoing a change at the moment and one must not expect immediate result.

"We have had change of coaches. It takes time for somebody to acclimatise himself. Once you get into the rhythm it becomes easy. It does not happen overnight. Rozario is a wonderful coach to have. He is very motivating. I wish him luck," Chhetri said.

"The important thing is to start well. The first 10-15 minutes will be very crucial. Taking the lead at that point of time may well decide the course of the match. All teams are equally competitive and we are not taking anybody lightly," he said referring to their opening tie against Chirag United.

Chhetri, who makes a healthy combination upfront with captain Baichung Bhutia in the national team, says at club-level it's different.

"We are all professionals, we know our roles when playing for the country or the respective clubs," said Chhetri.

The East Bengal-Mohun Bagan rivalry on the field has been healthy over the years but when the fans engage in riots off the field it becomes a concern, felt Chhetri, who had joined the red-and-gold brigade following his stupendous show in the AFC Challenge Cup.

Urging the fans to behave and support the sport in true spirit, Chhetri added: "The rivalry is well known. But I feel sad when fans engage in riots after a match. They must realise that it's a sport after all... one has to win or lose. This should not happen."

At 23 he is considered as India's best but the East Bengal striker thinks his best is yet to come.

"I've many memorable moments but I don't remember of the most cherishing one. There's more to come, and I'm looking forward to it."

Heading: Police announce security measures for Pujas - Indian Express
Content:
The state government on Thursday decided that recruitment of all government staffers, including constables and clerks, will strictly take place through the Public Service Commission (PSC). The decision was taken at the state cabinet summit. Earlier, state government employees belonging to Group A and Group B and some categories in Group C were recruited through the PSC. Rest used to be recruited through employment exchange. Now, till up to the panchayat level, employees will be recruited through the PSC.

"This will bring more transparency to the system," said Asim Dasgupta, State Finance Minister.

Heading: Minority Affairs Dept gets govt nod for recruitment - Indian Express
Content:
To ensure security during the upcoming Durga Puja celebrations, Kolkata Police Commissioner Gautam

Mohan Chakrabarti announced a slew of measures, including security cover for senior citizens, mobile medical vans and missing persons' units.

"Senior citizens can avail of medical care during the Pujas through a tie-up between the Kolkata Police and the Apollo Gleneagles Hospital by dialling the toll-free number 1066. They can also report any untoward incident to the police. Six major Puja pandals will have a medical cell comprising doctors, nurses and paramedics," Chakrabarti said.

The police have also arranged medical vans to conduct patrolling of various areas.

While the police will offer four vans, five are being provided by NGOs, he said.

"Through tie-ups with corporates, we are also coming out with 5.5 lakh badges to be distributed free of cost to children. Parents can write down their details and contact number on the badge, which will make it easier to trace missing children.

Two police vans of the missing persons' squad will be deployed, one each in north and south Kolkata," said the commissioner.

The city police has also tied up with mobile telephone provider Vodafone for regular traffic updates during the Pujas.

Heading: GJM back to bullying tactics - Indian Express
Content:
The state Minority Affairs and Madrasa Education (MAME) Department has obtained the much-awaited nod from the state Cabinet to start its temporary recruitment process in the state on Thursday.

To fill up the posts of the department's offices at district level, which will soon be set up by the government, the Cabinet has decided to recruit retired government employees.

"West Bengal will be the only state in the country which will have district offices of MAME at places where minority communities form 25 per cent of the population," said Minority Affairs Minister Abdus Sattar.

The recruitment process entails employing for various posts — ranging from district officers who would be running minority affairs, to Group D staff. In all these cases, the cabinet approved a period of engagement that ranges from six months to one year, while engagement on contractual basis will be allowed up to the age of 62 years.

Twelve districts in Bengal are slated to have MAME offices, namely Malda, Murshidabad, South and North Dinajpur, Coochbehar, Nadia, West and East Midnapore, Howrah, Burdwan, Birbhum, Darjeeling, Jalpaiguri, Bankura Purulia and Hooghly.

The offices will be responsible for duties like preparation and maintenance of database of all Central and state government schemes, preparation of minority development plans, education schemes, loan schemes, etc.

Heading: Fresh ragging cases crop up despite strict actions - Indian Express
Content:
After hinting last week that it may relax the ongoing non-cooperation movement in the Hills to create a conducive atmosphere for the second round of tripartite talks in November, the Gorkha Janmukti Morcha (GJM) has again donned an inflexible approach.

Terming the first round of talks involving the Centre and the West Bengal government positive, GJM spokesperson Binay Tamang told The Indian Express: "We are not thinking of offering any relaxation in our movement. If the second round of talks shows progress, we may consider it." The decision seems to have reached at the party's central committee meeting, where a wait and watch approach was agreed upon.

He added, "At the moment, we are busy preparing for celebrations to mark the first anniversary of the GJM's formation on October 7, which would involve a series of functions at Darjeeling, Kurseong, Kalimpong, Mirik, Siliguri, East, West and the Central Dooars."

Tamang also mentioned the GJM's programme to further extend the non-cooperation movement. "The numberplates of taxis operating in Darjeeling will be changed. A taxi, coming from Siliguri, can carry WB(West Bengal) plates till Darjeeling Mor (crossing), after which it will have to switch over to the GL (Gorkha Land) plates. Similarly, taxis running from Sikkim and Kalimpong will have to change their plates from WB to GL at Sewak," he said.

Since July 7, the GJM's diktat has forced the private vehicle owners in Darjeeling to change their numberplates to 'GL'. Taxis, however, have been exempted so far. Government vehicles, too, have been brought under the purview of the diktat, but the government has so far avoided changing the plates of its vehicles by not using them and hiring private taxis.

Heading: Salim Group stands firm on all investments in state - Indian Express
Content:
Although academic institutions have been dealing with ragging cases with an iron fist, fresh instances have been reported in three Bengal universities over the last couple of days.

Enquiries have been initiated in many of these cases.

This academic session, ragging has been dealt with strongly by the universities in the state, with Jadavpur University setting an example by suspending 24 students for being involved in ragging, a few weeks back. However, the punitive action taken against the students has drawn sharp reactions from them.

In the latest case, two first year students (girls) of the Bengal Engineering and Science University (BESU) have complained that they were "mentally harassed" by six third year students. On September 24, Vice-Chancellor NR Banerjea issued orders that the six girls be expelled from the hostel.

Later, the students 'gheraoed' the vice-chancellor and eventually forced the management to withdraw the expulsion order.

In a startling U-turn, however, the vice-chancellor on Thursday said the primary report of the teachers indicated that there is no evidence of ragging.

"I have asked the girls to issue a written apology for what happened, and we will withdraw the decision to suspend them from the hostel," Banerjea said.

In Asansol Engineering College, a first-year girl student has accused her seniors of ragging.

Vice-Chancellor of the West Bengal University of Technology Sabyasachi Sengupta visited the college and tried to pacify the girl. He said: "I met the girl and her mother, and I have advised them to rent separate accommodation near the university. We cannot eradicate such instances (of ragging) completely. Both sides need to be counselled."

Even in Jadavpur University a first-year student has complained that he was ragged by a group of students of the engineering department.

An enquiry committee has been set up to look into the complaint.

"There is a directive from the Supreme Court to take strict measures against ragging. But the universities are not investigating agencies. Moreover, for students coming from nuclear families, sometimes anything and everything is ragging. So the educational institutions have to maintain a balance when such instances crop up," said Subimal Sen, chairman of Higher Education Council.

Heading: No more investment in state if govt returns Cash, warns German Consul - Indian Express
Content:
With the spectre of Tata Motors pulling out of Singur becoming more evident, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee received a shot in the arm from another investor — the Salim Group from Indonesia.

At the end of a marathon meeting with the chief minister, Beni Santoso, Salim Group's managing director, said: "We are committed to the state. All our investments in the state are secure." With the state government burning its finger in Singur, Prasun Mukherjee — partner in Salim's project — made it clear that in case of obtaining land they would not be adamant on any single procedure. "But be it acquisition or purchase, we will go ahead only when there is a consensus," he said.

"We have submitted a progress report of our projects to the chief minister. We have discussed at length about the Mahabharat motorcycle factory, bridge between Raichak and Haldia, chemical hub at Nayachar, power project at Nayachar, and the Kolkata west housing project," Mukherjee said.

The Mahabharat factory, which is being set up with an investment of Rs 1,200 crore at Uluberia in Howrah, the entrepreneur said 65 per cent of the construction of the factory has been completed. "By June 2009 the motorcycle with the TVS brand will start rolling out. Our target will be 7,000 motorcycles every month," Mukherjee said.

As for the chemical hub at Nayachar, where the group will invest Rs 10,000 crore, Mukherjee said they were waiting for the Centre's clearance.

Heading: Bomb hoax in High Court, panic in city - Indian Express
Content:
There will be no scope for any German investment in the state if German MNC Metro Cash & Carry is not given the Agriculture Produce Market Committee (APMC) licence to trade in the state.

"We have plans to pump lot more investments in the state," said Günter Wehrmann, the German Consul General in Kolkata. "But if Metro Cash & Carry does not get the license, it will signal the death of German investments in the state. It seems that the state is not ready to accept the investments," he added.

"The German Consul is clearly trying to threaten us and mislead the people," said agriculture minister Naren De. The issue is to be sorted out at a meeting between the CPM and the Bloc on Monday.

The German company decided to set up shop in the state after Commerce and Industry minister Nirupam Sen's 10-day visit to Germany to woo investment.

The Consul's ultimatum comes on the heels of the continuing deadlock over the Tata Motors factory in Singur, which is sending shudders thorough business circles. But this time, it is not Trinamool Congress which is playing spoilsport, but the Left ally Forward Bloc — which holds the agriculture as well as agriculture marketing portfolios. Its ministers created a bottleneck, when the APMC licence of the German wholesale major was withdrawn in June 2007 on the ground that the company did not start operation within the promised time frame.

"The delay was caused by an injunction of the court owing to the land litigation. We were never at fault and have fulfilled all promises. So if we are denied the licence, we have to consider other options," said Martin Dlouhy, the company's managing director in India. The options, he said, includes legal option as well.

Dlouhy added that a delegation which met the agriculture minister this week tried its best to make it clear that the company will never switch to retail business in the state as per its agreement with the government. The Metro Cash & Carry is supposed to cater to the retailers instead.

'Metro Cash & Carry is committed to the state'
Kolkata: Metro Cash & Carry on Thursday sent a letter to Biman Bose, saying that the Germany-based retail chain is still committed to going about business in Bengal. In the letter, Cash & Carry's head of corporate communications, Vishal Saigal, wrote: "We are committed to the state of West Bengal and it is our belief that we can contribute to the progress of the state. It is this belief that has driven us to continue with our investment in the state in spite of several unforeseen delays."

Heading: Bengal’s Renaissance man remembered afresh - Indian Express
Content:
Tension gripped the city's top courts on Thursday as anonymous calls claiming that explosives were planted inside the court premises sent the Kolkata Police into a tizzy.The anti-sabotage squad of the city police immediately conducted a thorough search of the Calcutta High Court and the City Civil Court. No bomb, however, was recovered. The call was later traced to a PCO near the High Court.

Deputy Commissioner (HQ) Vineet Goyal said an unidentified male called up Lalbazar's police control room and said that bombs had been planted in the court buildings.

"The first call was made at 2.24 pm, and the second at 2.30 pm. The calls were made in Bengali. We dispatched a special squad with sniffer dogs to the site. We did not find it necessary to evacuate the court, which was in session then," he said.

The squad conducted a search of all the floors of the old building and the new centenary building of the HC, the adjacent civil court, advocates' chambers and rooms of the Bar Association.

"We have traced the calls to a phone booth located on Kiran Shankar Roy Road. The booth owner, however, could not recall who had made the call," said Goyal.

He added: "At this stage of the investigation, we cannot divulge the name of the PCO, the proprietor or the numbers from which the calls were made."

Interestingly, Goyal said the police have not classified the calls as hoax as yet. "Until we apprehend the caller and interrogate him, we cannot say if he was a prankster or had a larger motive."

Heading: Nano dreams turn sour, vendors’ exodus on - Indian Express
Content:
With the 188th birth anniversary of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar arriving on September 26, the administration has decided to commemorate the occasion in a major way.

The day will see the unveiling of a Rs 4 lakh terracotta mural on the life and times of the eminent scholar. Nearly half the amount is borne by the Victoria Memorial authorities and the rest is funded by the Vidyasagar College for Women (VCW).

The house of the Renaissance man, however, was lying in neglect. Less than a decade ago, 36 Vidyasagar Street was just another decrepit building in a north Kolkata neighbourhood, popularly known as "Badurbagan".

With squabbling tenants and the structure in total disrepair, there was nothing about the two-storeyed building that could lay claim to an illustrious past. It was in this building that the nineteenth century social reformer, Ishwar Chandra Bandopadhyay spent his last years until his death in 1891.

Constructed in 1876, the building was heading for ruin until local citizens persuaded the civic authorities to take over the structure and declare it a heritage building in 2000. The maintenance was handed over to the VCW.

Thanks to the relentless efforts of the college authorities, the premises has been restored to its old grandeur.

Rechristened "Vidyasagar Smriti Mandir", the building has received a complete facelift and now has two archive rooms on the first floor documenting the life of Vidyasagar. The tranquil surroundings provide the perfect space for people willing to flip the pages of history.

"This was the house where Ramkrishna Paramahansa had visited Vidyasagar. The building changed many hands since his death and its facade underwent many changes made by the tenants," said Pulakesh Roy, professor of history at VCW. The renovation undertaken by the college also offered chance discoveries. "Rummaging through the waste, we came across a portrait of young Iswar Chandra painted by an Englishman. The painting was later restored at the Victoria Memorial," said Roy.

Heading: CPM pounces on the Governor again - Indian Express
Content:
While a person was arrested on Thursday in connection with the assault on two security guards inside the Nano factory, the cloud of gloom over the unit darkened as ancillary units and contractors shifted their employees and material from the project site. Amid increasing speculations about Tatas leaving Singur, most of the transfer is being done in the dark since the last two days to avoid attention, sources said.

Employees of Premier Infracom, a firm employed by the Tatas to construct foundations for the factories and ancillary units, were sitting idle at the gates of the Nano factory. A civil engineer of the company said, "The head office has asked us to shift the machinery." He, however, refused to disclose whether the Tatas had said that the project would be closed down or not. "We are waiting for security clearance. Once we get it we will move our material. Our transport is ready," he said.

Factory sources and locals said machinery is being removed from the factory.

Balaram Das, owner of a small food stall outside gate no 5 of the factory, said, "Machinery, loaded in big trucks, was being taken mostly at night."

Regarding the arrest of the person accused of assaulting the guards, the police said Tajuddin Ahmed (24) participated in the protest programme of the Save Farmland Committee of Singur. A resident of Joymollah village of Singur, he was arrested from a hideout inside Gopalnagar village.

The committee, while accepting that Tajuddin was its member, claimed that the police have falsely booked him. Two private security guards were beaten up inside the Nano factory on Monday night.

Heading: Mamata announces second round of protest plans - Indian Express
Content:
The CPM leadership once again heavily criticised the Governor for his Wednesday's remarks on industrialisation.

"Empirical evidence has shown that options other than compulsory land acquisition are possible," the Governor had said during a speech in Science City.

On Thursday, transport minister Subhash Chakraborty said the statement is totally unconstitutional.

Chakraborty's argument is that all land is acquired under the Land Acquisition Act of 1894. "How can a Governor show empirical evidences keeping aside the act of the land?" he asked.

But if Chakraborty has called him unconstitutional, veterans like Binoy Konar have openly attacked Gandhi. "The Governor seems to be a know-all in all spheres," Konar remarked.

Relations between the ruling party and the Governor had soured since Gandhi lambasted the government after the March 14, 2007, police firing in Nandigram and the recapture of the area in October 2007.

Party leaders like Benoy Konar, Biman Bose and Shyamal Chakraborty had labelled him a mentor of the Trinamool Congress. Now Chakraborty has joined the bandwagon. "We have Governor who almost always holds a different view from the government on all issues," he said, adding for good measure that the agreement between the government and the opposition in presence of the Governor was "illegal".

"Land has been acquired in Singur according to the Land Acquisition Act, the High court has upheld the same. If it has been upheld by the High Court as valid, how can there be another agreement?"

Chakraborty's cabinet colleague, RSP leader and PWD minister Kshiti Goswami, meanwhile, backed Gandhi.

"If they don't get his support, they are peeved by his behaviour," he said. When the Governor had played mediator to resolve the Singur deadlock, the ruling party had welcomed his initiative. "How can an agreement signed in his presence become illegal now?"

Heading: Probe a suspect, grill a brother - Indian Express
Content:
In a rally on Thursday afternoon, flanked by supporters from 21 political parties and NGOs — Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee unveiled her Singur Day plans.

The rally, as she spelt out, will span the entire 2.4 km area over which the 21camps are located. Admonishing the Left Front government's latest compensation package for farmers, she stuck to her stand, declaring that she would accept nothing short of the disputed 400 acres.

"In spite of being promised the maximum possible land from the project area in a statement signed in front of the Governor, the CM has now changed his stand on it," she said.

Regarding the latest skirmish with the Left Front government when she was forced to end her "satyagraha" outside the factory gates at Singur, she declared that in spite of resisting peacefully, she was forced by the police to end it.

Heading: High marks for trains in eyeball war, Railways’ ad revenue up - Indian Express
Content:
Day after, Sadiq brother quizzed and released

A day after the arrest of five alleged Indian Mujahideen (IM) members, the police picked up the brother of one of them and released him after questioning.

Tariq Shaikh is the brother f Mohammed Sadiq Israr Shaikh, touted as the prime catch and co-founder of the IM. A doctor from Mumbra was also questioned and later released. The Crime Branch said it had been given some fresh leads by the arrested group, and that teams had been sent outside the city to follow up on them.

"Today we had called Sadiq's brother Tariq for enquiries. There were certain doubts that we wanted cleared, and once this was done he was allowed to leave. We also called a doctor from Mumbra for questioning, as circuitry expert Arif Shaikh was staying at his dispensary," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria.

"The arrested accused have provided us some information during interrogation. Teams have been sent to different locations outside the city to verify the information but I would not like to disclose these locations. We are sharing information with other states and central agencies," said Maria.

The Crime Branch said it would hand over all five accused to the state Anti-Terrorism Squad since they are involved in the 7/11 serial blasts. The group was planning to trigger blasts at "crowded areas" in the city and had surveyed areas, the police said without naming specific targets.

The Crime Branch also said that the arrest of Roshan Khan alias Riyaz Bhatkal, an absconding co-founder of the IM, would be the key to cracking the mystery of who had sent out terror e-mails after hacking into unsecured WiFi networks.

"Bhatkal was in charge of communications and arrangements of material resources necessary for the group's activities. He is the man who will know whether it is Abdus Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqir or someone else who sent the terror e-mails," said Maria.

The Crime Branch said that the finance for the group's activities was in the form of several lakhs of rupees sent to the city via the hawala channel and received by Mohammed Sadiq Shaikh.

Heading: Old habits die hard: carpet area remains a hype that govt built up - Indian Express
Content:
It's a win-win situation: Advertising companies find the Mumbai suburban railway network a potential medium for relaying messages to lakhs of commuters, while figures from the Central Railway (CR) and Western Railway (WR) show a significant increase in revenue from advertisements on local trains and platforms in the last two years.

So, for daily train commuters who have got used to teasers of everything from saas-bahu serials to the latest mutual fund offering while scampering to catch a train, here is the economics working behind the display screens: The CR, which bagged Rs 10.23 crore from advertising rights in the year 2004-2005, has seen the revenue getting doubled in 2007-2008. Similarly, the WR raked in Rs 30 crore from advertisements in 2007-2008 (see box).

The suburban railways have, for the past few years, been leasing advertising space including the exterior of the bogeys, exterior panels of the trains, wall paintings at stations, hoardings and screens. Last year, the painting for one train went for a whopping Rs 2.05 crore per month. When the WR, some 8 years ago, had started giving its suburban rakes for advertisements, it received Rs 20 lakh as the initial amount.

In fact, many corporate companies are using suburban trains to advertise because of their reach — after all, 64 lakh passengers use the suburban trains every day. "Banks and cellphone service providers are using this medium to a large extent, but media companies top the list. Channels such as Colors, NDTV Imagine and Sony use such advertisements to promote their channels and serials to be aired," said Brig Mittal of D S Mittal and Sons. The company currently has 15 EMU rakes (suburban local trains) which it gives to corporate companies for advertisements.

"Earlier, smaller companies preferred to advertise with the railway, but the corporate sector has realised the importance of advertising with the railway because of its reach. Plus, the 'A' and A+ (upper middle class, middle level executives) now prefer trains to commute because of the traffic, so we get a wider scope to reach our target audience. Also, these advertisements are cost-effective as compared to hoardings. For example, a hoarding can cost Rs 2 lakh to Rs 6 lakh per month depending on size and location, but an advertisement on any local train would cost Rs 3 lakh for the entire month," said a senior executive with an agency dealing in advertisements with the railway.

With the good response, the WR now plans to earn Rs 350 crore from advertisements. "We are issuing a mega-tender under which we will give all the suburban platforms, from Churchgate to Dahanu, to the winner of the bid. The WR, over a period of five years, is expected to earn Rs 350 crore from this. But this doesn't include advertisements on suburban trains," said Shyam Sunder Gupta, chief spokesperson for the WR.

But the railway is also losing out on revenue as unauthorised advertisements occupy space. "We do conduct drives wherein we take action against people who paste these unauthorised posters and in many cases we have lodged complaints against the erring people," said Sriniwas Mudgerikar, chief spokesperson for the CR.

Heading: Admit you can’t do anything: court to state on MNS stir - Indian Express
Content:
Stamp duty documents are still registered on the basis of built-up area, despite a recent legislation that makes it mandatory for developers to sell flats on the basis of carpet area alone.

Carpet area is the actual wall-to-wall area of a flat while built-up area includes the thickness of the wall. Being arbitrary by nature, a flat that is sold on built-up area is anything over 15 per cent more than the actual area of the flat. As almost all developers have been selling their flats based on built-up or super-built-up area, most buyers looking for a flat with a certain area end up with a livable space that is much less.

In May, the state legislature approved a bill to amend the Maharashtra Ownership of Flats Act, 1963, making any developer who does not sell flats on the basis of carpet area liable to face imprisonment for three years. Again, last month, the state housing department issued instructions that only carpet area be used the basis for stamp duty registration, one of the chief ways to monitor the sale of flats.

"We have circulated the instructions to everyone including the Inspector General of Registrations (IGR). Maybe the instructions are yet to reach the lower levels," said housing secretary Sitaram Kunte.

IGR Ramrao Shingare was not available for comment, while deputy IGR (Mumbai) AR Devgunde said, "We haven't received any orders yet asking us to register the documents on the basis of carpet area."

"Merely amending an Act without following it up with proper monitoring is an exercise in futility. This is a sheer lack of coordination between departments. The amendment was proposed by the housing department headed by the Chief Minister while stamp-duty registrations come under the revenue department headed by the Deputy Chief Minister," said housing expert Sreedhar Sharma.

He added that this is the very reason why the state government should push for a housing regulatory commission.

Heading: Steal and explode: Afzal Usmani was a man with a passion for car bombs - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Thursday pulled up the Maharashtra government for failing to take action on the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena for its agitation on Marathi signboards for shops and establishments.

If the government could arrest terrorists, a division bench of Justice J N Patel and Justice K K Tated asked why it could not arrest agitators too. "If you don't have the political will, then give that message to the people that we cannot do anything. Why has no action been taken against respondent number six (Raj Thackeray)?" Justice Patel said. Justice Patel also asked if these people were "untouchable" for the government.

The court observed that the various affidavits filed by the state did not speak of the action it would take against the party and Raj Thackeray. The court also asked why the government had not taken any steps regarding two letters sent by the party. Justice Patel cited the example of emails from terrorists and said the provocative letters from the MNS, too, could instigate riot-like situations in the absence of prompt action by the state.

The court also took note of Raj's tirade against Joint Commissioner of Police K L Prasad. "Your Home Minister has failed to back up the police officer," the court said.

The affidavits filed by Prasad, Principal Secretary (Home) Ajit Parasnis and Thane Police Commissioner Anil Dhere state that the party and its president have been effectively restricted from distributing posters, defacing and damaging properties and such violent gestures. They add that preventive action was taken under CrPC against party 2,390 activists before August 20, and against 1,494 between August 28 and September 23.

The court was also informed that opinion has been sought from the law and judiciary department regarding the two letters sent by Raj to shop-owners and police authorities. The court today gave time to the government till October 16 for filing an affidavit regarding what action has been taken.

Heading: Riyaz brother was picked up 2 years ago - Indian Express
Content:
Indian Mujahideen's "favourite toy" — cars that can be used as bombs — is what got Afzal Mutalib Usmani (32) into trouble.

Afzal was picked from Uttar Pradesh on August 27, his name having cropped up while the police were investigating the theft of a Zen from Kapurbawdi in Thane City. The Mumbai crime branch is now looking for two others involved with him in the theft. The group had stolen two more cars between July and August, after they stole the four CNG cars from Navi Mumbai.

The Mumbai crime branch say the order for the cars came from Madhya Pradesh and was specifically for CNG vehicles, for a double explosion impact. Afzal's arrest will be crucial in tracking the movement of the cars and the people involved in assembling the explosives there.

Two of the cars, a Black Wagon R and a Silver Wagon R, were stolen on July 9 and delivered to Surat the next day, according to Rakesh Maria, joint commissioner of police (crime). Two other cars were stolen on July 15 and driven to Ahmedabad the next day. "The cars were then laden with explosives after which Afzal drove one each to Ahmedabad civil hospital and the marketplace. We are also checking the role of Qayummudin and Atif," adds Maria.

Afzal's role is still believed as that of a foot soldier; Maria said he took orders from Sadiq.

Afzal's first tryst with crime was in 1996, when he and alleged SIMI member Abdul Hamid Chaughule were booked for an attempt to murder a man named Pandey, who wanted to open a video parlour next to a mosque.

Maria said Afzal's name also cropped up in 2002, during investigations into the firing in front of Sea Princess Hotel in 2003 and later in many firing cases. He was then a member of the then active Fazlul Rehmani Gang.

"The last case against Afzal was under MCOCA, registered in Oshiwara police station. He was in jail for 18 months" Maria adds.

Heading: Mumbai FC not an easy opponent - Indian Express
Content:
Roshan Khan alias Riyaz Bhatkal, the alleged co-founder of the Indian Mujahideen, has been giving the Mumbai Police the slip since the 7/11 and Malegaon serial blasts. The closest that the police managed to get to Bhatkal was when the Crime Branch picked up his brother Iqbal as a suspect in terror financing two years ago.

Following the serial train blasts in the city, the Ghatkopar Unit of the Crime Branch had received information that Bhatkal and his brother were providing money for sending newly radicalised local youth to Pakistan for terror training.

"We knew that Riyaz Bhatkal, who owned a leather tanning unit in Kurla at the time, was arranging finances for sending people to training camps in Bahawalpur and Muzzafarabad in Pakistan. We also suspected that his brother Iqbal was also involved. Iqbal, a computer expert, has a construction business in Karnataka's Bhatkal area," said a senior police official on conditions of anonymity.

While the Crime Branch had sent out its sleuths in search of the Bhatkal brothers, their search led them only to Iqbal.

"We managed to locate Iqbal, and we grilled him thoroughly. Since we did not get any evidence against him, we let him go. He did not divulge any details concering the whereabouts of his brother. We searched for Riyaz for several months, and visited different parts of the country. A lot of money was also spent from our secret service fund in paying informers for information about Riyaz, but we never managed to get him," said the officer.

According to the police, after the IM was founded Riyaz Bhatkal was active in Hyderabad, Maharashtra, Delhi and Gujarat. He had visited Pakistan, and is now believed to be in the country.

A probe conducted by the Crime Branch and the state Anti Terrorism Squad following the Malegaon blasts  revealed that arrested accused Mohammad Ali Shaikh (also an accused in the 7/11 case) had allegedly received Rs.1.85 lakh through hawala channels from Riyaz Bhatkal. The money was spent on sending two other accused Shabbir Ahmed Masiullah alias Batterywala and Nafeez Ansari to Pakistan for terror training.

Heading: Mangaonkar’s Power-ful inspiration - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai FC might be a new entrant to the second edition of the I-League, but their British coach David Booth in banking on successful fusion of youth and experience to throw out a tough challenge to other heavyweights during the tournament starting on September 26.

"We might be new in the league, but that does not mean we'll be easy opponents. We have some good young and experienced players and it's a challenge for them. Not the survival, but winning as many matches as we can would be on our mind," Booth said today.

The coach, who guided Mahindra United to their first Federation Cup triumph in 2003, feels the footballers like

Noel Wilson, Koluthangan, Subhas Chakraborty and Amit Nandy, who have previously represented Kolkata clubs will have some advantage.

"Our team might be new but the boys know what it is in I-League. We have some four-five players who in the past represented Kolkata clubs. So adapting to the situation won't be a factor," he said.

The Group B toppers in the second division I-League last season Mumbai FC will take on Mohun Bagan on Saturday before taking on East Bengal the next day.

In the foreign recruit line-up, the Mumbai outfit feature Abel Hammond, who has played in the junior Serie A, besides Felix Abue and James Desirama.

Heading: Rajputs prove to be the real Pandits - Indian Express
Content:
The perspiration-inspiration percentage breakup in that oft-quoted success formula varies from poster to poster, but Mahesh Mangaonkar believes he can have the whole 100 percent of both. Since Egyptian trainer Ahmed Yousif was getting India's No.1 U-15 squash player to sweat plenty at the Otters Club — on-court squash practice starts only after Ahmed's wards have exhausted all their energy doing other physical workouts in what is squash's pet training technique — the lanky Mangaonkar decided it was time to go hunt for inspiration. He dropped in an e-mail to his ultimate hero, the Canadian former No. 1 Jonathan Power, no less. And surprise will be a neat understatement for what Mahesh felt, when there was a prompt reply from his idol.

Now, the Canadian is considered one of the game's greatest shotmakers - even known beyond squash circles as the game's equivalent of John McEnroe by those who reveled in celebrating tennis's most famous temper tantrums. But still, a master of deception, specialising in drop shots - all in all, a perfect hero for impressionable youngsters around the world. Mangaonkar was no exception. Only, it's not often that fan-mails requesting for specific advice find point-by-point answers from the world's top professional sportsmen. Like imagine, Roger Federer's response in your inbox when you are still counting your steps to the net to volley at the MSLTA! But squash's smaller, lesser hung-up playing-community is obviously different.

"Power's strength is deception, and the wrist. He answered most of my mailed questions on ball-striking and mental toughness. But I was just amazed that he replied and that a top squash player could be so responsive," Mahesh says, of the inspirational words which travelled via broadband. Power retired a day after he reclaimed his No.1 spot for the third time after a titanic struggle with British hero Peter Nicol, and there's much in the Canadian's character, besides his strokes, that has left the youngster mighty awed.

Mangaonkar himself caused a mini-stir this year when he made the quarterfinals of the Senior Nationals, when still 14, and this, on the back of a season in Europe where he stands ranked No 2 in the U-15 category after a win at the German Open. This year-end, Mahesh will be gunning for the prestigious British Open - an event where the world's best assemble, and there's another bit of advice from Power, the boy is hanging on to. "He's told me how to react and change my game in certain situations, and I'm hoping I can follow it up in the big competitions," he says. The former World Open champ's demo CDs - JP Exposed and Above the Tin - have also been devoured by the Mumbai youngster, though the snatches from the e-mail remain his favourites.

But beyond the star-struck Class 9 student born to sporting parents (his father was a weight-lifter, mother a shuttler, while the boy is shooting up while dabbling at basketball) is a committed youngster, keen on pursuing squash as his profession. "I know that's where my future is, and from hereon wherever I study, there'll be a squash programme for sure," he says. A month in Egypt under the world-renowned Amir Wagih was arranged for by Mangaonkar's Mumbai coach Waman Apte, and finances-willing, the boy will hitch up to Canada, for a session with the legendary Power, whom he's briefly met when the star played the World Team event in India.

Till then, there's Ahmed Yousif, the beefy taskmaster, stretching Mahesh to his stamina limits at Otter's, while sticking to the motto: When perspiration dries up, inspiration usually kicks in.

Heading: Fast and frivolous: Patience goes at premium - Indian Express
Content:
Chandrakant Pandit XI crashed to a humiliating innings and 49 run defeat at the hands of Lalchand Rajput XI on the second day of the Shalini Bhalekar Memorial Cricket (Mumbai Cricket Association under-22 trials) Tournament on Thursday at the Ramesh Dhadkar Maidan in Matunga. Balkrishna Shirke and Vishal Dabholkar shared the spoils with three wickets each for Rajput XI as they shot their opponents out for a paltry 42 in the second innings.

Earlier, Rajput XI ended their first innings on 178, 91 runs ahead, with Pandit XI opening bowler Ravishankar Singh finishing with remarkable figures of 7 for 40. In response, the Pandit XI batsmen never got going and wickets tumbled at regular intervals as they crashed to 42.

It was a disappointing show all around by them, as they failed to reach triple figures in either of their innings (they ended their first essay with just 87 runs). Anand Singh's defiant knock of 43 in a match where all the batsmen struggled to find their feet, deserves special mention, as he seemed to be the only batsman to apply himself for his team's cause.

Meanwhile, Dilip Vengsarkar XI finished the day at 4 without loss in their second innings in pursuit of 220 on the final day of their match against Hemant Waingankar XI. Vengsarkar XI were bowled out for 130 in their first innings, with Dhawal Parab shining with figures of 4 for 15. Waingankar XI then finished with 158 second time around, as Pratik Kar and Ganesh Narsumayya shone with the ball with three wickets apiece. Bravesh Shetty top-scored with 36.

Heading: Coming soon - Indian Express
Content:
Film folks sum up the contradictions that mark Bollywood's new phase

SALMAN KHAN
Of blockbusters and multiplexes
The prevalent corporate climate hasn't altered my scheme of things much. I never signed any agreement or contract. I still don't do that. I believe in trust. Nothing has changed for me, just that the prices have shot up phenomenally. The only perceivable change is that moviegoers have gone back to the theatre. And it isn't just the multiplexes. People are also watching films in single-screen theatres because of the upgraded facilities all around. Things are really looking up.

VIDHU VINOD CHOPRA
More than business
WHEN I saw Loins of Punjab, I realised that there is an alternate cinema quietly taking shape in India. With Rock On!!, my belief has just been strengthened that maybe young filmmakers can steer clear of the kind of compromises that many have had to make to get their foot into this very competitive but intoxicating world of movies.

But at the same time, I'm disturbed by the increasing obsession we have developed for the opening weekend. We seem to have stopped asking certain crucial questions, like what are the values our film propagates. When we green-light a project or begin to write a film, these are the first of the many questions we must ask ourselves.

So if we have taken a step forward, it feels like we may have taken two steps back because of the force with which marketing, projection and box-office pressures have begun to impact our filmmaking. Cinema is more than "over Rs 100 crore in three days".

FARHAN AKHTAR
Varied scripts
ACTORS are willing to take risks with their roles, something which was not the case a few years ago. And this new unpredictability where we don't know in what role we will see an actor is a very good sign. Scripts rule, with people like Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra, Amole Gupte and Ashutosh Gowariker coming up with gripping projects. I think Mehra's Aks had a rare and off-beat subject for a film. Marketing of films too has reached another level altogether. Films launching merchandise in their name, contests, stars on reality shows — this trend can only get bigger. There is also a large audience for Indian films outside India that comprises not only NRIs but also people from all nationalities. It's the new and gripping content of our films that is getting attention. Single producers who were churning out the same stuff with no new ideas have been replaced by corporate houses ever ready to experiment with new concepts and formulas. Multitasking is also the new mantra with actors like Aamir Khan producing, directing and acting in a film like Taare Zameen Par. I wrote Rock On!!, produced it, wrote dialogue, acted and sang in it.

MADHURI DIXIT
Indian, not Bollywood
I HATE the term 'Bollywood' but an Indian film has everything for any kind of audience. I try to watch every film, and with Internet and with multiplexes coming up all over the place, it has become so easy to catch up with the latest releases. Lately, there have been some very good films, many with messages. The quality of films has also improved and I am happy that the Hindi film industry is progressing very well. People are coming in with good scripts and good planning.

SOHA ALI KHAN
Changed scenario
I BELIEVE Indian cinema is the finest form of art in our country. Films are the best medium for reaching out and conveying the message to a large chunk of audience. Indian cinema is undergoing a slow change, though it is not very apparent and drastic. Mindsets are breaking, trends are changing and people are open to experimentation. Directors are willing to cast newcomers in their films, there are varied films being made, like Bheja Fry and Love Story 2050, and multi-starrers have won over actors interested in solo leads. Films like Mumbai Meri Jaan that send out social messages should be made. Along with entertainment, some kind of social message should also be imparted.

RANI MUKERJI
Newfound respect
'NEW and improved' are strong words and I would use them sparingly, but yes, there have been changes in every decade. There was a change from silent to the talkies, black-and-white to colour — it's been a natural progression of sorts. The most wonderful part of it all is that films are now looked at with respect. Parents are now encouraging their children who want to be a part of it. It's also more professional like being a doctor or engineer—there are a lot more people who are looking for a career in the technical side in Bollywood. Also the attitude towards making films is that everybody wants to make a good film.

DEEPIKA PADUKONE
Public demand
I FEEL today's audience is lot more intelligent. Newer people have come into the industry. Those who are scripting films are touching upon new subjects. Many films are connecting with the audience, even offbeat ones. Films are back to being realistic. Films like Jab We Met and Jaane Tu...Ya Jaane Na had a fresh treatment.

RANBIR KAPOOR
Breaking norms
THE 1950s saw the best of Hindi cinema. Movies then were made straight from the heart by filmmakers like Raj Kapoor and Guru Dutt. Cut to 2000 and cinema is progressing very fast. There's an influx of new and young directors and scriptwriters. Everybody is ready to break norms and take risks. I believe this is a progressive trait. It makes it easier for me to play interesting roles. I had a dream launch with Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Saawariya, an unusual film as a debut. Plot-driven films are gaining importance.

Heading: Growing pains - Indian Express
Content:
Bipasha turns designer

After Indian cricket captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni, it is now the turn of Bipasha Basu to turn designer for sportswear brand Reebok. Basu, who is also a brand ambassador of the label, has worked closely with in-house designers to develop a line of women's gym wear that will hit the stores soon. The look of the collection, in keeping with the actor's image, is funky and energetic with a lot of classic colours like blues, pearl whites and blacks.

That apart, Basu is also excited about her forthcoming regional film, Pankh by Bengali director Sudipto Chattopadhyay, where she plays an alter-ego to a boy going through gender confusion. "It's a delightful role, quite different from anything I have done before in my career. The script was so convincing that I just could not give up the offer," she says.

Heading: Shock value - Indian Express
Content:
Chick-lit catches its chickens really young

Indian publishers continue to be obsessed with chick-lit after the raging popularity of books like Almost Single, Zoya Factor, Trust Me and You Are Here. The latest one to join the pack is Pink or Black (Rupa & Co) by 18-year-old Tishaa Khosla.

Khosla is a shy teenager who spent the larger part of her days at her boarding school, Lawrence School, Sanawar. Her experiences there form the inspiration for her book which really started out as a diary when she was 16. "I had a lot of time after my board exams. What began as a diary finally turned into a book."

Khosla writes in a lucid, straightforward style about the ups and downs of being young. Through Tiana, the central character, Khosla recounts her own experiences at school—the constant need to fit in and finding your own individuality. "I wrote this book for other teenagers who go through the same dilemmas," she says importantly.

Khosla proclaims she was always passionate about writing. To hone her interest, she joined An Actor Prepares, an acting school run by Anupam Kher in Mumbai. There she trained in scriptwriting among other things. Khosla also intends to pursue a career in Film writing and has already gained admission into the New York Film Academy.

Khosla was only 15 when she declared to her parents that she wanted to write a book. They were always supportive about her ambitions, she says. Pink or Black was done by the time she was 17. What followed was the hunt for a publisher and the re-writing of the first chapter, until finally Rupa & Co showed interest.

"Tishaa's book is fantastic for its simple writing style and the way it connects immediately to the reader. It takes you back to your own school days," says Kapish Mehra of Rupa who has also published books by the likes of Chetan Bhagat and L K Advani. The market for chick-lit is certainly growing in India, he says, slotting Khosla's book in the same category. But for the girl, the book is an earnest attempt at making sense of the 'Wonder Years' for herself and for others her age.

Khosla's book was launched in Mumbai on Thursday by her mentor Kher. Her next book, she says, will also be about youngsters. "But this time it will be a romantic one," she discloses coyly.

Heading: Right on track - Indian Express
Content:
K K Raghava returns with art that upchucks the pretty for the ugly

One may be justified in asking who K K Raghava is given that the artist's last solo was almost four years ago. Add to it the fact that at that time he painted with his hand and did playful work that ran the risk of being called gimmicky. The prodigal returns with a solo at Art Musings, titled Drawn and Quartered, an attempt to link the different styles that excite him.

From caricatures and a predominantly graphic style to a more painterly, photorealist approach this solo has four suites of work: Lady Lazarus, Arrival of the (Swan), I Hate Fat Boys and his latest series Incoherent Scraps of (Gluttony).

The titles itself indicate that Raghava has taken it upon himself to uncover the seamier side of life. The visuals confirm the pretty pictures of his youth. They have been exchanged for images that are more confrontational and disturbing. Bodies are punctured; flesh is ripped, bloated and distorted, all for the express purpose of revealing the darker underbelly.

"Life revealed to me that things were not perfect, there was much ugliness and harshness in this world and I have allowed it to permeate my canvas," says the artist who began his career by teaching children to animate and cartoon.

Raghava has explored dark themes like paedophilia which are reflected in his Arrival of the (Swan) series. I Hate Fat Boys is dedicated to his own experiences of not conforming to the six-pack muscle-bound imagery that is prevalent for men in today's milieu. "I don't conform myself and I understand that there would be anxiety among those who don't conform either," says the artist about the underdog or the 'fat boy' who is seen as less masculine. In this series, Raghava employs his sense of wit and renders caricatures that often border on self loathing. While the Lady Lazarus explores the artist's curiosity over his own gender—he merges Greek myth with contemporary concerns and the resulting hybrid creatures that result are neither male nor female but a composition of gender.

The other series that may be difficult on viewers, especially if they happen to be women—is the Incoherent Scraps. Here gluttony has been interpreted in bloated female bodies, the result of binging on excesses—whether it's food, love or life in general. It would however be unfitting to read these as misogynist since the artist's empathy lies with the large ponderous women. The series also creates an interesting contrast with the near-perfect creatures one encounters in the Arrival of the Swan series. "The subversion is intended and complete," says the artist.

(The show is on from August 25 to November 5 at Art Musings, Admiralty Building, Colaba)

Heading: After mishap, BMC to go slow on paver blocks - Indian Express
Content:
Independent bands making music for films state Bollywood isn't the last bastion

Randolph Correia, of the relatively small electronica duo band Shaai'r+Func, has for the first time composed a full soundtrack for the movie Saas Bahu aur Sensex. The movie may have been a dud but Correia feels that it's a head-start for him, since it's his first serious exposure to Bollywood,

and towards making mainstream popular music.

Though music from the Indian film industry has always been catchy, the predictability of the tracks is about to change, with bands that have focused on creating original sound coming in. "A lot of music from Bollywood sounds exactly the same," says Correia, whose tracks for Saas Bahu have a lot of progressive electronic sounds instead of dance and bhangra beats.

Kailasa is another group that has created a separate Bollywood identity for itself. They like to call themselves the Kailash-Paresh-Naresh trio. Departing from their conventional Sufi sound, the trio is ready to bring in unplugged and acoustic beats with their composition for Sushant Shah's Dus Vidhaniya starring Vinay Pathak and Neha Dhupia.

"The music that we have done for the film is new for us as well," says Paresh Kamath, guitarist of Kailasa, who have recorded their music live. "There's a certain human element that lengthens the song's shelf-life when it's live," adds Kamath. The trio has also composed two tracks for the forthcoming Chandni Chowk to China that even includes a qawwali with a twist.

But not all consider Bollywood a progression, though all musicians acknowledge it the fastest way to get noticed and top the charts. "I'm not progressing to Bollywood. In fact it is a step down for me as a musician since it cannot provide any inspiration. But it is a decent money-making proposition," says Correia, who has also produced a track for Drona. Agrees Rahul Ram, bassist, Indian Ocean who says, "Bollywood is not our final bastion. The filmmakers are coming to us for our sound." The band has composed the soundtrack for the recently released Hulla and a film titled Bhoomi is in the pipeline. "The soundtrack for Hulla basically has one main song and three versions of it, apart from the background score. But the sound for our films, be it in the past or the future, will continue being the sound that is Indian Ocean," says Ram.

Most of these bands are continuing with their independent work that only benefits from their exposure to Bollywood. "It aligns your creative thought process with what people want to hear which can be a challenge," admits Ram. "Working on a script written by someone else makes us think differently which may not have been possible otherwise," says Kamath.

While Correia is busy trying to take his group Shaai'r+Func and Pentagram to the next level by cutting new albums, Kailash-Paresh-Naresh turn back to Kailasa to record their third album. And Indian Ocean has just released their DVD, Indian Ocean Live.

Heading: Spurt in juvenile crime: Mobiles stolen, parents worried - Indian Express
Content:
BMC will reconsider tenders if corporators find fault with paver blocks: Municipal Commissioner

After persistent opposition from corporators, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) on Wednesday decided to go slow on paver blocks. Clearing the air on the issue, Municipal Commissioner Jairaj Phatak said, "If any corporator finds fault with paver blocks, we will reconsider the tender."

Since last week's Jacob Circle incident— in which a paver block side strip caved in, killing three persons —corporators have been opposing the use of paver blocks on the city roads. The issue was once again discussed in the civic standing committee where members cried foul over the excessive use of paver blocks to lay roads without ensuring quality in the workmanship. However, Phatak said the quality could be compromised only in cases when a tender is passed at the ward level. "When central office passes the tender, quality is not compromised," said Phatak.

Paver blocks were introduced in 2003 to surface junctions and footpaths in the city. But, over the last two years entire stretches of some roads have been laid using paver blocks. Though it only takes two weeks or a month to lay a road with paver blocks, they may wear out easily.

Several corporators have been mooting the idea of using only cement-concrete (CC) mix or asphalt mix to lay roads, despite the fact that it takes almost four to six months to complete the laying of such roads. But, according to the municipal commissioner, the Merani Committee — the standing technical advisory committee for roads and bridges — did not find any major problems with the paver blocks though it stated that CC roads were better.

Heading: MLA saves his allowance to buy ambulances for constituency - Indian Express
Content:
There has been a spurt in incidents of harassment by school-going boys in ladies compartment. Two mobile thefts were committed in ladies compartment on Monday. Two minors were arrested by the police in this connection.

According to the railway staff deputed on platforms, women commuters lodge complaints against gross misbehaviour by these students everyday. On Monday, acting on the complaint of a woman commuter, Vasai police caught two students of class 9, both residents of Borivali (east). These children were committing  thefts to cater to their unfettered desire for a luxurious life. Seven mobiles were recovered from their possession. Two mobiles were confiscated on the spot, while the rest of the mobiles were hidden and was recovered after a search from a damaged auto-rickshaw.

Their parents were not aware of their activities as they reached home on time after school hours. On September 23, the two students were produced before the juvenile court. The court ordered their judicial custody.

"When we received the complaints from the ladies, we actually doubted the complainants as we had not thought that such small children could commit such crimes, according to a police officer.

MD Raskar, senior police inspector, GRP, Churchgate station, while he was posted at Andheri station, had caught a student stealing mobile from the ladies compartment two years back. "But considering his tender age, I handed him over to his parents. Instead of convicting them there should be some process to reform them. Children residing in hutments near stations also indulge in petty crimes to get money," he added. A ticket checker posted at western suburban said," These students are 14 to 16 years of age and they travel in ladies first class compartment, while they are old enough to travel in general compartment. They have passes of second class but they travel in ladies first class. Despite complaints, neither the ticket checking staff nor the police take these complaints seriously. As and when we take it seriously, other commuters tell us to be kind towards them and spare them."

Archana Shinde, a daily commuter, said, "It is very difficult to travel in the ladies compartment between 6.30 am to 9 am, 12.30 pm to 2 pm and 5.30 pm to 7 pm. These teenaged boys pass indecent comments on ladies and misbehave with them. Sometimes they make graffitis inside the coach. I complained about this to a TC at Borivali station, but they did not take any action."

Heading: Students union activists arrested for disrupting university meeting, vandalising property - Indian Express
Content:
Kisan Kathore, a member of the Legislative Assembly from Ambernath in Thane district has decided to dedicate four ambulances to his constituency. Deputy Chief Minister RR Patil will be handing over the ambulances on Friday. Though many elected representatives dedicate ambulances and other services with the election round the corner, Kathore's ambulances have a different tale to tell.

Kathore who was elected from Ambernath as MLA for the first time in 2004, has not accepted any donation to buy these ambulances. According to him, he credited his monthly allowences to a separate bank account which he didn't disturb for last four years. "The monthly allowence that I accept from the State belongs to the people. I had credited the money I have received in the form of monthly allowences for future use without any particular plan in mind," said Kathore.

Kathore, a farmer, earns his income from agriculture and owns 30 acre of cultivable land. He claimed that he had been extending medical assistance to underprivileged people on the occasion of his birthday, which falls on September 19, for the last 17 years. "There was a need for ambulances in my constituency. So, I made good use of my monthly allowences," he said.

A legislator receives a monthly allowance of Rs 19,000 and in four years Kathore could accumulate a whopping amount of Rs 9.12 lakh. According to Kathore, he spent around Rs 11 lakh to buy four Maruthi Omni vans and convert them into ambulances.

Ambernath legislative constituency has significant rural areas and slums located in remote areas which are far away from hospitals. Lack of timely medical attention often increases the mortality rates in the constituency.

The ambulances will be handed over to non-governmental organisation Arogya Hith Vardhini Upakram, a trust which Kathore had set up for helping the people get medical attention in time.

According to him, the ambulances would be deployed in four remote regions of the constituency — Haji Malang, Wagni, Ambernath and Badlapur— and provide the service free of cost.

Besides this, Kathore has also come up with a medical card for 25000 villagers in his constituency. The medical card will give access to free medical care for diagnostic and treatment of all major ailments, except trauma cases.

"In villages, trauma cases happen only because of violence or police action. Hence, such cases are left out from the ambit of free medical care," said Kathore.

To fund the free medical care scheme, as many as 200 NCP activists have become the members of the Arogya Hith Vardhini Upakram and make a monthly contribution of Rs 50.

Heading: Panel submits report on ‘poor box’ fund scam - Indian Express
Content:
A few student union workers of Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) along with nine Samtawadi Chhatrabharati students were arrested on Thursday when they were protesting against the academic council meeting at the University Fort campus. Some engineering and pharmacy students were also arrested. The MNS workers were demanding the extention of the ATKT (Allowed To Keep Term)system in one more subject for the first year of the engineering degree course. The protestors claimed that since two more subjects had been introduced in the first year taking the number of subjects to 12, the university should increase the number of ATKT as well.

Currently, students can get four ATKT subjects for ten subjects in a semester.

The students were arrested by the police after a lathicharge when they demanded the University of Mumbai to lower the passing percentage and increase the number of ATKT subjects in the B Pharma exams. Manoj Tekade of the students union group alleged that the police beat some students while they were protesting 'peacefully'. However, senior Police Inspector Prakash Shishupal of Azad Maidan police said, "The students barged into the convocation hall where the meeting was taking place and started shouting slogans against the vice chancellor and vandalizing. The university security officer lodged a complaint with us." He added that non-bailable warrants have been registered against the students.

Heading: AAI colony residents choke, suffer as Sahar elevated road project moves at snail’s pace - Indian Express
Content:
Two months after the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) initiated an inquiry against the KEM Hospital officials for allegedly misusing funds meant for poor patients, the inquiry committee constituted by the BMC submitted the report on Thursday. The civic body is considering what action to take, based on the report.

According to civic sources, senior hospital officials had allegedly used around Rs 2 crore for the purchase of medicines, but they had failed to replenish the amount.

"I have received the inquiry report. I'm going through it and considering what action is to be taken. We'll decide it soon," said Additional Municipal Commissioner (Health) Kishor Gajbhiye.

In a press conference in July, Gajbhiye had said that funds from the 'poor box' placed in the KEM Hospital have been misused. "We had received a complaint regarding the misuse of funds and have initiated an inquiry accordingly," he had said.

Though this fund can be used for administrative purposes, the same should be replenished. "There was an emergency to purchase medicines, however, the amount was credited back to the fund box. The fund had more than Rs 6 crore," Gajbhiye had said.

Heading: TMC agrees to modify design of tunnel under Thane rail bridge - Indian Express
Content:
It's been a year since tin sheets were put up next to the colony park at the Airports Authority of India (AAI) colony at Sahar. The purpose was to start work on the Sahar elevated road project that would eventually connect the Western Express Highway to Terminal 2 of the Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport (CSIA), which, according to Airport Master Plan, will significantly ease passenger movements after the airport's renovation.

However, the colony residents allege that in the past six months the construction work has taken quite a toll on the their lives due excessive cement dust, clogged drainage, broken water pipes and constant noise. Expectedly, residents who are also employees of AAI, are grumbled with the ongoing construction and blame the agencies involved in it including Mumbai airport's private developer which has also undertaken the colony's regular maintenance.

"Most of us work in shifts and often when we come back after a night shift, we cannot sleep due to the continuous noise from the heavy machines. This effects our productivity at the work," said R S Kamale, a senior assistant manager with AAI and a resident of the colony. The machinery in question here is a concrete botching plant along with medium capacity earthmovers being used in the initial phase for the elevated road project.

The general secretary of AAI staff union, M K Ghoshal, had raised the issue in front of CPI (M) leader Sitaram Yechury during his Mumbai visit as the Chairman of the Parliamentry Standing Committee for transport, tourism & culture.

While Kamale blamed the Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL) for ignoring civil maintenance work in the colony, Madhuri T Batule (43), a housekeeping attendant from AAI and a colony resident, said that the colony's water pipes have been broken six to seven times and residents' toilets are chocked due to blocked drainage. Smita Jande, another AAI employee and a colony resident, complained of cement dust contaminating resident's food and thus leading to breathing problems. "Even children are getting disturbed due to the ongoing construction work," she added.

However, a MIAL spokesperson said that the issue is being blown out of proportion. "MIAL routinely carries out maintenance work inside the AAI colony premises. The actual construction of the flyover has not yet started as preparatory works are going on. In any case, the concrete batching work is done intermittently and does not exceed more than 2 hours in a day on an average," the MIAL spokesperson said in response to residents' allegations. He added that since cement was being stored in 25 meters high silos and no mixing work was going on, there could not be any pollution. "Although the main water pipe was broken due to construction work, it was repaired in coordination with L&T, the project contractors," he said.

Meanwhile, S R Raghvendra Rao, Regional Executive Director (western region), AAI, said that despite best protective measures, the situation cannot be helped beyond a point. "Theoretically they are right. But it's like if your neighbour carries out some construction, you're bound to be affected," Rao said. However Dilip Kawathkar, Joint Project Director (PR) of the MMRDA, said that the agency has not received any complaints from colony residents. "We'll look into the matter anyhow," he said.

Heading: Making 12-yr-old a ‘sadhvi’ violates child rights: report - Indian Express
Content:
Motorists commuting on the Thane-Belapur Road will have to wait till next year to get relief from traffic bottlenecks on the stretch under the Central Railway line bridge between Thane and Kalwa.

Thane Municipal Corporation has agreed to the latest changes suggested by the Central Railway to the path underneath the embankment of railway lines. "The changes would incur an additional expenditure of Rs 3 crore and would take 5-6 months for completion of work. Moreover, approval of the general body will have to be taken before calling for fresh tenders for the work," said TMC chief engineer KD Lala.

Lala is hopeful of making necessary changes to the design within a fortnight, and submitting the new design of the tunnel to the Central Railway. The TMC is aiming to complete the work by June 2009 before the onset of the monsoon.

TMC approved the change in design in a meeting with the railway officials at Mantralaya on Tuesday which was attended by the regional elected representatives.

Under the railway line bridge, the two lane road is the cause of major traffic jams during peak hours. In March 2003, TMC had envisaged to construct two tunnels alongside existing road for light vehicles. One tunnel is complete, while the design of the second tunnel is causing the delay. The tunnel is used for one-way traffic of light vehicles from Thane to Belapur, while the traffic from the opposite direction uses the narrow path under the old railway bridge. Previously the Central Railways had approved the design to insert pre-cast slabs over and between the two concrete boxes abutting the entrances. The design of the slabs was changed thrice thereby delaying the project by a year. The Central Railway again changed their plan when TMC sought six mega-blocks of 12 hour each for inserting the pre-cast slab. The methodology was to remove the soil embankment underneath the tracks and launch the slab over and between the two concrete boxes. The Central Railway took the stand that six 12-hour mega-blocks would not be possible and instead suggested that another concrete box should be pushed underneath the tracks. Hydraulically pushing the concrete box into the railway embankment would not require mega-blocks, mere speed restriction of 20 km per hour by the trains running above would be sufficient, said Lala.

The work to clear the bottlenecks was undertaken by the TMC after several protests by people residing on both sides of the railway bridge.

Heading: Breeding grounds? Suspects lived or worked here - Indian Express
Content:
The committee has observed that she knows nothing about childhood such as playschool, friends, quarrels or games

A report has been submitted to the Bombay High Court in the glaring case of a twelve-year-old girl Priyal who was allowed to renounce the world at the tender age of eight. Priyal, now known as Sadhvi Preet Varsha Shreeji, was interviewed by a three-member committee, which prepared the report, on September 14 on the direction of the court. The committee, comprising Adeline Rodrigues, registrar/prothonotary and senior master of the court, Rajani Iyer, senior advocate, and Shaila Mhatre, chairperson of Child Welfare Committee, in their report submitted on Friday states that "it is certainly not possible for this child with limited exposure at the age of six to understand the consequences of her decision to go and stay with sadhvis and gurus in this environment and to "decide" to take up 'diksha' at the age of eight." The committee has observed that she knows nothing about childhood such as playschool, friends, quarrels or games. "Even while noting that the minor appeared to be healthy, spirited, intelligent and alert, the decision taken on her behalf as above cannot be said to be in the best interest of the child since it actually violates her right to childhood, freedom, education and recreation, family life and home. The committee further states that the child being highly intelligent would have achieved academic excellence. "This opportunity has been denied to her, given that she has been living in the environment of a "sanstha" since the age of six and has been exposed to a similar way of life to the exclusion of all since the age of three." The report says that many of the replies she gave were superlative which did not appear to be right. "This does point to the child having been helped and partly tutored in formulating her answers to possible questions posed by the committee members." Priyal, who has worn only white since taking up 'diksha', says that she has not taken a regular bath for the last four years. After attaining puberty she will be required and permitted to bathe once a month. The interview reveals that she walks barefoot and sometimes she is allowed to use slippers made of cloth. But she is happy to be in the sangh premises in Khandala and Lonawala. She is further forbidden to use electricity in any form and has to rely on "outside" light. Although her parents visit once a month, she is not permitted to touch her father or even her one-and- a-half year old brother. "In fact, she has never caressed or even held her younger brother, since he was born after she took "diksha". When asked whether she prays for others citing the Bihar floods, she stated that she does not, including her parents and siblings as she prays only for her own 'moksha' and 'atma kalyan'. She also justified taking up 'diksha' by stating that she has seen 100-200 children, some even younger than her, taking 'diksha'. She also asserts that she does not miss her parents as she gets so much love and care at the ashram. The committee also observed that the child appeared to be relaxed in the company of three senior sadhvis. "A "decision" taken at the age of six is today sought to be justified by her with reference to others, younger to her, who are taking 'diksha'. This clearly indicates the total absence of positive volition on her part at the time the decision was taken for her and an absence of thinking about the consequences by and for her," the committee concludes. The court was hearing the petition filed by parents of the child, Ashok alias Santosh Bagricha, challenging the jurisdiction and proceedings initiated by the CWC under the Juvenile Justice Act. The case has been adjourned till October 17. "We got the report only today and we will be replying to it before the next hearing," said petitioners' advocate Milind Sathe.

Heading: Godhra flames: Nanavati report fails to douse it - Indian Express
Content:
Film folks sum up the contradictions that mark Bollywood's new phase

SALMAN KHAN
Of blockbusters and multiplexes
The prevalent corporate climate hasn't altered my scheme of things much. I never signed any agreement or contract. I still don't do that. I believe in trust. Nothing has changed for me, just that the prices have shot up phenomenally. The only perceivable change is that moviegoers have gone back to the theatre. And it isn't just the multiplexes. People are also watching films in single-screen theatres because of the upgraded facilities all around. Things are really looking up.

VIDHU VINOD CHOPRA
More than business
WHEN I saw Loins of Punjab, I realised that there is an alternate cinema quietly taking shape in India. With Rock On!!, my belief has just been strengthened that maybe young filmmakers can steer clear of the kind of compromises that many have had to make to get their foot into this very competitive but intoxicating world of movies.

But at the same time, I'm disturbed by the increasing obsession we have developed for the opening weekend. We seem to have stopped asking certain crucial questions, like what are the values our film propagates. When we green-light a project or begin to write a film, these are the first of the many questions we must ask ourselves.

So if we have taken a step forward, it feels like we may have taken two steps back because of the force with which marketing, projection and box-office pressures have begun to impact our filmmaking. Cinema is more than "over Rs 100 crore in three days".

FARHAN AKHTAR
Varied scripts
ACTORS are willing to take risks with their roles, something which was not the case a few years ago.
