And this new unpredictability where we don't know in what role we will see an actor is a very good sign. Scripts rule, with people like Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra, Amole Gupte and Ashutosh Gowariker coming up with gripping projects. I think Mehra's Aks had a rare and off-beat subject for a film. Marketing of films too has reached another level altogether. Films launching merchandise in their name, contests, stars on reality shows — this trend can only get bigger. There is also a large audience for Indian films outside India that comprises not only NRIs but also people from all nationalities. It's the new and gripping content of our films that is getting attention. Single producers who were churning out the same stuff with no new ideas have been replaced by corporate houses ever ready to experiment with new concepts and formulas. Multitasking is also the new mantra with actors like Aamir Khan producing, directing and acting in a film like Taare Zameen Par. I wrote Rock On!!, produced it, wrote dialogue, acted and sang in it.

MADHURI DIXIT
Indian, not Bollywood
I HATE the term 'Bollywood' but an Indian film has everything for any kind of audience. I try to watch every film, and with Internet and with multiplexes coming up all over the place, it has become so easy to catch up with the latest releases. Lately, there have been some very good films, many with messages. The quality of films has also improved and I am happy that the Hindi film industry is progressing very well. People are coming in with good scripts and good planning.

SOHA ALI KHAN
Changed scenario
I BELIEVE Indian cinema is the finest form of art in our country. Films are the best medium for reaching out and conveying the message to a large chunk of audience. Indian cinema is undergoing a slow change, though it is not very apparent and drastic. Mindsets are breaking, trends are changing and people are open to experimentation. Directors are willing to cast newcomers in their films, there are varied films being made, like Bheja Fry and Love Story 2050, and multi-starrers have won over actors interested in solo leads. Films like Mumbai Meri Jaan that send out social messages should be made. Along with entertainment, some kind of social message should also be imparted.

RANI MUKERJI
Newfound respect
'NEW and improved' are strong words and I would use them sparingly, but yes, there have been changes in every decade. There was a change from silent to the talkies, black-and-white to colour — it's been a natural progression of sorts. The most wonderful part of it all is that films are now looked at with respect. Parents are now encouraging their children who want to be a part of it. It's also more professional like being a doctor or engineer—there are a lot more people who are looking for a career in the technical side in Bollywood. Also the attitude towards making films is that everybody wants to make a good film.

DEEPIKA PADUKONE
Public demand
I FEEL today's audience is lot more intelligent. Newer people have come into the industry. Those who are scripting films are touching upon new subjects. Many films are connecting with the audience, even offbeat ones. Films are back to being realistic. Films like Jab We Met and Jaane Tu...Ya Jaane Na had a fresh treatment.

RANBIR KAPOOR
Breaking norms
THE 1950s saw the best of Hindi cinema. Movies then were made straight from the heart by filmmakers like Raj Kapoor and Guru Dutt. Cut to 2000 and cinema is progressing very fast. There's an influx of new and young directors and scriptwriters. Everybody is ready to break norms and take risks. I believe this is a progressive trait. It makes it easier for me to play interesting roles. I had a dream launch with Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Saawariya, an unusual film as a debut. Plot-driven films are gaining importance.

Heading: Nanavati panel reached premature conclusion, says retired IPS officer - Indian Express
Content:
Stormy onset: Opp walks out in protest against 'gagging'

Commotion after Gohil is not allowed to make point of order on Nanavati report

Angry scenes were witnessed in the state Assembly with the Opposition staging a walkout on the first day of the monsoon session on Thursday after Congress legislator and Leader of the Opposition Shaktisinh Gohil was not allowed to make a point of order while the first part of the Nanavati Commission report was being tabled.

Speaking to mediapersons outside the Assembly, Gohil termed the episode as an "insult to democracy" akin to "dictatorship". "What happened in the Assembly today tantamounts to the murder of democracy because the Opposition was not allowed to put forth its view on a vital issue," said Gohil and added that the Opposition had not been allowed to discuss the post-Godhra episode.

Describing the first part of the Nanavati report as a pre-planned conspiracy to cover up the wrongdoings of the state government, he said, "The part report of the Commission tabled in the House was intended to misguide the people, gain political mileage in the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections and hide the wrong deeds of the state government in the 2002 Godhra and post-Godhra episode."

He also alleged that Minister of State for Home Amit Shah had misled the House over the lack of Intelligence Bureau inputs about SIMI's plans to bomb Ahmedabad.

He further said that while the Congress wanted to fight terrorism, the BJP was trying to draw political mileage from terrorism. He said that though his party had lost two of its leaders — Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi — to terrorism, it had never made a political issue out of it.

Taking a dig at BJP's commitment to fight terrorism, he said the worst terror incidents like the attack on the Raghunath Temple, Akshardham, Parliament, the Red Fort and murder of former minister Haren Pandya had taken place during the NDA rule, and the former external affairs minister Jaswant Singh had even escorted a terrorist to Kandahar.

Heading: It has boiled down to ‘our’ probe vs ‘their’ probe - Indian Express
Content:
Sreekumar was Intelligence chief during post-Godhra days, and shunted for his 'anti-govt' stance

The 168-page Nanavati-Mehta Commission of Inquiry report was tabled in the Gujarat Assembly on Thursday. The report has termed the Godhra carnage of February 27, 2002 on the Sabarmati Express as a conspiracy.

"Even I was forced to call it a conspiracy. But I refused, as there was no evidence," remarked senior IPS officer R B Sreekumar. The officer held the office of the Additional DGP (Intelligence) during the post-Godhra riots in 2002. He was, however, shunted from the post later. After his retirement, he was promoted as DGP of Gujarat Police.

Speaking from Kottayam in Kerala, over phone Sreekumar said: "Calling it a conspiracy is a premature conclusion made by the Commission at this juncture, when the Supreme Court-appointed Special Investigation Team (SIT) is already investigating the case further. The Commission should have waited for the SIT to submit its findings."

Sreekumar had fallen out with the Modi government in 2002, when as the state police Intelligence chief, he had reported to the then Chief Election Commissioner, J M Lyngdoh that the situation in the state was not conducive for conducting free and fair polls. He later filed affidavits before the Nanavati-Shah Commission showing alleged complicity of the police in the 2002 riots as well as the roles of some "highly placed" persons in the conflagration. The cop was later charge-sheeted.

"I was being forced to toe the government line and call Sabarmati carnage a conspiracy. I was pressurised and even intimidated. I have clearly mentioned this in my affidavits no 2, 3 and 4 that I submitted before the Commission. They were, however, never cross-examined," he said.

The 'firebrand' Gujarat cop, who had fought a single-handed battle against the Narendra Modi government, was transferred to less important posts. In 2005, his junior K R Kaushik superseded him. A legal battle between Sreekumar and the state government ensued and the former approached the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT).

In a subsequent ruling, which had come a few hours before his retirement on February 28, 2007, CAT termed this supersession illegal and "bad in law".

Sreekumar had also submitted his controversial diary before the CAT and later the Judicial Inquiry Commission, in which he reportedly noted how the government tried to pressurise him to go soft on the rioters and target minorities during the post-Godhra riots.

Asserting the authenticity of his diary, Sreekumar said, "The diary has signatures of the present Ahmedabad City Police Commissioner, OP Mathur, on every page."

Heading: Zakir Shaikh’s family pins hope on judiciary - Indian Express
Content:
Findings of Banerjee and Nanavati panels are a study in contrast

While the first part of the Nanavati Commission of Inquiry report has mentioned a conspiracy angle in the Sabarmati Express incident, the Justice U C Banerjee Committee that the Railway Ministry had instituted to ascertain the precise cause of the fire, had rejected both the "Petrol theory" and the "miscreant activity" theory.

"Both being totally absurd, the fire on Sabarmati Express on February 27, 2002 cannot but be ascribed to an accidental fire that engulfed the coir, foam and latex on the berths coupled with luggage of the passengers. A burning smell was sensed, after which dense smoke filled the coach. It resulted in leaping flames. It was not a deliberate attempt," the Commission's Interim Report of 2005 had said.

The Commission had gone on to observe that "in the event of fire being caused by any inflammable liquid, it would, in fact, catch fire upon ignition immediately and there would thus be a change of total sequential aspect to it. First, the flames, then the smell, and smoke at last. The factum of user of any inflammable liquid in the coach, in my view, stands completely ruled out, but since the fire was there it cannot but be concluded that the fire originated in the coach itself without any external input," the report had observed.

Taking note of the report of the Gujarat Forensic Laboratory, which was submitted on May 17, 2002, suggesting the use of about 60 litres of 'highly inflammable fluid' to 'set the fire', the Banerjee Committee had stated that "a plain reading of the Laboratory's conclusion as above cannot be said to be a totally non-acceptable conclusion. Sixty litres of petrol or any other inflammable material would be thrown out in an overcrowded coach from the entry point to deep inside the coach and not one whisper would be raised by anyone in the bogie—it is not only improbable but absurd".

Negating the claims of the then Divisional Railway Manager, Baroda that the fire in the train was a miscreant activity, the Committee had observed, "The corroborative statements of the witnesses before the High Level Committee stand out to be in one direction, viz., dominant presence of the Kar Sevaks in the coach. If there was such a miscreant activity, would the Kar Sevaks allow to get themselves burnt without a murmur: the answer cannot but be in the negative and it is in this context, the undersigned feels it expedient to conclude that the question of there being any miscreant activity does not and cannot arise and the report of the DRM containing such an assertion cannot but be termed to be a figment of imagination without ascertaining the matter in its proper perspective, which a Railway official of more or less in the highest rank ought not to have introduced."

The report had further maintained: "There has been a preponderance of evidence inclusive of the Kar Sevaks themselves and without any variation but corroborating with each other to the effect that there was first a smell of burning in the sequence of events and after that only there was dense smoke, and the flames were noticed much later…."

Heading: Cong corners BJP for ignoring IB warning on blasts - Indian Express
Content:
Local cops unaware about his role in planting of bombs; he is innocent, says elder brother

The family members of Mohammed Zakir Shaikh are shocked after his name surfaced in the Surat live bombs and Ahmedabad blasts cases. "We don't rely on the police investigations. We have full faith in the judiciary and we will accept the decision of the court," said Zakir's elder brother Mohammed Danish Shaikh. Zakir (28) was picked up from his house in Bhiwandi, Mumbai.

During his interrogation, he confessed to his involvement in the terrorist attacks. He has a masters degree in Psychology from Shibli College in Azamgarh (UP) and belongs to a family of landlords.

He has six brothers and his elder brother works as an accountant in a private firm in Bhiwandi. Danish had come to Surat from Azamgarh in 1977 and started a betel nut business. After his business took shape, Danish purchased properties in Rehmatnagar in Rander area and even called his two younger brothers from Azamgarh to start a scrap business.

Two years ago, Zakir came to stay with his elder brother Danish in Surat, after completing his studies. He joined the scrap business. After sometime, he started a shop near Sheetal Talkies at Adajan area in Rander. He married Rukhaiyabanu a year ago, but continued living with Danish. Three months ago, he went to Bhiwandi and started a scrap cleaning factory over there.

Mohammed Danish Shaikh said: "My brother is innocent and he is not involved with any terrorist organisation. Two days ago, we came to know from my elder brother Shahid, who is in Bhiwandi, about the arrest of Zakir. We don't have faith in police investigation but have full faith in the judiciary. We never had any problem during his two-year stay in Surat. The arrest will definitely affect our business. Our family is reputed in Azamgarh and we don't do such things. Our entire family is disturbed over this issue. Even his wife is in a state of shock and has stopped talking to the family. He had also applied to go for Haj this year and all the documents have been sent and the process is on. We have full faith in God."

Surat Police Commissioner RMS Brar said: "We don't have official information about Zakir's involvement in planting of bombs in Surat and also in the Ahmedabad blasts. We have sent our team to Mumbai and they are gathering information. We will apply for his custody later."

Heading: ‘Govt planning to siphon off GMB funds for its own gains’ - Indian Express
Content:
Home minister denies having being cautioned, says Cong must put pressure on Centre for clearing GUJCOC

Gujarat Assembly was a scene of chaos on the first day of the three-day monsoon session on Thursday when Congress legislator from Porbandar Arjunbhai Modhwadia, in a supplementary question, asked Minister of State for Home Amit Shah about his negligence in taking timely action on the four-month old Intelligence Bureau (IB) report pertaining to SIMI plans to bomb Ahmedabad.

Modhwadia told the House that 11 SIMI activists arrested in connection with the Ahmedabad blasts had been named by two SIMI activists Safdar Nagori and Aamil Pervez arrested by Madhya Pradesh (MP) Police in March 2008. During interrogation, they had told the police about the training camp held in Halol and conspiracies to bomb Ahmedabad. The Congress leader said IB had provided this information to the Gujarat government but the latter did not respond to it.

Modhwadia and Shah exchanged heated arguments when the latter replied that IB had not furnished any information about SIMI plans either to him or to the director general of police. However, Speaker Ashok Bhatt asked the members of the House to use civilised language and expunged an objectionable sentence used by Modhwadia for Chief Minister Narendra Modi and an offensive phrase used by Shah for Congress leaders.

When the speaker asked Shah not to use political language in answering Modhwadia's questions, Shah said the state government has zero-tolerance for terrorism and is committed to provide security of life and property to the citizens.

Shah also made a statement saying that the Delhi Police busted the terror module in Delhi on the information provided by the Gujarat Police.

In response to another question by Dabhoi MLA and state Congress president Siddharth Patel, Shah said that the GUJCOC (Gujarat Control of Organised Crime) Bill be passed immediately and Congress MLAs must put pressure on the Central government on the issue.

Answering another question by Siddharth Patel, Shah said that GUJCOC was proposed in 2003 and an amended version was passed by the Assembly in 2004 following Centre's suggestion to remove certain portions of the Bill. By the time it was sent to the Centre, UPA had come to power. "It has been sitting on it ever since; it has neither recommended it to the President nor sent it back to us," Shah said. In all, the state government has taken up the GUJCOC matter 16 times with the Centre, but all in vain, Shah added.

Heading: No World Bank help sought for upgrading Civil Hospital: Vyas - Indian Express
Content:
Congress accuses state govt of destroying Gujarat Maritime Board's autonomy

The Congress has accused the Narendra Modi Government of attempting to "destroy" the autonomy of Gujarat Maritime Board (GMB), and expressed apprehension that the government may misuse the funds being collected by the Board by way of waterfront levy and landing, shipping and lighterage charges at its minor ports.

Initiating a debate on the Gujarat Maritime Board (Amendment) Bill in the State Assembly on Thursday, Leader of the Opposition Shaktisinh Gohil said the government's decision asking the GMB to transfer the amount being collected from the various charges and fees to it (the government) would not only undermine the autonomy of the Board, but also have an adverse impact on the development of ports sector in the State.

Gohil said: "There is all possibility of the government misusing this money on tamashas and publicity. The amount being collected by way of waterfront levy, licence fees, landing, shipping and lighterage charges at the GMB-managed minor ports should remain with the Board itself".

The revenue thus collected should be utilised for the development of ports being managed and controlled by the Board, he demanded.

Participating in the debate, senior Congress MLA Siddharth Patel said the amount sought to be transferred from the GMB to the government would retard the development of the Board's ports, particularly the minor ones. Another Opposition member Arjun Modhwadia lamented that barring a few technical hands, the GMB has made no new recruitment since its inception as an autonomous body in 1981.

Moving the amendment Bill in the House earlier, Health Minister Jay Narayan Vyas said that under the existing provisions of the Gujarat Maritime Board Act, 1981, the waterfront royalty on the basis of per ton cargo handled at minor ports is levied by the government from the GMB. In order to ensure direct credit of "State Charges" leviable for waterfront use, it is considered necessary to review the existing arrangements and levy the landing, shipping and lighterage charges and also license fees at the minor ports.

The minister said the government would pay administration charges to the GMB computed at the rate of 15 per cent of the State Charges levied by the government. He assured the House that the amount would be utilised for the various developmental activities. Later, the Bill was passed by majority in the House.

Outside the House, a senior GMB officer told Newsline that it was a "technical amendment" in the Act, and there was no question of the government misusing the funds. He said the GMB collected about Rs 250 crore annually by way of various charges, with a major chunk of it coming from the waterfront charges.

The House also passed by majority two more Bills — the Gujarat Forensic Sciences University Bill and the Gujarat Homoeopathic (Amendment) Bill. While the first Bill seeks to establish a university in the State for higher training and education in forensic sciences, the second one seeks to increase the number of members of Council of Homeopathic System in the State, including government nominees.

It also seeks to raise the existing fees of Rs 25 for registered practitioner in homeopathy.

Heading: CBI files case against two FCI officers for manipulating contract - Indian Express
Content:
Dismisses media report, saying World Bank can't be approached directly

State health minister Jay Narayan Vyas on Thursday firmly dismissed a report published by an English daily about the Health Department's proposal to seek aid from the World Bank in order to develop the city's Civil Hospital into the world's largest hospital.

Commenting on the report, Vyas said: "Eighty per cent of what has been written in the report is pure fiction. Neither have we approached the World Bank, nor do we have any plans to do so. The report clearly amounts to misguiding the public."

He added: "The World Bank cannot be approached directly. The Government of India does it through lines of credit and more importantly, it is the World Health Organization (WHO) which is the nodal agency for these kinds of projects. We have not submitted any application to the World Bank or WHO. So there is no question of funding from the World Bank."

The hospital is being developed to match up to the standards of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) under the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY).

Vyas confirmed that the development planning by the Health Department is in the initial stages.

He further said: "We are planning some development projects. And developing the Civil Hospital into the world's largest hospital will not be a big problem for us. It is already Asia's biggest hospital. I only have to make marginal improvements in the existing plans for the same to happen."

Heading: Centre loosens purse strings for Phase II of BRTS in city - Indian Express
Content:
They facilitated a private firm owner get a Rs 50 crore Central government contract

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Wednesday evening filed a case of corruption against three people, including two senior officers of the Food Corporation of India (FCI) in Gujarat and proprietor of a private firm in Vadodara.

The trio is accused of conspiracy and corruption in a Rs 50-crore Stevedoring Clearing Handling and Transportation (SCH&T) contract of the Central government in 2006. The contract was meant for stevedoring more than 13 lakh metric tons of wheat that India imported through Kandla port that year and later transporting packaged wheat to various places across the country, the CBI said.

According to CBI sleuths, FCI General Manager (Gujarat region) Abdul Rub, along with Assistant General Manager P R Anil, allegedly manipulated some terms and conditions of a government tender. This, the CBI said, was done to facilitate owner of Vadodara-Kailash Enterprises, Pradeep Jha, get the contract.

Jha, who is accused of forging documents to grab the contract, has been booked along with Rub and Anil, the CBI added.

According to the case details, in 2006, the Indian government had imported huge quantity of wheat through various ports in the country. About 13 lakh metric ton of this consignment was offloaded at Kandla and the SCH&T contract for this consignment was given to Jha.

This happened despite Jha's firm neither being financially sound enough to get the contract, nor having the qualified stevedores, the CBI said. During investigation, the CBI also found that Jha had used forged documents to show assets worth Rs 1.5 crore, as had been specified in the tender.

The CBI filed a formal complaint against the trio after strong evidence against the three was collected in simultaneous searches conducted by the agency at seven premises on Wednesday morning.

Heading: Govt to set up Rs 10-crore rolling fund to create new breed of ‘designpreneurs’ - Indian Express
Content:
JNNURM panel also clears Central instalments for six other projects submitted by AMC

Ministry of Urban Development has cleared the Central share of the Rs 488-crore second phase of the Bus Rapid Transit System (BRTS). The Central share comes to Rs 170.85 crore (35 per cent), of which, the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC) has sanctioned Rs 42.71 crore (25 per cent).

The Committee, which sanctions projects under Submission I of Urban Infrastructure and Governance (UIG) of the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM), in its meeting on Wednesday also approved the Central share towards the second and third instalments of six other projects submitted by Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC).

The total amount sanctioned as part of the Central share of 35 per cent comes to Rs 64.30 crore.

A sum of Rs 10.74 crore has been sanctioned as second instalment of the Central share of Rs 42.99 crore to implement a storm water drainage project worth Rs 122.83 crore for the north and east zones of the city. It has also sanctioned Rs 99 lakh as second instalment of the Central share of Rs 3.97 crore to renovate the existing Sewage Treatment Plant at Vasna at a total cost of Rs 11.35 crore.

Besides, Rs 1.31 crore has been sanctioned as third instalment of Central assistance worth Rs 5.25 crore for the construction of a four-lane over-bridge at Ambica Tubes crossing between Vatva and Maninagar stations on Ahmedabad-Mumbai broad gauge line. The bridge will come up at a cost of Rs 15 crore.

Apart from these sanctions, Rs 6.05 crore has been sanctioned as third instalment towards Central assistance of Rs 24.22 crore for the construction of a sewage treatment plant at Pirana costing Rs 69.22 crore, and Rs 1.62 crore as third instalment of Rs 6.49 crore to meet the cost of constructing a flyover on Sola junction. Another Rs 1.32 crore has been sanctioned as third instalment of Rs 5.5 crore to build a Rs 15.13 crore six-lane flyover at Memnagar junction.

Heading: Advani visits Somnath, prays country is rid of terrorism, inflation - Indian Express
Content:
The fund will be set up at NID's National Design Business Incubator to support those young designers who want to become entrepreneurs in the design field

A Rs 10-crore rolling fund will be set up at the National Institute of Design's (NID) National Design Business Incubator (NDBI), to help aspiring designers become entrepreneurs. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Kamal Nath made the announcement in New Delhi on Wednesday.

According to an official release, Nath also announced that NID faculty will be allowed to share consultancy fees on the lines of other premier institutions like IIMs and IITs.

Nath said that the proposed fund would be used to support those young designers who want to become entrepreneurs in the field of design. "Young designers who are keen to pursue their business ideas through incubation route at NDBI can now avail this rolling fund support," he said.

He also said that the objective of the Incubator (NDBI) was to encourage the spirit of innovation embedded in the creative culture of designers, thus paving the way for the creation of a new breed of "designpreneurs". In addition, he said, the Government had agreed to permit the NID faculty to have a share in their consultancy work. The pattern of consultancy sharing would be on the lines of other premier educational institutions in India such as IITs and IIMs.

NDBI was set up by NID in 2005 with an aim to develop India's design strengths. Lack of adequate support in pursuing designers' ideas into business models has so far been a debilitating factor for young designers in setting up their businesses.

The need to set up a separate Rolling Fund has arisen especially when most of the financial institutions do not support young designers who are fresh, and first generation entrepreneurs just out of the academic institutions, without industrial experience, the release said.

Heading: Six years on, trial yet to start - Indian Express
Content:
Leader of the Opposition Lal Krishna Advani visited Somnath Temple on Thursday and said that he prayed that the country is exonerated of the "devils of terrorism and inflation — two devils the country is facing the most".

After an overnight stay at Rajkot, Advani boarded a chopper and reached Somnath Temple at 9.38 am. He offered prayers at the temple. Later, he addressed the local BJP leaders at the VVIP guesthouse.

This was Advani's 18th visit to the temple since 1990, when he had commenced the famous Rath Yatra that changed the political scenario of the country.

During his brief interaction with mediapersons, Advani said that each year he makes an oath at the Somnath Temple. "This time, I prayed to get rid of terrorism and inflation. My countrymen should get complete relief from the clutches of terrorism and inflation and I prayed for it".

Heading: Medium polluting units put on fast track to clearance - Indian Express
Content:
Total of 141 were accused in Godhra case; four died and six fled to Pakistan

Of the 141 people accused in the Godhra train fire of 2002, 106 were arrested under Prevention Of Terrorist Act (POTA). While none have gone under trial, four died awaiting it and six others fled to Pakistan.

Two of the accused were bailed out, as one was HIV positive and the other suffered from bone tuberculosis. Those who died in jail are Fakruddin Musallman, Siraj Jamsa, Qutubuddin Ansari and Latif Rasul. Musallman and Rasul died of bone tuberculosis. Jamsa and Ansari died of paralysis.

Musallman died in Sabarmati jail in 2005, where the rest were bailed out due to deteriorating condition of the jail. In 2008, Mohammed Ansari and Idris Charkha got bail on health grounds.

Ibrahim Charkha and Salim Badam alias Panwalla, who fled to Pakistan, spoke to Newsline over phone. They claimed to be innocent and wanted to return to India, but said they could not trust the police to be fair to them.

Sources said another accused, Faroukh Bana, is also in Pakistan.

In August 2008, POTA court had allowed three of those convicted in the Godhra incident to visit their families as part of the parole, including Godhra advocate Ruhulamin Husain Hathila. The other two sent on parole for 24 hours are Shaukat Padriya and Rafi Ahmed Jamnu.

Heading: Commercial garba banned in Surendranagar - Indian Express
Content:
'Orange' industries allowed to file online application; now only 'Red' ones require to submit hard copies

In a bid to reduce red-tapism and ensure smooth decision-making, the Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB) has decided to allow all applications filed by the Orange category industries relating to consolidated consent and authorisation order, to be channelled through the XGN (Extended Green Node) from September 25.

The XGN, which was started on June 5 this year, is an online application put in place by the GPCB where all applicants are given a registration number and password. They can just log in and track the status of their application.

Sanjeev Tyagi, member secretary, GPCB said: "We are trying to introduce total transparency by this. The processing time right now is about 120 days. We are aiming to reduce it to 30 days progressively."

Gujarat, with over nine per cent industrial growth and more than 15,000 operational industrial units, has waited long for such an initiative.

It may be mentioned here that all industries in India are classified as Red, Orange and Green, by the Ministry of Environment & Forests, Government of India, on the basis of their potential to cause pollution.

The Green category is of the least polluting small-scale cottage industries such as flour mills, tailoring, bakery etc. The Red category includes the most polluting industries such as distilleries, pulp and paper, smelters etc.

The Orange category is of medium polluting industries such as soft drinks, fish processing, perfumes etc.

Though the XGN application was open to all the three categories of industries, except for the Green, each of the other two categories had to submit three additional hard copies of their application in the respective regional offices of GPCB.

One copy was sent to the GPCB's head-office in Gandhinagar along with the inspection report, another was sent to the water cess department and the third kept at the regional office for future reference. Now, only the Red category of industries will have to submit the three hard copies.

"In about a month, this waiver will come for the Red category as well. We need our staff to be well-trained for online handling of applications before we switch to XGN completely," said Tyagi.

Heading: Nirma Univ to host two-day management conclave - Indian Express
Content:
Commercialisation of garba in any form has been banned in Surendranagar. As per the notification issued by District Collector J D Bhad, the step will also help maintain law and order.

Those found violating it will be prosecuted under the provisions of the Bombay Police Act and the Indian Penal Code.

"There is no entry fee in religious functions such as Ganeshotsav and Durga Puja," the notification states. "In Surendranagar district, there are some places where celebration of the auspicious festival of Navratri is being polluted. Some professional people and organisations are doing it to earn money," the notification adds.

To maintain the sanctity of the festival and law and order in the district, the menace needs to be curbed, it states.

However, the district collector has allowed the display of commercial banners at different garba venues.

Bhad told Newsline: "There are places where the organisers charge Rs 300-400 as entry fee at the garba venue. To maintain the sanctity of the festival apart from law and order, the order has been issued. Many a time, people start fighting when they fail to get entry to a particular venue".

Speaking on the ban, Meghal Shah who organises commercial garba in Ahmedabad under the banner of MitMegh Garbas said that the problem in Surendranagar is more of law and order than of commercialisation. "We ensure good security arrangement for the garbas," he said.

Heading: Leopard carcass found at dam site - Indian Express
Content:
Prayaag '08, a two-day management conclave of the Institute of Management at Nirma University, will begin on Friday at the varsity campus, bringing great minds together on one platform. Industry experts will give a sneak preview of the management industry to aspiring managers.

'Technology driving business for the country's growth and prosperity' is the theme for the conclave. It underlines the importance of technology as the key to continuous innovation.

This year's speakers include industry leaders and bureaucrats like Vimal Ambani, P D. Vaghela, S C Rastogi, Krishna Gopa and Manish Bhardwaj among others. In the past, the likes of J J Irani, Sam Pitroda, D Ravi Shankar, and Sanjay Lalbhai have addressed the conclave.

The Institute of Management, earlier known as Nirma Institute of Management, is a constituent of Nirma University of Science and Technology, Ahmedabad. It was established in 1996 and has now emerged as an excellent business school having ranked amongst the top 10 Business Schools established post-1990, according to a survey carried out five years ago, says the Institute release.

Heading: ‘Wild card’ for regularising animal articles and trophies - Indian Express
Content:
The carcass of a full grown leopard was found at the Kalindri dam site, near Kutiyana town in Porbandar district on Thursday. Forest officers have ruled out foul play maintaining that the animal's death was natural.

Forest Officer (Kutiyana range) V P Thumar said, "The leopard was about 10 years old. There was no sign of any external or internal injury. Besides, all its claws were found intact."

The autopsy could not ascertain the exact cause of the death as the carcass was found perhaps about 24 hours after the death and was deteriorating, he said.

The viscera of the animal has been sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory, Junagadh for a detailed clinical examination.

Heading: VMC gets into action mode after largescale fish mortality in Sursagar - Indian Express
Content:
Social forestry dept swings into action to issue ownership certificates

In what could be an absolute regularisation of wild animal articles and trophies acquired by the erstwhile Baroda royal family scions and renowned businessmen of the city, the Vadodara Social Forestry Department is finally gearing up to offer ownership certificates this year, under a central government notification, which was issued in 2003.

Interestingly, most of the animal trophies, which consist of antelope horns, elephant tusk articles, leopard trophies, stuffed tiger heads and spotted dear horns belong to the city bigwigs. Some of them are Chirayu Amin, the chairman and managing director of Alembic, erstwhile Baroda Royal family members including Ranjisinh Gaekwad, former Mayor Rajendrasinh Rathod and various other businessmen in the city.

Social Forestry Department records show that Amin possesses shahtoosh shawls. The wool for this garment is obtained from an endangered species — Chiru (Pantholops Hodgsoni), commonly known as Tibetian antelope. According to the records, Amin's family owns 27 such shawls. Though shahtoosh trade has been banned now, social forestry officials have regularised Amin's ownership of the shawls as it was proved that they were purchased many years ago.

D B Ande, Conservator of Forest (CF), Social Forestry, Bharuch, who is the signing authority in giving the ownership certificate in the entire south Gujarat, said: "The Central Government released a notification on the certificate of ownership in 2003. According to the notification, the possessors will be allowed to regularise their possession of wild animal busts and trophies provided the articles are not for sale and the possessors have facilities for housing, maintenance and upkeep of the animal trophies."

When asked about the reason behind the delay in regularising the ownership of animal articles, Ande said: "Most people who had acquired animal articles were very old. They were mostly from the royal families and were given these articles when they were passing on their realm to the government. Though the Central Government had made the announcement, there was not much awareness amongst the people."

Out of all the Social Forestry circles in south Gujarat, Vadodara circle has the maximum number of animal articles.

Nayan Desai, District Conservator of Forest (DCF), Vadodara Social Forestry Division, said: "There are around 305 wild animal articles possessed by various individuals in the city." He added that nearly 50 per cent of the regularisation work has been completed.

Former Mayor Rajendrasinh Rathod, who has a tiger trophy and a pair of antelope horns, said: "Both the articles are priceless to me since my family has been carrying the legacy from my forefathers for the last 100 years. There was a delay regularising the possession as the signing authority was in Bharuch. However, now we have completed all the protocols."

Heading: Modi gives his piece of mind to Opposition, others - Indian Express
Content:
Almost 500-600 kg of fish have died following this year's Ganesh visarjan

With over 600 kilogrammes of fish species left dead after this year's Ganesh visarjan, the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) authorities have swung into action to curb the steep decline of marine life in Sursagar Lake.

The daily dumping of garbage combined with the yearly immersion process creates a crust formation of Plaster of Paris (PoP). This drastically reduces the oxygen level in the lake, thus killing aquatic life in large numbers.

Keeping in view the alarmingly high mortality rate of marine creatures in the lake, VMC is now planning to install fountains in the lake, which will help in increasing the oxygen level in the water.

"Around 1,700 idols were immersed in the lake this year and almost all of them were made of PoP. The PoP remains accumulate in the lake bed, thus decreasing the oxygen level in the lake. In addition, harmful chemicals used in the paints also pollute the lake. We cannot ban the practice as it is a religious and sentimental issue," said a VMC official.

VMC Mayor Balu Shukla said: "We have decided to install fountains in the lake to solve the issue. This will help in aerating the water and increasing the oxygen level in the lake. We will take the help of some NGOs in this as well."

A recent study found that the sudden drop in the oxygen level after the immersion process is the main cause of marine deaths in Sursagar Lake. The study, which inspected seven spots across the lake, revealed that the oxygen consumption for the chemical degradation process called Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD), which should ideally not be more than 30 mg, was ranging between 85 to 145 mg.

Another VMC official said on condition of anonymity, "There are fishes dying every year, but this time bigger fishes, weighing over 7 to 8 kg, died in huge numbers. It has been estimated that almost 500 to 600 kg of fishes have died this season."

Heading: Nanavati panel report draws flak from Cong, civil society groups - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Narendra Modi has sharply criticised the Opposition's stand on the Nanavati Commission of Inquiry report. He said that while he has been silent on the Godhra train carnage issue for the last six years, the first part of the report that was tabled in the Assembly on Thursday has cleared all confusion surrounding the incident.

Addressing a gathering at his own constituency, Maninagar, on the occasion of the 92nd birth anniversary of Pandit Dindayal Upadhyaya, Modi said that with this report clearing the air, Congress should now stop spreading falsehoods.

"I have been silent on this issue for the last six years, as I was waiting for the inquiry committee's report to be tabled first," Modi said, adding that the Congress and others, who had spread lies about the incident, should now apologise to the people of Gujarat.

Modi also came down heavily on the appointment of the Justice UC Banerjee Committee by the Union Railway Ministry and said the committee was appointed only to serve the political interests of the railway minister. "However, the Bihar electorate was not convinced and voted against him," he said.

"Congress has used the issue to the maximum possible extent for its vote-bank politics, but it did not even have the courage to sit on the floor of the House when the report was being tabled," Modi added.

Heading: Taking stock - Indian Express
Content:
Film folks sum up the contradictions that mark Bollywood's new phase

SALMAN KHAN
Of blockbusters and multiplexes
The prevalent corporate climate hasn't altered my scheme of things much. I never signed any agreement or contract. I still don't do that. I believe in trust. Nothing has changed for me, just that the prices have shot up phenomenally. The only perceivable change is that moviegoers have gone back to the theatre. And it isn't just the multiplexes. People are also watching films in single-screen theatres because of the upgraded facilities all around. Things are really looking up.

VIDHU VINOD CHOPRA
More than business
WHEN I saw Loins of Punjab, I realised that there is an alternate cinema quietly taking shape in India. With Rock On!!, my belief has just been strengthened that maybe young filmmakers can steer clear of the kind of compromises that many have had to make to get their foot into this very competitive but intoxicating world of movies.

But at the same time, I'm disturbed by the increasing obsession we have developed for the opening weekend. We seem to have stopped asking certain crucial questions, like what are the values our film propagates. When we green-light a project or begin to write a film, these are the first of the many questions we must ask ourselves.

So if we have taken a step forward, it feels like we may have taken two steps back because of the force with which marketing, projection and box-office pressures have begun to impact our filmmaking. Cinema is more than "over Rs 100 crore in three days".

FARHAN AKHTAR
Varied scripts
ACTORS are willing to take risks with their roles, something which was not the case a few years ago. And this new unpredictability where we don't know in what role we will see an actor is a very good sign. Scripts rule, with people like Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra, Amole Gupte and Ashutosh Gowariker coming up with gripping projects. I think Mehra's Aks had a rare and off-beat subject for a film. Marketing of films too has reached another level altogether. Films launching merchandise in their name, contests, stars on reality shows — this trend can only get bigger. There is also a large audience for Indian films outside India that comprises not only NRIs but also people from all nationalities. It's the new and gripping content of our films that is getting attention. Single producers who were churning out the same stuff with no new ideas have been replaced by corporate houses ever ready to experiment with new concepts and formulas. Multitasking is also the new mantra with actors like Aamir Khan producing, directing and acting in a film like Taare Zameen Par. I wrote Rock On!!, produced it, wrote dialogue, acted and sang in it.

MADHURI DIXIT
Indian, not Bollywood
I HATE the term 'Bollywood' but an Indian film has everything for any kind of audience. I try to watch every film, and with Internet and with multiplexes coming up all over the place, it has become so easy to catch up with the latest releases. Lately, there have been some very good films, many with messages. The quality of films has also improved and I am happy that the Hindi film industry is progressing very well. People are coming in with good scripts and good planning.

SOHA ALI KHAN
Changed scenario
I BELIEVE Indian cinema is the finest form of art in our country. Films are the best medium for reaching out and conveying the message to a large chunk of audience. Indian cinema is undergoing a slow change, though it is not very apparent and drastic. Mindsets are breaking, trends are changing and people are open to experimentation. Directors are willing to cast newcomers in their films, there are varied films being made, like Bheja Fry and Love Story 2050, and multi-starrers have won over actors interested in solo leads. Films like Mumbai Meri Jaan that send out social messages should be made. Along with entertainment, some kind of social message should also be imparted.

RANI MUKERJI
Newfound respect
'NEW and improved' are strong words and I would use them sparingly, but yes, there have been changes in every decade. There was a change from silent to the talkies, black-and-white to colour — it's been a natural progression of sorts. The most wonderful part of it all is that films are now looked at with respect. Parents are now encouraging their children who want to be a part of it. It's also more professional like being a doctor or engineer—there are a lot more people who are looking for a career in the technical side in Bollywood. Also the attitude towards making films is that everybody wants to make a good film.

DEEPIKA PADUKONE
Public demand
I FEEL today's audience is lot more intelligent. Newer people have come into the industry. Those who are scripting films are touching upon new subjects. Many films are connecting with the audience, even offbeat ones. Films are back to being realistic. Films like Jab We Met and Jaane Tu...Ya Jaane Na had a fresh treatment.

RANBIR KAPOOR
Breaking norms
THE 1950s saw the best of Hindi cinema. Movies then were made straight from the heart by filmmakers like Raj Kapoor and Guru Dutt. Cut to 2000 and cinema is progressing very fast. There's an influx of new and young directors and scriptwriters. Everybody is ready to break norms and take risks. I believe this is a progressive trait. It makes it easier for me to play interesting roles. I had a dream launch with Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Saawariya, an unusual film as a debut. Plot-driven films are gaining importance.

Heading: Advance booking - Indian Express
Content:
Kirron Kher takes a break from playing Punjabi characters

Bahut ho gaya, chaddo tussi. Thankfully, I am no longer playing the character of a Punjabi woman. I think it's time I started exploring other roles," chuckles actor Kirron Kher, 53, who plays a Bengali character in her latest movie, the delightfully titled Saas Bahu Aur Sensex. The plot is based on middle class aspirations juxtaposed against the regular fluctuations in the Stock market. The star cast may not be too impressive, but there is consolation since it is the first Hindi film Warner Brothers is representing in India.

Kher plays a middle class woman, Binita Sen, from Kolkata who lives in a Mumbai neighbourhood with her daughter played by Tanushree Dutta. She wants to start life afresh but she lives in a flat with saas bahu serials obsessed women. So is she a fan of the Kyunkis? "No way. There is already so much drama in real life," smiles Kher. The stock market angle is provided by veteran actor Farooque Shaikh, who is a broker in the film and educates Kher on the stock market. "I am clueless about the stock market. I keep away from such things. Working with Farooque was a pleasure since he is a complete ladies man," says Kher. Will it work? It just might, considering Bollywood can be as unpredictable as the Sensex..

Heading: Worm in McDonald’s burger: A year on, couple waits for justice - Indian Express
Content:
With glossy pictures, catchy punch lines and an enticing outline of the story, booklets are the new- age tools for film publicity

There have been films that created history. So much so that books were written on them. Today, irrespective of whether a film is worth being written a book on or not, booklets are written for sure and that too before the films are released. Arjun Bali, director, Ru Ba Ru explains the film maker's thought process as he says, "The market today is competitive and extreme visibility is important to sell your product in the market. With corporatisation taking over Bollywood why shouldn't films follow the promotional strategies?"

Stating the importance of promotion Bali explains, "In case of big budget films, the stars speak for themselves. But with low budget films where characters are more important than the stars, promotions are of utmost importance to attract audiences and media. Promotion I feel is an irreplaceable part of the entire process of film making like casting, script, shooting and editing."

And once promotion is made an irreplaceable part of filmmaking, then sky is the limit. Be it hoardings, posters, CDs, wallpapers or mascots the advertising agencies leave no stone unturned. Additional, and quite recent introductions in the field of film publicity, are booklets. Stuffed with all the information about the film, designed to grab attention and loaded with eye catching wallpapers, these booklets are sent to media houses before the movie releases. Aarti Jadhav, a PR professional who's worked on the promotions of a number of films like Jodha Akbar, Rock on, Mithya and so on explains, "The most important factor in case of promotions is media. A booklet is designed to grab attention of the media and it is observed that it hits the bull's eye."

Swapnil Rane, creative head with one of the advertising companies throws light on the demand for booklets and the intricacies in designing them. "The designs of the brochures depend on various things. For instance the theme of the film, the budget, the masses targeted. We call this the brief of the movie. I have designed a number of brochures for films like Fashion, Mughal-e-Azam and so on. And to explain how theme decides the design let me tell you, the brochure of Fashion that I designed looks like a makeup kit. The brochure for Mughal-e-Azam contained the entire set of the film and the moment one opened the brochure, the set came alive in front of his eyes," Says he.

With so much of creativity, moolah and productivity gone behind, do the booklets have the desired effect? A media professional who does not want her identity to be disclosed says, "I must say they catch your attention. Further, they give us the basic idea of what the film would be like. For instance, the layout of a comedy film is peppy. That of a serious film would be according to the theme. And yes, it also makes all the information available at one place which makes our job easy."

Tahaan: The picture of an innocent kid with his donkey, the brochure conveys that it is an emotional story.
Drona: Designed with strong colours like gold and black, swords, rugged looks- the brochure of this Abhishek Bachchan, Priyanka Chopra starrer conveys nothing but power.
Wednesday: Stills from the movie, quotes from the actors, use of dark colours and punch lines that generate curiosity.
Welcome to Sajjanpur: Colourful brochure, friendly characters, and director's note the brochure makes an impression that it is a light movie.

Heading: PMPML’s  school bus: NGO invites points from schools, parents - Indian Express
Content:
A year after Gregory Belsher and his wife Irene's bitter experience at the McDonald's, the couple is still waiting for justice.

Last year on May 25, The Indian Express had reported the experience of Gregory and his wife when they found a worm in the Chicken Maharaja Mac they had ordered at the Mc Donald's on J M Road.

When they complained to the manager in-charge of the store, he refused to replace the snack. What followed was a string of calls and visits to various authorities to prove the case.

However, when no conclusive results were obtained, the harassed couple moved the consumer court.

The case, finally, came up for hearing more than a year after they filed the complaint. Gregory Belsher said, "We have been running from pillar to post since the last one year, hoping to hear something from McDonald's. They failed to respond to the notices we sent them. So we moved the consumer court."

He said that they have filed a case of inconvenience and mental harassment against the food giant. Advocate Yogesh Shinde is representing McDonald's in the court. "As this is the first hearing, we have applied for an extension," Shinde said.

When asked if the food giant will accept the claims made by Gregory he said, "It's too early to say and as of now all I can say is we will proceed according to the progress of the case."

Heading: Man demands CBI probe into son’s death, threatens self immolation - Indian Express
Content:
Pedestrians First, a city-based NGO, has appealed the school managements and parents to submit their suggestions regarding the special school bus service which has been started by the Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal (PMPML) for the convenience of students of various schools.

"The suggestions on proposed starting point, desired route and departure time should be submitted to us so that they can be considered to improve the service," said Prashant Inamdar, convenor of Pedestrian First in a press release.

"The buses being operated on trial basis in the evenings have received overwhelming response from schoolchildren. The service is likely to be introduced on other routes as the PMPML has begun assessment of requirement on particular routes," Inamdar said.

Heading: Courier company employee held for kidnapping, robbing colleague - Indian Express
Content:
Shivaji V Borkar, a resident of Haveli Taluka, on Thursday threatened to immolate himself on October 7 in front of the Mantralaya if his demand for a fresh CBI probe into the alleged murder of his son are not met.

Shivaji's son Ramesh Borkar (23) was working as a site supervisor with a builder, Sandeep Walimbe. On April 11 2007, Shivaji received a call from Walimbe saying that Ramesh had committed suicide by hanging himself inside a bathroom at the construction site.

Later, he was asked to immediately remove the body from Sassoon General Hospital after it was declared a suicide. Shivaji said, "The bathroom where my son was found dead was about four-and-a-half feet high and he was over five-and-a-half feet tall. How could he have hung himself there? Ramesh was unhappy with his job. I asked him to stay on till his marriage, which was to happen soon. This is a big cover-up by the builder and the police."

Nilesh Bade, a social activist, said, "The police did not consider Shivaji's complaint and for the last one and a half years, he has been trying to get the authorities to arrest the builder. Deputy Chief Minister R R Patil had demanded an inquiry into the matter after Shivaji had gone on a fast at the Azad Maidan near the Mantralaya in Mumbai.

"However, in the subsequent enquiry by the Sahakarnagar police, I got the same response — that my son's death was a suicide," said Shivaji.

In a note to media persons, he said if his demands of a CBI enquiry in the case against the builder and police officers were not met, he would immolate himself in front of the Mantralaya in Mumbai.

When contacted, DCP Satish Khandare said, "The postmortem report has confirmed that this is a suicide case. Investigations have revealed that Shivaji had taken a loan sometime back. Due to his inability to repay it, the boy was under stress. This is a possible cause, which we are looking into. However, if the complainant has any proof to support his claim, the police will investigate the matter thoroughly."

Heading: Veggie plate ruined by rain, smashed by price blow - Indian Express
Content:
The Khadak police on Wednesday arrested a courier company employee along with two accomplices for allegedly kidnapping and robbing his colleague of Rs 5 lakh.

Though the incident had taken place on September 5, the police said that victim Mahesh Madhurabi Patel (40) had lodged the complaint late.

The police have identified the accused as Jitendra alias Kanhiyalal Manihar (35), Lalsingh Vihol (26) and Hemant Vihol (33), all natives of Rajkot in Gujrat.

According to the police, Patel and Manihar were working at Jaykeshwar courier company in Budhwar Peth. Patel was asked to take Rs 5 lakh cash to their Mumbai office. On September 5, Patel left office with cash. Manihar dropped him at Swargate bus depot.

Patel noticed that a car was chasing them and told Manihar about the it. But Manihar ignored it. He dropped Patel at Swargate and left the spot.

Two persons in the car forced Patel into the car and took him to Katraj ghat and stole the cash at knifepoint. The duo then left him there and escaped.

Patel reached Mumbai and narrated the incident to the company owner. Patel expressed doubts about Manihar. The company initiated an internal inquiry. But Manihar denied his involvement in the crime.

Patel lodged a complaint with Khadak police station. The police arrested Manihar. During the interrogation, he confessed to committing the crime with the help of two accomplices.

A police team, led by assistant inspector Nandakumar Suryawanshi, arrested Lalsingh and Hemant. The accused have been remanded to police custody till September 29.

Heading: To curb expenses, KCB members opt for less remuneration - Indian Express
Content:
If retailers quote better prices, they don't have supplies in the first place

Within a fortnight, vegetable prices have almost quadrupled with heavy rain destroying crops across the state. True, many low-cost retailers are quoting a price half of what vegetable vendors outside are charging, but they don't have most vegetables in the first place.

Take french beans for example. It's being sold by local vegetable vendors at Rs 80 a kg. Subhiksha stores is charging Rs 30 per kg and Aditya Birla's More Rs 35. But most of these low-cost retailers have not been selling french beans since the vegetable prices skyrocketed in the last two weeks. The reason: there are no supplies from the fields to sell at that price. Bucking the trend is Reliance Fresh, which has priced the vegetables slightly higher (french beans at Rs 50 per kg) and has the supplies.

A senior official of a leading retail store said vegetables and fruits being the driving segments of any retail chain that includes many other segments, their prices cannot be pegged too high for fear of losing customers to other segments of the store.

True, quality supplies are very low because of the rain, especially in the vegetable belt of Nashik and some other districts, including the outskirts of Pune. "We get our vegetables from the common collections centres. That is how we maintain the price line. We could buy these vegetables from the open market, but the prices would be very high and unaffordable for our customers. There would also be less control on quality," said a senior executive with another leading vegetable retail chain.

He said that according to market research, a family spends not more than Rs 60-70 a day on vegetables and if prices are higher, vegetables may not be sold. "Some vegetables are being procured from the local markets because of the demand. We incur some loss on these, but it cannot be done across the segment," he said. This chain has tried to keep tomatoes and cauliflowers low-priced.

"We have to maintain a price that is comfortable for the customer," said Pramod Patil, head procurement, Subhiksha. At Subhiksha, lady's finger costs Rs 30, cauliflower Rs 40, spinach Rs 6, tomato Rs 18, bottle gourd Rs 35 and cucumber Rs 25 a kg. But stocks are running low.

Of the 30 outlets in the city, only five get regular supplies. "We get only about 50 kg of tomato, but it disappears even if 15-20 customers pay a visit," said a Subhiksha attendant.

At the receiving end are the people. "We buy only essential items day by day. With prices soaring, we are not buying extra vegetables," said Mahesh Shah. "I am not buying less vegetables, usually around 250 gm or so. We are going in for more dal and soybean instead of vegetables," said Sharda, a housewife.

Heading: Four new SEZs, Rs 8,000 crore investment, 60,000 jobs - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to reduce unwarranted expenses, members of the Khadki Cantonment Board (KCB) have opted for an honorarium amount of just Rs 4,000 a month. "The idea is to curb the spendthrift attitude and reduce unnecessary expenditure," KCB vice president Manish Anand said on Thursday. "We were initially against the idea of taking any remuneration, which would have set an example. But owing to certain legal provisions, all members were bound to accept the honorarium," Anand said.

Discussing the steps taken by KCB to accelerate development, Anand said the board had approved a proposal from its education committee to provide uniforms, schoolbags, books and other stationery to school kids in Khadki region. "We are aiming at giving a major fillip to education in Khadki," said Anand. He said the board will soon issue trade permits to hawkers, provided they go through police verification and produce adequate proof of residence and identity. "However, only 254 hawkers will be given permits for commercial activities at any given point of time. This will serve as a deterrent to hawkers from outside the Cantonment area," he said.

Heading: Crackdown on landlords who didn’t check out on tenants - Indian Express
Content:
Four SEZs from a total of nine, spread over 2,100 hectares, will bring in Rs 8,308 crore as investment and create 60,000 new jobs, putting Pune district firmly ahead of the rest of the state in the industrial race.

Two of the four SEZs will be in the IT sector and the other two multi-product ones. Both IT SEZs feature new entrants - Cavalcade Properties and Skyzone - while the multi-product ones involves players already into SEZs: DS Kulkarni and Bharat Forge.

Bharat Forge's SEZ at Khed and Shirur is a joint venture with the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC), with the main promoter holding 74 per cent equity.

It will need 2,000 hectares; an official from the industries department said 1,222 hectares have already been acquired. The SEZ will see investment of Rs 5,000 crore and its export earnings have been projected at Rs 50,000 crore.

A rehabilitation package has been introduced successfully at three villages in Khed and one in Shirur taluka, said the officer. It is the only one of the four that involves acquisition; the other three already have the land they need.

The DS Kulkarni multi product SEZ at Fursungi will span 101.2 hectares and involve an investment of Rs 2,303 crore. The developers have projected their exports at Rs 2,550 crores and say they will employ 10,000 people.

The two IT SEZs, one in Dhanori and the other at Mohammedwadi in Haveli taluka, will be equal in size at 10.8 hectares each. The Skyzone SEZ, coming up at Dhanori with an investment of Rs 698 crore, is projected to have an export earning of Rs 326.4 crore and is looking at employment of 15,000 people. The Cavalcade SEZ will see an investment of Rs 307 crore and has put its export potential at Rs 324 crore, with 20,000 jobs.

For the first five years, the SEZs will enjoy total tax exemption; for the next five, they will pay 50 per cent tax; for the five years after that, the exemption will be worked out depending on each SEZ's earnings.

Bharat Forge was given sanction in principle two years ago. The other three SEZs were proposed on July 31 and cleared on September 23. With 139 SEZs lined up, the state aims to create 74 lakh new jobs. There are as many as 18 more proposals for SEZs in the district in the pipeline.

Heading: Let maths stay tough as ever: Schools shun simpler version - Indian Express
Content:
The police on Wednesday night cracked down on sections of the society adopting a lackadaisical attitude towards orders and warnings. The police came down heavily upon house owners who had not submitted details of their tenants, and the roadside food stall owners.

In the wake of terrorist activities across the country, Commissioner of Police Dr Satyapal Singh had repeatedly issued orders that house owners and the real estate agents need to inform the police about the tenants.

But very few had furnished the information.

Taking a serious note of this, on Wednesday Singh passed an order asking all police stations to file cases against property owners who are defying the orders.

Accordingly, cops at 11 police stations filed cases against 41 house owners under Section 188 of Indian Penal Code. Other police stations are also trying to scan the defaulters.

The police have appealed to the house owners to submit a proper report, including the names, native address and photographs of all the tenants at the respective police stations. Recently, four house owners were arrested for renting the apartments to four Sudanese students who were overstaying, despite expiry of their visas about two years ago.

The police also cracked down on 71 anda bhurji and Chinese food stalls in the city for allowing hooliganism and illegal consumption of liquor. Singh had been receiving several complaints about miscreants who were consuming liquor at various food stalls and then troubling the local residents, especially the women, in the night.

Cases have been filed against such stalls owners operating in localities such as Khadki, Viman Nagar, Yerawada, Budhwar Peth, Warje, Pune Cantonment amongst others. However, Bund Garden and Swargate police stations failed to comply with the orders and did not take any action.

The police have asked residents to inform about any such stall in their vicinity on phone number 21626296 or at the nearest police station.

Heading: Rs 15 lakh seized in hawala bust - Indian Express
Content:
It was a move aimed at making life simpler for students weak at mathematics; only, it hasn't quite taken off.

In June, the Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education introduced a simpler version of the subject - general mathematics, as compared to 'regular' mathematics. Several months on, the idea has still not found favour with schools. In fact, many students don't even know that such a version exists.

There are two reasons why schools are reluctant to introduce the subject. One, it would dent their reputation: it would create the notion that their students are not strong enough at maths. The other thing going against the subject is that any student who opts for it will not be eligible for admission to the science stream in Class XI. In other words, it will close the door for admission to medical and engineering courses.

Only a handful of civic-run schools have introduced general mathematics so far. On record, most other schools cite non-availability of faculty. Many students find regular mathematics tough. It has been a low-scoring subject for years.

The board had issued a circular on the introduction of the simpler version for the weak in Class IX. It plans to extend the option to Class X students next year onwards.

But because so few schools have taken it up, many students have never heard of general mathematics. "I surveyed 59 schools in the city and found ambiguity about this among teachers and students," said Narendra Sidhaye, who is studying the new subject as part of his M.Ed thesis. "At some PMC schools, students have already been directed to take only general mathematics in Class IX," he said. "On the other hand, major schools don't want their students to take general mathematics as they fear losing their reputation. This is true of boys' as well as girls' schools," he said.

City schools are ready with their explanations. "The board conveyed the decision very late, when the academic year had already started. To introduce a new subject, it is necessary to increase a division and also arrange for the faculty, which was not possible at the eleventh hour," said T S Mundhe, principal of Ramanbaug High School. "."

Mundhe admitted that some students might have wanted to take up general mathematics at Class X next year, but would not be able to do so. "We are not introducing general mathematics at Class IX from next year either," he added.

"There is no demand for general mathematics at our school; no one has opted for it," said Shobha Shimpi, principal of MIT Marathi High School. "We had called a meeting of parents after we received the circular, but no one showed interest." Board chairman Vijaysheela Sardesai insisted that the schools had been informed well in advance about the decision. "We had also called a meeting of principals to inform them. If some schools are not implementing the decision, the parents should inform the board or nearest education officer," said Sardesai.

Heading: Study says by 2010 India will have 60 % of world’s heart patients - Indian Express
Content:
The crime branch of Pune police has busted a hawala racket with the arrest of four persons at Rasta Peth on Thursday evening. Police have recovered Rs 15.12 lakh in cash from the suspects.

The suspects were identified as Bhagirath Giridharilal Sharma (26), Padmanath Sidh (23), Virainath Sidh (31) and Shivnath Sidh (19), all residents of Shantisarovar Apartment near Shiralsheth Chowk in Rasta Peth. All the suspects are natives of Rajasthan and had come to Pune a few months back. Acting on a tip-off, a crime branch team led by inspector Vijaysingh Gaikwad raided the apartment and nabbed the suspects who had  Rs 15.12 lakh in their possession.

Police said that these suspects provide a link to a bigger hawala racket. Primary interrogations have revealed that they were transferring money to any place in the country on a commission basis through hawala transactions.

"The suspects were charging Rs 2,000 as commission for transferring Rs 1 lakh. They were using code words for transferring money to big cities like Mumbai, Ahmedabad and Delhi," said Inspector Gaikwad.

Additional Commissioner of Police Rajender Singh, Deputy Commissioner

Anil Kumbhare and Assistant Commissioner Sangramsinh Nishandar are monitoring the investigations. The main operators of the hawala racket are believed to be located in different cities. The crime branch is also on a lookout for the kingpins and businessmen from Pune who were connected to the suspects for transferring their "black money" through hawala.

Heading: Angry mob pelts garbage containers - Indian Express
Content:
Going by a latest study published in the Lancet, by 2010 India will be home to world's 60 per cent of people suffering from heart disease. And every four heart attacks will happen without any symptoms or at least none that the victim associates with a heart problem like chest pain.

"It may be silent, but it can be deadly and devastating, says Dr Shirish Hiremath, Director, Cathlab, Ruby Hall Clinic.

During a silent heart attack, the patient is not aware of the cardiac event and because recoverable time is wasted, the heart becomes permanently damaged. Often we find that the patient's heart is seriously damaged because he could not act right at the time of silent attack. Once it occurs, the patient will have only a few years left, says Hiremath.

People should understand that the absence of pain, however, does not mean the absence of damage. The heart has a built-in reserve capacity, allowing it to suffer a certain amount of scarring and weakening from a heart attack and continues to meet the body's needs. But further ischemia or another heart attack, even a mild one, may prove fatal because that reserve capacity is no longer there.

Meanwhile the Poona hospital has completed 12 years of its Reversal of heart disease programme led by Dr Jagdish Hiremath. Almost 10,000 patients have taken advantage of this program till today, says Dr Nitin Unkule, yoga therapist.

Four-km walk and fitness talk on World Heart Day
As the world prepares to observe September 28 as World Heart Day, a host of city-based associations has organised several events including four-kilometre walks and a discussion on the importance of fitness.

Shrikant Mundade from the Hriday Mitra Pratishthan said that a book will be released on the occasion of World Heart Day about exercise and fitness. Mundada said that youngsters are becoming prone to high blood pressure and cholesterol levels. Recently, a 26-year-old was admitted for an angiography, Mundada said emphasising the need for a good diet and fitness regime.

Dr Arvind Inamdar, head of the Cardiac Department at Sassoon General Hospital said that they perform about 20-25 heart surgeries every month. He said that though they can set a target of 50 surgeries but due to space shortage and with only a five-bed ICU, the number of patients taken were less.

Heading: 500 villages flooded in UP - Indian Express
Content:
Villagers want depot out of Urali Devachi, PMC says no alternate place

Pressing their demand to shift out the garbage depot, the residents of Urali Devachi and Phursingi village pelted stones on Pune Municipal Corporation's garbage containers.

A few MLAs, who are part of the states legislative advisory committee, along with Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi and Mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale, visited the garbage depot at Urali Devachi on Thursday morning.

In a meeting with PMC authorities and the MLAs, Pardeshi said the garbage depot is filled to its capacity. But there was no alternate place available to dump garbage. The MLAs asked Pardeshi to arrange for an alternate place as soon as possible.

The meeting was arranged by members of the Garbage Depot Hatao Samiti, including Sarpanch of Urali Devachi Balasaheb Lende, vice-sarpanch Sanjay Harpale and businessman Dilip Mehta.

Of the 29 MLAs in the advisory committee, only eight of them turned up for the meeting.

The villagers turned angry as the meeting lasted only a few minutes and the MLAs left without listening to their complaints.

Agitated villagers stopped the garbage containers on the road at 12.30 in the noon. They pelted stones and broke the glasses of about ten containers. They fled the spot before the police were alerted.

The agitators have decided to block all garbage containers going towards the depot till the government does take up steps for shifting the garbage depot.

A villager said that PMC authorities and MLA's winded up their meeting quickly because they were not able to bear the stench that was emanating from the garbage depot.

Heading: UP faces a fresh crisis: No anti-gangrene serum - Indian Express
Content:
24 deaths reported in 24 hours, toll now 1102

With the release of water from barrages of Nepal coupled with the continuous downpour, the flood-situation in various districts of the state remained grim.

Twenty-four more deaths were reported from the flood-ravaged areas in the last 24 hours, taking the toll to 1,102.

"The toll could go up considering that reports of deaths often get delayed from far-flung villages," said G K Tandon, State Relief Commissioner.

The continuous rise in the water level of Ghaghra, Saryu, Sharda and Rapti has submerged new areas along the riverbanks. Worse, breaches in various dams of Gonda and Barabanki have wreaked havoc in the area.

The Army has been pressed into service to assist the civil authorities in Gonda, Barabanki, Basti and Lakhimpur-Kheri districts, where over 500 villages have been submerged. The district administration is evacuating people on a war footing from around 200 villages in Gonda.

"Excess water flow from the upper reaches of Ghaghra and Sarda river, entering from Nepal are likely to worsen the situation in Lakhimpur-Kheri, Gonda and Barabanki over the next 48 hours," Tandon said.

The state government has announced a financial package of over Rs 11 crore for the flood victims of the Barabanki district, said an official.

"Housing and Irrigation Minister Nassemuddin Siddiqui, who inspected the flood-hit areas on Wednesday, directed us to provide the financial assistance of Rs 11.39 crore at the earliest," said District Magistrate R Nair.

More trouble is clearly in store, with met officials predicting another round of heavy downpour in large parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh, he said.

For the third consecutive day, the national highway leading to the districts of Gonda and Bahraich from Lucknow has been blocked, owing to the floodwater, which has engulfed over 30 km of the road.

In Faizabad, after 38 years, the surging Saryu has crossed the danger level — flowing at 110 cms above it, in Barabanki at 128 cms and in Basti at 106 cms above the danger level.

Rs 2,000 instant relief to flood victims
Flood victims will now be given immediate relief of upto Rs 2,000 in the form of house building assistance by the Uttar Pradesh government. "In view of the problems faced by flood-affected people, the relief will be distributed through bearer cheques while any amount above Rs 2,000 will be given out through account payee cheques," said Atul Kumar Gupta, Chief Secretary. Chief Minister Mayawati has instructed district magistrates to ensure that the relief reaches the victims within 10 days of the issuance of cheques in all the districts of the state. New cheques will be issued to those victims who did not receive the relief through account payee cheques earlier.

Heading: Sadiq’s net in Mumbai built around Sanjarpur - Indian Express
Content:
Saroj Kumar Rai (40) met with a road accident on September 20. While doctors were able to save his life, they could not save his left leg. Reason: Despite a two-day search across the state, his relatives could not find the 40,000 units of anti-gangrene serum that was required.

An inquiry by The Indian Express revealed that the serum is not available in chemist shops even in bigger cities of Uttar Pradesh. Even hospitals like Chhatrapati Shahuji Medical University, Balrampur Hospital and Baranas Hindu University have not received any supply for a year.
