Heading: Why has no action been taken against Raj: HC to state Govt - Indian Express
Content:
Lawmakers agree on bailout, Bush administration to vote on deal

WASHINGTON: Warned that time was running short to bolster the distressed economy, US congressional Republicans and Democrats reported agreement in principle on Thursday on a $700-billion bailout of the financial industry, and said they would present it to the Bush administration in hopes of a vote within days. Emerging from a two-hour negotiating session, Democrat Senator Chris Dodd, said, "We are very confident that we can act expeditiously." Said Republican Senator Bob Bennett, "I now expect that we will have a plan that can pass the House, pass the Senate (and) be signed by the president." The bipartisan consensus on the general direction of the legislation was reported just hours before president Bush was to host presidential contenders Barack Obama and John McCain and congressional leaders at the White House for discussions on how to clear obstacles to the unpopular rescue plan.

German FM says US could lose financial superpower status

BERLIN: The financial meltdown on Wall Street could reorder the world economy and cost the US its status as the world's financial superpower, Germany's finance minister said on Thursday. Finance minister Peer Steinbrueck told federal lawmakers that the collapse of storied US banks and financial firms such as Lehman Brothers would leave "deep marks" on the world economy. "The US will lose its status as the superpower in the world financial system," Steinbrueck said. "The world financial system will become more multipolar." Steinbrueck made his critique, among the harshest yet from an economic leader abroad, just hours after US president Bush painted a portrait of dire US economic prospects in a television address from Washington on Wednesday night. Steinbrueck told members of Germany's lower house of parliament that the US will cede financial credibility and clout in the wake of the current crisis, opening room for European banks as well as sovereign wealth funds and investment banks in Asia and the Middle East to exert more influence on the world economy

'Celtic Tiger' is first eurozone nation to fall prey to recession

DUBLIN: Ireland on Thursday became the first eurozone member to fall into a recession since the US subprime home loan crisis sparked a global economic slowdown, official data showed. Ireland's economy, rocked by a domestic property market meltdown, entered recession for the first time in 25 years after shrinking in the second quarter of 2008, the Central Statistics Office said in a statement. European neighbours Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Spain sit on the brink of recession amid global economic turmoil. Denmark, which is not in the eurozone, fell into recession — two successive quarters of negative growth — earlier this year. Irish GDP shrank 0.5 per cent in the second quarter of 2008 compared with the previous three-month period when the economy contracted 0.3 per cent, according to the CSO. The "Celtic Tiger" economy has not experienced a recession since 1983.

SEC to investigate movement of over two dozen hedge funds

New York: US regulator Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has ordered more than two dozen hedge funds to hand over trading information, in a bid to crack down on rumour mongering and short-selling, a Wall Street Journal report said. Quoting people familiar with the matter, the Journal said: "the SEC ordered more than two dozen hedge funds to turn over trading information as it ramps up its investigation into whether traders were spreading rumours to manipulate shares." Hedge funds maximise absolute returns using a broad range of strategies including unconventional and liquid investments. In an order dated September 22, SEC said, six financial institutions — American International Group, Goldman Sachs, Lehman Brothers, Morgan Stanley, Washington Mutual and Merrill Lynch — may have been subject to such manipulation, the Journal said.

GE cuts third-quarter forecast, citing financial market woes

HARTFORD: General Electric, whose shares have been battered by anxiety over the health of its big loan and lease business, lowered its earnings forecast on Thursday, saying the unit's profits were falling and that it was taking action to bolster its reserves. GE Capital, the company's financial business that provides consumer and real estate financing, and corporate lending and leasing, has been caught in the downdraft hurting financial stocks in recent weeks. The unit provides nearly half of GE's profit. Shares of the Dow Jones industrial component and industrial bellwether sank $1.04, or 4.2 per cent, to $23.55 in premarket trading. "Given the recent dramatic developments in the financial markets, we have made some tough decisions to further reduce risk and strengthen our balance sheet while maintaining our dividend," said GE chairman and CEO Jeff Immelt. GE said it expects its financial services businesses will earn about $2 billion in the third quarter. In the second quarter, the GE Money and Commercial Finance segments made a combined profit of $2.45 billion.

Buffett makes $783 mn within hours of Goldman buy

London: Warren Buffett's decision to salvage troubled Goldman Sachs by pumping in $5 billion yielded immediate dividends to the legendary Wall Street investor who raked a notional profit of $783 million (over Rs 3,621 crore) within hours of the deal's announcement. According to The Times, within hours of revealing his investment desire in Goldman Sachs on Wednesday, Buffett had made a theoretical profit of $783 million . The Wall Street investment bank astounded its rivals by raising $10 billion in fresh capital — $5 billion from Berkshire Hathaway, Buffett's main listed company, and $5 billion through a public share offering. "Shares in Goldman rose six per cent to $133, giving Berkshire an instant theoretical profit on a side deal, under which it has warrants to buy up to $5 billion of new Goldman shares at $115 a share at any time in the next five years," the newspaper said. The publication quoting analysts noted that Buffett's decision to take the plunge in financial stocks "might come to be seen as the turning point in the financial crisis".

Heading: Kandhamal: Over 100 houses burnt, Centre tells Orissa to be tough - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Thursday pulled up the Maharashtra Government for failing to take action on the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena for its agitation demanding Marathi signboards for all establishments.

If the Government could arrest terrorists, a division bench of Justice J N Patel and Justice K K Tated asked why it could not arrest agitators too. "If you don't have the political will, then give that message to the people that we cannot do anything. Why has no action been taken against respondent number six (Raj Thackeray)?" Justice Patel said. Justice Patel also asked if these people were "untouchable" for the Government.

The court observed that the various affidavits filed by the state did not speak of the action it would take against the party and Raj Thackeray. The court also asked why the Government had not taken any steps regarding two letters sent by the party. Justice Patel cited the example of emails from terrorists and said the provocative letters from the MNS, too, could instigate riot-like situations in the absence of prompt action by the state.

The court also took note of Raj's tirade against Joint Commissioner of Police K L Prasad. "Your Home Minister has failed to back up the police officer," the court said.

The affidavits filed by Prasad, Principal Secretary (Home) Ajit Parasnis and Thane Police Commissioner Anil Dhere state that the party and its president have been effectively restricted from distributing posters, defacing and damaging properties and such violent gestures. They add that preventive action was taken under CrPC against party 2,390 activists before August 20, and against 1,494 between August 28 and September 23.

The court was also informed that opinion has been sought from the Law and Judiciary Department regarding the two letters sent by Raj to shop-owners and police authorities. The court today gave time to the government till October 16 for filing an affidavit regarding what action has been taken.

The MNS last month had set a deadline for shop-owners for putting up Marathi signboards, warning that if they failed to comply, they would be taught a lesson. The Federation of Retail Traders Welfare Associations had moved the court after that. The court then directed that state should ensure that nobody was harmed, and tied down MNS from indulging in violence. These orders remain in force.

Heading: Shoot anyone who waves Pak flag in Valley: Rajnath - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik on Thursday asked for 10 more companies of CRPF from the Centre as over 100 houses and a couple of churches were burnt or damaged in Tikabali, Daringibadi and G Udaygiri areas of Kandhamal district in the last 24 hours.

As senior police officials maintained that the situation was "under control", a terse missive from the Union Home Ministry asked the state Government to ensure that the prevailing situation of lawlessness is effectively brought under control. The National Commission for Minorities (NCM) has also pulled up the BJD-BJP coalition for its inability to handle the situation and called the police ineffective.

About 30 houses and two prayer houses were burnt and damaged at Simanjodi village of Daringibadi block by an unruly mob. In Batingia village of Chakapada block, 50 houses were torched while angry tribals blocked the Raikia town demanding release of their brethren arrested in arson cases. Kandhamal officials imposed Sec 144 in Raikia and curfew as the paramilitary forces marched on the street. Kandhamal SP S Praveen Kumar said night curfew has been continuing in nine sensitive areas in the wake of fresh violence and arson in this region.

In Rakingia village of Raikia block, a team of Orissa Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) that had gone to clear roadblocks was attacked forcing the accompanying police to open fire. Two tribals have reportedly been killed. Sources said tribals with bows and arrows launched an attack on the ODRAF. As many as 26 companies of the CRPF and three companies of the Rapid Action Force have been deployed in the district. In another incident, a mob of about 400 people chased an ex-serviceman into a forest at Damiguda in Tikabali area after he threatened to fire at miscreants who tried to torch his house.

One more person was killed in Raikia block after Dalit Christians of Gundhari village hurled bombs at the tribal-dominated village of Sirsapanga in the afternoon. Sources said the deceased, Raghav Digal, a Dalit Hindu, was a government employee.

In New Delhi, a senior Home Ministry official described the situation in Orissa as "pretty bad", something that required the state government to take "very tough measures". In its communication to the state, the Home Ministry said a "situation of apparent lawlessness" prevailed in certain parts of the state and asked it to "review" the steps that have so far been taken by the law enforcement agencies. "Strict instructions should be issued to all concerned to ensure that the prevailing situation of apparent lawlessness in some areas is brought under control," it said.

Heading: As Tatas shift, Buddha loses hope - Indian Express
Content:
"If someone waves the Pakistani flag in the Valley and says 'Pakistan zindabad' he should be gunned down. Such persons have no right to live in India," BJP president Rajnath Singh said on Thursday as he addressed a mammoth gathering of BJP workers in Bhopal's Jamboori Maidan.

The state's ruling party had mobilised a massive crowd with vehicles being parked hundreds of metres away from the venue. The party claimed it had registered 2.38 lakh workers but the final turnout was much more. In his speech, Rajnath served an aggressive dose of Hindutva, while criticising the UPA Government for being soft on terror.

"It's true that there were terror strikes when the NDA was in power but we shot dead all terrorists," Singh said referring to attacks on Parliament and Akshardham. "If we come to power we will immediately hang Afzal Guru," he said, adding that the Centre should frame a stringent anti-terror law.

Later, the BJP's prime ministerial nominee L K Advani, who arrived from Gujarat, also spoke but took a different line, focusing more on the Lok Sabha elections than the Assembly polls in MP. "The next general elections will be a turning point in India's polity," he said, adding that the general elections in 1977, 1989 and 1998 were the most crucial elections in the country's history. Using the cash-for-vote scandal in Parliament to drive home his point, he added that Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's Government is the most inefficient and corrupt that the country has seen.

Asserting that the greatest leaders that India has witnessed are Shyama Prasad Mukherjee, Deendayal Upadhyay and Atal Bihari Vajpayee, he also stated that his rath yatras of 1990 and 1997 and Murli Manohar Joshi's Ekta Yatra of 1992 have been the most important such events in India.

Heading: 2 yrs back, Bhatkal’s brother was picked up for funding terror - Indian Express
Content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee on Thursday told his Cabinet colleagues that not much hope is left for the rollout of the Nano from the Tata factory in Singur.

At the end of the Cabinet meeting, Bhattacharjee's Cabinet colleagues wanted to know from the Chief Minister if the Tatas were really pulling out from Singur. Buddhadeb who was said to be looking distinctly in "despair", reportedly replied: "The situation in Singur has deteriorated to such a point that there is hardly any hope of the Nano rolling out from there. Hope for Singur is almost lost."

Following the CM's briefing on the grim status of the Singur plant, it was unanimously decided by the Cabinet that a joint appeal will be made to Tata Motors, urging them to stay in Singur. Accordingly an appeal was issued: "The Cabinet appeals to the Tata Motors authority not to withdraw from West Bengal." The statement also assured all help and cooperation to the company. In Singur, a massive rally was taken out on hursday afternoon by the CPI(M) and pro-Tata factory supporters. Villagers carried posters saying: "We want Tata to stay."

According to official sources in the Chief Minister's secretariat, there are two major concerns for Bhattacharjee at the moment. First, the Tatas are holding regular discussions with CMs of other states, evidently to look for alternative sites to shift the Nano plant. Secondly, the new compensation package offered to unwilling farmers, has virtually been rejected by a majority of them. Of a total of 2,251 unwilling farmers, only 69 accepted the new package.

Meanwhile, there were telltale signs of the Tatas shifting gear from Singur. Local residents and police officials confirmed that in the past couple of days a huge quantity of machinery and plant equipment had been moved out. It appears as if this will continue and the scale of trans-shipment would only increase. All indications suggested that Pune Tata Motors factory is going to be the alternative launch pad for Nano.

"They (people of West Bengal) desire and deserve a solution to the issue. They have confidence in those who are dealing with the issue," West Bengal Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi reiterated.

Heading: Car theft trail led to Afzal’s arrest - Indian Express
Content:
Roshan Khan alias Riyaz Bhatkal, the alleged co-founder of the Indian Mujahideen, has been giving the Mumbai Police the slip since the 7/11 and Malegaon serial blasts. The closest that the police managed to get to Bhatkal was when the Crime Branch picked up his brother Iqbal as a suspect in terror financing two years ago.

Following the serial train blasts in the city, the Ghatkopar unit of the Crime Branch had received information that Bhatkal and his brother were providing money for sending newly radicalised local youth to Pakistan for terror training.

"We knew that Riyaz Bhatkal, who owned a leather tanning unit in Kurla at the time, was arranging finances for sending people to training camps in Bahawalpur and Muzzafarabad in Pakistan. We also suspected that his brother Iqbal was also involved. Iqbal, a computer expert, has a construction business in Karnataka's Bhatkal area," said a senior police official on the condition of anonymity.

While the Crime Branch had sent out its sleuths in search of the Bhatkal brothers, their search led them only to Iqbal. "We managed to locate Iqbal, and we questioned him thoroughly. Since we did not get any evidence against him, we let him go. He did not divulge any details concerning the whereabouts of his brother. We searched for Riyaz for several months, and visited different parts of the country. A lot of money was also spent from our secret service fund in paying informers for information about Riyaz, but we never managed to get him," said the officer.

According to the police, after the IM was founded Riyaz Bhatkal was active in Hyderabad, Maharashtra, Delhi and Gujarat. He had visited Pakistan, and is now believed to be in that country.

Heading: Law student arrested for Advani e-mail threat - Indian Express
Content:
Afzal Mutalib Usmani, 32, one of the five held by the Mumbai Police, left a car theft trail from Thane to Uttar Pradesh, leading to his arrest. His name cropped up in the case of theft of a Zen (MH 04 VV 8980) from Kapurbawdi in Thane City. The Mumbai Police Crime Branch is now looking for two other persons who are also involved in the theft.

Investigations revealed that the group was also involved in a couple of other car thefts between July and August, after they stole four CNG cars from Navi Mumbai for the Gujarat attacks. The Mumbai Crime Branch had earlier said that CNG cars were specifically sought to double the impact of the explosion.

Officials said Afzal's arrest would be crucial in understanding the movement of cars and the persons involved in assembling the explosives in the car. The first two cars, a Black Wagon R and a Silver Wagon R, were stolen on the morning of July 9. The cars were driven out of the city limits the same evening, and delivered to Surat on July 10, said the police. The Crime Branch also found that two other cars were stolen on July 15 and driven to Ahmedabad the very next day.

"The cars were then taken to separate locations where they were laden with explosives before Afzal took them to the Ahmedabad civil hospital and the market place. We are also ascertaining the roles of Qayummudin and Atif in this," said Joint Commissioner of Police, Crime, Rakesh Maria.

Afzal was first booked in 1996, in an attempt to murder case, along with alleged SIMI member Abdul Hamid Chaughule. "They attempted to murder a person who wanted to open a video parlour next to a mosque," siad Maria.

Heading: Sadiq brother questioned - Indian Express
Content:
A 30-year-old student of Shillong Law College was on Thursday arrested for sending an email, threatening to kill BJP leader L K Advani during his visit to Shillong on September 29. He has confessed to his crime.

Inspector General S B Singh told mediapersons that investigations were on to ascertain whether Maminul Haque, the accused, had any links with the Indian Mujahideen. He, however, refused to either confirm or deny that the police had identified the cyber café from which the mail was sent. "I cannot divulge the details at this stage as it is very sensitive," he added.

Asserting that they had informed the Union Home Ministry and were working together with the Central investigative agencies to get to the bottom of the matter, Singh said the police were taking the email seriously as the Islamic fundamentalist groups were capable of having a network everywhere. "If the fundamentalist group is known to have global network, Shillong might also be on their radar," he said, refusing to comment on whether the Indian Mujahideen of the SIMI had sleeper cells in Meghalaya.

The police had detained eight suspects in connection with the email. Later, the remaining suspects were let off.

Earlier in the day, Meghalaya Chief Minister Donkupar Roy held a high-level meeting with top officials. "We are taking the threat very seriously and have asked the police to track down the culprit," he said, assuring that all necessary steps would be taken during Advani's visit to Shillong.

Meanwhile, the BJP has said there is no change in Advani's programme. "None of our programmes would be affected by any terrorist threat," party sources said.

However, the party demanded a thorough probe into the incident. It said neither Advani nor any other leader had so far heard anything from the Government on the issue so far.

Heading: No plan yet to roll out Nano from Pantnagar: Uttarakhand - Indian Express
Content:
A day after five suspected Indian Mujahideen (IM) members were arrested by the Mumbai Police Crime Branch, the police on Thursday picked up the brother of alleged co-founder Mohammed Sadiq Israr Shaikh. He was released after questioning. A doctor from Mumbra was also questioned and later released.

"Today, we called Sadiq's brother Tariq for questioning. There were certain doubts which we wanted to get cleared, and once this was done he was allowed to leave. We had also called a doctor from Mumbra for questioning, as circuitry expert Arif Shaikh was staying at his dispensary," said Joint Commissioner of Police, Crime, Rakesh Maria.

"The accused have provided us some information during their interrogation, and teams have been sent to different locations outside the city to verify them. I would not like to disclose these locations as they are operational details. We are sharing information with other states and central agencies," said Maria.

The Crime Branch said it would ultimately hand over all the five accused to the state Anti-Terrorism Squad since they are alleged to be involved in the 7/11 serial blasts case. The group was planning to trigger blasts at "crowded areas" in the city and had surveyed some areas, the police said, without naming specific targets.

The Crime Branch also said Roshan Khan alias Riyaz Bhatkal (not Bhatkar as was reported today), the alleged co-founder of IM who is yet to be arrested, would be the key to cracking the mystery behind who sent the IM e-mails by hacking into unsecured Wi-Fi networks.

"Bhatkal was in charge of the communications aspect as well as arranging the material resources necessary for the group's activities. He is the man who will know whether it is Abdus Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer or someone else who sent the terror e-mails," said Maria.

Heading: In Taj backyard, a police station lies in ruin - Indian Express
Content:
Scotching speculation that the Tatas had made up their mind to manufacture the Nano from Uttarakhand, Chief Secretary, Indu Kumar Pande, said on Thursday that there was no such proposal from the Tatas so far. The announcement follows a much-hyped meeting between the state Government and Tata Motors officials regarding certain pending issues apropos the Pantnagar manufacturing facility of the automobile giant.

"They (officials from Tata Motors) have conveyed to us that no decision on the Nano has been taken. There is no proposal regarding its manufacturing from Uttarakhand as yet," said Pande after the meeting with a two-member delegation of Tata Motors led by general manager A S Puri. Puri did not comment on the prospects of the Nano rolling out from the Pantnagar manufacturing facility.

Pande disclosed that the issues on the agenda pertained to providing 100 acres of land sought by Tata Motors for their residential complex. "We have identified 50 acres of land for the purpose and this will be given to them in due course of time," he said. Another bone of contention was the rent for the 1,000 acres of land already leased out to the Tatas, with the company pushing for the rent to be fixed at Rs 1 per square metre currently fixed at Rs 5 by the state Government. "We are looking into the matter with a positive approach," said Pande.

Pantnagar is one of the possible destinations for Tata Motors for their Nano production facility following the suspension of work at the Singur plant in West Bengal due to protests led by Trinamool Congress. The Tatas are already manufacturing 'Ace' mini trucks at the Pantnagar plant.

Uttarakhand Chief Minister B C Khanduri has been hard-selling Uttarakhand as an ideal destination for setting up of the Nano plant by Tata motors because of what he claims are the manifold benefits of the location, namely, the peaceful general and labour atmosphere in the state, the ample availability of water and power and the clean administration. The state also enjoys excise exemptions and other tax concessions under an industrial package implemented by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government in 2003 slated to be in force till 2010. Khanduri has gone on record to state his intention of extending all possible help to the Tatas should they choose to set up their production facility in the state.

Heading: Bihar looks at Gujarat and TN for houses for flood-hit - Indian Express
Content:
The central courtyard of the 19th-century Taj Ganj police station in Agra has a mazar, a small temple and a Hanuman shrine, yet the place looks like it could do with some divine intervention. The police station monitors law and order in areas around the Taj Mahal and serves a population of nearly six lakh — all from a musty, run-down building that the British built in 1889.

"There is no place to sit or even write our case files. We carry them home," said Sub-Inspector J N Srivastava. Sixteen sub-inspectors and three head constables operate out of four dank rooms with worn-out brick floors. It helps that the constables — 118 of them — stay out on their beats and hang around in teashops and street corners.

A 4 sq ft room is where head mohrar Suresh Chand sits, lost in the middle of towering piles of files and record books. "We will soon get new computers," Chand said, striking a surprisingly positive note in the midst of all that gloom. Another room is reserved for administrative work. Complaints are registered here, but there are no chairs. Half the room has been converted into a maal khana (storeroom for confiscated items), where gas cylinders and illegal liquor bottles lie in a heap. The 16 sub-inspectors share a room called the 'Chowki Division' that has water seeping out of yellowing walls and roof.

The thana has no telephone connection. A hotline with the Taj Mahal chowki has been out of order for months now. "The Station Officer has an official mobile phone. Kuch information dena hota hai tab wahi dete hai," said a head constable. The other policemen use their own cell phones for official work. The police station — and the seven police chowkis under it — has only 22 walkie-talkies.

The thana has five toilets but all them

are choked and have long been abandoned. "We have an arrangement with the neighbouring shops and use their toilets," admitted Suresh Chand.

The police force of 138 has two jeeps and four patrol motorcycles —the others get around on their cycles. "We get Rs 20 per month as cycle allowance," said K L Sharma, a constable. The mess, where a staple of daal-chawal-roti is cooked, is a ramshackle shed with monkeys pounding on the tin roof.

However, Station Officer Raj Kumar Sharma operates from the comforts of a quaint bamboo structure, with a green tarpaulin roof and a carpet to match it. His office is a darbar that holds 25 chairs and is busy with complainants, local politicians and other bigwigs. He didn't seem too worried about the appalling conditions in which his colleagues work. "This is how we work. Sab chalta hai," he said, dragging his words for effect and then smiling to reveal his paan-stained teeth.

Obviously, there is very little that 'works'. On September 25, 2007, a Japanese tourist who was raped in Agra by a guide did not have the courage to register her complaint at the Taj Ganj police station. She came all the way to Delhi and filed her complaint at the IGI police station. An embarrassed UP police then opened a police station for tourists while its Taj Ganj station lies in a mess.

Factfile

Built in: 1889

Area: 1406.50 sq metres

Sub-Inspectors: 16

Head Constables: 3

Constables: 118

Walkie Talkies: 22

Ammunition: One INSAS rifle, .38 bore revolver, 7.62 mm SLR and .303 bore rifle

Heading: Using economics to unload history’s baggage - Indian Express
Content:
With the Bihar Government planning to provide the "best" house models, as offered to victims of 2004 tsunami and 2001 Gujarat earthquake, more than 15 lakh people in the state, who have been rooted out of their moorings due to the Kosi flood, are likely to get new homes over five years. The state Government, which has started distributing 1 quintal of grain and Rs 2,250 to each of the flood-hit families, will start the rehabilitation phase after October 15.

Speaking to The Indian Express, Bihar Deputy Chief Minister Sushil Kumar Modi on Thursday said: "We have closely studied house models that came up after the tsunami on India's eastern coast and the Gujarat earthquake. Our officials have been working on possible models for the flood-hit people here."

He said the Government had estimated Rs 4,500 crore for reconstruction of three lakh houses in its additional demand of Rs 9,000-crore flood package from the Centre. Under the Central Relief Fund, only Rs 25,000 is allocated for the reconstruction of a house.

The Disaster Management Department recently assessed that 3.5 lakh homes would have to be reconstructed.

Lightweight concrete houses with earthquake-resistant technology will be the focus of the scheme. Experts will prepare a model for five affected districts in Bihar taking into account the state's seismic profile," the Deputy Chief Minister said.

Modi said he had been in constant touch with Gujarat and other BJP-ruled states for additional inputs on rehabilitation. Supaul and Madhepura alone would require construction/reconstruction of over two lakh houses.

The house reconstruction phase, however, will take some time as the Government has to wait for the new Kosi course to dry up after plugging the breach.

State Development Commissioner S Vijayraghavan, who visited Bhuj in Gujarat and Cuddalore in Tamil Nadu last week to study house models, said: "Bhuj took seven years and Cuddalore four years for house reconstruction. We are preparing a workable house model for Bihar incorporating the two major rehabilitation models."

The Development Commissioner said the state Cabinet was likely to take up the matter next week.

Disaster Management Department Additional Commissioner Pratyay Amrit said: "We plan to reconstruct houses by giving them a concrete base. As in most cases, thatched and mud houses were washed away, it would mean raising new homes," said Amrit.

Asked how the Government arrived at the number of houses to be reconstructed, Amrit said: "We have data of villages with us besides field assessments by officials at district to panchayat levels." He, however, said as several villages were still under water, the number of houses to be reconstructed might increase.

Following Cuddalore and Bhuj models

• 3.5 lakh houses to be reconstructed, about 2 lakh in Supaul and Madhepura alone

• Rs 1.5 lakh for each earthquake-resistant house

• Cabinet go-ahead to model next week

• Reconstruction to start after October 15

Heading: Breakthrough on Punjab-Panjab and Rajasthan-Sindh trade - Indian Express
Content:
The decision to let goods flow across the border in Jammu and Kashmir from next month, announced in New York by India and Pakistan, has much symbolism attached to it; but it is the promised trade liberalisation across the two Punjabs and between Rajasthan and Sindh that could turn out to be far more consequential for the two nations.

Unlike their plans for carefully regulated intra-Kashmir trade, India and Pakistan have now agreed to open the gates for overland commerce on their international border that has been closed to business for decades.

If they do implement the proposed trade liberalisation, India and Pakistan will be on their way to reconnecting the two Punjabs as well as Sindh, Rajasthan and Gujarat that were once part of a deeply integrated economic space. It should also allow Pakistan's traders to import goods from India for re-export to Afghanistan and Central Asia.

After their warm embrace in New York, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and Pakistan's President Asif Ali Zardari made three major trade-related announcements. One was about commencing "cross-LoC trade on the Srinagar-Muzaffarabad and Poonch-Rawalakot roads on October 21".

India and Pakistan have been negotiating intra-Kashmir trade for more than three years, and two days before the leaders met in New York, officials from two sides had reached an agreement on all the necessary procedures.

The surprise from New York lay in the other two decisions. Asserting that the expansion of commercial cooperation "provides an effective platform to develop and strengthen bilateral relations", the two leaders decided to open the Attari-Wagah road link on the Punjab border and the Khokrapar-Munabao rail route between Rajasthan and Sindh to all permissible items of trade.

As is the norm in Indo-Pak relations, the cryptic announcement hides the extraordinary significance of the decision. Although a limited amount of trade does take place now at the Attari-Wagah border, Pakistan and India had consciously discouraged trade between the two Punjabs all these years.

The two governments restored the old train link between Khokrapar and Munabao only a few years ago. Allowing overland trade on this border will reconnect not just Rajasthan, but also Gujarat with Sindh.

The opening of the trade routes on the international border would not have made much sense if Pakistan had not been open for business with India. Since the peace process was launched in January 2004, two-way trade has begun to expand.

Bilateral trade between India and Pakistan reached US $1.6 billion in 2006-07 from US $835 million in 2004-05. For the first time, imports from India to Pakistan have crossed the $1billion mark and stand today at more than $1.25 billion. Pakistan's exports to India on the other hand have grown slowly from $280 million in 2004-05 to only $370 million in 2006-07.

Despite the unfavourable trade balance, Pakistan's newly elected civilian government took a major political decision last July to expand the list of items that India could export to Pakistan, by adding 136 new product lines. The new list allowed imports of fuel oil, diesel, machinery such as paddy harvesters, rice driers, and mining equipment.

This bold move by Pakistan's civilian government went largely unappreciated in New Delhi that was angry about the bombing of the Indian Embassy in Kabul on July 7. With Singh and Zardari now agreeing to address the issue of cross-border terrorism in general and, more specifically, the Kabul bombing, the latest decision on overland trade acquires a positive dynamic of its own.

(The writer is a Professor at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore and Contributing Editor, The Indian Express.)

Heading: Centre against scrapping of law outlawing homosexuality - Indian Express
Content:
Next month when trucks loaded with apples, handicrafts and other items start rolling on the Srinagar-Muzaffarabad road, it will bring back memories for elderly Kashmiris of the days when the Valley used to see bullock carts carrying goods pass through the same route. It was then called the Jhelum Valley Cart Road.

In 2005, Caravan-e-Aman, the bus between the two neighbouring countries, drove through this road in a bid to reunite divided Kashmiri families. Three years down the line, India and Pakistan have mutually agreed to start duty-free trade across the LoC in Kashmir and the modalities were recently finalised in New Delhi by both the countries. The outcome of this meeting was widely appreciated in Kashmir, even though the details of the modalities agreed upon are yet to be made public. Trade bodies and common people are already waiting anxiously wait for cross-border trade to start.

President of the Kashmir Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI), Dr Mubeen Shah, termed the move an important milestone in the history of Kashmir. "For the Valley's traders, the start of cross-border trade would mean an important alternative for trading their wares like handicrafts, fruit and other items."

However, Shah has some apprehensions too. "If bottlenecks are not removed, then the cross-LoC trade will become more of a confidence-building measure (CBM) between the two countries, rather than an attempt to boost the economy," he said.

To explore trade possibilities, a trade delegation from Pakistan occupied Kashmir (PoK) is likely to meet the authorities in Srinagar and Jammu in mid-October. The visit would be reciprocated by a similar delegation comprising traders from Jammu and Kashmir. "We are expecting to host a trade delegation from PoK in October," said Shah.

Once, the cross-border trade resumes, the fruit industry here will be the biggest beneficiary. At present, Kashmir's fruit industry is worth Rs 2,600-3,000 crore. "Presently, our fruit industry has a national market and if cross-border trade is started, it would add an 'export' dimension to our trade, with the entire Pakistani market at our disposal," said Shah.

Already, the Union Ministry of Commerce has approved a list of 23 items from Kashmir. Pakistan, too, has sent a list of 26 items. The items from the Indian side include fruit (fresh and dry), spices, saffron, carpets, wall hangings, woollens, aromatic and medicinal plants, cricket bats, black mushrooms, green tea, imli, dhania, rajmah. There are several items that are common in the two lists. Islamabad will export onions, garlic, animal hides, wedding dresses, leather and leather products, hand-woven fabrics, fish and fish products.

The trade through the Srinagar-Muzaffarabad road has a historical dimension too. President of Fruit Growers' Association, Ghulam Rasool Bhat, said the road is Kashmir's old link to West Asia. "The trade will revolutionise our fruit industry," Bhat said, adding that fruit growers had been eagerly waiting for opening of the road. "We had even organised a protest," he said. However, he has apprehensions too. "We don't want this road to become like the peace bus that runs twice in a month. We want trucks to ply every day from both sides." Bhat added that only after hundreds of trucks laden with goods passed through this route without any bureaucratic hassles that the real purpose of cross-border trade could be realised.

The handicraft industry hopes that the trade will boost their business. "We will get bigger markets once the cross-LoC trade becomes a reality," said Shah. The Valley's handicraft industry is worth Rs 2,000 crore. Official say handicrafts from here reach Pakistan via Dubai at present.

The J-K Government claims that 95 per cent work for raising pre-fabricated structures providing warehousing, immigration and customs facilities, scanning units and weighing bridges have been completed. On this side of the LoC, the sprucing up of the 12 km-long stretch from Salamabad to Kaman Post is going on at a great pace.

Heading: Sohrabuddin: Johri ‘let down’ probe, Subramaniam tells Supreme Court - Indian Express
Content:
Setting the record straight on the hitherto contradictory views of the Home Ministry and the Health Ministry on legalising homosexuality, the Centre on Thursday confirmed its intention to take a firm stand against scrapping Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code. Widely referred to as the 'anti-sodomy law', the section pertains to Unnatural Offences and criminalises homosexuality.

A day before he is to submit the government's unanimous response on the removal of Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code before the Delhi High Court, Additional Solicitor General (ASG) and lead counsel for both ministries, P P Malhotra, confirmed that the Centre would "obviously" object to the removal of the law. "Obviously, we will take a stand against the scrapping of Section 377 IPC that classifies sex between two men as a criminal offence. We object to their plea," he told The Indian Express after a hearing before a Bench of Chief Justice A P Shah and Justice S Muralidhar on a PIL filed by the NAZ Foundation for modifying Section 377 IPC to exempt "private, consensual, adult love" between persons of the same sex.

The government's position on the fate of Section 377 IPC had been vague after the Health Ministry endorsed the move to exempt adult homosexual love from the provision, even as the Home Ministry firmly supported the law.

When asked whether he would argue against the Health Ministry's stand in court, Malhotra said the Government would take its stand on Friday.

Heading: CJI against simple impeachment procedure - Indian Express
Content:
Adding A fresh twist to the 2005 murders of Sohrabuddin and his wife during a 'fake' encounter in Gujarat, Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Gopal Subramaniam on Thursday alleged before the Supreme Court that Geeta Johri, the Gujarat Police IGP (CID) who is heading the investigation, has "let down" the probe that is being monitored by the SC.

Urging the court to hand over the investigation to the CBI, Subramaniam, who was appointed an amicus curiae (a lawyer assisting the court) in the matter, said: "She is conniving with the state to create false records." As the Bench comprising Justices Tarun Chatterjee and Aftab Alam perused his submissions, the ASG added, "the investigations have been let down by Johri."

Ironically, the SC in May 2007 had refused a CBI inquiry and accepted a plea from Subramaniam and the victims' family to entrust the supervision of the probe to Johri — they had argued that she was deliberately removed by the Gujarat Government to protect senior police officers — D G Banjara (DIG), Raj Kumar Pandiyan (SP) and Dinesh M N, a Rajasthan-cadre IPS officer.

Now, however, Subramaniam claims that there was a systemic collapse in the probe, which needs to be examined. Raising doubts about Johri's approach, he said she sought permission to interview Tulsiram Prajapati, who was accompanying the alleged gangster Sohrabuddin and his wife when they were picked up from a bus before being killed. Although it is believed that Prajapati was killed in another staged encounter in 2006, the ASG said that Johri wrote a letter to her seniors on January 5, 2007 seeking permission to interview him.

However, this argument of the ASG was countered by Gujarat's counsel, Hemantika Wahi and Sourav Kripal, who placed an affidavit saying that Johri had sought permission to interview Sylvester, an acquaintance of Prajapati. She did so, they said, as part of her investigation.

Heading: India bans Chinese dairy products - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Justice of India K G Balakrishnan today said he was not in favour of simplifying the procedure for removal of errant judges.

"Too much simplification of the procedure (for impeachment) is certainly not good," he said during an interaction with mediapersons in the Supreme Court.

The CJI said the process of removal of such judges was purely a political decision. "If an impeachment motion fails, it is not the lack of will to remove the judge, since we all know it has to be done by Parliament, where representatives of political parties take a decision," he added.

Prodded whether recommendation by the CJI, based on the in-house committee report, should be considered as a motion of impeachment, he said, "I am just an individual. A judge should not be thrown out of job like this on a simple procedure. It's a constitutional provision. Too much simplification would not be good."

As regards the case of Justice Soumitra Sen of Calcutta High Court, he said after an in-house inquiry, judicial work was withdrawn from him. Despite being given an opportunity to resign, he did not do so. Then a recommendation for his impeachment was made.

Justice Balakrishnan, however, said appointment of a high court judge had been made more tough, with details being sought like whether any case is pending against him with Bar Council or any criminal case is pending against him. "As for elevation of judges from high courts, details like how many cases the judge has disposed of during his tenure are being sought from the chief justice of the high court concerned," he added. "Most of the times, we don't know the candidate as he may be practising in faraway courts, say Bombay or Calcutta."

While the CJI, being assisted by secretary-general V K Jain, expressed concern at the huge number of vacancies, especially in the subordinate judiciary, he admitted that there had been "some difficulties" in finding good candidates for appointment as judges. Certain mistakes were made in the past, he added, hinting at selection of wrong candidates as judges.

The CJI, however, refrained from voicing his personal opinion on the present system of appointing judges — the collegium system — unlike Union Law Minister H R Bharadwaj who said this system had failed.

Heading: Ajit Singh likely to go with BJP - Indian Express
Content:
The Commerce Ministry on Thursday imposed a ban on the import of Chinese dairy products after these items were found contaminated with melamine that killed children in China recently.

The ban, which comes into immediate effect for three months until further orders, follows the Union Health Ministry's letter to the Customs Department and Commerce Ministry in this regard.

"We had asked the Customs Department and the Commerce Ministry to look into the milk products which are imported from China, as Chinese milk powder, sweets and chocolates containing milk are seen in the market," said a senior official in the Health Ministry.

Earlier this month, nearly 10 per cent milk samples from three top Chinese dairy companies were found to be contaminated with melamine. A nationwide inspection then also found contamination in dairy products — up to 8.4 milligrams of melamine per kilogram — which led to falling ill of about 6,200 infants. Starbucks Corp. immediately pulled milk from around its 300 stores in China as the milk was supplied by Mengniu, a company which was tested positive for supplying contaminated milk.

Other countries then stepped up testing of foods imported from China. The French authorities banned the sale of products containing derivatives of Chinese dairy products. However, import of biscuits, candy or other such foods has been allowed. The South Korean officials made a similar move, banning imports of Chinese-made products containing powdered milk. The Myanmar authorities have also decided to destroy 17.5 tonnes of Chinese powdered milk.

Heading: Services to hold pay report till Lt Cols moved to higher band - Indian Express
Content:
After shuttling between the BSP and the Congress-SP combine, Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) chief and 'Jat' leader Ajit Singh looks set to seal an electoral tie-up with the BJP for the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls.

Though a formal declaration in this regard may take some time, reliable sources said that the RLD boss has talked about finalisation of the alliance with his party leaders. "We have been informed about the tie-up. The RLD will get between 8 to 10 seats," a top party leader told The Indian Express.

RLD leaders said that the decision over the poll-alliance is likely to be taken during the BJP Parliamentary board meet on Friday, though a declaration in this regard may not be made due to the inauspicious 'pitrapaksh' period now. Internally, however, the alliance proposal is facing stiff opposition from senior UP BJP leaders like Kalyan Singh.

Talking about the seat-sharing accord, an RLD leader said that so far, the party is set to bag 8 (6 in Western and 2 in eastern UP) seats in the alliance. Of the 27 seats in western UP, Jats — RLD's backbone — have a substantial presence in 11.

Singh was left in the lurch after Mayawati's BSP decided to contest all the 80 seats in UP. The RLD leader had backed Mayawati and opposed the trust motion over the nuke deal moved by the UPA Government in the hope of an electoral tie-up with the BSP. On being spurned by Mayawati, Singh had wanted to ally with the Congress-SP combine but as the two parties continue to fight over seat-sharing in UP, he drifted towards the saffron brigade.

Fear of losing its Muslim support base due to the pact with the BJP, however, is worrying many RLD leaders. Muslims have a good presence in western UP and the RLD had painstakingly firmed up the winning Jat-Muslim alliance. "Muslims are sure to desert us and in some seats, they can lead to our defeat," remarked an RLD leader.

Sitting party MP Munshi Ram is learnt to be very perturbed as a whopping 35 per cent of the electorate in Nagina (formed after delimitation) Lok Sabha constituency are Muslims. "I am not concerned about my fate. Whether I win or lose, I am with the party and its leader Chaudhary Ajit Singh," Munshi Ram told The Indian Express.

Despite this danger, the party looks set to align with the BJP in the hope of securing the votes of Banias and Gurjars.

Heading: PDP leader shot dead in Valley - Indian Express
Content:
Admiral Sureesh Mehta, Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee, in consultation with the Army and Air Force Chiefs is learnt to have decided to withhold the implementation of the Sixth Pay Commission report in the armed forces until the government agrees to the place Lieutenant Colonels and their equivalents in the higher pay band even as the Defence Ministry has again asked the Finance Ministry to reconsider this key demand. The contentious issue has now become a war of nerves between the Armed Forces and the government with only five days left to implement the pay commission report.

Government sources said that Admiral Mehta has decided not to issue "government draft letter" that is required by the Defence Ministry to implement the new pay scales and arrears on October 1. The three service chiefs apparently took this decision as the existing pay band 3, as per the Pay Commission, is unacceptable to Lt Colonels and their equivalents. Backed by their seniors, the Lt Colonels want the next pay band, which is 4, so that they at least get more salary than their counterparts in the Coast Guard. Even though the Defence Ministry has quietly reminded the services for issuing the draft letter, the service chiefs are under tremendous pressure not to yield to the government till the pay disparities are rectified.

The Defence Ministry has again requested the Finance Ministry to reconsider the armed forces demand of placing the Lt Colonels in pay band 4. But this time they have not referred to the other key demand that Lt Generals be placed in the Higher Administrative Grade plus scale so that their parity with the Director Generals of Police is maintained. Defence Minister A K Antony has already written to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on the Lt Colonel issue after Finance Ministry rejected the South Block request on grounds that it did not want to reopen a Pandora's box by revisiting the Pay Commission report.

Heading: 17 babies die in top J-K hospital in two months, probe ordered - Indian Express
Content:
In the first strike targeting a mainstream political activist in the past three months, unidentified gunmen shot dead a zonal president of the People Democratic Party in north Kashmir's Baramulla district.

The police said 60-year-old PDP leader Ghulam Mohammad Mir of Behrampora, Dangiwacha Baramulla, and a close aide of senior PDP leader and former minister Mohammad Dilawar Mir was shot dead in the main market of the village.

"Mir was shot in his head by a youth carrying a pistol at around 2 pm from a point blank range after the leader had offered zuhar (mid-day prayers) at a nearby mosque," a police officer said. "He died on the spot."

The police and security force launched a massive search operation to nab those behind the killing of Mir, but no arrests were made till last reports came in. The police have registered a case and started investigations. No militant outfit has so far claimed responsibility for the attack.

There was no police protection for the slain PDP leader who was also a prominent figure in the locality. A police spokesman, however, said Mir was offered protection by the local police but the latter refused. "Mir had refused in writing to have any kind of protection for him," the spokesman said.

Mir, police sources said, was also allotted a residential quarter by District Magistrate of Baramulla at Ushkara Colony, which also he did not accept.

The PDP leadership in Srinagar, however, termed the killing of Mir as a deep rooted conspiracy and demanded a judicial probe into the incident.

"There appears to be a design behind the killing," senior PDP leader and member Legislative Council Nizam-ud-Bhat said. "Mir was feeling insecure from past few days and I feel there is a deep conspiracy behind his killing. That is why we demand a judicial probe into the murder to bring the culprits to book."

J&K is all set to go to polls in next few months and the Election Commission of India is finalising the dates for the polls besides the arrangements for the same.

Heading: Six siblings booked for abandoning old mother - Indian Express
Content:
While Kashmir is in the middle of a political crisis, newborn babies are dying in its top tertiary-care hospital, the Sher-e-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences (SKIMS), because of a lack of basic infrastructure. According to an internal report, 17 newborn babies died in the hospital's paediatric surgery department between March 3 and May 1 this year, leading to an internal probe.

These facts first surfaced when Dr Nisar Ahmad Bhat, assistant professor, paediatric surgery department wrote a letter to the hospital's director Dr Abdul Hameed Zargar. "The department has seen 13 deaths over the last month and a half alone. Mortality at this pace is a matter of concern for all of us," the letter said. "Most of these deaths could have been avoided with the availability of basic infrastructure and better support from the concerned specialties."

Bhat also asked the hospital administration to investigate the deaths of each of these babies "so as to avoid such eventualities in future". A copy of this letter was also sent to SKIMS's medical superintendent and the heads of almost all the departments. The paediatric surgery department does not even have basic equipment like ventilators, incubators and infusion pumps. "Whenever we operate upon newborn babies, they need respiratory support but there are no ventilators. This is basic," a doctor in the ward said. "An incubator is essential. In fact, we would need a transport incubator as well. But we are forced to keep these babies under radiant heaters to keep them warm. This is all a mess."

According to the hospital's website, its paediatric surgery department is the only super-specialty of its type in J&K.

According to a preliminary investigation on the recent deaths, it was found that the "incidence of mortality is definitely higher". The probe report revealed that "patients (newborn babies) are not being properly evaluated pre-operatively, re-exploration is being done by senior residents and not by consultants, and most of the surgeries are being done by senior residents and not by consultants".

The report also found that "the consultants do not make rounds of Accident and Emergency and patients get stuck".

Heading: Andhra’s handloom district hit by debt-driven suicides - Indian Express
Content:
Acting upon the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act 2007, Kerala Police have registered a case against six children of a family after they failed to take care of their widowed mother. One of them was arrested by the Kottiyam police in Kollam district.

The police said Lakshmi, 70, was found abandoned in her house with no one to look after her. Learning about her plight, social activists informed the District Collector, who in turn asked the District Probationary Officer to probe the incident. Based on the officer's report, police registered a suo motu case against the children, all grown up and well settled. The arrested son Ramanan, 50, was later released on bail.

In Kerala, abandoned old people has become a social problem. Many expatriates from the state have left their old parents to languish in old age homes, which have come up in large numbers in the state.

Heading: Reunite regional parties for LS polls: Mahanta to Sangma - Indian Express
Content:
P Venkataramudu, 45, had borrowed Rs 2 lakh two years ago to invest in his handloom weaving business. But it proved too much of a burden when the business did not do well. On Monday, unable to face debts and hardships, he hanged himself to the same handloom machine in which he had invested the money. Venkataramudu of Yadiki Mandal was the fourth weaver in Anantapur district to commit suicide in the last fortnight.

After farmer suicides, Andhra Pradesh is faced with suicides by traditional handloom weavers, especially in Anantapur district. Living in abject poverty and burdened with debts, many are ending their lives. The suicides are happening even as Chief Minister Y S Rajasekhara Reddy has said the Government is making all efforts to reach out to the beleaguered handloom sector and help the weavers tide over the crisis. Only last week, Praja Rajyam president Chiranjeevi met weavers in Sircilla in Karimnagar district and sought their support, assuring to bail them out if his party comes to power.

G Chandrayudu, Revenue Officer, Anantapur, says a majority of the handloom owners are neck deep in debt. "The problems they are facing are manifold. It takes a month to produce one saree while powerlooms produce more in the time. Handloom weavers more often than not take raw material and money from middlemen and mediators and are forced to sell the products at the price that they decide. Though the middlemen sell the hand woven sarees and cloth at a very high price in the market they don't pass the benefits to the weavers. Thus, they always remain poor. The conditions of weavers working as daily wagers for handloom owners is even worse, working for as little as Rs 25 per day," says Chandrayudu, who is investigating the suicides. The Anantapur District Collectorate has investigated 41 suicides by weavers in the past five years.

Most of the handloom weavers are also not covered by the cooperative societies, which means they have to depend on middlemen for loans and cannot directly sell their products to traders or the Andhra Pradesh State Handloom Weavers Cooperative Society (APCO).

Director of Handlooms and Textiles Sri Naresh says weavers who are shifting from handloom to powerloom are at the risk of falling into debts and financial hardships leading to suicides. "Most suicide cases are by weavers who were in transition from traditional handloom to powerloom which requires heavy investment. Even powerloom industry is not doing well because now jetlooms have taken over and there is a huge difference in quality and quantity of cloth which brings down the price. Handloom and powerloom weavers are unable to compete in the market. Anantapur has a turnover of nearly Rs 200 crore from both handloom and powerloom, still some weavers fall into debts who are both inside and outside the cooperative fold," says Sri Naresh.

Yarn of trouble

• Traditional handloom weavers are losing out to the powerloom industry which itself is in doldrums because of power cuts

• Handloom weavers are also unable to cope with new designs churned out by powerlooms

• In Anantapur, at least five lakh people are directly or indirectly involved in the handloom industry. The other major hubs of handloom weavers are Dharmavaram, Hindupur, Udavakunda, Rayadurgam and Pochampalli

Heading: Cancer survivor heads for Himalayan expedition - Indian Express
Content:
Former Assam Chief Minister Prafulla Kumar Mahanta while gearing up for his return to the Asom Gana Parishad (AGP), is making an effort to unite all the regional parties in northeast before the Lok Sabha election. He has asked former Lok Sabha Speaker and NCP leader Purno A Sangma to rejuvenate the North-East People's Forum (NEPF).

Mahanta met Sangma in Shillong on Thursday and underlined the need of regional parties in the eight north-eastern states, including Sikkim to fight the Lok Sabha polls under one political platform.

The NEPF, a group of 17 political parties was formed in 2003 to address chronic problems of the region including insurgency and illegal immigration.

Emerging out of the meeting with Sangma at the main secretariat Mahanta said: "I have requested Mr Sangma to hold talks with the leaders of the regional parties."

Mr Sangma made it clear that the forum will not follow any pre-poll alliance with the Congress-led United Progressive Alliance or the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance in the region. He said under the NEPF he will try unite all the regional parties to fight the Congress in elections.

Heading: Old age, tiger attacks take toll on Kaziranga rhinos - Indian Express
Content:
A 26-year-old patient of lung cancer, who was almost written off by doctors in Mumbai, has not only claimed he is cured and fit, but has announced an expedition to the Himalayas. And, if everything goes well, he hopes to go as high as the last advanced base camp located at an altitude of about 20,000 feet.

"One year ago, I thought I was heading for the grave. Doctors in a reputed hospital in Mumbai had written me off, and asked me to spend my time with my close ones since there was apparently no hope left of my survival," said Sanjeeb Baruah, who claimed it was controversial cardiac surgeon Dhani Ram Baruah (of the pig-heart surgery fame of 1996) that had given him a second life.

Sanjeeb Baruah, who runs a small local news and feature syndicate in Sivasagar in Upper Assam, had suffered from lung cancer, and claimed it was Dhani Ram Baruah's genetic engineering treatment that had apparently cured him of his ailment. Sanjeeb Baruah, whose expedition was flagged off from here by former Assam Finance Minister Devananda Konwar, would leave from Kathmandu on October 2 as part of a team of mountaineers under the UK-based Himalayan Expedition.

"I have taken part in several expeditions between 2000 and 2007, which includes Shivling, Gangotri-Gomukh and several peaks in Arunachal Pradesh. It was only a couple of months back that I did a motorcycle expedition to Tawang, crossing the Sela Pass located at about 13,000 feet," the cancer-survivor said.

He, however, admitted he would not dare to target Mt Everest itself. "The point that I want to make is that one should not give up hope even under the worst circumstances. There was a time when even friends and relatives came to see me for the last time. Now they are back to wish me good luck," Sanjeeb said.

Heading: Karnataka cops probe explosives trail in Kerala - Indian Express
Content:
The Kaziranga National Park, the last home of the highly endangered one-horned rhinoceros, is facing a peculiar phenomenon: while a considerably large number of rhinos are dying due to old age, tigers are also contributing their own way by killing at least 20 rhino calves every year.

This year, for instance, as many as 53 rhinos have already died due to old age, while exactly 20 calves have fallen prey to tigers. Over and above these two reasons of Kaziranga losing so many rhinos a year, poachers too have contributed their might, often decamping with its horn after killing a rhino.

"But that does not mean Kaziranga's rhino population is dwindling," pointed out Mohan Chandra Malakar, chief wildlife warden and principal chief conservator of forests (wildlife), Assam. "The number of calves born every year is much more than the death figures, and I am sure the national park as on date has no less than 2,000 rhinos," he said.

There is, however, no study or reliable data to know exactly how many rhino calves are added to the Kaziranga family every year. "But it is a common sight that there is a calf with almost every full-grown female rhino in the Park," said Malakar. While Kaziranga had 1,552 during the 1999 census, the figure rose to 1,855 in the 2006 census, with Malakar saying the figure would not have risen if the casualty rate were higher than the birth rate. Kaziranga, while celebrating its 100 years of rhino conservation in 2005 was touted as the world's greatest conservation story of the century.

"Old age is definitely a major reason for rhino deaths in Kaziranga," said Prashanta Boro, a vet who heads the Wildlife Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre near the national park. While rhinos are believed to have a life expectancy of anywhere between 70 and 80 years, there was a tendency among the younger animals to push out the ageing ones from their nature-defined territory, he added.

"Rhino behaviour will surely make very interesting study. There is an unexplained tendency among the younger adults to push out the ageing members of their species. This also becomes evident from the fact that most of the rhinos that stray away from Kaziranga are generally older, ageing ones," Boro said.

Boro also points at the downsliding physical capability of the ageing rhino that leads it to a slow death. "The rhino's teeth get worn out as it grows older, making chewing a difficult task. This leads to digestive disorders, which in turn flares up the natural parasite growth in its anatomy," Boro said. And then, the natural problem of normal reflexes slowing down makes an ageing rhino more vulnerable to drowning during the high flood season.

But what is more interesting is the number of rhino calves falling prey to tigers. Kaziranga has, in the last four years, lost on average 20 rhino calves to tigers. "Rhino calves have a tendency to move away from their mothers, and the tiger takes full advantage of the situation," points out Dibyadhar Gogoi, divisional forest officer at Kaziranga.

Heading: One more terror module at large, suspect cops - Indian Express
Content:
The probe into the recent terror attacks in the country was extended to Kerala on Thursday with a team of Karnataka Police, which has been tracking the route of explosives used in the blasts, visiting Kozhikode city, which had witnessed several mysterious blasts in recent years.

According to sources, the Karnataka team, headed by ADGP (law and order) A R Infant, inspected the SM Street, where a major fire in April 2007 had claimed seven lives. Besides, the team also inspected the two bus stands, where serial blasts had taken place in March 2006, and Beypore fishing harbour, where a boat was found gutted under suspicious circumstances in September 2005.

The Kerala Police probe into the SM Street tragedy and serial blasts had made little breakthrough. The CBI, which investigated the harbour incident, has approached the High Court to wind up the case for want of evidence. The remains of the gutted boat were destroyed in another blast in January 2007 in a bid to flush out evidence. The first blast occurred minutes before the fishermen were to set out for sea. The incident was seen as a deliberate attempt to foment violence as some of the boat owners were accused in the Marad carnage, in which seven Hindus were killed by Muslim extremists in May 2003.

Police suspect some of the explosive materials had been smuggled into Karnataka from Kozhikode. In January 2006, Kerala Police had seized gelignite sticks from the cloak room at transport bus stand in the city.

Heading: TN puts temples, daily under security cover - Indian Express
Content:
Apart from the module of 14 persons, which was reportedly headed by Atif Ameen, Delhi Police officials suspect that there is one more module of Indian Mujahideen youths operating from the outskirts of Delhi or Uttar Pradesh.

Drawing this conclusion after analysing phone records and interrogating five arrested suspects, officials feel this module could be providing hideouts for Atif's module members who are on the run.

Meanwhile, police said they had recovered clips of Ahmedabad, Jaipur and Delhi blast sites from the mobile phones and laptop recovered after the encounter at L-18 Batla House in Jamia Nagar. However, the five arrested IM members — Zia-ur-Rehman, Saqib Nisar, Mohammad Saif, Zeeshan and Shakil—have not admitted to their involvement in the Hyderabad blasts.

The police also checked their bank accounts, but not much money was found. Officials said while Atif's module had been cracked after the Delhi encounter, the Mumbai Police had busted another module with the five arrests. But the police suspect there is one more module at large.

The Delhi Police are now looking for one Shah Rukh, who hails from Karnataka and reportedly provided explosives for all the serial blasts. He is said to have accompanied Atif to Ahmedabad before the July 26 blasts there.

Meanwhile, a team from Kolkata arrived in Delhi to interrogate the five suspected IM men here in connection with the American Center attack. A Delhi Police team has also gone to Mumbai to interrogate the five suspects detained in Mumbai.

Heading: At Tauqeer’s childhood address, a building full of strangers - Indian Express
Content:
Following an intelligence input that warned of possible terror strikes at prominent places of worship across Tamil Nadu, the state police have beefed up security at many temples and the offices of a vernacular daily that recently felt the heat of communal fury after publishing cartoons of the Prophet.

Kapaleeswarar Temple in Chennai, Meenakshi Temple in Madurai, Ramanathaswamy Temple in Rameswaram, Lord Murugan temple in Palani, and Sri Ranganathar Temple in Srirangam in Tiruchy have been put under a tight security blanket after the warning that they could be possible targets.

Dinamalar, a vernacular daily that invited the ire of Muslims for publishing cartoons on Prophet Mohammed, also figured in the list of possible targets according to intelligence officials. They have advised the newspaper management to take precautionary steps. For additional safety in sensitive areas, armed personnel have been deployed at some branches of the daily.

Meanwhile, speaking to the media after a high-level coordination meeting on Thursday, DGP KP Jain downplayed the security efforts, maintaining that it was a general alert. Pointing out the busting of a module of suspected terrorists who were allegedly hatching a plan to bomb few targets in Chennai, Jain said the state police team was prepared to meet any eventuality.

Though there were no 'sleeper cells' of any proscribed organisations working in the state, the police were keeping tabs on fundamentalists who are associated with communal organisations, he said. Also, in view of the blasts in Delhi, public areas like markets, malls and other shopping areas would also be under close monitoring, added the officials.

Two days ago, the DGP had reviewed security arrangements at the Meenakshi temple in Madurai, and suggested setting up closed circuit cameras. After the recent alert, the state officials have turned their attention to the security arrangements at major temples where anyone can walk in literally unchecked.

Heading: Report has cleared confusion: Modi - Indian Express
Content:
The three-storey building is dilapidated inside, with wooden stairs shrouded in darkness. Once the home of the elusive Abdus Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer—whose precise role in the terror e-mails and the attacks remains to be established—is the unremarkable Chaiwala Building in Israel Mohalla, in one of the bylanes off Mohammed Ali Road.

A neighbour, who had lived in Israel Mohalla since 1972 until he shifted to Mira Road, says Tauqeer used to step out of the house twice daily, once at 7 am to go to Antonio D'Souza School in Byculla and then at 3 pm to visit Khwaja Sunni Masjid in the adjoining lane. "He was a loner since childhood. His brother used to at least join us in our gully cricket games, but Subhan never did," says the man, refusing to divulge his name.

Like him, 40-odd families in Chaiwala building refuse to give their names. "Most of the residents here are recent tenants who moved in a few months back. No one here knows about the Qureshi family," says a woman in her early twenties who stays in a house right next to Room Number 14 where Tauqeer grew up.

Though there are voices from inside, the door of Room 14 remains shut despite repeated knocks. Another resident on the same floor says: "We moved in a couple of months ago. We do not know anything about the Qureshi family. We learnt about them from the papers and news channels recently, but we have no idea about them," she claims.

A local shopkeeper helpfully points out a nearby building where Rehman Qureshi, the paternal uncle of Tauqeer lives. At the third floor residence, the door is partially opened by a woman in her late forties, who says she is Rehman's wife. "He has gone out and will return late at night," she says. Asked about Rehman's connection to the Qureshi family, she says angrily, "I do not know any Qureshi family. We have no idea."

At the Antonio D'Souza School, vice-principal Ashok Joshi can't recollect anything about the boy. "He passed out in 1988 and was part of our school for a good 10 years, but it is difficult to recount any incident," he said. After his schooling, Tauqeer completed his diploma in Industrial Electronics (Polytechnic) from Bharati Vidyapeeth College in Belpada, Kharghar. Vice-principal Prof P N Tandon, who also failed to remember his face, said: "He seems to have been an average student. He is one of the only ones to have left without a certificate."

Heading: Sabarmati fire wasn’t deliberate: Banerjee - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday said while he had been silent on the Godhra train carnage issue for the past six years, the first part of Justice Nanavati Mehta Commission's report, which was tabled in State Assembly on Thursday, had cleared all the confusion which was being spread around the incident.

Addressing a gathering in his Maninagar constituency, Modi said the Congress and others who had spread lies surrounding the incident should now apologise to the people of Gujarat.

Modi came down heavily on the appointment of the Justice U C Banerjee Committee by the Union Railway Ministry and said the committee was appointed only to serve the political interests of the Railway Minister. "However, the electorate of Bihar was not convinced and voted against him," he added.

"The Congress has used the issue to the maximum possible extent for its vote-bank politics, but it did not even have the courage to sit on the floor of the House when the report was being tabled," Modi added.

Heading: Panel should have waited for SIT report, says Sreekumar - Indian Express
Content:
It was not a deliberate fire, and not a petrol-induced one for sure. I don't know what Justice Nanavati has said but after examining a large number of witnesses, my inquiry had concluded that it was an accidental fire which started inside the coach," said Justice U C Banerjee, who had headed a Centre-appointed Committee to inquire into the Sarbarmati Express coach burning incident.

Speaking to The Indian Express over the phone on Thursday, Justice Banerjee, declining to comment on the contents of the Nanavati Commission report, since he had not gone through the report, reiterated that the fire incident in S-6 coach of the Sabarmati Express on February 27, 2002 was not "petrol-oriented". "In a petrol-induced fire, the sequence is generally fire, smoke and smell. In this case, eye-witnesses told me that the sequence was first smell, then smoke and finally fire," Banerjee said.

"An Income Tax officer who was travelling on the train said he climbed down from the upper berth and crawled on the floor as he made his way out. Had petrol been used, the flames would have engulfed the floor of the coach too," he added. "How could that Income Tax officer crawl out of the coach had it been a petrol fire?" he asked, adding that around 250 out of the 300 people travelling on the coach had escaped unhurt.

On the theory that the train was pelted with stones to prevent the passengers from coming out of the coaches, Justice Banerjee said the coaches had been pelted with stones by some vendors at the Godhra station after some of the passengers refused to pay them money for the items they had taken. "It was after the train had left the station and had reached the first signal that the fire started," Banerjee said.

What the banerjee panel said

• The fire in Coach Number S-6 originated in the coach itself without any external input.

• No possibility of an inflammable liquid having been used since there was first a smell of burning, followed by dense smoke and flames thereafter. This sequence is not possible in case the fire is caused by inflammable liquid thrown on the floor of the coach or an inflammable object thrown from outside the coach.

• The 'inflammable liquid theory' also gets negated by the statement of some of the passengers who suffered injuries on the upper portion of the body and not the lower body and who crawled towards the door on elbows and could get out without much injury.

• "On the basis of available evidence, the Committee has found it unbelievable that 'Kar Sevaks' armed with Trishuls, would allow to get themselves burnt without a murmur by miscreant activity like a person entering S-6 coach from outside and setting the coach on fire".

• Based on the forensic laboratory's experiment, it was impossible to set fire to the train from the outside.

• Some evidence of cooking inside the coach by Kar Sevaks was also given before the Committee.

• The Committee found that the train left the platform around 7.48 am and stopped on account of vacuum failure in some coaches only to start again at about 8.00 am. "Relying on the Survey of India Mapping of Distances and given the speed of the train at that time, the Committee noted that the engine ought to take about five minutes to be near the post at 468/19 and the Guards' coach at 468/45. It is at this juncture that the smoke was not only noticed but had been reported to GRP, RPF and Vadodara Control. There was thus no scope for any miscreant activity from any external agency during this period."

Heading: Amar Singh alleges blackmail bid, targets Patil for ‘cold’ response - Indian Express
Content:
"I was forced to call it a conspiracy, but I refused, as there was no evidence," remarked senior IPS officer R B Sreekumar, who was Additional DGP (Intelligence) during the post-Godhra riots of 2002.

Speaking to The Indian Express from Kottayam in Kerala, Sreekumar said: "Calling it a conspiracy is a premature conclusion made by the Commission at this juncture, when the Supreme Court-appointed Special Investigation Team (SIT) is already investigating the case. The Commission should have waited for the SIT to submit its findings."

Sreekumar fell out with the Modi Government in 2002, when as intelligence chief of the state police he reported to then Chief Election Commissioner J M Lyngdoh that the situation in the state was not conducive for conducting free and fair polls.
