Pretexts are not a substitute for action. There are several fundamental changes which have taken place in the nature of terrorism in India and the approach of the Indian society towards terror.

First, those involved in acts of terror are no longer the socially oppressed and victims of injustice where frustration has misled them into crimes of terror. They are educated young men from comparatively affluent backgrounds. The involvement of medical professionals, technology-savvy and educated, is a cause of concern.

Second, we are no longer in the age where terrorism in India is exclusively prompted by cross-border forces. A large number of terrorists are homegrown, indoctrinated by religion into acts of terror.

Third, an attempt by a section of the media — particularly television channels — to find faults with the investigation create a halo of martyrdom about those who commit these crimes against the society. The day the Gujarat police picked up Abu Bashir from Azamgarh, media reports indicated an 'aura of martyrdom'. After the Delhi blasts, Azamgarh became the 'nerve centre of terror'.

Fourth, every terrorist organisation carries with it its own edition of a human rights organisation. Human rights have a valuable place in a Republican constitution. Even in times of terrorism, human rights have their place. But a section of these organisations have become the over-ground face of the under-ground, bringing a bad name to the human rights. Some of these are admittedly funded from outside the country and are donor-driven.

Fifth, a special effort is made to discredit the army, security forces, and local investigations in an attempt to project the terrorists as victims of police misadventures.

Sixth, an aura of victimhood is sought to be built up around the terrorist. If he is either arrested or killed in an encounter, grieving women relatives will vouch for his innocence even though there exists overwhelming evidence to the contrary.

Seventh, arguments are rendered to develop a perceptional equality between the terrorist and persons belonging to other religions and communities. The separatists in Kashmir were equated with the Amarnath Shrine Sangharsh Samiti, an organisation which held the national flag close to its heart and chanted 'Bharat Mata ki Jai' during the protests. Similarly, it is said that if you ban the subversive SIMI, you must also ban RSS and allied organisations. There can be no moral or political equivalence between a subversive and a nationalist.

Eighth, the response of the state has been weak and timid. The government has sought to link the battle against terror not with security considerations but entirely with vote bank considerations. The repeal of POTA, the refusal to give Central assent to state laws, the withholding of the death sentence to the man guilty of attacking Parliament, the encouragement of illegal infiltration from Bangladesh are only illustrative examples.

Ninth, national discomfort is the highest because of an ideological shift in the Congress Party's position. The Muslim League and the Communists traditionally took an extreme position which did not privilege national interest. The Jana Sangh/BJP propounded the cause of aggressive nationalism. Historically, the Congress occupied the centre-stage where it tried to correlate its own brand of secularism with nationalism. In the last two decades, India has witnessed a series of mainstream politicians such as V.P. Singh, Mulayam, Lalu Prasad, and even Arjun Singh who attempted to redefine secularism as a euphemism for majority bashing. Historically, this was never the Congress position. In fact, Indira Gandhi at times overtook the Jana Sangh/BJP in her aggressive nationalism. But the Congress under Sonia Gandhi and Manmohan Singh is primarily concerned with continuity in power and an alliance with those whose political compulsions are decided by vote banks. As such the alliance can comprise of those who are SIMI friendly. The Congress today finds itself in a chakravyuh. If it continues its soft-on-terror 'policy' it loses national support, if it is hard on terror it loses out on the vote bank it has tried to create in the past few years. Either way it is a no-win situation.

Tenth, the only silver lining appears to be that the world today is no longer willing to accept any excuses — 9/11 has altered the global vision on terrorism and any terrorist attempt to internationalise any issue with the support of terror will fail. Faced with these obvious contradictions, the Congress and the government are only contributing to the confusion. Each spokesperson says something different. Rahul Gandhi has now said that POTA is a failed law, but India must have a strong anti-terror law. Will he educate the nation with regards to the changes that he has in mind?

The writer is the BJP general secretary

Heading: Needed: tech pill for Himachal apple - Indian Express
Content:
Allahabad based agriculture scientist Anshuka Srivastava has developed a robot that would help farmers detect Downy Mildew, a parasite that affects grape cultivation.

'Robo Kisan', which got rave reviews at the recently concluded International Conference on Intelligent Mechatronics and Automation in China, will soon get a patent. Srivastava worked on her robot at Ma Lab, FOE, Ibaraki University in Hitachi in Japan, on a Japanese Government scholarship.

According to Srivastava, it would be the first of its kind robot and is designed to inform the farmer after collecting data on the disease from the fields.

"The information collected from the farm is transmitted through radio waves to a super computer where the data is processed to find out whether the grapevine has been infected with the Downy Mildew Disease or not," said Srivastava.

Presently, an Associate Professor with the Farm Machinery & Power Engineering, CAET of the Allahabad Agricultural Institute, Srivastava said she was prompted to take up research because of the disastrous nature of the disease, which affects the quality and productivity of grape in India and other countries.

Grape cultivation is done on a very large scale and requires preventive and remedial spray of fungicides, which pose environment and health hazards besides increasing the cost of production. "Besides, infection spreads very swiftly and if proper care is not taken in time the whole crop is destroyed," she said.

Srivasatav said the current practice is to spray pesticide as soon as crop cultivation starts. "In such circumstances, if there is no disease money is unnecessarily wasted. At the same time urea or for that matter any other pesticide is not good for human consumption especially when grapes are eaten raw. When the disease is detected pesticide is sprayed again. Often, by the time the disease is detected the crop is almost destroyed."

"This automated robot can now detect the disease in its early stages by using artificial intelligence and contribute to a healthy way of grape production," said Anshuka. "The sensor is capable of detecting the disease on its very onset. Pesticides can be used only in the infected region to control the disease and this, in turn, would save the whole vine."

Srivastava's discovery was also discussed at the 88th All-India Technology Entrepreneurship Promotion Program Screening Committee meeting in the Department of Science and Technology at Banaras Hindu University. "Scientists from different countries appreciated the product and urged the Government to take up its commercial production," she said.

The estimated cost of the robot would be around Rs 4,000 and when bulk production starts the cost is expected to be less. Srivastava is now working on a sensor to detect diseases that infects other crops.

Heading: Now, a device with sensors for desired yield - Indian Express
Content:
Despite an annual turnover of more than Rs 2,000 crore, Himachal Pradesh's apple orchards have witnessed a decline in the yield.

According to horticulturists, global warming, increasing attacks of pests and the failure to adapt to new technology by orchard owners have resulted in the low production and poor quality crop.

Incidentally, the industry has seen a growth from a mere 400 hectares during the 1950s to 91,840 hectares with an annual production of over 60,000 metric tonnes over the past five years. However, while the average production of apple is four to five tonnes per hectare in the state, the global average stands at 12 to 15 tonnes per hectare.

The growing challenges that face the industry, however, have prompted scientists from the Dr Y S Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry in Nauni to bail out apple growers by providing them with improved varieties of apples that are suitable for cultivation in mid hill zones—Shimla, Kullu, Mandi, Kinnaur, Chamba and parts of Solan and Sirmour districts—where most of the orchards are located.

"After noticing the problem of poor quality fruits and its production, the scientists have introduced spur type varieties for the mid hills zones and these varieties have started delivering the desired results," said vice chancellor K R Dhiman.

Dhiman said the only way to get out of the present crisis is to grow several varieties of apples and to avoid mono culture. "During the recent survey, scientists have identified diseases in almost all orchards in the region. To get rid of these problems and produce quality product that would fetch good price, we need to replace old orchards and plant new improved varieties," he said.

The scientists were also of the view that apple growers should undergo training in technical advances that are followed in major apple producing countries. "Nutrition is poor and post harvest handling is an area where one needs to be very careful. We are working with them to help them understand how to get rid of pests and maintain quality," said Dhiman.

However, one of the leading growers of Kotgarh area, Hardyal Chauhan, held officials of the extension department of Parmar University and the Department of Horticulture for poor quality production. He said despite repeated requests from growers to provide quality planting materials, these officials always chose to impose their decision on them instead of letting them know about the latest technology.

Heading: It’s high time farm pricing got a booster dose - Indian Express
Content:
Precision farming is set to invade Indian farms.

IIM Calcutta and the Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidalaya (BCKV) have developed a technology to get desired yield through sensors used in farms.

The "agro-sensors" will monitor parameters that influence yield and quality. Researchers and farmers will now have the option to maintain a database from the findings. The data, in turn, would help generate guidelines that would prompt farmers make corrective changes and get the desired yield.

The experiment was first carried out in a 500-squarefeet poly house for growing capsicum at the BCKV campus, about 50 km form Kolkata. The sensors were set up in the farm and were used to monitor moisture content of the soil, temperature of the soil and soil conductivity.

The data collected from the sensors were transmitted to an intermediate station close to the field (or poly farm) with the help of routers. Data collected from the field can be transmitted to the control station over a distance of 500 metres.

Initially, the researchers had used three sensors to study the soil ( soil PH, Soil EC and Soil Moisture), three sensors to prepare reports on the climatic conditions -- ambient temperature, moisture and sunshine - and three routers. The experiment was carried out in three modules -- sensing agricultural parametres, data gathering and transmitting data from the field to the control station.

"The data is uploaded on the net and we have made provisions to keep an online vigil on the farm. By this, decision can be taken on what the crop requires and what it does not and to make the necessary changes accordingly. To develop an effective management information system, we needed data which can be only be obtained after work," said Professor Somprakash Bandopadhyay, project co-ordinator of the programme from IIM-Calcutta.

The type of crop does not matter as different parameters exist for different crops. "We have not yet decided on the type of crop that would be used for a large scale trial. The aim was to develop a low cost technology to reduce input costs," said Professor S K Samanta of Bidhan Chandra Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, the project consultant. "This can be of help for farmers in Bengal where the size of the farm is often small compared to other states."

The field tests have been conducted on a one-acre plot of the agricultural university. "In the area of farming there is not enough information available to farmers. The sensors will help farmers prevent any kind of damages to the crop, based on circumstances in each field" said Bandopadhyay.

"For a few weeks the researchers monitored the situation in the crop from the control station situated about 500 metres from the project area," said Samanta.

The project, with an estimated cost of Rs 34 lakh, was assigned by Media Lab Asia, an agency set up by the Union Ministry of Information Technology and is is expected to be completed by October. Once the project report is handed over to Media Lab Asia, the organisation would implement the project commercially.

Heading: Intercropping is the way for Sugarcane Industry: UP Govt - Indian Express
Content:
With the World Bank giving a call to shift focus on agriculture to tackle food crisis, data gleaned from Punjab's villages only add to its urgency.

The national census for the year 1991 showed Punjab as having 11 lakh farming families. Of these, 45 per cent were small or marginal farmers who owned fields measuring less than five acres. This figure in the next census in 2001 slid to 9.7 lakh and the percentage of small farmers to 30 per cent.

In other words, 30,000 farmers on an average quit agriculture each year. The primary reason for this has been the decline in profitability of crops, particularly paddy and wheat—a phenomenon that agricultural experts are trying to tackle along with suicides by farmers. For example, take the case of Gurdip Singh, a small farmer from village Mehla Kalan. Gurdip, who owns two acres of land, says, "I can just manage to raise food grains for my domestic use from these two acres."

The situation of Avtar Singh, a farmer with 20 acres of land in Alamgir village, is no different. "My inputs costs over the years have skyrocketed while the prices of crops haven't risen. And what we all forget is that farmer too is a consumer. I have to pay the college fees for my two children, which runs into lakhs per annum. Then there are the medical costs of my family."

To drive home his point, Avtar Singh says, "A couple of years ago, one of my kidneys was damaged in an accident. I could not afford treatment. I know there will be a day when all my 20 acres will be lost in medical treatment."

R S Sidhu, head, Department of Economics, Punjab Agricultural University, agrees as he explains, "The data speak so. The best period for agriculture in the recent past was between 1990 and 2000, more precisely till 1995. While the crisis in agriculture began around 1995, it was nationwide then. Now, however, Punjab alone is suffering. Our calculations have shown that while input costs have gone up dramatically, the rise in Minimum Statutory Price (MSP) of crops is very slow and this has resulted in reducing of profit margins for the farmers."

Sidhu adds, "Since 2001-2007 the input costs have risen by 8-9 per cent while the MSP growth has been hovering around 2 per cent. The wheat MSP announced this year (Rs 1,000 per quintal) had brought a relief for farmers and when the picture was easing out the latest news of Rs 850 as MSP for paddy this year is like a bolt from the blue."

Heading: Night and easy: Track gets green light from drivers - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh Government has asked the sugarcane industry to adopt agro-techniques to boost productivity. Twenty representatives of sugar mills and agriculture departments from 11 states attended a training workshop organised by the Directorate of Extension, Ministry of Agriculture, recently to learn techniques that would help them sustain growth.

Since 2001, the Indian sugarcane industry has been dogged with sluggish growth and the productivity of sugarcane has declined. While the average yield, which peaked at 71.2 tonnes per hectare in 1998, has dropped to 64.3 tonnes per hectare, rising production costs and lower returns have resulted in heavy losses for farmers.

Now the state Government has asked sugarcane growers to adopt intercropping—cultivating two or more crops in the same place and at the same time — as an answer to these issues.

Specialty crops such as pulses, legumes, cereals, vegetables, forages and spices can easily be grown with sugarcane. "Potato, mustard, maize and garlic are some of the crops farmers are being advised to grow. They will generate intermittent returns that will supplement sugarcane's annual harvest," said an official.

Potato, according to a study by the Indian Institute of Sugarcane Research (IISR), is the most lucrative, and will help the farmer earn an additional Rs 56,537 per hectare, while mustard could rake in around Rs 6,354 per hectare.

"Sugarcane has traditionally been preferred by farmers as cultivation costs are low but reaps large profits," said Dr D V Yadav, head of the Department of Crop Production at IISR.

For over eight days, participants at the workshop will learn intercropping techniques such as use of biofertilisers, effective nutrient management and soil analysis, among others.

"We will also tell them how to select remunerative intercrops, identify diseases, pests and weeds, water management techniques, as well as participatory rural appraisal and post-harvest processing techniques. The workshop will arm them with the knowhow to become experts, enabling them to return to their home states to disperse information as trainers," the official said.

"Intercropping is necessary. Practical knowledge of how to go about it will be very useful," said S P Rai, Cane Manager of Hasanpur Sugar Mills, Upper Ganges Sugar and Industries Ltd based in Samastipur in Bihar. He said there are around 14,681 farmers in Bihar who would benefit from this data.

According to Yadav, Nagaland has the right weather and could yield quality cane, but commercial cultivation of sugarcane had stopped in the state for well over a decade. "Production is only on a small scale. Farmers have lost interest in sugarcane due to ineffective government policies. We need to obtain the knowhow on how to make sugarcane an economically viable crop," said M Ben Yanthan, sub-divisional agriculture officer from Wokha district in Nagaland.

Experts said intercropping would also help maintain the soil quality as sugarcane has a tendency to deplete natural resources. "Plants like legumes can be grown to enrich nitrogen-content in soil. Sugarcane demands an exhaustive supply of nutrients and water and knowledge of crop residues can help reduce costs," the official added.

Cane is currently cultivated in over 42 lakh hectares countrywide and this year's growth stands at 266.64 million tonnes. Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu are the major sugarcane producers, making up for 67.57 per cent of the market.

Heading: Vasco hope to begin return with a bang - Indian Express
Content:
Singapore's street circuit for this weekend's inaugural nighttime Formula One Grand Prix received the green light from a host of drivers on Thursday.

Championship leader Lewis Hamilton and McLaren team mate Heikki Kovalainen along with Red Bull's David Coulthard and Mark Webber all endorsed the city-state's circuit and said they were eager to get cracking on the 5.067 kilometre track.

"It looks as though they have done a really good job," Australian Webber said.

"I had thought there might be some bumpier sections because there is some reclaimed land but it looks great.

"I think the visibility looks like it is going to be really good... the most exciting thing for me is (racing under) the lights. It is going to look spectacular."

Coulthard agreed. "The track looks well groomed," he said. "I am looking forward to getting out there."

Room to overtake

Finn Kovalainen was also full of praise. "I think it looks great," he said of the steel barrier-lined circuit. "I ran it on Tuesday night when I got in.

"I think it will be an exciting race. It looks like there is room to overtake people. It should be a spectacular evening .... and one which we are not used to."

Briton Hamilton, who leads the standings with 78 points to Ferrari driver Felipe Massa's 77, agreed with Kovalainen's analysis. "There is definitely room to overtake," he nodded.

"We are going to be driving at 200 miles per hour at night with lights flashing in our eyes. That is what I am looking forward to the most."

Heading: i-league call for sleeping giants - Indian Express
Content:
Sporting Clube de Goa will open their 2008 I-League campaign against Vasco at Goa's Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on Friday. Vasco are back in the top flight after going down in the 2004-05 season, and will be hoping to celebrate the re-entry with a bang at the start.

Both teams have undergone a shuffle in the coach's post. Vasco replaced Roberto Fernandes, the man who guided them to the I-League, with Elvis J Goes. Vishwas Gaonkar will take charge of Sporting Clube de Goa in place of Clifford Chukwama.

Meanwhile, another Goan club, Churchill Brothers, have appointed Serbian Zoran Djordjevic as their new coach, having sacked Nigerian Emeka Ezeugo. "Hopefully, the appointment of the new coach will end the earlier problems of coordination," the club's patron Churchill Alemao said. Zoran, who flew in on Thursday to join the team, has vast coaching experience. He started his coaching career in Yugoslavia in 1978 and has plied his trade in the UAE (Al-Rams), Qatar, Kuwait, Yemen, Sudan, Saudi Arabia (Al Hilal) and Iran, according to Alemao.

Heading: Money doesn’t talk: Big names hesitant to take selection job - Indian Express
Content:
East Bengal need to wake up from a slumber. On the heels of a failed Calcutta Football League campaign, where they barely managed to hold on to the third spot but lost their manager, the red-and-golds have their task cut out as they take on Chirag United in the I-League opener at Barasat on Friday.

Chirag probably go in with a psychological advantage, with a win over their more fancied rivals during that CFL campaign, but East Bengal's squad strength is undeniable. With the likes of Sunil Chhetri and Edmilson Marques upfront, Surkumar Singh in defence, Renedy Singh to operate through the flanks and Mehrajuddin Wadoo to do the holding job, it's a line-up to be wary of.

New coach Stanley Rozario, though, has his own trump card, having identified Nigerian Yusif Yakubu as his key man. The two-time NFL top-scorer will be seen performing a new role for his new club — that of a play-maker. Having impressed during practice, Rozario thinks Yakubu can play a pivotal role in the midfield.

"Yakubu has the ability to send incisive passes in the penetrative zone. I am confident he will adapt to his new role," Rozario said.

Yakubu's transfer to East Bengal wasn't free of controversy, with old club Salgaocar raising objections initially. But now the moment of reckoning has arrived for the 35-year-old. East Bengal, however, will miss the experienced Alvito D'Cunha, who is yet to recover fully from his knee injury.

Chirag will look to play the waiting game, hoping to hit their opponents on the break. They don't have big names, but the collective effort of youth, and coach Subrata Bhattacharya's famous match-reading skills are their strengths.

Making their I-League debut, Chirag could fall into the trap of getting overawed by the occasion, especially with thousands of partisan fans cheering the opponents. Bhattacharya, however, feels that his boys can handle the pressure. "I have told them to be patient. There will be butterflies in the stomach, but the idea is not to concede an early goal and then take it from there," he said.

Chirag's big-name signing

There is one name everyone will seek out on the Chirag United team sheet. Sourav Ganguly is giving his old love football a professional go this season, having signed with the Kolkata club. Team director Kaustav Roy confirmed that Ganguly, who is also Chirag's brand ambassador, will be signed on as a player. Though coach Subrata Bhattacharya and assistant Anjan Nath remained non-committal about Ganguly's possible inclusion in the playing XI in the near future, the other players seemed to be excited. "It will be a big morale boost for us," they echoed.

Heading: Australia determined to win, says Watson - Indian Express
Content:
About a month back, when the BCCI working committee decided to pay its selectors Rs 25 lakh per annum, it was seen as an incentive that would attract the big names of Indian cricket to the national panel. Somehow, as the Annual General Meeting approaches, bringing along with it the day to pick a new national selection committee, a majority of names doing the rounds are those of first-class players or those with negligible international experience.

If former Indian skipper Dilip Vengsarkar doesn't get an extension, it is likely that another ex-captain, Krishnamachari Srikkanth, might replace him as the chairman. But when it comes to the other members of the committee, as was the case earlier, the pool has former cricketers who aren't quite household names in Indian cricket. There's no mention of Sunil Gavaskar, Ravi Shastri, Navjot Singh Sidhu or even the likes of Sanjay Manjrekar, Arun Lal or L Sivaramakrishnan. The names doing the rounds in the corridors of the BCCI headquarters, instead, are those of Parthasastri Sharma, Vinod Mathur, Kailash Gattani, Gopal Bose, Raja Venkat, Raghuram Bhatt and Sambran Banerjee.

So why hasn't the yearly package of Rs 25 lakh plus the perks attracted the bigwigs? The answer to the question is simple: it doesn't make financial sense for the stars to turn selectors. Since a place in the selection panel also means an end to their highly lucrative media contracts, not many are keen on confining themselves to the Rs 25 lakh annual pay packet. Vengsarkar brought this issue into focus when the BCCI asked him to stop writing columns for newspapers.

BCCI chief administrative officer Professor Ratnakar Shetty admits that the offer isn't that tempting, but insists that the board had to make a start somewhere. "I know about the media boom and the kind of commitments top players have. The amount of Rs 25 lakh isn't fixed since the issue of the selectors' salary isn't in the constitution. The members came to this figure at the working committee meeting. We can take stock of the situation and maybe take a fresh look at it next year," said Shetty.

But Shetty adds that while the figure might not be big for a top player, for a modest player Rs 25 lakh was a substantial amount. "It is a six-month job for a selector. And I think an amount of Rs 2 lakh per month is good enough. It's also important to remember that, in the past, high-profile names have been selectors even when it was an honorary post," he says.

Different times

But in the present context, things are different. It is learnt that when players like Yashpal Sharma and Srikkanth were short-listed for the job of selectors, they were in a quandary. Yashpal, as a television expert, gets almost double of what he might get as a selector while for Srikkanth, the annual loss might be even bigger. The former India opener, who has turned down offers to become a selector several times in the past, has three brand endorsements besides his media commitments.

But Shetty says that the BCCI wouldn't stop selectors from promoting brands. "That is something personal, we will not stop that. But they can't write columns or be on television as experts," he says.

Heading: Back home, Munaf on song - Indian Express
Content:
Doug Bollinger was out of breath after a session with the medicine ball when Stuart Karpinnen, the physical trainer, threw him a sandbag and ordered three sets of squats. A newcomer in the Australian team, the paceman was going through all the drills with great intensity even as Shane Watson walked past him with a huge grin on his face. "Well done," he quipped.

Watson, after all, knows a thing or two about heavy training — both its benefits and the risks attached with overdoing it.

Now a replacement for Andrew Symonds, he was the obvious first choice all-rounder before frequent breakdowns kept him out of action. "It's a long story," Watson said after Thursday's training session. "How much time have you got?" he asks.

"During my initial years, no matter how hard I trained, I never used to let go until I was completely satisfied that I got the results I'd set out to achieve. That took a toll on my body. I'm a lot smarter now, I don't mind if I skip a few hard exercises," he said. Watson's role in this team will require him to bowl long spells alongside Stuart Clark, and to keep up the pressure even as the impact bowlers — Brett Lee and Mitchell Johnson — bowl in short bursts. "My style of bowling suits Indian conditions and I'm happy to bowl a particular length and bowl wicket to wicket," he said. "I can adapt to any role to play Test cricket."

The unofficial two-day encounter against an RCA XI starting on Saturday is practically a home game for Watson. At the RCA Academy, there's a huge photo of Watson in his Rajasthan Royals attire. His impressive performances through those 45 days helped him fight back into the Australian set-up. The next 45 days will be a different cup of tea, but Watson will be hoping Jaipur again provides a happy spark to his stop-start Test career.

Heading: Royal treatment for Team Australia, BCCI not happy - Indian Express
Content:
In a game of constantly changing fortunes, Rest of India captain Anil Kumble moved from having plenty of problems to problems of plenty. Munaf Patel's (picture right) deadly spell of accurate pace bowling saw Delhi getting dismissed for 177, giving Rest of India a vital 75-run lead, and with Rahul Dravid (34) and S Badrinath (33) still there at stumps with the score reading 90/1, Delhi seemed to have lost their grip on the game. But it's not just the match situation that would have delighted the Rest of India skipper. Even the 'India captain' in Kumble would have had a big smile on his face. Munaf's '9-0-31-4 show' means Kumble's pace options have increased after Ishant Sharma's tidy spell on Wednesday.

Munaf was on the bench all through the three-Test series in Sri Lanka, but his impressive show in the subsequent ODIs and now the Irani Cup tie means it will be tough to keep him out of the playing XI in the Tests. But with neither Zaheer Khan nor Ishant putting a step wrong, Kumble will have a few tough calls to make ahead of the opening Test — both with regard to personnel (whom to play) and combination (four bowlers or five).

Eventually, it might be the state of the pitch at Bangalore that is the deciding factor, but Munaf's four wickets on a docile track showed that he doesn't quite need pace-friendly conditions to fire.

He didn't get the new ball on Thursday, but he was quite charged up when he came in to bowl. Mohammad Kaif's brilliant one-handed diving catch in the slips to dismiss in-form Delhi opener Aakash Chopra was the trigger Munaf needed. This early wicket meant his bowling had more bite but wasn't quite carried away as his off-stump never faltered.

Special performance

From the time Munaf landed at the IPCL Stadium a few days back, there was something about him that showed he was in for a special performance.

After drifting to Mumbai and Maharashtra, Munaf has moved to Baroda for this domestic season. It was a sentimental move since Baroda happens to be the place where, many years back, Munaf walked on to a cricket ground with big dreams and a pair of slippers, after making the trek from his village in Ikhar.

It has been a 'return of the prodigal' kind of reception that Munaf has got here. His every wicket has been appreciated noisily by the local crowd while his smooth run-up ends with a crescendo of claps and cries.

Former Baroda Ranji pacer Mukesh Narula, who has seen the early days of Munaf, is delighted to see the pacer back in familiar territory. "It is good that he is back in Baroda. Such bowlers need to be given full freedom — give them the freedom to express themselves and only then will you get results from them," he said.

Not just Narula, even those in the rival dressing room were singing Munaf's praise. Delhi coach Vijay Dahiya calls Munaf's four-wicket effort outstanding. "The best part was his in-swing and the length at which he bowled," he said.

Besides Munaf, there were other significant bowling performances today. Zaheer Khan, Harbhajan Singh and Kumble took a couple of wickets each as Delhi lost their way after a good stand between Chopra and Virender Sehwag in the morning.

The Delhi bowlers failed to repeat their first innings show as Dravid and Badrinath consolidated after Wasim Jaffer's early loss. But in this game of ever-changing odds, nothing is predictable. The only thing that can be said with certainty today was the fact that Munaf finally seems to be getting his act together. The enigmatic pacer, who has had several fitness and attitude issues in the past, is no longer that frustrating mystery.

Heading: Funds for Games, but few takers - Indian Express
Content:
Rajasthan is traditionally known for its hospitality. But the magnanimous, red-carpet welcome to the Australian cricket team by the Rajasthan Cricket Association (RCA) has prompted officials in the Indian cricket board to raise objections over why Lalit Modi's state board is bending over backwards for the visitors.

Various sections within the Indian board had questioned the legality of this ongoing camp, and the two-day practice match scheduled from Saturday despite the BCCI having formally turned down a direct request from Cricket Australia (CA) for an additional tour game before the Test series.

"We wouldn't get such facilities if India went abroad. We would've got the bare minimum. The RCA is being a little too obliging to the Australian team," Ratnakar Shetty, the board's chief administrative officer said on Thursday.

Australia had initially planned to come to India on September 29, before making arrangements with RCA to land a week in advance. In its sprawling complex here in Jaipur, the RCA has provided seven nets to the Aussies. Three wickets in the main square have been prepared with specific inputs from Greg Chappell — one is a flat, batting wicket, one a slow turner, and one a dry pitch with spots on the wicket. Some experts feel that such detailed facilities could even reduce India's home advantage in the four-Test series starting in Bangalore on October 9.

Incidentally, even the pitch for the practice match will be decided upon by the tourists, rather than the hosts, as is the norm. The RCA has prepared two pitches — one with a fair covering of grass and another a slow wicket conducive for batting.

Modi factor?

Several insiders feel one of the factors behind this red-carpet treatment is Modi's relationship with CA in view of the global Champions League, and raise concerns that the board's business interests may be coming in direct conflict with the cricket team. Modi's RCA already has links with Australia: Rupert Murdoch's son Lachlan is one of the investors in Jaipur's Rajasthan Royals IPL team, former Australian skipper Chappell, now the head coach of the Australian Centre of Excellence and currently assistant coach of the Australian team, is also the coach at Rajasthan's Future Cricket Academy, and former India bio-mechanist Ian Fraser is now working with the Rajasthan Ranji team.

Modi, however, denied that his association was going out of its way to help the Australians. "After the postponement of the Champions Trophy, the Aussies decided to come to India early to acclimatise. The facilities at the RCA's Future Cricket Academy are world-class and we intend to make them even better. In the future, we will have seven different types of pitches for the trainees to practice on. It is also a privilege that the facilities we have created at the academy are being tested by one of the world's best teams. Our youngsters who are looking forward to the domestic season will also learn a lot from their presence," he said in Mumbai on Thursday.

No tit-for-tat

Interestingly, during India's tour to Australia early this year, the Indian team had cried foul over the absence of net bowlers and said that those provided by Cricket Australia were not even of club standard. When asked why India didn't get such facilities when they toured Australia, Modi said: "The Indian team, due to their hectic calendar, have very little time to prepare ahead of a series. Because of their tight schedule, if India were to tour Australia, normally they wouldn't reach there so early."

Bimal Soni, vice-president of the RCA, ]added: "We see this as a great chance to extend our friendship with Cricket Australia that our president (Modi) has developed. It is not like we are preparing them for any war against India. They are our guests and we are happy to extend our facilities to them."

Soni was also the manager of the Indian one-day team that struggled with poor practice facilities on that Australia trip. "I believe in the Gandhian philosophy. Just because Australia didn't give us the basic facilities, does that mean we treat them the same way?"

Heading: From Mumbai to Munich, mallkhamb going places - Indian Express
Content:
Most sporting nations would feel that a two-year period is too less to prepare for any major Games — Great Britain, for example, had started their Beijing preparations after the 1996 Atlanta Games.

In India though, things are different. With less than two years to go for the 2010 Commonwealth Games, the various National Sports Federations (NSFs) are still in go-slow mode. The sports ministry had written to all NSFs, asking them to provide information related to preparations for the New Delhi Games, in June. But only seven NSFs have submitted proposals with all relevant information. As many as nine federations haven't responded.

"We are ready with the funds, but some of the NSFs have to be told and retold to send their requirements. All these proposals have to be put up before the screening committees before they are cleared and funds released," a ministry spokesperson said.

The ministry had asked the federations to send names of probables for coaching camps (juniors and seniors), the number of coaches (both Indian and foreign), funds required for their training programmes and the infrastructure they would need.

"If there is a procedural delay on our part, they create a ruckus and go to the press. But when they are at fault, nobody raises the issue," he pointed out. As for the coaches, particularly foreign, he said, the SAI needs to check on the antecedents of the support staff, which takes time. Apart from boxing, the athletics, bowling, cycling, gymnastics, netball, paralympics, Rugby and swimming federations are yet to respond.

The ones that have complied include archery, badminton, squash, tennis, table tennis, wrestling and weightlifting, while the shooting federation has submitted only a partial list. Another incomplete list has been submitted by the ad-hoc committee of the hockey federation manned by the Indian Olympic Association. "It's in their interest that they come up with a complete list," he said.

The spokesperson also said that the ministry wants the federations to make their websites operational for transparency.

"Everybody should know what is happening and who is training where. Besides, we will also monitor the progress of athletes every three months and that of coaches every six months. We want the NSFs to update their websites on the progress each one of them is making," he said.

Meanwhile, the ministry today cleared proposals worth Rs 94.19 lakh following the approval of the Departmental Committee under the scheme "assistance to NSFs", the beneficiaries being disciplines like archery, bridge, football, canoeing and kayaking, golf, handball, ice-hockey, kabaddi, rowing and tug-of-war.

Archery was sanctioned the highest grant of Rs 32.25 lakh for its junior team (24 archers and four coaches) taking part in the Junior and Cadet World Outdoor Target Championship to be held in Antalaya, Turkey, from October 6-12. The under-16 football team, preparing for the AFC Championship in Tashkent from October 4-18, got a grant of Rs 26. 10 lakh.

How things stand

• Only seven federations have submitted complete proposals for funds — archery,badminton, squash, tennis, table tennis, wrestling and weightlifting.

• Nine federations haven't even responded — boxing, athletics, bowling, cycling, gymnastics, netball, paralympics, Rugby and swimming.

• Two federations have given incomplete lists — shooting and hockey ad-hoc committee.

• The ministry required the NSFs to give a complete list including probables for camps (juniors & seniors), number of coaches (Indian & foreign) and the funds and infrastructure needed.

Heading: 64 archers chosen for Commonwealth Games training - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Bus with 51 civic employees plunges into gorge, 4 die - Indian Express
Content:
The sports ministry on Tuesday selected 64 archers to provide them specialised training for the 2010 Commonwealth Games in New Delhi. The ministry has also chosen 39 of the 64 archers for inclusion in the 'core group' of sportspersons. Three Indians and one foreign coach, Wang Woo Lee of South Korea, have also been identified in consultation with the Archery Association of India (AAI).

The ministry has also asked the AAI to submit the names of support personnel such as sports analysts, doctors, physiotherapists, masseurs and masseuses for approval. The AAI in consultation with the Sports Authority of India (SAI) will also have to prepare the Annual Calendar of Training and Competitions for 305 days of training for the period from August 2008 to March 2009. The AAI has informed the ministry that SAI Eastern Centre in Kolkata, Tata Sports Academy in Jamshedpur and Army Sports Institute in Pune have been identified as centres for training to the core group. For providing infrastructural and equipment support, the ministry has asked the AAI to submit their requirements.

Men

Recurve: Rahul Banerjee, Mangal Singh, Jayanta Talukdar, Hrish Kerai, Priyank, W. Ranjan Singh (Jr.), Tarundeep Rai, Kapil, Adonda Raju, Rajiv Basumatary, Gautam Singh; Compound: Ratan Kumar, Chungda Sherpa, Baban Kumar, Umesh B.K., L. Haridas Singh, Isaiah Sanam, Sumit Mishra, Sanjay Swansi, Deepak Kumar, Palton Hansdah Women

Heading: They were on study tour to Kulu-Manali; rest survive as tree blocks 150-foot fall - Indian Express
Content:
Ankush Garud
"He was more a friend than a younger brother," says Lav Garud, elder brother of Ankush Garud, before breaking down uncontrollably. The crowd at Ankush's house near Mati Ganpati has been picking up throughout the day, since news of his death broke. "He was friendly, always helping family members and friends," said a neighbour. Inside, a devastated Savita Garud, his wife and a homemaker, sat listening to words of sympathy from visitors. Ankush's son Chetan is in standard 11 and works part time in a workshop, while younger son Nachiket is in standard 10.

"We got the news from the television around 2.30 pm on Friday. Later, some PMC officials came and told us about the accident," said Lav. The last time the family spoke to Ankush was when he left for the trip. It was his first visit there and he was very excited, said a neighbour.

Anil Narsappa Koli

On Friday, September 26, 19-year old Lakshmi Koli was a day short of completing six months of her married life. There will be no celebration. What has come instead is the news that Anil Koli, her 24-year old husband, has died in a bus accident in Himachal Pradesh.

While Lakshmi was still trying to grapple with the devastating news, Anil's mother had to be admitted to an ICU to be treated for shock. "Everybody in the family was dependent on him," said Shankar Koram, his uncle. Anil was the only earning member in the six-member household as well as its sole male member.

"He last spoke to us two days ago. The signal was weak in Manali and he was excited about the places they were visiting," said Tulja Koram, his aunt. Anil worked with the store manager at the water works department of the Pune Municipal Corporation.

Heading: Crackdown on sleaze hotel, minor among three rescued - Indian Express
Content:
For four employees of the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC), an annual study tour to Kulu-Manali turned into a date with death on Friday. The bus carrying them from Kulu towards Delhi via Manali plunged into a gorge, injuring 31 of the 51 civic employees on board besides killing the four.

The driver lost control, sending the bus hurtling down the 150-foot-deep gorge. However, midway, it got wedged onto a tree. The bus had been hired locally.

Additional municipal commissioner Macchindranath Devnikar said, "One of our colleagues, who was injured in the accident, said the bus was tossed in the air and spun a number of times before getting wedged in the tree. That was providential as otherwise, it would have led to more deaths."

The spot was at Dobhi village, about 20 km from Kulu. The four killed were Anil Narsappa Koli (23) of Dhankawadi, Ankush Ramchandra Garud (41) of Narayan Peth, Vitthal Dadu Jagtap (52) of Wadgaon Sheri and Narsinh Chintaman Joshi (50) of Bibvewadi.

Koli, Jagtap and Joshi worked in the civic water supply department as labourer, carpenter and assistant electrician respectively, while Garud was a peon in the PMC roads department. One of the injured is in a serious condition and has been admitted to TGI Hospital, Chandigarh. Six others have been admitted to the Chandigarh hospital and the rest to a government-run hospital in Kulu.

Manali district collector M Sudha Devi said, "Four people died on the spot but others managed to get out by breaking the windowpanes." If the tree had not blocked the plunging bus, the consequences could have been more serious, she felt.

She had rushed to the spot with a Red Cross Society team. The Himachal Pradesh government announced financial help to the victims while Governor Prabha Rau is keeping track of the situation, she said.

The victims were part of a team on a study tour of local civic bodies in Jalandhar, Amritsar, Chandigarh and Simla. These training sessions, conducted for municipal employees since 1976, include lessons on labour rights, leadership qualities and communications skills. The present tour began on September 18 and was scheduled to end on September 30.

The PMC announced Rs 5 lakh as compensation to the family of each of the dead. At a grim PMC headquarters, mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale expressed her grief.

A group of PMC officials as also a group of elected members including Anil Bhosale, Vikas Mathkari and Shyam Deshpande left for Kulu.

Heading: Laws too old to tackle terror, says top cop - Indian Express
Content:
Freed from brothels earlier, only to land up in Hotel Pyasa

The police raided Hotel Pyasa in the red light area of Budhwar Peth on Friday afternoon and rescued three girls, including a 16-year-old, who had been locked in the lift room on the fifth floor .

The teenager, from Hyderabad, had earlier been rescued from a brothel in March and then sent to an observation home in Tirupati on July 14. It is not clear how she returned.

On information she provided, the police rescued two more minors from brothels near Shukrawar Peth police chowky across the road. Even these two girls, both of Andhra Pradesh, had been rescued a few months ago from brothels. The police are investigating how they returned to the red light area so soon.

The hotel raid was conducted by a team from Faraskhana police station, led by senior inspector V T Pawar, on a tip-off from Sham Kamble, an activist of Freedom Firm, an NGO.

Pawar told hotel owner Babasaheb Dhere to open the doors for checks. Faced with resistance, the police had to break into some rooms, including the lift room on the fifth floor. They recognised among the three girls the teenager they had rescued earlier; the other two were from Bangalore and Nepal.

"We knew the girls were kept at the hotel and informed the police," said James Varghese of Freedon Firm. "When the raid was on, a hotel employee locked me in a room and escaped. Police let me out," he said.

The police detained a hotel employee, Vijay Walhekar (38), besides manager Pramod Kashinath Gaikwad (42). Saroja Ramesh Nilwani (40) of Budhwar Peth was arrested for forcing the girls into the sex trade.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Suresh Pote said action would be taken against the guilty.

Dhere claimed he had co-operated with the police. When asked why he had not given all keys to the police, Dhere said, "I have contracted Ravidra Dangat to manage the hotel. Dangat was not present, so we could not provide the keys to the police."

The Indian Express had carried a story on September 11 about the failure of the Pune police to combat the menace of trafficking of minors. The trade enjoys the support of influential people.

Heading: Exams after Diwali: Decision upsets many schools, delights Youth Games participants - Indian Express
Content:
Director General of Police A N Roy said the current laws are archaic and pose a barrier in terror investigations. The laws are over 140 years old and conviction can take up to 15 years, he said.

Roy was answering questions on the mass threat perception due to recent terror attacks all over the country. He was speaking on the sidelines of a function with retired policemen.

"The police are handling crimes of the present day with laws that were made 140 years ago. These laws become barriers in the way of investigations needed to tackle the current situation. Conviction in some cases takes 10 to 15 years," said Roy.

The paucity of information is the single largest issue that the police face today, he said. "We have put up a proposal before the state government to make changes in the Intelligence Bureau in such a way that officers join the Intelligence Bureau at the start of their careers and render their services to the same department till their retirement," said Roy.

Addressing the retired policemen, Roy said, "You were lucky to have worked for the police in earlier times; now the job of the force is difficult. The situation is such that their hands and legs are tied and they are asked to swim. The responsibilities are growing but the manpower and the facilities are limited."

Speaking on the Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) threat, Pune police commissioner Satyapal Singh said, "When I took charge in Pune, there were records of only 48 SIMI members. After we conducted a thorough inquiry we found that there were 304 SIMI operatives in the city."

Heading: Air Cargo Club demands better cargo facility at city airport - Indian Express
Content:
The Education Department's decision to conduct term-end exams after the Diwali vacation has not gone down well with the city's schools, with many of them having to cancel their exams scheduled to start on Monday (September 29). A few principals whom The Indian Express met criticised the decision, pointing out that the Education Department had conveyed the decision too late and that it would upset the second term's timetable.

However, the 70 schools that are participating in the Commonwealth Youth Games have welcomed the decision.

The Pune Zilla Parishad Secondary Education Officer had issued a circular on September 20 saying that the term-end exams should be conducted after the Diwali vacation. The decision is applicable to all schools in the city, including government aided, non-aided and private schools.

Said a visibly dismayed SPM English School Principal Medha Pandit, "We had announced the start of the term-end exam from September 29. But at the eleventh hour, we had to cancel it owing to the Secondary Education Department's recent circular which we received only yesterday (Thursday)," she said. "The students, too, are disappointed as they had prepared for the exams and will now have to study again during the vacation," Pandit added.

"We had constantly been in touch with the Education Department, even before the academic year started. It was clear from the very beginning of the academic year that the dates of the Commonwealth Youth Games and term-end exams would clash. Why then did the Education Department wait till September 20 to take a decision?" she asked.

It was way back in March that the Education Department had convened a meeting of principals of all schools in the city with the CYG Organising Committee. "But no decision was taken at that meeting," said Pandit.

Shobha Shimpi of MIT Marathi High School, too, expressed disappointment over the exam postponement order. "If the exams are conducted after the Diwali vacation, teachers won't get enough time to correct the answer sheets. Moreover, immediately after the term-end exam, students will have to prepare for the unit test," she pointed out.

Meanwhile, principals of schools taking part in the Games have welcomed the Education Department order. "It is good that students can experience an international event happening right in the city," said Jayashree Pai, principal of Abhinav English Medium School which is participating in the Games.

Pai opined that there would be no problem completing the remaining portion in the second term. "There are enough working days and we can manage," she claimed.

Ramanbaug High School Principal S B Mundhe, too, welcomed the decision, saying that the Education Department has taken it considering all possible options. Around 600 students of Ramanbaug are participating in the Games as volunteers and as performers in cultural programmes.

Heading: Mind Spark ’08 to begin on October 2 - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Pune-bound airliners are operating 1000 tonnes of domestic cargo per month from the city airport, two of the airline companies - Spice Jet and Indigo - don't even have facility for cargo clearance at the airport. They accept the cargo in the city owing to non-availability of space at the airport.

The members of Air Cargo Club of Pune in a meeting with Pune airport director G Chandramouli revealed this fact on Friday. The members of the club submitted a memorandum of their demands in the meeting.

The club demanded better cargo facilities at the city airport citing the increase in the growth of domestic cargo movement from the city. "There is so much of development taking place in and around the city and the industry will need the cargo facility in a big way to move their goods," said Dhairyasheel Vandekar, president of the Air Cargo Club. Presently, perishable items like vegetables and flowers, medicines, auto parts and engineering goods are transported.

Vandekar also said that there was an urgent need of cold storage facility for perishable cargo and custom clearance at airport for international cargo. "For the customs clearance of international cargo, one has to do the formalities at Dighi, which is very time consuming. As a result, the exporters prefer to send their cargo from Mumbai bringing down the share of the city," he said.

Chandramouli agreed that the facilities were not up to the mark. "We will solve the problem of space as soon as we are ready with the terminal building. The cargo complex is also on cards but it will need land and for that we have to take clearance from the higher authorities at the Air Force," he said.

According to an estimate by NASSCOM, there is an immediate need for four lakh skilled professionals in the field of computer hardware, security and networking in the country. Interestingly, the supply is only ten per cent of the requirement as there are very less number of institutes in the country imparting training in these fields. This statistics was provided by Deepak Kulaskar, zonal head of The Indian Institute of Job Oriented Training (IIJT) at the launch of IIJT's Pune centre on Thursday.

IIJT is working towards imparting training in computer hardware, security and networking. "According to an estimate by NASSCOM, these fields will require 12 lakhs professionals by 2010," e said. Students are running after courses in computer programming, but hardware, securities and networking have more opportunities. Indian hardware sector is expected to touch $62 billion by 2010, he added.

The IIJT has presence across the country and it is the 276th centre of the institute. "We have 17 different modules of short-term courses for which students can apply after class 12. The fees are in the range of Rs 50,000 and job is guaranteed after the completion of the course," said Kulaskar. "We are starting with batches of 10 students from this year," he added.

The IIJT has invested Rs 18 lakhs for the Pune centre and has tie-up with a multinational company Tiger Global, which has 25 per cent stake in the company.

Heading: Steak Stick - Indian Express
Content:
Rejecting the Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL)'s plea that Maharashtra Energy Distribution Agency (MEDA) should waive off the penalty slapped on MSEDCL for not generating enough energy through non-conventional means, the Mumbai High Court ordered MSEDCL on September 15 to pay the stipulated fine of Rs 199.77 crore.

Speaking about it on Friday, Mahesh Zagde, Director General, MEDA said, "MSEDCL had filed a case against MEDA saying that the agency cannot penalise the company as the gestation period of generating energy through non conventional energy resources is very long."

The Renewable Purchase Specification (RSP) policy makes it mandatory for power companies to produce renewable energy equal to five per cent of their total output. Renewable energy refers to electricity produced through alternate sources like solar, biomass and wind resources. According to the RSP policy, Rs 5 has to be forfeited for each unit of shortfall in 2007-08 and has to be deposited into the MEDA account within 15 days.

Accordingly, MEDA has slapped a fine of Rs 199.77 on MSEDCL, Rs 183.63 crore on Reliance Energy, Rs 90.22 crore on Brihanmumbai Electricity Supply and Transport and approximately the same amount on M/s Mula Pravara Electric Cooperative Society Limited for not fulfilling the five per cent target, Zagde said. He added that the target has been raised to six percent from this year. The MSEDCL officials, were not available for comment.

Nagtilak is new MSEDCL chief engineer

S P Nagtilak took charge as the new chief engineer of the Pune division of MSEDCL. R B Gautam who occupied the post has now been transferred to Aurangabad, said an official statement issued here. Nagtilak joined service in 1981 as junior engineer and later held various posts including assistant engineer and chief engineer at HQ in Mumbai.

Mandatory energy audits of 50 industrial units

Considering the fact that 43 per cent electricity consumption in the State is by industries, the MEDA has decided to make it mandatory for 50 industrial units in the state to conduct energy audits, said Mahesh Zagde, Director General, MEDA while speaking to the media on Friday. "We are in the process of issuing notification to these 50 units," he said.

These establishments — termed as 'designated consumers' by MEDA include cement, steel and textile industries, railways and thermal power generation plants — consume more than 30,000 tonnes of oil equivalents in a year. "Designated Energy auditors, with accreditation by Bureau of Energy Efficiency, will be appointed to conduct energy audits and determine how much energy usage can be saved," Zagde said.

The audit will include verification, monitoring and analysis of use of energy including submission of technical report containing recommendations for improving energy efficiency with cost benefit analysis and an action plan to reduce energy consumption. Though the Energy Conservation Act was formed in 2001 to conduct energy audits in all establishments, MEDA has started implementing it only from this year. Phase one of the project will see energy audits of the 50 units.

'Generate energy from non-conventional sources'

"Of the 1,40,000 MW energy that India generates, only 8,000 MW is generated by non-conventional resources," said Mahesh Zagde, Director General, Maharashtra Energy Distribution Agency (MEDA). He was speaking at a national symposium on 'power for sustainable development' organised by All India Shri Shivaji Memorial Society's (AISSMS) College of Engineering and Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Board of Research in Nuclear Sciences (BRNS) and the University of Pune.

He explained the need for generating energy from non-conventional resources. "Instead of focusing on higher power generation, the paradigms of sustainable development should revolve around saving energy," he said. Citing examples of the vast difference in usage of energy by India and other countries, he said, "In India, there are 12 vehicles per 1000 population, while in the UK and USA, there are 500 and 800 vehicles per 1000 population. Also, an Indian uses 0.4 tonnes of oil equivalent, while the usage is 4 tonnes oil equivalent in UK and 7 tonnes oil equivalent in Canada."

Also present for the function were Vivek Ghate, vice president of Reliance Industries and Shahu Chhatrapati Maharaj, President of AISSMS.

Heading: Turning over - Indian Express
Content:
Puneites are spoilt for choice as Barbeque Nation opens its first restaurant in the city

Cooking gets exciting for once as the skewers fasten Tandoori Bagich, Lebanese Mushroom, Chicken Sheek Wook, Murgh Zaffrani, Indonesian Prawn and much more on a sunken pit with red hot charcoal and a table grill in the center of each table.

With a live barbeque on the table and the do it yourself concept Barbeque Nation has opened its fifteenth outlet in thecountry and first in the city at Kalyaninagar.

Prosenjit Roy Chaudhury, CEO, Barbeque Nation Hospitality says, "This is a unique concept that offers the opportunity to our customers to actually grill the food right on the table. The barbeques are 90 percent cooked in the outlet's see through kitchen and then transferred on to the table for the finishing touches on the live charcoal grill by the customer himself. There are choicest of marinades on the table. The choice of barbeque is drawn from Pan Asian, Oriental, Mediterranean and Continental cuisines. A range of spice rubs and hemming sauces let you experiment with your culinary skills."

The menu has five vegetarian and five non-vegetarian varieties of barbeques brought to the grill in limitless quantity. Planned on the lines of European country home the restaurant is designed with exposed brick cladding and worn wood walls. It also has an inbuilt reverse exhaust to do away with the smoke and a seating capacity of 220. In addition to barbeques a buffet and desserts follow the starters. The alcoholic and non alcoholic drinks on the floor complete the carte du jour.

"We plan to open our next outlets in Deccan and Wakad. The city has a culture of eating out and with the inflow of more students and professionals, the cuisine has to be expanded and there need to be newer choices. We are just on time," smiles Chaudhary.

Heading: Meal ticket - Indian Express
Content:
California roll

(Pronounced Ka-ly-for-nee-ya roll)

One of the most famous fusion foods in the world, the California Roll is combination sushi at its best. This sushi roll is made inside out (the sticky rice is on the outside) and has a filling of cucumber, crab and avocado. Imitation crab sticks are also used sometimes in place of crab. The rice is covered with sesame seeds.

A quick history: The California Roll was first created in Los Angeles when Japanese chefs began to flock to the USA in search of fortune. Soon chefs began to experiment with substitute foods—this was when tuna was replaced with avocado. A chef made it an inside-out roll when he realised that Americans did not prefer the nori wrapped rolls. This type of roll is also called Uramaki.

After popularising sushi in America, the California Roll went on to become one of the most popular versions of sushi in the world. In Mumbai, try the roll at Tiffin, The Oberoi, Nariman Point, and Wasabi at Taj Mahal Palace and Tower, Apollo Bunder.

Heading: Personified looks good - Indian Express
Content:
Parshuramians won their opening match in the K P Jadhav Memorial tournament organised by VOBA football club held at the St Vincent's football ground, defeating Range Hills 2-0 on Friday.

Parshuramians started the game positively and were passing the ball around well. In the sixth minute of the game, they had a chance to take the lead when a good cross was floated in from the left wing. However, the chance was missed.

Range Hills had a comparatively slow start to the game and their opening chance came in the 12th minute when their striker had a free shot on goal. This chance was missed as the player hit the ball wide off the target. Parshuramians were then attacking the opposing goal with purpose. A player struck a thunderous volley directly from a corner, only to be denied by the keeper. In the last few minutes of the half , a driving run from the Parshuramians right back nearly resulted in a goal, but there was no one at the end of the cross.

They took the lead in the last minute of the half. The right-winger ran past three defenders crossed the ball in hard and low and it deflected off the defender and into the goal. The half ended 1-0.

Range Hills responded well and fought hard in the second half. They had a good spell of possession, but could not manage to get the ball past the Parshuramian garrison. They took some shots on goal but none troubled the keeper. Parshuramians absorbed all their pressure and made their moves on the counter-attack. They could easily have taken the lead on a couple of occasions but missed both opportunities. The last ten minutes of the game was open as attacks were launched back and forth by both teams. Range Hills had a golden chance to equalise after a good ball was played in from the left wing, but the striker squandered this opportunity.

Parshuramians then had a chance to extend their lead when their striker dribbled past two defenders and blasted the ball at the face of goal, but the keeper pulled off a great save. Range Hills turned on the pressure in the few minutes of the game, rattling the post on one occasion and narrowly missing a free kick on the other.

Their hopes were dashed, however, when in the last minute Mario Fernandes blasted the ball into the net and sealed the game for Parshuramians.

Heading: DSA ‘B’ division league from Oct. 3 - Indian Express
Content:
Calling the Army Boys, Bangalore, an all-star outfit wouldn't be wrong as the players were selected from across army stations of Shillong, Danapur, Lucknow and Bangalore. But behind their title win in the u-17 title of the 49th edition of the Subroto Cup, the players from Shillong had a bigger role to play than anybody else.

Not that they were extraordinary; they simply outnumbered members from all other centres. T Jackichan Singh, Tej Kumar Singh, Rosendro Singh, Lokendra Singh, Bobo Singh, Elvis are all from the Shillong centre. Interestingly, none of them are from Meghalaya -- hailing from various parts of Imphal, they set the final camp at Bangalore and the tournament in Delhi abuzz with their performance.

With communication an issue, the rest of the players in the team had put in extra effort. Biman Nandi, the goalkeeper from the Danapur centre, had to learn a new language. "Usually we speak in Hindi, but to be more communicative I had to learn Nepali. Now I can speak it very well," Nandi said. But it was not a one-way effort. "I also had to learn Hindi. Now, it's good enough for communication," Elvis said. The fact that they emerged victorious after only a month's session together proves that communication, for once, was not an issue.

But since this was their final Subroto Cup appearance, the players from the north-east are aware that their future lies with the army. "The army provides security and that's the reason I'm sticking to it. My parents are farmers and we need security more than money," said Elvis, who scored four goals this year. Meanwhile Bobo Singh, who got an invitation from the Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Bangalore, said, "I got a call, but I declined it because if you get injured playing for a club you might end up losing your place. And to play for a club you have to quit army."

Coach G Venugopal, on his first assignment with the team, agreed. "Officially, they aren't allowed to play for the clubs, but we are looking for a few amendments in the regulations," he said.

Heading: Delhi team for North Zone Inter State Badminton Championship - Indian Express
Content:
Finally, the Delhi Soccer Association (DSA) has got the grounds to start its state league. DSA 'B' division league, which will kick off on October 3 at the Ambedkar Stadium and Air Force Ground, Race Course road, was postponed for nearly three months. Though the inter-club and inter-state transfers were over by June, the DSA couldn't start the state league.

"We were helpless. We had so many tournaments going on that we could not start our league. We had Durand which started in August and then it was followed by Subroto Cup. We couldn't even conduct matches at the Air Force Ground as it was an alternative venue," DSA secreatry N K Bhatia said.

The league will see participation from twenty teams divided into three groups. Two teams from each group will qualify for the Super League to be played on round robin basis and the top two teams will be promoted to the 'A' division.

Shakti FC will take on New Friends and Victory FC meet Columbus FC on the opening day. Though 'B' division will be on, the DSA is yet to decide on the groupings for this year's 'A' division league, which will be decided in the second week of October as the association is still waiting for confirmation from Delhi Police and Raisina Sporting Union clubs. Both these clubs have failed to turn up for past two years. "These two clubs haven't been participating for last two-year. We have send them reminders and if they dont turn up or reply to it then from next year we will make them a non-active club," Bhatia added.
