Heading: Jay Talking - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Fashion Week announces the designers for its maiden edition

It seems Delhi is gearing up for an active fashion season this October. Jostling beside the customary Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week Spring-Summer by the Fashion Design Council of India (FDCI) will be the newly floated Delhi Fashion Week (DFW), backed by Sumeet Nair, former executive director of the FDCI, who set up the Fashion Foundation of India.

As he hosted a packed lunch at Ai, the Japanese restaurant at MGF Metropolitan mall, Saket, Nair, looking dapper in a chic pink shirt, announced the names of the designers at the DFW. "Going by Paris, Milan and New York standards, fashion weeks pack in a lot of events, solo shows and studio shows. Our endeavour promises more options to buyers and benefits designers as well. It wouldn't create any confusion," said Nair, who confirmed the presence of 33 designers and 35 buyers for the Week.

From the look of it, DFW promises some big moments for fledgling designers. There are six debutant designers. Delhi-based designer Rajvi Mohan, known for her exclusive menswear, will be presenting a grunge collection for the first time on the ramp. Mohan, 27, will send down a pack in long, dapper jackets with kurtas in a muted palette. "The collection is inspired by the rag-pack gang of the 1940s and '50s endorsed by personalities such as Frank Sinatra, Dean Martin and Sammy Davis Jr," said Mohan, who has worked for British designer Vivienne Westwood.

There is also Smita Singh Rathore, owner of Celldsgn store at Hauz Khas, who will be launching her label 11.11. The alumna of the prestigious Domus Academy in Milan promises "a real masculine look to womenswear with cheery voluminous skirts and drape jackets".

Greco-Lebanese Alecca Carrano, who has been working out of Delhi for the past two years, too has finally managed to put herself on the Indian fashion map. "I was trying to participate for the last couple of years but couldn't because FDCI only allows designers of Indian nationality. I have a stall this time and will showcase a very feminine collection for mature women," smiles Carrano, who is heading for the Dubai fashion week next. Besides the punk vibes, Vineet Bahl, showcasing for the first time in Delhi, will crank out a cocktail collection aptly called Mojito. Watch out for a heady cocktail.

Heading: The New Poet’s Society - Indian Express
Content:
While his single Ride it climbs up the charts and wins awards in London, singer Jay Sean travels to Delhi to belt out some rhythm 'n' blues

Londoners might not know Kamaljit Singh Jhooti, but mention Jay Sean and everyone with a little bit of rhythm and some blues in the soul will hum Ride it, the hit single that is riding up the charts and winning awards. At his recent Mumbai act, the British-Asian singer, however, nonchalantly threw in a bit of rap in his otherwise melodic pop R&B. Oh, that was just for fun, he laughed. Expect something similar when the 27-year-old performs today at Elevate in Noida, as part of Ray-Ban VH1 Global Music Xpress.

"The set list is a mix of my old songs and new ones. But what I love doing is to add something that people have not seen me do before, like rapping," smiles Jay Sean, who debuted with Rishi Rich and Juggy D in Dance with you in 2003 and went on to belt out hits such as Eyes on you. "Rishi Rich and Juggy D are good friends and it was a wonderful experience, but we all have moved onto our solo projects and are happy for each other's accomplishments," he says.

So when Jay Sean released his latest album, My Own Way, whose track Ride it has won the 2008 UK Asian Music Awards for Best Video and Best Urban Act, he did it under his own label 2Point9/Jayded. "When someone else is putting money on you, it gets frustrating after a point when a lot of what you do is decided by them. So I trusted my instincts and 2Point9/Jayded was born," he says. He is the only artist his label has signed on till now, but he says with relief that he is flooded with demos.

After a brief interaction with Bollywood — his track Dil mera was part of Kya Kool Hai Hum while actor Bipasha Basu appeared for his song Stolen — he is ready for more and is in talks with Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy. "I'm a huge Bollywood fan. I love the way the films offer everything — emotions and comedy and music. I am really look forward to working with the SEL trio," says Jay Sean, who wants to bring here his experience of the West.

But how did Kamaljit Singh Jhooti become Jay Sean? "Well Jay comes from my last name Jhooti and my grandmother used to call me shaan which is where Sean comes from," he laughs. That is a little bit of West in his name as well.

Heading: Brownie Sahib - Indian Express
Content:
A performance poet goes for an entertaining blend of words and pictures

Standing under a lonely spotlight, Arka Mukhopadhyay surveys his audience to find a few heads craning up from Retro Sushi's plush black sofas. The absence of a crowd doesn't faze him; after all, being a poet is a lonely existence. But allowing him to turn that loneliness around is the concept of performance poetry, a trend that is slowly making its presence felt in cities across India.

Mukhopadhyay, 28, goes by the moniker StillDancer and is a Bangalore-based performance poet, actor, director and storyteller. In Delhi this week with his witty yet sensitive verses, Mukhopadhyay attempts to popularise spoken word, a synonym for poetry, and set up collaborations between spoken word and other art forms like video, installation, sound and movement. On Wednesday night, Mukhopadhyay recited the works of Dylan Thomas and American poet Billy Collins, while photographs taken by Bangalore-based photographer Honey Bajaj complemented the verses. "I'd like to convert photography into a performance as well. With poetry and images, it is possible to transport an individual to a different world of fantasy and imagination," says Mukhopadhyay.

The evening began with Mukhopadhyay reciting his own piece called Writing a Poem, followed by two poems by Collins. His verse revolved around urban existence, childhood memories and an urgent need to reach out and be recognised by his audience. Among the ones that brought in the most applause from his scanty audience was The Khan and I, a middle-class teenage girl's lustful fantasy featuring a sudden encounter with Shah Rukh Khan.

His straight-from-the-heart style of delivery is not without purpose. "I want the audience to realise that poetry is something they can enjoy, be entertained by, laugh at, drink in and live. I consider poetry primarily meant for performance, and I want to wrest it from the shackles of academic intellectualisation," says Mukhopadhyay. To further his project, he has formed the SpeechMagic initiative in Bangalore, which deals with various forms of storytelling and brings about a dialogue between different art forms.

For more information, log on to www.logostheatreindia.org

Heading: How VK won the race: after biggies opted out - Indian Express
Content:
After Birdy's from Mumbai nestled in the posh localities of Greater Kailash and Mukherjee Nagar, another bakery has strutted north. Brownie Cottage, which boasts seven outlets in Mumbai, has now set up a tony kiosk at Select Citywalk Mall, Saket. Located in the food court on the second level, it can turn every sinful chocolate fantasy into reality.

The outlet stacks 20 varieties of fusion brownies (priced between Rs 45 and Rs 85 a piece). Popular chocolates like Ferrero Rocher, Twix and Lindt have been skilfully turned into delicious muddy blocks. A block of Ferrero brownie, for instance, will offer a dense chocolate square with a crusty top while the centre is buttoned with a half moon of the chocolate. A Lindt 70%, meanwhile, will fetch a brownie studded with a chocolate square. If these options look hedonistic, sink your teeth into classic brownies, the ultimate gooey brownies (for Rs 35 and Rs 45 a piece), or the ubiquitous walnut and choco-chip brownies. The staff, sporting cowboy hats, also serve a mean brownie shake (Rs 65).

If you aren't in a mood to indulge in a block, go for brownie toffees in colourful wrappers. You can choose from a choco-chip toffee (Rs 12), walnut toffee (Rs 12) and guliyan toffee (Rs 18). The outlet also takes orders for mud cakes (Rs 500 to Rs 1,350 per kilo). However, be warned. Place you orders in advance and don't stroll in too late. The stall cannot refurbish its empty trays as the kitchen is based out of Mumbai and batches of brownies are flown in every afternoon.

Contact: 09820291196

Location: Select Citywalk, Saket

Heading: Week on, Jamia Nagar offers Jumma prayers, mother of suspect abstains - Indian Express
Content:
It was just touch-and-go for senior leader Vijay Kumar Malhotra as the central parliamentary board of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) met on Friday to decide its chief ministerial candidate for Delhi Assembly polls.

According to sources, BJP president Rajnath Singh turned to Venkaiah Naidu first to solicit his view. Naidu said the party had two names to start with: former Delhi chief minister Sushma Swaraj and party general secretary Arun Jaitley. There would have been no hitch had either of them agreed to take up the responsibility, but both declined the offer, sources said.

The only name left for the party then was of the Lok Sabha MP's.

Jaitley said Jagdish Mukhi, as Leader of Opposition in the Assembly, has a claim over the post, and called state BJP president Harsh Vardhan a "nice man".

Malhotra is the party's seniormost leader in the Capital.

Swaraj backed Harsh Vardhan's candidature. She said he had built the state unit and taken up all the battles against the Sheila Dikshit government all these years. She suggested that the party follow the Himachal Pradesh formula: one leader being projected for chief ministership, and another for a major responsibility at the Centre. IN HP, the party has gone for this 'division of labour' between Prem Kumar Dhumal and Shanta Kumar.

But all others who spoke at the meeting, including Murli Manohar Joshi, backed Malhotra's case. Sources said the RSS did not pitch in for anyone in particular and left the choice to the BJP. Surprisingly, the name of general secretary Vijay Goel, who was lobbying hard for the responsibility earlier, did not find mention at the meeting.

Sources said Goel, who had the blessings of general secretary Ram Lal, had opted out of the race in favour of Malhotra in advance after he found the going tough.

His immediate gameplan, sources said, was to block the path of Harsh Vardhan — the calculation being that a younger chief minister like him would cloud Goel's own future prospects, while Malhotra would be a safer bet due to his age.

Heading: Delhi Gym votes: Airman off faster than Army rival - Indian Express
Content:
"Our mother is sick. She is in serious shock and ill ever since our elder brother was arrested by the police," says Shariq Nasir, first year BA student at Jamia Millia Islamia and younger brother of Saqib Nasir, arrested for alleged involvement in the September 13 serial blasts.

Exactly a week since the encounter that killed two alleged militants, Shariq, 18, and brother Shaqir, 15, take turns to look after their mother, too sick to pray on Alvida Jumma, the last and holiest Friday before the month of Ramzan gets over. On Friday, one remained by his mother's bedside at all times as the other brother went out for the Friday prayers.

"Everyone in Jamia has always known me as Saqib's younger brother," Shariq says. "He has always been good in studies; I have been the weak one — he got 62 per cent in BA first year (Economics), 63 per cent in second year, and 59 in third year. He is also an NCC gold medalist and was second topper at the university, something I can never achieve."

Younger brother Shaqir, a class X student in a government school, says, "Someone somewhere has made a mistake about our brother. We will fight his case."

A week on, the police presence is minimum but the tension in Jamia Nagar is still palpable. Many are still seething — against what they call a "fake encounter". "Congress leader Kapil Sibal visited today; that is an acknowledgement that police went wrong somewhere," former MCD councillor Asif Mohammad Khan says.

Meanwhile, even a week later, youths are still apprehensive of leaving their houses in fear of being picked up by the police. "We can't see the uniforms but we know the police is here in civil clothes,'' a young Jamia Nagar resident says.

Heading: With blasts on menu, hotels beef up security, keep cabs at bay - Indian Express
Content:
One could cut the tension with a knife at the Delhi Gymkhana Club on Friday evening as more than 1,600 permanent members of one of the country's most prestigious clubs went to polls to select their next president and 16 general committee members.

The fight for the top post is almost a repeat performance from last year: between candidates from the Army and the Air Force, Lt Gen. Rajender Singh and Air Marshal Padamjit Singh Ahluwalia, respectively.

While counting was stopped briefly around 9.30 pm, after supporters of Air Marshal Ahluwalia alleged there were some "bogus voting", there were indications that Ahluwalia sped off the block faster. But loyalists of Lt Gen Singh were confident of his victory. "He is a more qualified and highly decorated officer," one club member said. "He has a good service record, which makes his credentials more believable."

Sq Ldr Ashok Kumar Ahuja, a member for 20 years, pooh-poohed "rumours" of "tension" between the candidates, which soured the environment at the gymkhana club. "These are baseless," Ahuja said. "It is just a case of a closely fought battle; everyone has the right to stand up for elections."

But many members preferred to distance themselves from the "fracas", saying such incidents are tarnishing the club's image. "The candidates are not focusing on other important issues," one member said (name withheld on request). "They are instead concerned more with which side will take over as president."

The list of members seeking candidature was announced at 4 pm in the annual general meeting; the voting that took place between 6 pm and 8 pm was extended by half-an-hour due traffic congestion outside the club.

It is believed that Air Marshal Ahluwalia's victory president would severely dent the Army's morale as Lt Gen Ahluwalia had withdrawn his candidature for the post of president last year to avoid things from turning "nasty". The results were expected past midnight.

Heading: Is NCR game for 2010? - Indian Express
Content:
Luncheons at city five-stars would now get a touch time-consuming as hotels pad up their security system following the September 13 serial blasts.

"Hotels usually follow a vigilant security policy but going with the current scenario we have increased our security checks," says Aubrey Mullerworth, general manager, The Metropolitan Hotel. The hotel, located close to the Connaught Place blast site, would now let in only taxis registered with it. "Any other taxi without passengers cannot enter the hotel premises," Mullerworth says.

"Even valet parking has trained security personnel to keep a check on any dubious activities."

The hotel, Mullerworth says, has updated its CCTV system and has posted additional guards at the entrance.

The concierge desk at The Metropolitan has also been briefed to encourage tourists to avoid market places and keep their shopping scheduled for afternoons, Mullerworth says.

The concierge at The Claridges, near India Gate, is also advising "tourists to be a little more alert in market areas," says Hemant Jaggi, the hotel's director of securities. "Security measures have definitely been enhanced following the blasts," he says. "We do not allow cars to be parked next to the hotel walls outside. And we have increased patrolling on individual floors and lobby covers are present in plain clothes."

The hotel has also stacked up sand bags to "cover any unattended baggage, in order to minimise effects."

This apart, the hotel has also sealed off its service shaft and delivery vans bringing in vegetables and goods are thoroughly skimmed through.

Le Meridian, fenced with Janpath and Raisina Road, is also closely monitoring its entry and exits. "Checking the boot compartment and undercarriage of cars is a common feature at hotel security posts. We have added more CCTVs and DVRs (digital video recorders) on the outdoor to track all movements outside the hotel," says Col Jayant Krishna, director of securities at the hotel. "We are keeping a record of number plates (of vehicles) and people who are visiting our hotel."

The hotel has also posted six physical barriers, weighing 200 litres each, at entry and exit points. "The barriers are positioned in three different tiers to avoid any vehicle from barging in," Krishna says.

Shangri La's director (security) Balwinder Bhardwaj says special training sessions is going on at the hotel; Taj Mahal Hotel, too, has raised security procedure.

The staff at Intercontinental The Grand, meanwhile, have orders to decline private packages meant for in-house guests. "We cannot accept packages on behalf of in-house guests unless it is opened and scanned through," a hotel official says.

Heading: Malhotra gets green light to lead the saffron fight - Indian Express
Content:
Off the block to get ready for Commonwealth Games, Ghaziabad police send proposals for improving infrastructure, additional manpower

It's exactly 736 days to go for Commonwealth Games 2010, and Ghaziabad is tightening its seat belt to tackle the traffic spillover from the Capital during the 12-day event.

While the district administration has submitted a traffic management proposal to Ghaziabad Development Authority (GDA), the police, too, have sought broadening of roads, among others, in a communiqué sent to the development authority.

"Most people from western Uttar Pradesh (coming to watch the Games) are expected take the route though Ghaziabad. So roads need to be broadened to handle this expected rush of traffic," GDA's executive engineer Ram Tripathi says. The development authority has zeroed in on NH-24, NH-58 and GT Road for expansion.

The projects have already got a go-ahead from GDA, and work on inviting tenders would start "soon", Tripathi said.

Newsline takes a look at proposals submitted by the district police:

Flyovers and bypasses
The proposal by the police cites the need for flyovers at: Vijaynagar crossing (on NH 24), NH 24, Model Town, UP border, Maharajpur, NH-58 Mohannagar, and NH-58 Meerut T-point. Construction of a separate bypass on Outer Ring Road is also proposed.

Service lanes and underpasses
To cut the clutter in residential areas and to avoid affecting traffic movement inside colonies, the police have suggested service lanes on NH-58 (from Meerut to Morta), and on NH-24 bypass (from Lal Quan to UP gate). The traffic police say the number of cuts on these stretches result in heavy logjam. "The cuts on the main roads have to be blocked and underpasses should be made at necessary junctions to avoid traffic congestion at these points," Ghaziabad's Superintendent of Police (SP) Vijay Bhushan says.

Low-floor AC CNG buses
Taking lessons from the Capital, Ghaziabad Traffic Police has proposed starting low-floor, CNG-run buses. SP Bhushan says these chic-looking, environment-friendly buses and regularised taxi service are the need of the hour. After all, "Ghaziabad should not gain a bad reputation for poor transport facilities," he says. The proposal to the GDA also suggests making "CNG-run autorickshaws compulsory in the district".

Prepaid auto, taxi stands
The traffic police have proposed four prepaid taxi and auto booths: at Maharajpur, New Bus Terminal, Old Bus Terminal, and Mohan Nagar. The police department has also sought a taxi stand at Lal Quan.

CCTV control rooms and synchronised traffic lights
The police have proposed CCTV control rooms at Mohannagar, Meerut T-point, Choudhary crossing, court and thana link road. "Many traffic lights do not work in the district," a police official says. "We have also suggested the need for new traffic signals on Dasna crossing, police lines gate number 1, Sales Tax barrier entrance, Rajendra Nagar Sector-5, and Shastri Nagar T-crossing on Hapur Road."

The police say traffic lights on NH-24 and NH-58 should also be synchronised.

Training public transport drivers
Drivers of all public transport vehicles in the district will be trained, keeping in mind the visitors expected during the Games. The traffic department will be involved in the awareness programmes and giving basic training to drivers. The proposal says two traffic police lines needs to be set up — "one for the main city and the other for trans-Hindon areas" — since the traffic police are expected to impound many more vehicles every day to keep the flow in check.

Facilities for traffic cops
To raise levels of patrolling, the traffic police have sought additional vehicles such as trucks, a mobile interceptor, two ambulance vans, one disaster management van, and four traffic mobile vans. A senior officer says the district needs additional traffic police personnel to manage the scene during the Games: "We a have sent a proposal for recruitment of two traffic inspectors, 15 traffic sub-inspectors, 45 head constables, and 266 constables."

Heading: Human rights groups seek ‘independent’ probe - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party announced on Friday that 77-year-old veteran leader Vijay Kumar Malhotra will be its candidate for the chief minister's post, ending months of careful consideration that had also looked into the popular claims of state president Dr Harsh Vardhan and general secretary Vijay Goel.

Senior leader Arun Jaitley said on Friday afternoon: "Malhotra is a senior and acceptable leader. He has the potential to lead the party to the Assembly elections and come out victorious."

Between celebrations, Malhotra — the party's MP from South Delhi — listed what was on his agenda: sadak, bijli, pani, a clean Yamuna, less pollution and welfare of the poor in slums. Another priority for him will be to complete all procedures to hang Afzal Guru, the man convicted for the Parliament attack in December 2001, Malhotra told reporters.

"Terrorism is the main issue," Malhotra said. "If we come to power, we shall also demand statehood for Delhi."

Meanwhile, while Dr Harsh Vardhan was present at the announcement, party leader Vijay Goel chose to stay away. Jaitley said he was in Sonepat to attend a meeting.

It is learnt that the party overrode the candidacy of these two as pipping one for the post would have made enemies of the others' supporters. The BJP could not afford resentment in its ranks, party sources said.

Goel, a former Union minister, was backed by leader Rajnath Singh for the chief minister's chair. He has a name for organising successful rallies, the last being at the Ramlila Grounds earlier this month.

But Dr Harsh Vardhan emerged a strong contender when he led the party to victory in the municipal elections last year. However, Malhotra's seniority silenced all, and more so because both Harsh Vardhan and Leader of Opposition in the Assembly Jagdish Mukhi consider him their political mentors.

Senior leader Rajnath Singh and L K Advani had also considered Arun Jaitley to lead the party but it is understood Jaitley has his eyes on the general elections next year.

After the announcement Harsh Vardhan said Malhotra was the right man to end the "corrupt and inefficient rule of Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit". Other party leaders said while Malhotra has served the BJP for long, he had not been singled out for greater roles. He has not got his due, one said, adding this was the party's acknowledgment of his contribution. There were also those who think Malhotra will be a hit with the Punjabi votebank in the Capital.

V K Malhotra was the member of the first Metropolitan Council of Delhi in 1967 and has also served as the Chief Executive Councillor of Delhi (chief minister protocol) between 1967 and 1972.

Others in race
Harsh Vardhan
President of BJP's Delhi unit since December 2003 and an ENT surgeon by profession, he entered politics in 1993 when Delhi voted for its first Legislative Assembly. He was elected from Krishna Nagar constituency in East Delhi and went on to retain that seat in the 1998 and 2003 elections.

Born in December 1954, Vardhan was a student of Anglo-Sanskrit Victoria Senior Secondary School, Daryaganj, and attended GSVM Medical College, Kanpur, for his MBBS and MS (specialisation in ENT). He returned to Delhi to set up private practice as an ENT surgeon and reportedly pioneered the pulse polio programme in the Capital.

Vijay Goel
A controversial leader within the party, Goel was catapulted into national politics from student politics in Delhi. A former president of Delhi University Students Union, he gained popularity within the party by defeating stronger opponents in three consecutive Lok Sabha elections, winning the Chandni Chowk seat twice, and the Sadar seat once.

Goel served as Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports and was also the Minister of State for Parliamentary Affairs during the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government.

Heading: Congress might gain from Goel’s ire: BJP leader - Indian Express
Content:
A fact-finding team constituted by Janhastakshep and People's Union for Democratic Rights raised several questions regarding the Special Cell encounter, which left two alleged terrorists and an inspector of the Special Cell dead. The seven-member team included Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan and teachers of the Jamia Millia Islamia.

The team claimed the fact-finding exercise was undertaken on September 21 and they have found many "holes" in the police theory. They have demanded an "independent, time-bound and comprehensive probe" into the matter. Dr N K Bhattacharya (from Janhastakshep group) raised the following questions at a media conference:

* How did Atif suddenly become the mastermind of the blasts? Different state police have already blamed HUJI, SIMI and IM for the blasts.
* If police knew the terrorists were holed up in L-18, why did they just not seal the building and ask the terrorists to surrender?
* Why was deceased Inspector M C Sharma not wearing a bullet-proof vest if the team knew they were up against terrorists?
* In case they did not know they were terrorists, how did they come out of the building and claim they were terrorists without even an interrogation?
* How did two terrorists flee, considering the only exit was sealed by armed police personnel? (Initially police had claimed that the alleged terrorists had fled, but later they said that the two did not enter the building noticing police presence)
* How come the "terrorists" gave their correct information in tenant verification form they submitted at the Jamia Nagar Police Station?
* If the documents were forged as claimed by the police, how did the caretaker of the building hand the document to media within two hours of the encounter?
* Why was not a Test Identification Parade of the alleged terrorists done by eyewitnesses?
* Why has an FIR not been lodged in the encounter at Jamia Nagar Police Station, as required by the National Human Rights Commission guidelines?
* According to Holy Family Hospital statement, X-rays of the chest and abdomen of M.C Sharma had not "revealed any foreign bodies." What has happened to the bullets fired on him?

The team has demanded that the continuing arrests and harassment of Jamia Nagar residents must stop immediately. Rajan Bhagat, Delhi Police spokesperson said, "Investigations are still on. Any comment at this point will hamper the investigations. All issues will be addressed at a later stage."

Voices of protest at Jantar Mantar, Friday prayers
The Coordination of Committee of Indian Muslims on Friday carried out a rally at Jantar Mantar. Over 1000 people attended the rally, including students and social activists. At Jantar Mantar, in the peaceful rally which began at about 3 pm, people demanded that the government should take note of the questions raised by several citizens' inquiry teams about the recent Okhla encounter and initiate a judicial probe into the matter. They also demanded no community should be blamed without proper inquiry and evidence. The heavy police in Jamia area have prompted the committee to demand their phasing out. They also demanded the arrested youths, who have evidence of their innocence, should immediately be released. The Shahi Imam of Jama Masjid has condemned the authorities, accusing them of ill-treating the Muslims and "branding every Muslim a terrorist." Addressing a gathering during the 'Alvida Namaz' on Friday at Jama Masjid, the Imam said Muslims are being targeted. "Whenever any Muslim is picked up by police, he is declared the mastermind of the terror attacks," he said.

Heading: Power meter maintenance responsibility of discoms, says panel - Indian Express
Content:
While the Bharatiya Janata Party declared Vijay Kumar Malhotra as the Chief Ministerial candidate for Delhi, a prominent leader, active in the Capital since long, was absent from the party office.

Vijay Goel, the National General Secretary of the party, one of the contenders for the post of the Chief Minister, went missing from the conference though he was present at the party office a little earlier. Explaining Goel's absence, Arun Jaitley, the Party General Secretary, said, "We also have a Haryana state committee meeting and being a member of the committee, Goel is in Sonepat, attending the meeting."

Goel had been positioning himself as a candidate for the post with increased rancour against the Sheila Dikshit government in Delhi. He had organised the 'Unauthorised Colony Mahasangh' last month where senior party leaders L K Advani and Rajnath Singh, including Malhotra, had been present.

A party leader told Newsline on the condition of anonymity, that his absence meant a "big loss to the party" in Delhi, indicating he and his supporters could stay away from campaigning.

Insiders also say the declaration of the candidate has been done "too soon" and it could hurt the party. "We should have adopted the approach similar to that of Uttarakhand, where the party went to polls without a Chief Ministerial candidate," a source said.

However, sources in the party office say the early declaration of the candidate was "a necessary step keeping in mind the popularity of Sheila Dikshit", who has been declared as Congress party's CM candidate.

Speaking about Goel's absence, J P Agarwal, President of the Delhi Pradesh Congress Committee said, "It is clear that not everyone in the BJP is with Vijay Kumar Malhotra; the decision on a candidate should be taken with consultation of the final candidates, and not without consulting them."

Heading: PWD proposal for new foot overbridges approved - Indian Express
Content:
The Electricity Consumers Advocate Committee (ECAC) in its latest meeting has suggested that the "the safety as well as maintenance of meters should be the responsibility of the discoms". The issue was deliberated on when members of ECAC suggested that in cases where the electricity meters were located away from the premises of consumers, as is the case in most DDA houses and grouping housing societies, discoms should step in to take responsibility of the meters. "This ought to take care of allegations of tampering, as well as enhance the safety of consumers. Steps in this direction are already being taken and the committee has requested that a report be tabled regarding the same before its next meeting," a member of the ECAC said.

Set up under the aegis of the Public Grievances Cell, ECAC, chaired by retired High Court Judge R C Chopra, yields considerable influence on electricity regulatory bodies. In the past, the committee has made some radical suggestions to the Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission (DERC), such as ensuring that the recovery of arrears is completed strictly within two years of electricity consumption, as opposed to the model followed by discoms — which is two years after they actually raise the bill.

"We have always truly represented consumers' problems and our recommendations usually result out of a long and grueling process of duly examining each issue," the member said.

ECAC has also told the DERC to issue directions to all discoms for providing a toll-free number for lodging complaints. "We have recommended that the DERC should direct discoms to install voice interactive systems so that consumers can lodge their complaints automatically and are also able to track the status of their complaints," the member added.

Discoms have also drawn the ire of the committee as it has been felt "that the functioning of the special courts in the premises of the discoms was not in consonance with the spirit of justice and fair play". This issue was highlighted a few months ago by the more powerful State Advisory Committee (SAC) as well and Power Minister A K Walia had said that his ministry was keen on resolving the issue. "The general public is under the impression that these special courts are under the influence of discoms. We have recommended that a request be made to the Delhi High Court for moving the special courts to the district court building.

Heading: IGNOU courses now on broadband - Indian Express
Content:
The expenditure finance committee of Delhi government on Friday approved PWD's proposal for constructing 18 new foot overbridges (FOBs) across the Capital at the cost of Rs 72.35 crore.

The government said the FOBs will be constructed within 12 months. They will be constructed at the Mehrauli-Mahipalpur Road, Moti Bagh across the Ring Road, Shaheen Bagh at Road no.13-A, Mansarovar Garden, Nehru Nagar, Maa Anandmayee at Kalkaji DTC Bus Depot, Bala Sahab Gurudwara near DESU Colony, Hauz Rani Park across MB Road, Wazirpur Industrial Area T-point, Moti Nagar T-Point, Shalimar Bagh near Kendriya Vidyalaya, Britannia Chowk, Punjab Kesari, Road no 43 in Shakur Basti, Rani Bagh, Vishwas Nagar across Road no 57, Hasanpur across Road no 57, Sarita Vihar (Road no 13-A) and Prahladpur across MB Road.

Heading: Truth and integrity is the way ahead, students told - Indian Express
Content:
The Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU) today signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the city-based Times Broadband to broadcast the varsity's channel 'Gyan Darshan' on the Internet.

This, experts say, will capture signals for IGNOU's channel and provide study material, using Internet Protocol Television (IPTV). This will also help students access IGNOU's content on mobiles and through broadband. IPTV is a cable TV delivery platform that uses high-speed Internet connection to reach customers. "Even though IPTV will take another 2 to 3 years to get a footing in India to reach over 18 million homes, Times Broadband is already on it and will launch the services by December," said Dr V K Arora, Director, Electronic Media and Production Centre, IGNOU.

"The high point of providing IPTV services would be the easy accessibility for subscribers and the reach," Time Broadband CEO Sujata Dev said.

Experts predict that today's MoU will make more people subscribe to IPTV services.

Heading: No evidence to nail senior IAS officer for sheltering Sushil Sharma - Indian Express
Content:
Besides everything else, Dada Jashan P Vaswani is a storyteller. His stories about his uncle and guru T L Vaswani, the founder of the Sadhu Vaswani Mission, and little anecdotes about his own life kept students hooked at an address at the Vaswani International School for Girls on Friday.

Dadaji, as he is commonly known as, had ambitions too, he said. But inspired by his uncle, he let go of those to serve others.

He recounted another incident from his own experiences. When Sadhu Vaswani was a student, he used to always stand first in his class. Once, as he was going through his answersheets, he realised the teacher had wrongly calculated his marks. Sadhu Vaswani immediately went up to the teacher and told him the truth, even though it meant losing the first place. It was that sort of integrity anf truth that he expected from the students, he said.

From development of village to providing healthcare, the Vaswani Mission is involved in a number of initiatives.

But it is education that is of prime concern to Dadaji. Says Vice Principal Nirmal Bhalla who has been at the school for 21 years, "The institution's duty is to improve education."

Heading: Cops thrashed relative of kidnapped boy to get ‘confession’: family - Indian Express
Content:
With a city court finding no evidence to indict D K Rao, a senior IAS officer accused of giving shelter to former youth Congress leader Sushil Sharma after the gruesome murder of his wife Naina Sahni in 1995, it seems that the matter has finally reached its grave. Notably, Rao was sent up for prosecution in 2003 by the trial court judge while convicting Sharma for shooting dead his wife and burning her body in a tandoor (oven) of a restaurant in the Capital on July 2,1995.

The judge had asked the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate to prosecute Rao, the then resident commissioner of Gujarat Bhawan, for allegedly providing shelter to Sharma after the grisly murder of his wife who he doubted was having an affair with her classmate and fellow Congress worker Matloob Karim.

Metropolitan Magistrate Naveen Arora on Friday acquitted Rao of the charges of screening an offender from punishment after observing that in the light of lack of evidence and the Delhi High Court's contentions, he could not be asked to stand trial.

The matter was disposed of today after observing that the High Court had already recalled the complaint made against Rao on the ground that he had not claimed during his testimony that he knew about the murder on the day Sharma came to him. Terming the offence as rarest of rare, Sharma was sentenced to death by the trial court in 2003, which was confirmed by the Delhi High Court February, 2007.

As Sharma approached the Supreme Court against his conviction, execution of his sentence has been stayed pending the appeal.

Heading: Two women held, extortion gang busted - Indian Express
Content:
When three-year-old Ashish went missing from his home in Rasawali village near Dadri on July 16, little did family members know that the police would beat up one of their family members to seek a confession for the alleged kidnapping.

The Dadri police allegedly beat up 26-year-old Ajay Kumar who is admitted in the Intensive Care Unit of Yashoda Hopsital.

According to Omprakash Singh, the grandfather of the kidnapped boy, the police picked up one of the relatives, Ajay Kumar for allegedly kidnapping Ashish, son of Omkaar Singh.

"The police picked him up on September 24 and released him yesterday. He was bleeding profusely when we admitted him to the ICU of Yashoda Hospital.

The police beat him mercilessly and we have registered a complaint with the R K Chaturvedi, Special Superintendent of Police, Gautam Buddha Nagar.

Doctors at the hospital also confirmed that Kumar has been admitted to the hospital. "He has lost a lot of blood and has several internal injuries," said the doctor on duty.

The family members alleged that Kumar was picked up from home around 10 am and was released around 11 pm.

Taking to Newsline, SSP, R K Chaturvedi said that an inquiry has been ordered into the incident.

"We have set up an inquiry in the incident. We have to confirm certain facts cited by the family. The facts available with the police and those cited by the family are different. I will comment on the incident after the preliminary investigations completed by the investigation officer," he added.

Heading: No relief for Bhasin as HC denies bail - Indian Express
Content:
The Southwest Delhi Police have arrested two women and claimed to have busted a gang of women who extorted money by threatening to implicate men falsely in rape cases. Police officials said that the arrested women have been identified as Sunita (29) and Preeti (27). Police officials said a complainant, Nishant Gaur, a resident of DDA flats in Mansarovar Park, complained to police that three women had extorted money from him by threatening to implicate him in a false rape case.

"Gaur said that he worked in a private company in Safdarjung Enclave. He was walking from Bhikaji Cama Place to Chanakyapuri on Africa Avenue Road, when he stopped his motorcycle to answer his phone.

Three women came to the spot. One woman sat behind his motorcycle, another stood in front and the third took its keys and demanded money, threatening to trap him in a rape case," DCP, Southwest, Shalini Singh said.

Police said a police team roamed the area with Gaur and he pointed the women to the cops. Police immediately placed them under arrest.

Police officials said that Sunita is a resident of Tughlaqabad and Preeti resides in Mayur Vihar Phase-III. Police officials said that the women have confessed to having extorted other people in similar fashion, the details of which is being verified.

Heading: Last Friday of the month? Time to ride through the city - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court on Friday denied anticipatory bail to Utsav Bhasin, accused of running over a youth in South Delhi with his BMW car in an inebriated state.

The court took into account the conduct of Bhasin at the time of the accident, especially on the prosecution's version that he had fled the spot instead of taking the injured victim, Anuj Singh, a call centre employee, to the hospital.

Also against Bhasin is the eyewitness account of Mrigank Srivastava, Anuj's friend, who was with him at the time of the accident and was injured as well. Srivastava told the police that Bhasin had continued to drive even though he knew that Anuj's clothes had gotten entangled with the car wheels through the rearview mirror of his car.

Srivastava's version, the court found, was a "relevant fact" underlining its decision to charge the teenager with Section 304 of the IPC (culpable homicide not amounting to murder).

"Taking into consideration the totality of the facts and circumstances, the present case is not a fit one for the grant of anticipatory bail," Justice Veena Birbal said in her decision.

Bhasin was earlier denied anticipatory bail by a trial court on September 18.

Heading: Moview reviews - Indian Express
Content:
On any other day the sight of over 300 cyclists riding in harmony in the heart of Delhi's rush hour traffic would have been unusual. But on Friday evening when a large number of cyclists came onto the Delhi roads they carried forward the torch of a historic movement, the Critical Mass movement that started in San Francisco in 1992 as a peaceful statement to show how unfriendly the city was for cyclists. And after 16 years of its origin, the movement has spread like wildfire to over 300 countries, with cycle rides being organsied on the last Friday of every month.

In Delhi, the cycling community had the fire. All it required was a spark. That spark was supplied by a general email sent to all the members of an online cycling community, the Delhi Cycling Club by one of its members, Chander Lall. "I had wanted to organise something like this for long. So I just sent out mailers to everyone informing them of a get-together on September 26 at Vijay Chowk. Surprisingly people turned up in large numbers," says Lall, 42, an intellectual property rights lawyer. The sole aim behind the critical mass movement is not clearly defined, except that it is a large group of cyclists meeting at a set location at a given time and riding through the city in large groups. "We just want to show that we can also merge with the traffic ," said Lall.

Among the 300 cyclists, many expatriates participated in the ride that started from Vijay Chowk and culminated with around Connaught Place in a span of two hours.

"This is a leaderless movement and involves people who share a passion for riding. People of all ages are welcome," says Simon Bishop, 41, a transport planner from London, who has worked in building cycle-favourable policies in London. The cyclists were dressed in proper gear complete with helmets and knee pads and fluorescent jackets.

Many were first timers also. "I used to cycle in my home town of Sydney, Australia, where this movement is quite popular," she said. Owing to custom, the group plans to continue with such mass cycling movements, on every last Friday of the month. "It is just the first time and we have seen a good turnout. Let's hope we are able to sustain this effort," says Bishop.

Heading: Jackichan takes a step to stardom - Indian Express
Content:
HARI PUTTAR, A COMEDY OF TERRORS
CAST: Zain Khan, Sarika, Saurabh Shukla, Vijay Raaz, Swini Khara, Lilette Dubey, Jackie Shroff
DIRECTORS: Lucky Kohli and Rajesh Bajaj
Warner Bros were getting antsy for nothing. Hari Puttar has nothing to do with the Harry Potter films, other than the fact that both have been filmed in England. Hari isn't a young wizard with a scar zigzagging though his forehead. He's just a ten-year-old who gets left behind in a large mansion, somewhere on the outskirts of London. Sounds familiar? Yep, it's got a lot to do with 'Home Alone', with Zain Khan doing a desi McCaulay Culkin.

Hari is dumped on by everybody: his elder brother thinks he is a total wimp, his cousins  laugh at his accent; in fact, the whole caboodle thinks he should neither be seen nor heard. His mom (Sarika) is the only one who dotes on her beloved 'puttar', but even she forgets him, as the family hares off somewhere, leaving behind our young hero, and his one cousin (Swini) who likes him.

If you remember the first Home Alone flick, you know what happens: the youngsters (Zain, last seen in Chain Kuli Ki Main Kuli, is likeable; Swini, last seen in Cheeni Kum, is not) beat a couple of thieves back, with all their arsenal: dragging them across lawns, throwing smelly liquids whooshing on their heads, shooting sharp pointed objects at various body parts, and so on.

And because it is a Hindi film, it has an item number, fronted by Shamita Shetty. A larger-than-life villain, who has one false eye and a hideous Mumbaiya accent. A couple of hoods called Diesel and Filter (Saurabh in waist-length Rasta curls who lets loose noisy smells from his rear end at regular intervals, and Vijay in florid flowery suit). A scientist who's working on a secret computer 'cheep' (chip). And a script which doesn't know the meaning of sense, and so full of holes that several large-sized trucks can drive right through.

Who cares, though? Certainly not the six-year-old sitting right ahead, who chortled his way through much the film. Plot to have your tykes whisked off to the film by elder siblings, while you take in that film you've been wanting to: that's what multiplexes are for!

RAFOO CHAKKAR—FUN ON THE RUN
CAST: Yuddhisthir, Aslam Khan, Nauheed Cyrusi, Nisha Rawal, Archana Puran Singh, Mita Vashist, Shakti Kapoor, Sadashiv Amrapurkar
DIRECTOR: B H Tharunkumar
And this one has nothing to do with that mid-70s barrel of fun-on-the-run starring Rishi and Neetu, other than the fact that they share the same name, Rafoo Chakkar.

Two middle-aged sisters (Archana and Mita) have to marry within 24 hours to fulfill the conditions of their father's will. Two ne'er-do-wells (Yudi and Aslam) land at their doorstep, and are reeled in, kicking and screaming. In addition to this happy foursome are two curvy airheads (Nauheed and Nisha), who claim they are penniless, but appear to be dressed (if you call Nauheed's plunging tees 'dressing') to the nines every time they appear on screen.

B H Tharunkumar's previous outing Nayee Padosan had fake sets, loud actors, and a story which didn't have a subtle bone in its body. Rafoo Chakkar takes all these ingredients, and ratchets them up a hundredfold, making it way beyond bad.

The lines are worse. Sample this exchange between the two fellows, about to be led off to their 'suhaag raat': "hamari bohni itni purane customers se nahin ho sakti".

Yeah, it's like that. All of it.

shubhra.gupta@expressindia.com

THE X-FILES: I WANT TO BELIEVE
CAST: Gillian Anderson, David Duchovny, Amanda Peet
DIRECTOR: Chris Carter
Some files are meant never to be closed, and many would argue that The X-Files fits that category. Six years after the series ended and 10 years after the last film, Scully and Mulder take barely a scene between them to get The X-Files back in its rhythm. It isn't the best case that the two have solved, it isn't the most difficult, it isn't even the best of science fictions, and it barely fits into the category of paranormal, but it is perhaps the closest look at two characters that TV audiences have loved for years now.

Older and wiser, less flashier and argumentative, Scully (Anderson) and Mulder (Duchovny) here are retired from the FBI and at peace. Yes, they are living together, and the film just lets that drop, casually. After all those years of speculation about whether they would do "it", when they would do "it", this matter-of-factness sets the pace for the rest of this adventure. This Scully and Mulder are not here to impress us — that battle was long won— they are here to be themselves, do what they believe in. And if you think about it, the Scully and Mulder we know would go about their love in their own way, at their own pace.

When the FBI seeks their help to look for a missing agent — the only clue they have is a psychic who claims to be able to see her — they get into it grudgingly. With everybody doubting the psychic, Mulder, who is the "believer" of The X-Files, is quickly drawn in. Scully, now working as a doctor in a church-run hospital, is as always the sceptic.

More than the search for the FBI agent, the film at many levels is about the larger question of faith, and how far one would go for it. The film pits stem-cell therapy against religion, is about scientists taking organ transplant far enough to play god, about a serial paedophile priest who prays with the belief that God will forgive him, about Scully debating reason and emotion in trying to save a dying patient, and about Mulder who seeks no reason at all for his beliefs.

There are many things stunningly out of place. Such as a top-notch surgeon like Scully "googling" to find out about stem-cell therapy, and apparently using the information on her patient to save his life. But Anderson is so earnest, her portrayal of a doctor torn between what she knows and what she would like to believe so tortured that you can almost believe she is doing everything in her power to save the boy.

Yes, it is not The X-Files we know, but be as it were about former FBI agents Scully and Mulder, let it herald the beginning of a whole new adventure: The Ex-Files. I want to believe.

CHARLIE BARTLETT
CAST: Anton Yelchin, Robert Downey Jr, Hope Davis, Kat Dennings
DIRECTOR: Jon Poll


Now what exactly is this film about? A poor little rich kid missing his parents? A principal trying to run a school of hardboiled kids? Misguided teens and their angst, with no one to listen to them? Misuse and the easy availability of drugs? Or perhaps, as in case of most teen emergencies, almost nothing at all?

Even that would work, except that Charlie Bartlett decides to be faux serious, and keeps adding layer upon layer till it is playing on your nerves. Half that effort, and this could have been American Pie.

You feel the worst for Anton Yelchin who plays Bartlett. He is a true find and a natural as a teen forced to don the role of an adult in the absence of a father — who is in jail — and in order to take care of a mother — who refuses to take charge. Remember Juno? Bartlett could be the male version. However, here he is dishing out wisdom and psychobabble, apparently without any reason and without applying any of it to himself.

The rest of the school is apparently full of no-brainers, who will take Bartlett's words or the drugs he freely distributes, in the men's toilet, no questions asked.

Robert Downey Jr as the alcoholic principal and Hope Davis as Bartlett's cheerfully clueless mother try to inject a much-needed levity, but the film keeps pulling them down and down.

shalini.langer@expressindia.com

Heading: All eyes on household waste disposal scheme - Indian Express
Content:
Named after Hollywood star Jackie Chan, the Manipur lad bags Subroto Cup's 'Player of the Tournament' award

So, what is in a name? In T Jackichan Singh's case, quite a lot, an apparent spelling error notwithstanding. The stocky Manipuri lad has got it all: spectacular kicks, lightning-quick reflexes and speed. Unlike his filmstar namesake, however, Subroto Cup's Player of the Tournament employs them to floor opponents on a football turf.

While his skills leave rival defenders with no answer, Jackichan himself draws a blank when asked why he was so christened. A long-distance call to his mother, Telem Ibemcha Devi, back home in Imphal, brings a semblance of clarity. She says she named him after Jackie Chan as she wanted him to become famous.

Wish granted. The Army Boys (Bangalore) midfielder scored five goals in as many matches, including one in the final against Mizoram, and set up a number of others in the tournament to help his team capture the under-17 title.

This despite the fact that he claims he fared badly in the title clash. "I was loose during the match. The award distracted me. I knew I'm going to get it as the organisers had taken me for the registration of the two-wheeler for the best player," says Singh, who assisted Tej Kumar Singh in scoring the first goal for Army Boys and then netted the winner from an indirect kick from the right corner of the box.

Selectors Ranjit Thapa, Anadi Barua and Kallol Chakroborty, voting players separately and on different parameters, chose Singh unanimously, saying that there was no competition for the seventeen-year old.

"He wasn't at his best during the final, but we didn't need to calculate much while choosing him," says Thapa.

"He scored in all the matches, even when he wasn't at his best. His special ability is creating chances from very small areas, small angles, like Thursday's first goal. He can beat any player in one-on-one position," says Barua. Thapa quickly adds to Barua's point, saying, "He is an opportunist. Give him the slightest of chance, and he will make you pay."

Singh's 41st minute strike in the final seemed to have inspired Thapa's late, but significant observation.

Coach Venugopal dismisses Jackichan Singh's small stature as disadvantageous, drawing comparison with Sunil Chettri on height. "He's isn't tall enough for his position. But that's irrelevant. Look at Sunil Chettri, he is the shortest, but is the main player in India's strike force."

Meanwhile, after ducking the unforeseen media glare, Singh tries doing a Jackie Chan driving the two-wheeler with four of his team mates. On stopping, after a few ground officials complained to the coach, he promises to come with a better reason next time for his name. As for his future, Singh says he would love to play for Churchill Brothers. But why not Mohun Bagan or East Bengal? He says, he doesn't like their names.

Heading: Keylong-Leh road reopened for traffic - Indian Express
Content:
One of the biggest environmental hazards, the unscientifically disposed household waste littered over Shimla hills has lately attracted attention of civic bodies of the town and educational institutions as well. With Pollution Control Board's (PCB) and forest department's constant eye on the issue, a way has been paved for formulation of immediate steps for household waste management.

Beginning October 1, the Shimla Municipal Corporation would launch cleaning up operations of all hill tops, where garbage is littered, causing the nullahs to choke. The failure of natural drainage system of the town forces the water channels to change its course, leading to landslides.

A special task force with 15 members, primarily safai karamcharis, would clean the hill tops and nullahs on a regular basis in some wards.

This would be followed by door-to-door driven by girls of different educational institutions.

They would be involved in educating people about segregation of bio-degradable and non-bio degradable waste at the source.

Senior officials in the Municipal Corporation said St Bedes College had volunteered for the door-to-door campaign and soon RKMV would be roped in to form teams of three girls each who would move about in localities covering 40 houses each. Over 1,000 such teams would be formed.

It was the joint action of Shimla Municipal Corporation, Forest department and state PCB that set in a motion the campaign to clean up critical areas in Shimla. Thirty-seven sites were successfully cleaned up.

"But the question of ensuring cleanliness of the town in long term still remained. The MC would soon start two campaigns. The intention make the residents use green and black packets for garbage segregation and later providing separate dustbins for it.

The initiative of providing packets would initially be supported by the corporation," said the official.

In the past all waste management schemes including door-to-door garbage collection scheme had failed. "Now all eyes are set on a long term measure," said Abha Singh, a retired teacher and resident of Chotta Shimla since 60 years.

Heading: Illegal structures to be regularised - Indian Express
Content: Leh road  has  been  reopened  for  vehicular  traffic after a snow-clearance operation was launched by General Road Engineering Force(GREF), a wing of Border Roads Organisation (BRO). C Pal Rasu, Deputy Commissioner Lahaul and Spiti said so far he had no information about any casualty on Keylong-Leh road particularly at Baralacha Pass.  He said no  tourist or passenger is stranded at Baralacha Pass or Chander Tal area of Spiti. Though several  persons were stuck in Spiti valley after heavy snowfall. He appealed to the people particularly  the media persons to  beware of rumours about the  snow and alleged reports of missing persons in Chandertal and Baralacha  region were wrong. Though he confirmed death of one Chhering Dorje.

Heading: Consular access provided to 15 Pak prisoners in Amritsar - Indian Express
Content:
Institutes, hotels, industrial units can avail the offer

In a major decision, the Punjab government has offered regularisation of illegal structures, constructed in violation of the Punjab Urban Planning and Development Authority (PUDA) Building Rules outside municipal limits, across the state.

Under the policy decision, the government has asked all those institutes, hotels and industrial units that had been constructed or developed without requisite permission to avail the offer.

The structures, which had come up illegally before or after the enforcement of the Rules on January 21, 2005, were asked to apply to the chief administrators (CAs) of the development authority concerned, including PUDA, Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA), Greater Ludhiana Area Development Authority (GLADA), Jalandhar Development Authority (JDA) and Bathinda Development Authority (BDA), within 30 days of the public notice, which was issued on Friday.

As per the policy, the promoters and developers of the illegal structures will have to deposit the applicable change of land use (CLU) charges, external development charges (EDC) and licence fee with their respective building plans for approval.

Confirming the decision, Secretary, Housing and Urban Development (SHUD), Punjab, Arun Goel told The Indian Express that only those structures that conform to all the prevailing rules and regulations and where the full and final levies applicable have been deposited will be regularised.

"The policy does not mean that all illegalities will be legalised," clarified the Secretary, Housing and Urban Development, adding that the applicants will have to first amend their building plans as per rules and remove violations, if any, before getting regularised.

Goel disclosed that the government took this decision while considering representations from certain developers and promoters who were willing to conform to all prevailing rules and regularisation, besides paying all applicable charges, for getting their structures regularised.

Chief Town Planner (CTP) of Punjab Rajinder Sharma divulged that the hotels applying for regularisation will have to be in accordance with the policy for hotels and, likewise, professional institutes will have to fulfill the rules and regulations of their statutory body, All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), before seeking regularisation.

"Any violation or illegality will not be regularised at any cost, but under this policy, all the structures obeying the rules will be regularised without any fine," revealed Sharma.

PUDA CA Som Parkash said though the decision was taken at the government level, PUDA was made the nodal agency to issue notice on behalf of all the development authorities to inform the public in this regard. "All applications received under this policy will be forwarded to the government, which will consider them in consultation with the CTP," he disclosed.

Greater Mohali Area Development Authority Chief Administrator Vivek Partap Singh said, "Regularisations will be made as per the draft master plans of the area concerned as nothing violating the planned developed criterion could be given assent."

Heading: Kidnapped boy recovered; 3 held - Indian Express
Content:
In what has instilled hope among Pakistani prisoners lodged in Amritsar Central Jail, India today granted consular access to 15 such prisoners. The prisoners include three women and a minor child, who have completed their sentences and are now waiting to go home.

A two-member team of the Pakistan High Commission, comprising officials of the Pakistan Embassy, including Mukhtiar Hussain and Asghar Ali, today interacted with the prisoners here, including the three women, who have been identified as Roshan Bibi, Zaibun Bai, Amna and her three-year-old child.

Sources said these prisoners had landed in jail on account of travelling without valid documents, overstaying visas, visiting cities not specifically covered by visas and inadvertent border crossings and had completed their sentences long back.

The antecedents of 25 other Pakistani nationals had been verified earlier and they are now waiting to go home, said Jail Superintendent S.P. Singh. "We have given these officials the lists and other documents carrying the names and other details of these prisoners," he said.

Meanwhile, Mukhtar Hussain, an official of the Pakistan High Commission, said the decision about the release of these prisoners depended on the verification of their antecedents. "Whether their country is ready to take them back or not depends on the verification of their antecedents. We have taken their details from the jail authorities here and would verify these on returning to Pakistan and a decision would be taken accordingly," he said.

He added that this process of consular access is normally followed in cases where the prisoners have completed their punishments and are awaiting release.

Meanwhile, SP Singh stated that a similar exercise had been held two years ago as well.

Heading: Jalandhar admn ties up with pvt industry for providing jobs - Indian Express
Content:
Ten-year-old Tejinder Singh, who was kidnapped from village Samravan Khas on Thursday, was recovered today. Police have arrested three persons in the case.

One of the kidnappers, Sukhjinder Singh, is a resident of the same village and worked as a driver for relatives of the kidnapped boy. Police said lack of money for a marriage led to the kidnapping of the boy. The kidnappers had demanded Rs 30 lakh as ransom.

Among the arrested are Sikander Kumar of Dheena, Sukhjinder Singh of Partapura and Gurdev Kaur of Samravan Colony. The main accused, Amandeep Singh, is still absconding.

Police said Amandeep Singh of Kot Sadik wanted to marry his girlfriend and planned to kidnap the boy along with the other accused to generate money for the marriage.

The boy told the police that yesterday when he was going on a bicycle, a Honda City car stopped close to him and the driver asked the way to some village. He said after that he was pulled inside the car. The kidnappers took the boy to a lonely house in Samravan Khas village and kept him on the first floor of the house. However, the boy said he was not tortured in any manner.

SSP Pawan Rai said the boy has been handed over to the family and further investigation is on.

Heading: Smit Singh makes it to Indian shooting squad for C’wealth Youth Games - Indian Express
Content:
The district administration has joined hands with private industries of Jalandhar to provide employment opportunities to lakhs of unemployed youth in the state.

It may be noted that in industry in Jalandhar, nearly 75 per cent employees, including labourers, are outsiders and the industry is perpetually facing acute shortage of staff.

The youth would be employed through an "employment fair" being organised by Jalandhar Chamber of Industries and Commerce (JCIC) on October 3 at District Industries Centre at Focal Point. Training would also be provided to the recruited youth to enhance their abilities further. The Chamber has invited applications under six categories, including security personnel, computer operators, founderymen, electricians, mechanical engineers and other technical persons.

Narinder Sehgal, president of the Chamber, along with DC A.S. Pannu said in a joint press conference here today that there was an acute shortage of labourers. This policy would not only help the unemployed youth, but also the industry, which will get labour for the entire year.

Heading: Question me before an HC judge or a judicial officer: Nirmal Yadav - Indian Express
Content:
One of the many compelling images that inspire young shooter Smit Singh is Abhinav Bindra's calm face even after winning an Olympic gold in the 10-metre air rifle event in Beijing last month. As Smit makes it to the Indian team for the Commonwealth Youth Games to be held it in Pune next month, there was only one thing that he wanted to say: "Abhinav has made shooting a household name in India and put Chandigarh on the shooting map in the world. I hope I can do even ten percent of that."

Singh's big break comes in his favourite event, skeet, and he expects to give his best shot.

"Youth Commonwealth Games will give me a chance to rub shoulders with some of the world's best shooters in the junior category and I am looking forward to this experience," says the 18-year-old shooter, adding: "I have to perform well. I will attend a coaching camp in Patiala till October 11 and after the Games, which will be held from October 12 to 18, my target will be to perform well in the national meets."

India will field a 12-member team in the event and Singh, the only shooter from Punjab, hopes to do well in an event dominated by Italy.

"India is sending a 12-member team to the Games and all top junior Italian shooters will be there. It will be tough but I hope to do well," says Smit.

A student of DAV Public School, Sector 15, Smit plans to train abroad in the coming months, which will give him a chance to get training from some of the world-class coaches and trainers. "I am just back from the Italian Grand Prix. The performance helped me improve my world junior ranking from 42 to 28. I plan to take part in more international tournaments next year to improve my world ranking further before I move to the senior circuit," feels the shooter who also went to Germany prior to Italy for special coaching.

Ask him about the pressure in the senior circuit and he is quick to respond: "I hope I will learn with time. Shooting needs a lot of concentration and apart from physical fitness, there are various other aspects related to it. I hope the transition from junior circuit to senior circuit will be smooth."

Heading: ‘Stop this wasteful expenditure at once’ - Indian Express
Content:
CASH AT JUDGE'S DOOR : Judge sends request to HC Chief Justice; CBI says no objection

Justice Nirmal Yadav of the Punjab and Haryana High Court has requested Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur to ensure that her examination by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in the cash-at-judge's-door case is done "in the presence of a third person".

The packet containing Rs 15 lakh in cash that was wrongly delivered at Justice Nirmaljit Kaur's residence on August 13 was allegedly meant for Justice Nirmal Yadav.

She said the third person, who could be a judicial officer or even a High Court judge, should be appointed by the Chief Justice, and the officer would act as an independent witness during the examination.

The demand has also been conveyed to the Delhi CBI, which will shortly question Justice Yadav. The CBI said it did not have any objection to the demand "as long as we get the answers to our questions".

"The demand cannot be legally challenged since she is being examined as a witness by the CBI and not as an accused," said a senior CBI official. "It appears the judge wants to ensure that her statements during the questioning are not changed by the CBI team, keeping in view the sensitivity of the case," he added.

The CBI has already questioned Justice Nirmaljit Kaur in connection with the case. According to information available with the agency, two more judges — one from the Supreme Court and one from the Punjab and Haryana High Court — were reportedly present at her residence on August 13 when the money was delivered. During the questioning, which lasted for over 30 minutes, the judge is learnt to have clearly denied this.

On the other hand, Ravinder Singh, the Delhi hotelier who had allegedly sent the cash, has admitted to knowing a few HC and Supreme Court judges "because they visited my hotels in Delhi". Ravinder denied his involvement in the case, but said he often gave gifts to friends on festivals and special occasions.

The CBI took him to Solan to confront him about a property that he allegedly co-owned with Justice Nirmal Yadav. He has denied his involvement in the property deal too. The registry documents of the property had among the 18 share-holders one person by the name of Ravinder. The hotelier denied it was him.

The CBI team did not take Ravinder to Delhi. They questioned him about the properties owned by him there, which was cross-checked by a unit of the CBI in the Capital. "We are looking into the properties owned by him," said an officer.

Ravinder will be produced before the Special CBI court in Chandigarh on Saturday, when his police remand ends.

Heading: FM stations to go off air for 3 days from today - Indian Express
Content:
With revelations under the Right to Information Act highlighting the fact that more than 130 people work at the Punjab Raj Bhavan to take care of UT Administrator and Punjab Governor General S F Rodrigues (Retd), various sections of the society feel it is time for the "laat sahib" regime to go.

They are all unanimous in terming the expenditure "extravagant and wasteful" and demand an immediate check on this.

A local NGO, Society for Prevention of Crime and Corruption, has even moved an appeal to the Prime Minister, Public Accounts Committee, Lok Sabha and the local MP, apprising them of such "extravagant and wasteful" expenditure being incurred by the Chandigarh Administration for taking care of the comforts of one man.

The appeal says: "The issue needs to be placed before the Public Accounts Committee and such extravagant and wasteful expenditure should be stopped."

Heading: Students protesting n-deal baton charged - Indian Express
Content:
Radio buffs in Chandigarh and nearby areas will not be able to enjoy the FM stations for three days, during afternoon and night hours, from Saturday. Due to certain technical maintenance work, the All India Radio will shut the transmission from 2 to 5 pm and midnight to 6 am. The stations to be affected include 92.7; 94.3, 103.10 and 107.20. It is perhaps the first time that radio programmes will be off air for such long durations.

Talking to Newsline, programme head, All India Radio, Poonam Singh said: "It may not be a complete blackout, but the service will definitely be disrupted. We are trying to improve our transmission quality."

Station Engineer Vikas Bhatt said: "All four stations, including the private players, are likely to be disrupted as we will be tuning our transmission signals. Certain complaints had been received at the station regarding poor quality transmission, mainly in the Mohali region, because of which we wanted to check and improve the transmission quality. It is not certain if it is going to be a complete blackout, but disruption for a few hours is likely."

"All stations use a common antenna, because of which disruption will be likely in all transmissions," Bhatt added.

"94.3 My FM is scheduled to observe a shutdown of services during certain hours for three days. In its letter dated September 9, 2008, Broadcast Engineering Consultants India Limited (BECIL), which works as a consultancy agency, a system integrator and as a turnkey solution provider in the fields of broadcast engineering and information technology, had requested the AIR to permit the shutdown," said Ritu Ghai, regional programme head, My FM.

The transmission from Delhi, Kasauli and Jalandhar stations will continue uninterrupted.

Heading: Landslide blocks Ghaggar again - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh Police had to use force on members of the Punjab Students' Union, who were protesting against the nuclear deal, after the latter tried to cross barricades to reach the Punjab Governor House on Friday.

The police used water cannons and baton charged the protestors to control the situation, leaving six students injured. The injuries were, however, not serious.

The union demands the nuclear deal to be struck down.

"We were carrying out our protest peacefully and just wanted to submit our representation to the Governor. But the police used force on us," said Gurmukh Singh Maan of the union.

Denying the allegations, Deputy Superintendent of Police (East) P K Dhawan said: "Things were under control until one of the protestors provoked the entire group, saying peaceful protest would not yield anything, after which the protestors tried to cross the barricades. We were forced to use water cannons."

Heading: Three gangsters arrested from former SP’s house - Indian Express
Content:
Flood threat looms large over five villages

With a major landslide having blocked the path of the seasonal rivulet of Ghaggar in Morni, there are strong chances that as many as five villages on the banks of the rivulet will face floods in the coming days. The five villages include Thana, Sirmara, Umri, Dangranwala and Kumwala.

"It has been nearly four days now since the landslide took place. Large number of fields in Umri village was destroyed due to the landslide that blocked the course of the river. It was for this that a 40-feet lake-kind formation was created at the spot," said Paramjit Singh, a panch of one of these villages.

"It was around 20 years ago that a similar condition was witnessed, when a landslide took place, due to a major earthquake, and blocked the rivulet, thereby washing away almost all the houses of the nearby villages. While several persons left the region after that, there are nearly five villages still present in the area", said Ramesh Kumar, another villager.

While villagers complain about the lack of concern shown by officials, the Divisional Forest officer, Pratap Singh, while speaking to Newsline maintained, "We are keeping a close watch on the situation. We are trying not to touch the landslide area to allow the rivulet to make way naturally. If the problem, however, becomes serious we will have to remove the blockage."

Heading: ‘Young at heart’ senior citizens no longer lonely - Indian Express
Content:
The Himachal Pradesh Police arrested three gangsters from the Sector-69 residence of a retired Panjab Superintendent of Police (SP) today.

The arrested persons have been identified as Navpreet Singh and Hargobind Singh, both residents of Amritsar and Inderjeet Singh Chahal, a resident of Mansa, said Sub-Inspector Mohinder Singh, Station House Officer (SHO) of Gagret.

He told Newsline over phone that the arrested persons are members of an inter-state vehicle lifters' gang. The SHO did not comment on the role of the former Punjab officer.

A resident, on condition of anonymity, said the police carried out a search of the house of the former Punjab police officer for over an hour.

He said the area residents were skeptical of a few vehicles, including a Balero, Scorpio, Tata Indica among others, parked outside the former cop's house. He added that a youth, who drove the vehicles, used to stay at the cop's house.

SHO Mohinder Singh said the police had got a lead after the arrest of a few members of the gang, who revealed that their accomplices were staying in Mohali. "We had recovered a few stolen vehicles, including cars and tractors, from the arrested members of the gang," he said.

While area residents claimed that the police carried away some stolen vehicles, the police denied the same.

They also said the police party searched the house for a second time in the evening and took away household articles, believed to belong to the arrested gangsters.

Meanwhile, Navneet Kumar, Phase VIII SHO, under whose jurisdiction the area falls, categorically denied any knowledge of the raid, Swarndeep Singh, DSP (City-II) confirmed the police raid and arrests.

Mohinder Singh, meanwhile, said that after slapping charges of theft, the arrested gangsters were interrogated to get further leads, including information about how they came in contact with the ex-Punjab SP.

Repeated attempts to contact the retired SP, however, proved futile.

Heading: Movie reviews - Indian Express
Content:
In a gesture to remind senior citizens of their importance in the social fabric,

'Elders' Day' was celebrated on Friday at the Kalagram Baithak.

Former Governor of Punjab, Lt General B K N Chhibber(Retd) was the chief guest on the occasion, which was organised by the Senior Citizen Welfare Association, Modern Housing Complex.

Elderly people above the age of 75 years were honoured for their contribution to the association.

A cultural programme was also organised for the entertainment of senior citizens. Sufi songs and ghazals were performed by various artists at the function.

Most of the seniors present at the function felt that to keep oneself busy is the key to get over the vacuum that is created once children leave for work or other

purposes.

Not one to be bogged down by the 'Empty Nest Syndrome', Varsha Shavi, whose children are working in other cities says, "We keep ourselves so busy that we do not get time to dwell over loneliness. I and my husband have joined various clubs which keep us busy for most of the day."

Her friend Janak Sehgal adds that being a member of various kitty parties keeps her busy. "It is a good way to meet friends and it also keeps one occupied," she says.

Baba Ramdev seems to have caught the fancy of the senior citizens with most of them spending upto two hours watching him do yoga on television.
