"I start my day with yoga followed by a walk at the Sukhna Lake. Other than this, we spend time socialising and catching up with old friends," says Santosh Sharma, whose children are settled in the US for over two decades now.

"I am a big movie buff. So to pass time, I catch up with the latest flick at a city multiplex," smiles Usha Sharma.

Heading: Students now pay more to colleges - Indian Express
Content:
HARI PUTTAR, A COMEDY OF TERRORS
CAST: Zain Khan, Sarika, Saurabh Shukla, Vijay Raaz, Swini Khara, Lilette Dubey, Jackie Shroff
DIRECTORS: Lucky Kohli and Rajesh Bajaj
WARNER Bros were getting antsy for nothing. Hari Puttar has nothing to do with the Harry Potter films, other than the fact that both have been filmed in England. Hari isn't a young wizard with a scar zigzagging though his forehead. He's just a ten-year-old who gets left behind in a large mansion, somewhere on the outskirts of London. Sounds familiar? Yep, it's got a lot to do with 'Home Alone', with Zain Khan doing a desi McCaulay Culkin.
Hari is dumped on by everybody: his elder brother thinks he is a total wimp, his cousins  laugh at his accent; in fact, the whole caboodle thinks he should neither be seen nor heard. His mom (Sarika) is the only one who dotes on her beloved 'puttar', but even she forgets him, as the family hares off somewhere, leaving behind our young hero, and his one cousin (Swini) who likes him.
If you remember the first Home Alone flick, you know what happens: the youngsters (Zain, last seen in Chain Kuli Ki Main Kuli, is likeable; Swini, last seen in Cheeni Kum, is not) beat a couple of thieves back, with all their arsenal: dragging them across lawns, throwing smelly liquids whooshing on their heads, shooting sharp pointed objects at various body parts, and so on.
And because it is a Hindi film, it has an item number, fronted by Shamita Shetty. A larger-than-life villain, who has one false eye and a hideous Mumbaiya accent. A couple of hoods called Diesel and Filter (Saurabh in waist-length Rasta curls who lets loose noisy smells from his rear end at regular intervals, and Vijay in florid flowery suit). A scientist who's working on a secret computer 'cheep' (chip). And a script which doesn't know the meaning of sense, and so full of holes that several large-sized trucks can drive right through.
Who cares, though? Certainly not the six-year-old sitting right ahead, who chortled his way through much the film. Plot to have your tykes whisked off to the film by elder siblings, while you take in that film you've been wanting to: that's what multiplexes are for!

RAFOO CHAKKAR—FUN ON THE RUN
CAST: Yuddhisthir, Aslam Khan, Nauheed Cyrusi, Nisha Rawal, Archana Puran Singh, Mita Vashist, Shakti Kapoor, Sadashiv Amrapurkar
DIRECTOR: B H Tharunkumar
And this one has nothing to do with that mid-70s barrel of fun-on-the-run starring Rishi and Neetu, other than the fact that they share the same name, Rafoo Chakkar.
Two middle-aged sisters (Archana and Mita) have to marry within 24 hours to fulfill the conditions of their father's will. Two ne'er-do-wells (Yudi and Aslam) land at their doorstep, and are reeled in, kicking and scr eaming. In addition to this happy foursome are two curvy airheads (Nauheed and Nisha), who claim they are penniless, but appear to be dressed (if you call Nauheed's plunging tees 'dressing') to the nines every time they appear on screen.
B H Tharunkumar's previous outing Nayee Padosan had fake sets, loud actors, and a story which didn't have a subtle bone in its body. Rafoo Chakkar takes all these ingredients, and ratchets them up a hundredfold, making it way beyond bad.
The lines are worse. Sample this exchange between the two fellows, about to be led off to their 'suhaag raat': "hamari bohni itni purane customers se nahin ho sakti".
Yeah, it's like that. All of it.

shubhra.gupta@expressindia.com

Heading: Chhatbir welcomes 3 new inmates - Indian Express
Content:
When the academic session began this year, the Punjab University issued directions to its affiliate colleges to implement a uniform fee structure. The move invited criticism as the colleges had anticipated financial losses. They, however, implemented the same, although reluctantly.

Three months down the line, the colleges don't seem to be making any "loss".

They have already come up with means to compensate themselves — in form of increased hostel fees, compulsory vocational courses, among others.

As a result, students who could have got a relief of around Rs 7,000 now have to shell out between Rs 2,000 and Rs 4,000 more than what they were paying before the uniform fee structure was implemented.

In some colleges, hostel charges have gone up by as much as Rs 7,000 a year. Left with no option, students have accepted the hike. The Administration and the PU, too, has failed to take any action against this.

Officials, meanwhile, are tightlipped and say they cannot do anything till they receive a formal complaint in writing in this regard.

While the DAV College, Sector 10, has increased its hostel fee from Rs 15,000 per annum to Rs 23,000, the MCM DAV College in Sector 36, has hiked it from Rs 42,000 to Rs 47,000.

In Dev Samaj College, Sector 45, the charges have gone up from Rs 36,000 to Rs 41,000, while SD College, Sector 32, has increased the fee from Rs 30,000 to Rs 32,000.

Dev Samaj College, Sector 36, has also accommodated students from other colleges, under a monetary understanding with them.

Making self-finance courses compulsory is another tactics that the colleges have adapted, to charge more money from the students.

SD College has mentioned in its prospectus that it is compulsory to opt for an add-on course for any student taking admission there. A similar practice is prevalent at DAV College too.

The fee for each add-on course varies between Rs 1,200 and Rs 2,400.

The PU had helped the colleges make up for the 'loss' they might have incurred by following the uniform fee structure, approving ten additional seats per unit for all the colleges. At the recent Senate meeting, five more seats per college were approved.

The Administration had said it would review the hike in hostel fees, but nothing seems to have been done in this regard.

Talking to Newsline, Director, Higher Education, Raji P Srivastava said: "The changes were made suddenly and we were busy implementing them. With things having settled down now, we will review the entire matter and take action with regard to charging extra money from students. We may work out a uniform fee structure for hostels too."

Heading: Plastic ban: shops stock paper, jute bags - Indian Express
Content:
Three new species of animals were introduced in the Chhatbir Zoo as part of an animal exchange programme with Mysore zoo. The new species include a pair of Fallow deer, a Hamadryas Baboon and a Black Swan.

Dharmendra Sharma, field director of the zoo said, "Fallow deer are mainly found in Mediterranean region. This is for the first time that the zoo will house a pair of these exotic animals. The Black Swan, which originates in Australia, too, will be a pleasant attraction for the visitors, who are used to seeing White Swans."

While talking about the arrangements made for the animals in view of the approaching winter, Sharma said, "The Baboons, which are found in Africa, need to be taken special care of during the winter season. We are taking appropriate measures to protect the animals from any harm," said Sharma.

The zoo also houses a Bison, which has been declared as an endangered species under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. "We already have two females of the species and the male has been brought for the purpose of breeding," said Sharma.

Heading: Senate: 5th victory for Rabinder Nath - Indian Express
Content:
Shopowners across the city are preparing themselves for the impending ban on polythene bags, expected to come into effect from October 2. While the bigger brands have switched over to paper and jute bags, many shopowners are still waiting for an official notification from the Administration.

The Benetton Store in Sector 17, will not be affected by the ban.

Reason: Ever since the store started operations, it used paper bags, which are supplied to the store from its head office.

Baldev Thakur, the manager of the store, said: "The store will not be affected by the ban as we already use paper bags. We also try to promote the habit of discarding polythene among our staff. They are told about abstaining from using polythene even in their houses."

At some places, meanwhile, the shopowners are busy finishing their stock of polythene bags before the ban comes into effect. "Though our stock of paper bags has arrived, we are, at present, in the process of finishing our stock of polythene bags first. The polythene bags, which we were using, are of good quality and large size. In fact, there are many customers who demand for the same. The paper bags cannot hold too many clothes," said Shahi, a staff at Lee Jeans.

Other shop keepers, meanwhile, believe using paper bags will add to their expenses. A shop owner in Sector 22 said: "Paper bags are not made in the city. These have to be brought from different places, which further adds to our expenses. The cost of one paper bag ranges between Rs 7 and Rs 20. This cost will be passed on to the customers."

Some, meanwhile, look upon the ban as a boon in disguise. Rajiv, the owner of a book shop said: "Customers used to demand for polythene bags and we had no option but to keep them. Now, I tell people that polythene has been banned. I believe paper bags are more economical."

The UT Administration had decided that no person, including shopkeepers, vendors, wholesalers, retailers, traders, hawkers or rehri owners, would be allowed to use plastic bags for the supply of goods, from October 2. The Administration has banned, not only the supply of polythene bags, but also its manufacture, store, import, sale or transport.

People found with polythene bags will be fined and a trial under the Environment Protection Act would be held in the District Court.

Heading: PU students to get accidental insurance cover - Indian Express
Content:
The declaration of the Panjab University Senate election results for the graduate constituency today saw smiles on a few faces while some returned home dejected.

The results saw the election of Rabinder Nath Sharma, for the fifth consecutive time. He, however, maintains that he always expected to win.

While there are a few new faces this time, the old senators, who won the elections this time too, form a majority.

Sitting senator Rabinder Nath Sharma, was elected for the fifth time this year, with the maximum number of votes.

After eight rounds of counting over the last few days, 15 candidates, out of the contesting 42 for the constituency, were declared elected.

Putting an end to the anxiety after tedious rounds of counting, sitting senators Prabhjit Singh, Dharinder Kumar Tayal, Malwinder Singh Kang, Anu Chatrath and Ravinder Kumar were re-elected.

Talking to Newsline, Kang said, "I am really happy to be elected as a Senate member and it will be my priority to work out benefits for the students of far-away colleges. Also, I am keen on improving the standard of sports in the University."

Adding similar thoughts, Anu Chatrath said, "I shall utilise this opportunity to work for the development of the students of the University and its associate colleges".

The first-timers who have secured their seats this year are: Dayal Pratap Singh, Kailash

Nath, Munish Verma and S S Randhawa.

Sources reveal the defeat of sitting senator and BJP candidate Praveen Kumar Sharma, has come as a major surprise.

He had given a tough competition to other candidates and was in the fray till the last two rounds, before he was eliminated.

Sources also add that the elimination of sitting senators S S Hundal and Madanjit Sahota was also unexpected.

After the first round of counting, five persons including principal M L Aeri, director of DAV Colleges, Katra Sher Singh from Amritsar and Junesh Kumari from Jalandhar have secured their seats in the Senate.

Others who have made it this time are Jagpal Singh, principal of Government College, Ludhiana and Jarnail Singh, principal of DAV College, Hoshiarpur against the two reserved seats for Punjab.

Heading: No judge’s phone being tapped: UT to HC - Indian Express
Content:
Students of the Panjab University will now get an accidental insurance cover; as an outcome of the long pending demand by different students' bodies.

A committee has been formed to look into the matter and has been asked to come up with a feasible sum that can be offered to students as an insurance cover.

Dean Students Welfare Professor Naval Kishore, said: "We have formed a committee to look into the matter and shall soon be finalising the insurance cover for the students."

The committee formed, shall take into consideration, the amount that can be kept aside by the university for the same.

The university, meanwhile, has not come upon any final decision yet.

It has only announced the acceptance the of long standing demands by the various students' bodies.

Authorities maintain that the newly elected students' council will also be involved in taking the decision, which is expected to be implemented in the next couple of months.

Talking to Newsline, Pulkit Jindal, member, National Students' Union of India (NSUI) said: "We are happy with the move as it was our long standing demand. Insurance cover is provided to students in various universities. The Panjab University has, at least, started with the accidental insurance cover for students."

Heading: Robe controversy: plea to quash FIR against Dera chief withdrawn - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh Administration submitted in the Punjab and Haryana High Court on Friday that no agency or officer of the UT Administration had ever attempted to tap mobile phones of any High Court judge.

The Administration had been asked to file a reply after the court took a suo motu notice of a news item appeared in an English daily, highlighting that post the judge bribery scam, a few judges feared their mobile phones were being tapped.

Notices had been issued to Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh. While law officers for Haryana and Chandigarh sought time to file replies, the counsel for Punjab government had already submitted that none of its agencies had tapped the mobile phones of any HC judge.

With UT Inspector General of Police S K Jain filing a reply on behalf of the Administration on Friday, it is only the Haryana government that is yet to file its reply.

Heading: State Bank of India to sponsor education of 50 girls - Indian Express
Content:
The counsel for the Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh, on Friday, withdrew the petition demanding quashing of the FIR registered against the Dera Chief in the controversial robe issue.

More than a year after the Dera Chief had moved the High Court demanding quashing of the FIR registered against him in the controversial robe case, his counsel, on Wednesday, had vehemently demanded that the Chief Minister of Punjab Parkash Singh Badal be made party to the case.

Surprised with the 'sudden discovery' after more than one year of filing of the petition, the High Court had turned down the request of the counsel.

The counsel had levelled allegations of malice against Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal and accused him of playing a pivotal role in getting the FIR registered against the Dera Chief.

The High Court, however, showing no conviction in the averments raised by the Dera Chief's counsel refused to grant any relief.

Resultantly, the petition was dismissed as withdrawn.

Heading: Common Sense - Indian Express
Content:
In an effort to boost the literacy rate among girls, the State Bank of India, Medical Institute branch decided to sponsor the education of 50 girls at a function held at the Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 10, on Friday. The children are students of Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 10, and Government Model High School, Sector 12.

Speaking on the occasion, Ajay Swaroop, Chief General Manager, State Bank of India, Chandigarh Circle, said that the bank has initiated an 'Adoption of Girl Child' scheme, wherein the bank will sponsor their education upto Class XII. He said that under the scheme, which was started last year, as many as 600 girls have already been sponsored by different branches of the bank in the states of Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir.

Elaborating on the scheme, V K Garg, Regional Manager, State Bank of India, said, "According to the scheme, the bank will provide financial assistance to students for books, uniforms, school fee and sponsorships for students who excel academically. The scheme was started to benefit underprivileged or physically challenged girls between the age group of 6 to 14 years."

Heading: Two  Much - Indian Express
Content:
Shekhar Suman makes a lot of it

He is what we'd like to call an uncommon commoner. In a world of copycats, Shekhar Sumna comes across as one of the originals. He may not have his set of Sumanisms, but he sure does make a lot of common sense, a pretty uncommon trait. Shoot any question, and the quote martial is a gratifying one. Take for instance the recent Shiv Sena Mumbai episode. While celebs raise their hands in 'please don't quote us', Shekhar is upfront: "In a cosmopolitan like Mumbai, this is the height of paradox, of dichotomy. Mumbai is considered to be the melting pot, but it's sad that such a heavily politically motivated thing has taken place. It's the responsibility of individuals to see through this divisive policy." He expects the government to be consistent and persistent, for the people to be more rooted, aware and conscious. "It's our constitutional right." In town for the Punjab Government's function to commemorate the birth centenary of Shaheed Bhagat Singh, Shekhar updates our Google info on him. "I've opened my production house, Windmill Entertainment and there are a couple of films coming up next year." Apparently, he wants his production house to focus on non-fiction programming. One is already on the floor for NDTV.

Shake and move to other facets of life, and Suman says he's "tired of doing comedy". "For me, an act of comedy is all about wit, satire, humour and a spontaneous take on life, not something that's borrowed or double meaning." This was one of reasons he opted out of Laughter Challenge. "You can see its progressive degeneration," he's sick of the nauseating humour. "We are living in an era of multi-tasking and the greatest thing about creativity is that you can do anything and be anyone," he's happy to see the fresh raw appeal in Rock On. "Precisely why you can't have stars as Ram or Sita. Ramayan and Mahabharata are already great stories, you don't need stars to sell these." But then, everyone succumbs to market pressure. "Because we are star driven," he smiles. So is son Adhayan too eyeing stardom? "You know Mahesh Bhatt said that Adhayan's capability to perform is amazing, has to be genetic," Bhatt has the talent to spot talent! "If you are grounded, self-righteous, then Bhatt is your camp. If it's overnight stardom, look to Yash Raj." Adhayan, in the meanwhile, will be seen in Bhatt's Raaz II and Jashan which is about the life of a rockstar. Whatever they say, Suman is the real rockstar!

Heading: In a Flash - Indian Express
Content:
MTV Roadies is back and this time around Raghu Ram isn't alone

First things first. It's a show that's given soppy saas-bahus and their whole programming kitty a run for their money. Into Season Six, MTV Roadies has become not just the country's longest running reality show but has topped whatever TRP charts they are, showing its huge popularity among not just the youth but across diverse age groups. This year, however, they are doubling up not just the stakes and the tasks but the man himself. If you thought one Raghu Ram was enough to tackle in the auditions, there are now two of them. "We didn't want Roadies to get predictable," grinned the man behind the show, MTV's dishy looking executive producer Raghu Ram as he introduced us to his twin Rajiv Laxman, also a producer with MTV and from what we hear he too has a mean side to him.

In town to kick-off auditions, we caught up with the brothers. "I love Chandigarh. I think there's some Karmic connection I have with the city," Raghu mentioned as we prodded him on what makes him come back each time he's doing Roadies or a new show for that matter. "It's simple. I have always got what I have come looking for here," he shoots. The past record speaks for itself. Past winners - Rannvijay and Ayushman Khurana - are from here, so are Bani and Varun and Vishal...most of whom have found careers with the channel as well. "You know unlike other cities of India, where youngsters try and put on an attitude, to Chandigarhians it all comes rather naturally," adds Rajiv who last came with Raghu scouting for contestants for their show Splitsvilla which too ran to a full house. And the brothers look exactly the same, though we still feel Raghu is more charming when he's not losing his temper that is! "It's not intentional," he chuckles. But why bring in the brother? "We wanted to add a new dimension. We don't want contestants to come prepared. Two of us is something no one can be prepared for," says the brain behind the show. Speaking of doubling up, the prize money at Roadies this year is a whopping Rs 10 lakhs apart from the Hero Honda bikes. While the show did go international last season, they are now headed for Down Under. "Australia is said to be the most dangerous country in the world with its hungry sharks, lonely deserts, venomous spiders," MTV's general manager Ashish Patil chipped in with more 'painful' details. Also the number of Roadies this year will be 20. "That gives more people a chance to be a part of the show on one hand while the competition will be fiercer given there's just going to be one winner," added Raghu. But before you actually get that far, you'll have to chat up the brothers!

The auditions will be held on September 28 and 29 at Indradhanush auditorium, Sector 5, Panchkula.

Heading: Star Gazing - Indian Express
Content: Quick was an understatement for they left before they even fully arrived. Yup, we are talking about Saif Ali Khan and his lady love, Kareena Kapoor. The couple in louve made a quick stop at Taj Chandigarh on their way back from Shimla where Bebo was shooting for Raj Kumar Hirani's Three Idiots with Aamir Khan. Saif had flown down to be with his girl on her birthday, and both flew back today from Chandigarh. Saifeena will soon be 'heard' on Yashraj's animation, Roadside Romeo. So much for puppy love!

Heading: ‘I love playing Ravana’ - Indian Express
Content:
Tinsel Town comes to town

For a minute it felt like Mumbai. As celebrities made their way in at the Taj Chandigarh, all rumours turned into reality. A very groggy eyed (even the bugs couldn't conceal the fatigue) Archana Puran Singh stilletoed in followed by Shekhar Suman fresh like crisp white linen, Mr and Mrs Udit Narayan always happy to pose, Prem Chopra in his signature black suit and hat, and villain Joginder. Phew! Need we mention that the hotel is already host to Rani Mukerji, Rakhi Sawant, Vrajesh Hirjee, the cast of Hrippa, and that Shahid Kapoor along with a bevy of stars is expected somewhere next month! Meanwhile, these guys are here for Punjab Government's function to commemorate Bhagat Singh's birth centenary at his native village Khatkar Kala. "They will be releasing coins in his name," tells Prem Chopra who remembers his days of playing Sukhdev in Shaheed. Currently, he's looking forward to his films Daddy Cool and Dilli 6. "I'm playing the good guy," he smiles. Joginder, on the other hand, was the most vocal about martyrdom and freedom fighters. "These are ways to remember the sacrifice and we need to instill love for this country and patriotism in today's generation," he was loud and clear. Raving about their son, the singer, performer and actor Aditya Narayan, parents Udit and Deepa said he would focus more on films. As for Deepa, Bhpjpuri films have proved to be a trump card and she's on a high. Wondering what happened to Archana? Well she excused herself but yes, she said no more television. "You'll be seeing less of me on the small screen." Aloha to the big boss then!!

Talking of star gazing: Don't miss out on Harman Baweja's performance tomorrow night.

Heading: All Grown Up - Indian Express
Content:
Twelve years since he played Kroor Singh on Chandrakanta, actor Akhilendra Mishra is living his dream on television

It's the voice. You feel as though he's performing right in front of your eyes. Actor Akhilendra Mishra doesn't take a minute to credit it all to his continuing innings with Indian Theatre. "At times such as now, I like to quote a quotation I've made of my own," the actor says across telephone lines. We listen in eagerly. "An actor earns from theatre and spends it on himself," he says in crisp baritone. And we couldn't agree more. For Mishra, who first debuted on television as the caterpillar-eyebrowed Kroor Singh on Nirja Guleri's Chandrakanta as many as 12 years back, theatre has been his backbone.

"As much as I would have loved to do television, there was nothing that truly excited me. At the same time, today's television requires a lot of an actor's time," says Mishra who couldn't quite say no when approached by NDTV Imagine for their adaptation of Ramayana. "I have always wanted to play Ravana. Today, when programming on television is all about illegitimate relationships, it was a delight to be approached for a mythological show," admits the actor who prefers to communicate in unpolluted Hindi, which by the way is a delight to hear. And Mishra wasn't unaware of Ravana's true character. "Most people just know one aspect of his life. There's much more," he says adding, "I have always been impressed by him having read not just the Ramayana but Ravana Sanhita, which gives the true picture of the man who knew much before of his own death."

Having read all that he could lay his hands on, Akhilendra decided to give the character his best shot. "I am leading a satvik jeevan even while I shoot for the show," you hear him say. And all that hard work has paid off. "What's nice to see is that parents are getting their children to watch the show. There are many in this generation who haven't even heard the Ramayana, let alone read it," rues the actor who is happy to seethe resurgence of mythology on television. With Dussehra not too far away, how is the show gearing up. "As of now the fight between Lord Ram and Ravana has begun," says the onscreen Ravana. As for the actor Akhilendra Mishra, there are three films to look forward to. "First you'll get to see me play a small role in Goldie Behl's 'Drona'. Then I am shooting for Rakeysh Mehra's next," he lists them for us before mentioning, "I am associated with the IPTA group of theatre and I make it a point to do at least one or two plays a year. That's where I get my energy from."

While he's living his dream playing Ravana there's another character, not from Indian mythology but history that the actor would like to portray in any form of media. "And that's Maharana Pratap. That's a role I would love to essay," Mishra lets us know. Now that's a cue for producers!

Heading: It’s a spread! - Indian Express
Content:
City's Ayushman Khurrana has finally carved his space in big, bad Bombay

The last time we didn't meet him but spoke to him over the phone. That too from Mumbai. It's been long since we caught sight of city bred Ayushman Khurrana on home turf. "This visit comes after a year," tells Khurrana who was in town to kick-off the auditions for MTV Roadies' season six. No one knows the show better than Ayushman, who actually won the top spot a few years ago. "And life never really was the same after that," he twinkles back as we notice this boy from next door has grown up. "I feel it too," he laughs. Post his win on MTV, Ayushman took to RJing with Big FM in Delhi and never really looked back after that. "My stint as a radio jockey was a lot of fun. In fact I will never rule it out as a career option again. It's my insurance," he admits.

While radio jockeying took him to Mumbai, Ayushman turned VJ soon after. "I have been hosting a lot of shows since. There's Wassup and then I filled in for Nikhil Chinnappa on Super Select," lists out the VJ for us. Then there was the campus show 'MTV U' that saw Ayushman hop across various universities. So what's his latest? "You know I have always been associated with theatre. So now I am airing my acting talent by way of Fully Faltoo movies on MTV," answers Khurrana who will 'star' in 'Check De' and 'Jadoo Ek Bar', both of which are spoofs on the Bollywood flicks Chak De and Jodaa Akbar.

Given the acting move, will Bollywood be his next big step; we can't help but ask Ayushman who answers in his trademark funny style. "I am not headed towards Bollywood the Ranbir Kapoor way but definitely the Ranvir Sheorey way. Remember they used to do spoofs too," answers our man. As for the clichéd question one asks all successful Chandigarhians, we shoot one at Ayushman too. How has the transition from Chandigarh to Mumbai been? To this he smiles, takes his time and answers: "It wasn't as difficult as I thought it would be. In fact I have recently bought my own flat." That, is an accomplishment we agree. Here's looking to more home visits.

Heading: Police resort to lathicharge after students protest at GJU - Indian Express
Content:
This World Tourism Day, tuck into international food flavours

It couldn't be better timed. With the World Tourism Day falling over the weekend, September 27 to be precise, CITCO is making the most of it. And for a change they are going international. Rolling out this Saturday and Sunday will be an international food festival at Hotel Mountview that will bring in the likes of Mexican, Italian and Continental fare. If Italian fare excites you then expect to dig into the likes of 'Lamb Ala Pomodoro' which will bring in lamb that's been cooked over slow fire and then tossed with basil flavoured tomato concase. Then there's the uber popular 'Ratatouille' which is a vegetarian extravaganza with its All English vegetables tossed in garlic and then mixed with classic tomato concase sauce and herbs and spices covered with cheese and baked to the perfection. Speaking of Italian cuisine the chefs at the hotel have brought in a version of Lasagane too. But if you fond of all food baked then opt for the Continental fare here which will see 'Creole Fish', 'Summer Chicken', 'Cottage Cheese overlay' and 'Cauliflower Mornay'. The latter brings in a baked delicacy with florets of cauliflower mixed with mornay sauce, herbs and spices. Completing the global spread is Mexican fare with 'Polo Loco', 'Veg Tex Mex' and some Cottage Cheese Fajitas. According to CITCO's Managing Director Niharika Rai, the food festival will lay out the international cuisine in the form of a buffet priced at Rs 399 (inclusive of all taxes) per person. The two-day festival will be on all day till September 28 at Hotel Mountview.

Heading: IT is the way to women empowerment: Govt - Indian Express
Content:
Students wanted to install Bhagat Singh's statue near V-C office

The police today resorted to mild lathicharge after a group of students at the Guru Jambeshwar University protested against the university's decision to not allow a statue of Bhagat Singh in the university campus.

The scuffle started at 11:30 am, after the 50-odd students, led by Sandeep Chaudhary, a student of mass communication at the university, beat up a security man who stopped them from entering the main gate of the campus and forcibly entered the gate. They had brought a statue of Bhagat Singh and wanted to install it at the shopping complex located near the office of the vice-chancellor, permission for which, they said, had been denied by the university

authorities.

They disrupted the exams being held by tearing examination papers and raised slogans against the Pro V-C (students), who, they claimed, was behind the decision to not allow the statue.

However, no one was seriously injured in the incident. Sources said most of those invloved in the scuffle were outsiders.

The whole episode lasted for an hour and the statute of Bhagat Singh brought by the students was taken into possession by the police.

University authorities said the students never met the V-C to seek permission for the statue's installation. They said the executive council of the university was the body which had authority to give permission for installation of a statue, and that too, after taking prior permission from the Haryana government.

Vice-Chancellor Lt Gen (retd) DDS Sandhu said it was the handiwork of certain disgruntled elements who were trying to disturb the atmosphere of the campus.

"We have deep respect for Shaheed-e-Azam Bhagat Singh, but it is only the authority concerned that can take a decision in such matters," he added.

The Pro-VC (students) later met Sandhu and demanded strict action against student leader Sandeep Chaudhary.

Heading: BJP fails to reach consensus on alliance partner - Indian Express
Content:
Given its vast reach and usage, the Haryana government has planned to make use of information technology for the empowerment of women in the state.

A village-level programme for women and scheduled castes was launched through gram panchayats in a bid to prepare them for contribution towards the development of their villages. The programme, sponsored by the Central government for the Haryana Women and Child Development Department, is being executed by the Haryana State Electronics Development Corporation (Hartron).

About 200 women and girls, from the Sakshar Mahila Samoohs (SMSs), and village-level NGOs of ten districts of the state, have already been trained in computer fundamentals, typing and data-punching.

A senior officer of Hartron said that on completion of their training programmes, these women and girls would help collect and store data at the village-level to help the gram panchayats in planning and execution of various projects and schemes in a scientific manner.

In all, 800 women and girls, two from each SMS, nominated by the Haryana Women and Child Development Department, are to be trained in four batches in a year. Each course, being conducted at the e-Education franchisee centres of Hartron in the ten districts, are of three months duration. The classes are for two hours daily, five days a week. Not only does the course come free of costs, but as an incentive, they are being provided a monthly stipend of Rs 500 each.

At present, about 6,000 SMSs are registered in the state, each comprising of 25 to 60 educated women and girls, whose qualifications range from matric to MA. This organised pool of educated women and girls in the villages are not only helping generate awareness on key issues of sex ratio, literacy, health and sanitation, but also contributing to social audit, which is absolutely necessary to improve delivery at the grassroot level.

Hartron has also taken upon itself the task of imparting six months computer training to about 8000 scheduled castes students from government colleges in the state with a view to empower them for getting employment or self employment.

The training is being provided free of cost by the Department of Higher Education. The department has decided to provide a computer, UPS and printer to those who secure 40 per cent marks in the university examination and 60 per cent marks in computer skills.

Heading: Court stops work at ropeway site in Jakhoo - Indian Express
Content:
No consensus on the choice of a partner for the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls could be reached at the BJP state executive meeting held at Sonepat today, under the chairmanship of Haryana BJP incharge Vijay Goel. However, sources say, majority of the leaders seemed to support an alliance with the Indian National Lok Dal (INLD).

Venkaiah Naidu, who was scheduled to attend the meeting, could not make it due to an engagement in New Delhi.

Ram Kumar Gautam, BJP's Leader of the House in the Haryana Vidhan Sabha, agreed there was differences in the party leaders on the issue of selecting an alliance partner. It was decided that it would be left to the party high command to give a final decision, he said.

"Majority of the leaders seemed inclined towards an alliance with the INLD and some even favoured a pact with the newly-formed Haryana Janhit Congress of Kuldeep Bishnoi," said Gautam.

"Personally, I am in favour of the party going it alone in the polls instead of selecting a partner. Everyone knows the bitter experience of the past,'' he added.

Rekha Sharma, BJP leader from Panchkula, said the meeting was "fruitful", though no decision was reached. The partymen were asked to respect the feelings of workers as they were the backbone of the party, she said. The party high command was likely to make its choice on the partner issue by the end of the month.

Heading: Rs 3,100 cr investment cleared - Indian Express
Content:
A Civil Court in Shimla today ordered stopping of all excavation, digging and construction activity at the Jakhoo Ropeway site, constructed by Jagson International, till the promoter takes precautionary steps to protect the ecology and local houses from larger damage.

The order was given by Senior Civil Judge-I on the petition filed by Sanjeev Kuthiala for permanent prohibition and mandatory injunction. Kuthiala, resident of Jakhoo, lives in one of the houses that is under threat by the construction activity at the site.

"The Municipal Corporation had issued stop orders on the site of the ropeway couple of days ago, but the contractor and the promoter company did not pay heed and the MC also seemed to turn a blind eye," said Kuthiala. The work on the site was on during the day on Friday too.

The petition was filed against Managing Director of Jagson International, Contractor and Site In-charge.

According to Kuthiala, on the north side three hotels in the vicinity, Shivalik, Woodland and Atihi and 20 government buildings above the site, housing about 100 families were endangered.

While on the right side government buildings housing seven families and another house with four families are under threat.

The company should adopt safety measures and build retaining walls along the sliding area and embankments along the trees that stand in danger zone. On Thursday, after the intervention of forest secretary, the forest officials were asked to ensure that no heavy machinery is deployed in the area for excavation till protective structures are put in place.

Heading: Modi’s profit-sharing dream runs into rough weather: Aggrieved investors may knock on SEBI, court doors - Indian Express
Content:
Dispelling fear of a possible slow down in the investment climate, Himachal Pradesh government today cleared at least 18 projects worth Rs 3,100 crore, of which a biggest and innovative project proposal is of Solaryan Technologies with an investment of Rs 2,400 crore.

The project to be set-up by a Delhi-based company is expected to provide job avenues to hundreds of persons. This will be an environment-friendly project designed to produce a different product for the markets, both within and outside India.

The projects were cleared at a meeting of state-level Single Window Clearance and Monitoring Authority, held here today. Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal presided over.

An important project cleared today include Rs 400 crore investment proposal of M/S Indorama Industries.The company already has some units in Himachal Pradesh. Other prestigious industrial houses such as Pidilite Industries, Meditech Garments of the Advantage Organic Naturals Technologies and Crew BOS Products have also received the government nod for major investments.

The Meditech Garments will set up its unit in Dochi area of Solan district to manufacture special type of garments. Patiala Industrial Investment company has also been given approval for a tractor unit in Baddi industrial area for its Rs 20 crore project and Pritika has chosen Una district for investing Rs 58 core to manufacture auto and tractor spare parts.

During the meeting Chief Minister said he had taken up the matter with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and Union Finance Minister P.Chidamabaram for extending the industrial package upto 2013, as was originally planned in 2003. "The government has given reasons why the package requires to be extended in the larger interest of the country and state," he added.

Chief Minister said a large number of investors have shown interest in investing in Himachal despite pressures mounted by the neighbouring states asking the centre not to extend the package beyond 2010.

"Himachal Pradesh started late in the industrial development but has created basic infrastructure for the investors," he added.

Dhumal said the government would consider authorisation to the Director of Industries to apply for permission to purchase the land under Section 118 on behalf of the approved industrial units to save time. The investors can start construction work and resume productions.

However, for non-serious investors, the government has decided to issue notices so that others can take-up projects at the sites occupied by them. He said a labour officer would also be posted in Baddi to motivate the youth to find suitable job in the industrial sector.The state has a provision of 70 percent employment for the locals.Dhumal proposed to approach the centre with a proposal to construct labour hostels in the industrial areas.

Heading: GUJCOC, the new bone of contention between BJP, Cong - Indian Express
Content:
Aggrieved investors are reportedly planning to approach SEBI and move the courts against those Gujarat-based Public Sector Enterprises that have agreed to set aside part of their Profit Before Tax (PBT) for Corporate Social Responsibility. They have said the move violates the rights of minority stakeholders.

Sources have said that the Chief Minister's vision to accelerate social development in Gujarat from funds raised as compulsory contributions from the cash-rich PSEs have not gone down well even with a section of his most ardent supporters. They have said while his motive is right, the manner in which he has gone about scripting the state's social upliftment is being questioned.

The Gujarat Industrial Power Corporation Limited (GIPCL) and the Gujarat Mineral development Corporation (GMDC) have already ceded to the proposal to cough up a maximum 30 per cent of their PBTs to the Gujarat Socio-Economic Development Society (GSEDS) headed by the CM himself. The other four PSEs are expected to formally do the same at their AGMs over the next few days.

Besides the stiff resistance from investors, the announcement has also caused an almost 25 to 30 per cent erosion in the value of the scrips of these PSEs in less than a month.

A top broker of the city said there has been a bear run on the shares of the six PSEs over the past month ever since the proposal was made public. "The Gujarati investors were banking on Narendra Modi's track record in the economic arena where under his stewardship many loss-making PSEs like GSFC were nursed back to health. They had invested heavily in these blue-chip companies and are now booking their losses," he said.

It is also feared that the move might set a dangerous precedent, which the till-now popular BJP government might have to regret. Gujarati investors are not only the most discerning and market-savvy in the country, but are also the largest in terms of sheer numbers, they said.

"Never in the history of PSEs has there been such misuse of its majority status by a state government," said an agitated investor. Even within the ruling party's state rank and file, murmurs of dissent are now getting audible against the way the government is forcing its decision on the hapless managements of state run PSEs, he added.

According to the broker, there is a widespread feeling that this enforced Corporate Social Responsibility will erode the profitability of these companies and hurt the investors.

But it is not the small retail investors alone who are losing confidence in these companies. Even mutual funds, which had earlier evinced keen interest in ploughing funds especially in blue-chip companies like GMDC, are now doing a re-think.

"We feel this move will affect the company's long-term profitability and this in turn will affect its expansion plans," said a senior executive of a leading MF house. The share price of the GMDC scrip, which was hovering around Rs 264 in the last week of August, has dipped by almost 30 per cent to Rs 165 on Thursday, he said.

Irked investors are also crying foul over the government's rationale for utilising the PBT for social causes.

Heading: Blast accused says he was in ‘D’ Company of don’s aide - Indian Express
Content:
Cong says Centre has enacted laws more stringent than those in BJP's pet Bill, Saffron party says Bill would have been a deterrent for blasts

The state Assembly on Friday witnessed a war of words between the ruling BJP and the Opposition Congress over an official resolution moved in the House by the government urging the Centre to clear the GUJCOC Bill at the earliest.

Leader of the Opposition Shaktisinh Gohil initiated the debate on the resolution and accused the BJP government of politicising the issue of terrorism by raising the pitch on the controversial Bill.

"Only laws will not help stem terrorist activity. What is needed is the political will of the government to curb this menace. The provisions made in the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act enacted by the Centre are more stringent than the ones in the GUJCOC Bill. The state government can use these provisions of the Central Act," he said.

He said it was the previous BJP-led NDA regime that had not cleared the GUJCOC Bill, adding that it was the then Union Home Minister L K Advani who had sent it back to Gujarat.

"The Bill was passed in the Assembly on March 26, 2003, but the then Governor had sent it to the NDA government for Presidential assent. The Bill was not cleared and sent back to the Assembly Secretariat.

"Later, when the Congress came to power at the Centre, the state government passed the Bill again with certain amendments by a voice vote and sent it back to the Centre for clearance, just to draw a political mileage out of it, Gohil said.

He said the erstwhile BJP-led NDA government, and even the incumbent UPA regime had a reason not to clear the Bill. He said the provisions mentioned in the Bill directly clashed with the Central Acts like the Indian Evidence Act, 1972, the Transfer of Properties Act and the Criminal Procedure Act.

"Chief Minister Narendra Modi often makes public statements boasting that he is brave enough to fight terrorism. But when terrorists really strike, he starts blaming others and playing politics with GUJCOC," Gohil said.

Participating in the debate, senior Congress MLA Sidhdharth Patel said there were certain objectionable clauses, which might be misused if the Bill is cleared by the Centre. These include, considering as evidence in the court confessional statement made by an accused before the police, non-granting of bail to the accused for six months and a provision seeking extension of police remand of the accused up to 30 days.

Emphasising the need for legislation like GUJCOC, BJP member Shankar Chaudhary said it was due to the non-clearance of the Bill by the UPA government that serial blasts took place in Ahmedabad, killing innocent people. There are stringent provisions in the Bill that will help the government check terrorist activity in the state, he said.

Earlier, Gohil made a vain bid to thwart the government's resolution on GUJCOC by raising a point of order in the House. He argued that since the matter is sub-judice it cannot be discussed in the Assembly. He said the Gujarat High Court is still seized with the matter following a petition by an NGO.

This was countered by Minister of State for Home Amit Shah who contended that the matter was not sub-judice, for it was only at the admission stage in the High Court.

Giving his ruling after hearing arguments and counter arguments, Speaker Ashok Bhatt said GUJCOC resolution could be debated in the House. He said the High Court has still not admitted the matter and rejected Gohil's point of order.

Moving the resolution in the Assembly, Shah further underlined the need for a strong legislation like GUJCOC to curb organised crimes in a border state like Gujarat. Such legislation becomes more relevant and important especially in the wake of serial blasts in Ahmedabad, he said, urging the Centre to clear the Bill at the earliest. Later, the resolution was passed in the House by a majority.

Heading: Bank strike: Operations affected for second day in a row - Indian Express
Content:
Afzal Usmani arrested on Sept 24 confesses to his links with Fazl-ur-Rehman, who ran Dawood Ibrahim's extortion racket in Gujarat, Maharashtra from the Middle East

This could perhaps be the first link between the perpetrators of the July 26 Ahmedabad serial blasts and the underworld.

Afzal Usmani, one of the five arrested by the Mumbai police on Wednesday, has confessed to his links to Fazl-ur-Rehman, the notorious gangster, who was earlier handling an extortion racket in Gujarat and Maharashtra at the behest of underworld don Dawood Ibrahim.

Joint Commissioner of Police Ashish Bhatia, who interrogated Usmani, said: "He has confessed to having worked for the Fazl-ur-Rehman gang since 2002. He was introduced to the gang in 2002 by Riyaz Batkal, a close aide of Fazl-ur-Rehman. He was also involved in some extortion and murder cases, which he committed at the behest of Batkal. In 2005, the Mumbai police arrested Usmani and Batkal in a case of extortion and released them in 2008."

According to the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB), Usmani played a key role in stealing four cars from Navi Mumbai, which were later used in the two massive blasts at the L G Hospital and the Civil Hospital. The other two cars loaded with explosives, were later recovered by the Surat police. In fact, Usmani had first delivered the cars in Surat and then in Ahmedabad.

"Usmani and Atif Ameen, who was killed in an encounter in New Delhi recently, had supervised the fitting of explosives in the two cars that exploded in Ahmedabad. Usmani had been assisted in the theft by two others, who are yet to be arrested," said Bhatia.

According to the police, Rehman belongs to Bihar, who later established links with Dawood Ibrahim in Mumbai and began handling his extortion racket from the Middle East. He was, however, deported to India, and is presently lodged at the Tihar Jail in New Delhi.

He is also involved in many cases of extortion and kidnapping in Gujarat, which include the abduction of a well-known industrialist in the Sarkhej area of Ahmedabad and the Bhaskar-Paresh kidnapping case of Rajkot.

Heading: We know what happened six yrs ago: kin of Godhra accused to tell all on streets - Indian Express
Content:
Banking operations in the state remained affected for the second day on Friday with a majority of public sector banks remaining closed in response to a call for a nationwide strike.

"Cheques worth Rs 800-900 crore could not be cleared today due to the strike," said a senior official at the Bank of Baroda 's (BoB's) , Magnetic Ink Cheque Recognition (MICR) centre.

"Due to the nationwide strike, cheques worth Rs 450 crore of various branches could not be presented for clearing in the last two days," a State Bank of India clearing house official said.

However, a senior RBI official at the clearing house claimed that over 50 banks participated in cheque clearance operations today and cheques worth Rs 520 crore presented by them were cleared in the city. Over 34 banks did not participate in clearing house operations, he added.

"Alternative arrangements for clearing of cheques at leading private sector banks by RBI in certain major cities of the state like Vadodara, Surat and Rajkot continued today," a senior RBI official said.

Heading: Bomb threat keeps Surat cops on their toes - Indian Express
Content:
A motley group of actors trying to challenge the Nanavati Commission Report, tabled at the Gujarat Vidhan Sabha on Thursday, are planning a series of streetplays titled Halla Bol.

Incidentally, all the actors working in the play are the kin of the 25 of the 106 arrested in connection with the Godhra train burning incident of 2002, which killed 59 karsevaks on board the Sabarmati Express.

Newsline caught up with the team during their rehearsal at Godhra, as the actors put in final touches to take the play all the way to Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. Interestingly, the play doesn't have a director and everybody chips in with their own innovative ideas.

"For the last six years, I ran from pillar to post asking everyone what my brother had done. The police took him away one-day because someone mentioned his name. I know he is innocent, but people don't believe it. Be it the human rights activists, mediapersons or government officials, all of them patiently listen to our stories but nothing comes out of it. The truth must be made public, not just by clearing the names of people accused of involvement in the incident, but also about what their relatives like us have been through," said Maqsood Hathila, brother of advocate Ruhul Amin Hathila, who has been arrested under POTA.

The play comprises three parts. It shows how the incident took place, from the perspective of the eyewitnesses who have testified in front of the investigation teams. "The first part shows, where exactly the so called witnesses were when the tragedy occurred. Then it goes on to show what the investigators have missed out," said Shoaib Jujaia, brother of the Ibrahim Charkha, who was recently granted bail after he developed bone tuberculosis in 2005 while in Sabarmati Jail.

The first part also shows infighting among various groups in the Godhra Municipal Corporation. "We consider them as the original culprits and we are not afraid to portray their roles in the play because we have, over the last so many years, seen how opportunistic they become when it comes to pursuing a communal agenda," he said.

Shoaib, a government school teacher said: "In the second part, we have shown how the arrests were made overnight. Be it the Railway Police or the Godhra police or the district sessions court judges, we are showing how they failed to protect people, even those who were on the fateful S-6 coach." He said the final or the third part shows the hardships faced by the kin of those arrested by the authorities.

Interestingly, two women, whose husbands are booked under POTA, are also acting in the play. "One is my brother's wife, Zarina [name changed] and the other is the daughter of one of the accused. Zarina will be playing the role of a controversial district sessions court judge while the daughter will play Zarina's role. We are also showing an imaginary conversation between Zarina and Sonia Gokani, where two women face other on the day of redemption," Maqsood added. Other characters to be featured in the play include a former Deputy Superintendent of Police and Chief Minister Narendra Modi himself.

Around 25 people will be in the cast to perform the plays.

He added: "We are not educated and have run out of all resources, but we need to tell the truth to the people, even if it is uncomfortable."

Asked why the team decided to call their play "Halla Bol", Maqsood and Shoaib said that the late theatre activist Safdar Hashmi was killed while enacting a play by the same name in New Delhi during the late 1980s. Hashmi had tried to bring out the nexus between the politicians and the local criminals, and here they are trying to bring out the facts in the Godhra incident.

"We cannot afford to don the roles of terrorists and take up guns against the state. It is not right. We will like it if they arrest us and put us in jail, now that most of us do not have an alternative. With these street plays, we will make our voice heard," said Maqsood.

"We knew this was going to happen, but it has not deterred us. We will be more strong and vocal about what we have been going through. Now our only hope is the Supreme Court and the Special Investigation Team headed by former CBI chief R K Raghavan," he added.

Heading: Woman found murdered, cops suspect husband’s hand - Indian Express
Content:
The letter also threatened to carry out a blast at the Income Tax office, indoor stadium and Chowpaty in the coming days

The Surat police received a call threatening of a bomb at the Trade House Complex in Nanpura area on Friday afternoon. However, it soon turned out to be a hoax. A quick search revealed a parcel box that contained a threat letter, a deo-spray bottle with some white powder, electric wires, nails and a wrist watch.

The police said some unknown person had made a phone call to the Parth Enterprise office at the third floor of the Trade House Complex in Nanpura on Friday.

The caller informed shop owner Parimal Joshi about four live bombs that had been planted in the complex at different places. The caller also asked Joshi to come out of the office and check for himself near the garbage bin on the passage that he was not bluffing.

Joshi said: "I had just entered my office and was doing puja when the phone rang. The caller told me that bombs had been planted in the complex and will explode soon. When I told him not to joke, he got angry and told me to come out of the office and see the parcel kept near the garbage bin. I was shocked after seeing the parcel and informed the police. I have noted down the number from which the call was made as I have caller-ID facility on my landline phone."

He said the caller spoke in Hindi and seemed to be around 30 years of age.

The Athwalines police and the Bomb Disposal Squad rushed to the spot and carefully took the parcel to an open ground in nearby area.

According to the police, the letter, which was written in Gujarati and Hindi, said this was the fourth bomb and three others were still in the complex at different places and will explode soon. The letter also threatened to carry out a blast at the Income Tax office, indoor Stadium and Chowpaty in the coming days.

Later, the police made different teams and started a search operation in the complex till late in the evening but did not find anything. Forensic Science Laboratory officers also arrived at the spot and took samples for analysis.

Athwalines Inspector M P Patel said: "Somebody has played a mischief by attaching some wires and a wrist watch to using a deo-spray bottle. The caller intended to spread panic. We have checked the phone number and found that it has been made from a coin operated phone at Anand Hospital in Nanpura."

Heading: Weight of dues: Industrial houses owe nearly Rs 2,500 cr sales-tax to state govt - Indian Express
Content:
A 45-year-old woman was found murdered in her house at Ramnagar in Udhna on Friday afternoon. According to the police, the deceased, Chandrika Tailor, had been tied with a rope and her throat slit.

The police said the victim's son, Nirmal (20) came back from the college and found his mother lying dead on the floor of her bedroom. He then informed his father Chandu and brother Abhishek.

Chandu, who runs a tailoring shop in Pandesara immediately rushed to his house. Abhishek also came home after sometime.

Udhna police rushed to the spot after learning about the incident and sent the body to the New Civil Hospital for a post-mortem.

The police have ruled out robbery or theft as the motive behind the murder. They suspect that Chandu might be involved in the crime. The police said Chandu had an affair with a woman staying near his shop in Pandesara.

The couple had regular quarrels over this issue. Chandrika had warned Chandu to end the relationship, but he was continuing with it. Apparently, Chandrika once even went to the woman's house and scolded her in this regard.

Assistant Commissioner of Police B division M V Mehta, said: "Chandu and his two sons left for work early in the morning and Chandrika was all alone in the house. We found that there were some injuries on her body, which suggests that she had tried to defend herself before the murder. Her throat was slit, which led to her death."

He added: "The motive behind the murder is still not known as nothing is missing from the house. We suspect that Chandu might be involved in the murder as the couple had regular quarrels."

Heading: Deputy Speaker’s vacant chair stirs a hornet’s nest in state Assembly - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 47 industrial houses across Gujarat have still not paid their sales-tax dues to the government, which amounts to a whopping Rs 2,482.86 crore. Among these, the maximum amount of ST dues has been pending against B G Exploration (Rs 905.27 crore) and Essar Steel Units 1 and 2 (Rs 660.25 crore).

In a written reply to a non-starred question asked by Congress MLA Bavkubhai Undhad and tabled in the House on Thursday, Finance Minister Vajubhai Vala said that as on February 7, 2008 these industrial houses owe the state government sales-tax dues to the tune of Rs 2,482.86 crore. He also said that the government has initiated the process of recovery and not given any relief package to these industries either.

Besides B G Exploration and Essar Steel, the other private as well as public sector companies that owe ST dues to the government are: ONGC (Rs 227.60 cr), Reliance Industries (Rs 111.21 cr), Saurashtra Cement (Rs 68.95 cr), Gujarat Sidhdhi Cement (Rs 49.77 cr), Gujarat Alkalies and Chemicals Ltd (Rs 47.32 cr), H M P Cement (Rs 44.59 cr), Crompton Greaves Ltd (Rs 41.51 cr), Searchchem Industries (33.78 cr), Triveni Industries (Rs 30.31 cr) and Tata Chemicals (Rs 5.12 cr).

Heading: Self-financed pharmacy courses get costlier by 30 per cent - Indian Express
Content:
Opp says Speaker should have ensured his deputy's appointment

The issue of appointment of Deputy Speaker reverberated in the state assembly on Friday, with Leader of the Opposition Shaktisinh Gohil stating that it was the responsibility of the Speaker to ensure that his deputy was appointed on time.

Gohil said that the post of Deputy Speaker traditionally went uncontested to the Opposition. He added that the Speaker should have ensured that the Deputy Speaker was appointed soon after the new Assembly was constituted.

Gohil raised this issue with regard to the appointment of the Petition Committee of the Assembly, which is always headed by the Deputy Speaker. However, this time, in the absence of a Deputy Speaker, a BJP legislator had been appointed as the chairman of this seven-member committee.

Speaker Ashok Bhatt was, however, quick to brush off the allegations and said that he had already appointed Narayan Patel as chairman of the Petition Committee and the appointment of Deputy Speaker was the responsibility of the House.

It may be remembered that before Narendra Modi took over as the Chief Minister, the Deputy Speaker in the state Assembly was selected from among the members of the Opposition. However, this tradition was dropped once Modi became the CM in 2001.

Later on, talking to Newsline, Gohil said that as per the rules of the Assembly, the Deputy Speaker should be appointed after every Assembly election, but before the new Assembly is constituted. "This rule was not being followed for the last two terms since Modi came to power,' he said.

Senior congress MLA and chief spokesperson of Gujarat Pradesh Congress Committee Arjun Modhwadia said that leaving the Deputy Speaker's post vacant was not only undemocratic but also amounted to taking away the rights of the Opposition. He alleged that the Deputy Speaker's post had been deliberately left vacant so as to rob the Opposition of this privilege.

Heading: 129 industrial units to become pollution-free by March next - Indian Express
Content:
New fee structure to range between Rs 42,000 and Rs 65,000

The Justice R J Shah (Retired) Fees, Admission and NRI Committee on Thursday decided to increase the fee of the self-financed institutes (SFI) offering pharmacy courses by up to 30 per cent for the academic year 2008-09, 2009-10 and 2010-11.

Till now, the fee for SFIs offering courses in Pharmacy was between Rs 32,000 and Rs 45,000. The revised fee, however, will range between Rs 42,000 and Rs 65,000.

The Committee also declared the new fee structure of eight Diploma Pharmacy SFIs. The new fee will be somewhere between Rs 22,000-32,000.

Out of the 71 SFIs, which offer courses in Pharmacy in Gujarat, the fee structure for 68 SFIs has been declared.

While the fee structure for two SFIs, Gitanjali Pharmacy College in Sabarkantha and Shri Samanvay Institute of Pharmacy in Botad, has been kept the same at Rs 32,000, the Committee is yet to finalise the fee of the remaining one SFI.

The students, who took admission in the academic year 2008-09, have to pay the fees as per today's new structure. Around 4,500 students will be affected by the new development.

The new fee structure is categorised into nine ranges. The Institute of Pharmacy, Nirma University, Ahmedabad is the only SFI which falls under the maximum range i.e. Rs 65,000.

Three SFIs fall under the second range of Rs 62,000, while seven come under the third range of Rs 60,000. The fourth range of Rs 57,000 has been kept for two SFIs, the fifth range of Rs 54,000 for four SFIs and the sixth range of Rs 51,000 for four SFIs.

Seventeen SFIs fall under the seventh range of Rs 48,000, nine under the eight range of Rs 45,000 and 20 under the ninth range of Rs 42,000.

Heading: Carcass of lioness found in Gir sanctuary - Indian Express
Content:
To make the city pollution free, about 129 industrial units of the city have decided to comply with the norms set up by the Air Action Plan — launched in the city on World Environment Day in 2004 — by March next year.

The Supreme Court-appointed Environment Pollution Control Authority (EPCA), under the chairmanship of Bhure Lal, had approved the overall strategy of the action plan, under which, the industries will have to replace the old multi-cyclone system with electrostatic precipitators and bag filters, to control the emission levels.

Sanjeey Tyagi, Member Secretary of the Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB), said the replacements will be carried out in three phases. "In the first phase, we have covered 32 industries. Around 57 will be covered in the second phase. We intend to cover the remaining 40 by March 2009."

He added that the level of respirable suspended particulate matter (RSPM) has dropped to 82 micro-gram per cubic metre in 2008 as compared to 198 micro-gram per cubic metre in 2001.

"Our aim is to further reduce the RSPM level to below 60. With CNG auto-rickshaws already in place and the BRTS due to be opened shortly, we are hopeful of achieving our goal," said Tyagi.

Continuous efforts have worked wonders and the city, which was ranked as the fourth most-polluted city in India in 2004, has slipped to the fiftieth rank in 2008.

About 500 foundry units of the city that are a major cause of pollution are also being made non-polluting by making use of the scrubbing technology, developed by the

L D College of Engineering.

This technology serves the dual purpose of a heat exchanger as well as a dust collector.

Emissions have also been controlled at the Sabarmati Thermal Power Station, said K C Mistry, Regional Officer GPCB, Ahmedabad.

Mistry added that there are five more power projects in the region that are virtually smokeless. "The pollution caused due to the solid fuels consumption by these projects has seen a steep decline in recent years," he said.

As part of the action plan, the GPCB has stationed 17 ambient air quality monitoring stations all over the city, at the designated height of 12- to-5 feet to record the pollution levels in Ahmedabad.

The GPCB, which happens to be the coordination agency, and the AMC, AUDA, RTO, GSRTC, AMTS, police commissioner, district collector, Oil Companies, GSPC, GIDC and NIOH, that are the implementing agencies — have taken several measures to make the industries and city pollution-free. Some of the them include: include pre-mixing of 2T lubricating oil, special drives to check quality of petrol at stations, a special charter for industries in Ahmedabad to control air pollution, mandatory compliance to Bharat Stage norms for all vehicles, smooth traffic management; and constructing common effluent treatment plants and secured landfill sites for solid waste management in the industrial estates of Naroda, Vatva and Odhav.

Heading: Youth strangled by minor girl’s mother, relatives - Indian Express
Content:
The carcass of a lioness was found in a highly decomposed state at the Gir sanctuary on Friday. According to forest officials, the decomposed state of the animal suggests that it might have died at least 5-6 days ago.

However, the skull, bones and claws of the big cat were recovered intact. Forest officers have ruled out foul play saying that the animal's death was natural.

Officials said that the lioness was about six-years-old. The carcass was recovered from Chikhalkuva forest settlement village, which falls under the Jashadhar forest range in the Gir sanctuary.

When contacted, deputy conservator of forest (Gir East) S M Raja, said: "The carcass was recovered from the outskirts of Chikhalkuva village. A post mortem was not possible as the viscera of the animal had decomposed almost completely. However, we have sent the soil sample collected from the spot to the Forensic Science Laboratory for clinical examination."

Heading: Johri says she will file her reply before SC soon - Indian Express
Content:
A 19-year-old youth from Hansalpur village of Viramgam Taluka of Ahmedabad district was allegedly strangled by the mother and relatives of a minor girl he was in love with, on Thursday afternoon.

Viramgam police have registered a case of murder under provisions of the IPC against four persons and investigations are on to nab them.

A complaint has been registered in this regard with the police by Lilaben Thakor, sister of the deceased youth, Vishnu Thakor. The four accused have been identified as Manju Thakor, Vikram Thakor, Dhiru Thakor and Meru Thakor.

According to the Viramgam police, the youth was in love with the daughter of Manju Thakor, one of the accused. The incident occured on Thursday afternoon when Manju's daughter, Vandana (name changed), went to meet Vishnu on the pretext of visiting some of her friends.

"When Vandana did not return home for quite some time, Manju went into the village in her search, where she found them sitting in a house. She first slapped Vandana and then, asked her to go home. She then summoned some of her relatives and strangled Vishnu with the help of a rope," said police sub-inspector R K Prajapati who is investigating the case.

Prajapati said that the accused tried to mislead the police by hanging the body from a ceiling fan. "But we have strong evidence in the form of an eye-witness against the accused and can prove that it is a murder," he added.

Heading: Government decides on committee for integrated development of metros - Indian Express
Content:
A day after being accused in the Supreme Court (SC) of allegedly letting down the probe in the 2005 Sohrabuddin Sheikh fake encounter killing, CID Inspector General of Police Geetha Johri said that she would file her reply before the apex court soon.

"These are allegations and I will file my reply before the Supreme Court soon," Johri told Newsline.

Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Gopal Subramaniam had on Thursday alleged that Johri had "let down" the probe being monitored by the Supreme Court, by 'conniving with the state to create false records'.

Subramaniam, an amicus curiae (a lawyer assisting the court) in the matter, urged the court to hand over the investigation to the CBI.

In May 2007, the court had refused a CBI inquiry and accepted a plea from Subramaniam and the victims' family to entrust the supervision of the probe to Johri. They had argued that she was deliberately removed by the Gujarat government to protect suspended IPS officer D G Vanzara and his subordinate Rajkumar Pandiyan.

Sohrabuddin Sheikh was killed in an alleged fake encounter on November 26, 2005, by a joint-team of the Gujarat Anti Terrorist Squad and the Special Task Force of Rajasthan Police. His wife Kausarbi went missing after the incident. The Gujarat government later accepted before the Supreme Court that Kausarbi was also killed and her body disposed off by the accused. A total of 13 policemen were arrested in the case.

Heading: Bhavnagar municipality clears alleged encroachment by Asaram Bapu - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has decided to set up a "Metropolitan Planning Committee" in each of the four major municipal corporations of Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Surat and Rajkot for the integrated development of infrastructure and environmental conservation in these metro areas.

An official Bill — the Gujarat Metropolitan Planning Committees Bill — was passed unanimously to this effect in the state Assembly on Friday. Each of the metropolitan planning committees will prepare the draft development plan for its respective metro area and forward it to the state government for the final approval.

Moving the Bill in the House, Urban Development Minister Nitin Patel said a planning committee will be set up in the metropolitan area having a population of 10 lakh or more. He said it will consist of two or more municipalities, panchayats or other contiguous areas for taking up infrastructure development activities there. The government will set up these committees as mandated in Article 243 ZE of the Constitution, he added.

Patel said each of the planning committees will take into account the plans to be prepared by municipalities and panchayats located in a metropolitan area, and also consider matters of common interest between these local bodies. These will include co-ordinated spatial planning of the area, sharing of water and other physical and natural resources, besides the integrated infrastructure development and environmental measures.

The chairperson of a planning committee will be a minister to be nominated by the government. The municipal commissioner, the district collector and the district development officer concerned will be its ex-officio members, while the mayor of the civic body and president of the district panchayat concerned will be its members, he added. He said the chief executive officer of the urban development authority concerned will be its member secretary.

Patel told the House that the government will also include persons with expertise in the fields of economics, planning, finance, engineering and administration, and also elected members from local bodies, in the planning committees. The MLAs representing constituencies falling under the metropolitan areas will be permanent invitees to the committees.

"The government proposes to have minimum of 30 and maximum 45 members on each of the committees," he said.

Dispelling the doubts of the Opposition members, the minister clarified that the functioning of the urban development authorities or municipal corporations in each of the four major cities will not be affected by the decision to set up these planning committees there. In fact, the office of each of the UDAs will serve as the secretariat of the committee.

Participating in the debate on the Bill, Leader of the Opposition Shaktisnh Gohil of the Congress suggested that the government should also induct the Opposition leader of a municipal corporation in the planning committees. The government should also constitute a sub-committee of MLAs to supervise and monitor the functioning of metropolitan planning committees, Gohil added. The minister said the government will consider these suggestions.

Heading: Sohrabuddin ‘encounter’ case: Prosecution says it’s a conspiracy, defence refuses it outright - Indian Express
Content:
The Bhavnagar Municipality on Friday cleared an alleged encroachment by the Asaram Bapu Ashram in Sindhunagar area of the city. On Thursday, Gujarat Minister for State (Home) Amit Shah had washed the government's hands off land allocation to the Ashram on the floor of the House.

Bhavnagar Municipal Commissioner P M Sharma said: "We cleared some illegal encroachment by the Ashram today in the presence of the local police. The land was given to one Modh Brahman Gnati Sanstha for constructing a boys' hostel in 1977, but was usurped by the Ashram authorities." Sharma added that the Ashram authorities had constructed a compound wall and a few rooms and had earlier refused to vacate the land.

"Today, we demolished the land and handed over the possession to the Sanstha. Though there was a minor resistance from the people, everything finally went off peacefully," he added.

Bhavnagar Police Superintendent Manoj Shashidharan said: "The Municipal Corporation cleared the illegal encroachment by the Asaram Ashram in the Sindhunagar area of the city today. We did have some bandobast in place for the same. Some people did gather at the spot, but there was no untoward incident during the process."

Asaram Ashram administrator Udai Sanghani denied the Ashram's involvement in the entire episode.

"I have been told about the demolition of some temple in Bhavnagar, but prima facie our Ashram was not directly involved with this," he added.

Heading: Chance of Tatas staying back slim, admits Buddha - Indian Express
Content:
The framing of charges in the Sohrabuddin Sheikh fake encounter case moved a step further, with both prosecution and the defence making their opening statements before the Ahmedabad City District and Sessions Court.

Thirteen policemen including suspended IPS officer D G Vanzara and Rajasthan Cadre IPS officer Dinesh M N are charged with the murder of Sohrabudin in the guise of a fake encounter in Ahmedabad in November 26, 2005.

Appearing before the court, special public prosecutor V P Atre contended that there was enough evidence and record to establish that there was a conspiracy planned by the accused that ultimately led to Sohrabuddin's death. The special public prosecutor said that bringing Sohrabuddin from Hyderabad to eliminate him in a fake encounter was a part of the conspiracy.

In their opening statements, the defence lawyers refused to accept the charge of murder foisted upon the policemen. They also objected to charging the accused for the murder of Sohrabuddin's wife Kauserbi.

Kauserbi was allegedly killed and her body disposed between November 28 and 29. The defence lawyers pleaded before the court that charging the accused policemen with the murder of Kauserbi was premature and there was no direct evidence to bolster the charge.

They further said that accepting the charge of murder will go against the court's recent order, which has asked the investigating agency to further investigate certain aspects relating to Kauserbi's death.

The case is next slated for hearing on October 3, when the charges are likely to be framed.

Heading: Bloc ‘Carry’ grudge over CM’s order: ministers to boycott work - Indian Express
Content:
