At a CPM secretariat meeting held on Friday morning at Allimuddin Street, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee told party colleagues that the chance of the Tatas staying back in Bengal and operating in Singur were very slim.

Nonetheless, the government would try its level best to keep the Nano project in the state.

Emerging from the meeting, Commerce and Industries Minister Nirupam Sen said the chief minister had appealed to the Tatas to stay on in Singur.

"You will not encounter any problems in continuing work at Singur. There are adequate security arrangements. If needed, security can be increased," said Sen, quoting from the Chief Minister's letter to Ratan Tata.

In his letter, the chief Minister has tried to convince the Tatas that an overwhelming number people from West Bengal want the Nano project to stay.

Apart from Bhattacharjee, Sen and Left Front chairman Biman Bose have also appealed to the Tatas on the same lines.

"The opinion of a handful of people cannot be held as the ultimate decision," said Sen, "out of 13,000 dispossessed farmers, 11,000 had accepted compensation. So how can one say that the majority does not want the Nano plant?"

Biman Bose said: "I can understand that the small car will miss its deadline, but I still feel that the Tatas should stay in Bengal."

Trinamool Congress chief, Mamata Banerjee, meanwhile, remained defiant. On Friday, the party held a protest rally in front of the Tata plant, demanding the return of the disputed 400 acres.

From her speech, it was evident that she was aware of the latest developments. "What is the problem if the Tatas leave? There are many investors who want to invest in West Bengal," she said.

"The Tatas have already acquired agricultural land. If they leave now, Bengal will have neither factory nor the farmers will have their land. Bengal will have neither industry nor agriculture and the West Bengal government should be held responsible for this, not me," she added.

Heading: Nano on way to Pune, but Tata ready to talk - Indian Express
Content:
The Forward Bloc decided that the party's four ministers will not attend office from Monday to protest against the use of "discretionary powers" by Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee in granting APMC license to German wholesale major Metro Cash & Carry.

The CM had ordered the chief secretary to complete the formalities needed to issue the licence to Cash & Carry by September 30.

While announcing the decision on Friday night, the Bloc also threatened that the ministers will resign if Bhattacharjee's order to that effect is not revoked immediately. The party, however, did not issue any threat to pull out of the Left Front as a coalition partner. Bloc happens to be the second largest party in the Front with 23 legislators and three parliamentarians.

Bloc general secretary Ashok Ghosh said: "The CM cannot issue such diktats. We want to know from Biman Bose if the party stands by the CM's decision."

The crisis had snowballed after a Bloc state secretariat meeting on Friday morning decided against granting the APMC license to Metro Cash & Carry. The license had been withdrawn in June 2007 and the company had been pleading for its renewal as it was fully prepared to launch operations. To solve the issue, the CPM had convened a meeting on September 28.

But the Bloc secretariat decision not to grant the license this morning irked Bhattacharjee, who used his discretionary powers to make way for the issuance of a license, following which the Bloc met again in the evening.

Biman Bose, the chairman of the LF, declined to comment on the issue. Other Front partners were divided on the issue. General Secretary of CPI Manju Majumdar said the decision of the Bloc was unfortunate. "Still, the problem can be solved through bipartite meeting," he said. Manoj Bhattacharjee, central committee member of the RSP, said: "The CM took a unilateral decision. These sort of unilateral decisions are not acceptable in a coalition."

Heading: HC: Tata pact with state to remain out of public domain - Indian Express
Content:
The Tata Motors officials have agreed to talk to the Bengal government on September 28 following Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's personal letter to Ratan Tata, urging him to restart work in Singur. But Pune is still emerging as the most favoured destination for the Nano launch.

The biggest hint of this came from the vendors who have been asked by Tata Motors to meet in Pune on October 16. The meeting — described as a "national level" one — will have the Singur impasse on agenda.

A vendors' meeting on such a scale had not been held in the recent past. Sources in the vendor companies said in the meeting, the Tatas will take a final call on the site from where the Nano ancillaries will be delivered.

Confirming the meeting, the Tata Motors, however, said it had nothing to do with the Singur impasse.

A spokesperson said: "We will have the annual vendors' convention on October 16. This is not at all related to the Singur issue. It is a routine yearly meet." He, however, was not able to give the date or the venue of the last year's meet.

The vendors, however, are hoping for a decision on the impasse. "The Tata Motors has informed us about the meeting and we will attend it. We are hoping that there will be a decision on Singur as we have been in the dark for over a month now," said a senior executive of Endurance Group, which is to supply the aluminium die cast components for Nano, mainly gear housing, engine castings and bracket.

"There needs to be a solution to this. Our imported equipment is gathering dust in Singur. We have decided to shift all our machinery to our other plants on Monday," said a senior executive of Endurance Technologies, which was supposed to supply exhaust, converters, and suspensions. The company, he said, had received a schedule for order from October 1 for supply to the Pune plant. "We will be supplying the components from our plant in Nashik," he added.

Heading: State loses out on US investment too - Indian Express
Content:
The Calcutta High Court has ruled that the agreement between the Tata Motors and the state government on setting up a small car factory at Singur will not be disclosed.

Delivering the order on Friday, Justice Dipankar Dutta also directed the Chief Information Commissioner (CIC) to hear Tata Motors' objection and contention of other private parties within eight weeks regarding the disclosure of the agreement.

Justice Dutta also set aside the earlier order of the CIC in which the latter had asked the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) to make the agreement public by making it available on its website.

Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi had also requested the Chief Information Commissioner to publish the agreement that was signed on March 9, 2006. Following this, the WBIDC had published a portion of the agreement on September 9 on its website in accordance to the CIC's order.

This had led Tata Motors to file a petition in the Calcutta High Court urging for a stay on making the secret part of the agreement public. The company had argued that any such disclosure would affect the interest of Tata Motors.

Trinamool Congress leader and the Leader of Opposition in the Legislative Assembly, Partha Chatterjee, had also filed a petition in the High Court calling for the disclosure of the agreement.

In a related development, Amitava Chaudhury, a social activist, moved a plea in the High Court on Friday stating that the Ministry of Commerce and Industry had not provided information on the memorandum of understanding and other relevant records of the Singur project.

Chaudhury had approached the ministry on December 12, 2006 for obtaining the information but the department had rejected the plea citing legal provisions of the Right To Information Act.

Hearing the plea moved by Chaudhury, Justice Dutta also directed the CIC to hear the petition of Chaudhury.

Heading: Now, Japanese Encephalitis makes an entry, KMC admits things out of control - Indian Express
Content:
It is not merely Tata Motors' Chairman Ratan Tata who is feeling the heat due to the ongoing Singur impasse; the American investors are also feeling the same.

On Friday, United States Consul General Beth A Payne stressed the importance of resolving the deadlock as quickly as possible since it was scaring away potential American investors.

Referring to the recently held US-India Business Council meeting that was represented by companies like Boeing and Cargill, Pyne said: "These companies were supposed to visit the state as part of their India trip and would have introduced many American companies to Bengal."

"These companies were apprehensive that if Ratan Tata cannot succeed in West Bengal, then how can an American investor hope to do the same? Therefore, they decided to bypass West Bengal for the time being," she added.

American investors are watching how conflicts such as the one in Singur are resolved. They are also noting whether they are resolved quickly and in a non-violent manner with an understanding that signed agreements must be upheld. "They want to know that their investment project is free from political battles," she said. Payne, who assumed office in Kolkata on August 1, spoke about the growing US-India relationship and stressed on the importance of West Bengal as an important part of the investment plan.

"I am confident that West Bengal's private sector, given the freedom to act, and not limited by political considerations, can help find the solutions to the challenges that come with industrialisation and globalsation," Payne said.

Heading: By next week, CBI to begin fresh probe in Nobel theft case - Indian Express
Content:
After malignant malaria and dengue cases, Japanese Encephalitis (JE) has made its entry in the city, taking the Kolkata Municipal Corporation by surprise.

According to the civic authorities, the city has so far witnessed 625 malignant malaria cases with two deaths and 24 dengue cases with one death.

Fakirchand Das (78), a resident of 1/11 Ramkamal Street, died of malignant malaria at Sambhunath Pandit Hospital while Indrani Ganguly (9), a resident of Monaharpukur, died of dengue at a private nursing home two days ago.

Praloy Chowdhury, a resident of Sarsuna, suffering from JE, has been admitted in the Assembly of God Church Hospital.

In the last week, around 168 malignant malaria cases have been detected from borough VI alone. Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya has denied the reports of malignant malaria cases detected in borough VI in spite of the report being prepared by the KMC.

"The report of the malignant malaria cases in borough VI is factually incorrect," said Bhattacharya.

"We are really not being able to cope with the spread of vector-borne diseases in the city. We have failed to spread awareness among people. So, a circular has been passed by the joint commissioner for carrying out an awareness drive in all the wards of the city at least once a week," said Subodh Dey, Member Mayor-in-Council (MMiC).

At the MMiC meeting on Friday, the issue of malaria and dengue deaths was, however, given a miss.

On way to meet Mayor, youth Cong workers get police baton
The police allegedly beat up supporters of Burrabazar Zilla Yuva Congress who went to the office of Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) to submit a deputation to Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya against the increase in cases of vector-borne diseases in the city.

The incident happened when the members of the group was stopped at the gate of the KMC by the police and were told that the Mayor was busy at a meeting. But at the same time when a car carrying the Mayor entered the KMC premise the group members gheraoed him.

To bring the situation under control, police resorted to a lathicharge and arrested 22 protestors. Bikash Jadav, Pradip Sarkar and Ranjit Sonkar were severely injured in the clash. They were taken to the Calcutta Medical College and Hospital (CMCH).

"We went to submit a deputation since the Burrabazzar area has been neglected by the KMC. The place is very dirty. There are several patients suffering from malaria. But our deputation has not been accepted by the civic body; instead we were beaten up," said Mahesh Sharma, president, Burrabazar Zilla Yuva Congress. "Three of our supporters have been severely injured and taken to CMCH but the hospital did not admit them," he added. Mayor Bhattacharya, however, washed his hands off the incident.

Heading: To keep terror at bay, CCTVs to monitor Puja pandals - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) will begin fresh investigations into the theft of Rabindranath Tagore's Nobel medallion. The agency is set to begin the probe within a week.

On Friday, the Bolpur sub-divisional court allowed the CBI to reopen the case which was closed in 2007.

S Sunderrajan, Special Superintendent of Police (CBI), said: "We have got the permission from the court. We would begin investigations into the Nobel theft case within a week".

On September 1, the CBI had appealed to the court to start investigation afresh after it claimed of receiving fresh leads in the case. Sources said the CBI is quite hopeful of cracking the case this time.

"We have formed teams and planned an extended and detailed inquiry into the case," Sunderrajan said.

He, however, refused to divulge the details of the clues that the CBI claims to have got.

The Nobel medallion was stolen from Viswa Bharati on March 25, 2004.

The CBI took up the case on March 30 the same year, but three years later in August 2007, the agency decided to close the case, as the investigations had reached a dead end.

Incidentally, Jiban Bagdi (35), a local criminal, who was picked up after the medallion theft and was a prime suspect, was killed on September 11 at Parota village in Labhpur in Birbhum.

Police said he had a history of stealing artifacts and was active in the area when the theft took place. Many believe this could turn out to be a setback to the fresh investigations by the agency.

Heading: CESC gears up to provide uninterrupted illumination - Indian Express
Content:
The terror strikes across the country have made Puja organisers in the city a bit tizzy. So, to ensure that no untoward incident ruins the revelry, most organisers have decided to beef up security at the pandals by installing closed-circuit cameras (CCTVs).

The idea of installing CCTVs at the pandals was also suggested by Kolkata police.

"We have advised all Puja committees to install CCTVs for security reasons. It is more of an advisory and not a regulation," said Vineet Goyal, DC Headquaters.

Sanjay Tewari, member of Suruchi Sangha, which organises Puja near New Alipore petrol pump, said the club has arranged for eight CCTVs which will be installed at various points in the area.

"We will have one each at the main gate, the VIP entrance, inside the pandal and near the exit which opens up to an area lined with stalls," Tewari said. The club has spent over Rs 25,000 on security arrangement.

College Square Sarbojonin Durgotsab committee which erects its Puja pandal opposite the Calcutta University will install around five to six cameras. Bibhash Mukherjee, general secretary of the College Square Puja committee, said: "We had installed around four CCTVs last year. But with the recent spate of terror attacks we have decided to increase the number. We have spent around Rs 14,000 for this and a private security agency has been hired to install them." The crowd visiting the pandal will be monitored from the security outpost that will be set up just opposite the main entrance of the Calcutta University.

Clubs like Ekdalia Evergreen that record footfall in lakh have also decided to set aside a portion of their budget for enhanced security measures, apart from the usual police assistance they receive. "We witness a heavy rush of pandal hoppers every year. We have decided to install four cameras near the pandal entrance and at the gate on the main road. We will be having CCTVs inside the pandal too," said Goutam Mukherjee, joint general secretary of the club. The Maddox Square Puja that is spread over a sprawling 6,000 square feet area, however, will have to do with only three closed-circuit cameras this year. "We have spent a little more than Rs 17,000 to set up the three cameras at the entrance-exit points in Maddox Square Park," said Shibshankar Basu, member of the organising committee. "It is for general security. We held separate meetings with the bigger blocks to ensure that there are no loopholes in the security arrangement," said Subhankar Bhattcharya, SDPO of Salt Lake.

Pujas in Salt Lake that attract many devotees have also installed CCTVs in the pandals.

"We had a meeting with the Bidhannagar police and they prescribed certain security measures. We are installing three CCTVs with the help of the police," said S Biswas, vice-president of the FD Block Puja Committee.

Heading: Puja shopping washed out — yet again - Indian Express
Content:
As the city is busy with the last-minute preparations for Durga Puja, Calcutta Electricity Supply Corporation (CESC) is also leaving no stone unturned to ensure that the festive season this year remains hassle free.

In 2007, CESC had conducted inspections at 1,034 pandals. This year, too, it will carry out a similar check. Apart from inspections, CESC will have a special team of supervisors and engineers during the Pujas who will man their regular batch of workers operating round-the-clock in the control room at CESC house and command station.

"We have our 24-hour toll free numbers — 1912 and 44031912 — where one can register complaints. During the Pujas from Saptami to Dashami we will operate two special mobile numbers to attend to special emergency services," said Biswaroop Mukherjee, senior manager, PRO, CESC.

CESC officials, however, do not expect the demand of power to cross the maximum of 1,444 MW.

Apart from the usual 162 mobile vans to handle emergency situations and repair work, the company will be hiring about five generators for the first time to meet any eventuality.

"We will be hiring a few generators to deal with any power crisis that pandals might face. It will prove handy when an underground cable fault occurs," said Mukherjee.

The inspections and services that will be rendered by CESC Ltd will cater to their licence area of 567 sq km covering Kolkata and its adjoining suburbs.

"We have completed the first round of talks with the Puja committee members. The second meeting will be held soon. For information on safety aspects in pandals, we have distributed leaflets attached with the consumers' bills this month," said Sayantan Chatterjee, executive director, corporate development, CESC.

The power authorities also unanimously agreed that theft of power and tapping from overhead wires have reduced with time and awareness.

Last year, CESC had received 2,983 applications for temporary power connections in Puja pandals recording a total load of about 43 MW.

According to power officials, there were 3.21 million units of power consumption based on their applied load.

Heading: KMC embarks on hoarding demolition drive for revenue - Indian Express
Content:
With Pujas less than 10 days ahead, city shoppers are keeping away from the shops in New Market due to incliment weather.

Facing the brunt of this are the shopkeepers of New Market. Worse, the Met department's prediction of a depression over Bengal-Bangladesh could spell more bad news for shoppers and traders.

"Last year, our shop used to be crowded and we were all overworked. But this year, we have already faced a 40-50 per cent loss in our sales," said Rajiv Choudhury, proprietor of Kundu Stores in Bertram Street.

He added, "In fact, these days when we open our shops in the morning, the bad weather makes us apprehensive if shoppers would turn up at all. The few who do come leave quickly to avoid getting caught in the rain."

Muhammad Nadim, proprietor of a shop that sells readymade garments in New Market was of the same opinion.

"This year, we have experienced 40 per cent losses in revenue. This is usually one of the busiest times of the year for us but the weather has ruined it," he rued.

For many shopkeepers who set up their shops on the pavement, the losses are even more. Md Sabir, who sells fancy bags and purses on the footpath opposite Hotel Peerless Inn, said the rains have already spoiled nearly 20 bags.

"We earn around Rs 3,000 per day during this festive season but that is not happening this year.

Moreover, the rains force us to seek shelter all the time and we are not able to run our business smoothly," said Sabir.

Sukanya Dagupta, a resident of Lake Gardens, who had come to New Market for shopping, admitted that the rains have made too many trips to the place impossible.

"Last year, we visited New Market nearly six times, but this year we have visited just once due to the rains. Bad weather makes it impossible to go for shopping," she claimed.

Heading: Service panel worried over poor SET results - Indian Express
Content:
The Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) has started a hoarding demolition drive at night, and plans to keep it on till the beginning of Durga Puja next month.

Interestingly, the drive is aimed at retaining the revenue that was lost due to the failure of the tender process floated by the civic body for inviting agencies to bid for Puja hoardings.

Last year, the civic body had earned Rs 50 lakh through tenders.

Around eight agencies had formed an organisation — Sanskriti — which had earned a huge amount of money by handing out hoardings to several companies, sources said.

This year, however, there was no tender process involved. "We were surprised to find that no companies have submitted tenders this year. There were some disputes among the companies for the profit share. So, we have again started giving permission to individual companies," said Debasish Sen, manager of KMC's advertisement department.

Since the tender plan flopped, the department geared up to carry out demolition drives at night. The first drive that was carried out on Wednesday night in the area between Burrabazar and Hatibagan through Kalakar Street fetched the civic body Rs 13.5 lakh.

Heading: Govt gives nod to recruitment of non-teaching staff through SSC - Indian Express
Content:
Only 4.27 per cent of candidates successful

Despite thousands of vacancies in colleges across the state, only 305 candidates have cleared the State Eligibility Test (SET) for college teachers.

More than 7,000 candidates appeared in the test conducted on July 20 this year, but the College Service Commission (CSC) failed to find a single suitable candidate in subjects like mathematics and geology. Only 4.27 per cent of the candidates came out successfully in the results declared on Friday.

"I am very disturbed with the results. Despite conducting the examination repeatedly, we are unable to find suitable candidates," said Himanshu Sekhar Ghosh, Chairman, CSC.

"We lose our bright students to streams like engineering and medicine. Since the candidates appearing for the test are mediocre, the results are poor in science subjects," Ghosh said.

The performance of candidates in other science subjects is also poor. While 11 candidates cleared in Life Sciences, only seven could make it in Physical Sciences.

The number of candidates qualifying in subjects like Bengali and History is comparatively high. 78 candidates have qualified in History and 31 in Bengali.

Of the 305 candidates, 86 candidates from the reserved category and 217 candidates from the general category have passed the examination.

"The commission is facing a shortage of candidates in reserved categories. Most of the vacancies are in SC and ST categories," Ghosh said.

Last year, about 1,400 vacancies were reported to the commission, of which, 613 are in SC, 213 in ST and 158 are in OBC categories, the chairman added. The commission could fill only 600 posts because of the shortage of qualified candidates.

Heading: Eastern India’s first perishable cargo centre inaugurated - Indian Express
Content:
Despite opposition from within the CPM, the state Cabinet on Thursday went ahead with the decision to appoint non-teaching staff in the state-run schools through the School Service Commission (SSC). SSC has been recruiting teachers in the state for the last eight years.

"The recruitment of non-teaching staff through SSC will have far-reaching consequence on transparency, efficiency and recruitment process," Finance Minister Asim Dasgupta said.

Until now, the appointment of non-teaching staff in schools was done by management committees of schools through employment exchanges.

"I do not think this is going to work out. This will put an extra pressure on the SSC," said Kanti Biswas, former education minister and member of the CPM Education Committee.

This year, the SSC received about 350,000 applications for nearly 10,000 teaching posts. If non-teaching staff are recruited through commission then there will be quite a large number of candidates who will approach the commission for appointment, said Biswas. He said it would have been better had a separate commission been formed to recruit non-teaching staff.

"We have no information about the appointment of non-teaching staff," SSC Chairman Ranajit Basu said.

On whether any feedback was taken from the commission before coming up with the directive, Basu said, "We are not to reason on the issue." A section of CPM leaders believe that it is easier to transfer teachers to other parts of the state, but it will not be so with the non-teaching staff.

Heading: Govt decides to modify RTI rules - Indian Express
Content:
The first ever Centre for Perishable Cargo (CPC) in the eastern region was inaugurated at the Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport in Kolkata on Friday. The Union minister of state for power and commerce, Jairam Ramesh, inaugurated the 742.5 square metre centre.

The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) of the Union ministry of commerce has borne the investment cost of Rs 6.75 crore for the CPC, which has been on trial operation since June this year.

The CPC has an annual storage capacity of 12000 metric tonnes, ten times higher than the present export of perishable goods from Kolkata airport. India's ninth CPC is now under construction with an investment cost of Rs 3 crore, and will open at the Bagdogra airport by March 2009. APEDA will also assist in the creation of a pineapple post-harvest centre in Siliguri and a potato centre in Hooghly, besides financing a Rs 5.5-crore export cargo complex at Haldia.

Heading: PAU, Mahindra ink pact to promote industry-academia partnership - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has decided to modify the Right to Information (RTI) rules by making postal orders, bank drafts, non-judicial stamp papers and banker cheques acceptable in government offices along with applications for seeking information under the act.

Sandip Srimani, additional government pleader of the state government, informed a Division Bench comprising Chief Justice S S Nijjar and Justice Sanjib Banerjee that the state Cabinet had taken the decision on Thursday.

Sudip Mukherjee of Human Rights Law Network, an NGO, had filed a petition in the High Court that the court fee stamps were not available in all the places which are required to be attached with the RTI applications.

Heading: Students call off strike as V-C assures time-bound solution - Indian Express
Content:
To facilitate industry-academia interaction on a regular basis, Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the farm equipment sector (FES) of Mahindra and Mahindra, a leading tractor manufacturer.

According to Dr P K Gupta, Dean, College of Agricultural Engineering, PAU, the MoU will aim to set up collaborative training facilities and mechanisms for common benefit, and encourage resource and development facilities among students and faculty on projects mutually agreed.

Speaking on the occasion, Vice-Chancellor Dr Manjit Singh Kang said both PAU and FES had a common goal of serving the farmers and termed the signing of the MoU as a welcome step. Dr Kang expressed confidence that the tie-up would immensely benefit students, enabling them to keep themselves abreast with the latest technology and industry requirement. He said PAU had signed agreements with several other industrial organisations too.

Gautam Nagwekar, chief operating officer of FES, said: "The MoU is a trend-setting initiative in the industry-academia partnership to address the problem of skill resources in Indian industry." He said Mahindra had two tractor manufacturing plants in Mohali and had a programme beyond tractors.

Under the farm tech prosperity programme, Nagwekar said, Mahindra was focusing on grapes, potato value chain and seed business. "It has developed Smridhi Centres and provides soil water testing service," he said, adding that using farm wastes for generating power could be a good agenda for an economically viable business model.

Replying to the queries of mediapersons after signing the MoU, Nagwekar said they produced more than 1 lakh tractors last year and carried out export of grapes worth Rs 250 crore, adding that their main focus would be seed potato.

He said training to farmers would also be imparted by the company.

Besides deans, directors and officers of PAU, Prof V K Sehgal, Estate Officer-cum-Chief Engineer, was present on the occasion.

Heading: Gabria gives industry a ray of hope - Indian Express
Content:
After a four-hour meeting with Vice-Chancellor Dr Manjit Singh Kang on Friday evening, the protesting students of PAU decided to call off their three-day strike.

While the details of the meeting are yet to be made public, sources said Dr Kang had assigned a time frame for meeting each of the demands put forth by the students.

Dr Kang said: "Students chose the time just before the examinations to launch the strike. Nevertheless, we are here for the students and will do everything within our reach to ensure that students on the campus do not face any problem." The list of demands include reopening of PAU students' home canteen, provision of Internet on the campus, hot water in hostels, development of infrastructure in the university and hostels, provision of coaches for all games and lighting of the courts.

On Thursday, the students had declared to boycott examinations and had even locked the examination hall. Dr Manjit Singh Kang had earlier met the students in the morning and invited them for talks in the evening. The evening session continued till around 8.30 pm.

Heading: Vigilance team inspects LIT records - Indian Express
Content:
MASTER PLAN: Minister says he will get residential areas with thick industrial growth declared for mixed land use

With Cabinet Minister Hira Singh Gabria officially announcing that he will soon get those residential areas, where industry is operational in a large scale, declared for mixed land use, the notification of Ludhiana Master Plan has taken a political turn.

More than 6,000 industries operational in Shimlapuri, New Shimlapuri and adjoining areas are at present located in residential areas. The notification gives them 10 years' time to relocate.

Speaking on the issue, Gabria said: "Already, nearly 72 localities, where industry and residential properties are co-existing, have been declared for mixed land use. But problems still prevail in a large number of other areas. We have asked the local bodies department to drop the residential town-planning schemes in the areas with thick industrial growth. These can then be declared for mixed land use. The Chief Minister has already conveyed this to the department."

Gabria said he was hopeful this would be done in about two months' time. "Thereafter, these industries can also heave a sigh of relief, as they will not have to shift anywhere else to carry out their expansion plans."

The minister categorically stated that the change would be re-notified in the master plan soon.

It may be recalled that industrialists had met Gabria even before the master plan was notified, but despite assurances nothing was done in this regard.

According to the allegations of the industry associations, they were not even called for hearing of the objections filed by them.

The Town Planning wing, however, said they had studied the master plan in the best possible manner. Officials said dropping of town planning schemes followed a long procedure and they would not be able to comment on this issue at the moment.

The industry has, meanwhile, categorically stated that they cannot comply with 204 conditions in the master plan.

They are particularly against the clause that no industry can be set up in the lanes with a width below 10 metres.

Gabria said he would get these problems solved.

Heading: Double murder: accused remanded in police custody - Indian Express
Content:
The vigilance team of the local bodies department visited the Ludhiana Improvement Trust (LIT) office on Friday and inspected the records of various ongoing projects.

The team comprising Chief Vigilance Officer A K Parbhakar and other officers checked the records of Rajiv Gandhi 'super flats', which are under construction at Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar, and also of the commercial complex ready at Rani Jhansi Road. Besides, records of a few other buildings were also checked.

The officials said it was an annual inspection and they would study the records thoroughly to find out the details.

Heading: Stinking problem: tonnes of garbage but little space to dump - Indian Express
Content:
A local court, on Friday, remanded Lakhvir Singh, the prime accused in Thursday's double murder at Kotla Bharri village, in police custody till Monday.

Lakhvir allegedly killed his father, Sher Singh, and brother, Balbir Singh, with a sword. He also injured his mother Gurdev Kaur, chopping off her hands, brother Jasdev Singh, sister-in-law Kamaljit Kaur and six- year-old nephew Amarinder Singh.

In his complaint, Jasdev Singh accused the village sarpanch Sarbjit Singh and his brother Jasvir Singh of also being involved in the conspiracy.

Sadar SHO Dharam Pal told Newsline that the murders were the fallout of a property dispute. Lakhvir Singh, a dismissed Army man, reportedly told the police that his father was not giving him his share in their agricultural property. The injured are, meanwhile, undergoing treatment at the DMC Hospital in Ludhiana.

Heading: New Focal Point on cards, Gabria tells industrialists - Indian Express
Content:
The garbage dumps located at the Tajpur Road and the Hambaran Road appear grossly inadequate to cater to the garbage disposal needs of the city.

With incessant rainfall over the recent past, heaps of garbage lying in the open were washed away to leave the entire area littered with garbage.

Officials with the Municipal Corporation (MC) entrusted with the job of cleaning the sites are, meanwhile, waiting for the garbage heaps to dry up as working in the waterlogged garbage dump is difficult, said sources.

The development has spelled woes for city residents as the frequency of garbage collection from various locations has reduced due to lack of adequate dumping space.

"Garbage collection from various sites is being done on alternate days. Also, the total number of dump trucks plying in the area has reduced," said an MC employee, on condition of anonymity.

When the Newsline team visited areas like the Feroze Gandhi Market, Malhar Road and the Pakhowal Road, it found heaps of garbage lying in the open.

The private sweepers have also reportedly stopped regular garbage collection owing to lack of space in the bins.

The problem of littered garbage during the rainy season has been a seasonal problem for the city. While the Pollution control board had sent notices to the Corporation a number of times regarding the issue, with no land fills still present in the area, the Solid Disposal Act stands violated.

When contacted, Joint Commissioner B K Gupta said, "This is a common problem experienced not only in Ludhiana but in other cities as well.

The JCB machines will clear the sites soon and, to my knowledge, there is no problem at the moment."

A team from Delhi that visited the MC office on Friday, meanwhile, proposed to adhere to the Punjab Pollution Control Board (PPCB) norms and store garbage in landfills, which can later be converted into manure.

Heading: Kang puts his foot down, says Lubana will stay - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Agricultural University non-teaching employees may not like this, but then the vice-chancellor, Dr Manjit Singh Kang has made up his mind. His secretary, Dr P.P.S. Lubana, whose posting came under a lot of flak from the non-teaching section recently despite all the opposition, will stay.

When asked to comment on the opposition of the non-teaching employees, Dr Kang remarked, "It is well within my purview and it is my prerogative to decide who my secretary will be. I have chosen Dr Lubana for I need a person who shares my vision." Dr Kang adds, "The basic fact is that I need a person who can look beyond the files and his appointment is perfectly as per the university laws."

Notable here is that Dr Kang's decision to appoint a teacher on this post which is not a norm on campus had drawn a lot of flak from the employees. The non-teaching staff claimed that as this post belonged to them it should not have been saddled with a member of faculty. Lakhwinder Singh Sandhu, vice-president, PAU Non Teaching Employees, stated, "It is strange as to why a teacher, who is at professor level would work at a post which is meant to me handled by the accounts officer. This post needs a man who is well versed with the university laws and statutes. In short, this is an administrative post." The union had asked the V-C to revert his decision failing with the union would be forced to launch a stir.

Unfazed, Dr Kang says, "I have a certain vision for this university, for which I need some people, especially those who can understand and even share my vision. I have the right to have such people around me and my secretary is one of them. Thus there is no question of going back on this decision, at least for now."

Punjab Agricultural University, at present, has two of its most important administrative posts being handled by the teachers. The post of registrar which was usually handled by an IAS or an PCS officer is manned by Dr R.K. Mahey, only second person after Dr V.R. Sharma to have been entrusted with this post. Dr Lubana's appointment as SVC is the first time ever from teaching cadre.

Heading: Free health check-up camp for women held at Daba village - Indian Express
Content:
Rest rooms on roadsides may soon become a reality in Ludhiana.

A private company has given proposal to municipal corporation to start this public-utility service all across the city on the lines Delhi and Chandigarh. Aman Kumar, the project leader of this private company, today met Commissioner G.S Ghuman and floated this idea.

The private company has proposed to invest in this project and also to maintain it later on as well. However they have asked corporation to give advertisement rights to them so that they can earn revenue from this project.

According to information available, the rest rooms will be made on the main approach roads and even in a few inner lanes as well.

Meanwhile, reports said that MC Commissioner has liked the proposal and has made a four-member committee to study this project in detail. The members include joint commissioners B.K Gupta, Ashok Bajaj, SE Dharam Singh and Municipal Town Planner.

The committee will be surveying the viability of the project, the sites for toilets, appropriate roads and many other things. Public utility service is the need of the hour because it causes great inconvenience to the commuters, who are travelling on the city roads having no toilets. A few built a long time back by MC are in a bad shape and ill maintained due to which they are almost useless for the masses.

Heading: BSNL staff hold demonstration - Indian Express
Content:
In an attempt to cater to social and medical needs of women, the Federation of Obstetric and Gynaecological Societies of India (FOGSI) has launched a campaign — FOGSI Astra Bharat Jagruti Yatra 2008 — covering the entire country. Divided into four groups of 15 to 18 members each, FOGSI members travel in four different routes with three groups, starting from Kanyakumari, and another group covering the north and eastern states.

The group arrived in Ludhiana today and along with LOGS (Ludhiana Obstetrics and Gynecological Society) adopted the Daba village. A health camp was organised at Daba.

The camp focused on education of adolescent girls, eradication of anaemia, regulation of population and fertility, promotion of contraception and safe abortion, safe delivery and cancer detection. Free health check-up camps for women will be held in sub-centre Daba on every third Wednesday of the month, said Dr Vaneet Kaur, a gynaecologist.

Speakers at the camp emphasised on the need to educate women. They also pointed to anaemia as the most common problem of women. The Civil Surgeon, Ludhiana, Dr Satpal Sharma, Simarjit Singh Bains (councillor, Doaba), Dr Arun Mitra (President, IMA) and many other eminent persons from the city took part in it.

Dr Vaneet Kaur said to commemorate the occasion, an Aamla sapling, named after FOGSI, was planted at the sub-centre in Daba village. All the teams would converge in Delhi on October 1, where they would meet the President, Pratibha Patil and present a tour summary, she added.

Heading: Meet on skills for effective fashion illustration held - Indian Express
Content:
On a call given by the central headquarters employees, the members of BSNL Employees Union held a massive demonstration in front of the office of General Manager, Ludhiana Telecom. The employees were demanding early release of bonus and minimum pay of Rs 10,000.

Addressing the gathering, Balbir Singh, circle secretary, and Balwinder Singh, district secretary, Ludhina unit, lamented that the management of the BSNL was not releasing the payment of bonus on the pretext that the profit of BSNL had reduced during the last financial year.

They further said that the employees could not be blamed for the reduction of profit. The profit has gone down mainly due to inability to provide connection due to lack of capacity of mobile lines. The stiff competition in telecom sector has compelled the management to reduce the tariffs, which has also resulted in reduction of total revenue for the year 2007-08.

The other reasons for profit decline are that the government has abolished ADC charges and reduction in USO Funds. The Union demanded minimum bonus of Rs 10,000 and release of bonus immediately as the festival season has started. Prominent among other speakers were Paramjeet Singh, district president, Hari Narayan Singh, Balbir Singh, Budh Singh and Tejinder Singh.

Heading: Birthday of special child celebrated in a unique way - Indian Express
Content:
Ivanna Institute of Fashion Technology conducted a special workshop on "Skills for effective fashion illustration", here on Friday.

Harjeet Kaur from NIFT, New Delhi, addressed the students and demonstrated her skills on fashion illustration. She told the students about different colours and other mediums used for illustration.

She demonstrated the use of different mediums to illustrate varied fabrics, different fashion details, and different folds in garments. Fashion illustration from a classroom to the garment industry has a long way to go, she said.

"Fashion Illustration is one of the most important subjects taught to fashion technology students world over. Students here are given many opportunities to practice and learn from many sources. Ivannaiets are fortunate that they are getting an opportunity to learn from an artist today", said Manmeet Sodhia, Director.

Heading: ‘Healthy Heart’ expo begins at SPS Apollo hospital - Indian Express
Content:
Like any other birthday party, special children were totally absorbed in enjoying the occasion when Varun Garg, an autisic and blind student of Darpan, an NGO, was celebrating his 14th birthday.

The birthday bash was organised by Darpan, a school of autistic and special children. And reciprocating their sweet gesture, Varun was clapping and passing smiles to his friends. The whole atmosphere was charged with a merry-making and enthusiasm. Some children were dancing while others were clapping to mark birthday of Varun. Adding to it, Poonam Kalra, the coordinator of Darpan, along with staff members sang the birthday song and made children tap their feet when Varun cut the birthday cake.

Poonam said, "Varun is an ambassador of Darpan. He is a very pushing and inspiring child. Three years ago, he joined Darpan. The boy, who was unable to talk at that time, can now utter many words of daily usage and is very good at beading. One day, he will shine like any other child."

Varun having these disabilities since birth was not given admission by any of the schools in the city teaching through Braile. His mother said, "The school authorities denied him admission by saying that for learning Braile, speech is must. Now he speaks many words and also moves his hands very fast and wants to do some activities. But I have no way to help him out."

At Darpan, Varun gets speech therapy along with some activities like making blocks and beading. Poonam said, "I will make him an expert in making beautiful garlands and some other activities which he can do."

There are about 25 children at Darpan, who are autistic and mentally challenged. A teacher said, "Children have progressed leaps and bounds after coming here."

After the birthday party, children were also given a tonga ride. Poonam said, "Such outings put them with mainstream. They are of course part of it."

Heading: Protect potato from scruf: Experts - Indian Express
Content:
Over 400 persons got the check ups of their hearts done at the Health Heart Expo 2008, which began at the SPS Apollo hospital today. Jugdiep Singh, Managing Director, SPS Apollo Hospitals, inaugurated the expo by lighting a lamp. Heart attack survival kits were also launched and distributed free on the occasion.

According to a spokesperson of the hospital, on the first day itself, 1,200 people visited the exhibition and 400 got their heart check up done. "We have assembled outstanding physicians and the most advanced technology to bring comprehensive and compassionate care to all those, who turn to us for the health of their heart and their life," said Jugdiep Singh.

SPS Apollo Heart Centre has designed the "Heart attack survival kit", which acts as "First aid for a heart attack" for the victim, said Dr Chetan Sharma, a senior cardiologist. This will be a first-of-its-kind first-aid kit for heart attack in India. The kit will have Sorbitrate (5mg), Disprin (325mg), Emergency Ambulance Numbers, a CD illustrating CPR, various educative and informative materials. Step-by-step, the kits let you self-aid and direct as what to do during a heart attack.

According to Dr J.S. Grewal, senior consultant cardiologist, every minute of delay means more heart muscle is damaged, therefore chew one water soluble Disprin (as contained in the first aid kit).

"Most heart attacks are caused by blood clots in the arteries, and Disprin reduces the growth of these clots." The patient shall also take one Sorbitrate (5mg) bilingual to relieve the chest pain. Research shows that getting Disprin and Sorbitrate early in the treatment of a heart attack, along with other treatments that Emergency Department physicians provide, can significantly improve your chances of survival.

"Do not waste time trying to reach your own doctor," says Dr K.C. Mukherjee, a renowned cardio-thoracic surgeon, the safest bet is to summon an ambulance. Why? Because within the first few hours after a heart attack, there is a high risk of sudden fatal arrhythmia (irregular heartbeats), and only ambulances with paramedics are equipped to revive you should your heart suddenly stop beating. If a patient having a heart attack tries to "ride it out" at home for a while, hoping the symptoms are due to indigestion or muscle strain, or if the medical personnel delay instituting therapy for any reason, the delay can lead to devastating and permanent results.

Heading: KIMT students make a cut - Indian Express
Content:
Surveys of cold stores have revealed that 5-60% potatoes are affected by scruf, a fungal disease, said Dr. H.S. Rewal, Head of the Department of Plant Pathology.

He said that the commonly grown varieties such as Kufri Chandermukhi, Kufri Badshah, Kufri Bahar, Kufri Pukhraj, Kufri Chipsona-1, Kufri Sindhuri, Kufri Jyoty etc were affected.

The disease manifests itself as black scurfs on the potato peal and leaves impression as if clay is adhering to potatoes. The affected potatoes fetch lower market price.

To protect crop against the disease, disease-free tubers should be selected for sowing and dip-treated for 10 minutes with Monceron at 0.25% solution (250 ml dissolved in 100 litre water). Dr Rewal said that further information may be had from the Department of Plant Pathology.

Heading: Don’t compare children, experts tell parents - Indian Express
Content:
Students of the Khalsa Institute of Management and Technology for Women, Civil Lines, have brought laurels to the institution by obtaining excellent results in the examinations conducted by the Punjab Technical University in May 2008.

Shivangi Sachdeva has topped the institute in MBA-II by scoring 88.5% marks while Paramjeet Kaur secured second position with 85.75% followed by Mandeep Kaur who scored 84.75%.

Students of M.Sc (IT) achieved cent per cent result in fourth semester examination. Salma Khanum bagged first position by securing 85.33% while Vinny Kaushal secured second spot with 85% while Gaganpreet Kaur with 81.67% was placed at third position, according to a release issued by the institute.

"All the students have passed in first division with majority of them obtaining distinctions in their areas of specialization," said Dr Vijay Asdhir, director of the institute.

Heading: Pinal, Patel anchors Indian Oil win - Indian Express
Content:
"Each child is unique and parents should not compare their children with others," said Dr Manisha Sahni Prabhkar, a child psychiatrist and dental surgeon, while addressing the parents at a seminar organised by Fun Club here on Friday.

"Parents should not send their children to school before the age of three years. Many a time, parents overburden their children by forcing them to learn many things simultaneously. This should not be done. A child should be made to learn one thing at a time. And after a few years, it becomes clear in which activity he or she can excel," said Manisha.

She also tipped gave parents on how to deal with a stubborn child. "The parents should behave in a balanced way. They should not pamper the children by ignoring his/her mistakes. The parents should also not beat them and learn to be patent with them.

Talking about the junk food, Dr Meenu Bhagria and Dr Tarun Kumar, both experts, said, "There shall be only one day in a week for the junk food. Parents themselves should eat healthy food and only then the children will automatically follow them." Sheetal Thapar, the coordinator of the Fun Club, said that awareness created by the experts would come in handy for the parents.

Content:

Heading: A knack for playing with names, their own and their group’s - Indian Express
Content:
Tender for regional rail museum to be floated soon

A regional rail museum coming up at Lonavla that promises to be larger than the National Rail Museum in Delhi, is right on track. The tender for the ambitious project cleared by the Central Railway (CR) recently will be floated soon, according to railway officials.

The regional museum will come up on 17 acre of picturesque area surrounded by the hills of Lonavla, as compared to the National Rail Museum spread over a 13 acre. When the project costing Rs 11.6 crore is completed, it will showcase the advent and growth of trains. It will also be part of rail history, because of the land where it's being built.

"When work for the Great Indian Peninsular (GIP) Railway at Bhor Ghat (between Karjat and Lonavla) started, we never expected that more than 150 years later, we would meet to declare the proposed site for a rail museum at the same spot," said Rajesh Agarwal, executive director (heritage) of the Indian Railways. "We want to bring alive the romance of the train through this museum," he added.

The museum would house various locomotives used by the Indian railway network over the years and also those used by the erstwhile GIP Railway. It will also display artefacts of historic importance such as antique clocks, station bells, lamps, block instruments, platform benches, old insignias, OHE portals, signalling equipment, block instruments, tracks, track fittings and old railway tickets and passes. People can also see rare old photographs gathered by the railways that show various stations, locomotives and old train rakes.

"This great piece of history is scattered. We want to compile it and bring it at one place to let people learn about the railways," said Agarwal.

"We have chosen Lonavala because of its strategic location. People can also get a view of Bhor Ghats that witnessed the evolution of the railways. Plus, it's a tourist spot close to both Mumbai and Pune that will make it easier for people to visit it from both cities," said Sriniwas Mudgerikar, chief spokesperson for the CR. "The museum is likely to include a toy train that will take visitors around the 17 acre museum," added Mudgerikar.

There are plans to exhibit the rare photographs showing the evolution of the railway network in India at Lonavala station during the Commonwealth Youth Games, commencing next month.

Move to put Neral-Matheran on World Heritage map

The documents for getting the Neral-Matheran train service listed as a World Heritage Site is in the final stage. "It should a take a couple of months after which we will approach UNESCO for the same," said Sriniwas Mudgerikar, chief spokesperson, Central Railway.

Heading: ‘Indian Mujahideen’ was coined before Jaipur blasts to draw attention: Cops - Indian Express
Content:
TERROR ARRESTS: Travelling between Gujarat and Delhi, used common Hindu surnames like Gupta and Sharma while booking tickets at New Delhi station

When operatives of the Indian Mujahideen (IM) involved in the Ahmedabad and New Delhi terror strikes travelled between the two cities, they used 'conventional' or common Hindu names while booking railway tickets for themselves, sources in the Mumbai Police revealed to Newsline today. The tickets were booked from New Delhi, they added.

The details of the railway bookings will be included in key evidence against the arrested five men.

"After planting the improvised explosive devices in Ahmedabad, a group of eight Indian Mujahideen operatives boarded the Rajdhani from Surat and left for Delhi. Atif, the Delhi encounter victim, was one of these men," said a senior police official who did not wish to be named. One group is believed to have boarded the Rajdhani that arrives in New Delhi, while another group boarded the August Kranti Rajdhani about an hour, arriving at Nizamuddin railway station.

"The tickets for their travel were booked under conventional Hindu names, ending with surnames such as 'Gupta', 'Sharma' and 'Agarwal', to evade any sort of surveillance. The tickets were booked from Delhi," said the police official.

Following the arrest of five alleged IM terrorists by the Mumbai Police Crime Branch on Wednesday, the police claimed that it had exposed the backbone of the organisation and that the arrested group were involved in all major blasts in the country since 2005. With the onus now on the police to back these claims, the Crime Branch has already begun the work of collecting evidence to nail the accused. Details of railway bookings to establish the presence of certain accused in a city on a certain date would serve as crucial evidence in this regard.

"The process of collecting evidence is already underway, and we have substantial evidence already. One such piece of evidence we already have are the railway bookings of the accused. We know exactly when and from where their tickets were booked," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria, not wishing to divulge any specific details.

Besides the trail left by the terrorists leading back to their railway bookings, the police have also ascertained the source of the consignment of explosives and fire-arms recovered from the arrested accused. "We know that the gelatin and ammonium nitrate was sourced from Mangalore, and we have the precise location. The sub-machine carbine seized was also sourced from Mangalore," said Maria.

Whenever they group required explosives, Mohammed Sadiq Shaikh would allegedly call Roshan Khan alias Riyaz Bhatkal, who in turn would ask him to send some men to Mangalore. Bhatkal would provide a PCO telephone number, with orders to call on it when the consignment could be received.

Mumbra Arrests

Although illegal constructions in Mumbra are something of a legend, it is no longer as easy to go undetected in this suburb. Real estate agents and owners of various premises have to report to the local police the details of the persons renting the premises.

In the case of Mohammad Arif, one of the five IM men arrested and believed to be an expert with timer devices, the real estate agents and owners had not informed the police. On Thursday night, the Mumbra police arrested seven persons including three real estate agents under Section 188 of the IPC, for disobeying orders of the police authority.

Heading: Final High Court judgement quashes percentile system - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Police Crime Branch on Friday stated that the name 'Indian Mujahideen' was adopted by the co-founders of the terror organisation a short while before the Jaipur blasts in May this year. According to the police, the top-rung of the organisation were hungry for 'publicity' about their activities and felt that such an anointment would draw attention.

"The name Indian Mujahideeen was coined by co-founders Mohammed Sadiq Shaikh, Atif and Roshan Khan alias Riyaz Bhatkal shortly before the execution of the May 13 Jaipur blasts. While the trio had broken away from their former SIMI roots and were involved in practically all major blasts in the country since 2005, they felt that they were not getting enough publicity for these acts of terror. That is why they decided to name themselves the Indian Mujahideen," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria.

The Crime Branch had arrested five alleged Indian Mujahideen operatives, including a co-founder, on Wednesday. The police claimed that the group had planned to carry out blasts at crowded spots in the city.

According to the Crime Branch, central agencies and police teams from different terror affected parts of the country are camping in the city to share information with the Mumbai Police. While teams from Karnataka, Gujarat and Delhi are already in the city, a teams from Uttar Pradesh is expected to arrive on Saturday.

Meanwhile, the Crime Branch has seized the desktop computer on which Mohammed Sadiq Shaikh used to work, from the Content Management System (CMS) office in Andheri. The computer has been sent to the Kalina Forensic Sciences Laboratory for analysis.

The Crime Branch also stated that it was officially investigating only the case made out against the accused under the Explosive Substances Act and the Arms Act, and that a supplementary chargesheet in the 7/11 serial blasts case detailing the arrested group's involvement would be filed by the state Anti Terrorism Squad (ATS).

"At this stage, we are only investigating the seizure of explosives and arms from the accused. The case of the four stolen cars used in the Gujarat terror strikes is registered with the Navi Mumbai Police. Since the ATS is the investigating agency in the 7/11 case, we will hand over the accused to them and provide all possible assistance to them. The ATS will file a supplementary chargesheet," said Maria.

Heading: Three-year-old dies of drug reaction at Nair Hospital - Indian Express
Content:
In a setback to the State government, the Bombay High Court has quashed the government resolution for implementing the percentile system which sought to 'normalise' marks obtained by students of the SSC, CBSE and ICSE boards for admission to junior college. But admissions already done on this formula would not be disturbed.

A third judge, who was hearing the case following a split verdict by the Division Bench, concurred with Chief Justice Swatanter Kumar who had quashed the resolution in August. However, Justice A P Deshpande, who had heard the matter with the Chief Justice, deferred his opinion and upheld the government resolution.

Subsequently the case was heard by Justice J N Patel, who has now agreed with the view taken by the Chief Justice and quashed the GR on grounds that it was upsetting the right to equality.

Chief Justice Kumar, in his judgement, had restrained the government from acting on the resolution but stated that the admissions already given on the basis of the formula would not be disturbed. "The remaining vacant seats and additional 10 per cent seats sanctioned and allowed by the State, particularly in preferential colleges, shall not be filled on the basis of the percentile formula," he had held.

"Admission would be strictly on merit-cum-choice with reference to the percentage of marks obtained by students in the qualifying examination," Chief Justice Kumar had observed. He had, however, concluded that "till the judgment is pronounced by a third judge, the state is injuncted from making any further admissions" with certain exceptions and disposed of the petition.

Justice Deshpande, on the other hand, had held that "the introduction of the statistical formula of 'percentile' goes to achieve normalisation of percentage of marks secured by students of different boards and is, hence, not violative of Article 14 of the Constitution". "I also hold that assuming that the percentage formula extends some benefit or preference to students from the SSC board, the same is permissible and not illegal," he had observed and dismissed the petition.

The court was hearing a PIL by a parent of an ISCE student aggrieved by the newly implemented normalisation policy for admission to junior college. During hearing, the Court did not stay the admission process.

As a result, admissions got over in most colleges. But the Court had specified that the process would be subject to the outcome of the judgement.

Will go through text & decide next move: Minister

Sports, Education and Youth Affairs Secretary Sanjay Kumar said after the High Court verdict, "I have not yet gone through the entire judgement; so I will not be able to comment. Once I get to go through it, we will decide whether to go in for an appeal."

However, academicians from all the boards of education welcomed the ruling. While many agreed that a system to ensure uniformity in the admission process was necessary, they disapproved of the way in which the controversial issue was being implemented during this year's admission process.

Mithibai College (Vile Parle) Principal Kiran Mangaonkar said, "The decision to introduce the percentile system was taken and implemented rather hastily. Also, no officials from any of the other boards were consulted. To derive a formula to ensure uniformity in the admission system, the government should form a committee comprising representatives of all boards of education as also expert statisticians. We are glad that admissions this year will not be affected." Dayaanand Anglo Vedic (DAV) Group of Schools Western Regional Director K Kushal suggested that standardisation of the curriculum and evaluation methods of all boards might help ensure the much-meeded uniformity — instead of the percentile system.

Heading: Two years on, civic body yet to implement Chitale Committee recommendations - Indian Express
Content:
A three-year-old boy died after suffering a drug reaction at B Y L Nair Hospital on Tuesday. Hospital officials inquired into the case and said post mortem reports show that it was a drug reaction. They described it as an isolated case, which has not been reported in any other child. The entire batch of the drug has been sealed and samples sent to the FDA for checking.

Saurabh Jadhav of Siddharth Nagar, who was being treated for a valve default in the posterior wall of the urinary bladder, was admitted to the hsopital for a post-operative check-up on September 22, almost a month after his surgery.

As part of the procedures before the endoscopy to gauge his recovery, he was administered the drug Taxim, which belongs to the penicillin group. On the fourth injection, he suffered an "anaphylactic shock", a delayed reaction to the drug. Penicillin is known to have such adverse reactions and is now administered only after a pre-test. "It is a very rare incident. It happens in one among a lakh patients," said Nair Hospital Dean Sanjay Oak. "However, to avoid another such instance, a committee has been formed to look into the death," he informed.

Nair Hospital Deputy Dean Mahesh Shah added, "The boy had a severe reaction to this drug. He suddenly collapsed. Efforts were made to revive him but unfortunately he died."

Agripada police have registered an accidental death report and are inquiring into it. "We are looking into the matter and the Nair Hospital team is giving its report," said Agripada Senior Police Inspector Ravindra Khandagale. He added: "Based on our findings, we will decide whether it is a case of negligence."

Heading: Family of trainee pilot killed in crash expected to arrive in city next week - Indian Express
Content:
BMC doesn't have topographic maps to tackle floods in city during monsoon, says Chitale

Madhav Chitale, chief of the fact finding committee appointed to investigate the Mumbai floods of 2005, lamblasted the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC)for failing to learn lessons from the 2005 deluge. Calling the efforts taken by the civic administration as 'inadequate' ,Chitale said that safety of the people of Mumbai cannot be guaranteed as the civic body doesn't have basic topographical survey maps.

Speaking at the Engineers Day function organised by the civic body on Thursday, he said,"It's embarrassing that the city still does not have topographical survey maps which would show land level and help determine the flow of rainwater." According to him, the efforts taken by the civic body to tackle the floods in the city during monsoon are inadequate. "'We're not prepared to cope with floods in future and at an extremely nascent stage," he said. The fact finding committe led by Chitale had submitted a detailed 283-page report two years ago after the 944-mm deluge of July 26,2005.

Stating that land survey is the first step of engineering, he said in the coming years, intensity of the rainfall is going to be on the rise and the maps will be the most useful to tackle the flood situation in the city. "But, intensity of the flood situation and its impacts may not be the same in other parts of the city," he said. According to him, equal attention should also be paid to the rivers —- Dahisar, Poisar and Mithi —- as the flooding at the 48 nullahas in the city might swell them.

He said the maps would help plan the development and avoid construction in low-lying areas. "Once the direction of the flow of rainwater is known, all the other plans for water outfall, level of plinth and stilts for construction project, storm water drains etc can be easily made. But what is the point in making all the advanced plans, including flood-model, if the maps are not prepared? Without the maps in hand, we cannot guarantee the safety of people," he said.

The report prepared by Chitale and seven other members probed into the causes of the deluge and did the topographical and hydrological studies. The committee had given recommendations —long and short term— including contour maps, topographical survey maps, doppler radar and nullah management.

Stressing the importance of 'cloud science', Chitale said for a city where rainfall was as varied, the study is very important. "The rainfall in Byculla-South Mumbai on July 26 was 50 mm whereas in Andheri it was 330 mm. The difference in the intensity of rainfall in the same city is six times and therefore cloud science should be studied to understand the intensity of rainfall," he said. While the civic administration has recently got permission for conducting low-lying aerial photography to prepare the contour maps, Chitale said the consultants were misguiding the BMC. "The consultants are giving wrong information to the BMC and seem to be inexperienced. Focus should be given on physical mapping and not aerial. Even if the civic body prefers aerial mapping which will be super-imposed on the base maps, it will not take two years for completion," he said. However, civic officials maintained that the contour maps will help in the BRIMSTOWAD project. Municipal Commissioner Jairaj Phatak, who was present in the function, said that the BMC is implementing the recommendations of the report and will consider Chitale's suggestions.

When contacted, Additional Municipal Commissioner R A Rajeev said, "The topographical survey maps are same as contour maps which will be prepared with help of aerial photography. It gives undulations of land also. Instead of physical ground-level survey, we're doing an aerial maps as proposed by our consultants."

Talking about his other recommendations, Chithale said,"I'm happy that the BMC has installed additional weather station and rain gauge that give updates in every 15 minutes during monsoon."

Heading: Man found hanging from tree on court premises - Indian Express
Content:
Parents of Rahul Sharma, the 20- year-old who was killed in a plane crash on Thursday in Sydney, are expected arrive in the city by next week

The family is based in Muscat, but used to shuttle between Mumbai and Muscat often till Rahul joined Mumbai's Bhavan's College and spent the last five years of his life in Mumbai. "After his class X board exams, he joined Bhavan's College and was living in Mumbai before he went to Australia to pursue pilot training," said a resident of Symphony Apartment, where Rahul's family has bought an apartment, not willing to be named. "The family is in a state of shock and we do not wish to hurt their sentiments," he said.

The Sydney Flight Training Centre, where Rahul was getting the training, is based outside Bankstown Airport -30 kilometers from Sydney, refused to divulge any further information about Rahul's family.

Residents of Lokhandwala's Symphony Apartments told Newsline that Rahul's body was expected to arrive in Mumbai sometime next week. According to friends from the building, who had known Rahul since childhood, he came across as a very cheerful boy and used to make everyone laugh when he was around. "He always wanted to fly planes. He was clear about that," said a friend.

News of Rahul's death while training on a single engine Liberty XL2 plane is the second to come by in less than a month's time. On August 27, another Indian student, 24-year-old Akash Ananth from Bangalore, died in an air crash in Melbourne when his Cessna 150 crashed into a populated Melbourne suburb. That was Ananth's solo flight. Commenting on these deaths, a Mumbai based flight instructor, on condition of anonymity, said that the fact that more Indian pilots are getting killed in Australia is not really surprising because more students are opting for pilot training in Australia as compared to India.

"There's a perceived aviation boom in this country and pilot training schools abroad offer much better facilities than their Indian counterparts and so students prefer other countries to India," he said.

Heading: Cops told to pay compensation for illegal detention - Indian Express
Content:
An undentified man was found hanging from a tree on the Kalyan court premises on Friday morning. The man who is in his mid twenties was dressed only in black shorts, the police said. The body was brought down by the police at 12.30 pm.

According to the police, they couldn't ascertain whether it's a case of suicide or murder. Interestingly, the scene of crime is near the office of the deputy commissioner of police and a stone's throw from the the MFC police station.

Heading: Explosion injures four of a family - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High court on Friday ordered Thane local Crime Branch to release Rajan Shankar Gamre, who had been illegally detained by the police, with immediate effect. His mother, Shantabai, had filed a petition in the court stating that her son was picked up from their house in Kalina on March 24. Gamre was detained in Osnamabad district prision.

The petition states that the Crime Branch of Thane police picked up Gamre following which she wrote several letters to the Commissioner of police, the Governor, the Chief Minister as well as the Home Minister, requesting them to intervene. However after failing to get any relief from the authorities, she moved the High Court.

Division bench of Justice Bilal Nazki and Justice Ashutosh Kumbhakoni pulled up the police after observing that even though the police had filed a discharge application in the MCOCA court, they failed to mention that the police no longer required the custody of Gamre as there was no evidence to suggest that he was his involved in the robbery case registered against him.

The MCOCA court had adjourned the hearing on the discharge application till September 29.

The HC has now reserved the case for judgement and granted the errant police officials a chance to come clean if they are ready to apologize and give compensation to Gamre from their own pockets. The court has kept a hearing on Tuesday regarding the proposed amount of compensation the officials are planning to shell out.

Gamre's advocate Khan Abdul Wahab said that Gamre was released after the order and that the compensation amount will be decided on Tuesday.

Heading: Ayurveda doctors sharpen skills with latest technology - Indian Express
Content:
Four members of a family were injured on Friday afternoon after a box filled with some unidentified materials exploded inside a house at Dharavi transit camp behind the Dharavi police station.

According to the Dharavi police, Prabhu Wadkar (45), a driver, found a small box wrapped in white paper kept near a tree next to the Sion police station. "Wadkar thought it contained tobacco and brought it home. While he was trying to cut the cello tape and open the box, it exploded injuring Wadkar, his wife Kamal (40), her sister Vimal who had come to visit them and Wadkar's 20-year-old son, Santosh, who was helping him to open the box," said Senior Police Inspector Rajendra Thakur from the Dharavi police station.

Santosh and Kamal suffered severe burn injuries while Prabhu and Vimal were discharged after first aid.

When asked about the material used in the explosive, Dharavi police officers said that they had given the explosive material for testing at the Kalina laboratory. "Though we have sent the materials found inside the box for testing, we think that it was the work of some local miscreants. However, the incident was not related to any terrorist activity," said DCP Milind Barambe (Zone 5).

Heading: City to get art parks in Dadar and Worli - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty doctors of ayurveda from around India are sharpening their skills and getting familiar with the modern technology that science has to offer.

The Government of India's Department of Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy (AYUSH), is conducting a training programme in Mumbai, in order to help doctors of ayurveda familiarise themselves with newer technological practices in the field of gynaecology and obstetrics.

Doctors from around the country, including Jaipur, Jabalpur, Manipal and other areas from the interiors of Maharashtra- Latur, Pune, Osmanabad, are attending the training sessions which are being held at various centres in the city.

The centres include Palep Hospital, KJ Somaiya Hospital, St. George Hospital, and Podar Hospital among others. There are 12 faculty members who are experts drawn from the field.

"These are teachers, professors and lecturers who will be given teaching materials in order to improve their teaching skills. They will also be given practical training in operation of ultra-sound and sonography equipment," said HS Palep, a faculty member and founder of the Dr Palep Medical Research Foundation.

The six-day programme which started on September 22, will conclude on Saturday.

An average day consists of clinical hands-on training in various aspects after which classes are held by the faculties in different hospitals. The day begins at 8 30 am and ends at 6 pm. The ayurvedic doctors are also taught in-vitro fertilization technique along with other assisted reproductive techniques. This helps them with total over view of obstetrics and other gynecological practices.

"These are the doctors who usually man the rural set up, so these techniques should be known to them," says Dr Palep. The doctors who all hold an MD in ayurveda can thus update their skills with this continued medical education programme. "This is the first time we are conducting this re-orientation with modern medicine, in ayurveda. The government has asked us to conduct a similar programme in January 2009," says Dr Palep.

Heading: Old Western Railway, Central Railway DC rakes to be converted into dual current - Indian Express
Content:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation has proposed to set up art parks using the three R's of solid waste management—reduce, recycle and reuse. Citizens can look forward to spending quality time in two new and improved gardens in Dadar and Worli areas.

Civic officials said that millions of tons of garbage which is generated and dumped everyday, can be recycled and put to good use. "The garden will have a space for conducting exhibitions. The BMC will spread awareness on how garbage can be reused," said Additional Municipal Commissioner R A Rajeev. The project will start soon at a plot in Pochkanwala Road.

Citizens of Worli can also look forward to spending quality time in a new and improved sea-facing children's garden which is being developed after beautifying and combining the existing Sant Dnyaneshwar garden and Veer Ratna Baji Prabu Deshpande garden. Work has already started for developing and beautifying the garden. The existing garden had provisions for amphitheatre and pathways. Now, both the gardens—2500 sq metre and 5500 sq metre plots— will be merged to have common access with fencing and gates.

Heading: Pipeline burst disrupts water supply, contractor to face music - Indian Express
Content:
As per the Railway Board's decision, the existing 60 D/c rakes of Western and Central Railways of the last two years will be converted into dual current (A/c D/c). First rake of this group will be put on track in mid-October.
