Thus investing a huge amount on old rakes, having completed more than fifty per cent of their codal life, will be wastage of time and money.

According to sources, Rs 13.5 crore will be spent on each rake for retro fitment work. The total expenditure on 60 rakes will be Rs 810.10 crore with each new rake of 9 cars costing Rs 30 crore.

"New equipments, electronics and other gadgets which are being taken for retro fitment from Siemens have their own life cycle of 25 years, while rakes, which will be retrofitted will have a remaining life of only ten years or more. Actually each coach has a codal life of 25 years. After 10-15 years, when these rakes will over-age, what will the railways do? Will the railways remove these equipments from the rakes, again spending crore of rupees?" questioned a senior official of the Western Railways.

As per a letter from a member electrical of the Railway Board, dated June 25, 2008 and addressed to general managers of both Western and Central Railways, in the financial year 2008-2009, each railway will retrofit 9 rakes of 9 cars. However, in the financial year 2009-June 2010, each railway will retrofit 12 rakes of 9 cars. Later Central Railways (CR) will get this work outsourced and get it done through outside agencies for the remaining 18 rakes.

Siemen's electric equipments and other fitments will be done by the local contractor including wiring, cabling and ducting etc at the Mahalaxmi workshop (WR) and Matunga workshop (CR), say sources. For the first two rakes, bogies, and wheels are to be supplied by the Integral Coach Factory, Chennai. For the remaining rakes, however, the Railway Board has to make purchases from other agencies.

In 2003-2004, 116 coaches were converted into A/c, D/c current and retrofitment work was done at the Mahalaxmi workshop. These rakes are, however, still found to be troubling. "Nobody knows whether the problem of these rakes is related to electric equipments or to manufacturing. Though this work is being done through local contract, there will be supervision of the Mahalaxmi and Matunga workshops. Since both these are maintenance and not manufacturing. units, safety problems may arise later." said a senior official on condition of anonymity.

When Newsline contacted, Shyam Sunder Gupta, Chief Public Relation officer, WR, he said, "The conversion work involves two parts, one is electrical work and fittings etc and other is work on the iron shell and the bogies' portion."

Heading: Court acquits man convicted for drunken driving - Indian Express
Content:
Estimated loss is around Rs 60,000; the pipelines are more than 100 years old and are dilapidated causing leakages

Residents of several areas remained without water on Friday due to a burst underground water pipeline at BA Ambedkar and Deodhar road junction at Matunga. The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation has decided to fine a MMDRA contractor for negligence to compensate for the inconvenience caused to denizens .

A burst in the 48-inch diameter pipeline on Thursday night disrupted water supply to Dadar, Elphinstone, Parel, Matunga, Lalbaug, Chinchpokli, Byculla area between 2.30 am and 9 am on Friday morning. The water supply would be restored by Saturday morning. Civic officials said the underground water pipeline was damaged by the MMRDA contractor. "J Kumar, the contractor who is carrying out the construction work of a flyover in Dadar, had damaged the pipeline. It is an act of negligence and we will take action against him," said additional municipal commissioner (projects), Anil Diggikar.

While the loss due to the burst pipeline is estimated around Rs 60,000, civic officials said that it is the inconvenience caused to the residents for which the contractor would be fined. "We are appealing to all the authorities to take care of underground utilities," said hydraulic engineer, MM Kamble. The city's pipelines are more than 100 years old and are in a dilapidated condition causing leakages at regular intervals.

Meanwhile, the civic administration is also proposing installation of water meters at civic gardens and schools to verify water wasted through leakages and thefts. Around 25 per cent of the city's water supply—around 650 mld, which is Pune city's daily water suppl—is wasted through leakages and thefts. Although the installation of Automatic Meter Readers has been delayed by a year 44 per cent of the existing meters in the city are non-functional and over 1 lakh consumers are without any meter connection. Diggikar said that tenders will be floated in a month's time. "We have reviewed the specifications for the AMR and accordingly the tenders will be floated and soon we will zero in on the agency for supply, installation and its maintenance.

Heading: Dawood cousin’s bail plea rejected - Indian Express
Content:
A sessions court has acquitted a man who was arrested for driving under the influence of alcohol in February. Rohan Nikam (21) was arrested on Valentine's Day ( Ferbruary 14).

He was convicted by a lower court for four days and a fine of Rs 3000 was slapped on him. However, Additional Sessions Judge RG Avachat, acquitted Nikam, and directed the police to repay the fine amount.

The defence in its argument told the court that the conviction had come merely on the basis of breath analyser count, and Nikam was also subjected to a blood test. Nikam's advocate Raja Thakur also argued that a copy of chargesheet, that should compulsarily be made available to the accused, was not given to him.

Heading: One-year masters degree to benefit students keen to go abroad - Indian Express
Content:
The Sewree fast track court on Friday rejected anticipatory bail application of Zanzeb Aamir Kamal Khan, who is Dawood Ibrahim's cousin, in an assault case.

The court also refused to grant him relief as the offence was of a serious nature and a chopper and a revolver was used in committing the crime.

Zanzeb had approached the Sewree sessions court seeking anticipatory bail in an assault case registered against him earlier this month. Earlier the court had asked him to remain present in the court but Zanzeb was absconding from the date of offence. This fact was considered by the court while rejecting his application.

Heading: Who you calling chic? - Indian Express
Content:
The academic council of Mumbai University has passed a proposal for the introduction of one-year masters courses at the academic council meeting held on Thursday. According to AD Sawant, pro vice-chancellor, "We have agreed to it in principle. Now it has to be passed by the government and the University Grants Commission."

He added that the new courses will follow a different system and will be service-oriented . "Discussions are on to improve the courses and we are taking in suggestions."

The proposal to start one year masters courses, similar to the rigorous one year masters courses in the UK, was first mooted after the vice-chancellor, Dr Vijay Khole visited some UK universities along with principals from 13 city colleges earlier this year.

Registrar K Venkatramani said that the one year masters course will be especially beneficial for students who want to go abroad for higher studies as many countries like the US want a minimum of 15 years of education for post graduate studies."Through this course the students can complete 15 years of education with a masters degree".

As of now, students who wish to go abroad for further education are compelled to spend two more years of post graduate study after completing their graduation in India in order to qualify for admissions to universities in most other countries.

Regarding the pharmacy issue wherein B Pharma students were demanding a cut in pass percentage and an increase in the number of ATKT subjects in the B Pharma exams, Sawant said that these demands were not accepted.

"As per All-India Council for Technical Education norms, these demands are not acceptable."

Heading: Star spotting - Indian Express
Content:
The Chivas Fashion Tours are a hark-back to the Eighties when fashion shows promoted liquor, and trends were few and far-between

In the 1980s and early 90s, fashion shows were parties with an added dose of glamour to promote a brand and for sponsors to make big bucks.

The Chivas Fashion Tour 2008 which commenced last night at the ITC Grand Central, Parel, is barely different. Call it the curse of a country that is forever navel-gazing at its past or the imagination brought out by creative heads of Chivas that sees its alcohol as stimulation for imaginative designs, we can now savour the essence of the bygone era.

Chivas, who is a sponsor at all the big fashion events in the country, like the India Fashion Week, Lakme Fashion Week and the India Couture Week, are trying to stamp their brand value in the world of fashion. Bikram Basu, VP-Marketing, Pernod Ricard India, says, "We have been associated with fashion weeks for long. But the fashion tour is different. Unlike the other fashion weeks, the individual consumers can immediately buy off the shelf."

Chivas Fashion Tour's multi-city format has brought together 15 of India's well-known designers— Ashish Soni, Rohit Gandhi and Rahul Khanna, Deepika Govind, Kiran Uttam Ghosh, Mandira Wirk, Malini Ramani, Raghavendra Rathore, Rohit Bal, Shantanu and Nikhil, Varun Bahl, Vikram Phadnis and Wendell Rodricks-who will be touring across the country. Starting Mumbai, the designers will then head to Bangalore, Kolkata and New Delhi before the finale on November 22 in Dubai.

The three-day long Mumbai leg began with Rohit Bal presenting a line inspired by Ashta Dhatu—a combination of eight different metals. Karan Johar, the face of Chivas walked the ramp for Bal and later, a Bal-style party was held at Dragonfly, Mumbai's newest watering hole.

For Vikram Phadnis who is showing his contemporary collection in Mumbai and Dubai, the tour is going to be kind of a party. "It is the most relaxed fashion events of the lot because of its format and it is not stressful like the other fashion weeks." Dubai-based designer Ayesha Depala who is participating in the event for the first time, too feels that this is a carefree atmosphere to showcase clothes.

But veteran designer Wendell Rodricks who will be showing at Mumbai, Delhi and Dubai has taken this tour in all seriousness. This is the most important outing for him this year. "I am not showing at any of the fashion weeks this year and that's why this one becomes very important to me. I have invited all my buyers here," he says. Rodricks, whose signature style is all about ancient India but with a relaxed Goan attitude has created a range of cocktail dresses and evening lounge wear. "My collection is named Romantica and I have used soft pastels with fewer embellishments and lots of bows, frills and ruffles which is unusual in my collection."

Heading: The Jay Way - Indian Express
Content:
Had it not been for his son Harsh, actor Anil Kapoor might well have ignored director Danny Boyle's offer of playing quizmaster in Slumdog Millionaire. "I had not seen any of Danny's work before, so when his office got in touch with mine I was a little skeptical, since offers for crossover films keep coming in all the time. Besides, I was not even the protagonist and I wasn't sure how much the script would have for me," says the actor.

But all that changed after a stray conversation with family members over dinner. "When I mentioned Danny's name, my kids jumped on me. Apparently, my son was a huge fan of his and even had posters of Danny's film Trainspotting on his bedroom wall. He kind of forced me into calling them back and when they sent me the script, Harsh was the first to read it. He gave me the go ahead and I went to meet Danny in Mumbai thereafter, without having read the script or my role in it but armed with two DVDs of his films, Beach and Trainspotting, which my kids wanted autographed," laughs the actor, who is now in London with Boyle to celebrate the movie winning the People's Choice Award at Toronto, before being screened at the London Film Festival on September 30. The film will release in India in November.

Even though Kapoor's role was first offered to Amitabh Bachchan and then to Shah Rukh Khan, he has no regrets about him not being the first choice. "I am glad I did it in the end. Working with Danny was a pleasure because he is so subtle and understated. He gave me a couple of referral points—Al Pacino in Scarface, for instance, and then pretty much let me do my thing. If you ask me, he is the real hero of the movie," he gushes.

Now that the movie is behind him, Kapoor is busy with his home production, Neeraj Vohra's Shortkut, which is near completion. But before that though, there is Subhash Ghai's Yuvraj, which also has Salman Khan and Katrina Kaif in it. Kapoor plays a person with mental disability but is an acoustic genius.

"Even though it became fashionable to do such a role after Koi Mil Gaya, I was among the first to have played a person with mental disability in Eeshwar, almost 20 years back. In fact, it was even before Forrest Gump became an iconic hit. So in a way I flagged off the trend," he shrugs.

Ah, well.

Heading: chatterati - Indian Express
Content:
Jay Sean on constantly pushing the boundaries in music

After a groovy performance to a packed house at the Hard Rock Café on a Wednesday night, rhythm and bass singer Jay Sean was at Planet M, Phoenix Mills, on Thursday evening to release his latest CD, My Own Way. It was blink-and-miss, as Sean was hustled onto the mini stage at Planet M by his agents. Avid fans had already queued up to see their idol and were obviously very excited as he took the mike.

Sean started with Ride It (Kya Yehi Pyaar Hai) from his new album. Using his usual mix of R&B and Hindi lyrics, Sean's CD seems promising. He was joined on stage by a 'beat-boxing' friend who added vital punctuations to Sean's singing and rapping.

The album, which is Sean's second, was to have released late last year as collaboration between his own label Jayded and 2Point9 Records. But it took longer when radio stations in UK decided to playlist the songs if the release was delayed till 2008. So after nearly two years away from the limelight, Sean is back.

The 25-year-old, Britain-born Sikh rapper shot to fame in 2003 with hit singles like Dance with you and Eyes on You, collaborations with fellow artists Rishi Rich and Juggy D under the Virgin Records banner. The songs that could be classified as Punjabi R&B weren't very different from what he has on offer now.

"I'm very excited about this album and have wanted to do something in India for a while now," says Sean who was visibly pleased with the response to his concert in Mumbai the previous night. Sean confesses he got some help to write the lyrics for his songs. And will he be diversifying into other genres of music too? "Well we are constantly experimenting, constantly trying to push the boundaries with what we can do."

Heading: Saturday night is here - Indian Express
Content:
Movie stars and celebrities stopping by at designer stores are passé. When the French minister of state for foreign trade, Anne-Marie Idrac (in picture, centre), was in the country, she paid a courtesy visit to the Louis Vuitton and Christian Dior stores at the Emporio mall, in New Delhi, and it was a deja vu moment for the elegant lady.

"The best LV stories are of old travel bags made for the maharajas and the stores here remind me of those in Paris," smiled Idrac, trussed in a chic beige dress. In the Capital for an Indo-French summit, Idrac was accompanied by Kalyani Chawla of Dior India, who showed her around the store. "Indian fashion is growing and it is important to have an economic and cultural exchange between India and France," said Idrac. Chawla, dressed in white, harped about the popularity of Indian fashion abroad.

Also in attendance were designers Suneet Varma, Satya Paul and socialite Tanisha Mohan.

Heading: Love and longing - Indian Express
Content:
Get set to be initiated into the whacky world of Saturday Night Live

Does your only dose of television comedy come in the form of unintentionally funny saas-bahu dramas? Fear not; relief is at hand as Saturday Night Live (SNL), the longest running comedy sketch/variety show on television, is finally in India. The show, which debuted on September 22 in India, airs on VH1, every week, from Monday to Saturday at 9 pm.

Few shows have a richer comic history than SNL. The legendary show launched many successful careers — Eddie Murphy, Adam Sandler, Chris Rock and Ben Stiller, to name a few. In a politically correct world, SNL stands out for its no-holds-barred humour, taking pot-shots at everyone from the Pope to Hillary Clinton to Mel Gibson. The show has also got celebrities to poke fun at themselves such as the famous episode where Britney Spears came on wearing inflatable breasts, in reaction to rumours that she'd had her breasts surgically enhanced.

The typical format of the show features a regular cast of comic actors, joined by a guest host and a musical act. In the past, guest hosts have included Steve Martin, Tom Hanks and Drew Barrymore. The musical acts, both mainstream and breakthrough, have included performers such as Paul Simon, Sting and Jennifer Lopez.

SNL had an audience in India long before VH1 finally decided to bring it here. Says actor and VJ Luke Kenny, "I've been a fan since the '70s. It is not just about comedy; it also brings acting skills to the fore." VJ Cyrus Sahukar agrees. "I've been a fan for at least seven-eight years," he says, "It's like an institution in the west —the Harvard or Oxford of comedy; every established comic actor from Jim Carrey to Chris Rock to Adam Sandler has been on SNL."

Ferzad Palia, Associate GM of VH1 India, says that they picked out SNL episodes that would suit the comic palate of the Indian viewer. "We didn't want to air episodes from the '70s and '80s; we were looking for more current content that had a certain topicality for Indian viewers. Also, we needed episodes with musical acts and celebrity hosts who're known in this country. For instance, on Tuesday, we aired an episode that had Ashton Kutcher as the host and Gwen Stefani as the musical act."

The concept of a comedy sketch combined with live music is not new in India. Movers and Shakers, which was based on the formats of SNL and the Tonight Show with Jay Leno, proved to be very popular with viewers. But even the peerless mimic Shekhar Suman, known for his spot-on imitations of various political and non-political figures knew where to draw the line. So will SNL, with its irreverent brand of comedy that combines mimicry, risqué jokes and many, many instances of cross-dressing, ever find an Indian avatar?

"Definitely," says Kenny, "But only for an English-speaking audience. As for a Hindi version of SNL, I don't think that'll happen anytime soon." Sahukar adds, "I don't see why there can't be an Indian version, since we have some excellent comedians and musicians here. But there are way too many restrictions in our society and people tend to get offended very easily, so it may take many years."

SNL who?

* Sting is the only non-American performer to appear as a musical guest at least five times; he has also performed in at least one sketch during each of his performances.

* The movies The Blues Brothers, Wayne's World and Wayne's World 2 are film spin-offs of SNL sketches.

* Sinead O'Connor's October 2, 1992, live performance in which she destroyed a picture of Pope John Paul II was substituted by her dress rehearsal performance from earlier that evening when she held up a picture of a starving African child.

* Britney Spears was 18 when she first appeared on the show on May 13, 2000, which makes her the youngest person in SNL history to act as a host and a musical guest at the same time.

Heading: chatter box - Indian Express
Content:
Miley Jab Hum Tum

Star One

Monday to Thursday, 9 pm

Rating**

What's it about? Life in Excel College, throbbing with teenage energy and charm. Since love rules the heart and mind at this stage of life, the storyline is replete with crushes, flirting, heartbreak and longings.

Who is in it? In this fictional hippest college of Mumbai, Diya sashays down the corridor showing off her diva-like persona. This is enhanced by the constant presence of loyal Annie, who idolises Diya, and stupid Chacko (Doesn't this just remind you of Kareena Kapoor as Poo in Kabhi Khushi Kabhi Gham? Only sour point is lanky Diya lacks any of Kareena's attitude and oomph). Diya is shocked when her small-town cousins—shy and intelligent Gunjan and full of life Nupur—from Morena come to Mumbai. Diya's eyes are set on cool and stylish Samrat, who wins hearts as well as basketball matches. Though he is often caught flirting with Diya, Samrat is still waiting for that special girl. Samrat faces stiff competition from intelligent Mayank when it comes to wooing girls.

What's hot? The title song of the sitcom, meant to draw young audience, has a peppy feel. It manages to build up the mood with all the major characters making appearances in it. It offers the promise of a nice candy-floss drama unfolding in a Riverdale kind of setup. Though the starting episodes have not quite kept that promise, it remains to be seen whether the characters and scriptwriters pull up their socks to deliver a TRP-booster.

What's not? The storyline, a mish-mash of a number of teeny-bopper lover stories and college romances, desperately needs some freshness and original ideas. That's what had worked for Remix, a series set in a school, which was aired by the same channel a few years ago, or the hugely popular Hip Hip Hurray. Being little more careful while deciding the getup of the characters can also help. We also don't mind emphasis on acting than wearing off-shoulder dresses or tight salwar-kameez. And please, those cheerleaders and convertibles don't belong to a Mumbai campus. Will someone also tell Nupur that Mumbai is not the city where people come to meet the man of their dreams.

Should you be watching it? Yes, if you are the kind who clings on to college memories as if it's the biggest solitaire in your jewellery box. So recommend to the tribe who love to see repeats and rip-offs of Kuch Kuch Hota Hai or Kabhi Khushi Kabhi Gham.

ALAKA SAHANI

Heading: Talking point with  Baba sehgal - Indian Express
Content:
Best fit

For Amit Tandon, playing the character of the NRI Abhay Singh in Saath Saath Banayenge Ek Ashiyaan on Zee TV was an easy task, because of his Canadian origin and the firang accent he sports. But after a successful run, Tandon has decided to call it quits. The channel has subsequently roped in Salil Acharya as a substitute in the show. Salil who has been a part of popular shows like Yeh Meri Life Hai, Kasauti Zindagi Ki, Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Thi, Kittu Sab Janti Hai and Kasturi, is very excited about the role he has bagged. But matching Tandon's American twang is going to be difficult.

Sob tale

The team of Golmaal Returns—Ajay Devgan, Arshad Warsi, Tusshar Kapoor, Shreyas Talpade and director Rohit Shetty—made it to the sets of Zee TV's Sa Re Ga Ma Pa to promote their latest venture. But it was Pakistani girl Sara Raza Khan's sob story that was the highlight of the show. The poor girl narrated a sordid tale of how she is being treated as an outcast here amongst her peers in Challenge 2009. This young girl who is away from home, in this metropolis of Mumbai, is actually facing a lot of objection from her people back home in Pakistan. While this definitely left everyone flabbergasted on the sets, we just hope her situation improves.

Home grown

Neena Gupta has her plate full these days. After her much talked about wedding with Vivek Mehra, Neena is now resurrecting her career. She will make a comeback with her character of Manno Bhabhi in Saath Phere. She has been given the liberty to design her costumes, jewellery and hairstyle. Interestingly, the lehenga- cum -saree that she plans to drape in the show has been inspired by her costume that she had worn in her mehndi-sangeet ceremonies. We'll keep our fingers crossed.

Heading: Cong RTI panel head arrested, party accuses Mayawati of ‘vendetta’ - Indian Express
Content:
You haven't been on the Indian music scene for long. Where were you all these years?

I was in US for many years because of certain family commitments. And I was also waiting for the right backing to release my music videos.

After being a part of the Indian

music industry for so many years, what prompted you to take up acting on television?

I have always been a part of television. I started my career by hosting a show called Superhit Muqabla on Doordarshan. After I came back from the US, I did two reality shows Dhoom Macha De and Bigg Boss. But in terms of a daily soap, this was my first one. Now I can say I have done everything on television.

Describe your role in Jugni Chali

Jalandhar.

I play Balwinder, who is the eldest of the four sons in the family. The concept of the show is to find ideal bahus, who are beautiful, disciplined and uneducated. The serial has a social message in it, whereby it talks about the importance of education for women.

Is the character similar to your real-life personality?

The character is very similar to me. I play a Punjabi who is a happy-go-lucky person. He is a jovial person who leads life on his merit.

Have you exhibited your singing talent on the show?

There is no deliberate attempt to exhibit my talent. But I am doing a bit of rapping in the show. Few of my dialogues in the soap have to be rapped.

Since rapping was an unconventional choice, was it tough for you to establish yourself initially?

I was lucky in terms of the backing I got from music companies and the support I got from the listeners. I was hailed as the King of Rap then. But then you have to consistently keep delivering hits. When you disappear from the scene people tend to forget you. To come back after a break is always difficult and it is similar in my case.

What do you think of the rap scene in India today?

Bollywood music is dominating the music scene today. There is too much piracy in the market which has reduced the sales of music CDs. Radio stations too do not encourage pop music, they play only popular numbers. It is not just the youngsters but even the established who are finding it difficult to sustain the rap scene in India.

Any upcoming projects?

After a long time, my music album will be releasing next month. The album is called Apni Life Ki Gaddi Ko Dakka Maar. There are 10 songs in this album. Also, I am doing a lot of playback for Telugu and Tamil films. I am a recognised voice down South. Recently I recorded a song for Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy for an upcoming film. Besides, if I get meaty roles I will not hesitate to act in films.

Heading: In Etawah, Dalit farmer commits suicide - Indian Express
Content:
The state unit of the Congress accused Chief Minister Mayawati of indulging in politics of vendetta after the head of the party's Right To Information (RTI) task force, Shailendra Singh, was arrested in the wee hours of Friday . Singh was arrested for holding a demonstration at the office of the State Information Commission (SIC).

Before arresting Singh, who was also a former deputy superintendent of police, the police had raided his residence.

The Congress alleged that the arrest was made to prevent Singh from appearing in the Supreme Court on September 29 in connection with a case on the misuse of public funds at Gomti Nagar's Samajak Parivartan Sthal, better known as Ambedkar Memorial.

On Thursday, Singh, along with the workers of the RTI task force, had staged a dharna at the office of the SIC. They protested against the new regulations for filing RTI applications, issued by one of the information commissioners, who allegedly did not accept applications on the letterheads of political parties.

Additional Superintendent of Police (East) Harish Kumar said the former DSP led a group that ransacked the office of the SIC, a constitutional organisation. A case under Sections 143, 147, 353, 504, 506 and 427 of the IPC, Criminal Law Amendment Act and Public Property Damage Act was registered against him.

Later in the day, Singh was produced before a local court which rejected his bail application. The Congress has decided to approach the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court for Singh's bail. Singh had filed a petition in the Supreme Court over the alleged misuse of public funds in the construction of Ambedkar memorial, including the proposed installation of over 60 stone elephants, the election symbol of BSP, at the cost of Rs 1 crore each. The hearing of the case was scheduled for September 29.

Former chief minister Ramnaresh Yadav and former state Congress president Jagdambika Pal said the action against Singh was a part of the political vendetta of the Mayawati government and was against the democratic values and conventions.

"The dharna at the office of the SIC is a lame excuse, the real cause for the arrest of Shailendra was to prevent him from appearing before the apex court," said a Congress leader. "The former DSP was treated like a criminal and was arrested at around 2 am. The door of his flat had been broken down and he was beaten up."

The Congress has announced a state-wide demonstration on Saturday against the police action. State party president Rita Bahuguna Joshi said if a former police officer could be treated in such a manner, the situation of the common man was anybody's guess.

Heading: Gorakhpur CJM asked to order FIR against BJP leaders - Indian Express
Content:
In his suicide note, he alleged BSP legislator encroached on his land, destroyed the crops

A Dalit farmer committed suicide on Thursday after Bheem Rao Ambedkar, BSP legislator from Lakhana constituency, allegedly encroached on his land in Morhi village in Etawah district. The legislator even began building a banquet hall with money from his discretionary fund.

On Friday, the police filed an FIR against Ambedkar and six other people, including a contractor, for driving Suggar Singh Katheria to commit suicide, on a complaint lodged by his brother Surendra Singh.

The family of Suggar alleged that on Thursday afternoon, the MLA's supporters picked him up from home and dropped him back in the evening. Soon, he beagn to feel sick and was taken to the Etawah district hospital, where he was declared dead on arrival.

Jitendra Singh Parihar, Inspector of Barthana police station, said the postmortem found evidence of poisoning and the viscera had been sent for test. Singh had left behind a suicide note, said Parihar.

According to sources, Suggar, in his suicide note, had blamed the MLA forcibly encroaching on his land and destroying the crop. He had approached various authorities and requested them for justice, but to no avail. In the note, Suggar reportedly wrote: "Jai Bheem, Mayawati zindabad, Kanshiram zindabad, Government murdabad. Since the administration has failed to protect me, I am ending my life."

Parihar said although the FIR alleged Suggar had been driven to suicide, it has not been proved yet.

The local authorities, however, seemed reluctant to accept it as a case of suicide. District Magistrate Madhukar Dwivedi said it was not a case of suicide. "Who told you that it's a case of suicide?" he said.

The Deputy Inspector General of Kanpur Range, Kamal Saxena, said he was not aware of the facts of the case and was collecting the details.

Additional Director General (Law and Order) Brij Lal said, "The police is investigating, and on the basis of the findings, action will be taken."

The MLA, Ambedkar had a different version. He said the gram pradhan had requested him to build the banquet hall on the land. "I approved the application and asked the administration to look into the matter.

The construction was to be done with the MLA fund, and it was the responsibility of the administration to verify details of the land," he said.

The village is under former chief minister Mulayam Singh's constituency — Barthana. His son Akhilesh Singh visited the family and demanded a compensation of Rs 10 lakh for them and the arrest of the MLA.

The one beegha gram sabha land was allotted to Suggar for cultivation by the district administration on "patt" in 1996. Six years later, on an application by the gram pradhan, the patta was cancelled.

Suggar, however, moved an application against the cancellation before the commissioner who directed the district magistrate to hear his plea and decide on the matter.

"The matter was still pending," said Etawah Superintendent of Police S R S Aditya.

Heading: On way to Rae Bareli, Sonia surprises all with out of the way stopovers - Indian Express
Content:
The Allahabad High Court on Friday directed the Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) of Gorakhpur to order filing of a case against BJP parliamentarian Yogi Aditya Nath, MLA Radha Mohan Das Agrawal, Gorakhpur Mayor Anju Chaudhari, MLC V D Singh, former minister S P Shukla and others.

In its order, the HC directed the CJM to act on the petition filed by one Parvez Parwaz in which he had alleged that a mob of Hindu men had looted several shops of Muslims in Gorakhpur and also put them on fire on January 27 and 28, 2007.

The High Court also directed that a proper investigation be conducted after an FIR is registered. Parwaz, who was also a victim, in his petition had requested for registration of a case against the BJP leaders for inciting violence and arson. The CJM of Gorakhpur, in his order dated July 29, 2008, however, rejected the application, saying that an FIR had already been registered and chargesheet was also submitted in the rioting incident. The HC has held that since the applicant was also a victim of the violence, registration of an FIR in connection with the incident involving him will not amount to registration of a second FIR. It said that from the perusal of the application, a prima facie cognizable offence was made out, thus it was not proper to reject the application.

Heading: Proposed four-point agenda to fight terror, says Kalam - Indian Express
Content:
On the first day of her two-day visit to Rae Bareli constituency, UPA chairperson and Congress president Sonia Gandhi made surprise stopovers and visited villages that have been affected by incessant rains.

The cavalcade of Gandhi, which was supposed to reach Rae Bareli city via Maharajganj, made a sudden turn near Sahengo Mor. She made surprise visit to several villages that included Sri Rajnagar, Sehgo, Dostpur, Bedara, Bhawanipur, Shivali and Badhawar.

"She queried the villagers about the money they are supposed to receive for the construction of their damaged houses. Many people told her that they have not received any help from the state government," said a source in the local Congress unit.

She also asked about the work that the villagers are entitled to get under the National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme. Some villagers suggested that the minimum number of working days be increased from 100 to 200 under the scheme.

After reaching Maharajganj, Gandhi met the family of local party leader Sunil Kumar Agrahari, who had passed away last month. She also met members of Self Help Group (SHG) who assembled at NTPC's Community's Centre, Unchahar, in the afternoon.

Speaking at a function, the Congress President said development is not possible without the involvement of women. She said the contribution of the SHG is that it has freed women from the clutches of moneylenders.

In the evening, Gandhi attended an Iftar party, which was organised by Rae Bareli district Congress Committee at Reform Club.

"This is the first time that Soniaji had attended an Iftar Party in my town," said Achche Khan (55), a local.

Two years ago, Congress general secretary Rahul Gandhi had organised an Iftar party in Rae Bareli.

Heading: LDA contractors resort to hungerstrike - Indian Express
Content:
With the country debating the terror issue following the serial blasts in New Delhi, former President Dr A P J Abdul Kalam said on Friday that the need of the hour was is a consolidated effort to combat terrorism.

Addressing a gathering of students in Allahabad, Kalam said: "I have given a four-point proposal to the government to fight terrorism. Involve people from all walks and make the issue a mass mission. Evolve a single intelligence agency system in the country, ensure fast trial in courts and ensure economic growth to eliminate terrorism."

He exhorted youths, teachers, women, politicians and members of judiciary to come forward and join the process of nation building and stressed on the need to

initiate a revolution to eliminate corruption from the society. "The country needs a revolution to enlighten women and girl students. Teachers should stress on quality education and knowledge," he said.

Dr Kalam emphatically stressed on beginning a drive against dowry, crime against women and female foeticide. "I respect three women in my life. My mother who had been a constant source of inspiration to me, noted classical singer M S Subhalaxmi and Mother Teresa who served the poor and downtrodden always with a smile," he said.

Administering an oath to the students to bring a change in the life of hundreds of women by helping them get education, employment and making them aware of healthcare, the former President urged them to lead an honest life, free from corruption and set example in eradication of corruption.

"If women are educated and respected, the country will reach a new height," he said.

Knowledge has three components besides its technical value. "They are creativity, righteousness and courage. Be creative and righteous in studies and have the courage to think differently, the courage to invent, the courage to discover the impossible and the country would soon be a superpower," he added.

Earlier in the day, the missile man was given a rousing reception by students of SS Khanna Degree College and Tagore Public School, the teachers and Vice-Chancellor of Allahabad University Prof essor Rajen Govind Harshe. The Chief Justice of Allahabad High Court, H L Gokhale, and Supreme Court judge Markandey Katju were also present on the occasion.

The students also satiated their scientific thirst by asking questions to the former president who patiently answered them with explanation. He also awarded medals and certificates to the meritorious students of the college and the school.

Heading: Two Lucknow labs get CSIR award - Indian Express
Content:
Protesting against the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) for allegedly withholding payment for work done two years ago, contractors started an indefinite hungerstrike on Friday.

They have also decided to put a stop on ongoing work at various LDA construction sites from Saturday.

Ajay Singh, a member of LDA Contractors' Association, said: "The LDA had stopped our payments on the pretext that they will review the quality of work carried out by contractors two years ago." The 150-odd contractors, whose payments have been withheld, had worked at various LDA schemes two years ago."During these two years, if LDA engineers were not able maintain the development works, how can the contractors be held responsible?" he asked.

Singh said on Thursday, the contractors had tried to meet LDA Vice-Chairman Mukesh Kumar Meshram and Secretary Mani Prasad Mishra — only to be turned away by both officials.

"The association has decided to stop the ongoing development works in all housing schemes and beg for money at the LDA office gates on Saturday," he added.

According to Meshram, however, the contractors do not have sufficient documents to prove that they had worked on LDA schemes. two years ago. "Another thing that raises suspicion is why their payments have not cleared in the last two years? This means there must have been some valid reasons for not making the payments," he added.

Now, panels comprising engineers will inspect all those areas where the contractors had worked two years ago. "If it is found that construction works have been conducted properly, payments will be cleared," Meshram said.

Chief engineer and executive engineers have been asked to regularly monitor the ongoing works on LDA schemes and submit their report with vice-chairman's office. "Constructions done at sites will be photographed to avoid any irregularity," Meshram said.

Heading: CSMMU docs on strike, Emergency shut down - Indian Express
Content:
Two premier laboratories of Lucknow bagged national awards on the occasion of Council for Scientific and Industrial Research's (CSIR) foundation day.

The the CSIR's Technology Award for Innovation was conferred on the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) for its discovery of Guggulsterone — a lipid-lowering antiodote for patients with high cholesterol levels — and development of analogues with novel action mechanism as hypolipidemic agent. The Lucknow-based Central Institute for Medicinal and Aromatic Plants (CIMAP) was jointly awarded Innovations for Rural Development Award with Central Salt and Marine Chemicals Research Institute.

The CIMAP received the award for its concept of bio-village. Speaking on the occasion, eminent neuroscientist and president of National Brain Research Centre, P N Tandon, said the country was falling behind in the global scientific arena.

Urging the national laboratories to partner with the industry for making the research products available to the masses, Tandon said: "We need to be aware of the requirements of the market, the people of our country."

He also advised the scientific community to work together. "In today's science, individuals do not matter," he said.

Professor Samir Bhattacharya, Indian National Science Academy (INSA) senior scientist, rued that research by Indian scientists was taken with a pinch of salt by their global counterparts.

Heading: At last, rural UP prepares to harness the sun - Indian Express
Content:
All the doctors of Chattrapati Shahuji Mahraj Medical University (CSMMU) went on strike after police registered an FIR against some of their colleagues on Friday.

Residents doctors Durgesh and others have been accused of beating up one Alok and his wife who had blamed doctors for the death of their niece.

According to the police, 14-year-old Alka, a resident of Gonda, was admitted for treatment on September 24. On Friday morning, her condition deteriorated and she died.

After registering a case against Alok for misbehaviour, the doctors of the medicine ward announced a strike on Friday evening, demanding adequate security. Within hours, they were joined by colleagues from other departments.The administration too, came out in their support.

The gates of the Emergency ward has been shut and the doctors plan to met the Vice-Chancellor on Saturday.

"Doctors do their best to save the life of a patient and the attendants beat them up. Do you expect the doctors to continue to work like this?" said Dr Saroj Chooramani, Vice-Chancellor of CSMMU. "The doctors have demanded security and the administration is working out the modalities, but how much would solve the problem?" she added.

Heading: Singapore basks in glow of dazzling F1 debut - Indian Express
Content:
No longer will the 40, 000 villagers in six districts of the state have to live in the dark. With the Aryavart Gramin Bank's solar home lighting scheme, 2,500 villages with partial or no electrification have opted for a subsidised solar unit.

The unit, offered by the bank in association with the manufacturer — Tata BP Solar — has been installed in villages like Kursi, Rasulabad, Miaganj, Newarsiwa and Gorwa near Hardoi.

Over 15,000 solar panels have been installed and by October, over 25,000 houses will be powered by solar energy, said N C Khulbe, Chairman, Aryavart Gramin Bank.

The unit, comprising a 35 watt panel, 12 volt battery, a charge controller and two CFL bulbs, can run a table fan, mobile charger, black and white telivision and two bulbs.

"It can provide light for a minimum of 5 hours a day and remains charged for 3 days," said Khulbe. Every month, eight litres of kerosene is used in lamps and generators, to power up a home for a mere two hours every night. With solar power, the bank claims 8,45,856 litres of kerosene can be saved annually.

The unit will cost Rs 13,520 and is being offered for an EMI of Rs 245, repayable in 5 years. The bank has set up a call centre at Lucknow to record all complaints regarding the unit.

"If the loan repayment history is good, other banks will also show enthusiasm," said Khulbe. The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development has authorised other regional and co-operative banks to replicate this scheme, which has been included in the mid-term review of the Monetary and Credit Policy of 2007-08.

To learn the techniques of maintening the solar panels — made of fragile photovoltaic cells — Tata BP Solar is training 20 youths in each of the six districts. The company equips each engineer with a kit worth Rs 10,000 and a cellphone.

The scheme also provides a consumer the opportunity to earn carbon credits. "Once 70,000 solar power units are sold, we will be able to offer them carbon credits," said Amit Kumar, deputy general manager and head of north India operations, Tata BP Solar.

The bank was recently awarded the Ashden accolade for excellence in the field of sustainable and green energy. The prize money — Rs 17 lakh — will be invested in training programmes and promotional activities to increase demand for solar units.

Heading: 'I have no sensitive information about Team India' - Indian Express
Content:
Formula One's first night race received a collective thumbs up from teams and drivers on Friday, with the Singapore Grand Prix delivering on its promise of a floodlit spectacular.

Tens of thousands of fans packed into stands along the street circuit for the opening practice sessions, roaring with excitement as the cars streaked through the city-state's business district and marina area.

Against the backdrop of Singapore's stunning skyline, skyscrapers framed by 1,600 light projectors to illuminate the 5.067km track, championship leader Lewis Hamilton posted the fastest time of the day ahead of Ferrari's Felipe Massa and Renault's Fernando Alonso.

Hamilton described the circuit as "an amazing venue" and said it presented a much tougher physical challenge than other street circuits such as Monaco.

"It's a very physical circuit -- more than I expected, actually," the McLaren driver said. "I'd say it requires double the energy of Monaco over a single lap."

'LIKE A MOVIE'

Mercedes motorsport vice-president Norbert Haug was full of praise for the Singapore setting and gave it a glowing review.

"Atmospherically probably the best pictures ever seen in F1," he said. "The scenery -- it's unreal, it's like in a movie. It's a big, big step forward for Formula One."

Ferrari's world champion Kimi Raikkonen enjoyed the experience of driving at speeds approaching 300kph under the artificial lights.

"The visibility is great and you don't really feel you are driving at night with all the lights on the track," said the Finn.

"Overall I think we will be competitive."

BMW-Sauber's Robert Kubica and Nick Heidfeld were just off the pace of the leading trio but were happy with the conditions. Team Technical Director Willy Rampf said Singapore had become the marquee race on the calendar.

"The atmosphere is fantastic, the style of the place is unique," he added.

"This was a good start to what will become the most exceptional race weekend of the year."

Heading: Saina crashes out of the China Masters semis - Indian Express
Content:
Clearing all rumours about his role as a double agent, former India coach Greg Chappell said he possesses no classified information about the Indian team, and if he did, would not hand it over to his new employer Australia.

Chappell, who stepped down as coach of the Indian team more than 18 months ago, is presently touring with Ricky Ponting's men as an assistant to coach Tim Nielsen.

His mere presence with the Aussies for the four-match Test series has flared up rumours that he would pass on vital information regarding the Indian outfit to Nielsen. However, Chappell, who is also advisor with the Rajasthan Cricket Academy, has rubbished such claims.

"To be quite honest we haven't discussed the Indian team. The Australians have played against India pretty regularly in recent times, I think they have got enough footage and personal experience with the Indian team to understand what they have to do," Chappell was quoted as saying by the 'Sydney Morning Herald'.

"I don't feel I have any sensitive information, and professionalism suggests there are certain things that are not available to the Australians. Anyway, there is nothing I know that they don't know," he added.

Using his influential contacts in the RCA, Chappell has managed to secure a precious extra week's preparation for the Aussies after the Champions Trophy was cancelled.

He also termed India as the 'mecca of cricket' and said, "The fact of the matter is this is the centre of the universe as far as cricket is concerned.

"If you want to be involved in cricket, India is going to be a part of it. If it wasn't for India, cricket would be a very minor game, so let's embrace that and understand that and it will put everything into perspective."

The former Australia Test skipper said although there were some bitter episodes, his tenure with the Indian team was one of his memorable experiences.

"I've had the most wonderful experience in three years in India. Sure, there were parts of it that were turbulent, but we also had some very successful times. Much as Australia is going through a transition, India is going through a transition as well, and whenever you go through that there is pain," said Chappell.

Heading: Kirsten checks out ‘bench strength’ in Irani Cup match - Indian Express
Content:
Saina Nehwal's semi-final outing in the China Masters Super Series turned out to be a lopsided affair as the ace Indian shuttler crashed out of the event after suffering a straight-game defeat at hands of her new nemesis Zhou Mi in Changzhou on Saturday.

Seventh seed Sania, who won the Chinese Taipei Grand Prix gold tournament a fortnight ago, was no match for her Hong Kong rival and surrendered 4-21 19-21 in just 26 minutes.

Zhou had cut short Saina's campaign in the first round of the Japan Super Series event last week. Zhou will take on local girl Lin Wang in the fight for the silverware. Lin prevailed over compatriot Yihan Wang 21-14 18-21 21-11 in the other semi-final.

Saina, who made it to the quarterfinals of Beijing Olympics, turned out to be an easy prey for sixth seed Zhou as the Indian could not match her opponent in any aspect of the game.

Zhou's played brilliantly at the net play and her smashes left the Indian gasping. The Hong Kong girl registered 11 smash winners, compared to five Saina.

Zhou's winners at the net ware also double the Indian's number. She won 15 points at the net in the entire match, while Saina could manage only seven.

Heading: Munaf fined 75% of match fee for abusing Sehwag - Indian Express
Content:
Irani Cup gave Gary Kirsten a chance to find out if he has the right ammunition to blow away Australia's redoubtable batting line-up in the upcoming Test series and the India coach says from whatever he saw over the last four days, he has no reason to be worried.

"Barring (last minute) injuries, the bowling unit looks in good shape," Kirsten said after Rest of India beat Delhi to lift the Irani Cup in Vadodara on Saturday.

For the winners, Zaheer Khan and Munaf Patel were among wickets, while Ishant Sharma stood out for Delhi with his hostile spells. Among the spinners, both Anil Kumble and Harbhajan Singh made their mark and Kirsten said he was happy with their intensity.

"I'm very happy with the way they went about their business. All of them looked in good form here and they were hitting the right areas. I'm also happy with the great intensity they showed here and they should feel confident.

"We still have 12 days before the first Test against Australia and we have to make sure that our preparation is right up there," Kirsten said.

The South African said Irani Cup proved a good dress rehearsal for the Australia series and the players need to carry the momentum.

"It was good match practice, the ideal simulation you can have. Australia are a competitive side, very organised. We have to maintain our focus and play good, positive cricket. We need to continue the momentum there," he said.

Kirsten refused to comment on the spat between Virender Sehwag and Munaf Patel, saying, "Match officials are taking care of that. We need to maintain our focus for the exciting series against Australia."

Kirsten donned the pads and gloves after the match and batted against Anil Kumble and Chetanya Nanda and had a word of praise for the Delhi leggie, who grabbed eight wickets in the match.

"He looks a good bowler and bowls a consistent line and length. He has got good pace as well. It was a great opportunity for him to bowl against some of the best batsmen and he impressed," Kirsten said.

Heading: Sehwag left Vadodara due to 'migraine' - Indian Express
Content:
Rest of India pacer Munaf Patel was fined 75 per cent of his match fee on Saturday for abusing Delhi captain Virender Sehwag during the Irani Cup.

Match referee R R Jadeja refused to disclose the fine but it was learnt that Munaf was docked 75 per cent match fee. "I am sending a report to the BCCI and I cant disclose its content," Jadeja said.

Asked who were present in the hearing, Jadeja said "Delhi were represented by coach Vijay Dahia, while Rest of India captain Anil Kumble, senior player Rahul Dravid and Munaf also attended the season."

Munaf had a altercation with Delhi opener Akash Chopra, forcing Sehwag to intervene. The pacer reportedly mouthed something foul to Sehwag, which infuriated the Delhi camp.

Subsequently Sehwag lodged an official complain with the match referee and hearing took place today after Rest of India beat Delhi within 4 days to lift the Irani Cup.

Incidentally, this is not the first time that the temperamental pacer has found himself in a spot of bother. During the recent ODI series in Sri Lanka, Munaf was found guilty of verbally abusing Gamini Silva after the Lankan umpire had turned down a leg before appeal.

Heading: BCCI to support CA in hosting Aussie version of 'IPL' - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi captain Virender Sehwag returned home midway through the Irani Cup owing to migraine and not because of any dissent, a senior team official said.

Delhi and District Cricket Association (DDCA) Sports secretary Sunil Dev said Sehwag returned with him on Friday night due to migraine and nothing else.

"He has not been feeling well and the pain was there all along. It increased yesterday and because he has already been dismissed in the second innings, he could well afford to return with me," Dev said from New Delhi.

Sehwag's abrupt return led to wild speculations in Vadodara with some claiming that the Delhi captain left in a huff to protest the poor accommodation and fuming why they were not accommodated in the same hotel where Rest of India players are staying.

A few also claimed that Sehwag was bitter after being abused by Munaf Patel and hence once he got out in the second innings, he didn't want to stay longer in the city.

Dev, however, dismissed such speculations and said, "This is all nonsense. He never had an issue with hotel and he returned purely because he was not feeling well and circumstances allowed him to comeback."

Heading: Srikkanth replaces Dilip, becomes new chief selector - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Cricket Board Vice President Lalit Modi has extended every possible support to Cricket Australia in its endeavour to organise a world-class domestic Twenty20 tournament next year.

Inspired by the success of the Indian Premier League, the CA is planning to beef up its domestic Twenty20 competition by hosting a glittering event, featuring the world's best teams in 2009-10.

Ensuring his full support, Modi, the chairman of the Indian Premier League said Indians stars like Sachin Tendulkar, Harbhajan Singh and Mahendra Singh Dhoni are free to play for Australian state teams if they wish to.

"We are very excited they are doing that. We understand they are looking at a franchise model, developing other models, too," Modi told 'The Daily Telegraph'.

"We are keenly watching that and are most supportive of that. The Australian Cricket Board has been most supportive of the Indian cricket board. They have asked us already if we would release our players for that and we said yes," he added.

However, the marketing guru of the BCCI whose brainchild the IPL is, said CA can never never ask for share in the financial exploits of the IPL.

"It's a domestic tournament. When county cricket (in England) was going well for hundreds of years, we never got the spoils.

"You have to understand, Indian cricket never made money until three or four years ago. It was always England first, Australia second, South Africa third and then India would get a little bit of money. Our market has developed, our game has developed," he said.

Modi feels that cricket has the potential to have domestic Twenty20 competitions in the mould of major soccer leagues.

"I think if you look at the soccer leagues around the world, you have the English Premier League, you have the Bundesliga in Germany, the Italian, the Spanish leagues. You have rugby going on in various countries," he said.

"I think each country will develop talent. It may not be on the same scale as the IPL. It may not be eight, 10 or 12 teams, but it may be six teams in Australia."

Heading: BCCI calm about ICC-ICL meeting - Indian Express
Content:
Former India captain Krishnamachari Srikkanth on Saturday became the new Chairman of the National Senior Cricket Selection Committee, replacing Dilip Vengsarkar at the helm of affairs.

He was appointed as the chief selector at the BCCI's 79th Annual General Meeting in Mumbai, BCCI sources said.

Raja Venkat (East Zone), Surendra Bhave (West Zone), Narendra Hirwani (Central Zone) and Yashpal Sharma (North Zone) are the other four selectors.

Former Mumbai and India pace bowler Abui Kuruvilla was chosen as the junior selection panel chief at the two-day meeting, the sources said.

The other junior selectors picked include Sanjay Desai (South Zone), Sanjeev Sharma (North Zone), Rajesh Bora (East Zone) and R S Hans (Central Zone).

Sharad Pawar, who stepped down as the Board President at the AGM and was succeeded by Shashank Manohar, will head the BCCI's Marketing Committee, while Rajiv Shukla was elected as Chairman of the Finance Committee.

N Srinivasan was elected as the Secretary, Sanjay Jagdale became the new Joint Secretary and M P Pandove will be the new Treasurer. The trio was elected unopposed, they said.

Also elected unopposed were the five Vice-Presidents -- Shivlal Yadav, Chirayu Amin, Arindam Ganguly, Arun Jaitley and Lalit Modi, the sources said.

Heading: Australia await security update after New Delhi blast - Indian Express
Content:
The BCCI, which has banned players who took part in the rebel Indian Cricket League, said on Saturday that it had no issues with the upcoming meeting between the International Cricket Council chief David Morgan and ICL owner Subhash Chandra.

"There's nothing wrong in that meeting. Mr Morgan will give details of what was discussed at his meeting with Mr Subash Chandra at the ICC meeting scheduled on October 14 and 15 in Dubai," said BCCI president Shashank Manohar just hours after taking over the reins from Sharad Pawar in Mumbai on Saturday.

Manohar also dismissed reports of the Sri Lankan board allowing its ICL-aligned players to play in the island nation's domestic cricket by saying it was an internal matter.

"It's an internal matter of Sri Lanka Cricket and we have nothing do do with it," he replied curtly to a query on the subject in his first media conference after becoming the BCCI chief.

Manohar also dismissed as "his private opinion" BCCI CAO Ratnakar Shetty's statement to a TV channel that the Rajasthan Cricket Association was going out of its way to oblige Australian cricketers by extending top-class training facilities to the visitors.

Pawar too set aside notions in the wake of Shetty's criticism that the BCCI was not happy with the top-class training facilities afforded to the Australians at Jaipur.

"The BCCI is not unhappy. They are our guests and as per our Indian tradition we extend our hospitality to the visiting guests," he said on the raging debate.

Earlier, RCA chief and BCCI Vice-President Lalit Modi too defended the decision by saying it was not wrong at all. "I don't see anything wrong in it. This is a unique year in that Australia had time on their hand with the cancellation of the Champions Trophy. They wanted to get acclimatised to our conditions and wickets and approached me (as RCA President) and I saw no reason to deny them." Modi had said at a media conference two days ago.

Heading: BCCI launches official website - Indian Express
Content:
The touring Australian team said they were awaiting a security update from Cricket Australia (CA) after a bomb blast in a New Delhi marketplace on Saturday.

The Australians were playing a warm-up match against a local side in Jaipur when the incident occurred in New Delhi, where the third Test is to be staged.

"If we have to do anything besides the normal security drill, we will do only after getting instructions from CA," Australia's spokesman Matthew Slade said.

The first Test starts in Bangalore on Oct 9.

Senior BCCI official Rajeev Shukla said in Mumbai: "The Australians should not fear about their security. We are in touch with the Home Ministry. There is no need to panic."

Australia were bowled out for 218 in their warm-up match against Rajasthan Cricket Academy.

Heading: Rest of India lift Irani Cup as Delhi capitulates - Indian Express
Content:
After a long delay, the Cricket Board finally launched its official website today following the conclusion of its 79th AGM at which Shashank Manohar took over as its President from Sharad Pawar.

The BCCI website, www. bcci.tv, will offer millions of Indian cricket fans across the world deferred streaming video and mobile content apart from 'live' scoreboard of matches, player interviews, profiles, statistics and fan interaction.

The website is being produced and maintained by Global Cricket Ventures, which also manages the official IPL site www.iplt20.com, as per a ten-year agreement it has signed with the BCCI. Pawar said that it will help in bringing Indian cricket fans closer to the game.

"I'm happy that this alliance between Global Cricket Ventures and the BCCI will further significantly enrich the user experience for the Indian cricket fans around the world with a direct window to the on-field action through next generation technologies", he said.

"I'm certain the forthcoming India-Australia series itself will generate a lot of traffic to the BCCI website," said Satyajit Swaminathan, president of GCV.

Heading: McCain, Obama spar on spending, taxes - Indian Express
Content:
Gautam Gambhir (91) stood tall amid ruins but his teammates could not show the same belligerent obduracy as Rest of India trampled Delhi by 187 runs to lift the Irani Cup with more that one day to spare at the IPCL Stadium in Vadodara on Saturday.

Seven wickets separated Anil Kumble's men from an imminent win while Delhi pinned its hopes on Gambhir to score another 268 runs for an improbable victory. In the end, the miracle Delhi needed never happened and Rest of India shot out the Ranji Champions for 190 in their second innings.

After his defiant 176-ball knock, which had 12 fours in it, Gambhir at least returned with the satisfaction that he didn't let down his team. The same, however, could not be said of his team-mates, who made a meek capitulation in the face of adversity.

Gambhir waged a grim battle, flaying the Rest of India attack even though his team-mates kept coming and going at the other end. He ran down Zaheer Khan through the slips and walked cut fiercely to add salt to the wound.

Gambhir also walked out to thrash Munaf Patel through onside and disdainfully hit RP Singh to find the long on fence.

All along, his partners kept changing at the other end. Aakash Chopra, who did not open on Friday after having twisted his ankle, took to the field with Virat Kohli in tow as his runner. But the gritty right-hander returned with a golden duck against his name, dragging the first ball he faced, from Zaheer, onto the stumps.

Veteran of many a battle, Mithun Manhas (12) wanted to leave Harbhajan Singh's first delivery of the day but the ball kissed the blade and flew to Rahul Dravid at slips.

Having removed Rajat Bhatia with his previous delivery on Friday, the off-spinner was on a hat-trick but next man in Puneet Bisht (9) foiled the bid.

Harbhajan was exasperate to see the diminutive Delhi stumper getting two lives - first Mahendra Singh Dhoni dropped him behind the stumps and then S Badrinath grassed one at leg slip - but the offie eventually had the last laugh.

Bisht forgot he needed to hang around to lend some support to Gambhir and stepped out to hit Harbhajan out of the park only to see Zaheer getting beneath the ball at mid-on.

Delhi had a tail but Kumble ensured it didn't wag. The Rest of India captain trapped Chetanya Nanda (1) and castled Pradeep Sangwan (1) before dealing the biggest blow to get rid of Gambhir.

The left-hander wanted to cut the delivery that bounced a tad more than he had expected and Dhoni didn't make any mistake in pouching the faint edge.

Harbhajan finally completed the formality by removing Ishant Sharma (0) as Rest of India tamed Delhi, with five full sessions to spare.

Harbhajan was the pick of the Rest of India bowlers, claiming four for 31, while Kumble and Zaheer got three apiece.

Heading: N-deal will deepen the strategic relationship: Rice - Indian Express
Content:
Democrat Barack Obama and Republican John McCain battled over spending, taxes and the Iraq war in their first debate on Friday, and Obama blamed the Wall Street crisis on failed Republican economic policies supported by McCain.

In a 90-minute televised debate, the two candidates repeatedly clashed over their economic and foreign policy approaches in a series of sharp exchanges that highlighted broad gulfs in their policy views.

But both men said they were optimistic Congress would come up with a $700 billion rescue plan for US financial services but agreed the huge price tag would limit their agendas as president.

McCain said he would freeze federal spending as president on most programs other than defense and veterans' care, and accused Obama of being a big-spending liberal who could not bring together Republican and Democrats.

"Senator Obama has the most liberal voting record in the Senate," McCain said. "It's hard to reach across the aisle from that far to the left."

Obama said McCain would cut taxes for the wealthy and slash corporate tax rates. He repeatedly tried to tie McCain to the policies of President George W. Bush.

"This is a final verdict on eight years of failed economic policy promoted by George Bush and supported by Senator McCain," Obama said of the economic crisis on Wall Street.

Obama, an Illinois senator, said he would not be able to do everything he wanted in his administration because of the bailout, but said McCain's proposal to freeze spending was "using a hatchet when you need a scalpel."

McCain ended days of suspense earlier on Friday when he flew to Mississippi for the debate, backing away from his promise to skip the showdown if negotiations were not completed on a rescue of the US financial industry.

The Arizona senator's campaign said enough progress had been made that he could participate in the first presidential debate, which could help decide a tight race in the Nov. 4 presidential election.

"We have finally seen Republicans and Democrats sitting down and negotiating together and coming up with a package," McCain said.

The debate was scheduled to focus on foreign policy and national security, but the turmoil on Wall Street has dominated the campaign trail for nearly two weeks and was the first topic raised.

White House talks among McCain, Obama and congressional leaders ended in disarray on Thursday with no agreement on a stalled $700 billion bailout plan proposed by the Bush administration.

'OUT OF CONTROL'

McCain, who has fought local pet spending projects in Congress, said spending restraint would be a vital part of any economic recovery. "The reason, one of the major reasons why we're in the difficulties we are in today is because spending got out of control," he said.

Obama said McCain had backed the spending plans of Bush and Republicans. "John, it's been your president who you said you agreed with 90 percent of the time who presided over this increase in spending," he said.

The debate was expected to be watched by far more than the 40 million Americans who saw the convention acceptance speeches of McCain and Obama, and could be a crucial factor for undecided voters in the Nov. 4 election.

Public opinion polls have shown Obama making gains over the past week on the question of who could best lead the country on economic issues, and most polls have Obama holding a slight and growing lead over McCain.

When the debate turned to foreign policy, Obama criticized McCain's judgment in supporting the US military invasion of Iraq. McCain has been one of the most staunch advocates of the war.

"The first question is whether we should have gone into this war in the first place," said Obama, an Illinois senator who opposed the war from the beginning.

McCain said the big question facing the next president will be "how we leave and when we leave." He said Obama had shown poor judgment by opposing the surge policy that sent more troops to Iraq and has been credited with reducing violence there.

McCain also attacked Obama for his willingness to talk with leaders of hostile nations like Iran without preconditions, but Obama pointed out that Henry Kissinger, the former secretary of state who is one of McCain's foreign policy advisers, supported the same approach.

The two candidates also clashed on Pakistan, with Obama saying the United States should attack militants in Pakistan if Islamabad was unwilling to do so. McCain said he would not back such a policy.

Heading: UK woos India to solve Wall St crisis - Indian Express
Content:
As the Congress considers the Indo-US nuclear deal, Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice lent strong support to the agreement and said its passage will clear the way to "deepen the strategic relationship" with India.

In a letter to House of Representatives Speaker Nancy Pelosi, she said Congress has an "unprecedented and historic opportunity" before it to ensure that the US and India "complete the journey we began together three years ago".

"I am writing to express my strong support for the 'United States-India Nuclear Cooperation Approval and Nonproliferation Enhancement Act'," Rice said in the letter that comes just hours after President George W Bush said his administration is "working hard" to get deal passed "as quickly as possible".

The agreement marks the culmination of a decade-long process of India's emergence on the international stage and the Indian government's "effort to steer a more pragmatic and realistic course in foreign affairs," Rice wrote to Pelosi, who is a key player in getting the deal through.

"For the United States, passage of this legislation will clear the way to deepen the strategic relationship with India," Rice said in the letter dated September 26.

She also maintained that the agreement will open significant opportunities for American firms, help meet India's surging energy requirements in an environment-friendly manner, and bring India into the "global nuclear non-proliferation mainstream".

Heading: Indian Army foils infiltration bid; fire exchanged across LoC - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to rope in countries like India to join hands in tackling the financial meltdown in the US, British Premier Gordon Brown has said it cannot be left to the elite G-8 club alone to come out with strategies and wanted the involvement of G-20, which includes developing nations, as well.

With ways to prevent recurrence of the financial crisis high on the agenda of the world leaders assembled for the UN General Assembly, the suggestion of Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, an economist-turned politician, for a new international initiative to bring structural reform in the global financial system got instant support of Brown.

During their meeting on the margins of the UN General Assembly, Brown agreed with Singh that the existing global financial architecture was not robust enough to deal with the international turbulence in financial markets.

Highlighting the need for broader strategies, Brown said the G-20 will be well-suited to deal with the problem.

Singh said restoration of financial confidence is the need of the hour for the healthy growth of the economy. He said he will be to happy to work with Britain and other countries to give his expertise and work on ways to overcome the financial crisis.

The Indian Prime Minister, a former World Bank economist, suddenly finds himself in a situation where world leaders are looking forward to him to evolve ways to deal with the financial turmoil.

US President George W Bush, who is in the midst of firefighting operations to deal with the crisis, has already set the ball rolling when he told Singh that the one person he wanted to spend time with was the Prime Minister for his calming and serene effect.

Addressing the UNGA session, Singh himself said there is a need for a new international initiative to bring structural reform in the world's financial system with more effective regulation and stronger systems of multilateral consultations and surveillance.

The explosion of financial innovation unaccompanied by credible systemic regulation has made the financial system vulnerable.

"The resulting crisis of confidence threatens global prosperity in the increasingly interdependent world in which we live," Singh said.

Brown and Singh felt it was high time there was a single monitoring mechanism for a surveillance of the world's financial system. Singh felt the system must be designed in as inclusive a manner as possible.

Singh said the existing financial system was not serving the purpose The two leaders felt that the financial meltdown earlier used to affect the periphery only but now it has hit the centre too. The financial fragility is leading to weakness of financial institutions and weakness in confidence.

The two leaders also felt that there should be better coordination for coordinated actions to increase the confidence level in the financial system. Singh was of the view that the capital has become more global and the financial system has become seamless.

There is no international regulation, the Prime Minister said. The issue of a financial crisis itself has come out on most occasions during Singh's bilateral meetings due to the Prime Minister's background as he is such a renowned economist with a lot of experience. "Of course, he said what he thought," said Foreign Secretary Shivshankar Menon.

The financial turmoil came up in Singh's discussions with World Bank President Robert Zoellick, where they went into much more detail about the role of multilateral organisations in dealing with and giving warning about such crises before they happen, Menon said.

The matter also figured in Singh's meetings with several leaders including Chinese Premier Wen Jiabao. In each case it was slightly different depending on what the nature of the conversation was. The Prime Minister is of the view that there are no simple answers on how to deal with the issue.

Heading: We will root out terrorism from India: Sonia - Indian Express
Content:
Indian troops foiled an infiltration bid by a group of armed militants on Saturday. The militants who tried to enter a border district in Jammu and Kashmir under the cover of firing by the Pakistani forces, a BSF spokesman said.

Pakistani Rangers opened fire on Chak Fagwari Border Out Post (BOP) along the International Border in Pargwal sub-sector of Jammu frontier in the wee hours of Saturday, the spokesman said.

He said a big group of militants tried to enter into Indian territory in Zeroline area under the cover of Pakistani firing.

The militants also fired and targeted troops with grenades, he said, adding that BSF troops and patrol parties retaliated the firing from the other side. The exchange of fire continued for nearly an hour, he said, adding that BSF troops also fired mortar bombs on militants.

BSF troops beat back the infiltration bid as the militants later escaped to the Pakistani side. There was no loss of life or injury in the cross-border firing and searches are being conducted in the area. The Pakistani troops also committed ceasefire violation, he said.

Earlier on August 25, three militants had infiltrated along Kanachak area after cutting fencing under cover of Pakistani firing. They were later killed in a gunbattle at Chinore area of Jammu which also left five civilians and three jawans dead.

Heading: 'NSG waiver vindication of our non-proliferation record' - Indian Express
Content:
Congress president Sonia Gandhi expressed shock over the bomb blast in Mehrauli and condemned the attack while assuring the nation that all steps would be taken to root out terrorism from the country.

"The Congress president expresses shock and desires that immediate action should be taken to nab the culprits with firmness," a party release said.

She deeply condemns the attack and reassures the nation that everything shall be done to root out terrorism from the country, it added.

Party spokesman Manish Tewari said investigations are on and those responsible for the blast will be brought to book.

Asked whether it was a terror attack, Tewari said the investigating agencies are probing it and the issue would become clear by Sunday.

"Let us not second guess the work of the investigating agencies and burden them with our theories."

Responding to a query on the demand of the BJP for resignation of Home Minister Shivraj Patil, Tewari said in the fight against terror, the entire nation should stand united.

"They (BJP) are trying to score brownie political points on the issue. How many times did L K Advani resign. It is not that bomb blasts and terror acts did not take place when he was the Home Minister," the spokesman said.

On a question on whether the blasts could have been prevented had POTA been in place, Tewari said if making laws prevented such acts, then the terror attacks during NDA's regime would not have taken place.

Asked whether an all-party meeting to discuss terror will be convened, Tewari said the Prime Minister is away and when he comes back all possible steps in this regard will be taken.

"It is the duty of the state to provide full security to every citizen," he added.

Heading: After the blast, Shivraj Patil reviews security - Indian Express
Content:
