In the BCCI's AGM on Saturday, Pawar is all set to nominate himself as the chairman of the marketing committee, taking over from BCCI vice-president Lalit Modi.

Modi, hugely responsible for why the BCCI kept laughing its way to the bank over the last couple of years, will most likely not be on the committee anymore — a move that also suggests members aren't entirely happy with Modi enjoying complete authority as far as the board's financial matters are concerned.

Also, the BCCI has made a couple of other crucial decisions, making it mandatory for all IPL-awarded contracts to enter an open bidding in future and nominating the board's secretary to sign on all IPL-related contracts henceforth. "This is to ensure that there is no favouritism," said a board official.

This could mean the Indian Premier League (IPL), which was seen as a body independent of the board's style of working and hugely under the control of its commissioner Modi, will now come under more direct control of the board.

The only respite for Modi comes with Pawar taking a softer stand on Rajasthan's Future Cricket Academy allowing the Australians world-class facilities ahead of the Test series. While certain members of the board have taken serious objection, Pawar clarified his stance saying: "It's not an issue. After all, we Indians are hospitable people."

Conflict of interest?

Now that the board has authorised the new secretary to sign on all IPL-related documents, the issue of a conflict of interest, as far as team owners and board officials go, grows bigger.

N Srinivasan, the president of the Tamil Nadu Cricket Association (TNCA), is all set to take over as the secretary, meaning he will now be the signing authority in all IPL-related decisions despite the fact that his company India Cements owns the Chennai IPL franchise. Srinivasan, apart from being the secretary, is also expected to be on the marketing committee under Pawar.

According to sources, Srinivasan wrote to Pawar asking permission to continue in the dual role and has been given the go-ahead.

Candy man

Pawar has managed to keep most factions happy. Gujarat Cricket Association president Chirayu Amin will be retained as vice-president from the west and the reason according to officials is that Amin was miffed at not being allowed to take over as the board's interim president in place of Pawar from July to September, as was discussed earlier.

Niranjan Shah, who had been lobbying for that post, has been awarded a place in the IPL Champions League governing council as vice-chairman.

Hyderabad Cricket Association (HCA) secretary Shivlal Yadav, who was once tipped to head the National Cricket Academy and had also spoken of shifting the NCA to Hyderabad, had been sidelined. But Yadav is now set to be awarded the post of the BCCI vice-president from the south zone.

Dalmiya to attend

For the first time since 2005, when Ranbir Singh Mahendra lost to Sharad Pawar in a fiercely contested election, Jagmohan Dalmiya will attend his first AGM on Saturday. Dalmiya has not decided to contest for any of the posts, nor has he nominated anybody, and the former BCCI president is most likely to be a mere spectator while Pawar will be replaced by Manohar as the board chief.

Modi, the vice-president who had always taken a hard stance against Dalmiya and highlighted the former chief's financial discrepancies, had said on Friday: "The time has come to move on. He's invited like everybody else."

Heading: SC refuses to stay publication of Nanavati report - Indian Express
Content:
Under attack from the BJP for his decision to provide legal aid to two students who have been accused of being involved in the serial bomb blasts in Delhi, Jamia Millia Islamia University vice-chancellor Prof Mushirul Hasan found a supporter in Human Resource Development Minister Arjun Singh.

Prof Hasan called on Arjun Singh on Friday to apprise him of the university's decision to provide legal assistance to Mohammad Shakil and Zia-ur Rehman who had been picked up by Delhi Police in connection with the bomb blasts earlier this month.

The HRD Minister justified Jamia's decision saying there was "nothing wrong in providing legal aid" to the students. "From what Prof Hasan has told me, I understand that the decision of the university is in the interest of the nation," he said.

The university's decision has evoked a sharp reaction from the BJP, which has accused Jamia of diverting Government funds to help terror suspects. The party also demanded the resignation of Prof Hasan.

The vice-chancellor on his part reiterated that legal aid is the constitutional right of every person.

Heading: Women to get permanent commission in four non-combat wings of Armed Forces - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Friday refused to stay the publication and circulation of the Justice G T Nanavati Commission report describing the Godhra train carnage as a "pre-planned conspiracy" and giving a clean chit to Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi regarding the subsequent riots.

The three-member Bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan issued notice to the Gujarat Government on a petition filed by an NGO, Citizens for Justice and Peace, contending that the publication of the report could disturb communal harmony.The petitioner claimed the publication of the report by the Commission would provide grounds to the state Government to take a liberal stand against the accused in the post-Godhra riots of 2002 that claimed over 1000 lives.

Before passing the order, the Bench, which also included Justices P Sathasivam and J M Panchal, asked senior advocate Rajender Sachar appearing for the Citizens for Justice and Peace if the Commission had given any specific direction to the state government for its implementation. However, when Sachar said "we have not gone through it", the Bench issued a notice and posted the matter for hearing on October 13.

Heading: Cash-in-bag: Judge wants ‘third person’ - Indian Express
Content:
Finally, the Government has decided to grant permanent commission to women officers in the three Armed Forces but with a rider — women will only be considered for permanent commission in four non-combat arms, including the Army Education Corps, Judge Advocate General and Accounts streams.

Also, 2015 is expected to be the earliest date by which women would be technically sworn in as permanent commission officers of the Armed Forces. A formal order to the effect was signed by Defence Minister A K Antony on Friday, and the three services will now work out modalities for training and induction of women officers in select branches.

Until now, the Armed Forces have been largely male-dominated with women being inducted only as short service commission officers with a service life of less than 15 years and not rising above the rank of Lt Colonel. With the permanent commission, women can now rise to the highest rank of Lt Gen.

While the ministry has given the go-ahead for permanent commission, it has left for the Armed Forces to sort out the more contentious issues like opening of the 'males-only' academies like the National Defence Academy (NDA) and Indian Military Academy (IMA) for women cadets.

Officials said there would be no reservation for women in the Armed Forces and selection would be based on a 'common merit and eligibility criteria, which would be decided by each Service Headquarters'.

However, serving women officers are likely to be disappointed as they will not be considered for permanent commission. Officials made it clear that the option for permanent commission would only be given to women officers who join the service from now on in the select branches.

While modalities will be worked out by the respective services, women will not be recruited directly as permanent officers but will be inducted into the select branches of the services through the short service commission route.

This would mean that a female candidate would first join as a short service commission officer and will be given the choice of a permanent commission only after five years of service only if there are sufficient vacancies in the Armed Forces.

In effect, the first permanent commission woman officer will not be inducted into the services till at least 2015 given a one-year training period and five years of working as a short service commission officer.

Another disappointment will be the limited branches, "which do not entail direct combat or possibility of physical contact with enemy".

Heading: Centre seeks SC help to implement smoking ban - Indian Express
Content:
Justice Nirmal Yadav of the Punjab and Haryana High Court has requested Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur to ensure that her examination by the CBI in the cash-at-judge's-door case is done "in the presence of a third person". The packet containing Rs 15 lakh in cash, which was delivered at Justice Nirmaljit Kaur's residence on August 13, was allegedly meant for Justice Nirmal Yadav.

She said the third person, who could be a judicial officer or even a high court judge, should be appointed by the Chief Justice, and would act as an independent witness during the examination. The demand has also been conveyed to the CBI, which is expected to question Justice Yadav in the near future. The CBI said it did not have any objection to the demand "as long as we get the answers to our questions".

"The demand cannot be legally challenged since she is being examined as a witness by the CBI and not as an accused," said a senior CBI official. "It appears the Judge wants to ensure that her statements during the questioning are not changed by the CBI team, keeping in view the sensitivity of the case," he added. The CBI has already questioned Justice Nirmaljit Kaur in connection with the case. According to information available with the agency, two more judges — one from the Supreme Court and one from the Punjab and Haryana High Court — were reportedly present at her residence on August 13 when the money was delivered. During the questioning, which lasted for over 30 minutes, she is learnt to have clearly denied this.

Heading: Shahabuddin gets 10 yrs in illegal arms case - Indian Express
Content:
With the October 2 deadline for implementation of smoking ban at public places drawing closer, the Centre on Friday sought the SC's intervention in ensuring that the ban was effective from the said date.

Additional Solicitor General Gopal Subramaniam submitted that various companies, similar to a petition filed in the Delhi HC this week, are trying to prevent the ban from being enforced.

The Bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan has posted the petition for September 29, when other petitions seeking transfer are also listed for hearing.

The ASG pleaded to the Bench to transfer to itself the entire petition against the anti-smoking order so that the government was not prevented from implementing the order.

Referring to earlier petitions filed by various tobacco manufacturing companies and associations challenging the packaging and labelling rules related to pictorial warnings, the ASG said the apex court had earlier stayed proceedings before various high courts.

Fresh writ petitions were still being filed in several high courts, seeking to block the implementation of the Act and the Rules, the application stated, adding that four petitions, including one each by ITC and Indian Hotels Association, had been filed in the Delhi HC.

The petitions have sought a stay on the May notification, relying heavily on the ex parte stay order passed by the Madras High Court.

While stating that the rule that bans smoking at work places was unjustified as it would include private offices as well, the petitioners alleged that under the present rules any person could detain someone who smokes in office and place him before a magistrate.

Heading: ‘The Tauqeer I knew couldn’t do this’ - Indian Express
Content:
A special court at Siwan on Friday sentenced RJD MP Mohammed Shahabuddin to 10 years simple imprisonment along with a Rs 10,000 fine in the 2005 Pratappur arms seizure case under the provisions of the Arms Act. Additional District and Sessions Judge Gyaneshwar Prasad Srivastava pronounced the sentence at a special court inside Siwan jail, where Shahabuddin has been lodged.

This is the sixth conviction in the last two years for the RJD MP including a life sentence for the murder of a CPI(ML) worker Chhote Lal Gupta. Twenty six cases of murder, extortion, kidnapping and rioting are pending before the special court. The case under the Arms Act,1959, was filed on 24 April 2005 against Shahabuddin after 200 live cartridges, one laser rifle of foreign make, foreign currency, stolen vehicles and wireless sets were seized during a raid in Pratappur by then Siwan district magistrate C K Anil and then SP Ratna Sanjay after a half-hour exchange of fire from both sides.

Reacting to the verdict, Additional Public Prosecutor Ramvilas Mahto said: "We are satisfied with the verdict". He, however, clarified that sedition charges had been dropped against the MP during the pre-chargesheet stage for lack of corroborative evidence. Shahabuddin's lawyer Abhay Kumar Rajan said they would challenge the sentence in the high court.

Heading: Rlys puts Rs 800-cr security plan on track - Indian Express
Content:
Sitting in a tiny clinic under shelves lined with medicines for common colds to kamzori, Hakeem Shahid Badr Falahi listens attentively to people and scribbles them prescriptions. Billaria is one of three places at which he sees patients — he has a second clinic near his village Manchoba, and a third in Azamgarh town, 12 km away.

Work keeps the unani doctor with a degree from Aligarh Muslim University busy, but he finds the time to follow closely news on the Delhi blasts and the investigation that has put Azamgarh on the global terror map.

Shahid Badr Falahi is a former national president of the Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI), the organization with which the Indian Mujahideen is believed to have deep fraternal ties.

"I didn't know these boys or their families but they seem to be educated and from good families. My heart says they were not involved (in the Delhi serial bombings)," says Falahi, who takes his last name from the neighbouring madrasa, Jamiatul Falah, where he studied.

"But I knew Abu Bashar. I met him at a seminar at the Madarsatul Islah in Beenapara. I remember him because he was the youngest speaker."Bashar is currently in custody for his alleged involvement in the Gujarat blasts. He studied at the Beenapara madrasa.

Falahi also remembers his association with Safdar Nagori, a former general secretary of the SIMI, and Abdus Subhan Qureshi or Tauqeer.

"Tauqeer was in SIMI. He was the editor of the English edition of our monthly magazine, Islamic Movement. I had appointed him editor. Woh ek nek aur sharif ladka tha. I have a feeling he's already in police custody. The police only highlight someone's name when they already have him or when they are sure he cannot run away."

Alleged master bombmaker Tauqeer is currently one of India's most wanted men. Nagori was arrested from a SIMI meeting in Indore in March.

Falahi shrugs off talk about his differences with Nagori — believed to be a hardliner who disagreed with Falahi's more moderate line. "I don't understand this. Pehle main garam tha, ab main naram hoon? If I was a moderate, why did the government put me in prison for 30 months?" he asks.

Falahi was arrested in Delhi on September 27, 2001, the day SIMI was banned. He was released on April 7, 2004. "The charge against me was that I made an inflammatory speech in Delhi. The police said Nagori and Shahbaz Hussain, who were present there, escaped. Shahbaz was in Lucknow all these years running a cyber café, but they could find him only now."

Falahi says the Nagori and Tauqeer he once knew could not have carried out the serial blasts. "If they have changed over the years, I can't say. Carry out investigations and if you find anyone guilty, punish them. But right now these are just allegations.

"I hear this talk about Nagori being a hardliner, but I don't know. In those days he was quite open-minded. In fact, he had a love marriage. We came to know about it only later. A love marriage is considered un-Islamic. "Maine unme Islam ki malumaat kam paayee (I found his knowledge of Islam to be limited). He couldn't read or write Urdu and knew only Hindi."

Falahi defends SIMI energetically. "SIMI's ideology has not changed. The government's agenda has changed. The BJP government wanted to follow an anti-minority agenda. And the Congress government has continued it. Nothing has been proved against SIMI. And why should you ban an organisation if you find only one or two people involved in something? Dara Singh was a member of the RSS and he killed Graham Staines in Orissa. Nathuram Godse killed Gandhiji. But was the RSS banned?"

He denies the Indian Mujahideen is a SIMI offshoot. "SIMI ceased to exist after the ban and the Indian Mujahideen is just a name floated by the agencies. Is naam ke zariye woh Mussalman naujawanon ka katl, halal kar rahe hain. Tell me, why would we carry out blasts at a time when we are so close to winning the legal battle? Do we want to spoil our own case?

"All I am saying is, don't rush to blame Muslims for every blast. Widen your scope of inquiry. Ek aankh aur aadhe dimag se dekhoge toh sach kabhi nahin dikhega (If you see with one eye and a half-closed mind, you'll never be able to see the truth)," he says.

Heading: Orissa flood victims suffer as relief measures not enough - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Railways has finally cleared a Rs 800 crore project to set up an integrated security system at over 100 railway stations across the country, including the ones located in the four metros as well as all the state capitals.

The idea to have an integrated security system at major railway stations was first considered after the 7/11 Mumbai train blasts but has remained "in the works" ever since, with the Railways failing to take a final call on the matter. The financial implication of the project, too, deterred the Railways, which had maintained that law and order was a state subject.

The project envisages setting up of a security system comprising high-end Internet Protocol-based CCTVs surveillance systems, access control systems, personal and baggage screening systems and explosive detection and disposal systems at the 100-plus "sensitive and vulnerable" railway stations across the country.

"We are looking to procure the latest technology available the world over. The plan is to have IP-based CCTVs, which have a minimum of 30 days recording facility along with inbuilt intelligent software like motion detector alarm, image identification and classification, intrusion detection, image tracking and traffic density monitoring. These CCTVs will also have features like pop-up signals for particular kinds of activities that the camera observes," a senior railway official told The Indian Express.

"The final stamp of approval from the Railway Board has been received and we are now sending out instructions to all the general managers of the Zonal Railways to implement the project and invite tenders. The funds for procurement will be made available by the Railway Board," the official said.

For the suburban railway stations at Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai, the Railways have decided to take the Public Private Partnership (PPP) route to implement this system.

Under the Build, Own, Operate and Transfer (BOOT) model, private players will be engaged to install, operate and maintain security devices like CCTVs, X-ray baggage screeners, door-frame metal detectors (DFMD), explosive vapour detectors and vehicle scanners at these stations for a fixed term.

Preliminary estimates suggest that around Rs 100 crore each worth of investments will be made for installing these systems in the suburban networks of each of the four metros.

For the remaining railway stations, the ministry has decided to go in for outright purchase of security equipment, as many of these stations are unlikely to attract private investments.

Heading: Birpur engineers left out of Kosi breach repair work - Indian Express
Content:
His hut reduced to a heap of mud and straw by the overflowing Chitroptala river, when Nilamani Samal, 75, fled from Bichana village of Garadpur block in Kendrapara district, he did so with hopes of finding a refuge that would not collapse around him and his family.

Seven days later, Samal and nine of his family members crouched for space under a torn polythene sheet that did little to protect them from the lashing rain. "I can stay hungry for a few more days, but we can't survive like this for long," said a visibly ill Samal. His plight reflects that of many of other people here, who are as much victims of a fragile relief machinery as they are of the floods, especially in the coastal districts of Kendrapara, Cuttack, Jagatgsinghpur and Puri.

On Friday, even though the waters of the Mahanadi showed signs of receding, the devastation wrought by the floods has not abated. The death toll mounted to 61 as floodwater entered more villages in the Mahanadi deltaic region through 459 breaches on the embankments. So far 41.33 lakh people and 1.35 lakh houses in 19 districts have been affected, while over 8 lakh people in 740 villages remain cut off from the rest of the world. Despite these figures, Additional Relief Commissioner Benudhar Dash told The Indian Express: "Everyone has got relief. Water is receding. Don't bother about small details. The situation is perfectly normal."

By this, he may mean that most areas of Kendrapara still can't be reached while all that that the worst-affected Gop and Nimapara blocks in Puri have are five flimsy country boats. Several villages of Garadpur, one of the most harshly-hit areas in Kendrapara are still out of reach while a few like Bichana are subsisting on scraps of flattened rice and jaggery.

Although Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Manmohan Samal said the Government was rushing more food for victims, it is clearly not enough. In certain Dalit hamlets in Kalapatna gram panchayat under Puri's Nimapara block, for example, there is next to nothing by way of aid. "The relief work started and ended with that (flattened rice). Whatever relief came to Puri, nothing dripped down to these villages. The Dalit families are hungry and without even a polythene sheet over their heads," said Bhramarabara Jethi, an NGO worker in Puri.

Heading: 7 ‘HuJI’ men shot in Assam encounter - Indian Express
Content:
The Bihar Government might have left it to a judicial commission to decide on any "individual or institutional failure" behind for the Kosi breach, but the Water Resources Ministry does not seem to be in a mood to sit back and wait for the final report.

As a first step, the ministry has not included engineers from the Birpur Barrage in armouring of the breached bank and pilot channel digging, currently underway.

Kosi Project's Birpur office is headed by a chief engineer. Under him is a superintending engineer, barrage. Kushaha, Kunauli and Nirmali divisions under the barrage have an executive engineer each as their heads. All these officials, including chief engineer R C Prasad, have been working either from Supual or Nirmali. Not a single of these officials has been considered for the post-breach work.

In fact, engineers from Kosi project's Darbhanga and Purnea office have been called to oversee the repair work.

While Darbhanga chief engineer G L Basak and his team of executive and assistant engineers have been supervising the repair work at 12 points of eastern bank at Kushaha and Purnea, chief engineer R P Ram's team is in charge of repair from 13.9 point of the breached eastern bank.

The teams are also taking care of pilot channels being dug from western side near Lokahi, Nepal, to take the river's course towards the barrage. A 50-feet-wide channel has already been dug for 3 km from Lokahi side.

When asked, Water Resources Minister Bijendra Yadav played down the "sidelining" Birpur/ Kushaha engineers, saying the Government needed "experts" and hence engaged Purnea and Darbhanga teams. "We cannot call it a punishment. We just wanted our best teams to get the work done," he said.

However, the minister could not explain why the government did not use the "expertise" of these teams when spurs were being eroded by Kosi's current from August 6 till the breach on August 18. He also had no answer if Birpur and Kushaha engineers were "incompetent and inefficient".

Heading: Meghalaya cuts perks for corporation, board heads under pressure from NGOs - Indian Express
Content:
Security forces gunned down as many as seven suspected Bangladeshi HuJI terrorists in the Bashbari reserved forest in Dhubri district of Lower Assam early Friday morning. The army also recovered several arms and ammunition from them. The incident occurred at around 3:30 am after the terrrorists crossed the Indo-Bangladesh border late Thursday night.

The seven suspects, whose identities are yet to be confirmed, were killed after they stepped into an ambush the troops of the 21 Jat regiment had laid out for them following specific information.

"While the incident occurred in the wee hours today, the troops recovered various documents that proved they had freshly entered from Bangladesh," Col Rajesh Kalia, spokesman for the army's Four Corps headquarters at Tezpur said. The documents included receipts of hotels in Bangladesh apart from SIM cards of Grameen Phone of Bangladesh, he added.

The army also recovered four revolvers and two pistols from them apart from one fully timed IED and several smaller explosive devices. Over 20,000 Bangladesh Taka, Indian currency notes worth Rs Rs 4,100 and Bangladeshi bus tickets were also recovered from them. The encounter took place about 15 kms from the Indo-Bangladesh border.

The authorities however are yet to ascertain where the suspected HuJI militants were heading to. "Since all the seven members of the group have been killed, there was no immediate clue about where they came from or where they were heading to," the army spokesman said.

Heading: Threat mail to Advani: student sent to 14-day police custody - Indian Express
Content:
Bowing to pressure from NGOs, the Meghalaya government has decided to cut down the expenditure on political appointees heading various boards and corporations. There are as many as 82 political appointees who are holding offices of chairman and deputy chairman of boards and corporations in the present MPA government.

The Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) and the United Democratic Party, both part of the incumbent Meghalaya Progressive Alliance, had, as part of the Opposition when the Congress-led Meghalaya Democratic Alliance (MDA) was in power, criticised the ruling dispensation's decision to appoint 105 of its members to these posts, terming it as "wasteful expenditure". However, these parties were quick to appoint as many as 82 of their partymen to these posts when they took over the reins of government from the Congress coalition in March.

The government's double standards invited the wrath of several NGOs who claimed that the current government was no different from its predecessor and threatened to launch an agitation unless the MPA scaled down the expenditure incurred on these posts.

The MPA Government has, in response, decided to reduce the honorarium, house rent and also restrict tours of these appointees. MPA spokesperson Paul Lyngdoh said that the government was aware of the weak financial position of the state and by its decision to cut down the facilities and curbs enjoyed by these politicians would save the state exchequer close to 3.50 crore annually.

Heading: Police track train ticket trail - Indian Express
Content:
Thirty-two-year-old law student Mominul Haque, who has reportedly confessed to sending an email claiming to be an Indian Mujahideen (IM) field commander and threatening to kill BJP leader L K Advani, has been remanded to 14 days police custody.

Haque was produced before the Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) on Friday. According to sources, an anti-terror police team is coming from New Delhi soon to interrogate Haque.

Meghalaya Inspector General S B Singh said: "We are trying to establish whether Haque has links with either the IM or the SIMI." He said the email which was sent from a cybercafe located in Laban is being compared with the other emails sent by the IM before and after the blasts that took place in Delhi, Surat and other places.

The investigators will also try to find out whether Haque was working alone or not. The Ministry of Home Affairs has been alerted about the threat to Advani and Singh said: "We have informed the Union Home Ministry and we are working together with the central agencies to get to the bottom of the email."

It is learnt that a team of the National Security Guards (NSG) will be arriving in the city before the scheduled visit of Advani on September 29.

Heading: Sadiq, Atif picked recruits, formed ‘Sanjarpur group’ - Indian Express
Content:
When the alleged Indian Mujahideen (IM) operatives involved in the Ahmedabad and New Delhi terror strikes travelled between the two cities, they used "conventional" or common Hindu names while booking railway tickets for themselves, said sources in the Mumbai Police. The tickets were booked from New Delhi, they added.

The details of the railway bookings will be included in key evidence against the arrested five men. "After planting the IEDs in Ahmedabad, a group of eight IM operatives boarded the Rajdhani from Surat and left for Delhi. Atif, who was killed in the Delhi encounter, was one of them," said a senior police official.

One group is believed to have boarded the Rajdhani from New Delhi station, while another group boarded the August Kranti Rajdhani from Nizamuddin station. "The tickets were booked under conventional Hindu names, ending with surnames such as Gupta, Sharma and Agarwal, to evade any sort of surveillance. The tickets were booked from Delhi," said the police official.

Following the arrest of the five alleged IM terrorists earlier this week, the police had claimed that they had busted the backbone of the organisation and that the arrested group was involved in all major blasts in the country since 2005. With the onus now on the police to back these claims, details of railway bookings to establish the presence of certain accused in a city on a certain date would serve as crucial evidence.

"The process of collecting evidence is already underway, and we have substantial evidence. One such piece of evidence we have are the railway bookings of the accused. We know exactly when and from where their tickets were booked," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria, not willing to divulge any specific details.

The police have also ascertained the source of the consignment of explosives and firearms recovered from the accused. "We know that the gelatin and ammonium nitrate was sourced from Mangalore, and we have the precise location. The sub-machine carbine seized was also sourced from Mangalore," said Maria.

Whenever the group required explosives, Mohammed Sadiq Shaikh would allegedly call Roshan Khan alias Riyaz Bhatkal, who in turn would ask him to send some men to Mangalore. Bhatkal would provide a PCO telephone number, with orders to call when the consignment could be received.

Heading: After Buddha’s appeal, Govt, Tatas to meet tomorrow - Indian Express
Content:
The "Sanjarpur group" came into being when Sadiq Sheikh — allegedly the key operator of Indian Mujahideen — and Atif Amin — who was killed in the Delhi encounter— met at a religious gathering at Azamgarh's Beena Para in 2006.

The intelligence unit gathering details about the terror module claimed that Sadiq recruited men from Sanjarpur who were living in Mumbai. Atif prepared them for "jihad". A founder-member of Indian Mujahideen (IM) as per the Mumbai police, Sadiq had begun making frequent visits to his village, Para, in Azamgarh's Sarai Meer. The idea was to take stock of the new recruits.

From about once a year, the visits became more frequent after 2006, said intelligence sources. Atif reported to Sadiq — in Azamgarh and later in Delhi.

Sadiq's maternal grandparents still live in Sanjarpur township. But he spent most of his time with Atif and one Saif at the former's home in Sarai Meer, mostly interviewing the new recruits. Atif's family had shifted to Sarai Meer from Sanjarpur five years ago.

Shahid, the leader of the community at Para, said Sadiq visited them last on August 20. On August 22, he had left for Mumbai with his parents. The house has been locked since.

Born and brought up in Mumbai, the boy belonged to a family of repute, said Shahid. His elder brother Mohammad Arshad is an engineer based in Muscat while another, Mohammad Arif, also an engineer, works in Singapore. Sadiq and the youngest brother, Tahir, were employed with private organisations in Mumbai. Sadiq was married five years ago and has a daughter, he added.

Another youth arrested in Mumbai, Zakir, has his roots in village Kanwra, near Para.

Md Abid of Kanwra said Zakir (32) was the youngest of five brothers and had completed his graduation from Shibli National College. Two years ago, he shifted to Mumbai to live with his brothers. His father, Abdul Haq and his mother had come back to the village from Surat, where they had settled earlier. Around two months ago, they, too, shifted to Mumbai.

The police are yet to trace the Azamgarh roots of two other men arrested in Mumbai — Arif Sheikh and Md Ansar — as their families had shifted a long time ago.

Heading: LF Govt faces Forward Bloc threat over German company - Indian Express
Content:
Following Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's personal letter to Ratan Tata on Friday, urging him to reconsider Tata Motors' apparent resolve to abandon work at the Nano car plant in Singur, the company has agreed to participate in a meeting with the CM and other officials on September 28.

At a CPI(M) state secretariat meeting held on Friday morning at Alimuddin Street, the Chief Minister told his party colleagues that even though the chances of the Tatas staying on in West Bengal were very slim, the Government would do its best to keep the Nano project in the state.

Quoting Buddhadeb's letter to Ratan Tata, Commerce and Industries Minister Nirupam Sen said: "You will not encounter any problems in continuing work at Singur. There are adequate security arrangements. If needed security can be increased¿ (the) people of Singur as well as the state want the Nano plant to stay in West Bengal."

Sen as well as Left Front chairman Biman Bose also appealed to the Tatas along the same lines. "The opinion of a handful of people cannot be held as the ultimate decision. Out of 13,000 land losers, 11,000 had accepted compensation. So how can one say that majority do not want the Nano plant?" said Sen. Biman Bose, on the other hand, said, "I can understand that the small car will miss its deadline but I still fell that the Tatas should stay in Bengal."

Meanwhile, Trinamool chief, Mamata Banerjee remained defiant in her speech after the Trinamool Congress held a protest rally in front of the Tata plant earlier in the day. "What is the problem if the Tatas leave? There are many investors who want to invest in West Bengal," she said. Nonetheless, she also made an attempt to deflect any 'blame' on herself for the company's exit. "The Tatas have already acquired agricultural land. If they leave now, Bengal will have neither the factory nor the farmers their land. Bengal will have neither industry nor agriculture. The West Bengal Government should be held responsible for this, not me," she said.

Heading: BJP, Left slam PM’s ‘love’ for Bush - Indian Express
Content:
The Forward Bloc, the second largest constituent of West Bengal's Left Front Government, announced on Friday night that the party's four ministers would not attend office from Monday in protest against the use of "discretionary powers" by Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee in granting the Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee (APMC) license to German wholesale major Metro Cash & Carry.

The Forward Bloc ministers also threatened to resign if the CM did not immediately revoke the licence order, which is supposed to come through by September 30. The party, did not say anything about withdrawing from the coalition. The crisis snowballed after a Forward Bloc state secretariat meeting earlier in the day decided against granting the APMC licence to Metro Cash & Carry. The licence had been withdrawn in June 2007, but the German company had been pushing aggressively to have it renewed. As the FB had reservations, the CPI(M) had convened a bi-partite meeting on September 28 to sort out differences.

However, despite the party's stand, the CM used his discretionary powers and issued an order to the state Chief Secretary asking him to take the necessary steps to get the APMC licence issued to Metro Cash & Carry by September 30. "If the licence is still not withdrawn, our ministers will resign from the Government. He made it evident he will take the final call and we will have to toe the line. The CM cannot issue such diktats. We want to know from Biman Bose (LF chairman) if the party stands by the CM's decision," said Ashok Ghosh, general secretary, All India Forward Bloc.

Although Biman Bose declined to comment, other Left Front partners were divided on the issue. Manju Majumdar, CPI general secretary, said the decision of the Forward Bloc was "unfortunate but the problem can be solved through a bipartite meeting. Manoj Bhattacharjee, central committee member of the RSP, said, "These sorts of unilateral decisions are not acceptable in a coalition".

Heading: Kalyan in mind, BJP still undecided on alliance in Haryana, UP - Indian Express
Content:
Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's remarks that the people of the country "deeply love" US President George W Bush on Friday drew strong reactions from the Opposition BJP and the Left. While the BJP condemned the remarks as sycophancy, the Left termed them "unbecoming of his office".

The BJP said the PM should not to be carried away by the charm of Bush. "Diplomacy should not be carried to the extent of sycophancy. The fact remains that the country is divided on the n-deal," BJP spokesperson Rajiv Pratap Rudy said.

Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of a function here, CPI(M) General Secretary Prakash Karat said, "Everybody knows that the PM loves President Bush. But why should he bring the people of India in it."

The ruling Congress, meanwhile, saw "nothing wrong" in the PM's remark but was non-committal on the party's stance on whether it endorsed the PM's views. "What is wrong in it? India does not believe in hate culture," AICC media cell chairperson M Veerappa Moily said at a press briefing.

Faced with a barrage of questions on whether the Congress believes that the people of India love Bush, a visibly exasperated Moily shot back, "If the people of India love him, the Congress loves him, the BJP loves him and the NDA loves him."

CPI National Secretary D Raja said the PM's comments "do not augur well" for his position.

Heading: The Thana That Stands On A Sewer - Indian Express
Content:
Though scouting for allies, the BJP on Friday was unable to take a decision vis-à-vis UP and Haryana in the absence of a green signal from both state units.

"UP and Haryana were discussed at the central parliamentary board meeting, but we have not taken a decision; we would inform you when we do," said general secretary Arun Jaitley.

Sources said former chief minister Kalyan Singh had threatened to quit the party in case the BJP leadership went ahead and formed an alliance with Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) leader Ajit Singh. Most state leaders are opposed to any tie-up with the Jat leader, but the high command is inclined to go ahead. Kalyan's threat has of late made several leaders think afresh and measure the fall-out of his exit. At a time when there are not many caste groups backing the BJP in the state, the party would lose the Lodh votes if Kalyan left. Things would get worse if he joined hands with Uma Bharati, a fellow Lodh.

As for Haryana, the board was informed the state executive was holding a meeting around the same time. The central leadership decided to wait for the state unit's recommendation. Reports from Haryana said the state executive had decided to leave it to the high command to take the call. The Haryana BJP is divided between pro-Om Prakash Chautala and pro-Kuldeep Bishnoi groups.

Heading: Fundamentalist Muslim outfit in Kerala plans a pan-Indian political avatar - Indian Express
Content:
The police station at Lanka, which is expected to ward off terror attacks and protect the Sankatmochan temple as well as the Banaras Hindu University, is in a shambles. Varanasi's most important thana, set up in 1986, is busy even at 4 in the morning, when policemen return after patrolling the surrounding area for five hours in the night. Six hours later, they are back on their feet again, on bank duty. "Two of us are deployed at every bank in the area, which has seven police stations. This is a 24-hour job. We don't get time to rest," one of them said.

The station has two toilets for 60 policemen. "We have to queue up to use the toilet in the morning. It stinks a lot," a constable said. As many as 20 men are accommodated in a dingy little barrack — the Lanka station has two of them. When it rains, water seeps in through a number of holes. Two fans hang precariously from the ceiling. A small black-and-white TV provides the only entertainment. "It was donated by a businessman a few years ago," a policeman said.

The police station has only eight staff quarters, most of which still remain in the possession of constables who have been transferred to other places. As a result, policemen have to rent houses on their own. The salary of a constable is Rs 8,500, of which he spends at least Rs 1,500 on accommodation. "Most policemen prefer to spend their free time at tea stalls or at the main gate of the police station," said a constable. There is a reason for that. The few chairs belonging to the station are kept in the office of the Station House Officer. "Kursi to door ki baat hai, yahan bench bhi nahin hai (forget about chairs, we don't even have a bench)," the constable added.

The building itself is constructed on a sewer, located underneath the room where FIRs are recorded. The opening of the drain is situated right at the door of the malkhana, which serves as the storeroom for weapons. "It often stinks in here," a policeman said. Except for a hand pump that supplies dirty water, there is no provision for drinking water. "The water is not potable," the policemen rued, adding that the partially covered tank, which has a capacity of 200 litres, is never cleaned.

The police station has one telephone and only one jeep, besides five motorcycles for patrolling. "We have to spend our own money for maintaining a mobile phone," a constable said, emphasising the need for communication. "We need to inform the station immediately if there is a blast threat or any other incident." The station, which has just seven walkie-talkies, lacks the facility of a CCTV to record the movement of visitors. In the name of sophisticated weapons, the Government has allotted two INSAS rifles and two AK-47 rifles, besides about 30 .303 and .413 bore rifles.

The Sankatmochan police outpost — the Lanka station has outposts at Nagwan, Sundarpur, BHU and Rewar — has a similar story to tell. It has two rooms, which were constructed with money donated by people. One room can accommodate not more than two beds, but eight constables have been posted here.

"About 1 lakh people gather here on Saturdays and Tuesdays. Besides the Uttar Pradesh Police, the Government has engaged the 1.5 Section of the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC), which possesses sophisticated weapons. Their job is to frisk visitors," said Rajeshwar, who is stationed at the outpost.

The PAC jawans cover a distance of 3 km from their camp to attend to their duty at the temple everyday, which begins as early as 6 am. "They do not stay in the temple at night," revealed a constable. Clearly, not much has been done to make policing easier in the holy city that attracts more and more pilgrims — and greater risk — every year.

Heading: With courts against handcuffing, cops plead helplessness - Indian Express
Content:
The Popular Front of India (PFI), a right wing Muslim organisation in south India, is planning a pan-Indian outfit to plunge into electoral politics. The PFI is an umbrella body of Kerala's National Development Front (NDF), Karnataka Forum for Dignity (KFD) and Tamil Nadu's Manitha Neethi Pasaria (MNP).

The PFI's move to form a political party — if it materialises — would have serious implications in Muslim-dominated areas, especially in southern India. At present, the Muslim voters are attracted towards parties like the CPI(M), Congress and Indian Union Muslim League.

The PFI was formed in November 2006 as a common platform of the NDF, KFD and MNP, which have made inroads into Muslim belts in three southern states.

In Kerala, the NDF — a key constituent of the PFI — has been involved in political clashes with the CPI(M) and RSS. Two NDF men had lost their lives in recent violence. Many NDF activists were allegedly involved in the recent political murders in Thalassery and Thrissur.

According to the Home Department, NDF was involved in 101 cases of attempt to murder or murder in the state in 2007. As many as 40 cases had been registered against NDF at Iritty police station in Kannur district. The NDF, a regrouping of mainly SIMI activists, was formed in 1993 to cash in on the disenchantment within the Muslim community after the demolition of Babri Masjid.

The PFI has already tested the electoral waters. It had fielded an Independent candidate from Mysore during the last Assembly elections in Karnataka. Its candidate bagged 10,000 votes and finished fourth in the race.

PFI sources told The Indian Express that though the plan for a political party was a serious one, it is at an embryonic stage right now.

"The Muslim vote is scattered among various political parties and bringing them, along with other backward minorities and Dalits, under one party umbrella would be the PFI's top priority," sources added.

According to one PFI leader, there has been a demand from within the Muslim community for a new political outfit that can address issues affecting the community like insecurity and inequality. As part of the spadework, a national-level campaign will be kicked off soon after Ramzan.

Sources said that the PFI and its state-level organisations have been indulging in 'negative' politics such as ensuring the defeat of candidates belonging to right wing Hindu organisations. "Now, we want to play positive politics, aimed at empowering the community. A final decision on forming the political party and its details would be decided only after the national political conference, slated for February in Kozhikode," sources added.

Reacting to the development, Indian Union Muslim League leader M K Muneer said that the PFI's attempt to form a political outfit was a dangerous one. "The Government and all secular forces have to be vigilant regarding such a move," he added.

Heading: Shatabdi grows vertical - Indian Express
Content:
Every undertrial who is taken to court for hearing or to hospital for routine examination or treatment — in case the person is still in police custody — is accompanied by at least two armed police personnel. In some states, the number of accompanying police personnel is more. This statistic was quoted early this year when the Punjab Assembly was passing the Code of Criminal Procedure (Punjab Amendment) Bill, 2008, which provides for use of electronic means — video conferencing — for production of an accused in custody or undertrial before a magistrate.

Another interesting statistic — this one is part of a study done by the Andhra Pradesh Government which has also introduced video conferencing in jails — is that on any working day, between 6,000 and 10,000 Andhra Pradesh cops are on duty with undertrials during their visit to courts.

Still, incidents of undertrials, including terrorists, escaping police custody while being taken for court hearings refuse to come down. Grappling with serious shortage of personnel, there is little the police and prison authorities can do to deal with the issue.

Senior police officers say guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court and the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) to prevent handcuffing of undertrials and convicts are one of the main reasons why cops can do little to prevent undertrials from escaping.

"We are perpetually short of manpower. How can we be expected to ensure that the accused doesn't escape if we can't even handcuff him? Since we can't handcuff the undertrial, we have to send more personnel than necessary to prevent him from escaping," says a senior police officer of Punjab Police.

On September 24, a Bench of the Punjab and Haryana High Court ordered the police chiefs of Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh to ensure that no undertrial is handcuffed without the prior permission of the court. The Bench also directed all judicial magistrates in the two states and the Union Territory to verify from each and every undertrial produced before them whether they had been handcuffed by the police or not.

Legal experts say in at least three oft-quoted judgments, the Supreme Court has ordered that handcuffing of undertrials is a strict no-no.

In its judgment dated August 30, 1978 in Sunil Batra versus Delhi Administration and others, a five-judge Bench of the apex court ruled that fetters, especially bar fetters, would be shunned as it violates human dignity, both within and outside prisons. "The indiscriminate resort to handcuffs when accused persons are taken to and from court and the expedient of forcing irons on prison inmates are illegal and shall be stopped forthwith save in a small category of cases where an undertrial has a credible tendency for violence and escape, a humanely graduated degree of iron restraint is permissible if other disciplinary alternative are unworkable," the court ruled.

In case the investigating agency feels that the undertrial has a credible tendency for violence and escape, it has to convince the court in this regard. In successive judgments, the courts have held that handcuffing and chaining in public degrades and puts to shame finer sensibilities and is a slur on Indian culture.

Going a step further, the SC in its 1995-judgment in Citizens for Democracy versus State of Assam and others ruled that in cases where the police or prison authorities are convinced that a particular prisoner is likely to jump bail or flee from custody, the prisoner has to be produced before the magistrate concerned and a prayer for permission to handcuff him has to be made.

The judgment says in rare cases where proof is available to establish the prisoner's tendency to escape or indulge in violence and on the finding that no practical way of forbidding escape is available, the magistrate may grant permission to handcuff the prisoner.

In cases, where a suspect is arrested without warrant, the police officer making the arrest can handcuff him only till the time he is taken to the police station and thereafter his production before the magistrate. Thereafter, handcuffs can be used only on the orders of the magistrate.

And what happens if the police officer doesn't follow the guidelines? Apart from disciplinary action by the department, he is liable to be hauled up for contempt of court.

In yet another judgment in Prem Shankar Shukla case (1980), the Supreme Court, while denouncing handcuffing of prisoners, observed: "Insurance against escape does not compulsorily require handcuffing."

Heading: At PM-Bush meet, it’s thank you and love - Indian Express
Content:
Having already enhanced the seating capacity of passenger coaches by making design modifications, Indian Railways is now set to take the idea a step further by introducing air-conditioned double-decker coaches with chair-car seating for Shatabdi trains.

After months of planning and study, the Mechanical Directorate of the Railway Ministry has finally approved a design for a double-decker air-conditioned chair-car coach, which will take the seating capacity up from the current 78 to 92 seats, pushing up the Railways' earnings in the process.

"The layout plan as well as the Railway Board's policy decision has been communicated to the Rail Coach Factory at Kapurthala. Instructions have been issued to get a prototype of a double-decker coach manufactured," a senior railway official told The Indian Express. Once all the trials and tests for the prototype are cleared, the Ministry wants to deploy these coaches for Shatabdi trains on key routes which have a higher volume of traffic.

The new design cleared by Rail Bhavan essentially envisages utilising the space between the two bogies (sets of wheels) under a coach, while also increasing the height of train cars.

"We have space available between two sets of wheels. The idea is to lower the floor of the coach by around 1.5 feet between these two sets of wheels, thus creating additional space in a well-shaped arrangement. Similarly, increasing the height of the coach by around 20 cm will give us extra room to create space for a double-decker configuration," explained an official, who is involved in the project.

Stairways on both sides of the coaches will enable passengers to access the upper deck.

However, this is not the first time that the Indian Railways has operationalised the concept of double-decker coaches. A few such non-AC coaches are still in operation on trains like the Flying Rani between Mumbai Central and Surat and the Mumbai-Valsad Passenger on the Western Railways. Nonetheless, these trains have certain disadvantages attached.

"A non-AC double-decker coach has its own set of problems. For instance, since the seating level in the lower deck is parallel to the platform level, a lot of dust and garbage generally make their way inside the coaches. That is why the idea this time is to have air-conditioned coaches so that the windows are closed and such problems can be avoided," an official said.

Now, Railways is gearing up to expedite the manufacture of the prototype, which will then be subject to rigorous tests — like crash tests, squeeze tests and oscillation tests. Once these are cleared, a go-ahead in the form of a safety certification from the Chief Commissioner of Railway Safety will be issued.

Heading: Cong’s Mumbai chief takes up Marathi cause - Indian Express
Content:
The delay in obtaining Congressional approval of the Indo-US civilian nuclear agreement may have upset Washington's plans to have Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and US President George W Bush raise a toast to what would have been a historic moment, but the two leaders did not allow that to come in the way of what was more of a "valedictory" meeting for Bush as they thanked, expressed gratitude, showered praises, with Singh even saying that "the people of India deeply love you".

The substantive element of the visit was still in on Capitol Hill, but hopes of its passage increased after principal critic and head of the House International Relations Committee Howard Berman extended support only after making some changes to the Senate draft the approval resolution. "We were told that it was close to being adopted by the US Congress," said Foreign Secretary Shivshankar Menon after the trip to Washington.

Bush, who is in the middle of dealing with the biggest financial crisis in the US, discussed the broad issue with Singh whom he respects as an economist too. In fact, he went on to tell him that in all this, the PM was somehow a "calm and serene influence".

On the civil nuclear initiative, both leaders were all praise for each other with US assuring India that it will try and ensure that the agreement satisfies both sides after it comes out of Congress. "You and I have worked hard to change the relationship between our countries... one such sign of the relationship is the Indo-US civilian nuclear agreement. It has taken a lot of work on both our parts, a lot of courage on your part, and of course we want the agreement to satisfy you and get it out of our Congress. And so, we are working hard to get it passed as a quickly as possible," said Bush after the meeting.

Singh was effusive in Bush's praise, telling him he had played "the most important role in making all this happen". He added: "When history is written I think it will be recorded that President George W Bush played a historic role in bringing our two democracies closer to each other."

Further, the PM underlined the importance of the nuclear initiative and said when the 34-year-old restrictive regime ends for India, a "great deal of credit will to President Bush and for this, I am grateful to you Mr President". He hoped that the agreement, which is now before the US Congress will be approved in a manner that satisfied both countries.

According to Menon, the two leaders discussed in detail the situation in South Asia and this was reflected in Bush's remarks later. "I thank you for your advice on a range of matters. I appreciated very much your briefing on the neighbourhood in which you live. It was very informative, and it helps me take decisions and it helps me formulate policy."

With Bush coming to the end of his presidency, there was little in terms of adding fresh content to the bilateral relationship. The effort was to consolidate the gains and take a few decisions like opening new consulates in Atlanta and Seattle, said officials.

The US President held a small and rare dinner at the old family room of the White House for Singh and a handful of senior officials accompanying him. On the financial crisis, during the talks and over dinner, Singh told him that there was no simple answer but there is now a case for strengthening oversight by multilateral financial institutions.

While the media focus was on the nuclear deal, Menon said the two leaders talked for some two-and-a-half hours, including the dinner, during which they touched upon a range of issues affecting the two countries and the world. "Frankly, I have not seen a conversation of this quality at this level. It is very rare," he said.

Heading: Extend PSEB unbundling deadline: Badal to Centre - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress seems all set to steal the thunder from the Shiv Sena and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) on the sons-of the-soil issue and the indication came on Thursday when recently-appointed Mumbai Congress chief Kripashankar Singh called for the need for Maharashtrians to be given priority in jobs.

While batting for the cause of Maharashtrians and Marathi language, the Santa Cruz MLA said the anti-outsider campaign of Raj Thackeray's MNS was a "battle for the Marathi brand" with cousin and Shiv Sena executive president Uddhav Thackeray.

Commenting on the MNS demand for at least 80 per cent employment in industries across the state for Maharashtrians, he said: "Maharashtrians must get priority in all employment avenues. Why just 80 per cent? Where can Maharashtrians get precedence except in Maharashtra?"

Referring to the contest between the Thackeray cousins on the sons-of-the-soil issue and their opposition to migrants, especially from the northern states, he said: "This is a domestic fight for the Marathi brand and not for the public." But Singh was of the view that "Maharashtrians must get priority in Maharashtra and Marathi must be respected".

He further said non-Maharashtrians in the state must make an effort to learn Marathi and "Marathi must get precedence in Maharashtra", adding: "People of Mumbai are cosmopolitan, but Marathi people and Maharashtrian culture are also important."

Singh also termed as "unfortunate" the recent comment by actor and Samajwadi Party Rajya Sabha MP Jaya Bachchan, which had evoked an outburst from MNS. Singh said, "It is a matter of shame that the issue of whether Marathi is to be spoken in Maharashtra was discussed. Even if someone does not speak Marathi, it is necessary to respect it."

Heading: SC issues notice to Punjab Govt on Amarinder expulsion - Indian Express
Content:
In a letter to Union Power Minister Sushil Kumar Shinde, Punjab CM Parkash Singh Badal has described the financial condition of the Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB) as "extremely precarious" and has requested that its unbundling be deferred further till May 31, 2009.

The letter, dated September 24, 2008, talks about "state Government's inability" to provide requisite funds due to its "financial constraints". "Restructuring of the PSEB without meaningful financial restructuring plan is not desirable," it says.

Badal says the Government is "exploring the possibilities such as re-evaluation of assets of PSEB, raising equity/loans from market etc before formulating a viable financial restructuring plan. I feel that any hurried attempt to do so may cause further difficulties. I strongly feel that the request of the state Government to allow continuation of PSEB as a STU (state transmission utility) and licensee up to May 31, 2009 should be agreed to."

On July 18 this year, the Punjab Government had sent a similar letter to the Union Ministry of Power, seeking extension in deadline for unbundling. The ministry, however, did not agree to continuation of the PSEB as an STU and a licensee beyond August 31, 2008. It asked for a clear road map to separate transmission activity by October 15, 2008. Unbundling of state electricity boards (SEBs) is a provision of the Electricity Act, 2003. It requires corporatising of SEBs into separate entities for handling generation, transmission and distribution of power. Punjab is one of the few states, which has not done it yet.

Heading: Ammonium nitrate: Govt proposes, then disposes - Indian Express
Content:
Declining to grant any relief to former Punjab chief minister Amarinder Singh, the Supreme Court on Friday refused to stay the order passed by the Punjab Assembly, expelling him for the remaining House term.

However, a Bench comprising Justices S B Sinha and Cyric Joseph issued notices to the Punjab Government on Singh's appeal, challenging his expulsion on September 10 this year.

Noting that Singh's appeal had raised a crucial point, the Bench even issued a notice to Attorney General Milon Banerjee, seeking his assistance in resolving the legal question: is an Assembly empowered to expel its sitting member?

The Bench referred the petition for hearing to a three-judge Bench on October 1.

The Punjab Assembly had expelled Singh after a resolution was passed on the basis of the nine-member special committee. The panel appointed by the Assembly found him guilty of causing pecuniary loss to the state exchequer worth millions of rupees by exempting from taxation a 32-acre plot of Amritsar Improvement Trust (AIT), which was allocated to a private builder.

Heading: Manmohan invites Zardari to Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
Days after the September 13 bomb blasts in New Delhi, the Home Ministry was sent a reminder by the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion of the urgency of making amendments in laws to regulate the sale of ammonium nitrate.

The reminder — and its timing — best illustrate the manner in which the country's top security establishment frittered away the opportunity to come up with a new system of regulation of manufacture and pilferage of ammonium nitrate, the most commonly used explosive in all major terror attacks.

For, ironically, it was the Home Ministry itself that — after a series in The Indian Express last October on the massive scale of explosive pilferage from Government depots — chaired a "highest-level" committee to examine all aspects of the explosive problem. Its terms of reference were spot on: to put in place an accountable regime for manufacture, supply and movement of explosives; prevention of pilferage and misuse of explosive materials and regulation of manufacture and sale of ammonium nitrate.

Deadline for the committee's report: three months. Chaired by Home Secretary Madhukar Gupta, the panel included the top brass of the security establishment — Secretary (Defence, Industrial Promotion & Revenue) as well as Chairman of the Ordnance Factory Board, Director, Intelligence Bureau, and Secretary (Research and Analysis Wing).

Nine months on and the report is nowhere in sight.

In fact, officials admit that after the group's first meeting itself, its composition was downgraded with most departments deputing Joint Secretary-level officers to it. Gupta turned out to be the only Secretary-level officer to attend the sittings. None of other Secretaries deputed, let alone the heads of intelligence agencies, showed up for any meeting.

Result: the job of charting change fell to officials of the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion (DIPP) and the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organization (PESO), with subsequent sessions being conducted by a Joint Secretary in the Home Ministry. It was the DIPP that, therefore, sent a reminder to the Home Ministry after the September 13 blasts. Officials now claim some movement on the recommendations of the committee which include amending Section 2(B) of the 1908 Explosive Substances Act to include ammonium nitrate as a "special category" explosive. This has been cleared by the Law Ministry and text for gazette notification is being prepared.

The others include:

• Regulation of manufacture, possession, sale and transport of ammonium nitrate. This may be done through the ordinance route and will need Cabinet clearance.

• Intelligence Bureau has recommended special explosive cells in police stations throughout the country.

• Bring even small-scale explosive manufacturers under the licensing regime and ensuring that no licenses for manufacture of high-grade explosives are issued without security clearance from the Intelligence Bureau. When and how this will happen, going by the record, is anybody's guess.

Heading: J-K: Cong gears up for Nov polls - Indian Express
Content:
As Pakistan President Asif Zardari works hard to legitimate his position in the international community, he received a significant boost when Prime Minister Manmohan Singh invited him to visit India. In turn, he also reiterated the pending invitation for Singh to visit Pakistan.

India's backing of the democratic government in Pakistan was reaffirmed this evening when the PM spoke at the UN General Assembly. "We welcome the return of democracy in Pakistan. We are committed to resolving all outstanding issues between India and Pakistan, including the issue of Jammu and Kashmir through peaceful dialogue. We also welcome the coming to power of democratically elected governments in Nepal and Bhutan."

In extra details that emerged from the Singh-Zardari meeting earlier, Foreign Secretary Shivshankar Menon said that the Pakistan President floated the idea of jointly developing the coal reserves in the Thar desert as a measure of energy cooperation. Menon, however, said the idea has to still be examined as no feasibility study has been carried out in Thar.

Zardari also raised the issue of what he claimed lesser flow on the Chenab due to storage of water in the Baglihar dam. India contested this, saying no such storage is underway and that the general quantum of water in the river is lower this year. Singh assured him that India would never violate the Indus Water Treaty and invited the Indus Waters Commissioner from Pakistan to visit the project site.

This apart, Zardari conveyed to Singh his commitment to the Bhutto plan for reconciliation as espoused by his late wife Benazir Bhutto.

He told him that Pakistan was a victim of terrorism and would join hands with India to combat the menace in the region.

Singh raised the attack on the Indian mission in Kabul, where leads pointed to role of Pakistan's ISI in the terror attack. Zardari, according to Menon, condemned the Kabul attack and agreed to hold a meeting of the joint anti-terror mechanism to evaluate the evidence available with India. He is believed to have assured the PM that stringent action will be taken against anyone found guilty.

Today at the UNGA, Singh again addressed the issue of terrorism and called for convention to combat it. "It is vital that we strengthen international cooperation to combat terrorism and to bring perpetrators, organisers, financers and sponsors of terrorism to justice. We should conclude expeditiously the Comprehensive Convention against International Terrorism," he said.

Heading: 20 more houses torched in Kandhamal - Indian Express
Content:
The ruling Congress is preparing for Assembly elections in Jammu and Kashmir in November, although the Election Commission is yet to take a final call on this issue. Top leadership of the party is learnt to have conveyed to the party's local units in Jammu and Srinagar to get into poll mode without waiting for the EC's decision.

With the ruling party at the Centre veering around the view that "democratic process" must start in the trouble-torn state to seize the initiative from separatists who have been seeking to occupy the political space in the Valley, the stage looks set for timely polls as the Opposition BJP is already in favour of it. An EC spokesperson had said earlier this month that the poll panel would not want to wait for the delimitation exercise to be completed in the state and election would be held "on time". The EC, which has been holding consultations with different stakeholders, is expected to announce its decision in the first week of October.

According to Congress sources, AICC general secretary Prithviraj Chavan visited Jammu on Thursday to hold a meeting with party leaders on election preparations. He is learnt to have told them to prepare for November election. He had visited Srinagar last week and conveyed the same to the party's local unit, said sources.

Chavan told The Indian Express, "We are prepared for all eventualities. We have left it to the EC. We do not decide the timing of election."

Congress sources, however, said the party was "reconciled" to November election, even though the timing does not suit the party politically. "It is not about our political interest. You cannot think of political interest on an issue of national interest," said a senior leader.

Heading: With UPA nod, Brajesh on global n-panel - Indian Express
Content:
After three warnings from the Union Home Ministry over its failure in containing violence in Kandhamal for over a month, the Orissa Government on Friday stepped up efforts to stop arsoning and killings even as violence continued in the district. For over a month, the district has been on the boil as it continues to be fuelled by a deadly cocktail of ethnic, religious and economic issues.

While Chief Secretary Ajit Tripathy described the situation in Kandhamal as 'very tense', Naveen Patnaik said the violence was under control. In Kandhamal, however, arsoning continued as 20 houses in Gesinghia in G Udaygiri block were torched. In a related incident, hundreds of women blocked the Raikia-G Udaygiri road protesting the arrest of 16 people including two minor girls who have been taken to custody over the attack on Raikia police station on Wednesday.

Though police and district administration officials hoped they would be able to contain the violence, they seemed to be worried over Thursday's attack at Sishpanga village in Raikia in which a Dalit Hindu was killed by Christian tribals.

Heading: Shoot ’em up - Indian Express
Content:
Brajesh Mishra, the national security advisor in the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government between 1998 and 2004, has been named as one of the 15 commissioners in the International Commission on Nuclear Non-proliferation and Disarmament established by the Governments of Australia and Japan.

Although the members of the international panel are said to have been chosen independently, sources confirmed that the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) was taken into confidence while finalising his name.

Mishra, who has been quite vocal in his support for the Indo-US nuclear deal, told The Indian Express on Friday, ''We are in favour of non-proliferation and disarmament and if you want to achieve these aims, you have to take India, Pakistan and Israel along.''

Does that mean that we are gradually moving towards signing the NPT? ''Obviously not,'' Mishra responded, ''we are a nuclear weapon state and we are not going to give up our nuclear weapons.''

He added that he was asked to be part of the panel by former Australian foreign minister and co-chair of the International Commission, Gareth Evans, in August this year.

Heading: 377 different arguments - Indian Express
Content:
Off with their heads — BJP President Rajnath Singh told party workers at a rally in Madhya Pradesh that anyone who waves the Pakistani flag or says Pakistan Zindabad should be gunned down. And if that wasn't enough shoot-shoot-bang-bang oratory, Singh thundered, "There were terror strikes when the NDA was in power, but we shot dead all terrorists." When leading politicians resort to hate-speech at this level, how can we expect any better from those who rampage through libraries and terrorise minorities?

And it's not a matter of electorally expedient tough talk — but unfortunately, it is characteristic of a worldview that casts all matters in its own stark palette, and a rhetoric that rejects all nuance as just so much noise distracting from the signal. Recall George W. Bush in his axis-of-evil days, vowing to stamp out terror, unabashedly employing a vocabulary of goodness and evil that made the rest of the world cringe. Politicians like Rajnath Singh fall back on the same simplifications, whether it is about fortifying our security or about the Kashmir situation — a case study in complexity, if there was any — and lower the discourse in dangerous ways.

Even as they seek to batter the government over contentious issues, opposition leaders like Singh cannot suspend the rules of public life. Rajnath Singh is the president of one of India's largest national parties — he is supposed to provide responsible stewardship and set out the terms of rational disagreement with the current government, not threaten to shoot down what offends his eye. The death of any human being, even one of proven culpability, is a sombre, tragic and ethically fraught thing. To make it a point of triumphalist swagger reveals a chilling lack of ordinary human sensitivity. Politicians might switch codes with ease as they try to mobilise every strand of support, but this kind of language is indefensible.

Heading: When she was here - Indian Express
Content:
Speaking to a packed Delhi High Court room on Friday, the additional solicitor general, P.P. Malhotra, said: "Legalising homosexuality will increase the spread of AIDS." Just a week earlier, the Union health minister — and qualified doctor — Anbumani Ramadoss publicly stated that de-criminalising homosexuality would, in fact, help prevent the spread of AIDS.

Permitting sex between consensual adults seems a task for a just-demised-theocracy newly empowering its citizens, not an established liberal democracy like India. But the evil that some men do seems to live on. Drafted by Lord Macaulay in 1860, with Victorian certainty, Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code criminalises "carnal intercourse against the order of nature". Subsequent courts have held this to include consensual sodomy, in effect criminalising homosexuality in India.

England, now Macaulay-less, has moved on: not only de-criminalising homosexuality, but even providing legitimacy to same-sex unions. But in India, homosexuality is viewed with suspicion; despite, according to a government study, 23 lakh people falling within the category. Political calculations — evident in ASG Malhotra's response to court — have ensured that Section 377 has remained on the statute books. Though hardly anyone has been prosecuted for consensual sex under Section 377, it has proved a handy tool for truculent families or crooked cops to blackmail and illegally detain homosexuals.

A hundred and forty eight years on, the validity of Section 377 is being debated at the Delhi High Court. In Naz Foundation vs Govt. of N.C.T. of Delhi, the petitioners — gay rights NGOs — seek to "read down" Section 377, so that it does not apply to sexual acts between consenting adults, while still being used to protect minors and non-consenting adults. They are arguing that Section 377 is unconstitutional, and denies basic human rights to LGBTs (lesbians, gays, bisexuals and transexuals). Mayur Suresh, a bespectacled young lawyer representing a coalition of NGOs calling itself Voices against 377, believes that "medical evidence clearly shows that homosexuality is not changeable. It is not a curable disease." As Shyam Divan, another lawyer for the coalition, argued in court yesterday, "For many homosexuals, their orientation is at the core of their identity... the moral argument cannot triumph over constitutional rights." The other NGO involved, the Naz Foundation, has — strategically — employed a more medical argument, arguing that the stigma of illegality makes it very difficult to reach out to LGBTs who are at high risk from AIDS.

Opposing this is the Orwellian sounding Joint Action Council, Kannur or JACK. JACK believes that AIDS is a Western myth, created by greedy pharmaceutical companies to sell panaceas for a non-existent malady. Their lawyer, Ravi Shankar Kumar, opposes legalising homosexuality on medical grounds, telling me that there has never been any link established between homosexuality and AIDS. Kumar is not from the Stone Age: he promised to send me a "soft copy" of his statements by email.

B.P. Singhal, former BJP Member of Parliament, has also intervened to oppose the petition, though his concerns are more moral than medical. Stocky, well-dressed, and with an old-world formal courtesy about him, he has had a long career in the Indian Police Service, and a shorter one as chairman of the Film Censor Board. "Homosexuality is neither congenital nor incurable," he told me, "and I have placed on record medical evidence about this." Heating up, he added: "Look at these malls growing all over the place. Don't you think that our morality is under attack? Anyway, the law will not change anything. Homosexuality is not accepted in society, and that will not change." Why then, did he care about the judgment? "Legalising gays will be calamitous," he responded, "It will encourage all kinds of vices... brothels."

In terms of their legal arsenal, neither Singhal nor JACK seems a match for the committed and better-coordinated NGOs they're opposing. Producing case after well-researched case, and affidavit after moving affidavit, their research led the Chief Justice to say, "You seem to have gathered much medical evidence that homosexuality is not a disease, unlike the [other side's] lawyer, who argued in court that 'homosexuality is a matter of fun'."

The government has other ideas. In an earlier affidavit, the home ministry had opposed the petition saying that legalising homosexuality would open the floodgates of delinquent behaviour.
