The Bush administration's proposal for a $700 billion bailout for distressed financial institutions was believed to have given fresh impetus to a buyout and new allure to Washington Mutual. Besides JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo & Co., Citigroup Inc., HSBC, Spain's Banco Santander and Toronto-Dominion Bank of Canada were all mentioned as possible suitors. WaMu was also believed to be talking to private equity firms.

Heading: Sensex loses 445 pts on Mutual scare - Indian Express
Content:
As Europe and Asia play down the need for an American-style bailout for their banks, the crisis may threaten a different class of countries: those in Eastern Europe, Latin America and Africa that depend on foreign capital and shoulder American-style trade deficits.

However, managing director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) Dominique Strauss-Kahn says the four largest emerging-market countries — China, Russia, Brazil and India or BRIC — which are running healthy trade surpluses or have hundreds of billions in foreign exchange reserves would not be affected, though Russia is vulnerable to a drop in oil prices.

Alarmed by the threat, Strauss-Kahn is calling for a multilateral consultation — involving the United States, Europe, China and other financial powers — to develop a coordinated response to the crisis. "We're facing a systemic crisis, and it needs a systemic response," Strauss-Kahn said in an interview on Wednesday.

"The IMF is the right place to organise a global response to weaknesses in the global financial system." His initiative is an attempt to thrust the fund back into the thick of world events — a role it played in previous financial crises in Asia, Russia and Latin America, but has not played in the current turmoil.

Whether or not he succeeds, economists agree that Strauss-Kahn, a former French finance minister, has identified a risk. The crisis, by squeezing the flow of capital, threatens countries from the Baltic to Africa that depend on foreign money to finance their deficits. "There are a number of countries where you can get quite worried if capital flows stop," said Thomas Mayer, the chief European economist at Deutsche Bank in London. "When you look at their high current-account deficits, Central and Eastern Europe seem particularly vulnerable."

A second category of countries are those who export oil or other commodities, and are vulnerable to a decline in prices — something that economists said would happen if the crisis hobbled growth. Oil plunged last week as Wall Street teetered, but it bounced back as hope rose for a bailout.

There are more than 20 countries with current-account deficits that exceed 5 per cent of their economic output, Strauss-Kahn said, putting them in what the fund considers the endangered category.

Heading: Hari Puttar, A Comedy Of Terrors - Indian Express
Content:
It is getting scarier as the ugly layers of the US financial crisis continue to peel off with every passing day. The reverberation of another casualty on the Wall Street was quite jarring on Friday as domestic markets found the spook too much to handle. With the $700 billion bailout plan still unresolved marketmen here felt the tremors and sold heavily pulling the Bombay Stock Exchange barometer Sensex down by 445 points to 13,102.18.

The 50-share National Stock Exchange index Nifty too came under heavy selling pressure and closed at 3,985.25 points a level last seen on July 16.

"A lot of stocks traded below their yearly lows today sending weak market undertones. Market participants who had bought capital goods sector stocks ahead of Indo-US nuke deal dumped them. The rupee too was beaten down as it fell further against the dollar," said head of research Geojit Financial Services, Alex Mathew.

On the BSE, realty stocks were hammered once again amidst continuing concern over upheaval in global financial markets and their sectoral index closed down by 6.33 per cent. Banking counter was also under severe pressure and bankex was lower by 4.27 per cent at close. Metal index was next biggest casualty at 4.76 per cent.

Heading: Rafoo Chakkar - Fun On The Run - Indian Express
Content:
Cast: Zain Khan, Sarika, Saurabh Shukla, Vijay Raaz, Swini Khara, Lilette Dubey, Jackie Shroff

Director: Lucky Kohli and Rajesh Bajaj

Warner Bros were getting antsy for nothing. Hari Puttar has nothing to do with the Harry Potter films, other than the fact that both have been filmed in England. Hari isn't a young wizard with a scar zigzagging though his forehead. He's just a ten-year-old who gets left behind in a large mansion, somewhere on the outskirts of London. Sounds familiar? Yep, it's got a lot to do with 'Home Alone', with Zain Khan doing a desi McCaulay Culkin.

Hari is dumped on by everybody: his elder brother thinks he is a total wimp, his cousins  laugh at his accent; in fact, the whole caboodle thinks he should neither be seen nor heard. His mom (Sarika) is the only one who dotes on her beloved 'puttar', but even she forgets him, as the family hares off somewhere, leaving behind our young hero, and his one cousin (Swini) who likes him.

If you remember the first Home Alone flick, you know what happens: the youngsters (Zain, last seen in Chain Kuli Ki Main Kuli, is likeable; Swini, last seen in Cheeni Kum, is not) beat a couple of thieves back, with all their arsenal: dragging them across lawns, throwing smelly liquids whooshing on their heads, shooting sharp pointed objects at various body parts, and so on.

And because it is a Hindi film, it has an item number, fronted by Shamita Shetty. A larger-than-life villain, who has one false eye and a hideous Mumbaiya accent. A couple of hoods called Diesel and Filter (Saurabh in waist-length Rasta curls who lets loose noisy smells from his rear end at regular intervals, and Vijay in florid flowery suit). A scientist who's working on a secret computer 'cheep' (chip). And a script which doesn't know the meaning of sense, and so full of holes that several large-sized trucks can drive right through.

Who cares, though? Certainly not the six-year-old sitting right ahead, who chortled his way through much the film. Plot to have your tykes whisked off to the film by elder siblings, while you take in that film you've been wanting to: that's what multiplexes are for!

shubhra.gupta@expressindia.com

Heading: The X-Files: I Want To Believe - Indian Express
Content:
Cast: Yuddhisthir, Aslam Khan, Nauheed Cyrusi, Nisha Rawal, Archana Puran Singh, Mita Vashist, Shakti Kapoor, Sadashiv Amrapurkar

Director: B H Tharunkumar

And this one has nothing to do with that mid-70s barrel of fun-on-the-run starring Rishi and Neetu, other than the fact that they share the same name, Rafoo Chakkar.

Two middle-aged sisters (Archana and Mita) have to marry within 24 hours to fulfill the conditions of their father's will. Two ne'er-do-wells (Yudi and Aslam) land at their doorstep, and are reeled in, kicking and screaming. In addition to this happy foursome are two curvy airheads (Nauheed and Nisha), who claim they are penniless, but appear to be dressed (if you call Nauheed's plunging tees 'dressing') to the nines every time they appear on screen.

B H Tharunkumar's previous outing Nayee Padosan had fake sets, loud actors, and a story which didn't have a subtle bone in its body. Rafoo Chakkar takes all these ingredients, and ratchets them up a hundredfold, making it way beyond bad.

The lines are worse. Sample this exchange between the two fellows, about to be led off to their 'suhaag raat': "hamari bohni itni purane customers se nahin ho sakti".

Yeah, it's like that. All of it.

shubhra.gupta@expressindia.com

Heading: Charlie Bartlett - Indian Express
Content:
Cast: Gillian Anderson, David Duchovny, Amanda Peet

Director: Chris Carter

Some files are meant never to be closed, and many would argue that The X-Files fits that category. Six years after the series ended and 10 years after the last film, Scully and Mulder take barely a scene between them to get The X-Files back in its rhythm. It isn't the best case that the two have solved, it isn't the most difficult, it isn't even the best of science fictions, and it barely fits into the category of paranormal, but it is perhaps the closest look at two characters that TV audiences have loved for years now.

Older and wiser, less flashier and argumentative, Scully (Anderson) and Mulder (Duchovny) here are retired from the FBI and at peace. Yes, they are living together, and the film just lets that drop, casually. After all those years of speculation about whether they would do "it", when they would do "it", this matter-of-factness sets the pace for the rest of this adventure. This Scully and Mulder are not here to impress us — that battle was long won— they are here to be themselves, do what they believe in. And if you think about it, the Scully and Mulder we know would go about their love in their own way, at their own pace.

When the FBI seeks their help to look for a missing agent — the only clue they have is a psychic who claims to be able to see her — they get into it grudgingly. With everybody doubting the psychic, Mulder, who is the "believer" of The X-Files, is quickly drawn in. Scully, now working as a doctor in a church-run hospital, is as always the sceptic.

More than the search for the FBI agent, the film at many levels is about the larger question of faith, and how far one would go for it. The film pits stem-cell therapy against religion, is about scientists taking organ transplant far enough to play god, about a serial paedophile priest who prays with the belief that God will forgive him, about Scully debating reason and emotion in trying to save a dying patient, and about Mulder who seeks no reason at all for his beliefs.

There are many things stunningly out of place. Such as a top-notch surgeon like Scully "googling" to find out about stem-cell therapy, and apparently using the information on her patient to save his life. But Anderson is so earnest, her portrayal of a doctor torn between what she knows and what she would like to believe so tortured that you can almost believe she is doing everything in her power to save the boy.

Yes, it is not The X-Files we know, but be as it were about former FBI agents Scully and Mulder, let it herald the beginning of a whole new adventure: The Ex-Files. I want to believe.

shalini.langer@expressindia.com

Heading: Hear & now: Signs that will cheer the differently abled - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Sohrabuddin case: Johri has a lot of explaining to do in her reply to SC - Indian Express
Content:
Two city-based youths come up with a mobile dictionary in Indian Sign Language

In an initiative, which is expected to bring smiles across the face of lakhs of differently abled people in the country, two city-based youths have come up with a pilot project on Indian Sign Language (ISL) on the mobile.

Vadodara-based Rajesh Ketkar (32), himself a 100 percent hearing-impaired, has come up with a self-explanatory dictionary for the likes of him.

Unlike a regular dictionary, the mobile-ISL (Indian Sign Language) dictionary enables people with hearing disabilities to have an image picture word with video-graphed sign language, all on the screen of a mobile.

Ketkar said, through this technology, they are attempting to enact the meaning of the words on camera, which will then be uploaded on their website. Those desirous of accessing this visual dictionary will have to log on to their website, which will be designed soon, and put the desired word in the search option. Once the search word is entered in the web page, it will be loaded with the video, which will explain the meaning of the word along with its picture. Ketkar said his attempt to digitalise Indian sign language with visual representation is the first of its kind across India.

Working on the new mobile dictionary for the hearing impaired for the last four months, Ketkar has created a set of 20 words as a pilot project. "A dictionary for the deaf doesn't work the same way as a normal English dictionary because the deaf don't understand words," Ketkar wrote on a sheet of paper to communicate.

Ketkar said he could complete his education only up to Class X, which the government provides, after which he took up vocational training in tailoring. He said the idea to come out with a dictionary for the hearing-impaired germinated, when he along with Virbhadrasinh Rathod, attended a conference by the World Federation for Deaf in Madrid, Spain last year. The two run an NGO, Mook Badhir Mandal, in Vadodara, for the hearing impaired.

"There were deaf people from across the world and we were amazed to see their confidence level. In India people still look at the deaf with sympathy unlike in other countries. There they ask for 'professional assistance' and not 'help.' We were exposed to their technology which is not used anywhere in India or even in any other Asian country," Ketkar said through an interpreter.

He added: "This is a pilot study that I have done because the Americans' way of interpretation and understanding does not match ours. We don't have much exposure to technology or education. The visual dictionary will help the deaf understand words on a daily basis which will also increase their vocabulary."

With the success of his pilot study, Ketkar now plans to create a comprehensive dictionary with all the words.

"There is not much research and technological advancements happening in the country for the hearing impaired. But it has to start somewhere and I am trying to bring in that change," Ketkar added.

Heading: Celebrations under siege: Garba to have a brush with metal detectors, CCTVs - Indian Express
Content:
ASG accuses senior IPS officer of letting down probe, conniving with state government

Gujarat Inspector General of Police Geetha Johri may have to explain to the Supreme Court in her reply in connection with the Sohrabuddin Sheikh fake encounter case, why she could not append the statement of Sheikh's accomplice, Sylvester Daniel Christian, in the charge sheet. Incidentally, Johri had reportedly sought permission to question Sylvester as part of the investigations.

Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Gopal Subramaniam had levelled allegations against Johri two days ago that she had "let down" the probe being monitored by the Supreme Court, by 'conniving with the state to create false records.'

An accomplice of Sohrabuddin and Tulsi Prajapati, Sylvester comes from a well-to-do family from Bhopalnagar in Udaipur and is presently lodged in a jail in Udaipur. Sylvester is believed to be holding some crucial leads in connection with the fake encounter of November 26, 2005 and the subsequent murder of Kausarbi. "Though statements of his family members were recorded during the investigation, the CID never questioned Sylvester on grounds that he was missing," said a police officer on condition of anonymity.

According to the Ahmedabad police records, Sheikh, Prajapati and Sylvester had stayed together at a house in Rasulabad in Shah-e-Alam between 1997 and 1999. A resident of the same area, Zahid Kadari, who works as a traffic inspector with the Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation (GSRTC) had stated this in his statement before a local magistrate in December 2005.

"Sohrabuddin, Prajapati and Sylvester were close friends and were always seen together during their days in Ahmedabad. Sohrabuddin used to stay under the alias Salim," the source added.

On Thursday, Subramanian had raised doubts on Johari's approach in the probe, which according to him had 'a systematic collapse.' He submitted before the Apex court that "Johri had sought permission to interview Tulsi Prajapati, who was accompanying Sheikh and his wife before they were picked up by a team of Gujarat Police on January 5, 2007, although it was believed that Prajapati was killed in another staged encounter in 2006." This argument, was, however, countered by Gujarat's counsels Hemantika Wahi and Sourav Kripal, who placed an affidavit saying that Johri had sought permission to interview Sylvester.

Incidentally, the CID charge sheet submitted before the city and sessions court here, does not have Sylvester's statement. V P Atre, the special public prosecutor in the case, also confirmed this.

Sylvestor, along with five others, Prajapati and Ahmedabad-based Ramjan Hanif Qureshi, Noor Nathuji Ghoghari, Mahendrasinh Jhala and Yusuf Menon, were arrested by the Gujarat Anti Terror Squad (ATS) on December 12, 2005, less than a month after Sheikh was killed in a faked encounter.

The arrests were in connection with a December 2004 shootout on the office premises of two Navrangpura-based builders. The ATS had claimed that they had solved a Rs 1.25 crore extortion case carried out under Sohrabuddin's direction.

While the Ahmedabad-based accuseds were arrested from their residences, Prajapati and Sylvester were brought to Ahmedabad on a transfer warrant from the Rajasthan Police. "The two were in an Udaipur jail in connection with the murder of one Hameed Khan Pathan alias Lala. Sohrabuddin was also an accused in this case," said a police officer.

About a year later, while Prajapati was killed in another "police encounter" on December 28, 2006, near Ambaji in north Gujarat, Sylvester was said to be missing. "Sylvester was arrested again in connection with a theft case of Ambaji and is presently lodged in a jail in Udaipur," said a CID (Crime) officer.

Heading: We stole power, but don’t penalise us, demand farmers in Bankantha - Indian Express
Content:
The recent serial blasts in Ahmedabad continue to haunt the memories of the average Gujarati. Keeping this in mind, the organisers of "garbas" here have propounded a new phrase "Navratri with Safety" to ensure maximum participation of locals in the extravaganza kicking off from September 30.

Undeterred by the perennial staff crunch in the Gandhinagar police force, the organisers of private "party plot garbas" have decided to make elaborate security arrangements of their own at all the major garba venues in the state Capital during the festival. As part of the plan, they are installing metal detectors at the entry points, Closed Circuit TV (CCTV) cameras in and around the garba venues and also erecting watch towers to closely monitor the movement of visitors to the venue.

"Keeping in mind the current volatile situation in the wake of terrorist attacks in Ahmedabad and elsewhere in the country, we have chalked out foolproof security plans to ensure safety of the participants as well as the visitors at our garba venue. At the main entrance, two metal detectors will be installed to frisk the visitors," said Krishnakant Jha of the Gandhinagar Cultural Forum. The forum has been organising traditional garbas every Navratri on a sprawling party plot near the Town Hall in the state capital.

Jha told reporters on Saturday that the Forum will also install at least eight CCTVs in the garba ground and the parking slots, besides setting up almost half-a-dozen watch towers to constantly monitor the movement of visitors. About two dozen trained security guards will be posted at the main entrance to frisk visitors with the help of metal detectors. The forum has set up a 12-member security committee, and also a special control room is being created at the venue, he said.

He added that the forum has also doubled up its security budget this year in view of the volatile situation on the law and order front. "Last Navratri, we spent about Rs 85,000 on security arrangements. This time, we have raised it to Rs 1.75 lakh," said Jha. Besides seeking the help of the local police, the cultural body has also engaged a Gandhinagar-based private security firm to maintain security arrangements in and around the garba venue, he said. The Cultural forum has over 3,000 registered members, and attracts nearly 10,000 participants at its garba venue on each of the nine nights during the dance festival.

The organisers of two other major "party plot garbas" in Gandhinagar have also made elaborate security arrangements at their respective venues. Thousands of garba revellers throng the CH 3 Circle and GH 5 Circle in the state capital, the venues where the Lions and Lioness Club and the local "Sahiyar" cultural body organises Navratri grabas every year. These organisers have also increased their security budgets this time. Gandhinagar district collector Sanjeev Kumar said there is a staff crunch in the local police force. He, however, said the administration will be able to maintain law and order during the festivities.

"Whatever police force is available with us, we will be able to cope up with the situation. If necessary, we will seek the assistance of para-military forces like the CRPF and also requisition the services of the newly created Gujarat Industrial Security Force (GISF) for the smooth conduct of garbas in Gandhinagar," Kumar told Newsline.

Dy Superintendent of Police K C Chudasma said the police will intensify the checking of vehicles and visitors at all the entry points of the capital city during the festival. Security personnel will be deployed at all the small garbas organised in the 30 sectors across the township and the mounted police patrol will also be intensified, he said. He further said that the 12 midnight deadline for stopping the festivities at all the venues in Gandhinagar would also be strictly enforced.

The Gandhinagar Shaher Vasahat Mahamandal, an umbrella organisation of local NGOs, has represented to the DSP that adequate police bandobast is made during the garba revelry keeping in view the "vulnerability" of the capital township.

"The district police are facing a shortage of about 600 personnel, as against the sanctioned strength of 1,700. It's the responsibility of the government to ensure the safety of the residents of Gandhinagar during such public celebration, especially when terrorist attacks like the one at Ahmedabad continue to create fear psychosis in the minds of the common man," said Arun Buch of the Mahamandal.

Heading: Missing from action: Scarcity of teachers hits students hard - Indian Express
Content:
Over 2,000 farmers give memo to DM, say dark zone system forced them to do so

Having accepted that they were indeed stealing power, over 2,000 farmers, under the banner of 'Bharatiya Kisan Sangh,' submitted a memorandum to the district collector of Banskantha on Thursday, and demanded the removal of the penalty levied on them under Section 135 of the 'Electricity Act 2003.' The section had been invoked against them for drawing electricity through illegal connection. The farmers held a rally before handing over the memorandum.

Under the Section 135 of the Act, anyone who steals electricity will have to pay a penalty and an FIR will be registered against the person. If an additional compound amount is paid along with the penalty, the FIR can be dropped in case it is the maiden offence.

The sangh pointed out in its petition that the Gujarat Electricity (GEB) officials had levied an unjustifiable penalty of Rs 3,360 for theft of every unit of electricity. This is injustice to the poor farmers and drives them to suicide. As such Section 135 of the Act should be removed, the sangh said.

Among other demands of the sangh is the removal of the dark zone system. The sangh has also demanded that the affected farmers should have a say under the land acquisition policy and agents commissions in selling fruits should be regulated. The sangh members have also demanded that farmers should be kept in mind while allotting land for Special Economic Zone.

When contacted, sangh zila commissioner Shyamal Jethabhi said that the dark zone system of the government has been really hard on the farmers. While they have no irrigation or electricity, they are forced to draw electricity by illegal means. "Our framers are unhappy with the existing penalties. It becomes heavy on their pockets. At present there are 3 tehsils in Banaskantha that fall under the dark zone and no new connection is given in these areas. The farmers have to pay heavily if they break the law." Babubahi Patel, the district secretary of the sangh added: "We have launched a campaign against this kind of injustice to the farmers."

District Collector RJ Patel said: "This kind of a demand is crazy. I received the memorandum a day back. It will be handed over to the minister."

Patel also confirmed the list of demands placed by the Sangh. "The farmers keep sending petitions but after stealing electricity, theit demand that they should not be penalised is ridiculous, he added."

Heading: Three detained in connection with recovery of eight peacock carcasses - Indian Express
Content:
Ban on recruitment of general subject teachers leads to over 400 vacancies

A freeze on recruitment of teachers in general subjects taught in high schools across the city for the last five years has left the students in the lurch. According to Ahmedabad Shaher Acharya Sangh the schools are not allowed to recruit teachers for subjects other than science, mathematics and English.

Sangh president Jayantibhai Patel said the ban had given rise to over 400 vacancies, which was impacting teaching of subjects like social studies, Hindi, drawing and physical education in schools.

"There are schools in some rural areas where the number of teachers is less than the number of classes because once a teacher retires, the post is not filled up," said Patel. He added that the quality of education in schools was suffering because of the absence of teachers and a lack of go-ahead from the state government.

Patel said the issue had been raised early this month during a videoconferencing with the minister and the Education department officials. "We had been given an assurance and even the officials had been instructed accordingly, but nothing has materialised so far," he added.

Principal of another city school said this was a common problem in many schools as a circular had been issued some years ago by the Commissioner of Higher Education — placing a ban on recruitment for posts falling vacant on the retirement of teachers in grant-in-aid schools, unless they were given a No-Objection Certificate (NOC).

A senior state government official, however, denied that there were any such appointment problems in grant in-aid schools.

"Once these schools get the NOC, they can make the required appointments. But, they are not given approval for general subjects. For science, mathematics and English, they can take the NOC from the district education officer concerned," he said.

Ahmedabad district education officer P B Gadhvi could not be contacted despite repeated attempts.

Heading: Message on the move: MSU students take out bicycle rally for social awareness - Indian Express
Content:
Three persons have been detained for interrogation by the Forest Department following the recovery of carcasses of eight peacocks from the agriculture fields located on the outskirts of Bhojde village on the periphery of Gir Forest. They have been identified as Narshi Gopal, Dinesh Naran and Chino Koli, who worked as labourers on the agriculture land owned by Kala Ahir, Uka Ahir, and Menasi Ahir.

Talala range forest officer B K Parmar said: "Two of the six carcasses had been partly eaten by wild animals. Though the veterinary doctor from Sasan (Gir) Forest headquarters carried out a postmortem, the exact cause of death has not been ascertained. The viscera of the birds have been dispatched to the Junagadh Forensic Science Laboratory for a detailed clinical examination."

He said since the three have denied any role in the death of the birds, they are awaiting the FSL report.

"We will take appropriate action once we get the report. The peacock is a Schedule-I bird; the killing of which is punishable with imprisonment up to 3 to 7 years. Beside, the peacock is a our national bird and has to be protected," said Parmar.

Lioness attacks farmer

A farmer was attacked by a lioness when he was working in the fields on the outskirts of Jetalwad village near Visavadar town on Friday. The man, who has been identified as Dhirubhai Bhalala (45), received injuries on his left hand, leg and chest. He was immediately rushed to the Junagadh Civil Hospital and is being treated at the trauma ward. Doctors treating him have declared him to be out of danger. Bhalala said at the hospital: "I was cutting grass on my land, when all of sudden a lioness appeared in the fields, and before I could understand what was happening, it pounced upon me. However, I shouted for help and somehow managed to wriggle out from her grip."

Heading: Lost in translation: Foreign students run into language barrier at MSU - Indian Express
Content:
Educate slum dwellers about HIV/AIDS, de-addiction,domestic violence

In an attempt to create awareness on social issues in the slum areas of the city, more than 100 students from M S University (MSU) Faculty of Social Work (FSW) took part in a two-day bicycle rally that started on Saturday.

The students used 50 bicycles in the rally to cover the three slums of Tulsiwadi, Kishanwadi and Pensionpura where they performed skits and puppet shows on issues such as HIV/AIDS, de-addiction and domestic violence. Later, they organised a group discussion mostly with the female respondents.

Kiran Suryavanshi, a final year student from FSW said: "Our faculty intends to conduct psychoanalytical survey on the reasons behind addiction and domestic violence. Most of the respondents in the group discussion were women who are facing domestic violence due to certain habits of their spouses."

He said even as the women toil hard for the family, the men engage in activities such as prostitution and liquor consumption. Arun Nathai, another student from FSW said, on October 19, a panel discussion on these deep-rooted problems will be conducted where various city-based NGOs will make their presentations. On Sunday three other slums, Kalyan Nagar, Jagnath Nagar, and Mujmahuda will be covered.

The cycle rally was flagged off by MSU Chancellor, Mrunalini Devi Puar, Vadodara District Collector Vijay Nehra and Commissioner of Police Rakesh Asthana.

Heading: VMC sports complex plan gets a push with some amendments - Indian Express
Content:
University authorities may start crash course in Hindi for them from next year

Even though the M S University (MSU) has admitted around 40 foreign students this academic year, many of them are finding it difficult to overcome the language barrier. However, the MSU authorities have been quick to act upon this, with the foreign students advisor now proposing the idea of running a crash course in Hindi language from next year.

Speaking to Newsline, Asri from Jaca city in Indonesia, who has taken admission in MSU Performing Arts after obtaining a scholarship from the Indonesia-based Indian Culture Central Relation (ICCR), said, "I took admission in MSU because I like the teaching procedures here. Though I had earlier got admission in the Delhi-based Shri Ram Music Institute, I opted to learn the Sitar from here. But for the last two months, I have been facing problems in understating some of the notes in Hindustani Classical Music and in the study of ragas. Though there are some Nepalese students who help me with my Hindi, it is not of much help."

A few days ago, Asri, and a US student, Williams, met advisor of foreign students, Sharad Bansal, and apprised him about communication problems being faced by them.

Williams, who is learning music here said, "I have been learning Hindustani Classical Music for the last four years from my tutor based in Anand. Initially, I did face some problems in understanding the ragas, but now there has been some improvement."

Speaking about the communication problems faced by the students from abroad, Bansal said, " I have spoken to the Dean of Performing Arts Ishwarchand Pandit about this. We have come up with a temporary solution wherein we have asked teachers from the Hindi department, who can understand both Hindi and English, to explain the musical notes to the students in Hindi."

He added, "This is the first time that students of Performing Arts have approached us with problems in understanding Hindi language. But there are also some students from Jordan who understand neither Hindi nor English. And, these students have made their own arrangement for learning English but since Hindi is still a problem, we are planning to start a crash course in Hindi for them."

Heading: Brawl between Jordanian and Indian students at MS University reaches police - Indian Express
Content:
Space crunch at proposed Sama site leads to bifurcation of outdoor and indoor games

The Rs 5-crore grant from the state government to develop a state-of-the-art sports complex in Sama has finally reached a logical conclusion. On Friday, officials of the Vadodara Municipal Corporation and members of sports associations came together to discuss the issue, which had earlier run into controversy.

The land initially decided for the sports complex at Sama, fell short of encompassing VMC's plans of incorporating facilities for all the major sports. The VMC has now come to a consensus to bifurcate the indoor and outdoor games at various grounds across the city.

"Our main purpose is to create a sports track that can encourage sports of national level in the city. The plan to have a 400-metre athletic track needs a bigger ground. Once the track is created, many other outdoor games will be incorporated," said VMC Mayor Balkrishna Shukla.

The land and area allocation for each sport is yet to be decided. The VMC is now in the process of sorting out the corporation owned land across the city for the purpose. "We are considering a land in Waghodia to take up under public participation," said Shukla.

The proposed ground will cater to athletics, hockey, football, basket ball, volleyball, table tennis, wrestling, chess, carom, skating and tennis. It will also include a gymnasium. To meet the national standards, the sizes of the skating rink at Karelibaug and Akota will be increased. "Children interested in sports will get proper amenities here. The new ground and the facilities available here will change the scenario of sports in the city," said Shukla.

Old grounds to get a facelift

The Vadodara Municipal Corporation, in its zeal to to bring about total reformation of its sports section in the city, has not forgotten its older grounds. After Newsline reported on the lavish plans of pouring grant money on the new grounds and forgetting the already existing ones, the VMC in its Friday meeting finally took into consideration the need to improve the conditions of Akota Grounds. The skating rink and the tennis court will be renovated as per international standards and the football ground will be cleared up and maintained properly.

Heading: VMC cracks down on hawkers, clears areas for smooth traffic flow - Indian Express
Content:
A Tiff between Jordanian and Indian students of M S University (MSU) Faculty of Arts campus turned ugly recently. According to the police officials, an application on this issue has been filed with the Sayajigunj police station on Friday. While, the varsity officials said that the uproar was an offshoot of an affair between a Jordanian student and an Indian girl, police officials said investigations were still on.

Sayajigunj police inspector D L Jhala, said, "The incident occurred near the Archeology department of MSU Arts faculty on Thursday when one group of Jordanian student came to blows with another group." While the police said the matter was not serious, sources at the varsity said the affair of the Jordanian student, who was recently admitted in the Bachelors of Arts (BA), with an Indian girl, was the reason behind the brawl.

Sources at varsity informed that the Embassy of Jordan, Registrar and Commissioner of Police have been informed about the incident in writing. However, A V Gupta, MSU Registrar said, "I have not received any formal complaint from either side, however, I will speak to the Arts faculty in-charge dean in this regard."

Heading: Bitter Bill?: GUJCOC divides legal fraternity - Indian Express
Content:
The Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) has embarked on a drive to evict hawkers from the non-hawking zones across the city. On Friday, Corporation officials evicted all the hawkers from the non-hawking zones at Nizampura.

The Corporation has identified 12 such zones in the city from where the hawkers will be evicted. The procedure is already underway between the stretch at Lal Baug and Kalaghoda and Amit Nagar Circle and VUDA Circle.

VMC Deputy Commissioner C M Makwana said: "The roads in the area are narrow and the presence of hawkers makes the place more chaotic. This is the reason why they are being removed from the place."

The other areas where the drive against the hawkers is being initiated are, Mandvi to Gendi Gate, Harni Jakatnaka to Makarpura, Shastribaug to Pariwar crossing, Susain crossing to Lal Baug railway crossing, Chakli circle to Akshar Chowk, EME circle to Fatehgunj and all the way to Alembic and from Shastri Bridge to Chakli Circle.

The hawkers will be relocated within 100 metres of the dislocated spot, which will decrease the intensity of the traffic problem.

Heading: Nanvati panel manipulated evidence, reached pre-ordained conclusion: JSM - Indian Express
Content:
Politics rules over reason as leading lawyers make their stance clear

The ruling BJP passed a resolution by a majority in the state Assembly on Friday demanding an early clearance of the GUJCOC (Gujarat Control of Organised Crime) Bill, 2003, by the Centre. The legal fraternity in the Gujarat High Court, however, appears to be divided over the issue.

Jumping into the debate over GUJCOC, the Gujarat High Court Advocates Association on Friday threw its weight around the state government and passed a resolution in support of GUJCOC at an extra-ordinary general meeting.

The association headed by Yatin Oza, a former BJP legislator, urged the Centre to "rise above the political considerations and act in the interest of the nation" by approving GUJCOC.

While advocating for the Bill, the association stressed that it must be passed in its original form as passed by the Gujarat Assembly for the first time in 2003, incorporating provisions for interception of communication.

It was in fact this provision that had made the NDA government in 2003 to return the Bill for reconsideration and amendment.

The association said that GUJCOC will severely hamper the nefarious designs of the terrorists and that political ideology cannot and should not be a ground or a reason to make 55 million Gujaratis suffer.

"Whatever hatred the Union government may have for the state government or vice-versa, that cannot be the reason for 55 million people of Gujarat to suffer," said the resolution signed by association president Yatin Oza and Secretary Sandip N Bhatt.

Former president of the association K J Sethna also voiced his support for GUJCOC, but the amended version of 2004. He said Oza was "misusing" the association's platform to promote his political interests and regain the position in the BJP which he held prior to contesting the Assembly elections against Chief Minister Narendra Modi from Maninagar after quitting the BJP.

Incidentally, Oza joined the party again on December 2, 2007, just on the eve of the Assembly polls, but was not given a ticket.

Other advocates including Amrish Patel, Dr. Mukhul Sinha, leading criminal lawyer Mahesh Bhatt and Harin Raval came out in opposition of GUJCOC. They said the Bill was not required as other laws existed.

Terming the association's resolution "a politically motivated" initiative, Amrish Patel said that GUJCOC will not be able to create a fear psychosis among the terrorists, as death did not deter them (terrorists) from carrying out their acts.

"But it will certainly create fear psychosis among the minorities whom some people want to harass and terrorise. GUJCOC will just be used to torture and extract confession by the police," he said.

At a recent rally organised against GUJCOC, Sinha and Mahesh Bhatt said that provisions of POTA have already been included in the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act and hence no new law was needed.

Heading: 19 child labourers rescued from city - Indian Express
Content:
Manch's own report trashes conspiracy theory behind Godhra incident

The Jan Sangharsh Manch (JSM) on Friday rejected Part one of the Justice Nanavati Commission's report on the Godhra incident. It said the report was a product of "unfortunate, manipulation of evidence" to reach a pre-ordained conclusion.

The JSM released its own report based on all the evidence and material placed before the Commission. It said the burning of the S6 coach of the Sabarmati Express on February 27, 2002 was an accident and not a part of the pre planned conspiracy as is being stated in the Nanavati report.

"The Nanavati-Mehta report has overlooked the wealth of evidence on record, taken them selectively, relied heavily on the investigation carried by Noel Parmar, which was not accepted by the Supreme Court and come to its own conclusion," said Mukul Sinha, who appeared on behalf of the JSM before the Commission.

The JSM said that while the Nanavati Commission had rejected almost point wise the accident theory, it had failed to provide any reasons for doing so.

Sinha said: "The conspiracy theory has many holes. If the train had come on time instead of being five and a half hours late, where would the mob come from? Also, no body knew that karsevaks were coming back by the train. There are many questions like this that have been brushed aside by the Commission."

The JSM pointed out that the Commission had wrongly come to the conclusion that there was no attempt of abduction of Sophia Banu by karsevaks at the Godhra Railway station.

The JSM's report said that Sopihya had appeared before the Commission and had on record sated that there was an attempt made by karsevaks to abduct her.

The JSM will soon present a copy of their report to the President, Governor and the Prime Minister.

Heading: Self over service: Doctors say a big ‘no’ to rural posting - Indian Express
Content:
In a joint operation carried out by the city police and the Labour Department, a total of 19 child labourers were rescued from some tea stalls and restaurants at Ellisbridge, Naranpura and Vastrapur areas of the city on Friday.

All the children have been sent to the Khanpur Remand Home for juveniles.

Labour officials said they could have rescued many more had news of the raid not spread like wild fire.

"We were keeping a close watch on the tea stalls outside V S Hospital and educational institutes including the IIM and Gujarat Vidhyapith as we had information about some stall owners employing juveniles at these places. A total of nine stalls were raided," said Assistant Labour Commissioner Shruti Modi.

The city police have arrested the owners of these tea stalls and restaurants.

Those arrested have been identified as Gajendrasinh Rajput, Kantabhai Thakur, Tushar Patel, Devilal Joshi, Naresh Pandey, Murlidhar Babara, Mohanlal Tekwani, Pukhraj Marwari, Bharat Patel and Ushabhai Teli.

In another incident, at least 20 people were injured in a road accident near Firozpiura Patia on the Himmatnagar-Ahmedabad Highway in Gandhinagar on Friday evening.

The mishap occurred when a speeding truck hit a State Transport bus. All the injured were rushed to the Civil Hospital in Ahmedabad and are out of danger, the police said.

Heading: Establishing industries made easier now - Indian Express
Content:
Out of 872 selected for primary and community centres, only 69 joined duty, says Health minister

Very few doctors had joined service in the rural areas in the last eight months despite the fact that such orders had been given to hundreds of doctors, Health and Family Welfare Minister Jay Narayan Vyas told the state Assembly on Saturday.

Out of a total 872 appointments of allopathic doctors between January 1 and August 31, 2008 for primary health and community centres in the rural areas, only 69 turned up to join their duties. Vyas said the rest did not even intimate about not joining their duties. Even doctors belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes did not show much interest in serving in the rural areas, he said.

He said out of the 52 SC doctors given appointments, only five turned up for duty. The corresponding figure was 13 out of 116 for ST candidates and 20 of 405 for general category candidates. He said it was not only allopathic doctors who had shown reluctance to serve in the rural areas. Out of the 238 homoeopathic doctors given appointments, only 98 came forward to join in the rural health centres. Only 457 of the 607 ayurvedic doctors appointed, joined their duties, he added.

Vyas informed the House that the Gujarat Public Service Commission was holding open interviews for appointment of doctors every Tuesday, yet few doctors turned up to take up the assignments. In response to a question by Opposition leader Shaktisinh Gohil, Vyas said that the state government paid full salary with all benefits to the permanent doctors.

On being questioned by Gohil as to what his ministry was doing to find out about the reasons for doctors not taking up rural assignments, he said his ministry planned to write letters to those who had not turned up and joined the assignments.

Regarding bonds signed by medical students to serve for at least one year in rural hospitals after completion of courses from government medical colleges in the state, Vyas said most of the doctors managed to bypass it by paying the bond amount.

He also informed the House that five new colleges with a total seat of 700 would be opened in the state from the next academic year to stop the flight of students for medical education to other states.

Heading: Pirated CDs worth Rs 8.51 lakh seized - Indian Express
Content:
The state Assembly passed the Bombay Land Revenue (Gujarat Amendment) Bill on Friday, which will enable investors to set up industries in areas within five-km outside the periphery of the land under the jurisdiction of any Area Development Authority or Urban Development Authority in Gujarat.

Moving the Bill in the House, Revenue Minister Anandiben Patel said the Bill seeks to allow prospective investors to set up their industries in this area without obtaining prior permission of the district collector concerned.

The Bill has amended Section 65(B) of the Bombay Land Revenue Code, 1879 under which it was compulsory for investors to apply for non-agriculture (NA) permission to set up industrial units within a five km periphery of such areas.

This will avoid frequent complaints of harassment by investors who want to set up their units in this area, the minister said.

Heading: Air Marshal victorious in Gymkhana club election - Indian Express
Content: The city police seized pirated CDs worth Rs 8.51 lakh from various shops in Vadodara on Saturday. The CDs were seized during raids at the Sainath Trade music shop at Anand Baug society in  Makarpura, Video World in Manjalpur and Maa Barahi Vision near Vadsar. Pirated CDs were also seized from one  Bhavesh Dave, who was selling them on a handcart near the premises of Novino company.

Heading: Hot wheels - Indian Express
Content:
It was business as usual at the Delhi Gymkhana Club a day after elections were held for the post of club president.

The 1,600 odd members were at ease once again after election results declared early this morning gave Air Marshal Padamjit Singh Ahluwalia a 930 to 730 victory over the Army's Lieutenant General Rajender Singh.

Club members were back to their routines. "It is all a political fracas. Ninety per cent of the members do not care who comes to power. I am only interested in a dynamic president, who can accommodate all points of view and give members better facilities," a member said.

The club has always been a favourite pastime for its members. The active lot can be seen at the tennis courts, the elderly bet high stakes in the bridge room, while overworked executives lounge around at the bar over a few drinks.

Some recall its popularity during the hay-days. "The Davis Cup tennis trials were held here in the '70s," a senior member said.

Founded for officers of the British Army, the club has a 35-year waiting list for membership.

Though often criticised for the stress on 'traditions' like shirt collars and proper footwear, members feel there is no harm in enforcing a certain level of discipline and decorum and that therein lies the beauty of this club.

"It has not seen a transition in character, as such institutions perpetuate tradition," Anil Gupta, a member for 30 years, said.

Heading: Fine Grind - Indian Express
Content:
Can't afford to buy a vintage car? Get one on a canvas

When artist Donovan Woodhouse, 32, saw a crumbling 1928 Morris car parked outside his Defence Colony home, he was fascinated by it. Woodhouse rushed for his camera, clicking as many as 102 images and used them as a reference for his canvas. "I processed the film and selected the best images. Within a week I had re-created a real-to-life image using stock images of the Morris complete with circular headlights, long grill and thin tyres," says Woodhouse, an automotive artists who specialises in painting vintage and classic cars. In August 2006, Woodhouse held his first solo exhibition of a dozen vintage car paintings

Automotive art is steadily gaining recognition in Delhi as some artists have dedicated themselves to painting cars, old and new. And with help from art connoisseurs and vintage car collectors, there are enough takers for paintings of Mustangs and BMWs. Among them is vintage car collector Diljeet Titus, who recently commissioned 73 vintage car paintings from Woodhouse. "Since you cannot bring your car into the living room, paintings was the closest I could get to my car," rues Titus, whose living room walls are dotted with various vintage car paintings.

All artists outline their passion for vintage cars as an underlying reason for doing this work. Some also recall childhood memories of growing up around vintage cars. "My father, grandfather, uncle owned a fleet of vintage cars in our ancestral home in Indore, Madhya Pradesh. I would often go for joyrides in my father's Ford Thunderbird and Cadillac. In fifth grade I presented a vintage car painting to my father who later encouraged me to pursue this passion," says 30-something Vidita Singh, a professional automotive artist for the last five years.

However, there is an inherent challenge in painting vintage cars. Artist Satish Chauhan, 51, is busy giving the final touches to the grills of his 1935 Buick series 90, an oil on canvas. "You have to get the dimensions right and cannot afford to go wrong in highlighting the proportions, or the painting is redundant," explains Chauhan, a vintage car artist for the last 25 years. Chauhan also works on portraits, landscapes and abstract art, but it is vintage cars he finds satisfaction in, he says. "Painting vintage cars has helped me grow as an artist. Because of the minute detailing, one begins to look at portraits and landscapes more carefully," says Chauhan, who is planning his first solo vintage car painting exhibition next year.

The style of paintings differs from each artist. While Woodhouse infuses a psychedelic touch in his paintings, Singh tries to romanticise the cars by using softer tones and colours. "These cars belong to a different era that evokes nostalgia in most of us," says Singh. The pricing also varies. While some charge per square inch, others charge depending on the complexity of the work. Sixty-one-year old artist Zameer Hussain charges an average of Rs 30,000 per painting. "The more complex the model, the higher will be rate of the painting. We have to increase the various components in exact proportions," clarifies Hussain, who has done over 25 automotive works. Woodhouse on the other hand prices his works on the basis of Rs 10,000/ square foot and sold his most expensive work of a "1912 Ford" for Rs 1.2 lakh to a collector in Baroda. After all, there is no better way to preserve your family car.

Heading: Saturday date for Capital again - Indian Express
Content:
A new coffee spot blends fusion brews and artistically crafts its pastry cups

Beanstalk, the new pastry shop-cum-coffee lounge at the chic Galaxy hotel in Gurgaon is done up in contrasting shades of black and red velvet sofas, while looming white lamp shades cast a cheerful glow on some artistically crafted pastries (Rs 95 a slice) and fresh brews placed behind a broad glass counter. The space is wi-fi enabled so you can surf while you munch. Barring Mondays, a pianist keeps the ambience lively in the evenings.

Sudarshan Bhandari, Galaxy's executive chef adds a special touch to each of his creations. The chocolate marquise pastry glazed in brown and white checks spurts out deliciously gooey dark chocolate. Check out the strawberry cream cake (Rs 900) — a heart-shaped pink cheese cake studded with several blobs of whipped cream and strawberry jam. There is opera pastry with fine layers of chocolate coffee and cream stacked one by one. Yellow ricotta cheese cake, another creation showcases a block of pale yellow pastry with a sliver of kiwi perched on top. In the pastry titled And there is Florida offers a creamy white platform that stacks chunks of colourful fruits in the centre with strips of chocolate stuck on the sides.

Among its list of regular hot brews, rose cappuccino (Rs 95) stands apart with a subtle flowery fragrance and there are organic teas (Rs 95), fruit smoothies (Rs 125) and lattes (Rs 125) to pick from.

Beanstalk also stacks tie bread (Rs 95) that puts together ribbons of flour meshed with slivers of olive and onions. Among cookies (Rs 125 for six pieces), salted ajwain is well done and vanilla tea cakes will go well with your evening cuppa. If this calls for a sugar rush, add some salted mouthfuls with roasted chicken frittata (Rs 95) and exceptionally well done baby carrot and potato toasties (Rs 95).

Location: Ground Floor, Shopping Outlet, Galaxy Hotel, Gurgaon
Timings: 11:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m.
Contact: 95124-4565000

Heading: ‘When I looked down, all I saw was white dust’ - Indian Express
Content:
Saturday's blasts at Sarai Market in Mehrauli is the ninth blast in South Delhi in the last few years in which no terrorist outfit has claimed responsibility. Police believe the blasts could be the handiwork of locals but in all the nine blasts, there has not been a single arrest so far.

On Saturday, a low-grade bomb exploded in Mehrauli, just two weeks after the serial blasts in Delhi and one week after the Delhi Police claimed to have busted the Indian Mujahideen (IM) module from Delhi.

However, Delhi police does not seem to be ready to believe that it was a "terror strike".

The previous blasts in South Delhi, reported in Hauz Khas, Malviya Nagar, IIT and Lado Sarai, in the last few years, also took place in the same manner but, earlier, the bombs did not cause much damage. Officials, however, said explosive material used in all the bombs were quite similar and nails were used in earlier bombs as well.

"The previous bombs were also made of chemicals and were of low intensity," added a South district police official.

Prior to this, a mysterious blast took place on May 7 this year in Malviya Nagar for which no one was held responsible. It was a low intensity blast in which one person was injured, some cars were damaged and the bonnet of a Mercedes car was blown off. The blast took place in a tin in which tiny nails with explosives were packed.

Police had claimed the blast was caused by some miscreants to create panic in the city.

Prior to the May 7 blast, this year, other than the serial blasts a fortnight ago, three blasts took place, first on January 16, 2008 near IIT Gate, and two consecutive blasts on February 1 at Lado Sarai and Malviya Nagar.

All of them were of same nature, claim the police. A similar blast was reported at the Lado Sarai T-point in July 2005 when at least three vehicles were damaged. Three more blasts took place before that.

"In all the blasts, forensic reports suggested that potassium nitrate and other chemicals (like used in today's blast at Mehrauli) was used and nails were packed in. In all the the blasts, cases were registered under the Explosive Substance Act at various police stations but all of them are still unsolved. We have been making efforts. We checked several chemical shops and questioned many local criminals but nothing came of it," said an official.

As in other such low-intensity blasts, the police denied the role of any terrorist organisation and also there was no intelligence inputs on these blasts including today's.

Freaky Saturday for Delhi:
It is a strange coincidence but all the three major blasts in Delhi in the last three years took place on Saturdays when most markets are crowded. As the blasts shook Delhi again on Saturday, people remembered the serial blasts two weeks ago and the tragic incidents of October 29, 2005 (pre-Diwali blasts) - both on Saturdays.
"I was planning to go out with my family in the evening but would now think twice before planning anything on a Saturday," said Mohit Vats, a software engineer from Outer Delhi.
In Saturday, October 29, 2005 blasts, 61 people were killed on the eve of Diwali three years ago and around 100 were injured.
In September 13, 2008 Saturday blasts, 24 people lost their lives and some 50 were injured while today (on September 27) one died and around 30 were injured. "Police should investigate this Saturday connection," added Mohit.
The serial blasts in Ahmedabad also occurred on a Saturday this year — it was July 26. About 45 people were killed in the Ahmedabad blasts.

Heading: Repeat of trauma: Condition of several victims critical - Indian Express
Content:
Sachin Hans, 25, lives in the same ward (no. 8) of Mehrauli where the explosion took place on Saturday. When the deafening sound rocked the locality at 2.05 pm, he was at home, and not at the cyber café that he runs in the area.

"When I looked down from my balcony, all I could see was a cloud of white dust," he said, recalling the initial moments.

When the dust settled, Hans saw a sea of people sprawled all over — wounded and helpless.

"Due to the impact, some of them had been blown away and landed on the adjoining streets. A 10-year-old boy, Santosh, who had picked up the black polythene bag containing the bomb couldn't be recognised. His body was found in front of an electronics shop a few metres away," he added.

"The area resembled a pool of blood."

Refusing to accept the police's claim that only one person died in the blast, Hans said: "I can't believe that. I alone took at least four people to hospital in an extremely critical condition."

Other eyewitnesses said the police reached the spot quite late. "At 2.20 pm, 15 minutes after the blast, two beat policemen came. Though we had made a call to the PCR soon after the blast, the first van came only around 3 pm and the Station House Officer came to the spot at 3.30," said Sajid, another eyewitness.

Devender Manchanda, yet another eyewitness who runs an electronics shop in the area, rushed five people to hospital in his car. "I didn't know what to do. The condition of at least six people was very critical."

Confusion and panic gripped those at the market after the blast. Devender Singh was fanatically looking for his wife and her sister in the market after the blast. "They had come here for shopping. I don't know where they are now and the police are not telling me anything. I don't know where to go," he said.

Baldev Khattar, another shopkeeper in the area, and his brother, Kale, sustained injuries in the incident. "A part of Baldev's thigh was ripped off," said Sajid.

Raj Kumar, another eyewitness, said: "I saw two people on a Pulsar motorcycle, both of them wearing helmets, dropping a black polythene bag and speeding away. Just when the boy who picked it up screamed at them it blew up."

The men on the motorcycle eventually escaped. Kumar said it was all so unexpected that no body could note down the registration number.

Heading: No terror shadow on historic fest: residents - Indian Express
Content:
Yet another blast struck Delhi on Saturday leaving a child dead and at least 23 injured. Newsline went round the hospitals where the injured were taken.

At AIIMS
21 people were brought into the Trauma Centre through the afternoon on Saturday. Ten people sustained minor injuries and their condition is said to be stable while 10 others are critical. Dr M C Mishra, Chief at the AIIMS Trauma Centre, said, "Five people have been operated upon and five others are also in critical condition."

Injured

7-year-old Siddharth Chaubey had gone to Mehrauli market with his mother Kusum Chaubey (40) and aunt Gyanendri (40) after school. They were a few metres from the site of the blast. Both Kusum and Gyanendri were injured and ran from the spot, which Siddharth says was "like a film scene". He was dragged along with the crowd and minor abrasions. Hailing from Kushinagar in Uttar Pradesh, Siddharth and his mother had come to Delhi meet his father D D Chaubey a few days back. His mother's condition is said to be serious. Nails that flew from the bomb pierced through her thighs, doctors told the family. Gyanendri is also critical with injuries in the face and right hand, her husband Daya Shankar said.

* 26-year-old Surinder Singh Rawat, an engineer with Maharaja Appliances in Karol Bagh, was being operated upon as his elder brother Vir Singh Rawat stood outside. His father Shyam Singh Rawat, meanwhile, was struggling to get inside as the police had cordoned off the area around the entrance. Politicians were visiting the hospital one after the other. "He has been calling incessantly and has been denied permission to enter the hospital," Vir Singh said. Surender was injured in the abdomen and doctors told him that his condition is not serious. The family lives in Delhi University at the government flats. Shyam Singh Rawat is a clerk at the University.

* 11-year-old Sheetal Rawat, a student of class 7 at Vashisht Sarvodaya Vidyalata in Mehrauli, was returning from school with her mother Pratima Rawat when the blast took place. She was walking towards her mother, who had come to pick her up, when the bomb went off. "She was carrying her bag in her hand to hand it over to me when the bomb went off," Pratima said. Sheetal is presently in the Operation Theatre of Trauma Centre.

Sheetal's father Bacchan Singh Rawat works in Munrika. He got a call at 2:35 and rushed to the Hospital. Sheetal has sustained injuries in the face and in the back. Her condition is said to be serious.

* Pradeep Singh Sharma, 21, from Hapur in Uttar Pardesh, had come to his father's house for some days and was returning home to have his lunch when the blast went off. His brother Anil got a call from the hospital around 3 pm that his brother was injured. "After the blast, we were shocked to learn that Pradeep is also among the injured," Anil said. He and his father Brahm Singh Sharma works as a security guard for a company. They were stuck outside the hospital for three hours before a doctor told them that Pradeep's condition was stable. Pradeep sustained minor injuries and his condition is now said to stable.

* Shyam Bhadur (22), who is pursuing his MBA from an institute in Mehrauli, had moved to Delhi barely three months ago. His parents were on their way from Kanpur while his cousin Vipin sat outside the hospital, hoping to hear about his condition. Shyam Bahadur stays in a rented apartment with three friends near the Flower market and was on his way home when the blast took place. All of them have been injured in the blast. "We have still not been able to meet him but doctors say he is fine and will recover," Vipin said. Families of other boys have also been informed.

* Allaudin Khan, 23, had just left home at Sarai market in Mehrauli to go visit a few relatives when the blast took place on Saturday afternoon. A cab driver with the Royal Bank of Scotland in Gurgaon, Khan suffered extensive injuries in his abdomen as pieces of shrapnel pierced his stomach. "We have operated upon him, but he is in a critical state and is being moved to the ICU," said a senior doctor at the trauma centre. revealed.

Heading: Cops hunt for local hand - Indian Express
Content:
With the deafening sound of the Mehrauli bomb blasts, Ram Naresh Singh, 52, thought that Jahaz Mahal - the site of the annual Phool Walon Ki Sair: adjacent to the blast site, would crash on top of him. Two months ago, some part of the ancient structure had collapsed. On Saturday, Jahaz Mahal stood tall, seemingly in defiance, of the terror strikes.

For the people of this small but crowded market, the Phool Walon Ki Sair, slated for October, must go on. The blast ruined three shops in the market. But this year, the people in the area, which has a large number of Muslims, are adamant that come what may, the festival must go on with no change in schedule.

Ram Naresh Singh has been the guard at Jahaz Mahal, a centrally-protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India, latticed with signature blue Lodhi tiles, for the past 10 years. He has seen another ancient structure in the complex crumble roughly two months ago. "When I heard the blast, I was sitting in the middle of the Jahaz Mahal. My first thought was that with the deafening explosion the monument would fall. But it didn't," he says, with pride.

The area where he sits transforms into a stage for the annual Phool Walon Ki Sair, a festival of flowers, Kathak dance and qawwali, which has been celebrated since the 19th century and was patronised by Bahadur Shah Zafar.

"No matter what happens, the Phool Walon Ki Sair must not stop," says Raqeeb from the Sarai market.

Today, Ramazan Taravi prayers (special prayers during Ramzan) were disturbed by the commotion after the blasts. Devotees prayed at the Auliya Mosque, a few paces away from the blast site. Down the same lane, is Auliya Masjid and Pankhewali Masjid. The site is close to Mehrauli's Archeological Park that has Balban's grave and the beautiful but desolate Jamali Kamali tomb — recently made famous when song sequences in the Shah Rukh-Preity Zinta starrer, Veer Zara were shot here.

Blast victim, 9-year-old Santosh Kumar was a resident of Islam colony, a predominantly Muslim colony.

Heading: ‘Blast’, not ‘terror strike’ - Indian Express
Content:
'Bad characters' quizzed

Hours after a bomb blast killed one and left 23 persons injured in Sarai market of Mehrauli on Saturday afternoon, the police suspect a local hand behind the incident.

Sources said several people, who the police called "bad characters" from adjoining areas, were detained for questioning. "There are vital clues that point towards the fact that some local/locals, well-versed with the area, is behind the blast," an officer said. "The modus operandi suggests that."

A senior officer of south district confirmed that some locals are being interrogated to know more about the mysterious blast. "The way the bomb was left, bomb ingredients and other evidence collected from the spot indicate that a local mind was behind the plan," the officer said. "But we are investigating it from all angles."

Joint Commissioner of Police (Southern Range) Ajay Kashyap also said the probe would cover "every angle". He said, "I would not be able to comment any further at this point of time — an NSG team was called and further investigations are on."

Meanwhile, police sources said they suspect Thursday night's incident in which a motorcyclist was killed following what witnesses called a "deafening sound" could also be a blast. The incident occurred near Qutub Minar, and police at the time had called it a case of "firing" at the motorcyclist — Sanjeev, alias Bablu — though locals insisted it was a bomb.

"The postmortem found no bullet injuries," the source said. "Evidence that came up during investigations of that case and today's blast have a lot of similarities, which has forced us to look at it from a new angle."

Heading: CEO of US firm alleges kidnap bid in Noida - Indian Express
Content:
Most signature features of the recent blasts in different parts of the country were missing from Saturday's mystery blast in Mehrauli. Unlike earlier attacks, there was no claim of responsibility or any mocking email accompanying the blasts, no serial blasts, and the location was not a high-profile area that militants usually target.

The explosions were not triggered by timer devices and no circuitry has yet been recovered from the blast site. Instead, chemicals like sulphur, potassium — and possibly ammonium nitrate, also used in previous bombs — were used along with nails. But sources said it is too early to say anything on the nature of the group that might have carried out this attack.

Investigators have blamed Indian Mujahideen and SIMI operatives for all recent terror strikes in the country. But intelligence sources were today careful even with the use of the term "terror attack". Instead, they just called it a "bomb blast". But daredevilry of the assailants — two youths on a motorcycle are said to have dropped off the bomb in a polythene bag minutes before the explosion — was certainly causing a lot of concern, they said.

The second blast in Delhi within two weeks sent the entire government machinery in a tizzy. With Prime Minister Manmohan Singh out of the country, Home Minister Shivraj Patil met his senior Cabinet colleague Pranab Mukherjee to discuss the security situation. Mukherjee later told reporters that the government would take "more stern" measures to contain militant attacks but did not specify what such measures would be.

Patil, under fire for alleged failure on the internal security front, also held a meeting with high-ranking officials during which he is said to have asked them to expedite steps being taken to raise security in Delhi.

Heading: ‘Every home needs a Mohan’ - Indian Express
Content:
The chief executive officer (CEO) of a US multinational reportedly escaped an abduction bid late on Friday night in Sector 61. Ashish Dwivedi, 37, was driving back home in his Swift car when four people allegedly intercepted him and pulled him out of the car. The accused fled after a few passers-by noticed them, but not before hitting Dwivedi on the head with an iron rod.

The incident occurred around 9.30 pm when Dwivedi, the CEO of Expedien E Solutions Ltd in A-block, Sector 63, was returning home after attending a video conferencing with his US office. He had sent back his driver earlier and was alone in the car.

Dwivedi said a Tavera driven by the assailants overtook him near Shivalik Apartments of Sector 61 and blocked his way. "I thought they wanted to rob me, but they did not do so. Instead, they pulled me out of the car and told me to sit in their vehicle," he said. Dwivedi tried to put up resistance. "I lay down on the road when they tried to force me inside the Tavera. I could not note down the number as the number plate was mudded."

It was due to the passers-by that he could reach home safe, said Vivek Kumar, Dwivedi's colleague and manager of Expedien E Solutions Ltd. "As he (Dwivedi) screamed for help, a few cars passing by the area stopped. Seeing them, the kidnappers fled," he said. "Before they got back to their car, one of them hit me with an iron rod," said the CEO.

Dwivedi was taken to the Kailash Hospital where he was given stitches on his head. "He was bleeding profusely when brought to us. We monitored him for a few hours and then discharged him," said hospital spokesperson V B Joshi.

A case was later registered against the unknown assailants.

Both Dwivedi and Kumar complained that there was no police patrolling on the entire stretch of Sector 61.

Noida's Senior Superintendent of Police R K Chaturvedi told Newsline that an inquiry had been ordered into the incident. "We are investigating the matter whether it was a kidnapping bid or a case of road rage. We will arrest the culprits soon," he said.

Heading: Teen picks up box to return, is blown off - Indian Express
Content:
Week after death, fortnight after blasts, visiting hero's house

Just over a week after the shootout at Jamia Nagar that left Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma dead, the family is stoic: still mourning the loss, but proud that Sharma has "set an example for others".

"We need a regiment of Mohan Chand Sharmas to remove terrorism from this country," Sharma's brother-in-law Girish Upadhaya said when Newsline visited the family's house in Dwarka. Indicating today's blast at Mehrauli, he added, "The police may have cracked the case (September 13 serial blasts) but that is not the end; we are still seeing blasts. At a time like this every home needs a Mohan."

Eight days after Sharma succumbed to bullet injuries sustained in the gun battle with alleged terrorists, his mother has the slain officer's photograph in hand and looks at it every few minutes, too shattered to talk. But the public empathy, Upadhaya said, is helping them cope with the crisis.

"People just drop flowers, messages and poetries at our gate," he said. "Mohan may not be physically present but I am sure he will continue to live in the hearts of people."

What is disturbing them, however, is being at the bitter end of wrong reportage, as a family member (name withheld on request) said. "A Hindi newspaper wrote the other day that we want Afzal (convicted in 2001 Parliament attack) to be hanged. We have not made any statement; we just want to live in peace."

Children of the housing society, meanwhile, want to emulate their favourite "uncle" now. "When I grow up I will also become a brave officer like Sharma-uncle," said David, a Class III student in the neighbourhood. And the children know they have to be with Sharma's son Divyanshu through thick and thin. "He plays cricket with us but is very sad these days. We hope that he comes out and plays again with us, soon," said Dev.

Heading: Traders, cops up vigil in markets - Indian Express
Content:
Santosh Kumar, 13, was on an everyday errand on Saturday afternoon, on way to buy eggs, when he saw two men on a motorcycle drop a tiffin box in the crowded Sarai market near Mehrauli's flower market. Eyewitnesses said the boy picked up the tiffin box to return it to the bikers, when the bomb exploded.

Death came instantly, say witnesses.

Late in the afternoon, Newsline found his uncle Fantoosh Kumar and elderly grandmother sitting outside the AIIMS trauma centre. They had been there for the last at least three hours, Fantoosh said. Unaware that Santosh was dead.

"I was home when a neighbour came running and said there's been a blast and my nephew was dead. But I don't know whether that is true," Fantoosh said. "I saw him at the blast site before the police bought him here; now I don't know what his condition is."

Santosh's elder brother Bambam Kumar, 21, a rickshaw-puller who worked at the egg stall in the evenings along with Santosh, said, "After the blast claimed Santosh, my mother has also fallen ill. We fear for her, too."
