Santosh's father Bachu Mahto and mother Rekha were also outside the waiting hall in AIIMS. With Rekha sobbing inconsolably, Mahto tried hoping, against hope: "Hope is alive till they let us in and see his body."

A helper at the local Sabzi Mandi, Mahto came to Delhi 20 years ago from Lakhisarai in Bihar; his family came some eight years back. The family stays within walking distance of the blast site — in a one-room flat of Islam Colony. "I had sent Santosh to get eggs," uncle Fantoosh said. "After the blast I rushed to the spot but there was so much pandemonium…. I saw Santosh lying in blood but the police didn't let me get closer."

Santosh was a Class VI student in a government school.

Heading: Minority panel examines L-18, initiates own probe - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi had barely come to terms with the serial blasts that shook the city two weeks ago, when a blast near Mehrauli this afternoon whipped up fear among the people once again.

Marketplaces wore a deserted look unlike any other Saturday evening, as the apprehension of serial blasts swept across the city. Most shops, however, remained open, with traders' associations and the police swinging into action quickly. At GK-I M-Block Market, the traders' welfare association did not wait for the police to take charge and took the initiative to tighten security in the area.

"The public address system used for making announcements for shoppers to be vigilant has been strengthened, while additional CCTV cameras have also been put up," Rajendra Sharda, president of the association, said. "We have also purchased four portable metal detectors to frisk pedestrians, while cars are being checked at all entry gates," he said.

The Delhi Police brought in more cleaners to clear out dustbins — used to plant bombs on September 13. "The cleaners are sweeping all streets and backlanes and after one round of clearing, we have upturned most dustbins," a beat constable, overseeing the cleaning at M-Block, said.

The Sarojini Nagar Market — which witnessed bomb blasts in 2006 — too wore a deserted look, with extra security personnel manning all entry points, and volunteers deployed by the traders' association checked all bags and belongings of shoppers.

"A strong vigil has been maintained today. A security meeting was called after news of the Mehrauli blast reached us this afternoon. We have begun issuing stickers as gate passes for vehicles that are parked inside the market," Bansi Lal Grover, president of the Sarojini Nagar Market Teh Bazari Welfare Association, said. "With such frequent blasts, trade has hit an all time low."

Some customers, however, seemed undaunted by the blasts altogether. "We have come from Pune and after the blast this afternoon we were asked not to go out and shop. But this doesn't make any sense. People should not get scared and stop coming out," Mrinalini Singh, who had come to shop with her family at Sarojini Nagar, said.

Elsewhere, the Delhi Police tightened security at all public places. "We have deployed extra reserve force personnel at the airport, railway stations, metro stations, bus stands, cinema halls and malls. Nearly 30 companies of armed police were brought in right after the blast this afternoon," Rajan Bhagat, Delhi Police PRO, said. "Extra metal detectors were set up at all these places and our personnel frisked all those who came here," he said.

Heading: How IT city is dressing up for the 2010 Games - Indian Express
Content:
The fourth floor of L-18 was opened for an "investigation" by the Delhi Minorities Commission today, for the first time since suspect terrorists Atif and Sajid were gunned down here in an encounter on September 19.

While residents of Jamia Nagar too clamoured for a look at the encounter site, Kamal Faruqui, chairman of the Delhi Minorities Commission, and commission members Pushpinder Singh and Arnold James were escorted by the police to the rooms of the alleged terrorists.

"We are here following an emergency meeting of the commission. We want to take stock of the situation and we have also video-graphed the area. We are setting up a fact-finding committee comprising four members from four different faiths to look into the matter. On Monday, we will submit a report to the Lieutenant Governor. This is not going to interfere with judicial processes. We have also requested the people of the area to maintain communal harmony," Faruqui said.

"We are responding to charges that Muslims are being ill-treated and memos that came to us," he said.

The residents are, however, not fully convinced. For the first time, women of the area gathered under L-18 to speak their mind. "There is a total alienation of the Muslim community," Nasim Ahmed, who brought her daughter with her, said. "A Muslim would never kill another Muslim during Ramzan. Why won't the police let us into the flat and see for ourselves?" she asked.

Another resident said: "If the boys were suspects they should have been arrested, not shot. Also, it's strange to assume that all the boys were terrorists. Living on a student's budget, boys will share accommodation. If one was wrong, how can all of them know?"

Elsewhere, former MCD Councillor Asif Mohammad Khan said: "The Minorities Commission is appealing for communal harmony eight days after the incident. They should see that we have maintained harmony for so many days."

Heading: Lights out, operations hit on 3rd runway - Indian Express
Content:
How IT city is dressing up for the 2010 Games

If nothing else, the 2010 Commonwealth Games would take care of the hapless traffic situation in the IT city. If all goes as per plan, wide and beautified roads, Metro connectivity, an extended expressway, and efficient public transport would welcome visitors to the city, which would host shooting events at the upcoming range near at the CRPF camp near Badshahpur village.

The state government, officials said, has already allotted Rs 770 crore to develop infrastructure, and a major part of it is slated to be spent on connectivity and traffic solutions. "An approach road will be required to connect the shooting range to Badshahpur-Kharagpur road. We are completing land acquisition formalities for that," said Madhu Pradeep, senior town planner of the Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA).

ROADS
According to officials, work has begun on the northern and southern peripheral roads to decongest traffic on NH-8. The 17-km northern periphery road, beginning from Gadhi Harsaru, will connect Gurgaon to Dwarka; the 14-km southern periphery road will start from Badshahpur. "The northern periphery road will also cover the Special Economic Zone (SEZ) proposed by Reliance," HUDA Administrator G Anupama said.
The eight-lane roads would also have 30 metres of green belt and two service lanes on each side. Once the project is completed, traffic bound for Dwarka and IGI Airport from Gurgaon and Jaipur would have the option of skipping NH-8 and avoid congestion.
HUDA is also coordinating work with other stakeholders for the projects, Anupama said. "Recently, we met officials from the Gurgaon Industries Association," she said. We invited their member companies to partner HUDA in beautification of all green belts along the roads and city parks."
She said the civic body had engaged services of a multinational consultancy to prepare a "traffic management plan" that would recommend the size of roads and number of flyovers, underpasses and crossings required for the city. "The agency would suggest a model for Gurgaon's Mass Rapid Transit System as well," Anupama said.

METRO
According to the state government, the 14.5-km Metro line between Qutub Minar and Sushant Lok, linking Gurgaon to the Capital, would begin operation by January 2010, before the Games get underway. Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) officials said the stretch would link 10 stations, five each in Delhi and Gurgaon: these include Garden Estate, Sikandarpur, DT City Centre, IFFCO Chowk and Sushant Lok in Gurgaon.
After Qutub Minar, the elevated Metro line would go underground, DMRC officials said. The line would also provide a direct link to Connaught Place and Delhi University, and is estimated to benefit more than 1 lakh commuters.

INFRASTRUCTURE
According to Gurgaon Administrator G Anupama, four bus depots and a 20-acre inter-state bus terminus will soon be built at Panchgaon in Gurgaon. This aside, 72 bus shelters will be constructed in the city, state government officials said.
The administration has also proposed setting up seven multi-level parking lots before the Games to make up for the lack of parking space in the city. These parking lots are proposed near the mini secretariat, and in Sectors 10, 43, 47, 48, 52, and the City Centre — all areas that get chock-a-block during rush hour.
"'We have already floated tenders to construct two parking lots," Anupama said. "For the other five, tenders will be invited in the first week of October."
She said these lots would be built on one-and-half-acres each, and each will have a capacity to park more than 1,000 vehicles. "Thousands would visit Gurgaon for the Commonwealth Games and we need to live up to the expectations of the residents as well as the visitors," Anupama said.
On a bright note, she added that state authorities have issued special instructions to HUDA to complete all major infrastructure projects in time for the Games.

Heading: Charges to be framed against Amarinder on Nov 15 - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the lights on the newly opened third runway at Indira Gandhi International Airport went blank, authorities have put the blame on BSES grid failure. For the moment, operations during the night have been suspended.

"The entire airport area was subject to power fluctuations from the incoming BSES Grid supply through Mahipalpur, late Thursday evening (September 25). The airport complex ran on the backup power supply until normal services were restored. As a result of high and frequent fluctuations of the power supply, we elected to switch to runway 27 and 28," said a DIAL spokesperson. The IGI has been reeling under frequent power cuts lately.

The initial plan was to open the runway in a phased manner. Initially, the operations were to be restricted till afternoon. This was to be followed by operations in the night only and then later for limited duration both morning and evening.

On Thursday, however, the authorities decided to extend the time till 8.10 pm after the day's smooth operations. The runway was opened at 6 am and continued till 1 pm. It was once again opened at 4:30 pm and the work continued till 8:10 pm.

DIAL has been facing problems with runway lighting. Earlier, the lights were damaged due to waterlogging. The DGCA has reacted sharply to the fact that the standby generator did not energise the lights automatically as soon as the primary supply had a problem.

Ironically, on the first day, DIAL had claimed the pilot of the British Airways flight which was the first flight to land after the runway was made operational, appreciated the lighting system of the runway.

"We are in the unique advantageous position of having a choice of running two out of three operational runways, in different configurations. This means we have a choice of quickly shifting to other runways without adversely affecting the normal operations and aircraft movement rate," the DIAL spokesperson said.

Heading: Gujranwala council honours city docs - Indian Express
Content:
Defence counsels of Amarinder Singh and others said that many of the documents along including the chargesheet, submitted by the Vigilance Bureau in the court were not readable

District and Sessions Judge G K Rai today fixed November 15 as the next date of hearing for framing charges against former Chief Minister Amarinder Singh and others accused in the much-hyped City Centre case.

Defence counsels of Amarinder Singh and others said that many of the documents along with the chargesheet, submitted by the Vigilance Bureau in court, were not readable. They alleged that the officials of Vigilance Police, Ludhiana had not provided them with all the necessary documents, which they had presented against the accused along with the chargesheet.

The lawyer of Amarinder Singh and Manmohan Singh also claimed that the said documents were needed by him to contest the case.

On the other hand, District Attorney Mitter Sen Goyal strongly opposed the application filed by Capt Amarinder Singh and other co-accused and stated that the defence was only attempting to delay the proceedings in the case.

After hearing both sides of the prosecution and defence, Justice Rai directed the defence counsel to complete the inspection of the documents along with the charge sheet by November 8.

Prominent among those who appeared before the court included former Chief Minister Amarinder Singh's son, Raninder Singh, his relative Raminder Singh Richi, former LIT chief engineer Manmohan Singh, former additional Advocate General Punjab, Harpreet Singh Sandhu, Today Home officials, Delhi-based businessman Chaten Gupta and other co-accused.

Five former trustees of LIT namely Sanjay Talwar, Navkar Jain, Bhupinder Singh Basant, Surinder Pal Singh Bindra, and Vikay Kumar Prati also appeared in court today.

Justice G K Rai also accepted the plea of the former Chief Minister and former Local Bodies minister Ch Jagjit Singh and allowed their exemption for personal appearance in court for today.

Also, S K Dev Chief Architect and witness of the prosecution had requested the court to cancel the bail bonds of the accused namely Ashwjit Singh, Sunil Kumar Sharma, Vice-President of M/s Today Homes & Infrastructure Private Limited, Vinay Subhiki, Sayed Arfaz Hussain Naqvi, Gulshan Kumar Ghambir, Saurav Gupta, Ashok Chopra, Baljit Singh, Jagtar Singh, Arun Nayyar, Davinder Kumar Anand, Sunita Ghambir, Natasha Ghambir, Vikram Ghambir, Yashu Ghambir, Sanjay Jatwani, Anil Narula and Naveen Thakur of New Delhi.

The lawyer of S K Dev Chief Architect, Ankur Ghai alleged that all the said accused had threatened him and filed a false case against him in Delhi.

Justice Rai also fixed October 6 as the day for consideration on the said application.

Heading: ‘Sugar mills will churn out power too’ - Indian Express
Content:
Dr LS Chawla, founder vice-chancellor of Baba Farid University of Health Sciences and Dr Gurpreet Singh Wander, professor and chief cardiologist, Hero Heart Centre, DMC Hospital were felicitated by the Gujranwala Khalsa Educational (GKE) Council on Saturday for their outstanding achievements in the medical field.

The renowned doctors, through their address, inspired budding medical professionals. Mayor Hakam Singh Giaspura was the guest of honour for the felicitation ceremony.

Prof Prithipal Singh Kapur, president of the Gujranwala Khalsa Educational Council and former pro vice-chancellor of Guru Nanak Dev University, Amritsar delivered the welcome address and highlighted the changing scenario of education. Dr L S Chawla stressed on the need for inculcating scientific temper. A series of lectures were delivered by experts and renowned doctors.

Among those present on the occasion were Harmohinder Singh, general secretary, vice-president Prithipal Singh, Gursharan Singh Narula, Harcharan Singh Narula, Kulwant Singh Dukhia Jasbir Singh Nalwa and Principal Jodh Singh.

Heading: ‘IT has made it easy to understand medical concepts’ - Indian Express
Content:
"A sugar complex is on the cards in which ethanol will be produced out of sugarcane juice which can further be used for generating electricity," said Co-operative Minister Captain Kanwaljit Singh while talking at a prize distribution ceremony of the sports tournament at the Budhewal Sugar mill on Saturday. He said that the government is spending Rs 1300 crore to modernise the sugar mills and reduce their losses.He also over-ruled the idea of privatisation of sugar mills,

which according to him was the plan of the previous government. "Genuine demands of sugar mill employees will be accepted and will come in the form of a Diwali gift," he said.

Heading: Man strangles wife to death - Indian Express
Content:
A symposium-cum-workshop on 'Recent Trends in Medical Education: Role of Information Technology' was held on Saturday in Dayanand Medical College Hospital under the aegis of the Medical Council of India (MCI) and Punjab Medical Council (PMC).

The symposium was part of the Platinum Jubilee Year celebrations of MCI.

The delegates were made aware about the latest innovations in information technology relating to medical education.

Dr LS Chawla, founder Vice-Chancellor, BFUHS (Baba Farid University of Health Sciences) and former chairman PG committee MCI was the chief guest on the occasion.

Prem Gupta, secretary of the Managing Society felicitated Dr Chawla on behalf of the DMCH fraternity. He spoke about the various developments made in MCI over the last few years.

The workshop included lectures and group discussions by various experts. The faculty members from DMCH who delivered addresses included Dr Daljit Singh, Principal of DMCH, Dr SC Chopra, Dean Academics, Dr Gautam Ahluwalia, professor of Medicine and Dr Rajesh Arya, consultant, Cardiac Anesthesiologist. It was stressed during the workshop that with the advent of IT in medical education, it has become easy for students to understand medical concepts in an interactive manner.

The guest resource faculty included Dr Jatinder Singh, professor of Pharmacology, Government Medical College, Amritsar who spoke on 'Web-based tools' and Dr Rakesh Jindal, associate professor of Computer Programming, Punjab Agricultural University.

Dr BS Aulakh, professor of Urology & Transplant and Head of the Transplant Unit at DMCH along with Dr BS Shah, Medical Superintendent, DMCH and member PMC were the designated observers for the symposium-cum-workshop.

Heading: Roads to be repaired in 10 days: Ghuman - Indian Express
Content:
Crime in city: Rajesh Kumar hides the body of 26-year-old Rinku in a trunk

A man allegedly strangled his wife and put her body in an iron box meant for keeping clothes. The body of the woman was recovered this morning, a day after her murder.

The police have booked Rajesh Kumar, a resident the Baba Namdev colony, for reportedly killing his wife Rinku (26). The motive of the murder is stated to be incessant feuds between the couple.

According to police, the couple was married for the past five years but used to fight often over petty matters. Sources said the man, who used to work as a labourer, had been booked in a couple of petty criminal cases.

Sources said that owing to their never-ending matrimonial dispute, Rinku's mother Sudheera Devi had called the couple to stay at her house till their dispute was resolved.

On Friday morning, when no one was at home, the accused reportedly strangled his wife and called up one of her relatives at 1.30 pm informing them about the murder. He also told them that he had hidden her body. When Sudheera Devi came to know about this, she took it as a prank. When she returned home the same evening, she did not find her daughter or son-in-law home and thought they had gone out somewhere, police sources added.

Sources said that the murder came to light this morning when Sudheera Devi opened the trunk and found the body.

After registering a murder case against Rajesh Kumar, the police have started searching for him. Meanwhile, Rinku's body was taken to the Civil Hospital for a postmortem.

Heading: MC makes garbage sites out of woodland - Indian Express
Content:
No road estimate will be made if the storm sewer work has not been done earlier on that road. This was stated by MC Commissioner G S Ghuman while addressing a meeting of MC officials this afternoon.

Ghuman said that in the past, a number such cases had come to light where road metalling was done before expanding sewer lines, which has often lead to wasteful expenditure.

However, he admitted that roads in the city are in a real bad shape and needed immediate repairs.

Ghuman said, "All the main roads will be repaired within 10 days while the inner lanes will be repaired within a month's time." The commissioner also inspected the quality of work on the Chandigarh Road and reprimanded officers for not appropriately designing the road. "It would have caused water logging towards one side of the road. The officers now have been directed to get the work rectified," said one of the officers. The Commissioner said, "No compromise will be made on the quality of work. If anyone is found guilty then the officers from junior engineer to superintending engineer will be pulled up."

He said the work to remove illegal hoardings from unipoles is in progress in the city. "In the next round, illegal hoardings on the private buildings will be removed." The Commissioner said that they plan to privatise the removal of garbage in the city. "Rs 9 crore is the bill of diesel of the vehicles that remove garbage from across the city. Talks are on to privatise streetlights where the expenditure is pegged at around Rs 4 crore," he said.

Heading: Dengue cases touch 200 mark - Indian Express
Content:
Forest department issues 1,500 notices to shopkeepers, MC and residents for blatantly misusing the forest land

Taking strict note of the misuse of the forest land, the district forest department has sent around 1,500 notices to shopkeepers, residents and the Municipal Corporation.

The notice sent to Municipal Corporation categorically states that garbage should not be dumped in the forest area along the roadsides.

More than 15 garbage sites have been made along the roadsides in between eucalyptus trees. The spill over rubbish from these sites often damages the trees apart from emanating foul smell. There are many shopkeepers who have encroached upon the forest land by displaying their products. Some have even used it for parking purposes while others have rented it out to vendors.

Taking a strict note of all this, the Forest department has asked the Municipal Corporation to find some solution to disposing of the garbage. The residents have also been directed to stop the misuse of the forest land and contribute in making the city clean and green.

District Forest Officer (DFO) Mahavir Singh said, "We have sent notices to residents and MC. If they don't comply with the same, legal action will be taken against them."

The garbage sites on the Ferozepur Road near GADVASU, another near Sherpur Chowk, Aggar Nagar, PAU gate number 2 and many other locations all fall under forest land. This means that the Municipal Corporation is clearly violating the Environment Act rules.

Garbage from nearly 13 localities was being thrown in a bin within the forest area near GADVASU. Garbage at this site used to spill out to about a kilometre. Though the Municipal Corporation has stopped throwing garbage at this site for the past many days following notices sent by Forest department, allegations are also being levelled that the MC staff is charging about Rs 400 for throwing garbage — the claim being refuted by Zonal Commissioner Kuldeep Singh.

Sanitory inspectors alleged that residents from Rajguru Nagar, Aggar Nagar and even the BRS Nagar were throwing garbage at this site. The residents were asked to install garbage bins in their colonies for the smooth removal of trash but no action has been taken as yet.

Meanwhile, Commissioner G S Ghuman had also directed the Sanitation department to identify some other sites and has also asked residents to place bins in the localities.

Zonal Commissioner Kuldeep Singh, however, said, "Everyone wants to keep their houses clean by littering the roadsides. This is totally unjustified."

Heading: Punjabis more prone to heart diseases: study - Indian Express
Content:
The number of suspected and confirmed cases reported from various hospitals crossed the 600-mark with different hospitals across the city admitting 37 suspected patients

The confirmed cases of dengue in the district touched the 200-mark today — almost a ten-fold increase in the number of patients in the past ten days.

The number of confirmed cases of the disease was 19 on September 17. The Health department officials today said that there are 100 more suspected cases of dengue.

Meanwhile, the total number of suspected and confirmed cases reported from various hospitals crossed 600 with different hospitals admitting 37 suspected patients.

Two major hospitals — Dayanand Medical College and Hospital and Christian Medical College Hospital —have together admitted about 500 patients so far.

The Indian Medical Association (IMA), while expressing concern at the high number of reported cases of dengue in the city, has demanded a coordinated approach between the health providers and civic authorities to sort out the yearly menace of dengue and gastroenteritis.

"Whereas the health providers can spread awareness about prevention and management of the disease, the civic authorities have to provide basic infrastructure facilities like housing, drinking water and sewage facilities and preventive measures like fogging of mosquitocidal agents. We have to adopt a holistic approach towards health care which is possible only through a coordinated approach," an IMA statement said, adding that it has already written a letter to the commissioner of the Municipal Corporation for fogging on war-footing.

Heading: Cops arrest three vehicle lifters - Indian Express
Content:
While the increasing incidence of coronary heart problems in the country is already ringing alarm bells, the situation in the state is indicating a high rate of incidence too.

According to a survey conducted in the western Punjab, which includes Ferozepur, Faridkot, Muktsar, Ganganagar and Barnala, the incidence of heart disease was pegged between 12 and 14 per cent.

The survey, which was conducted by Dr Chetan Sharma, presently associated with SPS Apollo Hospitals as senior consultant in intervention cardiology, listed the apparent factors leading to a high rate of incidence, wherein diet pattern was seen as a serious concern.

The report was also published in the Indian Heart Journal after Dr Sharma analysed the date of some 1,000 persons following the survey conducted from 2003 to 2005.

He said, "The survey concluded that with the changing

diet patterns and other related problems, the people were becoming more risk-prone to heart diseases."

Listing the factors, Dr Sharma said, one of the major contributory factors was hypertension, present in about 25 per cent cases, closely followed by diabetes in 15-18 per cent cases. "But obesity was observed in up to 30 per cent of the cases selected from both rural and urban areas, indicating how much damage present diet patterns are causing to the heart."

According to Dr Sharma, the data compiled over a period of two years showed how much the people were prone to the heart diseases in the state.

Showing concern over the increasing incidence of heart problems in the country, he said that there was little focus on the prevention of the disease which is acquiring a mammoth incidence rate.

"The more glaring factor was that it was present in younger patients than expected. Another noteworthy point that came to the fore was that in many cases, the disease was also not confined to the single vessel.

By 2015, we are going to become the heart disease capital of the world and at the rate of this increasing prevalence; the country will have half the heart patients in the world. This means that every tenth person in the country will be affected by a heart problem," he added.

Suggesting ways to counter the increasing incidence, he said, "It is high time we had a social movement to focus on the ever-growing problem. A national heart disease prevention programme is now the need of the hour since there are a considerable numbers of heart

patients who find it hard to meet the expenses of the disease. In any case, prevention is the best

solution."

Heading: Ajit Pawar extends support to warkaris - Indian Express
Content:
The Haibowal police have arrested three men and claimed to have recovered as many as 17 stolen motorcycles from them on Saturday. According to the police, the trio are drug addicts and used to steal bikes for arranging money for purchasing drugs.

The arrested persons have been identified as Hardeep Singh alias Deepa, Sukaran Kumar and Manoj Kumar. The police said that the Station House Officer (SHO) of Haibowal police station, Prem Singh had received a tip-off about the accussed, after which the police set up a check-post near the South City area along the Sidhwan canal. When asked, the trio could not provide the documents of the motorcycles they were riding.

The police said that on interrogating them, the trio confessed that they had stolen the bikes. Later, the police recovered 14 more stolen bikes which they had hidden after stealing them. Further investigations were on in this connection, the police said.

Heading: Few citizens enter development ring with new ideas - Indian Express
Content:
84-mm incendiary ammunition can penetrate brick wall, create high temperature effects and suffocating fumes; was demonstrated to army in June

Operations to flush out terror suspects from hideouts need not witness any unnecessary spilling of blood and if scientists at the High Energy Materials Research Laboratory (HEMRL) in Pune are to be believed, the bloodshed in the recent shootout between the Delhi police and terrorists could have been avoided.

That is, if the army had taken into its arsenal the ammunition developed by the HEMRL for such situations, say the scientists. They had demonstrated the capabilities of the 84-mm incendiary ammunition to the army around three months back.

The ammunition is designed to penetrate a brick wall, create high temperature effects and produce suffocating fumes, the combined effect of which can force the enemy including any anti-national elements holed up inside a room or a building to come out.

In fact, the ammunition had been developed specifically on the request of the army to be used against terrorists. Its capabilities had also been demonstrated to Lt General Rajender Singh, Director-General, Artillery, in June at HEMRL. But ever since, there has been silence from the army, said Dr RK Pandey, joint director, HEMRL.

"We have perfected it to the last detail and all tests have been carried out. It's the result of two years of R&D by our team. We demonstrated its capabilities to the Director General, Artillery, when he came here in June. He was impressed and said it was just what the army needed. After that, there has been no word from the army with the whole thing is presumably caught in procedural delays," Pandey said.

"The sanction should not really take so long because the ammunition has been proven and tested and is ready for supply. In the recent case of terrorist crossfire in Delhi, the police could have well benefited from this technique and the death of the police officer could have been avoided and perhaps the terrorists could have been caught alive," said Dr Amarjeet Singh, associate director, HEMRL, the leader of the product development team.

According to Singh, the material used in the ammunition is similar to what is used for making matchsticks, that is red phosphorous, which is modified by adding other incendiary materials. The simultaneous effect of high temperature and suffocating fumes is created by an unusual composition combining a high temperature producing metal and suffocating fume producing chemical dispersed in a polymeric binder.

"This ammunition can be effectively used to counter terrorists in urban areas without causing collateral damage to the populace and installations in the surroundings. Also, the production technology of such a unique composition can be readily transferred to ordnance factories," added Pandey.

Earlier, a 38-mm shell was developed two years ago by HEMRL and given to the Border Security Force. This, said Pandey, is being extensively used by the BSF to counter insurgency and flush out ant-national elements from their hideouts in the northern states, particularly Jammu and Kashmir.

This shell contains a 250-gm composition and can penetrate wooden doors, windows and barricades and one-inch-thick wooden planks from a distance of 60-70 metre, as opposed to the latest 84-mm munition that has a three-kg projectile with composition payload of 1.2 kg and a maximum range of 300 metre.

"Since this is heavier ammunition it should be ideally used by the army and paramilitary forces while the earlier lower one can be used by BSF. In fact even the 38-mm shell could have been used in the Delhi encounter," said Singh.

The HEMRL scientist are hopeful that the procedural delays would soon be overcome and orders would be placed for the 84-mm ammunition that has now acquired significance with a shift in the terrorist activities from border areas to heavily populated cities.

Heading: Bodies of 4 PMC employees to reach city today - Indian Express
Content:
The city, known for its high level of civic activism, has failed to take advantage of an initiative for people's participation in the development process, with the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) receiving only three proposals seeking funds for development.

To make matters worse, only one proposal was found good enough to be forwarded to the Union government for consideration. The Union government had launched the Community Participation Fund (CPF) under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) in August 2007 to promote citizen's participation in the development process.

"We received only three proposals despite a public invitation. Only one could be forwarded as the other two failed to meet the eligibility criteria," said Ashok Kalamkar, Joint Municipal Commissioner, PMC. The one that found favour with the civic administration is a proposal for a pre-fabricated plant to make biogas from garbage, mostly leftover food waste from 500 households in Gokhale Nagar. The other two were for a crèche at Hinganemala in Hadapsar and a library in Gokhale Nagar.

"The proposal of Dyanal Mahila Mandal for a pre-fabricated biogas plant was the only one found eligible for the CPF. The other two proposals were ruled out as the civic administration was unable to provide land," Kalamkar said.

He admitted that the process of seeking CPF is tedious and needs to have the consent of 51 per cent of the population of the area with an assurance of self-sustainability of the project.

Ranjit Gadgil, Director at Janwani that focuses on people's participation in governance, said he was not surprised by the poor response to the CPF as the process for sending the proposal is too complex. "The PMC has not been successful in creating awareness on CPF and there is no way the citizens can fulfill the tedious process," he said.

NGOs are ready to help in preparing the proposals only if the civic body takes up the responsibility to create awareness and convince people about the benefits of the CPF, he said.

"We were expecting the mandatory 51 per cent consent from the community members, but around 80 per cent came together in favour of implementing the biogas project," said Bhagyashree Orase, president of Dyanal Mahila Mandal.

In accordance with rules under CPF, around 30 community members have taken up the responsibility for its operations and maintenance to make it self-sustainable.

The members in the community have also assured in writing to raise 10 per cent of the project cost themselves. If waste from 500 households is recycled it could create energy that will help in reducing the consumption of LPG, Orase said.

Where people can help in development

* Projects eligible for CPF under JNNURM: Solid waste management, community biogas installation, crèche, centre for elderly, building or rebuilding local vegetable markets, legal education resource centre

* Maximum assistance of Rs 10 lakh; mandatory contribution of 5 per cent from poor communities and 10 per cent from other communities

* Resident associations, neighbourhood groups, youth clubs and market committees can apply for CPF

* Maximum duration for project implementation is one year

Heading: B’lore blast prime accused trained SIMI cadre in Pune - Indian Express
Content:
The dead bodies of the four Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) employees who lost their lives in an accident near Kulu in Himachal Pradesh on Friday will be brought back to Pune in a special chartered aircraft by Sunday afternoon. The dead bodies were taken to Chandigarh from Kulu on Saturday evening.

The condition of one of the 31 injured is said to be serious.

BJP corporator Vikas Mathkari, a PMC corporator, who rushed to Kulu after the accident, said, "Everything is under control now. The death figure has fortunately not gone beyond four. Two seriously injured persons are being given treatment at the Chandigarh hospital. The other injured, who had fractures, spine injury and flesh wounds, have been given the necessary treatment by the local medical staff."

"A special plane has been chartered and the bodies were sent to Chandigarh. We will leave for Pune on Sunday morning along with the injured people and reach Pune by afternoon," he said.

Heading: Soul salvation - Indian Express
Content:
Investigations have revealed that Mohammed Sami (23), the prime accused in the Bangalore serial blasts, had trained SIMI recruits in Pune. This came to light when a team of Bangalore police brought Sami to Pune on Thursday. Bangalore Police Commissioner Shankar Didari confirmed this but refused to divulge details.

"We will not give any statement to the media as investigations are on," Didari told The Indian Express over telephone from Bangalore.

Meanwhile, the teams of Ahmedabad and Delhi police are also zeroing in on a few suspects in Pune. The Anti Terrorist Cell of Bangalore police had arrested Sami at his native place Bijapur in Karnataka with jehadi literature. He was produced in the AMCC court, Bangalore on Thursday as the main accused in the blast at Madiwala bus stand, which claimed the life of a woman Sudha Ravi on July 25.

Sami was remanded to police custody for 14 days before he was brought to Pune the same day.

Investigations revealed that Sami was close to top Indian Mujahideen operatives including Abdul Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer and SIMI chief Safdar Nagori. Sami had provided IED (Improved Explosive Devices) for the Bangalore blasts, police said.

Sami's interrogation revealed he had visited Pune several times since 2002. Bangalore police were on the lookout for those who gave him shelter while he trained the SIMI cadre in Pune. A team of Bangalore police, led by Joint Commissioner (crime) Gopal Hoshur, brought Sami to Pune by flight on Thursday night.

The team was in Pune on Friday after which Sami was taken to Bijapur. Interestingly, the Gujrat police had earlier arrested Dr Mohammed Salim Honali, also from Bijapur, for his alleged involvement in the Ahmedabad blasts. Honali was a professor of dentistry at M A Rangoonwala College at Azam Campus in Pune for about a year.

Sami is a seventh semester student of Bijapur's Socio Economic Cultural Association of Biijapur. He had visited Bangalore with his friends several times and also stayed in the city with a friend at the time of the blasts.

Police are now trying to unearth the links between Sami and Honali, as the latter was proficient in making bombs and Honali had trained SIMI operatives in Dharwad where on Friday, two explosive devices were detected and disposed by the police.

Now that, Gujarat and Delhi police are also on the lookout for terror suspects in Pune, investigative agencies believe that Pune is emerging to be a major operation hub for terror outfits.

"Investigations teams of Maharashtra and other states are visiting various locations in the country to verify the information revealed during the interrogation of blast suspects," said state Anti Terrorism Squad (ATS) chief Hemant Karkare.

Heading: Puerile plot - Indian Express
Content:
Spiritual science has always believed that death is not the end of a being. And as the soul that departs from one incarnation, it leaves back the testimony of its existence in form of family, friends or relations that had been close to him. In Hindu tradition, Pitru Paksha or Mahalaya Shradh is dedicated as the most powerful and auspicious time, to pay homage and remember one's ancestors.

"Shradh is a memorial rite that is performed on the death anniversary of a person and Pitra Puja is a reverence to our ancestors," says Sunita Shide, who along with her family performs these rites every year. The fortnight of Pitru Paksha falls in the second half of the month of Bhadrapad according to the Hindu calendar. During this ritual spiritual practice such as chanting mantra and praying are observed and donations in form of food, money or planting a tree is followed as a ritual in different homes. "The puja and donation of meals is an offering for our Pitris (the lineage) who are believed to be reincarnated now. We pray for their departed souls to attain peace in their next birth," says Shinde.

The custom of Pitra Puja is not restricted to blood relations only. If one wishes they can perform these rites even for a deceased relative or friend. "The fortnight of Pitru Paksha is said to ensure salvation to the soul of Pitris. Mostly, this ritual is performed for three generations of Pitris — the father, the grandfather and the great grandfather but it may also be done for all Pitris on Amavasya. For this we invite some people home for a meal and we are also invited by others," says Datta Jagtap.

"According to our customs, we offer food to a crow, as it is believed to have a connection with our ancestors. Once the crow takes our offering, the ritual is done and we can resume our meals and other activities. We perform these rites according to our traditions under the guidance of a holy priest who is called as Jagam," says Meera Shinde, a housewife.

"It is a belief that during the period of Pitru Paksh, all auspicious and important activities such as investments, purchase of property or assets and matrimonial decisions must be avoided as this period is dedicated for the ancestors," adds Jagtap, who plans to buy a bike for his grand son and jewellery for his wife, once the fortnight of Pitru Paksha passes away.

Heading: ‘CM’s stay order at Dow site is just to help a smooth CYG’ - Indian Express
Content:
Film: Hari Puttar, A Comedy Of Terrors

Directed by: Lucky Kohli

Cast: Zain Khan, Swini Khara, Sarika, Jackie Shroff, Lillete Dubey, Vijay Raaz, Saurabh Shukla

Showing at: E-Square, City Pride Kothrud, City Pride Satara road, Gold Adlabs, Adlabs,Fame Akurdi, Mangala

Warner Bros were getting antsy for nothing. Hari Puttar has nothing to do with the Harry Potter films, other than the fact that both have been filmed in England. Hari isn't a young wizard with a scar zigzagging though his forehead. He's just a 10-year-old who gets left behind in a large mansion, somewhere on the outskirts of London. Sounds familiar? Yep, it's got a lot to do with Home Alone, with Zain Khan doing a desi McCaulay Culkin.

Hari is dumped on by everybody: His elder brother thinks he is a total wimp, his cousins laugh at his accent; in fact, the whole caboodle thinks he should be neither seen nor heard. His mom (Sarika) is the only one who dotes over her beloved puttar, but even she forgets him, as the family hares off somewhere, leaving behind our young hero, and his one cousin (Swini Khara) who likes him.

If you remember the first Home Alone flick, you know what happens: The youngsters (Zain, last seen in Chain Kuli Ki Main Kuli, is likeable; Swini, last seen in Cheeni Kum, is not) beat a couple of thieves back, with all their arsenal: Dragging them across lawns, throwing smelly liquids whooshing on their heads, shooting sharp pointed objects at various body parts, and so on.

And because it is a Hindi film, it has an item number, fronted by Shamita Shetty. A larger-than-life villain who has one false eye and a hideous Mumbaiya accent. A couple of hoods called Diesel and Filter (Saurabh Shukla in waist-length rasta curls who lets loose noisy smells from his rear end at regular intervals, and Vijay Raaz in florid flowery suit). A scientist who's working on a secret computer "cheep" (chip). And a script which doesn't know the meaning of sense, and so full of holes that several large-size trucks can drive right through.

Who cares, though? Certainly not the six-year-old sitting right ahead, who chortled his way through much the film. Plot to have your tykes whisked off to the film by elder siblings, while you take in that film you've been wanting to: That's what multiplexes are for.

Film: Rafoo Chakkar

Directed by: B H Tharun Kumar

Cast: Aslam Khan, Nauheed Cyrusi, Shakti Kapoor, Sadashiv Amrapurkar, Tinu Anand, Archana Puran Singh, Meeta Vasisht, Yudisthar

Showing at: Citypride Kothrud, Mangala

And this one has nothing to do with that mid-70s barrel of fun-on-the-run starring Rishi Kapoor and Neetu Singh, other than the fact that they share the same name: Rafoo Chakkar.

Two middle-aged sisters (Archana Puran Singh and Mita Vashist) have to marry within 24 hours to fulfill the conditions of their father's will. Two ne'er-do-wells (Yuddhistir and Aslam Khan) fetch up at their doorstep, and are reeled in, kicking and screaming. In addition to this happy foursome are two curvy airheads (Nauheed Cyrusi and Nisha Rawal), who claim they are penniless, but appear to be dressed (if you call Nauheed's plunging tees 'dressing') to the nines every time they appear on screen.

B H Tharunkumar's previous outing Nayee Padosan had fake sets, loud actors, and a story which didn't have a subtle bone in its body. Rafoo Chakkar takes all these ingredients, and ratchets them up a hundredfold, making it way beyond bad.

The lines are worse. Sample this exchange between the two fellows, about to be led off to their wedding night: "Hamari bohni itni purane customers se nahin ho sakti."

Yeah, it's like that. All of it.

Heading: Rural talent should be tapped: Ramasami - Indian Express
Content:
Warkari sect threatened agitation outside Balewadi Sports complex; says CM is buying time

Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh's one month stay order on the work at the Dow Chemicals site is a gimmick to buy time for the smooth operations of Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) scheduled for October 12, allege the warkari sect that has been agitating against the project.

As the warkaris have pledged that they will not allow the games to take place and threatened a mass agitation at the Balewadi Sports complex if the government did not take action, the CM was forced to take this decision, said Vilas Sonawane of Lokshashan Andolan, a part of the agitation. The warkaris had called a bandh in the temple towns of Dehu and Alandi — near Chakan and Khed — with the support of Shiv Sena on Thursday.

The Chief Minister had issued the stay orders on Friday. The Chief Minister's office said that a retired judge of the Bombay High Court will be appointed within the next few days. All issues raised by the warkaris and activists will be looked into and the report will submitted to the state government within a month.

Sonawane said that they had been protesting against the unit since January. "Earlier this week, we had threatened to gather over 10 lakh warkaris to stage a protest in Pune against the CYG. This prompted the CM to intervene,'' he said. "However," he said, "this will not stop us from confining our agitation in the village." The warkaris are up in arms against the project over pollution fears, Sonawane said.

He said that earlier also the government had appointed a committee, under principal secretary (environment) S K Goel, to examine the objections. However, nothing objectionable was found and the report was submitted after four months. "We feel even this committee also will take its own time,'' he said.

Heading: IIT Prof urges expansion of optical fibre network - Indian Express
Content:
The 66th anniversary of the Council For Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) was celebrated on Friday at the National Chemical Laboratory (NCL) on Friday. T Ramasami, secretary Department of Science and Technology, was the chief guest. Speaking on 'CSIR in the emerging science and technology landscape of India,' Ramasami said, "CSIR has been instrumental in changing the outlook of India towards the global context of science and technology. Since the 1970's, the Indian science and technology scenario has taken a quantum leap, with research and development taking place rapidly. Also, science and technology has now taken centrestage in the national agenda."

"With world-class institutes and universities coming up in the nation, talent should be nurtured from a young age. It should also be promoted such that it eventually helps in the development of the nation," he said.

Ramasami stressed on the importance of improving the quality of research and development. "The potential of people in the rural areas should be tapped. A plan has been approved by the central government in which talented students will be trained and promoted in a manner to take up a career in scientific research and development, right from the age of ten. The plan will include three stages: stage one will recognise students in the age group of 10-17 years, stage two will involve sponsoring their studies in science-related fields from the age of 17-22 and stage three will encourage graduates and postgraduate students aged between 22 and 32 years to take up a career in research. Various scholarships will be awarded.

"The programme should begin soon. This will ensure that there is no dearth of absorption capabilities of the science and technology sector in the near future," he said.

Speaking on the occasion, S Sivaram, director, NCL, said, "It has been a long journey for CSIR, during which it has given the nation some of its best scientists." Former and current employees of the NCL were felicitated at the function, apart from meritorious school students and winner of the annual CSIR Day quiz competition.

Heading: Traffic cops mull strict action against law-breakers - Indian Express
Content:
Optical fibre network is the answer for the information divide in the country, opined Ashwin Gumaste, professor, IIT-Mumbai and a researcher in computer network on Saturday. He was talking to media persons on the sidelines of an international conference on Computer Networks and Securities at Vishwakarma Institute of Technology (VIT).

Citing that the progress of broadband technology in the country has been stagnant for the last few years, Gumaste said the government should address the issue taking relevant policy decisions.

"Though wireless technology is jazzy, it has limitations when it comes to providing information. Considering factors like speed and amount of content, optical fibre network is far better than the wireless technology," he said.

Owing to the higher pricing structure of the optical fibre network, the service providers are hesitant in introducing it making the development of broadband services stagnant in the country. But to fulfill the need to access various forms of information like data, voice, video and IPTV, there is no option but to develop the broadband services, which are dependent on optical fibre network, he added.

Gumaste also called for developing research in computer networks. Anand Deshpande, chairman and managing director of Persistent Systems inaugurated the two-day conference. Rajkumar Agarwal, chairman, Vishwakarma Institutes, H K Abhyankar, principal, VIT, S N Mali, dean, students' activities and Manik Dhore, HOD, computer engineering department were also present.

Heading: Inside Mumbra, again on terror radar - Indian Express
Content:
In the wake of the recent attacks on traffic policemen by commuters and to prevent increasing number of road rage, the city traffic police is mulling to initiate strict measures against law-breakers.

Terming it unfortunate, deputy commissioner of police (DCP) Manoj Patil said that starting January this year, about fifteen incidents of violence against traffic cops have been reported.

"In the incident that took place on Wednesday where a traffic policeman and a traffic warden were beaten up by eight drunken youths, all the accused have been arrested and remanded to police custody," he said.

When asked whether any mechanism to put an end to such incidents will be adopted, he said, "As of now talks are still in the preliminary stage, but if such commuters are caught, it will result in suspension of their license in addition to a heavy fine."

He said, now, there are no plans to equip traffic wardens with batons. "But if need arises, we might have to consider that option too."

On the extremely congested traffic scenario in various parts of the city, especially the stretch from Sancheti hospital to CYG venue, Patil said, "once the road works are over, traffic flow will resume on its normal course. The main problem is due to the road works, which are going on at various parts of the city. Once the roads are repaired, the traffic policemen will be able to man the traffic better and more efficiently. We are hopeful that this will happen soon," he added.

Heading: Inquiry report on cop sent to higher officials: DCP - Indian Express
Content:
Formed by settlers who left South Mumbai after 1992-93 riots, housing here is still largely unregulated

"Market is down due to shortfall in supply. Nowadays there are more enquiries. However the deals do not click. There are completely authorized structures available on sale, but the price tag deters people," says Mohammad Bagdadi, a real estate agent in the Kausa region of Mumbra.

Getting a deal done hastily in a slumped market by turning a blind eye to a two-year-old directive of the police commissioner was what got three real estate dealers and a caretaker of a commercial space in Kausa of Mumbra in trouble with the police. The four were released on bail. However, the label of facilitating the renting of a commercial space to Mohammad Arif, one of the alleged members of the terrorist outfit Indian Mujahideen, will not fade easily. Incidents of Arif and those in the past such as the encounter of Ishrat Jahan, the arrest of alleged Kashmiri terrorist (acquitted by high court) got Mumbra its ill fame.

"In Mumbra you have the affordability and the anonymity. There is a sizeable population living in rented premises that have to keep changing their residences. The familiarity among residents in apartment with permanent occupation, is conspicuous by its absence in buildings with rented accommodations," says Hanif Pitalwala, principal of Holy Crescent High School at Kausa.

Residences on rent could be acquired for as less as Rs 3,000 to 4,500. Incidentally Mumbra after Ulhasnagar is one of the places in Thane district, which boasts of more number of unauthorized structures than legal ones.

"The official plan of a building takes as much as five years to get approved while on the other hand the officials and elected representatives eagerly facilitate unauthorized construction," said Hiralal Gupta, a noted figure and civic activist in Mumbra. According to Gupta, it is the step-motherly treatment given to Mumbra in terms of poor civic amenities that has forced the house owners to flee and put their residences on rent.

A stone's throw away from the Shimla Park, the complex where Arif hired a commercial place, commanding a table outside the Ashrafiya Mosque is 36- year-old Imam Maulana Abdul Salam. "When I had come to Mumbra four years ago, things I had been told about Mumbra would have scared me. However, I realized after coming here that people are the same like everywhere else. This place has got a bad reputation it does not deserve," says Imam Maulana Salam. The cleric said that he was not aware of the facts of Arif's case, however he volunteered that strictly following the directives of the police by the house owners and real estate agents was the only way to check on outsiders who come to Mumbra with bad intentions.

"We cannot call them Muslims as those indulging in terrorism and other anti-national activities are not Muslims," he adds.

Besides the Mumbra people there are also senior officers in the police who feel that Mumbra should not be isolated as a terrorist hide out.

"Following the ghettoization of 1992-93 there was migration from Mumbai by Muslims to places such as Bhiwandi, Mumbra, Jogeshwari, Lokhandwala and Malegaon, that were willing to give them cover. The stigma would only make the people turn more defensive all the time," says a senior police officer who has dealt in anti-terrorist activities.

Heading: Women take heart; you need cholesterol control too - Indian Express
Content:
The inquiry initiated against police inspector Suhas Raikar from Andheri police station for improper behaviour during Ganesh festival is complete and a report has been sent to 'higher officials' of the police department.

The inquiry against Raikar was initiated after residents of the Vazir Glass Compound in Andheri (east) complained to the Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone 10) KMM Prasanna about Raikar having lathi-charged some youths during Ganpati procession on September 9. They alleged that Raikar hauled up a few youths and took them to the police station and detained them. DCP Prasanna confirmed that the inquiry was over, but did not divulge the contents. He, however, said that action would soon be taken.

Momina Paingarkar, one of the residents of the locality and an eye-witness to the incident said, "We took out the procession at around 9 pm and were crossing the road at Natraj Cinema, when Raikar, who was dressed in civilian clothes and was under the influence of alcohol, advanced towards us and started shouting. He also hit a few people with his lathi. All the while he kept shouting on us for bursting crackers. He also summoned a police jeep from his mobile phone and dragged four youths from the procession to the police station."

Sadiq (19), a youth from the locality, who was taken to the police station, says, "When I was taken along with my friends to the police station, Raikar kept accusing us of being drunk when in fact, he was the one who was drunk. We do not drink and even if we do, during 'Ramzan' we do not consume alcohol. It was quite obvious that he was drunk and was harassing us just because we were bursting crackers and he got irritated with the noise as he was standing close to the procession."

Though the locals were later released late in the night, they approached DCP KMM Prasanna (Zone 10) two days later and filed a complaint against Raikar. Prasanna says, "I had ordered the ACP of that division to conduct an enquiry. From what we have gathered, it seems that Raikar was on reserve duty and the police inspector on duty at that time was Fadtare. Technically, Raikar was not supposed to have been there. It does seem that Raikar did not handle the situation properly. I have submitted the report of the enquiry to the higher officials. However, there is an element of confidentiality attached to the report and as such, I cannot comment on the contents of the findings."

Raikar remained unavailable for comments on the issue.

Heading: Five arrested for duping diamond merchant - Indian Express
Content:
On World Heart Day, doctors speak of increasing incidence of heart disease among women, call for precautions

Call centre employee Shweta Bandi (22) does not talk about her medical condition. For four years now, she has been on medication after undergoing a bypass for heart blockage. Severely obese, she even had to take a year's break from college during the treatment.

In 2004, she suffered a heart attack while preparing for her exams, leading to a long journey through angioplasties and bypass surgeries.

"Nobody in my family has had a heart attack. I was the first one and we were caught unawares. My left hand would hurt if I carried anything, but we thought it was because I was not used to carrying heavy stuff," Bandi says.

"We have not been able to narrow down on the cause of her heart attack, except that she is obese. We first conducted two angioplasties on her. As she redeveloped a heart problem, a bypass surgery was conducted," says Dr Vijay Surase from Jupiter Hospital who treated Bandi.

Surase and his colleagues initially checked for usual bone and muscle problems before deciding to conduct an ECG. That is when her heart blocks were revealed.

This World Heart Day, doctors are shifting the focus to women and the need for them to keep in mind the risks they carry, with increased work pressures and a sedentary lifestyle.

"Traditionally, women put on weight around the hips and thighs. But there are now cases of women coming in with fat around their abdomen. This is a peculiarly male problem and should ring alarm bells," says Dr A V Ganesh Kumar from Dr L H Hiranandani Hospital, Powai. "Smoking, sleep deprivation, target-oriented jobs are becoming common among women and they are catching up with men in their diseases as well. I think women should start including heart checks in their routine health checkups."

Doctors say that earlier there would hardly be any cases of women reporting heart attacks before menopause. It was believed that the estrogen released in the pre-menopause period protected women from clots. Moreover, women have shown lesser chances of surviving a heart attack, maybe because they cannot take the stress as well as men do.

"It is true that the number of cases being reported is increasing. There might be two reasons; the incidence is increasing across age groups and also the reporting is higher. Earlier people died of heart attacks and those would not be reported or recorded," saysDr Ashwin Mehta, interventional cardiologist, Jaslok Hospital. "Many women have risk factors like diabetes and hypertension, plus with family history, they are at higher risk. Women on high doses of pills are also at risk."

Vibha Khadye (37) has a busy day, running around for a hyperactive eight-year-old son and maintaining the house. Earlier this year, she was detected with over 90 per cent heart blockage and underwent an angioplasty. "I'm recovering slowly, now the medicines have also reduced. Earlier it used to be really difficult to climb or walk. I was in my hometown when the pain became unbearable and doctors asked us to rush to the city hospital," Khadye recalls. "I have to run around a lot for my child, that puts stress on me,' she says.

Dr Chetan Shah, the interventional cardiologist attached to Lilavati and Wockhardt hospitals, conducted the angioplasty on Khadye. "She had 99 per cent blockage in her main artery, it was a sudden onset. She has a strong family history of heart attacks and has a hyperactive child. He gives her a lot of stress. She has been doing well since the treatment," he said.

Heading: HC dismisses IT dept appeals due to delay - Indian Express
Content:
The Dahisar police arrested five people from various parts of the city on September 24 on charges of duping a diamond merchant.

The accused offered help to sell his diamonds worth Rs 3 crore and disappeared without paying him the money received from the sale.

According to the police, the complainant Bhupad Desai (35) is a diamond merchant based in Dahisar who sells his diamonds through his agents. Around five months back, Desai was approached by the two accused- Nattulal Gadche and Dilip Sanghvi- who posed as agents and offered to help Desai sell the diamonds at a fair price for a commission. Desai agreed and handed over the diamonds to them. Soon after the incident, the two agents stopped reporting for work which fuelled Desai's suspicion. He got worried when they did not give him the money for the diamonds and stopped responding to his calls.

"The two accused had actually sold off the diamonds to some businessmen and vanished without paying Desai the price for it. After waiting for some months, Desai filed a complaint with the magistrate court and we started our investigations based on the magistrate's orders," said Pravin Patil from Dahisar police station.

After preliminary enquiries and investigations, the police arrested the five persons, comprising three people who had purchased the diamonds and the two agents.

Those people who had purchased the diamonds from the two agents have been identified as Bhavesh Shah, Bharat Shah and Madhu Patel, and have been accused of buying the diamonds at a price of Rs 1.50 crore.

They were produced in Borivali Metropolitan Court which remanded them to police custody till September 30.

"We have yet to recover the valuables from the accused. We are grilling

them to trace the diamonds. During interrogation, if we come across any more people involved in the case, we will arrest them too," said Pravin Patil.

Heading: Contract outsourcing suffers due to lack of clinical researchers - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court recently dismissed 40 appeals filed by the Income Tax (IT) department challenging 40 orders of the IT Tribunal for not filing its papers in time. The IT department cited shortage of stamp papers as reason for the delay. The court dismissed the applications which were filed after a delay of over one year.

The court, however, held that a delay of one year in filing an appeal was not inordinate in case of a department like IT that undertakes "large-scale litigation."

The court however allowed those applications seeking condonation of delay between six days to 345 days on the ground, that they provided a "reasonable explanation" for the delay in filing appeal.

IT department contended that every time the department receives an order from the IT Tribunal, a scrutiny report is prepared and sent to the higher officials for approval.

Subsequently, the file is sent to a central government advocate for drafting of the appeal following which court formalities are done. The department contended that a delay can be caused at any of these stages.

Division bench of Chief Justice Swatanter Kumar and Justice A P Deshpande, citing earlier orders, stated that in these cases, government revenue is involved which may not be sufficient ground for condonation of delay but can certainly be considered and cannot ignored by the court.

The court, however, observed that in cases where there was a delay of 400 to over 1000 days, there has been no justification, much less a sufficient cause shown, for condonation of delay.

The court observed that in such cases where inordinate delay is unexplained, the reasons given are either fanciful or opposed to normal course of human conduct coupled with an element of negligence or irresponsible attitude.

Heading: Junior colleges’ website  to be spruced up to provide more facilities - Indian Express
Content:
The latest KPMG- CII report 'Indian Pharma Inc- An emerging Global Pharma Hub', released at the Pharma summit early this month made it clear that India is the preferred choice for clinical research in the world, with Indian pharma industry making impressive strides in the global arena across different business segments. However, one section of the industry, considered as the backbone- the contract research outsourcing- cannot meet the growing demand of clinical trial projects , the reason being a dearth of clinical researchers.

At the launch of the Mumbai chapter of Indian Society of Clinical Research (ISCR), researchers from top pharma companies got together to discuss the challenges faced by the still growing industry. KPMG in a report citing Cygnus Industry Insight, January 2008, stated that the country's clinical research market was estimated at $200 million in 2007 and is expected to touch $500 million to $600 million by 2010.

"The technology is constantly growing, and India is fast becoming a new hub for trials due to large patient population and strict compliance with the guidelines. However there is a serious dearth of researchers," said Dr S M Sapatnekar, dean and director of Clinical Research Education and Management Academy (CREMA).

Currently only 1000 students pass out as researchers every year in the country. According to an Ernst and Young report, India by 2010 would need 15,000 clinical researchers to match the flowing projects for clinical trials.

Now that the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization has relaxed laws and allows phase I human trials in India, industry believes the move is expected to increase contract research outsourcing business to India.

Currently global drug firms are only allowed to conduct mid-stage or phase II and last stage or phase III trials in India.

Only four to five organisations- all private- offer specialised degree in training in clinical research. The government does not recognize these courses. "Only recently Pune University has come up with the course and Mumbai University is planning to come up with theirs," said Dr Sapatnekar, who was actively involved in the government before taking charge of CREMA.

Heading: Singer Mahendra Kapoor dies of heart attack - Indian Express
Content:
After facilitating online application to junior colleges, the website by the deputy director of education, Mumbai region, www.mumbaiapplication .com is all set to spruce up with some additional facilities. One of them would be the provision for online approvals regarding staff members for junior colleges.

The newly introduced approval system is still in its testing stages with around ten colleges (two each from each of the five districts-Thane, Raigad, Greater Mumbai, Mumbai suburbs 1 and Mumbai suburbs 2) having uploaded their data entries on the website.

Sheila Tiwari, deputy director of education, Mumbai region said, "The idea is to streamline the process of approvals. The data entry in online forms will enable aided and unaided junior colleges to upload data regarding the number of staff members, students, subjects, divisions and other details for us to decide on workload for teachers." The college authorities can then be summoned with all the documented information for verification of data after which the deputy director's office will scrutinize the details before deciding on the workload for teachers based on the norms prescribed by the state government. Tiwari added, "Earlier it used to be a long winded and tiring process. Every year after admissions, college authorities from across all the districts would have to come to office for submission of the details."

An official at the deputy director's office said, "The system of approval is slated to become more transparent because all the data including surplus staff or vacancies in different colleges based on which the transfer orders are given, will be available on the website." The website is still not being used for the approval process because the approval software is under testing.

Formats of the table for approval and checklist of document for approval have been put up on the website.

Besides the approval system, the website now contains a list of learning resources on its homepage. Jeetendra Shah, architect, designer and mentor of the website said, "The learning resource section has some popular and renowned open source softwares for teachers to use and contribute to. We will be adding many more to the list." The list contains softwares like Internet Scout Report which has access to 'highly educated content specialists and a world-class array of computer science and library resources', Curriki which is Wiki for curriculum, Digital Media Learning competition that invites participation from innovators in the field of digital media and participatory learning, among others. The website is also set to change its name to www.mahadnyaandydemumbai.in.

Heading: Customs surprise UBI - Indian Express
Content:
Veteran singer Mahendra Kapoor, who gave us hit numbers like 'Chalo ek baar chalo' (Gumrah), 'Neele gagan ke taale' (Hamraaz) and many such melodious songs, passed away on Saturday at 7: 30 pm . He died of a sudden heart attack. He was suffering from kidney problems and was undergoing dialysis. He died in his sleep, said sources close to the family. He was 74 years old and is survived by his wife, three daughters and a son.

A favourite with the BR Banner, he also sang the title song of the hit TV show Mahabharata. Kapoor got his first break in V Shantaram's Navrang in 1958 and worked nearly for the next five decades. He sang more than 25,000 songs in various languages.

The Maharashtra Government had recently honoured him with Lata Mangeshkar Award for his lifetime contribution in playback singing. The funeral is expected to take place on Sunday.

Heading: Rizvi retain waterpolo title - Indian Express
Content:
Jagdish Shukla, former racing correspondent of The Indian Express succumbed to a year-long battle with throat cancer on Thursday. He was 82 and is survived by three daughters and three sons.

Shuklaji, popularly known as 'Ashwamitra' worked with The Indian Express from 1972 to 2001. Shukla was also instrumental in setting up the Western India racing Journalists' Association (WIRJA) along with well known journalists like Cecil Hendricks (Pegasus) and Surendra Dikshit (Shyamakarma). He served as the treasurer of the association until his last days.

"It is indeed a loss to racing. A man of principles is no more. I share the grief with his family," said Vivek Jain, Chairman, Marketing and Media, RWITC.

Heading: Homeless at home - Indian Express
Content:
In 125 years, the role of BNHS has switched from documentation to protection

As one steps into Hornbill House, the Bombay Natural History Society's history of 125 years and natural history of time immemorial overwhelm. Also palpable in the air these days is the excitement over the BNHS' 125th anniversary celebration lineup.

Raising a toast to this society, which has aged very gracefully, an exhibition highlighting the genesis and expansion of the society's functions was hosted by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya. After this photo-heavy peek into the society, now a hub of wildlife conservation, a year-long packed schedule has been worked out.

A look at the society's schedule is proof enough of their motto, 'Discover the living world'. Nature trails conducted shortly are a day trip to

Parsik Hill in Navi Mumbai, nature camp at Nannaj, near Solapur, and visits to the special camp for butterfly watching in Sikkim in October. Two other major outings of the year are trips to Periyar Tiger Reserve in

November and to bird watching camp at Little Rann of Kutch.

The Hornbill House that houses the BNHS, an NGO, is only 43-year old. It came up in 1965 with the government grant of Rs 3.3 lakh. By then, the BNHS had changed many addresses in the city, including Mr Pipson's wine shop. For those who wonder about the building's name, here is the trivia. William, a Great Pied Hornbill, arrived at the Society as a nestling in 1894, and it lived in the society's rooms till 1920. Hornbill House is named after William, affectionately known as the office canary. He also became the society's mascot.

When the society started in 1883 at the Victoria and Albert Museum (presently named as Bhau Daji Lad Museum), thanks to the enthusiasm of eight residents of Bombay, including six Englishmen, to the study of natural history, its main function was documentation, says Isaac

Kehimkar. "Over the years, it has swing into action to conserve the wildlife too," he adds.

After sounding alert over the rapid decline in vulture population, the BNHS has taken up their breeding. It is also working with the locals for the protection of Giant Clams in Lakshadweep and in Vidarva to conserve tigers. Next, it wants to check the extinction of Great Indian Bustard and the Lesser Florican. All these, keeping in mind its late president Dr Salim Ali's guiding principle of conservation based on scientific research. Though the society's operations are spread across India with 20 centres, Kehimkar says they now want to increase their presence in the eastern India.

The society's role has been further diversified as it dabbles in publication. The first step toward this was taken in January 1886, with the publication the Journal of the Bombay Natural History Society. In the following years, a

number of books on wildlife has been brought out by the BNHS. The most popular most them is the magazine, Hornbill, which was started to reach the common man.

To achieve its goals, the society needs to strengthen its corpus. Its director A R Rahmani says, "The corpus needs Rs 10 crore to ensure the society's financial independence in going ahead with its conservation and other plans." The society's membership helps its financial affairs to some extent. The number of members at present is over 4,000. Its honorary secretary J C Daniel says, "This figure is appallingly inadequate."

Heading: All’s well - Indian Express
Content:
Going to one's native state is often a cultural confusion

You can take a Malayali out of Kerala but you can't take Kerala out of a Malayali: That is a common adage given to most Malayalis around the world, even to Pseudo Malayalis like me. A Pseudo Malayali is one who has never lived in the state, is not totally connected to its culture and cannot properly pronounce pazham

(banana) and other such tongue twisters. After spending most of my life in Delhi and Mumbai and visiting Kerala occasionally, I had become a Pseudo Malayali for my home-state's denizens. While in the North, I was just a "Madrasi".

Despite the cultural confusion, I wanted to experience kerala on my own, without my parents tagging me along to relatives' homes. I want to explore Kerala like other tourists do, but knew that I will find it easier than them (after all I am a Malayali at heart).

The myth was to be shattered soon. While studying in Chennai, I shared my hostel room with five other girls. Three of them—Majusha, Sharika and Saumya—were Malayalis born and raised in Kerala. Every time I opened my mouth to speak in my mother tongue, they had a good laugh at my expense. I was the official circus clown for the Mylapore Room 8 (my hostel) family. But the jokes for me stopped when I realised that half of my faculty who were Malayalis did not even realise that I too was one of them unless I told them my name.

When I decided to embark on a journey on my own, my friend, Ayesha Arvind, always ready to try new things, readily joined me. The other five, including another girl from UP, Anindya Upadhyay, warned her of the dire consequences. "Bus drivers will get confused and you will land up at some obscure place, because Dhanya won't be able to pronounce them properly?" They laughed while helping me pack.

From Chennai, Ayesha and I reached Palakkad without any major event. But the journey and the confusion had just begun. After a roller-coaster bus ride, we had to reach a place called Cherkepadi, a place in the interior of Palakkad district. But thanks to my amazing language skills, we reached an obscure place a little outside Palakkad. While another bumpy bus ride took us to the right place after two hours, I finally admitted that my Malayalam truly sucked. But no one put it better than the conductor chetta, "Naat na alale bhasha onum sherikya aariiliya le?" (You are not from town and don't know the language right?) he smiled. Later he gave us directions and we reached our destination.

The rest of bus journey was totally worth it. Not only we got have an adventure, but we also partook of some breathtaking sights.
